description: A compact deciduous shrub with neat, oval, dark green leaves and clusters of slightly fragrant white flowers in summer and autumn
A scrambling deciduous shrub with slender branches bearing dark green leaves and racemes of forsythia-like, fragrant white or pale pink flowers 1cm across

alternative_names: European silver fir|Christmas tree|silver fir|single spruce|white spruce|Abies pardei|Abies pectinata
description: An upright-growing evergreen conifer to 45m in height, with dark green needles that are silver underneath. The yellow-green cones which appear in late spring are cylindrical in shape and ripen to brown
plant_range: Pyrenees to Carpathians and Balkan Peninsula

alternative_names: Pacific silver fir|Christmas tree|red silver fir
description: Large, conical, evergreen conifer tree growing up to 20 - 30m. New shoots are covered in pale hairs, and small, spherical, resinous buds. Needles, 2 - 3cm long are crowded, borne densely on the upper surface of each shoot, spreading forwards in two rows, neatly covering the branchlet. New female cones are purple, ripening to brown, 9 - 15cm long, ovoid to cylindrical with hidden bracts.

alternative_names: King Boris fir|Bulgarian fir|Macedonian fir|Abies alba var. acutifolia

description: An evergreen, coniferous tree of slender habit, reaching up to 20 - 35m when mature. New distinctive shoots are non-resinous, long and spindle-shaped. Sharp-pointed, dark glossy needles, silvery green beneath, are among the longest and widest of all Abies, growing to 5cm long and 3 mm wide. They cover branches in 3 or 4 ranks. The species is also distinctive by its unique, golden-brown seed cones. Ovoid, up to 8cm long cones have large, protruding bracts with long, narrow, reflexed points, often covered with drops of resin.

alternative_names: Greek fir|Grecian fir|Abies cephalonica var. cephalonica|Abies cephalonica var. apollinis
description: A large, fast-growing evergreen conifer with a cone-shaped habit and glossy green sharp, rigid needles with a blue-white stripe underneath. Brown cones appear in the autumn which break up into seeds when mature. The bark is grey-brown and becomes ridged as it matures. May grow up to 30 metres in height and 9m metres in width

alternative_names: white fir|Colorado fir|western white fir|Abies concolor var. concolor
description: Large, evergreen coniferous tree to 40m tall, with smooth grey bark, grooved and scaly on old trees, a conical crown and long slender blue- or grey-green needles. Cones are purple when young, turning to brown as they mature. Makes a nice specimen tree for a large space

Large, upright-growing conical, evergreen coniferous tree, reaching up to 25m when mature. Young branches are reddish and glabrous, darkening in 2nd - 3rd year. New buds are resinous, small and globular. Leaves are densely set in several overlapping ranks, covering shoots in radial way. Needles are glossy, dark-green above, with two stomatal lines underneath. Up to 3cm long and 2.5mm wide, they are often curved or ''S''-shaped, flattened at the end. Ovoid seed cones, up to 8 cm long and 4 cm wide, are dark indigo-blue when young, maturing to black.

alternative_names: Sikkim fir|Abies spectabilis var. densa|Abies spectabilis misapplied
Faber's fir|Abies delavayi var. delavayi Fabri Group|Abies delavayi var. fabri

description: A columnar, evergreen conifer tree with finely flaky, pale-brown bark. Year-old shoots are dark purple, with purple conical buds. Dark green needles are 2.5cm long and spread below and point forwards above each shoot. Seed cones up to 9cm long and 4cm wide are bluish purple when young, maturing to purplish-brown with protruding bracts.

An evergreen conifer to 40-50m tall, with stiff, tough needles that are light green above and whitish green under neath. Needles of young trees are forked with sharp tips, becoming notched or blunt when older. The cylindrical cones are yellowish green, with yellow bracts and mature to yellowish brown. Cones appear in late spring and are 10-15cm tall and 3-5cm wide

alternative_names: Forrest fir|Abies georgii|Abies delavayi var. forrestii|Abies delavayi var. forestii
description: A large conical evergreen tree with an open habit when young. Bark is smooth, silvery-grey, new shoots are red-brown with white resinous buds. Short needles are densely arranged around each shoot in multiple ranks. The needles are up to 3cm long and 2.5mm wide, dark green above, silvery white beneath. Ovoid-cylindrical seed cones are 8-15cm long, blue when young, with protruding bracts.

alternative_names: Fraser fir|Fraser's balsam fir|southern balsam fir|Pinus fraseri
description: A medium-sized tree, to 15m tall, forming a narrow, conical crown. Flattened, short leaves 1-2cm long are a shining dark green above with two white bands below and are densely borne on resinous stems. Cylindrical cones, 3.5-7cm long, are dark purple when young maturing to brown with conspicuously-protruding bracts that bend downwards hiding the scales

A fast-growing, tall conifer with a narrow conical habit. The flattened, needle-like leaves are dark green above with two silvery-grey bands below. Cones up to10cm long are bright green when young before ripening to a reddish-brown

alternative_names: Formosan fir|Taiwan fir|Abies mariesii var. kawakamii
description: Upright-growing, evergreen coniferous tree, reaching a height of 15m when mature and grown in optimal conditions. Bark on young trees is grey, later grayish-brown with scales. Needles are 10-15mm short, linear, rounded at the tip, dark green with white lines around the tip and on the below side, densely arranged around branchlets. New vegetative buds are very resinous, egg-shaped, approx. 5mm long. Pollen cones are yellowish, up to 1cm long. Seed cones are dark blue when young, up to 9cm long and 4cm wide, maturing through bluish-purple to purplish-brown.
Compact evergreen conical tree to 10m tall, with dark green needle-like leaves white beneath, and handsome, cylindrical blue or purple cones, some with protruding bracts, often borne on young trees

Tall, evergreen conifer tree with narrowly conical crown. In optimal conditions this species reaches up to 20m. Bark on young trees is smooth and grey. Needle-like leaves are flat, dark green on the top, with two silvery-white lines below. Needles up to 3cm long are spirally arranged on the shoots, twisted at the base. Seed cones are up to 12cm long, dark purple, almost black when young with fine yellow-brown hairy seed scales. Mature seed cones are brown.

Very tall, evergreen, conifer tree, reaching height up to 25-35m in optimal conditions. Crown on young trees is narrowly conical, becoming more open, barrel-shaped on older trees. The common name of this Fir refers to the reddish-brown bark of mature specimens. Needle-like leaves are up to 3.5cm long, blue-green in colour, glossy above, with two pale, grey lines underneath. Needles are spirally arranged along the shoots, slightly twisted, bending upwards. Barrel-shaped, golden-green seed cones are 18 - 25 cm long, with concealed bracts.

A large conifer tree with a narrowly columnar crown, broadening with age. This variety of Californian Red Fir is similar to the species. The difference is the smaller-sized seed cones that are 7-10cm long and approximately 2-3cm in diameter, and the bract scales are protruding.

alternative_names: Manchurian fir|Khingan fir|Abies sibirica var. nephrolepis

description: An evergreen conifer making a large tree to 30m or more, with narrow conical or columnar crown, with dense, glossy dark green foliage on down-swept branches. Young cones green or reddish, becoming brown

A large, evergreen conifer reaching a height of 15-20m with thick, stiff, deep green needles, radially arranged, 15-20mm long and whitish underneath. The seed-cones are barrel-shaped, 15-20cm tall x 4-6cm wide, light green with a purplish tinge in late spring, maturing light purplish brown

alternative_names: Abies spectabilis var. intermedia|Abies pindrow var. intermedia

description: An upright, evergreen conifer to 20m, with stiff, sharp-tipped grey-green needles, 8-15mm long and 2-3mm wide, which radiate along the stem. The conical cones are 10-15cm x 4-5cm, greenish purple in late spring and maturing to dark or light brown
An evergreen conifer making a slow-growing medium tree with blunt grey-green needles arranged all round the shoot. Cones pale green or purple when young, ripening brown
A vigorous evergreen conifer forming a large tree with broadly conical crown and upcurved blue-green needles. Cones large, deep purple-brown when young
A beautiful blue-grey conifer which grows as spreading ground cover

A large, evergreen, coniferous tree with a pyramidal crown that can grow over 20m tall. Dense needle-like foliage is pale-green when young, later maturing to dark green. Stiff, sharp-pointed needles are 1.5-2cm long, tips are bent upwards. Glossy green above, with two stomatal lines on reverse. Young shoots are pale-grey. Small purple seed cones develop on adult trees in spring, later maturing to purple-brown.

alternative_names: Sakhalin fir|Sachalin fir|Abies veitchii var. sachalinensis
description: An evergreen coniferous tree, with a broadly pyramidal crown, growing up to 30 metres high in optimal conditions. The needle-like foliage is dark green, with 2 narrow greenish-white stomatal lines on the underside. Needles are narrow and soft in texture, 1.2 - 3.5cm long and 1mm wide. Young seed cones (5-8cm long) are purple-brown, maturing to dark brown.
plant_range: Russian Far East to N Japan

description: An evergreen, coniferous tree up to 30 - 35 metre high, with conical crown. Needles are soft to touch, bright green with two pale stripes on the underside, 2-3cm long and 1.5mm wide. Young shoots are yellow-grey and resinous. Seed cones are cylindrical, 5-9cm long and 2.5-3.5cm in diameter. Surviving temperatures down to -50°C, this is one of the most hardy trees.
plant_range: E Europe to Russian Far East, NW China

alternative_names: Himayan fir|east Himalayan fir|king pine|Abies webbiana|Abies spectabilis var. spectabilis|Abies spectabilis var. brevifolia

description: An evergreen, coniferous tree growing up to 40m height when grown in optimal conditions. This species is characteristic for its flaky, papery bark, very similar to a birch tree. The reddish-brown bark develops on trees from around 6th year of growth. Shoots are densely covered with thin hairs. New vegetative buds are red-brown and resinous. 1.5-2.5 long needles are densely arranged, attractive blue-green, with two pale stomatal lines on the underside. Seed cones are dark blue when young, contrasting with pale foliage in spring.
A small evergreen tree to 4m, though occasionally trailing/prostrate. The 'leaves' are small silver-green triangles and the flowers bright yellow clusters of little pom-poms in spring

alternative_names: lignum vitae of New South Wales

description: A graceful evergreen tree possibly reaching 12m. Its 'leaves' are leathery grey-green and variable in shape. Some are ferny in shape with a slender stem, some have a saml leaf where the stem is flattened, but generally they are just the leaf stem alone, flattend into a 'leaf' longer than they are wide with a slight curve. In spring, the flowers are clouds of small, fluffy white to pale yellow flowers which may develop into 10cm brown, twisted-ribbon seed pods. The bark is grey with dark fissures
An evergreen shrub to 5m or more, with crowded, triangular leaf-like phyllodes and racemes of small rich yellow flower-heads in late winter and early spring

A wide-spreading, evergreen shrub with a dense habit. The young shoots are distinctly, angularly ridged and downy, with branches covered in spiky dark green phyllodes (leaves) that are almost hidden by the abundance of flowers. Masses of soft yellow pincushion-like flowers with a honey and almond scent appear in spring, loved by all pollinators. Suitable for most soil conditions including periods of water logging. Makes an excellent habitat for birds

primary_name: Acaena anserinifolia (J.R. Forst. & G.Forst.) J.B. Armstr. [1]

alternative_names: red-hot cat's tail|chenille plant|Acalypha sanderi|Acalypha sanderiana
description: An erect evergreen shrub of open habit, to 2.5m in height, with large ovate leaves and pendulous fluffy red catkin-like flowerheads to 45cm in length, produced sporadically throuhout the year
A compact, mat-forming perennial with narrow, dark green leaves and short spikes of deep pink flowers held just above the foliage

description: A perennial to 1.5m tall with mounds of deeply cut leaves up to 1m long and 20cm wide. Spikes of white to pink flowers are borne in summer under green or purplish hoods

description: A vigorous plant with large, glossy dark green leaves, pinnately lobed and, in late summer, tall racemes of white flowers with dusky purple bracts

alternative_names: spiny bear's breech|armed bear's breech|spiny bear's breeches|Acanthus caroli-alexandri
description: A handsome herbaceous perennial to 1.2m, with large, deeply lobed and spine-tipped, dark glossy green leaves. Erect spikes of white flowers with spiny purplish bracts in late spring and summer

alternative_names: trident maple|three-toothed maple|Acer trifidum|Acer buergerianum var. trinerve
description: A small, bushy tree with 3 lobed leaves, with the central lobe being the longest and giving rise to the common name of trident maple. The yellow green small flowers, appear before the leaves in early spring. The leaves are bronze in spring, later becoming deep green with a grey underside in summer and then turn red and orange in autumn. Mature trees develop an attractive red-brown flaking bark.

alternative_names: field maple|common elder|common maple|dog oak|hedge maple|masarnwydd lleiaf|maser tree|master tree|Acer campestre var. austriacum
description: A medium-sized deciduous tree with a compact bushy crown. Leaves with 5 blunt lobes, turning yellow or red in the autumn. Flowers small, green, forming typical winged maple fruits

A snakebark maple making a small deciduous tree with white-striped young branches and 3-lobed leaves to 12cm in length, red and yellow in autumn. Flowers green, in drooping racemes; attractive pink fruits

A medium to large deciduous tree to 20m tall with a rounded, spreading crown. The five to seven-lobed, pointed,glossy green leaves turn a rich yellow in autumn; the leaf stalks exude a milky sap when broken. Clusters of small yellow-green flowers in early spring are followed by winged seeds

This bushy, spreading tree with upright branches has distinctive drooping, oval leaves, with prominent veins, toothed edges and tapering at the tip resembling those of the common hornbean. The leaves are neater and opposite and turn gold and brown in the autumn.

alternative_names: Kawakami maple|snake-bark maple|Acer morrisonense Hayata|Acer ovatifolium|Acer kawakamii
description: A small to medium-sized, densely-branched tree reaching up to 12m in cultivation with smooth green to reddish-green bark marked with faint white stripes. Dull green leaves, paler on the undersides with serrated margins, are usually unlobed but may have three shallow lobes; leaves are up to 11cm long by 4.5cm wide, tapering to a point and turn shades of red, orange and yellow in autumn. Racemes of small purple to white flowers in spring are followed by reddish winged fruits in autumn that turn yellow as they mature
A spreading bushy small tree or large shrub with rounded, 7 to 9-lobed leaves turning red or orange in autumn. Clusters of small purplish flowers are followed by red-winged fruits
plant_range: N America, British Columbia to California

description: A small, spreading, rounded tree to 8m tall and 12m wide. Leaves comprise three oval, coarsely-toothed leaflets and are bronze-tinged when young, maturing to a dark green and turning shades of red and yellow in autumn. Tiny yellow flowers are borne in racemes, to 10cm long, in spring

A spreading, deciduous tree about 10m tall, with green and white streaked bark, and small variable, 3-lobed dark green leaves with toothed margins, turn orange in autumn. Small, pale yellow flowers in upright racemes are produced in spring

alternative_names: Père David's maple|snake-bark maple|Acer laxiflorum var. ningpoense
description: A deciduous tree with arching branches and green- and white-streaked bark. Leaves can be ovate, unlobed or shallowly lobed, and are mid-green to 15cm in length. In autumn, leaves turn orange to yellow, when pink-brown fruit are also borne

A deciduous tree to around 12m high or more, with large, broadly oval green leaves that are heart-shaped at the base and serrated at the edges. Small spikes of yellow-green flowers are produced in spring, followed by winged fruits. Leaves turn rich amber yellow in autumn

alternative_names: Forrest's maple|snake-bark maple|Acer pectinatum subsp. forrestii
description: A spreading tree up to 10m tall with arching branches, red when young, then green with white stripes. The broad, three-lobed leaves open tinged with red, turn dark green in summer and orange-red in autumn. Hanging clusters of small, red and green flowers appear in spring followed by green and pink, two-winged fruit

alternative_names: paperbark maple|Acer nikoense var. griseum Franch.
description: A small spreading deciduous tree with attractive peeling, papery chestnut-brown bark. Leaves with 3 leaflets, downy and whitish beneath, turning brilliant red and orange in autumn. Flowers small

A small, spreading tree, to 10m tall, with white and grey-green striped bark. Triangular, shallowly-lobed, mid-green leaves, to 7cm long, turn orange or yellow in autumn. Small yellow-green flowers are held in pendent racemes during spring

Deciduous tree about 10-15m in height with grey to pale brown bark, and distinctive, deeply divided 3-lobed dark green leaves 15cm long and wide, yellow to brown in autumn. Yellow spring flowers are produced in clusters and these are followed by large yellow-brown winged fruits in autumn

alternative_names: Balkan maple|Acer italicum var. hyrcanum|Acer opalus var. hyrcanum
plant_range: Balkan Peninsula to Lebanon and N Iran

alternative_names: snake bark maple|Acer pectinatum subsp. laxiflorum
description: A rounded, spreading deciduous tree, rare in cultivation, about 8-10m tall, with green and white streaked bark and leathery dark green leaves on red leaf stalks, turn orange in autumn. Bears brownish-green flowers in slender racemes in spring

A large, round-headed tree with deeply-lobed, dark green leaves up to 30cm across that turn shades of orange and yellow in autumn. Small, fragrant, yellowish-green flowers are borne in drooping clusters 10-20cm long in spring and followed by bristly, winged fruit
Forms a large shrub or small tree with arching branches and reddish young shoots and greenish-white flowers. Toothed foliage turns orange, yellow and red in autumn

A deciduous tree, up to 25m high, with green leaves to 15cm across, deeply cut into five bluntly toothed lobes, and held on long stalks that exude a milky sap when broken. Loose spikes of small yellow-green flowers are produced in spring, followed by winged fruits. Leaves turn yellow in autumn
A bushy, rounded small tree, to 8m in height, with leathery, glossy, dark-green leaves. Profuse yellow-green flowers in pendent racemes in spring are followed by red-winged fruit in summer
A vigorous deciduous tree with pinnate leaves on green young shoots, male and female flowers on separate plants; yellow autumn colour
A deciduous shrub or small tree with 5- to 7-lobed leaves, deep purple in spring and summer, becoming crimson in autumn

A deciduous tree, up to around 20m high, with large, shallowly lobed green leaves to 25cm across, with each lobe pointed at the tip. Leaves are textured, with deeply impressed veins, and covered with rust-coloured hairs on the undersides when young. Dense tassels of small yellow-green flowers are produced in spring, followed by winged fruits. Leaves turn yellow in autumn

A deciduous tree, to 25m or more in its native range, though often smaller in cultivation. Leaves are broad, shallowly 5-lobed, slightly glossy green, and often downy on the undersides. Clusters of small yellow flowers appear before the leaves in early spring, followed by winged seeds that are sometimes tinted silvery pink. Leaves turn yellow and rusty orange in autumn

alternative_names: Japanese maple|smooth Japanese maple|Acer jucundum|Acer palmatum subsp. palmatum|Acer palmatum f. polymorphum|Acer polymorphum|Acer palmatum unidentified cultivar
description: A variable small tree with small, deeply 5 to 7-lobed leaves often colouring well in autumn. Small red flowers in spring are followed by winged, red or green fruits

A small, deciduous spreading tree about 3-4m tall, selected for its autumn colour at The Garden House, Yelverton, Devon. Palmate, 7-lobed bronze-green leaves in summer turn light, bright, fiery red in autumn
A slow-growing shrub of broadly arching habit, with deep purple, lobed and finely toothed leaves turning orange in autumn

Vigorous, deciduous shrubby tree about 4m tall with a cascading habit. Leaves with deeply dissected 7 lobes, are rich brownish-red throughout summer, slightly brighter in autumn. Small purplish spring flowers are followed by red fruits in summer

A shrubby, deciduous, very ornamental tree about 10-15m in height, with green streaked bark, the young wood red-purple, and 3 to 5-lobed matt green leaves, paler beneath, red when young, turning yellow to orange in autumn with red petioles to 7cm long; purplish late spring flowers are followed by winged fruits in mid autumn

alternative_names: moosewood|goose foot|snake-bark maple|striped dogwood|striped maple|Acer striatum
description: A snakebark maple forming a medium-sized deciduous tree of upright growth, with white-striped green young branches. Leaves large, 3-lobed, turning yellow in autumn. Flowers yellow in drooping racemes
A vigorous deciduous large tree. Leaves 5-lobed, turning bright yellow, orange or brown in autumn. Scented yellow flowers in conspicuous clusters on bare branches

A large, dense tree with a columnar habit reaching up to 20m tall and 8m wide. Shallow-lobed leaves turn yellow in the autumn; clusters of small yellowish-green flowers borne on bare stems in the spring are followed by winged fruit

A medium-sized, deciduous tree to around 15m tall with a dense, rounded crown. Its deeply-lobed, variegated leaves have a green centre and broad, creamy-white margins; the leaves turn yellow in autumn. Clusters of yellow flowers open on the bare stems in spring before the leaves appear

A medium-sized, spreading deciduous tree to 15m tall. Irregularly-lobed leaves open creamy-yellow in spring before turning green with dense white speckles giving the foliage a greyish appearance when viewed from a distance.Small yellowish-green spring flowers are followed by winged fruit
A large, fast-growing, resilient, deciduous tree with dark green, five-lobed leaves 10-20cm long. Yellow-green, catkin-like flowers in spring are followed by bunches of green, winged fruit
plant_range: NW to C Europe, Italy, W Asia

alternative_names: Japanese red maple|hananoki|Acer rubrum var. pycnanthum
description: A deciduous tree to around 20m tall forming a rounded crown when mature. Shallowly-lobed leaves emerge bronze-green in the spring and turn shades of orange, yellow, red and purple in the autumn; the undersides of the leaves have a whitish bloom. Small clusters of red flowers are borne on the bare branches in spring and followed by reddish winged fruits in the summer

A round-headed tree growing up to 30m tall. In spring, tiny red flowers are borne in erect clusters before the appearance of dark green leaves with whitish undersides. The leaves turn bright red in autumn

alternative_names: grey snake-bark maple|snake-bark maple|Acer tegmentosum subsp. glaucorufinerve
description: A snakebark maple making a medium-sized deciduous tree with glaucous young shoots and white-striped branches. Leaves broadly oval, 3-lobed, yellow and red in autumn. Flowers yellow, in erect racemes

alternative_names: silver maple|soft maple|sugar maple|white maple|Acer eriocarpum|Acer dasycarpum
description: A very vigorous deciduous tree with deeply palmately-lobed leaves, white beneath, turning red and yellow in autumn; small yellow-green flowers before the leaves

alternative_names: sugar maple|rock maple|striped maple|Acer saccharophorum|Acer palmifolium
description: A large, deciduous tree to 20m with a dense, oval to rounded crown and large, dull-green, three- to five-lobed leaves that turn brilliant orange, red and yellow in autumn. The flowers are greenish-yellow in short, upright sprays in spring
plant_range: Alaska, Canada to SE United States

alternative_names: Cretan maple|evergreen maple|Acer heterophyllum|Acer creticum misapplied|Acer orientale misapplied
description: A slow growing, semi-evergreen, large shrub or small tree, about 7-10m tall, with bright green leaves, paler beneath, variously shaped from rounded entire to 3-lobed, often retained on the tree until late December with occasional autumn tints of yellow to brown. Greenish-yellow flowers with the new leaves in spring are followed by brownish-red winged fruits

A deciduous, large shrub or small tree about 6m tall, with rounded, mid-green, 7-11 lobed, finely toothed leaves to 9cm long, turning yellow-orange or red in autumn. Clusters of tiny yellow flowers in spring are followed by brownish winged fruits

A semi-evergreen maple, rare in cultivation suited to the mildest parts of the country. Ultimately to 12m tall, with red young shoots and usually entire, thick-textured leaves to 15cm long, emerging brilliant red in spring, maturing to glossy dark green, then crimson in autumn; clusters of small greenish-yellow spring flowers are followed by pendent racemes of small brown winged fruit

A small, deciduous shrubby tree to about 6-8m tall, with a short trunk and downy shoots. Long, pointed 3-5 lobed mid-green leaves turn brilliant red and yellow in autumn. Dense greenish-yellow flowers in slender upright panicles in early summer are followed by slender racemes of red winged fruits

A deciduous large shrub or small tree, to around 6m high, with a spreading habit and broadly ovate, serrated, glossy green leaves, that are sometimes 3-lobed on young trees. Small greenish-white flowers are held in upright clusters in late spring, followed later by red-winged seeds. Leaves turn red or yellow in autumn
A medium-sized tree that has attractive green bark streaked with white and bright green foliage which turns yellow in autumn

alternative_names: red bud maple|Acer heldreichii subsp. trautvetteri
description: An upright deciduous tree with dark green leaves that are deeply lobed and colour well in autumn. In spring yellow flowers are borne followed by fruit with wings that turn red when ripe
A bushy tree with leaves divided into 3 narrow, toothed leaflets, greyish beneath. Small clusters of yellow-green flowers in spring, and orange autumn colour

A deciduous tree, to around 8m high, with a rounded habit and glossy green leaves divided into five sharply pointed lobes. Small greenish-yellow flowers are borne in upright clusters in spring, followed later by winged seeds. Leaves turn red or yellow in autumn

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 50cm tall with deeply-divided, greyish-green, densely-felted leaves. Flat-topped flowerheads to 7cm across made up of tiny, golden-yellow flowers are borne on upright stems from late spring into summer

description: An erect perennial to 60cm tall with narrowly lance-shaped, finely-toothed, dark green leaves to 6cm long. Loose clusters of white flowerheads are borne in summer
A mat forming perennial with linear, finely divided, woolly, grey-green leaves. Dense clusters of bright yellow flowers appear in early Summer to Autumn

Upright, clump-forming, fibrous-rooted perennial to about 75cm tall, with plentiful, deeply lobed, dark green leaves. Spires of creamy-white, hooded, almost cylindrical flowers appear in early to mid summer

Fronds are slightly leathery and hairy, and faintly aromatic when crushed. Fertile fronds bear 'sori' (structures which produce or contain spores) all along the underside margins, protected by inrolled leaf edges

alternative_names: Christ's thorn|garland thorn|Jerusalem thorn|ram of Libya|Paliurus aculeatus|Rhamnus paliurus|Paliurus australis
description: A bushy shrub with slender, viciously thorny stems and rounded, glossy, bright green leaves. Clusters of small, greenish-yellow, star-shaped flowers in summer are followed by small, woody fruit, each surrounded by a large, disc-shaped wing, pale green at first, then brown, and lasting into winter
A tender, evergreen, palm-like tree to 6m, bearing glossy, sword-shaped leaves with stiff red spines along the margins. The foliage is arranged in a spiralling formation at the branch tips

A vigorous, twining, evergreen climber with compound leaves made up of six pairs of mid-green leaflets. The fragrant, tubular, creamflowers have variable reddish-purple markings, and areborne in clusters in winter and spring

A clump-forming, short-lived perennial, growing to 50cm tall, with rosettes of grey-green, hairy, elliptical, toothed leaves to 15cm long. Saucer-shaped, dull orange flowers, up to 6cm across, are borne on upright, hairy stems from late spring into autumn

A perennial poppy, to 90cm high, with bristly stems and finely divided, dark green leaves covered with silvery hairs. In early to mid summer, produces pendent buds that straighten and open to large, bowl-shaped, orange-red flowers to 15cm across, with small purple-black blotches at the base of the petals

A clump-forming perennial with lobed leaves up to 15cm long. In summer it produces solitary, bowl-shaped, light orange, single to semi-double flowers up to 8cm across. May self-seed and can be short-lived

A small-sized, semi-terrestrial evergreen orchid with rosettes of elliptic, mottled, mid-green and purple leaves. Each leaf is up to 20cm long and 3-4cm wide. Solitary flowers appear in winter and spring on upright stems up to 50cm tall, emerging from the centre of leaf rosettes. Long-lasting, glossy flowers are up to 12cm across, with slender, green and rose-pink petals darker, veined upper sepal and light brown pouch.

A small-sized, semi-terrestrial orchid with oblong, lance-shaped leaves up to 20cm long and 4cm wide. Leaves are pale green with darker mottling. In spring, upright terminal flowering stems up to 35cm tall appear from the centre of the leaf rosettes carrying a single, 10cm large flower. Petals are white, brown or pink at the tips, with thin, light-green lines and dark brown spots. The upper sepal is white with green lines, the pouch is bronze-red with dark green veins.

A medium-sized, semi-terrestrial, clump-forming orchid, with narrowly elliptic leaves. The leaves are dark, mottled with pale green, up to 15cm long and 3-5cm wide. Solitary flowers, 8-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 25cm long, upright stems. Flowers are waxy, lasting several week. The pouch (modification of the lip) is dark purplish-brown. Dorsal sepal is white with green and dark purple stripes. Two petals are narrow, with dark stripes and few protruding dark spots.

A medium-sized, epiphitic or semi-terrestrial evergreen orchid, with strap-shaped, green, glossy leaves. The leaves are up to 25cm long and 3cm wide. The flowering stems emerge from the centre of the leaf rosettes in summer and autumn and carry single, 8cm large flower. The flowers are long-lasting, with lime-green, brown-veined pouch and petals, and white, pink-patterned dorsal sepal.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with four to six, oval or elliptic leaves. Firm leaves are dark green, tesselated with pale green and spotted purple on the underside. Each leaf is 10-15cm long and 3-4cm wide. Flowers, approximately 7cm across are carried on upright, up to 10cm long stems, emerging from centres of leaf rosettes in spring and summer. Each stem carries usually one, occasionally two to three flowers. Petals and sepals are rounded, pale yellow, heavily spotted with maroon or purple.

An evergreen, tropical orchid, producing a clump of leaf rosettes with green, leathery leaves up to 40cm long and 5cm wide. Upright flowering stems appear from the centre of young leaf rosettes. They can be up to 40cm tall and bear three to seven, 10cm-large flowers. Each flower is glossy, with pink pouch and yellow-green, or pale pink petals. The upper sepal is white with dark green veins.

A small to medium-sized, evergreen orchid with linear, solid green leaves up to 30cm long and 2-4cm wide. Solitary flowers up to 8cm across are carried on upright, 25cm long stems, emerging from the centre of the leaf rosette in autumn and early winter. Petals and pouch are glossy, heavily veined with brown. White upper sepal carries dark brown or dark pink spotted pattern.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with narrow, lanceolate, pale-green leaves, 20 -30cm long. Solitary flowers, 7-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 15-30cm long erect stems. The pouch (or slipper) is a modification of lip that traps insects, and consequently provides with an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. The lateral sepals are largely fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. Petals are yellow-bronze, the upper sepal is yellow with red-brow spots and white upper margin.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with narrowly elliptic green fleshy leaves. Flowering stems that measure up to 1m in length, appear from the centre of the leaf rosettes and cary up to 5 flowers. Each flower measures apporximately 8 - 14cm. Pouch is brown, veined; petals are bright yellow-green with purple tips and dark brown spots. Upper sepal is yellow-green, brown-striped.

A small-sized, semi-terrestrial, evergreen orchid. Three to five, oval-elliptic leaves are leathery, dull, dark green mottled with pale green, with purple spots below. The leaves are up to 14cm long and 2-3cm wide. Solitary flowers up to 10cm across are large compared to the size of plants. Terminal flowering stems up to 25cm long emerge from the centre of the leaf rosettes in spring and summer. Characteristic, inflated lip is round, larger than petals and sepals, usually white or pale pink. Petals and upper sepals are pale green and pink with darker tesselated pattern.

A medium-sized, clump-forming orchid species. Linear, glossy leaves are bright green, up to 45cm long and 4-7cm wide. Light green flowering stems emerge from the centre of the leaf rosette. Measuring up to 60cm, the stem carries 3-12 large, glossy flowers, each 9-11cm wide. The pouch (a modification of lip) is bright green with darker, brownish veins. Long, thin petals are characteristically curled, dark brown or purple-brown. Dorsal sepal is pale yellow with green stripes.

A large-sized, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with linear, green, glossy leaves up to 50cm long and 5cm wide. Three to five flowers are carried on 60cm long flowering stems that emerge from the centre of the leaf rosette. Each flower measures up to 9cm across. Typical for this species are very long, dangling petals, that twist spirally along their length and can measure up to 20cm. The pouch (modification of the lip) is yellow or brown, often with darker veins.

A medium to large-sized, clump-forming, evergreen tropical orchid. Linear, glossy, bright green leaves are up to 60cm long and 5cm wide. Flowering stem up to 75cm long appears from the centre of the leaf rosette and carries 2 to 4 large, glossy flowers. The pouch is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. Lateral sepals are fused, pale cream with brown stripes, almost identical with upper, dorsal sepal. The petals are thin, very long and almost horizontal, pale green or yellow with brown stripes and small spots with tiny brown hairs.

A medium-sized, clump-forming, evergreen, tropical orchid. Bright green leaves are linear, glossy, up to 45cm long and 5cm wide. Flowering stems up to 60cm long emerge from the centre of the leaf rosette and carry 2-5 simultaneously opening flowers. The flowers are characteristic for exceptionally long, thin curled petals that measure be 60cm or more. The pouch is yellowish-green with brown or purple veins. Dorsal sepal is pale green with purple margin and 10 purple-brown stripes.

A small-sized, evergreen orchid species with narrow, elliptic leaves, with tesselated dark and pale green pattern. Solitary flowers, 10-14cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 13cm long, upright stems. The pouch (or slipper) is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. The lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. Petals are lime-green with numerous brown spots. The upper sepal is white, with lime-green stripes.

A small, semi-terrestrial, clump-forming orchid, with mottled dark and light green leaves, up to 25cm long and 4-7cm wide. Solitary flowers, 7-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosettes and are carried on 15 -30cm long, dark purple, upright stems. The pouch is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. The pouch is purple brown, petals are narrow with brown-purple spotting. Dorsal sepal is white with green and purple stripes.

A small-sized, terrestrial, clump-forming orchid with evergreen, narrowly-elliptic, mottled leaves up to 20cm long and 4cm wide. Solitary flowers, up to 10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 25cm long, upright stems, densely covered in thin short hairs. The pouch (or slipper) is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. Lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. Petals are white, lined with green, pink at the lower ends and with few dark, raised spots along the green lines. Dorsal sepal is white with bright green stripes.

A medium-sized, clump-forming, terrestrial orchid with strap-shaped, dull mid-green leaves, 25-40cm long and 3-4cm wide. Solitary, glossy, red-brown flowers, 8cm across, with green and brown upper sepals and light yellow-bronze to green pouches, appear from winter to spring on upright, 30cm tall, terminal stems.

description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 60cm in height, with greyish-green grassy leaves and erect stems bearing racemes of lily-like pure white flowers 4-6cm in length in early summer

A tender, deciduous herbaceous perennial for deep shade. Leaves in whorled groups of five to nine appear in spring, followed by flowers made up of leafy-looking green sections, topped by fine thin yellow wisps. Clusters of red berries follow.

A wide-spreading, often multi-stemmed deciduous tree or large shrub to 8m, with attractive flaking bark. Leaves turn yellow, red and purple in autumn. Small crimson flowers on bare twigs

A large deciduous shrub or small tree, to around 6m high and with an upright habit. Tiny flowers with bright yellow stamens surrounded by large white bracts are produced on bare branches in spring, and sometimes intermittently in summer. Bowl-shaped flowers to 8cm in width, are white, with blue and purple coronal filaments, flowering from summer to autumn, then followed by ovoid orange fruits 4cm long. Fruits are edible but not particularly tasty

A clump-forming perennial up to 50cm tall, with palmately lobed, mid-green leaves turning yellow in autumn. Branching stems support flower heads 10cm across consisting of small, trumpet-shaped, scented, yellow flowers with five petal lobes

An upright, evergreen perennial, up to 60cm tall, with succulent stems bearing fleshy, grey-green leaves. From spring to summer bears sparse clusters of star-shaped, salmon-pink flowers with long, narrow petals
A bushy sub-shrub, to 60cm in height, with softly-hairy, rose-scented, lobed leaves and clusters of pink, white or pale purple flowers, 2-3cm across, in summer

A bushy, somewhat spreading plant, to 50cm in height, with small, deeply-lobed, softly-hairy, celery-scented leaves. The flowers have red stems and narrow, rose-pink petals, and appear from mid-spring to mid-autumn

A tender perennial, vigorous species pelargonium with large, heart-shaped, scented green leaves and delicate-looking pink to pale pink single flowers with darker pink blotches and three linear lower petals from spring to early autumn.

A slow growing, tender subshrub, with a sprawling, branching habit and distinctive square, jointed, succulent stems. Plants have few leaves, these are small, fleshy and lobed, and sometimes have dark red zonal markings. Flowers are produced in pairs, and are pale pink or cream, with two large upper petals veined with dark red, and small or absent lower petals

A deciduous, low-growing, free-flowering, shrubby perennial to around 40cm in height, with pale green stems and pale green, softly hairy, lobed leaves. Bright, scarlet-red flowers appear from April through to September

A tuberous perennial with finely divided, trailing green leaves covered with fine silvery hairs. Clusters of small, night-scented flowers, with pale yellow or pale pink petals with dark red markings, are held on tall stems in late spring and early summer

One parent of most zonal pelargoniums, P. zonale is an erect, bushy plant with fleshy stems turning woody with age and smooth, rounded, mid-green leaves with a narrow, dark green zone. Generally grows up to 1m but up to 3m against a wall under glass. Clusters of narrow-petalled, pink, white or purple flowers can be produced virtually all year in warm, bright conditions, otherwise in summer and early autumn
An evergreen, tufted fern with erect, dark green, glossy fronds up to 75cm long. Fronds are divided into short, oblong to curved leaflets with margins that are sometimes wavy

alternative_names: button fern|New Zealand cliff brake|round-leaved fern|tarawera
description: A compact, evergreen fern forming a nearly flat rosette of pinnate fronds to 25cm long, composed of rounded, deep green leaflets borne on dark brown, pink-scaled stems. An ideal plant for terrariums and bottle gardens

A clump-forming perennial to around 50cm high, with deeply lobed, glossy green leaves, held on long stalks attached to the undersides near the centre of the leaf. Leaves are often tinted pink when young. Clusters of small, nodding, pale yellow flowers, with petals fringed at the tips, are held above the foliage in summer

A compact, bushy, semi-evergreen, drought-tolerant perennial with dark green, strap-shaped foliage. Upright spikes of long-lasting, tubular, rose-red flowers with white throats appear from June to October
Penstemon alpinus is a semi-evergreen perennial or sub-shrub up to 80cm tall with lance-shaped leaves. In early summer, blue to bluish-purple flowers, 2-3cm long, are borne on one side of stems

description: An upright, clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to 60cm, with wiry stems and dark green, toothed, lance-shaped leaves. Loose sprays of bell-shaped flowers up to 3cm long appear in early summer and are usually mid- to light purple with varying amounts of white, though red forms also occur

A rarely offered but easy to grow compact perennial with lance-shaped green foliage and dense spikes of small, flared, tubular lemon-yellow flowers which appear from April to June. Prefers a moist area by streams, in meadows or a woodland setting, although it will perform in a drier spot in cool conditions

Vigorous semi-evergreen perennial to 1m tall, with basal mid-green leaves to 15cm long and purple flushed stems. Panicles or tiers of tubular pale lavender or white flowers each 2.5cm long are produced during summer

A low-growing, semi-evergreen perennial forming basal rosettes of greyish-green leaves from which arise erect stems to 35cm tall bearing whorls of narrowly funnel-shaped blue to purple flowers from late spring into summer

An upright woody-based perennial to 70cm in height, with narrow evergreen leaves and one-sided panicles of slender, tubular, bright reddish-pink flowers 3-4cm in length, streaked with crimson in the paler throat
A dwarf evergreen subshrub to 25cm in height, with small, leathery ovate leaves. Tubular, deep rose-pink flowers 4cm in length are borne in clusters in early summer
A spreading evergreen dwarf shrub to 20cm tall, with short, needle-like leaves and tubular scarlet flowers 2.5cm long in short erect racemes in summer
A creeping dwarf evergreen sub-shrub to 6cm in height, with small, rounded glaucous leaves and tubular, two-lipped rosy-pink flowers 3cm in length opening from late spring

Evergreen perennial to 75cm tall, forming large clumps of rich green, lance-shaped, slender leaves and producing upright spikes of royal blue to purple tubular flowers, over a long period from early summer

A coarse, bristly, tap-rooted perennial with a basal rosette of pointed, oval leaves up to 40cm long. Upright stems carrying smaller leaves, are topped with sprays of bright blue, forget-me-not flowers in spring and early summer

description: An evergreen mound-forming perennial to 20cm tall, with thick, puckered, heart-shaped, dark green leaves to 5cm across; these are held on long, succulent stalks. From spring to autumn it produces upright, tail-like or club-shaped spikes of tiny greenish-white flowers. An ideal plant for terrariums and bottle gardens

A species of semi-upright to spreading fleshy, often variegated evergreen perennial succulent with thick, heart-shaped, felted green leaves and red stems. Green flowers with purple anthers may appear in the spring
A compact evergreen perennial to 20cm tall, with thick, glossy, droplet-shaped, dark green leaves. Makes a good houseplant for a bright spot

A compact, trailing, evergreen perennial with red stems bearing circular leaves to 1.5cm across. The leaves are dark green with lighter markings along the veins. From spring to summer it produces upright, slender, tail-like spikes of tiny brown flowers
A trailing evergreen perennial with heart-shaped, pale green leaves to 7cm long. From spring to autumn it produces tiny green flowers on erect, tail-like spikes

An evergreen subshrub to 120cm in height, with elliptic green leaves to 8cm long, and greyish stems. The flowers are magenta, in clusters of 2-3 in the axils of leafy bracts on a branched panicle. They are tubular, to 5cm long, strongly 2-lipped, borne mostly in winter

A clump-forming evergreen grass, with arching, lance-shaped, broad green leaves to 50cm long, with silvery white undersides. Fine, loose sprays of pale tan coloured flowers, on spikes to 1.2m high, are produced in late summer, followed by round, bead-like seed pods

An epiphytic, evergreen, tropical orchid and a popular houseplant. Upright, arching or semi-pendant stems emerge beneath older leaves and carry long-lasting flowers. Size and number vary, depending on the cultivar. Image shows a selection of Phalaenopsis; P. lueddemanniana, P. Sogo Rose and P. Taida 'King's Caroline'

A small to medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with bright green, oval leaves, up to 30cm long and 4-5cm wide. An evergreen, epiphytic orchid with semi-pendent, broadly-elliptic, fleshy leaves. A small-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with three to four, elliptic leaves, 20-25cm long and 4cm wide. Vigorous perennial grass with a running rootstock, forming an extensive colony of upright stems, to 1.5m tall in flower, bearing narrow, linear, mid-green leaves to 35cm long, and narrow panicles to 17cm long of pale green flower spikelets in summer

A deciduous fern to around 50cm high, with upright to arching, narrow, pinnatifid fronds up to 80cm long. Fronds are pale green when young and take on a slight blue-green tint when mature

A mat-forming perennial with rooting stems densely clothed in tiny silver-grey leaves. Silky-hairy, pale green or straw-coloured flowers to 7mm across are produced in summer

A slow-growing, small evergreen shrub of rounded habit with leathery, broadly-oval leaves and fragrant white flowers 2cm in width, in terminal panicles in early summer, followed by small, fleshy black fruits

A half-hardy, densely-branched, spreading evergreen shrub to 2m tall, armed along the shoots with long, thin spines. The sharp-pointed leaves are leathery and glossy. An evergreen perennial epiphytic cactus with bright green slender cylindical stems and small white flowers which appear along the stems in late winter to early spring. May grow up to 5 metres if space allows

An epiphytic cactus with slender, cylindrical stems that may be erect, spreading or weeping. The upper part is branched, often in whorls, and produces small, star-shaped, white flowers followed by white berries

A robust, upright, evergreen shrub to around 150cm in height, with glossy, dark green foliage. Masses of funnel-shaped, scarlet-red flowers appear in late spring

an erect small evergreen shrub, to 1.5m tall, with dark, glossy ovate leaves and small clusters of deep rose-pink, funnel-shaped flowers, 5cm in width, in late winter and early spring

A large, upright deciduous shrub with glossy mid-green leaves turning reddish-green in autumn. Strongly-scented, funnel-shaped white, pink-flushed flowers with red stamens are borne in early summer

A large, narrow, evergreen tree, with dark green leaves, to 20cm long, a smooth cinnamon-brown, fawn or silvery indumentum on the undersides. Flowers, produced in rounded trusses in early spring, are up to 5cm long and may be red, white or any shade of pink, usually with spotting in the throat

A species of evergreen Rhododendron with oval-shaped, blue-green foliage with hairy undersides. Bright, greenish-yellow funnel-shaped flowers with brown spots appear in May

A deciduous azalea, usually to about 2.5m high in cultivation, though occasionally to 5m in its native habitat. A large, spreading evergreen shrub to 10m in height, with long, narrow elegant leaves and large trusses of white or pale pink, bell-shaped flowers, spotted within with maroon, are borne in early spring

A large upright evergreen shrub to 4m tall, with glossy, dark, lanceolate leaves and, in mid to late spring trusses of funnel-shaped, clear pink to purplish-pink flowers to 4cm in width

A half-hardy, mid-sized evergreen shrub to 2.5m high, often epiphytic, with ovate, textured dark green leaves, and a fine covering of pale brown hairs on new shoots and the undersides of leaves. A small, spreading, evergreen shrub with dark, glossy green leaves which are red-brown and scaly beneath. Small trusses of rose-pink to crimson and occasionally white tubular flowers appear in June.

nikau palm|feather duster palm|New Zealand palm|Norfolk Island palm

A large deciduous perennial forming a spreading clump of large, more or less pinnately divided leaves, with erect, conical sprays of cream or pink flowers in summer

alternative_names: many-flowered rose|baby rose|bramble rose|Japanese rose|Rosa polyantha

An herbaceous perennial to 30cm, with erect leafy stems and terminal clusters of up to four purple, orchid-like flowers 4cm in width in early summer
