A compact, clump-formng herbaceous perennial with mid-green, lance-shaped toothed leaves and upright, slender erect stems of small, star-shaped pink flowers appearing in spring and summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with rough green narrow leaves to a height of 2m. In late summer and autumn bears yellow daisy flowers with purple-red, or sometimes yellow disks
A bushy, evergreen perennial with rounded, mid-green leaves, finely netted with yellow. Clusters of rich red, single flowers are produced from late spring to early autumn

A medium-sized, deciduous twining climber with mid green leaves and an abundance of mauve flowers with darker purple bar to 15cm in width and reddish anthers. Flowers appear from late spring to early summer and then again in late summer.
Has curved, partly decumbent pitchers to 45cm in length with narrow lids and red veins; flowers dark mahogany-red

A dwarf, hardy evergreen, spreading perennial with small and compact dark green oval-shaped foliage and small, tubular flowers in shades of bright blue to pink appearing in the spring. Great for rockeries or troughs and containers

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 125cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Salmon-pink spiky flowers flushed with pale yellow towards the base of the petals, appear from summer through until the first frosts

A vigorous evergreen shrub, with an upright, open habit and glossy dark green leaves with serrated edges. Flowers in mid spring, bearing bright red, incomplete double flowers, with smaller red petals in the centre sometimes touched with white
A mat-forming, evergreen compact perennial alpine with tightly-packed large green-grey rosettes with pointed, dark red tips. Leaves may vary in intensity of colour in cooler conditions

primary_name: Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. albiflorum 'Coquette'

description: A bulbous perennial to 20cm tall, with channelled, strap-shaped leaves appearing in autumn, and dense racemes of long-lasting, mid-blue flowers, pale green at the tips and rounded in bud, in spring

plant_range: Tropical Asia to Pacific N. Guinea

description: A compact, spreading evergreen azalea with small, mid-green leaves and funnel-shaped, bright crimson flowers, 3cm in width, borne in mid to late spring

A vigorous, upright-growing tree, up to 10m high, with large, deeply divided, shiny, seven-lobed or nine-lobed leaves, coarsely toothed on the outer half, the young leaves emerging dark red in spring, slowly ageing to bronze-green above and grey-green by late summer, and turning orange-red in autumn, and tiny, purple-red flowers in small, pendent corymbs in spring followed by red-winged fruit in late summer
Upright, bushy rose about 90cm tall, with healthy, leathery mid-green leaves, and very fragrant, free-flowering, buff apricot, cupped, fully double blooms, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

A bushy deciduous shrub to around 3m tall with deeply lobed green leaves. Large, deep purple fruits with sweet red flesh and a good flavour appear in summer and autumn. A high yielding cultivar ripening from September. Suitable for growing in containers

An upright, bushy, deciduous shrub with divided, pinnate leaves, variegated foliage with pale cream margins. Frothy panicles of tiny, scented, white flowers in summer are followed by round, glossy, black fruit.
A compact, bushy plant to around 25cm tall with evergreen, lobed leaves with a slightly lighter centre.Double white flowers witha pale pink flush are borne over a long season

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage with a silvery coating, and fragrant black flowers with a powdery grey edge, white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring
An herbaceous perennial producing spikes of funnel-shaped, deep sky-blue flowers in summer. It can reach 1m in height

A shrub up to about 75cm high, with an erect but rather sprawling habit, evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves up to 5.5cm long, becoming greener with age, and flowering stems up to 40cm long topped by loose spikes up to 10cm long of very fragrant, vibrant violet flowers in late summer

alternative_names: cherry laurel 'Castlewellan'|Prunus laurocerasus 'Variegata' misapplied [2]|Prunus laurocerasus 'Marbled White'
description: A slow-growing cultivar, but will eventually form a large dense, wide-spreading bush to 5m tall. Leaves are green and grey-green, marbled with white throughout

alternative_names: sweet autumn clematis|Clematis thunbergii misapplied|Clematis maximowiczii|Clematis dioscoreifolia|Clematis chinensis misapplied|Clematis flammula var. robusta|Clematis paniculata Thunb.|Clematis maximowicziana
description: Strong, vigorous deciduous (semi-evergreen in mild winters) climber 6m tall or more, with hairy stems, semi-woody with age, dark green leaves divided into leaflets carried on long leaf stalks, and large clusters of small fragrant, single, star-shaped, white flowers about 3cm across with cream anthers, flowering from late summer to autumn, followed by attractive seedheads

An early-season, cooking apple, conical in shape with ribbed sides. The yellow skin is flushed on the sunny side with orange-red, and the pale yellow flesh is firm and juicy with a sweet-sharp flavour. A very hardy, spreading tree producing heavy crops but tending to biennial bear; requires a pollinator from group 1, 2 or 3. Fruit is ready to pick late summer and keeps until mid-autumn
A bulbous perennial, growing to 60cm tall, with upright, lance-shaped, bright green leaves and sumptuously dark purple flowers with yellow markings on the purple falls. Perfect for cut flowers

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with lance-shaped mid-green leaves. In summer and autumn it produces large, single, golden yellow flowers that are flecked with red-orange on branched stems. The daisy-like flowers have a central boss of dark-red/yellow stamens.
A low-growing, bushy, spreading deciduous shrub with silvery-green pinnate leaves growing 60cm tall and 1.2m wide. Saucer shaped golden-yellow flowers appear from May through to July

primary_name: Centaurea triumfettii subsp. stricta from Macedonia

description: A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 40cm high, with slightly glaucous, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers from mid-spring, producing solitary flowers to 9cm across, with bright yellow outer petals and a large, golden yellow cup with a ruffled rim

An evergreen perennial to 40cm, with erect, oval, strongly purple-bronzed leaves with a rather open habit; the colour deepens in good light and cold weather. Slender reddish stems bear pendant clusters of deep pink flowers in spring
A vigorous upright medium-sized shrub with bright red, semi-double flowers to 13cm across
A perennial forming a clump to 60cm in height, with narrow, dark glossy green leaves and semi-double white flowers 10-12cm in width, with a trace of yellow in the centre

A deciduous shrub with large well-flavoured fruits which are produced from mid to late July. The bushes are vigorous and tall, making the currants easy to pick. Blackcurrants are self-fertile and produce insignificant yellow-green flowers in spring.
A dwarf bulbous perennial to 20cm with green foliage and delicate star-shaped dark pink and white flowers which open in the sun and appear in spring. Ideal for rock gardens due to its compact habit

An elegant weeping, grafted, large, slow-growing shrub/small tree up to 5m in height and with branches which cascade to the ground. It does not get any taller than the trunk it is grafted on. Leaves are green turning red, gold and purple in autumn. A profusion of large white pointed bracts surrounding small flower heads cloak the plant in late spring/early summer and turn pink at maturity. Small spherical, red-pink, edible fruit ripen in late summer

A dense, clump-forming perennial grass, about 3m tall, with evergreen, arching, sharply toothed blue-green leaves, about 2.5m long. Upright stems bearing large, plume-like panicles, to 90cm long, of white spikelets appear in late summer and early autumn

A vigorous, upright tree with long, pointed, shiny leaves and white blossom in spring. The medium-sized, oval, dessert pears have light green to yellowish green skin, with variable russetting, and firm, fine, faintly yellow, sweet and moderately juicy flesh with a pleasant flavour. Pick in mid-autumn and use to late autumn; a reliable cropper, even in cooler conditions. Not self-fertile, in pollination group 2

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing large fleshy rosettes in dense clusters, the velvety, spoon-shaped, silvery-green leaves covered in fine white hairs, flushed rosy pink, and turning dark pink in cold weather. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets
An upright evergreen shrub with dark, glossy foliage and creamy-white, anemone-form double flowers which shade to light yellow in the centre

alternative_names: hollyhock Chater's Double Group|Alcea rosea 'Chater's Mix'
description: A selection of vigorous short-lived perennials with lobed rounded leaves and long, erect pyramids of open funnel-shaped large double flowers in summer in a selection of white, yellow, pink and crimson colours.

Deciduous climber about 4m in height, with hairy stems, bright green leaves composed of five leaflets and single, rich, violet-purple flowers to 18cm across, shaded burgundy with a dark purple central bar to each petal, with deep, reddish-purple anthers, flowering from early summer to early autumn

primary_name: Rosa 'Madame Legras de Saint Germain' (A × N)
description: Large rose to 2m tall that can be grown as a climber to 5m, with pale to mid-green, almost thornless branches and soft, downy pale grey-green foliage. Bears highly fragrant, very-double, rosette-shaped, creamy-white blooms to 5cm across with a button eye, in large clusters in midsummer in one flush of flower
A vigorous suckering medium-sized deciduous shrub to 2m in height , with prominently veined, light green leaves and solitary bright yellow, single flowers from mid-spring

Clump-forming perennial with mid-green grassy foliage, and bearing upright stems about 1-1.2m tall with free-flowering and long lasting, pale primrose cylindrical flowers opening from greenish buds and fading to ivory-white, produced from midsummer
A herbaceous, rhizomatous perennial with dark green strap-like leaves. Sturdy stems of cornflower-blue flowers with a white beard and yellow throat appear from early until mid summer

A culinary cultivar in pollination group 2 and a triploid. A vigorous tree that produces heavy, regular crops of fruit that can be very large; apples yellowish-green flushed pink. Cooks to well-flavoured purée; not as acidic as 'Bramley's Seedling'. Attractive, deep pink blossom. Season of use is from late September to December
A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, ruffled mid-blue flowers appearing mid spring

alternative_names: lyme grass|amdowellt|European dune grass|sea lyme grass|sea lyme-grass|Leymus arenarius 'Glaucus'|Elymus arenarius
description: Densely tufted grass to 1.5m tall, with long rhizomes, forming loose, spreading clumps of arching, pale, blue-grey leaves about 60cm long. Produces stiff, upright stems bearing spike-like racemes 35cm long of blue-grey then buff spikelets throughout summer
Globose to slightly conical, evergreen, semi-dwarf conifer about 75cm tall in 10 years, with grey green short, needle-like growth

Fast-growing, evergreen climber to around 5m tall, with reddish stems, large, glossy, pale green 5-lobed leaves darker with age. Between late summer and late winter, small, greenish flowers, in umbels, followed by globular black fruits, ripen in spring or early summer, on mature foliage
A compact, bushy shrub to 60cm tall and wide with green foliage and yellow to golden flowers with overlapping petals borne from early summer to early autumn

A China rose of neat habit, about 80-90cm tall, with slender stems bearing small greyish-green leaves. Clusters of lightly scented, fully double cup-shaped pink blooms with a hint of lilac, slightly darker on the outer petals, almost continuously in flower from early summer onwards to late in the season

A dwarf, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with dark green palmate leaves divided into three lobes. Has white flowers with an outer circle of large sepals and a centre of intersecting smaller white petals from March to May after which it becomes dormant until late autumn.

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to 60cm high, with rosettes of mid-green leaves up to 25cm long, dusted with white meal. In late spring to early summer, flowering stems bear one to four clusters of small, pendent, scented flowers that are creamy white, white with purple eyes, or lilac purple

An alpine perennial with grey green, ovate foliage and outward facing, violet-blue, bell-shaped flowers providing a long flowering display in summer. An evergreen, easy to grow plant but dislikes wet winters

alternative_names: The Bloodie pink|Dianthus the Bloodie pink
Sempervivum ciliosum var. galicicum from Mali Hat, Albania|Sempervivum ciliosum 'Mali Hat'

description: A deciduous shrub to about 2m tall, with long, arching reddish stems and slender willow-like mid to dark green leaves. The single flowers have dark pink-red sepals and a dark purple corolla, produced from summer to autumn

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 90cm high, with divided, slightly glossy green leaves. Fragrant, anemone-form flowers are produced in late spring and early summer, with rose pink guard petals at the edges, ruffled pink petals in the centre, and narrow cream petalodes mixed into, or sometimes surrounding the central petals

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage coated with a silvery powder, and fragrant, yellow flowers with a small white centre, appearing in the spring

primary_name: Penstemon fruticosus var. scouleri f. ruber

description: A low-growing, succulent subshrub, with spreading stems bearing fleshy, yellow-green leaves that flush orange and red in bright, dry conditions. Dome-shaped clusters of lightly scented white flowers are produced in spring
A bulbous perennial to 45cm in height, with strap-shaped leaves and neat, double, creamy-white flowers 10cm in width, the inner segments shorter, deep orange
A spreading evergreen azalea to 1m tall, with small, mid-green leaves and double, rosy-pink flowers, 4cm in width, in early summer
An upright, clump-forming, semi-evergreen fern bearing green fronds with narrowly lance-shaped, glossy, oval to triangular, toothed leaflets.

alternative_names: alpine bartsia|alpine eyebright cow wheat|mountain poly|velvet bells

description: A hardy, clump-forming evergreen perennial with large, oval-shaped leathery dark green foliage with coarsely hairy margins. Clusters of shortly-branched, rose-pink flowers appear on strong stems above the foliage from mid to late spring. A good choice for borders, rock gardens or as ground cover
A diminutive evergreen perennial slowly forming a mat of narrowly ovate leaves to a height of just 4cm, with white flowers, opening in late spring and early summer

A large-flowered gladiolus, maximum height 1.2 m high, with rich grey-green sword like leaves and a flower spike with around 10-15 flower buds, which are at first a rich cream colour opening into large funnel shaped, pure white flowers with cream throats

alternative_names: common ivy|bentwood|bindwood|common English ivy|Crimean ivy|eiddew|ivory|ivy gum plant|love united|Hedera helix f. caucasigena|Hedera caucasigena|Hedera burgalensis|Hedera helix 'Taurica'
description: A vigorous, self-clinging climber with three to five-lobed, glossy, evergreen leaves, often with pale green veins, and some reddish or bronzy colours in autumn. Mature plants produce bushy, non-clinging branches with diamond-shaped leaves, and small, nectar-rich, greenish-yellow flowers in clusters of rounded heads in autumn, followed by black berries in winter. An important wildlife plant, providing food, shelter and nest sites for many birds, insects and small mammals
A dwarf, very slow growing pine forming a rounded cushion of long, silvery blue-green needles with an ultimate size of about 45cm x 60cm
A deciduous shrub to 2m tall, with elliptic or obovate leaves turning brilliant red in autumn; small white flowers are followed by long-lasting bright red berries

A compact perennial to around 20cm in height with lance-shaped, pointed, wavy, dark green leaves with narrow, white margins from spring to summer. Sturdy scapes bear bell-shaped, pale-lavender flowers in summer
An early-cropping, sweet cherry producing good yields of large, dark red fruit in early summer. It is not self-fertile
An evergreen large shrub or small tree reaching approximately 10m in height with dark green, oblong-elliptic glossy green leaves to 11cm that feel stiff and leathery.
An evergreen, epiphytic perennial to 40cm tall with long, slender, grey-green, grass-like leaves and small purple flowers emerging from red bracts in the spring and summer
An early-flowering bulb that produces grey-green foliage and single flowers. Petals are a cerise-purple with a internal yellow ring. Height to 10cm

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Single white flowers with yellow centres, sometimes with slightly drooping petals, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly

A tall evergreen shrub with dark shiny leaves, paler beneath. Pink buds open to funnel-shaped, fragrant white flowers, 9cm in width, tinged pink and speckled green in throat, borne in elongated trusses from late spring
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with golden, wavy foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer. A great variety for ground cover but also as a single plant

A hardy, upright, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial with lance-shaped, pointed, softly hairy, aromatic grey-green foliage. White to pale lavender-purple flowers with purple spots appear in summer. Does not spread as rapidly as other varieties. Loved by bees

A clump-forming perennial, to 1.2m high in flower, with long green leaves, finely cut or completely divided into narrow, lance-shaped leaflets. In summer and early autumn, produces large buds encased in overlapping, pale brown bracts, opening to bright yellow flower heads composed of crowds of narrow petals with prominent stamens

A bushy evergreen shrub, producing stems to 1.5m (5ft) high and 1m (39in) across, with oval to lance-shaped dark green leaves. The plant is covered with glandular hairs from which a sticky, aromatic, resinous substance called 'ladanum' is exuded, which is used in perfumery . White saucer-shaped flowers,with a maroon blotch at the base of each petal and a central boss of bright yellow stamens, are produced throughout summer and into autumn. The plant requires full sun and very well-drained soil in which to grow successfully, particularly overwinter, when rainfall may be higher.
A bushy small evergreen shrub of low, spreading habit. Leaves greyish, oval. Flowers 4cm in width, bright yellow, each petal blotched maroon near the base, borne in clusters from late spring
An upright evergreen shrub with small oval aromatic leaves, and short terminal racemes of purple or mauve, two-lipped flowers 1cm across, in early summer

An evergreen, epiphytic bromeliad to 30cm high, with funnel-shaped rosettes of long, smooth, strappy green leaves, held by dark green sheaths beneath. Produces upright flower stems of small creamy white flowers surrounded by large, bright red bracts in summer
A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Single, white flowers with a central rosette of green petals appear in the spring
A compact, evergreen shrub to about 2m with small, shiny, yellow leaves with an irregular dark green splash in the centre. Clusters of small, dark pink flowers are produced in late summer

Deciduous large shrub or small tree about 6m in height, with slender smooth branches and dark green leaves 18cm long, composed of up to 9 leaflets. Abundant, large, fragrant white flowers, each with four long petals, are produced in panicles, as the leaves unfurl in spring. Reddish-brown winter buds

A medium-sized, upright tree with shiny, oval leaves and white blossom in spring. The medium-to-large, conical to pear-shaped, dessert fruit have rough, yellowish-green to golden-yellow, russetted skin, and pale yellow, fine, melting, juicy flesh with a very good flavour. Pick in early autumn and use to mid-autumn. Not self-fertile, in pollination group 3

Old garden rose about 90cm tall and wide, with slender stems bearing small dark green leaves. Very fragrant, rich plum-coloured, semi-double blooms, edged and flecked with light magenta-crimson opening to display prominent golden stamens, once-flowering in early to midsummer and tolerant of part shade; introduced in 1850

A slow-growing, conical, evergreen coniferous shrub reaching an eventual height of around 6m, with soft, spiral-shaped foliage, pale green when young turning to blue-green as the shrub matures. A good accent plant for any garden and ideal for pots and containers

A low-growing, hardy bulbous perennial to around 40cm in height, with long, thin, grass-like blue-green foliage. Funnel-shaped bright blue flowers with darker stripes appear on long, slender stems from May to July. Suits smaller gardens well, bringing a splash of colour to rock gardens and small borders and may be left undisturbed to naturalise in wildflower meadows
A semi-evergreen perennial with variegated leaves edged with white. Yellow-centred, white spring flowers are followed by small, red edible fruits

A bushy, compact evergreen conifer with diagonally upright shoots creating a medium-sized shrub with an irregular outline. Sharply pointed, aromatic, needle-like foliage is blue-green, turning blue-grey in winter
A compact, deciduous, aquatic perennial which has small rounded dark-green leaves and deep red-pink cup-shaped flowers with narrow petals and deep yellow stamens
An herbaceous perennial to 90cm in height, with glaucous green leaves and large, pale pink flowers with paler falls bearing reddish-orange beards
An evergreen perennial to 15cm tall, forming a wide mat of grey-green foliage, with clove-scented, semi-double light pink flowers, each petal with a deep pink zone at the base
A bushy medium-sized deciduous shrub with clusters of funnel-shaped flowers 5cm wide, deep orange-red with a darker flare in the throat, in late spring; good autumn colour

Bushy, branching, shrubby rose about 90cm tall and 60cm wide, with healthy, glossy dark green foliage. Slightly fragrant, rosy pink, fully double, quartered blooms with white flecks and edges and a crimson blush, are freely produced almost continuously from late spring, through summer to autumn

alternative_names: prostrate speedwell 'Trehane'|Veronica austriaca subsp. teucrium 'Trehane Blue'|Veronica trehane|Veronica teucrium 'Trehane'
description: A prostrate, mat-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to 20cm high with linear-oblong, golden to yellow-green leaves and erect racemes of bright-blue flowers from late spring to mid-summer

plant_range: Australia (E Queensland to N E New South Wales)

description: A bushy, evergreen perennial with strongly scented, deeply cut foliage and clusters of single light pink flowers with a fuchsia centre. The pungent lemon scent is noted to deter mosquitoes

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Large, white flowers, flushing rosy-pink as they mature, with yellow stamens, appear in the spring

A rhizomatous perennial, to around 60cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have very pale shell pink standards, paler falls with greenish tan feathering, and a orange beard. Mid season

alternative_names: dill|anet|dill-oil plant|East Indian dill|Indian dill|meeting-seed|Sabbath day posy|Anethum sowa hort.non Roxb. ex Flem.
description: An upright annual or biennial herb 60-100cm tall, with finely dissected, aromatic blue-green leaves approximately 35cm long. Flat umbels of tiny yellow flowers are produced on upright, finely ribbed stems in mid-summer. Dill is often grown as a herb for fresh scented leaves and as a cut flower. Dill seeds are also important culinary additions. Essential oil contained in seeds has medicinal properties. Various cultivars of dill are available; cultivar 'Mammoth' can reach up to 1.5m tall and cultivar 'Mariska' is very popular with florists

An upright, evergreen shrub with thick, leathery, often deeply-lobed leaves. These are rich green, heavily veined with yellow when young and developing variable red flushing with age. Sprays of small, white, star-shaped flowers may appear in summer

alternative_names: Cornish heath 'Saint Keverne'|Erica vagans var. kevernensis|Erica vagans 'Kevernensis'
description: Small, spreading, evergreen shrub, about 16-20cm in height, bearing linear dark green leaves, and long sprays of bell-shaped, clear rose-pink flowers from summer to autumn
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, lilac-purple flowers with a white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring

Spreading, deciduous tree about 10m in height, with oval mid-green leaves, and large, salmon-pink, goblet-shaped flowers to 30cm across, paler inside, with 12 broad petals, produced in early spring before the leaves emerge

Small, deciduous tree to about 5m in height, with arching stems bearing large, waterlily-shaped lilac-pink flowers to 25cm across, with a darker pink flush on the outside of the petals, are produced over many weeks, from mid-spring

primary_name: Celosia argentea var. cristata Plumosa Group

description: Very vigorous, healthy and very large shrubby rose about 3m tall and 1.8m wide with slightly crinkled, glossy, dark green foliage and an upright then arching habit. Fragrant, large, fully double, pale lemon-yellow blooms, heavily flushed with pink, flowering in early to midsummer

alternative_names: creeping cotoneaster 'Little Gem'|Cotoneaster apiculatus 'Tom Thumb'|Cotoneaster adpressus 'Tom Thumb'
description: Low-growing, wide-spreading deciduous shrub about 30cm tall, with trailing stems and small dark green leaves to 1cm long, that turn scarlet in autumn. Small red-tinged white flowers in summer are followed by bright red fruits

alternative_names: scented mayweed|amranwen|German chamomile|horse gowan|sweet false chamomile|wild chamomile|Matricaria recutita|Chamomilla recutita
description: An annual with much divided, aromatic foliage, and scented daisy-like flowers, composed of white rays with yellow disc florets which are borne singly on stems from June to August
A bushy plant to 40cm in height, with pungently-scented, lobed leaves and large, deep red flowers, each petal marked with black
A tender evergreen perennial, scented-leaved Pelargonium with wrinkled, fan-shaped, mid-green lemon-scented leaves and pale pink single flowers from spring to autumn.
A compact deciduous perennial, to 30cm tall, with fragrant, rounded, canary yellow flowers with orange throat, to 7cm wide

Vigorous bushy rose about 90cm tall, with large, leathery, rich green leaves. Pointed buds held on long straight stems open to fragrant, scrolled, fully double, dark strawberry-red blooms shaded gold, becoming a blend of pink, red and orange as the petals age, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

A tropical evergreen shrub or small tree, to around 5m high in cultivation, with tiered branches bearing lance-shaped to elliptic, shiny bright green leaves that are tapered at the base and paler underneath. Leaves are flushed bright reddish bronze when young. Long clusters of small, fragrant, yellow-green flowers are produced at the base of young shoots in spring, followed by clusters of round, purple-black berries

alternative_names: Venus's looking glass|corn bellflower|corn violet|Campanula hybrida|Specularia hybrida

description: grows to 1m in height, with deep yellow flowers 11cm in width, flushed with deep orange
Grows to 35cm tall, with stems bearing up to three nodding, flowers with slightly reflexed, lemon-yellow perianth segments and a slightly deeper yellow cup
A herbaceous perennial up to 1.2m high with mid-green leaves and large semi-cactus flowerheads, up to 24cm across, of ivory-white florets, from summer to autumn, until the first frosts
A dwarf tuberous-rooted perennial that grows to 45cm in height, with bronze-tinged foliage and single, scarlet flowers 9cm across; ideal for bedding or containers

A spreading perennial with fleshy rhizomes producing a carpet of kidney-shaped leaves. Clusters of vanilla-scented, pale purple flowers appear from mid-winter to early spring, ahead of the leaves, providing a valuable early nectar source

A robust evergreen shrub forming a mound of neat foliage, to 1.5m tall, and over a long period in late spring produces trusses of funnel-shaped, bright yellow flowers, to 7cm in length, speckled- red on the inside

A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial usually grown as a houseplant with glossy green leaves, to a height of up to 30cm. The white flowers are often borne throughout the year indoors and in summer and autumn when grown outdoors as an annual

An evergreen shrub to 45cm high, with an open, spreading habit and upright stems bearing small, lance-shaped green leaves. Flowers are purple, urn-shaped and pendent, and produced from early summer into autumn

A fairly short, tuberous-rooted perennial to 50cm, with dark stems and mid-green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The orange blooms, up to 10cm across, have inrolled inner petals, creating a neat flowerhead

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to 1.1m, with mid-green foliage, blooming from mid-summer to the first frosts. Flowers are vivid purple-red, 10-15cm across, with quilled petals giving a spiky effect
An upright perennial to 1.5m in height, with white-eyed, light blue flowers in erect racemes to 90cm in length

A medium-sized deciduous climber with mid-green leaves composed of 3 leaflets. Slightly scented deeply veined, pale pinkish-blue flower tepals, lilac-pink inside and 5-6.5cm across, bell-shaped with recurved tips to the sepals and yellow anthers.

A fast-growing, variable tree up to 25m high in the wild but usually to 12m in cultivation, erect when young, later spreading to become broadly conical, with white-downy young branches, older branches purple-brown; the large leaves are simple, sharply toothed, usually elliptic-oblong, sometimes shallowly lobed, 15-25cm long, and are downy white when young, becoming glossy, dark green above and felted white or buff beneath, so that the whole crown appears light grey-green; the downy white flowers are scented like hawthorn and are in loose corymbs, up to 10cm across, in late spring, and are followed by round or pear-shaped fruits, 2cm across, green speckled and flushed with warm brown, or orange-red, ripening in early winter; Sorbus flowers are visited by many insects and their fruits are eaten by many birds
A double-flowered daffodil to 45cm tall, with rounded golden-yellow flowers in early and mid spring, the petaloid segments mixed with some deep orange-red coronal segments towards the centre

A compact perennial to 25cm high forming small clumps of narrow, grass-like, dark green foliage and bearing clusters of small, star-like, white flowers with yellow eyes from late spring intil late summer

An evergreen shrub to 15cm in height, of low spreading habit, with compact dark green foliage. Flowers double, rich pink, in long erect spikes

Spikes of creamy-white, bell-shaped flowers sometimes shaded purple-red are borne above the foliage in summer and may be followed by edible, banana-shaped fruit

Dainty umbels of white flowers above softly-hairy leaves, that are wavy-edged and heart-shaped. When rubbed, the leaves smell of spiced apple
A dense, spreading dwarf deciduous shrub with small, ovate, dark green leaves, and small but abundant heads of rose-pink flowers in mid summer

An herbaceous perennial to 90cm tall, with broadly lance-shaped leaves and terminal panicles of fragrant, pure white flowers in early and mid summer

Also works well as ground cover or scrambling through other plants in a herbaceous border if left unsupported
A compact plant to 25cm, with dark foliage and flowers with deep maroon upper petals and bright magenta-rose lower petals grading to white at base
A compact evergreen, self-clinging climber to about 1m tall, with glossy green leaves composed of 3-5 lobes, the central lobe is distinctively elongated

An old English culinary cultivar in pollination group 4. Fruits are medium to small size for a cooking apple, with pale green skin with a little red flushing, and crisp greenish white flesh. Cooks to a sharp puree. Season of use December to March.
A dwarf perennial to 40cm tall, with narrow strap-shaped leaves and loose, rounded heads of open funnel-shaped, light blue flowers, each petal with a darker mid-vein

A deciduous, vase-shaped tree about 8m in height with purplish bark streaked and striped white. Very large, unlobed, dark green leaves to 30cm long turn a striking golden to orange-yellow in autumn. Small yellowish-green spring flowers in panicles, followed by greenish winged fruits in late summer

A tropical shrub or woody-based perennial up to 1m high, with an upright habit and oval-shaped, leathery leaves that emerge lime green and mature to shades of green, red, yellow, pink and cream. May produce slender spikes of tiny white flowers in summer, though it rarely flowers when grown as a houseplant and is more prized for its bright foliage

A clump-forming, relatively short-lived perennial to 75cm, with mid-green foliage. Large, daisy-like, red flowers, with yellow tips to the petals, are borne on upright stems from mid-summer to early autumn

A culinary or dessert cultivar in pollination group 2. Produces a good, regular crop of apples; skin greenish-yellow flushed orange and red. Brisk eating apple; sweet and with a delicate taste when cooked. Striking, deep pink blossom. Season of use from late August to September

A herbaceous perennial with spreading rhizomes and arching, angled stems to 75cm tall, with ovate leaves and solitary or paired, double, cream flowers, tipped with green, in the leaf axils in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Berberis thunbergii f. atropurpurea 'Dart's Red Lady'
description: A dense, rounded deciduous shrub about 1m tall or more, with very dark, red-purple leaves to 3cm long, and turning bright red in autumn. Racemes of red -tinged, pale yellow flowers to 1cm long, produced along the branches in mid-spring, followed by glossy red fruit in autumn

alternative_names: rose of Sharon [Russian Violet]|Hibiscus syriacus 'Floru'|Hibiscus 'Russian Violet'
description: A vigorous, upright shrub to about 2.5m with deeply lobed leaves. Deep purple-pink flowers up to 10cm across, with a dark red centre, are produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn

alternative_names: geranium 'Mr Henry Cox'|Pelargonium 'Mrs Henry Cox'|Pelargonium 'Mrs H. Cox'
description: Grows to 35cm in height, the rounded leaves green at the base, with a broad purple and red zone and yellow margin; small clusters of pale pink flowers

A dwarf, compact evergreen old variety of azalea with oval leathery and glossy dark green leaves and masses of white flowers which appear in May. Ideal for cascading over walls or in the front of a flower border but not fully hardy so performs best in a sheltered location
A clump-forming, cormous perennial with long, ridged, sword-shaped green leaves. Produces arching sprays of golden orange flowers from red buds, from late summer into early autumn
A large climbing rose with plentiful, dark green foliage and pointed buds opening to tea-scented, deep apricot-yellow, double flowers 8cm in width

Compact, bushy rose about 1.2m tall, with prickly stems and light green foliage. Very free-flowering, very fragrant, small, cupped, fully double, clear pink blooms to 4cm across, with deeper pink centres open flat with a button eye, from rounded buds, once-flowering in midsummer but lasting for several weeks; Holland c.1800
A compact perennial to 45cm tall forming a mound of lance-shaped foliage above which are borne dense, cylindrical spikes of deep violet-blue flowers from midsummer into early autumn

A herbaceous perennial, 40-100cm high, with grey-green stems, woody at the base, leaves covered above and below in fine silvery hairs, giving them a grey-green appearance, flat and lanceolate to broadly ovate in outline, 7–20cm long and 5–10cm wide, deeply pinnatifid to pinnatisect, with 4–6 (sometimes 8) pairs of pinnatifid, cuneate–lanceolate segments, and dense corymbs, 5-20cm across, containing 50-250 flowerheads, each with usually 4-5 white ray florets, in early summer; not to be confused with Tanacetum macrophyllum
a medium-sized evergreen shrub to 2m, larger if trained to climb, with large, leathery, palmately lobed leaves and small flowers in globose panicles

A large, perennial bulb with long, strap-shaped green leaves which appear after flowering. Up to two stems with large, clear white flowers with a yellow green eye and 2 to 4 flowers per stem, appear in the winter

A fast-growing, evergreen shrub starting upright and spreading with age. The leaves are hairy, with five lobes and around 5cm long. Funnel-shaped, mauve-purple flowers 10cm across are produced singly from the leaf axils of young shoots from late spring to autumn

Vigorous, upright rose about 1.5m tall, with glossy dark green leaves, the new growth copper coloured. Large, full, classically shaped, lightly scented blooms borne on long stems, are dark red, tinted cherry, usually in small clusters or singley, from early summer to autumn

A perennial bulb, to around 12cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with long, curving outer petals, and inner petals marked with a small, dark green bridge at the tip and a diffuse, paler green blotch at the base

A vigorous, French heritage variety of dessert apple to around 6m in height, with semi-russeted pale green-yellow skin, sometimes flushed with orangey-red. Masses of white to pale pink flowers in spring develop into aromatic fruits with finely-textured, creamy-white flesh and a wine-like flavour which can be eaten freshly picked or used in cooking. Shows excellent tolerance to cold. Self sterile triploid requiring cross-pollination from another tree in the same or similar group in order to set fruit. Stores well for several months
A vigorous deciduous climber with paired ovate leaves and fragrant red-flushed white flowers, ageing to yellow, in early summer, followed by red berries

A bulbous perennial up to 40cm tall, with one flower per stem. Flowers are 11cm wide, with broad, overlapping, deep yellow perianth segments with blunt tips with a flared and fluted, deep yellow cup, with a serrated rim

A deciduous climber to about 3m, with light green foliage, flowering in late spring to early summer on last year’s growth, and again in early autumn on new growth. Flowers are single, pale pinkish-purple with a dark pink central stripe and dark red stamens

A tender perennial up to 4m high, with lance-shaped, slightly glossy green leaves to 80cm long. In summer, produces long, semi-upright flower spikes, with small white flowers surrounded by overlapping, bright red bracts

An upright, branching, deciduous shrub with attractive large, dissected, dark green leaves. Large and showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped, semi-double flowers borne from late spring into early summer have ruby-purple petals and a yellow centre
A bushy, evergreen regal perennial Pelargonium, with rounded mid-green deeply serrated leaves and trumpet shaped single red flowers in summer.
A large evergreen shrub producing trusses of funnel-shaped, frilled, deep rose-pink flowers, 6cm across, with a dark blotch in late spring
A medium-sized evergreen shrub of compact habit with narrow, bright green leaves. Flowers small, purple, female succeeded by clusters of bright red oval berries

A bushy, spreading, deciduous shrub, reaching around 4m in height with green leaves. Small red flowers clustered all along the stems appear in early summer, developing into bright scarlet berries which are loved by birds for food

primary_name: Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. hederifolium 'Antiochus'

description: Mat-forming succulent with open rosettes to 10cm across, with thick, bristle-tipped blue-green leaves flushed dark purple. Upright hairy spikes to 15cm tall, of starry red-purple flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

alternative_names: Camassia leichtlinii 'Blue Donau'|Camassia leichtlinii 'Blauwe Donau'|Camassia leichtlinii [Blue Danube]
description: A bulbous perennial to 1.2m high, with linear, strap-shaped green leaves. Clusters of starry, soft violet-blue flowers are held on flowering spikes high above the foliage, and open in sequence from the bottom to the top of the stem in mid to late spring

A clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 60cm high, with basal rosettes of hairy, pinnate leaves. Semi-double scarlet flowers are held, singly or in groups of two or three, on stems well above the foliage from early to late summer

alternative_names: red star 'Susan Garnett-Botfield'|Rhodohypoxis 'Mrs Susan Garnet Bottfield'
description: A compact perennial to 10cm tall, with narrow, hairy leaves and 6-petalled, pale pink flowers 2-3cm wide, in summer

A spreading evergreen shrub with dark-green leathery leaves. In late winter and early spring fragrant, yellow-green flowers are born in pendant clusters, providing a good early season food source for pollinators. Male and female flowers are produced on separate plants so more than one plant is needed for berries. Female plants produce red berries that ripen to black.

A late-flowering blackcurrant cultivar which therefore avoids the damage caused by late spring frosts. Large fruits on short strigs ripen evenly ready for harvesting from mid- to late summer with the heavy crops are borne on strong, upright branches

alternative_names: Sintenis woodruff|Asperula aristata subsp. thessala|Asperula nitida subsp. puberula
description: A tufted, cushion-forming, evergreen perennial with rosettes of narrow, blue-green leaves less than 1cm long. Narrow, tubular, pink flowers are produced singly or in pairs in early summer
An herbaceous, low, clump-forming perennial to 15cm in height, with narrow dark green leaves and daisy-like flowerheads to 5cm in width, with white rays and a yellow centre, from May to June
A hardy, evergreen shrub with an attractive compact habit approximately 31-45cm tall with a spread to 46-60cm. It has dark green foliage and mauve flowers in summer through to autumn.
A woody-based herbaceous perennial to 45cm in height, with silvery-white leaves 2-4cm in length, finely divided into linear segments. Flowerheads small, yellowish, in arching spikes
A compact perennial with glaucous green foliage and up to 5 flowers per stem, the standards light violet-blue, the falls white, edged with light violet

alternative_names: lupin Band of Nobles Series|Lupinus polyphyllus 'Band of Nobles'
description: Robust biennials or short-lived perennials with erect racemes of fragrant flowers in shades of blue, pink, cream, red and yellow, some bicoloured, in early summer
A bulbous perennial to 45cm, with reddish-orange flowers, the base of each petal yellow
A tender, mat-forming perennial succulent to 30cm tall with small, fat, grey-green leaves. Daisy-like, burnt orange flowers with yellow centres are borne in profusion in the summer
An evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 15cm in height, with ovate leaves and pinkish-mauve flowers 2.5cm in width in summer

alternative_names: Lawson's cypress 'Gold Splash'|Chamaecyparis lawsoniana 'Fletcher's Gold Splash'

description: A dwarf conifer, with an upright, conical habit, to about 70cm high in 10 years. Short, flattened green needles are tinted bronze when young, and turn purple as the temperature drops in winter

A compact, ornamental grass, forming evergreen mounds of foliage about 30cm tall, with densely-tufted, very fine, needle-like spiky, exceptionally silvery blue leaves. Produces upright flower stems with silvery blue flowers in spikelets during mid and late summer, that turn pale golden-brown

A bushy perennial to 90cm tall and wide with dark green leaves divided into oval to lance-shaped leaflets. Fragrant, semi-double, white flowers with golden-yellow stamens open from soft pink buds in late spring and early summer

alternative_names: Rocky Mountain raspberry|Rocky Mountain flowering raspberry|showy white-flowered bramble

description: A slow-growing evergreen conifer of conical habit, with dark blue-green foliage in small, dense, thick sprays

alternative_names: garden catmint|Faassen's catmint|mirrinminttu|Nepeta pseudomussinii|Nepeta mussinii misapplied
description: A herbaceous perennial, forming a clump of upright stems with aromatic grey-green leaves. Terminal whorls of pale, violet-blue flowers, to 12mm in length, appear in summer and early autumn

alternative_names: four-coloured silver inch plant|Tradescantia fluminensis 'Quadricolor'|Tradescantia 'Quadricolor Pink'
description: A trailing perennial to 15cm, with lance-shaped leaves longitudinally striped with green, cream, pink and white; pinkish-purple flowers appear intermittently throughout the year

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 1m, with dark green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The blooms are small pompoms, 6cm across, with many neat rows of tightly inrolled, bright red petals

Narrowly upright tree about 10m tall, with weeping branches. Smallish leaves emerge red-bronze then become burgundy-purple through the summer, turning golden-copper before falling. Bark smooth silver-grey with an interesting silouette in winter
A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 102cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant green-yellow flowers in summer

Has particularily fine flowers, opening white and blushing pink with age, and is very floriferous; flowers mostly in spring with sporadic flowers produced through to October. Small, shining green leaves with bronzed margins become redder in winter

A deciduous, clump-forming perennial with arching, strap-shaped mid-green leaves. From early summer trumpet shaped pale yellow flowers are produced on erect stems. Flowers will only last a day before the next one opens. Hemerocallis have a long flowering period

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 80cm in height when in flower. It forms clumps of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, scarlet-red flowers with a green and yellow throat to 14cm across in summer.

A clump-forming perennial to 90cm tall, with lance-shaped, aromatic, mid-green foliage. From mid-summer to early autumn each upright stem carries a whorl of two-lipped, tubular, white flowers with green bracts and a pale green centre

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial growing to 45cm tall with trifoliate green leaves. Creamy-yellow flowers are borne in rounded flower heads 2-4cm acrossin summerand are a good nectar source for bees and butterflies

alternative_names: Tasmanian brookweed|Tasmanian water pimpernel|wild thyme of Otago

alternative_names: robust Chinese fountain bamboo|Borinda scabrida misapplied|Fargesia scabrida misapplied [1]
description: A tough, evergreen bamboo forming dense clumps of deep blue-green canes to 4m tall, becoming paler as they mature, with creamy-white sheaths. Leaves are green and blue-green beneath and 15cm long
A compact evergreen shrub with small, dark green leaves, tinged bronze when young, and upright panicles of white, urn-shaped flowers in late spring
A low-growing, spreading evergreen shrub with golden yellow foliage.

alternative_names: Aspidium gemmiferum|Aspidium coadnatum var. gemmiferum|Aspidium cicutarium Sim non (L.) Sw.

A perennial bulb to around 50cm in height, with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. Double, peony-like rich, lilac-puple flowers appear in late spring

A vigorous fern with an arching habit forming a plant up to 3m wide. Individual bipinnately-divided fronds can reach up to 2m in length; young fronds vary in colour but often emerge orange-red before maturing to a glossy green; many tiny plantlets are produced on the upper surfaces of the fronds

A clump-forming daffodil to around 45cm high, with slightly grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are densely double, to 8.5cm across, with white petals interspersed with short sections of lemon yellow corona
A low-growing evergreen shrub to 30cm high, with a spreading habit and tiny, narrow, dark green leaves. Clusters of urn-shaped, pale purple flowers are produced from early summer into autumn
A perennial bulb to 30cm with upright, rich green leaves and stiffly erect spikes of fragrant, single pale salmon-orange flowers
A tall, robust perennial to 1.8m, with divided foliage, and large, flattened heads of bright yellow flowers. Good for drying

A large-flowered showy gladiolus, around 1-1.2m high, with green sword like leaves and an erect vertical flower spike with around 10-12 flower buds. The large flowers are a lavender purple colour with paler throats. Blousy, tall and dramatic blooms for the summer.
An evergreen perennial forming rosettes of fleshy, red and green leaves covered with hairs. Pink, star-shaped flowers may be borne in summer on stems arising from mature rosettes
A clump-forming evergreen perennial to 25cm; flowers white, with a deep yellow patch at the base of each fall

An upright, bushy deciduous shrub with ovate, dark green leaves. This triphylla cultivar produces clusters of pendent deep pink flowers, with long slender tubes and small, salmon pink petals in summer
A compact herbaceous perennial to 60cm, with finely divided leaves and deep golden-yellow daisies borne in an open, branched inflorescence
A medium-sized deciduous shrub with ovate leaves boldly margined with white. Flowers small, yellow, in clusters on bare stems in late winter, followed by glossy red fruits 1.5cm in length

alternative_names: queen palm|Cocos geriba|Cocos romanzoffiana|Arecastrum romanzoffianum|Cocos australis|Cocos arechavaletana|Cocos martiana|Cocos datil|Cocos acrocomioides|Cocos plumosa

A tall, clump-forming perennial to 1.8m high in flower, with mounds of lobed and toothed leaves at the base. Tall spikes packed with clear blue flowers with dark 'eyes' are produced in summer

A vigorous climbing rose about 5.5m tall, with lush, dark green foliage, and freely produced clusters of large hybrid tea-type, very fragrant, fully-double, cupped blooms of pale cherry-cerise wiht a golden-yellow and lemon base, repeat flowering from early summer to autumn
a tender perennial with narrow, grey-green leaves and deep mahogany-red flowers to 9cm across, held well above the foliage in summer and early autumn
A bushy plant to 45cm in height, with lobed leaves and clusters of mauve-pink, semi-double flowers marked with purple on the upper petals

A mat-forming, evergreen perennial comprising rosettes to 15cm across of fleshy leaves. Leaves are a silvery, blue-green flushed and tipped with pinkish-red. Mature rosettes may bear star-shaped pink flowers on stout stems above the rosettes in summer

alternative_names: snowdrop from Lagodekhi, Eastern Georgia|Galanthus ketskhovelii|Galanthus kemulariae
description: A perennial bulb, up to 20cm high in flower, with long, linear, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Late flowering, bearing solitary, nodding white flowers in early spring, with inner petals marked with a small, inverse v shape at the tip
An evergreen perennial to 25cm, with narrow, dark green leaves edged with yellow and cream, silvery beneath, and 7cm in width yellow or orange daisies, each ray with a black basal spot; disk yellow

alternative_names: Catalina ironwood|Lyonothamnus aspeniifolius|Lyonothamnus floribundus var. asplenifolius
description: A conical, evergreen tree to 12m with peeling, red-brown bark and fern-like, deep green leaves. Large, flattish sprays of small, white, five-petalled flowers are produced In spring and summer
A cultivar with a good tight growth habit. Flowers are violet-blue with a small orange eye
Evergreen climber with an array of sharply-pointed, glossy dark green leaf forms on long petioles, the leaves have downward curled lobes and pronounced veins

alternative_names: hornwort|cedar moss|coon tail|cyrnddail|fish blankets|horn weed|morass weed|rigid hornwort

Small, inconspicuous pale green flowers appear on the leaf axils between May and July. It thrives in both still or slow-moving water and works as a great oxygenator, providing a steady supply of oxygen and acting as a filter to keep ponds clear and healthy

A broadly columnar, deciduous tree to 25m in height, with red buds and orange winter shoots. The dark green leaves to 8cm long, blue-green beneath turnbutter-yellow in autumn. Small, fragrant, pale yellow flowers are borne in spreading clusters of up to 10 flowers, in midsummer

alternative_names: Primula marginata 'White Lady'|Primula 'White Lady'|Primula allionii 'White Linda Pope'|Primula marginata 'White Linda Pope'
description: A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage with a silvery coating, and fragrant, white flowers, appearing in spring
A mound forming perennial with mottled dark green leaves which develop red and copper tint into late summer and autumn. The pink flowers with a white eye produce a long lasting display for the summer

Bushy upright rose about 60-90cm in height and spread with healthy, glossy grey-green foliage. Long pointed salmon pink buds open to lightly fragrant, semi-double, blooms of pale to bright pink, suffused with yellow at the centres, almost continuously in flower from summer until the autumn frosts; introduced in 1887

A bulbous perennial, growing to 65cm tall, with narrow, upright, strap-shaped, green leaves and tall, sturdy stems bearing elegant flowers with dark blue standards and paler blue falls with a yellow signal. Perfect for cut flowers

Dwarf species rose, about 60cm tall and wide, with very prickly stems bearing glossy, serrated aromatic leaves composed of leaflets. Small, slightly scented, single bright pink blooms once-flowering in midsummer are followed by rounded, bright red fruits (hips)
A trailing plant with stems to 60cm and clusters of semi-double coral-flushed rose-pink flowers, with purple markings on the upper petals

A herbaceous perennial up to 60cm in height, forming clumps of hairy, toothed green leaves. Pendulous, tubular bell-shaped soft pink to creamy white flowers are speckled inside with deep maroon markings and appear in early to mid-summer. Ideal for shaded borders or wild gardens. Hardy and easy to grow, it adds delicate elegance and attracts pollinators to informal planting schemes
A vigorous herbaceous perennial with narrow, arching foliage and stems to 90cm in height, bearing two rich purple-violet flowers 18cm across
A double daffodil with large (10cm) flowers in mid spring. These have three rows of broad, white petals, interspersed with shorter, pinky-orange corona segments
An evergreen epiphyte with stiff, silvery-grey to whitish, linear leaves. Cream flowers emerge from bright red bracts borne on long flower spikes in summer
A bulbous perennial to 30cm in height, with glossy green leaves and shapely spike-like racemes of fragrant, soft mid-blue flowers
A perennial bulb with light green, lance-shaped foliage. The flowers reach 40cm in mid-spring and are coral pink with a yellow edge to the petals

A compact, upright, bushy deciduous shrub to 50cm tall and wide with ovate, toothed, dark green leaves. Single flowers with white to pale pink reflexed sepals tipped with green, and violet-purple corollas appear from summer into autumn
A small, compact, very slow-growing conifer, rounded when young, becoming conical with age, with silvery- green needles

A compact, mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing small colonies of pear-shaped, orange-bronze tinted, bright red rosettes, darker in cold weather, with tiny offsets. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers during summer, are produced from mature rosettes, these die off after flowering and are replaced by new offsets

alternative_names: Antwerp hollyhock|fig hollyhock|fig leaf hollyhock|Althaea ficifolia
description: A more vigorous species and short-lived perennial with distinctive lobed rounded fig-leave type foliage. Has long, erect pyramids of very large open funnel-shaped single flowers in shades of yellow, copper, pink, red and white in summer and early autumn.

An evergreen shrub up to 2m high, with a dense habit, and narrowly elliptic, dark green leaves up to 15cm long. Produces loose clusters of 12 broadly funnel-shaped, pale pink flowers, with deeper pink throats and dark red speckles on the upper petals, from late spring to early summer

alternative_names: holy rose of Abyssinia|holy rose|St John's rose|Rosa holy rose|Rosa Saint John's rose|Rosa sancta
description: Small shrub rose to about 90cm in height with arching stems and matt, dark green leaves. Small clusters of relatively large, single, pale pink, scented blooms with golden stamens, once-flowering in midsummer, suited to shade; Abyssinia 1897

alternative_names: Agapanthus campanulatus subsp. campanulatus 'Albovittatus'|Agapanthus 'Beth Chatto'|Agapanthus campanulatus 'Beth Chatto'
Neapolitan wolf's bane|Aconitum neapolitanum|Aconitum 'Lamarkii Pyreniacum'|Aconitum ranunculifolium|Aconitum pyrenaicum misapplied|Aconitum lycoctonum subsp. ranunculifolium|Aconitum lamarckii
description: Upright, clump-forming perennial to about 1-1.2m tall, with rounded 7 to 8-lobed dark green leaves, and large panicles of hooded yellow flowers, in mid and late summer

Tuberous-rooted perennial to about 75cm tall, with dark stems and dark green foliage. Fully double flowers, produced from midsummer until the first frosts, have pink petals, creamy-yellow at the base, and slightly incurved, creating a neat shape 10-15cm across

A small, spreading, deciduous tree to around 4m tall with deeply divided, seven-loned leaves that emerge a rich bronze-red in spring with bright green veining. In summer the leaves are reddish with green veining and the autumn foliage is bright gold with crimson-red tints

A herbaceous perennial, 60-100cm high, with rather floppy stems, undivided, narrow, dark green leaves, and loose clusters of double, pompom-shaped, pure white flowerheads, from early summer to early autumn

A vigorous perennial to 50cm, with glaucous green foliage and stems bearing up to 4 flowers, the standards light pinkish-brown, the falls similar but with a deeper rosy flush in the centre and a vivid orange beard
A tall and wide hardy evergreen shrub with ovate, glossy dark green leaves. Long-lasting, single, dark purple flowers appear in trusses of 2 to 4 per cluster in the spring

A vigorous upright deciduous small shrub with yellowish-green ovate leaves. Flowers large, single, with slender carmine tube and recurved sepals, the petals red-purple, and filaments red, from summer to autumn

alternative_names: apple of Peru|apple of Sodom|Peruvian bluebell|shoo-fly
description: A hardy annual with many, branched, erect, dark coloured stems to 1.2m and toothed, ovate green leaves to 10cm long, rather thin in texture. Short stalks produce short-lived, solitary pale blue or white flowers, opening in the middle of the day from June to October. Round, green-brown fruits are encased in green or black calcyes, similar to Chinese Lanterns, and can be dried for winter decorations

A tall, hardy, drought-tolerant perennial, related to teasel and scabious, with airy stems and rounded, creamy-yellow flowers which provide attractive winter seed heads. Excellent for pollinators and dry gardens
A bushy evergreen perennial with grey foliage and stems to 45cm, bearing fragrant, double creamy-white flowers 5cm in width

alternative_names: Persian shield|royal purple plant|Strobilanthes dyeriana 'Persian Shield'
description: An evergreen shrub to 1m in height, the lance-shaped dark green leaves with a striking silvery sheen over a reddish-purple flush; flowers light blue, funnel-shaped, 3cm in length, in short terminal spikes

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 35cm high, with blue-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are produced from early spring, often single but sometimes two or three to a stem. Flowers are creamy white, to 9cm across, with flat outer petals and a cup-shaped corona packed with smaller, densely frilled segments

An herbaceous perennial, to 45cm tall, with a rosette of toothed and prickly, lance-shaped, dark green leaves, each up to 40cm long and 8cm wide. In summer, short spikes bear creamy-pale-yellow flowers hooded with green bracts. The leaves, stems and flower spikes are covered with silky hairs

A deciduous, small and compact, bushy shrub with dark green foliage, and abundant pendent, double flowers which have a lavender-blue corolla and deep pink sepals and stamens, produced from summer through to autumn

A compact, deciduous climber. Single rich velvety reddish-purple flowers to 18cm across, with six to eight overlapping sepals, silvery on the underside and gently scalloped margins have bright-yellow stamens. Flowers midsummer to early autumn

alternative_names: Thalictrum saxatile Schleich. ex DC.|Thalictrum minus subsp. olympicum

description: A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 45cm high, with heart-shaped, matt green leaves with a very fine white margin. Produces loose clusters of bell-shaped pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

A mid-sized deciduous tree, to around 4m high in 10 years, and up to 10m high at maturity. It has an upright then spreading habit, and broadly oval, glossy green leaves. Large, fragrant, goblet-shaped flowers, dark pink on the outside and creamy white on the inside, appear before the leaves in spring
A bushy, tuberous perennial with dark green foliage. Fully double pompon-shaped white flowers, which may have a lilac-pink blush, appear from July until the first frosts

A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 50cm high with wavy-edged, upright green leaves flecked with white, and cranberry-red flowers which appear from summer to early autumn. May be grown as a house or conservatory plant or as a summer patio plant

A rosette-forming semi-evergreen perennial with green leaves and clusters of orange-yellow flowers with pink frilly edges which appear in the from January to April

A clump-forming perennial to 90cm tall with glossy, dark green, divided foliage. Flowers borne from late spring into early summer comprise deep red petals surrounding golden-yellow staminoides streaked with red

A slow-growing, shrubby conifer, 2-3m high after 10 years, with an irregular, spreading habit making it an unusual specimen plant. Long branches bear clusters of slender branchlets, that are cloaked in short, grey-green awl-shaped leaves. Foliage is tinted bronze in winter

An evergreen azalea to about 1.2m high, with a bushy habit, and small, ovate leaves that open bright green and mature to dark green. Produces clusters of 1-3 large, bright purplish red flowers with dark red spots, in late spring

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes, the long pointed leaves shading from purple-red to green at the tips, are especially bright in spring and summer, and green in winter. A compact bulbous perennial to 40cm in height, with greyish-green foliage and blood-red, goblet-shaped flowers 6-8cm in width, lighter red within and yellow at the base

A semi-evergreen, frost-tender fern with a creeping, hairy rhizome from which divided, triangular fronds to 20cm tall arise

A bushy upright rose about 1.2-1.5m tall, with greyish-green leaves. Very fragrant, large, deeply-cupped, fully double, silvery mid-pink blooms, borne singly or in small clusters, on strong stems that hold the blooms well above the leaves, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn; Bennett 1887

Very vigorous rose about 1.2m tall, with a trailing growth habit and glossy dark green leaves. Small clusters of lightly scented, semi-double scarlet-crimson blooms displaying prominent golden-yellow stamens, open from long pointed buds, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

A trailing plant with green leaves margined with creamy-white, and sometimes tinged pink in dry conditions; single white flowers marked with deep purple

a large, vigorous,deciduous shrub with bright green foliage and small clusters of tubular flowers in late spring and early summer, opening cream and aging to pink

An evergreen perennial to 50cm, with narrowly pointed oblong leaves, dark green with zones of silvery-grey and light green parallel to the veins; seldom flowers

A spreading, evergreen perennial to 50cm in height, with grey-green foliage and white flowers edged and marked with carmine-red

A clump-forming, erect herbaceous perennial, to 80cm tall ,with glossy green, lance-shaped foliage and, cylindrical panicles of fragrant, deep rose-pink flowers in summer

A bushy evergreen shrub with pinnate leaves composed of lance-shaped leaflets, and corymbs of bright yellow flowers 2cm across borne in the leaf axils in late summer
A variable perennial forming a spreading clump of divided, grey-green leaves, with erect stems bearing flat heads of pale yellow flowers in summer

A small, tufted evergreen fern to 45cm, with erect, narrowly lance-shaped, bipinnate fronds, with slender-pointed apex and pinnae

An evergreen perennial to 30cm in height, forming wide mats of rosettes of spoon-shaped, long-stalked leaves with scalloped margins. Small pink-flushed white flowers are borne in lax panicles from early summer

A bushy plant with broadly oval light yellowish-green leaves heavily blotched with reddish-brown, and sprays of small pale pink flowers in late spring
A bushy rhizomatous evergreen perennial to 20cm in height, with large, ovate, green-veined, bronze leaves, red beneath and with hairy, frilled margins, and large cymes of small pink flowers

A tuberous perennial with divided leaves and open racemes of slender-spurred pale pink flowers, tipped with purple on inner petals, in spring

A tall plant with flowers to 15cm across, with narrow, quilled rose-pink florets, the inner florets paler
A tuberous perennial producing 11cm wide white flowers flushed with pale purple-pink. It grows to 1m and has very dark, bronze-green foliage

An herbaceous perennial to 75cm in height, with glaucous green foliage and erect stems with up to 4 bright yellow flowers, the haft with brown veins and the falls a central blotch of deep reddish brown

A tender evergreen perennial, with a bushy habit and scented, lobed green leaves marked with bronze in the centre. Produces clusters of dark pink flowers with dark red markings, from late spring to late summer

A clump-forming perennial to 40cm high with heart-shaped, lobed leaves up to 10cm across. Tiny pale pink flowers are borne on erect, wiry stems above the mound of foliage in late spring and early summer

A fairly short, bedding dahlia to about 50cm with dark, bronzed foliage. Semi-double flowers in a wide range of colours, including red, pink, white, yellow and orange, are produced from mid-summer until frosted in autumn
An evergreen to semi-evergreen fern forming a vase-shaped clump of whorled, upright to slightly arching, green fronds divided into narrowly lance-shaped to oblong, lobed leaflets or pinnae.

A dual purpose apple tree showing good resistance to scab and bearing heavy crops of large, ribbed, greenish-yellow fruits flushed red on the side exposed to the sun. Apples produce a mild bittersweet juice and will keep well in cold storage for two months
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and near white flowers to 15cm across in summer

A slow-growing evergreen shrub, to about 1.5m high, with long, leathery green leaves. Produces large clusters of up to 18 white to very pale purple flowers with a contrasting dark red blotch, in late spring
A twining, woody-based perennial, often grown as an annual, with triangular-ovate leaves and salver-shaped, rich orange flowers 4cm across in summer
A bulbous perennial up to 25cm tall, with a single flower per stem. Flowers have creamy-white perianth segments and a lemon-yellow trumpet

A perennial forming a clump of oblong dark green leaves and branched stems bearing small, slate-blue flower-heads with narrow bracts

A herbaceous perennial up to 40cm high with deciduous strap-shaped green leaves and white flowerheads, which are larger than usual for a dwarf Agapanthus, in summer

A fast-growing, spreading culinary herb to around 30cm in height, with aromatic, semi-evergreen, dark green toothed foliage which develops a purple tinge if exposed to cooler night-time temperatures. The leaves have a sweetly intense flavour and contain camphor, but may be used sparingly in drinks and fruit salads
A vigorous, deciduous, self-clinging climber, with large, 3-lobed leaves to 25cm across. In autumn the leaves turn dark red and purple
Deciduous climber about 2.4m tall, with mid-green leaves and small, single, cup-shaped, ivory-white flowers to 10cm across with creamy-yellow anthers, flowering from late spring to late summer
Upright perennial to 1.5m tall forming clumps of large, broad apple-green leaves. From midsummer into autumn, stout stems bear iris-like spikes of yellow-edged, rich red velvety flowers

A bulbous herbaceous perennial with upright, lance-shaped mid-green leaves and arching stems of tubular, pink-flushed orange-salmon flowers which appear from summer until autumn

description: A compact, upright perennial usually grown as an annual, with oval leaves and dense spikes of tubular scarlet flowers with large red bracts, over a long period in summer and autumn

Vigorous, bushy rose about 90cm tall, with glossy green foliage and bearing loosely cupped, very fragrant, perfect rose-pink, fully double blooms blushed darker salmon, to 9cm across, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn
A clump-forming perennial, to around 60cm high, with deeply lobed green leaves. Slender stems bear velvety, vivid purple-pink flowers with dark centres from early to late summer

alternative_names: pelican flower|poisonous hogweed|swan flower|Aristolochia sturtevantii hort.|Aristolochia gigas

An evergreen shrub to 90cm tall, with neat, aromatic, light green leaves and and magenta-pink tubular flowers from mid summer to late autumn

An unusual rhizomatous perennial up to 150cm in height. The green leaves emerge in spring like a closed umbrella covered in silky hairs, opening out into deeply divided, circular leaves. Insignificant, semi-tubular, mauve flowers appear at the top of tall, upright stems in late summer

A clump-forming, upright perennial, to around 85cm high in flower, with narrowly sword-shaped, slightly grey-green leaves. Flowers have short, rich purple standards, and broad, pale purple falls with darker purple veining

Compact climbing rose about 1.8-2.4m tall, with thorny stems and small, healthy, semi-glossy, mid-green leaves. Small clusters of large, shapely, sweetly scented, golden-yellow fully double blooms, deeper in colour towards the centre, produced freely and repeatedly from early summer to autumn
Grows to 40cm with large, hairy dark green leaves wtih a peppery citrus scent, and clusters of mauve-pink flowers, each upper petal with a black blotch, the lower ones with a cerise blotch

An erect, woody-based perennial to 1m tall, with aromatic silvery-grey leaves to 15cm long, finely divided into very slender lobes, and slender sprays of small, dull yellow flower heads in late summer

Clump-forming perennial to about 80cm tall, with bright green lance-shaped leaves, and from summer to autumn bearing dark buds opening to rich, deep golden yellow funnel-shaped flowers, the inner petals bright yellow with brown streaks

Semi-evergreen to evergreen tree about 17m tall, with pale grey to creamy coloured bark and hairy branchlets. Oval, leathery, dark green leaves are 40cm long or more. Produces panicles of yellowish male flowers and single female flowers on the same tree, during summer, followed by large yellow or reddish, ovoid fruits that release winged seeds
A compact deciduous shrub with bluntly toothed, grey-green leaves paler beneath, and clusters of vivid blue flowers opening from deep indigo-blue buds in late summer.

Small evergreen shrub to about 1m tall, with a rounded habit and oval, very spiny glossy dark green leaves to 3cm long. Small white flowers in late spring and early summer are followed by small red berries that appear in the autumn if pollinated by a male holly plant. Suitable for bonsai

A mid-season dessert apple with a russet-textured yellow and red skin with soft but firm and chewy flesh and a rich, sweet, nutty pear-like flavour. The pale, white-green early foliage, white spring blossom and neat habit make this ideal as a garden specimen and for smaller gardens. It is self sterile, pollination group 3, crops in September and stores to December and sometimes even January

A very early-season dual purpose apple, with a heavily ribbed shape, pale yellow-green skin maturing to yellow, and tender flesh with a sweet flavour. Ready for harvest in early September. Requires a group 3, 4 or 5 pollinator
A herbaceous perennial, up to 45cm high, with green leaves and bright yellow circular flowers, 6cm across, in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 46cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and small, purple flowers that have a deeper purple eye-zone above a green throat to 9cm across in summer

A tall deciduous shrub, the pinnate leaves with broad leaflets, with bright golden-yellow flowers in summer and autumn
A bulbous perennial, to 15cm high, with glossy green leaves streaked and mottled with silver. In spring, upright stems bear nodding, very pale yellow flowers with swept-back petals

An upright herbaceous perennial growing to about 80cm with dark green leaves, stems and buds. The fragrant flowers are pale, pearly pink

Dense heads of rounded, multi-toned yellow flowers which change shade as they mature, appear from late spring into summer and through to the first frosts. Great for patio containers and hanging baskets or as ground cover in beds and borders. Heat and drought-tolerant once established
A palm-like erect evergreen shrub with reflexed, sword-shaped green leaves, broadly margined white

Greenish-yellow catkins in spring are followed by clusters of brown acorns about 2cm long
A compact perennial to around 50cm tall with rounded umbels of large white flowers on short, sturdy stems from mid to late summer
Grows to 1.3m in height, with deep crimson flowers 15cm in width from late summer

Large deciduous tree commonly known as the zebra beech, eventually reaching about 30m tall, with unusually patterned leaves that have green veins separated by yellow-green sections between the veins, giving a striped or ‘zebra’ effect, the colouring most visible close up. The leaves turn copper-brown in autumn
An evergreen succulent perennial to 25cm with rosettes of erect, mahogany-red leaves green at the base; reddish-pink flowers yellow within, borne in an arching raceme

A tall, upright, annual plant with green, strappy leaves. Flower spikes are covered in small greenish-brown flowers, ageing to dark brown. Can be grown in the UK as a bedding plant, providing height and structure in bedding displays
Makes a compact clump of ruffled, brownish-red leaves 10cm long, with purple undersides and tall sprays of small white flowers in early summer

An early-season dessert apple characterised by its deep pink spring blossom and small to medium-sized fruits with skins entirely washed dark red and red-stained flesh with sweet to tart, mild flavour. Apples do not store well
A spreading, semi-deciduous perennial, to 30cm tall, with narrow leaves and pink flowers, each 2cm across, borne in long racemes in summer and into autumn
A Tazetta daffodil with spreading foliage and up to 5 fragrant flowers per stem, each 4.5 cm in width with light yellow perianth segments and orange corona

Nonstop Series form neat plants with green foliage and double flowers from late spring/early summer onwards. They come in range of flower colours: white, red, yellow, orange, pink

Numerous, outward facing, white, bell-shaped, single flowers are borne on short stalks sitting just above its foliage providing a long flowering display in summer. An easy to grow plant that dislikes wet winters
Bears a profusion of pansy-shaped flowers throught the growing season. Lower petals are white at the centre, spreading outwards to pale pink. Upper petals are cerise, edged with pink

A dense, dwarf, clump-forming, deciduous perennial to around 120cm in height, forming rosettes of lance-shaped, dark green bristly foliage. Creamy-white, pincushion flowers which may develop a blue tint in cooler conditions, appear on short stems above the foliage from June through to October, sometimes beyond if conditions are favourable

A vigorous, spreading, sturdy plant, with erect green foliage to 106cm tall. Flower stems are erect, straight, to 140cm, usually with 3 medium-large flowers held well above the leaves. Standards are cupped, erect, velvety, violet with violet veining. Falls are circular, flaring, with slightly creped margins, violet blue becoming darker violet then yellow with violet veins towards the base, with a yellow-grey signal

Vigorous herbaceous perennial to 90cm tall, with dark green, 3-lobed, toothed leaves. Irregularly shaped, semi-double, rose-pink flowers with up to 7 overlapping petals edged dark pink, surround a central boss of yellow stamens, from late summer to late autumn
A hardy, evergreen shrub with a compact, bushy habit approximately 21-25cm tall with a spread to 31-45cm. It has dark green foliage and spikes of double white flowers in summer through to autumn.
Grows to 90cm in height, with white, double flowers 12cm in width, with rather broad, overlapping florets

An upright perennial grown as an annual, with lance-shaped silvery green foliage, hairy on the reverse, and slender racemes of small white lipped flowers in summer and autumn.
A vigorous perennial with yellowish-green leaves and stems to 45cm, bearing up to 4 flowers, the standards and falls very pale yellow with greenish-yellow veining, the falls with an orange beard

Clump-forming perennial about 90cm tall, with lance-shaped mid-green leaves, and bearing large clusters of greenish-white flowers, the outer petals with a central deep purple blotch, the inner ones with a brown-flecked yellow flush in the throat

Very free-flowering English rose about 1-1.2m tall, with healthy dark green leaves, tinted crimson when young.
