a small, long-lived deciduous fern 20-30cm in height, with softly hairy, simply pinnate light green fronds, the pinnae slightly sickle-shaped

A compact, deciduous, bushy shrub to around 45cm tall and wide with dark green foliage. Single flowers with green tips, pale pink sepals and a white corolla veined with pink appear from summer into the autumn
A robust, clump-forming perennial to 80cm tall with arching, narrow leaves and branched stems bearing several deep purple-blue flowers with white-yellow stripes and veining in summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to 80cm in height, with dark green, divided foliage and single flowers with large, lustrous, pinkish-red petals and a central mass of yellow stamens in late spring and early summer

Compact, deciduous climber to 2.4m tall, with mid-green leaves, and single ice-blue flowers to 14cm across, with deeper blue margins, and purplish stamens, flowering from late spring to early summer and again in late summer

Clump-forming, herbaceous perennial about 90cm tall, with lance-shaped mid-green leaves, and from summer to autumn produces clusters of large, pale yellow funnel-shaped flowers tipped white, the inner petals are a deeper yellow, streaked and flecked with dark brown
A deciduous perennial to 1.2m tall, with aromatic foliage and whorls of reddish-purple flowers above deep purple bracts

A rounded, deciduous shrub about 100cm in height, with glossy mid-green leaves. Clusters of free-flowering, single, bright red flowers with yellow anthers are produced in spring on bare branches, followed, in autumn, by aromatic green fruits ripening to bright yellow. These can be used to make jams and jellies but please see notes on toxicity for further advice

A compact, ornamental grass, forming small semi-evergreen cushions of very fine, needle-like bright yellow-green leaves, becoming greener in winter. From late spring to summer it bears narrow, bristly yellow-green flower plumes that turn golden-brown

primary_name: Rhus × pulvinata (Autumn Lace Group) 'Red Autumn Lace'

alternative_names: heather 'Mrs Parris Red'|Erica erigena 'Mrs Parris' Red'

A dessert cultivar producing medium-sized fruits with a thick skin that ripens to yellow and is prone to cracking. The yellowish firm and crisp flesh is juicy and sweet with a hint of aniseed flavour
Forms a compact, dense mound of green, slightly waved, narrowly-oval leaves with a white margin to around 20cm high. Purple flowers are borne on upright stems to around 35cm tall in summer

A medium-large, very late, bittersweet, vintage, cider apple with high tannin and high sugar, capable of making a balanced, single-cultivar cider. Fruit has a very dark, purple-red flush over green skin, and is ready to harvest in late autumn. Requires a group 3, 4 or 5 pollinator
A trailing tender evergreen perennial, ivy-leaved pelargonium with mid-green rounded, lobed foliage and clusters of abundant very pale pink to white flowers with magenta centres in summer.

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 45cm high. Leaves are broadly ovate and slightly twisted, and bright green with a narrow cream margin and deeply impressed veins. Produces loose clusters of trumpet-shaped, fragrant, pale purple flowers on upright stems to almost a metre high in summer

A summer-dormant perennial autumn-flowering bulb with large terminal umbels of wavy-petalled funnel-shaped fuchsia-pink flowers followed by the growth of varigated foliage with a creamy edge and metalic sheen in autumn once the temperature drops.

An upright perennial, to around 90cm high, with thin, lance-shaped green leaves. Late flowering, producing rounded clusters of fragrant dark pink flowers from late summer into early autumn

A climber 2.5-3m high with green leaves and flowers, 8-15cm across, composed of five or six overlapping, wavy-edged, dark blue-violet sepals, and pale yellow anthers on green-white filaments, from midsummer to autumn; many clematis are visited by bees for pollen, and some also provide nectar
A clump-forming evergreen perennial to 45cm in height, with strap-shaped leaves and erect stems bearing racemes of tubular green, yellow, orange or red flowers 5cm in length
An upright evergreen shrub, to 3m in height, with dark green foliage and mid-pink, semi-double flowers from mid to late spring
A clump-forming, deciduous grass to 1.5m tall, with narrow, arching leaves green to start with turning orange-brown in autumn. Upright red to dark red flowers turn silver-white through the winter

A vigorous, lax perennial, grown as an annual, with divided, blue-green leaves and bright yellow flowers 6-8cm wide

An herbaceous perennial to 70cm in height with glaucous foliage and up to four large flowers, the standards white tinged with pale lemon-yellow, the falls similar with greenish veins by the white beards
A compact perennial bulb, to around 30cm high in flower, with broadly lance shaped, greyish-green leaves mottled with purple, and bright scarlet flowers
A rare, exotic woody perennial with a bushy habit to around 60cm in height, with smooth, glossy green leaves. Vibrant, red-orange flowers appear from summer through until the autumn

A shrub-like begonia to 60cm with ovate, dark green leaves to 20cm long, clothed in soft, felty hairs, with red undersides. Loose clusters of white flowers are borne on red stems in spring and summer

An early-season, multi-purpose apple, traditionally used for cider but also for cooking and eating. Fruits have yellow skin flushed with red, and are ready to harvest from August. Requires a group 1, 2 or 3 pollinator

description: Stricta Group are narrowly columnar, evergreen conifers with dense, dark green foliage in short sprays on erect branches

A very slow-growing conifer forming a broadly ovoid dwarf shrub with rigid, deep green needles

description: Pumilio Group are spreading, low, bushy evergreen conifers making small shrubs with dark green needles to 4cm long, and small, ovoid, brown cones
Aurea Group consist of slow-growing, small, evergreen trees, the foliage bright golden-yellow in winter and spring, later dull blue-green

primary_name: Rhododendron sanguineum subsp. sanguineum var. haemaleum 'Phantom Rock'

description: A dediduous, bulbous perennial with strap-like dark green leaves and pollen-free, double yellow flowers with a handful of dark red speckles. Flowers are upward and outward-facing and appear in June and July. Ideal for cutting, pots and containers or borders

An Asiatic hybrid lily, a bulbous herbaceous perennial about 0.8-1m high, with alternate, mid-green leaves and strong stems of upward-facing, bowl-shaped double flowers, either cream edged with red, or red and green, in midsummer; the cream colouring becomes more green in hotter weather

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing a clump of small, oval-shaped pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb is covered in thin sheaths and carries one, up to 50cm long and 5cm wide, leathery, elliptic leaf. In autumn, flowering stems emerge from the base of the pseudobulbs. Each stem carries single, 15-20cm large, unusual flower. Petals are thin white and curled, giving the flower its attractive appearance. Mature plants grown in optimal conditions often produce large numbers of flowering stems, flowering simultaneously

primary_name: Euphorbia characias subsp. characias 'Perry's Winter Blusher'
alternative_names: Euphorbia wulfenii 'Winter Blusher'|Euphorbia characias subsp. wulfenii 'Perry's Winter Blusher'

A tuberous perennial producing a single flower in summer consisting of a shiny, red-purple spathe and tall, paddle-like, brown spadix. It has an unpleasant smell to attract pollinating flies.After the flower has faded a single, highly divided leaf appears with bright green leaflets and a stout, olive-green stem with white markings
An annual succulent with masses of green, glaucous oval-shaped foliage which develops purple at the edges as it matures or in cooler conditions. May produce orange flowers throughout the year
A vigorous cultivar reaching a height of up to 1.8. Showy and fragrantcream-pink flowersappear in thesummer all the way through until the autumn

A vigorous clump-forming perennial to 40cm, with stems bearing up to 4 flowers, the standards very pale, translucent yellow with golden shading, the falls bright yellow fading outwards to very pale yellow at the margin
A vigorous annual climber to 1.7m, with strongly fragrant pale violet-blue flowers 4cm across

alternative_names: London pride 'Clarence Elliott'|Saxifraga 'Elliott's Variety'|Saxifraga 'Clarence Elliott' (_umbrosa_ var. _primuloides_)|Saxifraga urbium primuloides 'Elliott's Variety'
description: A resilient evergreen perennial forming a pad of small rosettes of toothed, spoon-shaped fleshy green leaves with short, slender red stems up to 20cm in height, covered with small, pink-white, delicate star-shaped flowers, in May to June

primary_name: Saxifraga rotundifolia subsp. chrysospleniifolia var. rhodopea (12)

description: An annual climber, up to around 1.8m high, with curling tendrils and pairs of green leaves. Scented flowers, with upper petals marbled with rosy pink and a pale, near white keel, are produced in summer
A vigorous, annual climber to around 180cm in height, with curling tendrils and pairs of grey-green leaves. Strongly fragranced white flowers tinged with blue-purple are produced in summer

alternative_names: late spider orchid|black spider orchid|Ophrys arachnites

description: A vigorous, branching, upright perennial to 238cm, with medium to small pale green leaves. Main spikes to 100cm long, with a few strong side spikes. Flowers fully double, to 5.5cm across, giving a frilled appearance, pale violet blue, inner petals with yellow-green stripes

A clump-forming, bulbous perennial to around 20cm in height with wide, glossy mid-green foliage. Tight clusters of white, star-shaped flowers with green stripes on the reverse and yellow centres appear from May to June. Multiply fairly quickly so they are great for naturalising

alternative_names: Cheng fir|Abies forrestii var. chengii|Abies fargesii misapplied

description: A large evergreen conifer tree. Crown is columnar, broadening with age. Featured for its distinct, leathery needles up to 9cm long and 4mm wide that spread on both side of the shoots. Young shoots are pale yellowish-green, maturing to dark green. Vegetative buds are chestnut-brown, slighlty resinous. Immature seed cones are bluish-purple, maturing to brown, 10-14cm long and 4cm wide.

A wide-spreading herbaceous perennial to 30cm in height, with fragrant leaves splashed and margined cream, often heavily red-flushed and with dense spikes of small white flowers in late spring. The foliage is crinkled and deeper in colour than the similarly-marked H. 'Chameleon'
A large, rounded to spreading, deciduous tree with lobed green leaves that are reddish-purple beneath. Yellow-green catkin-like flowers in spring are followed by bunches of winged seeds.
A compact courgette variety producing high yields of dark green 'baby' fruits between July and October. Attractive golden-yellow flowers can be harvested and used in cooking

A vigorous variety with an erect, open habit producing attractive, edible yellow flowers in Summer followed by glossy, slightly speckled, mid-green courgettes that have a superb flavour and no bitterness. It will crop prolifically throughout the Summer with regular harvesting

A large, vigorous annual, 1.2m tall and wide, producing a short, fleshy, horizontal stem and large, deeply lobed, dark green leaves with silver markings. The stems and leaf undersides have sharp bristles. Large, yellow, edible flowers, male and female separate, appear in summer followed by slim, smooth-skinned, cylindrical, yellow fruit eaten as courgettes or summer squash

A compact courgette variety which produces a heavy crop of dark green, cylindrical fruits throughout the Summer. Regular harvesting helps to extend cropping up to the first frost. Harvest from June to October

alternative_names: hardy cloak fern|Gymnogramma marantae|Acrostichum marantae|Notholaena marantae

description: A bushy, free-flowering, upright shrub to about 60cm tall, with single to semi-double flowers having rose-pink tube and sepals with the palest pink corolla, and distinctive upright petaloids, flowering from summer to autumn

Upright, bushy, half-hardy annuals to 90cm, with divided, fern-like leaves. In summer and autumn produce showy, 5-7cm, single or semi-double flowers with slightly pleated petals in yellow, light orange, deep orange and red

An upright, half-hardy annual with finely-divided, green foliage. Stems to 1.2m high bear soft pink to white flowers, with a prominent yellow centre, from summer into autumn; each petal has a darker pink flare at its base fading to pale pink and then white at the petal edge

An upright, half-hardy annual, to around 1m tall, with finely-divided green foliage. The daisy-like flowers, borne from summer into autumn, comprise white petals striped and edged to varying depths with deep pink

A compact, bushy, self-fertile, early-ripening, British-raised nectarine cultivar up to around 3m in height , with long, slender green foliage. Pink flowers appear in spring, followed by sweet and juicy, melt-in-the-mouth yellow fruits, flushed with red. Cropping season: late July. A great variety for smaller spaces in a pot or container, and the fruit is perfect for bottling or making into pies and jams

A summer cabbage variety producing compact, round, shiny, green heads that stand well without splitting. It has an exceptionally sweet flavour, perfect for summer salads and stir fries. Harvest between June and October
A tender, perennial vegetable with compact, upright green leaves, producing waxy white flesh tubers in summer. Shows good resistance to slugs

A heritage, first early potato bred in 1942 with an excellent flavour. It is a good all-rounder, but particularly good boiled or as a salad potato. The deep red skin and pale, yellow, floury flesh make it an attractive variety to grow. It is generally preferred to the original Duke of York variety due to it being more vigorous, having larger tubers and a better taste. It has quite low disease resistance but its taste and looks still make it a popular variety

Forming good sized tubers, which have a smooth skin and a creamy white flesh, these fast-growing potatoes are ready to harvest early in the season. This is a sought after variety if you are growing for the shows, and it also has a good resistance to drought, heat, potato viruses and bruising

This traditional second early, bred over 100 years ago in Scotland, is easy to grow and produces a uniform crop with good yields. The tubers are oval, white skinned with white flesh and have a floury texture and delicious flavour. Suitable for all cooking uses but cook with skins on to retain the flavour

A popular second early salad variety which produces good yields of uniform potatoes. Tubers are oval, have yellow, smooth skin with a creamy-yellow flesh and a waxy texture. They are delicious hot or cold. Shows some resistance to potato blackleg

A perennial vegetable with branching stems, compound leaves, white flowers and green berries, forming swollen, waxy, edible tubers harvested in summer. This is a second early potato with pale yellow skin, firm flesh and fantastic flavour. Shows good resistance to eelworm

A second early that produces a high yield of attractive and uniform tubers. It’s firm flesh has a slightly sweet taste and is ideal for baking but is also suitable for boiling and chipping. The tubers are smooth, white skinned with cream coloured flesh and show some resistance to potato cyst nematodes and scab

A second early variety of potato which is fairly rare within the UK but more popular in France. Tubers are smooth with dark red skin and yellow, sometimes pink waxy flesh. A creamy, buttery flavour and good for potato salad

primary_name: Bupleurum salicifolium subsp. salicifolium var. salicifolium

description: A large-flowered Spencer cultivar with lightly-fragrant flowers of reddish-orange borne through summer

alternative_names: snow pea|edible-podded pea|mangetout|sugar pea|sugar snap pea
description: The subspecies of pea which has given rise to all the peas which have edible pods, 'eat all' or 'mange tout' in French. They include the flattened pods and the thick, fleshy pods often called snap peas. It is a green-leaved annual which climbs using tendrils. The flowers are white, pink or mauve and develop into green pods containing green peas
A dwarf pea to 75cm. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils. The flowers are white and develop into pods containing a good crop of peas in summer. It is an annual which lives for one summer.

A dwarf pea to 60cm which produces peas suitable for eating fresh or for drying and storage. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils. The flowers are white and develop into pods containing a heavy crop of peas. It is an annual which lives for one summer.

A medium-height pea to 80cm. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils. The flowers are white and develop into pods containing a heavy crop of peas. It is an annual which lives for one summer. This variety shows some resistance to Fusarium

A tall pea to 2m which produces peas suitable for showing in competition. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils. The flowers are white and develop into long pods containing a heavy crop of peas. It is an annual which lives for one summer.

alternative_names: capsicum|cayenne pepper|paprika|red pepper|sweet pepper|Capsicum annuum var. acuminatum

description: An evergreen shrub featuring soft, grey-green, feathery foliage and elegant arching branches. In late winter to spring, it bursts into clusters of bright golden-yellow, ball-shaped flowers that attract pollinators. Hardy and drought-tolerant, it thrives in full sun and well-drained soil, making it ideal for ornamental gardens and screening

Deciduous tree, to around 2m high in 10 years, and up to 5m high at maturity. It has a shrubby habit and is often grown as a multi-stem plant, with broadly oval, glossy green leaves. Masses of large, scented, star-shaped white flowers, flushed with pink in the base and each with up to 25 petals, are produced before the leaves in spring

A vigorous, fast-growing, early-cropping F1 hybrid, up to 60cm high, with an open habit, with thick-walled, very sweet fruits up to 10cm long, which ripen to deep orange, sometimes with green streaks. Sweet bell peppers, Capsicum annuum var. annuum (Grossum Group), are bushy annuals with ovate to lanceolate green leaves up to 12cm long, and white starry flowers in summer followed by bell-shaped, glossy fruits which turn from green to yellow, orange, or red.

primary_name: Capsicum annuum var. annuum (Grossum Group) 'Cuneo Giallo'
description: A compact, Italian heirloom sweet pepper variety producing large, square yellow fruits with a slightly pointed end. It is very productive and has a great crunch and flavour for using in salads and cooking
A round cabbage, green with pink-purple tinges, which stands well into winter for late harvesting

A dwarf, bulbous perennial, to 15cm in height, with narrow, erect leaves. Flowers appear in late winter to early spring and are pale-blue, with each fall marked with a central yellow band edged with white and dark-blue speckles
A rhizomatous perennial, 75-100 cm high, with glaucous leaves and scented, ruffled flowers in early summer. Flower have soft apricot standards, soft lavender falls and bright orange beards
A vigorous annual climber to 1.7m, with strong pink flowers 5.5cm across, fading to a lighter tone; scent slight

A tuberous, frost-tender perennial growing to 1.8m tall. Large, heart-shaped leaves to 60cm long are held on purple-black stems. The leaves emerge green then darken with age to a deep purple-black colour

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 50cm high, with slightly glaucous, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers from early to mid spring, producing solitary, double triangle shaped flowers to 9cm across, with yellow outer petals and a large, yellow cup with an orange rim

A large-cupped daffodil to 60cm high, with grey-green, strap-shaped leaves to 50cm long. Produces single flowers to 10cm across, with golden yellow perianth segments and yellow trumpets, in early to mid-spring
Fl. brilliant greenish yellow 3A; perianth segments smooth; corona cylindrical, with mouth slightly expanded and rim entire. Early

A robust trumpet daffodil to 50cm tall, with flowers to 12cm across in early and mid spring, the lemon-yellow perianth segments broadly ovate and overlapping, the trumpet white, with a widely flanged and notched rim

A large-flowered gladiolus, 1.2m high, with green leaves and spikes 55-60cm tall of 19 buds, of which 7 or 8 are open at one time, the flowers deep smoky-red fading to bronze-red, from midsummer to late summer

A large-flowered gladiolus, around 1.5m high, with green sword like leaves and a flower spike with around 10-14 flower buds. The large flowers are a mid to pale lavender-purple, fading to almost pure white deep inside their throats. An elegant gladioli for the summer garden

A large-flowered gladiolus, maximum height 1 - 1.5m, with green sword like leaves and an erect upright flower spike with around 10 -15 flower buds. The flowers have a satin like appearance and are a soft coral pink with a paler throat, and a cream splotch with a red mark on the inner bottom lip

A tall, herbaceous perennial to 2m or more, with green leaves and small, yellow sunflowers in late summer-autumn. It is grown for its edible roots which are smoother and thin-skinned compared to the species type

A dwarf, floriferous herbaceous perennial to around 150cm in height, with coarse dark green leaves. Bright yellow, sunflower-like flowers appear in summer. It is cultivated for its knobbly, elongated pale-cream or sometimes purple-tinted tubers
A large-flowered gladiolus, up to 1.5m tall, with green sword like leaves and flower spike with up to12 flower buds, large purple velvety blooms with crimson throats, striking blooms for the summer
Grows to 1.8m, with long stems bearing strongly fragrant flowers 6cm across, the standards deep reddish-purple, the wing petals vivid purplish-red

A small, angular tree with a stem which lies flat on the ground, with horizontal main branches to 3-4m in height. Leaves green with occasional bronze tints and good autumn colour. Petal-like broad, overlapping bracts, white tinged pink at maturity surround a greenish flower head. Red strawberry-like fruits appear in autumn.

Upright, evergreen, multi-stemmed shrub or small tree about 5m tall with leathery, toothed dark green leaves to 20cm long, and upright panicles of fragrant, white flowers in summer that are very attractive to bees

primary_name: Sanguinaria canadensis f. multiplex 'Paint Creek Double' (d)

alternative_names: heath bedstraw|briwydden wen|Galium montanum Huds.|Galium hercynicum

description: A dwarf Lilliput dahlia to 40cm tall, with single, light lemon yellow flowers 5cm across in late summer and autumn; ideal for containers

Vigorous, bushy rose to about 1m tall with healthy, shiny, dark green foliage and bearing sweetly-fragrant blooms in blended colours of coral, tangerine-orange and copper, in big, upright trusses of full-petalled flowers, produced repeatedly through summer and autumn
Vigorous, compact ground cover rose, about 40-60cm tall, with healthy, dark green foliage. Small, very double, rounded crimson-red blooms, with a light fragrance, repeat-flower from summer to autumn

An upright, well-branched rose to about 1.2m tall, with small, glossy, dark green leaves. Large clusters of very lightly scented, semi-double purplish-red blooms to 5cm across, have a white reverse and white centre, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn
A bushy, upright, hybrid tea rose, to 1m tall, with dark green foliage and large, fully double, high-centred, mildly fragrant, red flowers in summer and autumn
Reaches around 90cm in height. It bears double, scented flowers in a warm peachy apricot through summer and autumn

A bushy, upright rose to 90cm tall, with mid to dark green foliage and abundant clusters of fragrant, single blooms splashed and streaked red on a white and blush-pink background, often creamy-yellow in the centre, repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

Vigorous, bushy, upright hybrid tea rose to 1m tall, with plentiful healthy, glossy, dark green leaves and bearing subtly-fragrant, apricot-salmon high-centred blooms produced in flushes over a long period from summer into autumn
An old-fashioned pink,with narrow, evergreen, blue-grey foliage andclove-scented, double, pale pink flowers striped and flecked with red, from early summer
A dwarf, rosette-forming evergreen perennial to around 5cm with small, spoon-shaped, finely toothed mid-green leaves and small pale to dark lavender-purple flowers appearing in the spring

A deciduous climber, to around 3.5m high, with divided, irregularly toothed green leaves. Medium sized pale pink flowers, with textured petals with ruffled edges and recurved tips, are produced in the leaf axils in late summer

A vigorous, medium-sized deciduous climber. The first flush of flowers in late spring are usually double or semi-double with the second in late summer being single and sometimes paler in colour. All flowers are pale pink, each petal with a dark-pink central band and the central boss is made up of creamy-white to pale yellow anthers

A deciduous bushy perennial with dark green leaves. Small, hyacinth-like bell-shaped very pale blue to white flowers and yellow stamens, which turn more star-shaped as they mature, appear from July through to September. This variety scrambles rather than climbs

An evergreen, perennial, border auricula up to 20cm tall with rosettes of pale grey-green leaves. Clusters of fragrant, reddish-orange flowers with white centres and yellow-green eyes are produced on short stems in spring
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with pale green, toothed foliage and fragrant, velvety dark red flowers with white centres and a yellow eye, which appear in early spring

An evergreen, perennial, border auricula up to 20cm tall with rosettes of pale grey-green leaves. Clusters of fragrant, pale yellow flowers with white centres and pale yellow eyes are produced on short stems in spring

A rosette-forming perennial to 90cm high with spiny, narrowly oblong leaves up to 40cm long with woolly-white undersides. Erect, branching stems bear clusters of yellow flowerheads in summer, each up to 10cm across with paler yellow centres and surrounded by spiny bracts
An evergreen, perennial, double auricula up to 20cm tall with rosettes of pale grey-green leaves. Clusters of fully double, coppery-orange, fragrant flowers are produced on short stems in spring
An erect herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular pure white flowers with a deep pink eye over a long period of time in summer.

A small to medium-sized, hardy heritage cooking variety with green foliage and pale green fruit ripening to soft yellow with pure white flesh. A very productive variety which can be harvested from early September to October. Does not keep well. Suitable for colder areas
Compact, neat little rose to about 50-60cm tall with dark green foliage and lightly-scented, pinkish-red blooms produced through summer and autumn

A large, mid-season dessert apple, with a round, flattened shape, and golden yellow skin with an orange flush and scattered patches of russet. Flesh is crisp with a sharp sweet flavour. A vigorous tree, with an upright then spreading habit and serrated leaves. Triploid, requires a group 3 or 4 pollinator

An evergreen, scrambling vine up to 4.5m high with two leaf forms: flowering shoots bear ovate, unlobed leaves whilst non-flowering shoots bear spearhead-shaped leaves up to around 8cm long and lobed at the base. Small, hanging flowers borne singly or rarely in pairs have pink outer segments and white inner ones and may be followed by rounded, berry-like red fruits

A compact, upright deciduous shrub with narrowly ovate dark green leaves, flushed purple in spring and in autumn. A Japanese cultivar with flattened lacecap flowerheads of white sterile flowers with deep red edges and fertile flowers of pinkish-white

A compact, upright deciduous shrub with pointed dark green leaves flushed crimson when young and in autumn. A Japanese cultivar with rounded flowerheads of double blue (pink in more alkaline soils) ray florets neatly arranged around the frothy fertile flowers

A slow-growing, deciduous shrub to 70cm high, with narrowly ovate, serrated green leaves that are tinted with purple and bronze, and turn red and orange in autumn. In summer, loose lace-cap type flower heads bear clusters of tiny cream-coloured fertile flowers, with larger, double white florets held on short, delicate stems around the edges. Flowers may be spotted with pink as they age
An early season dessert apple bearing medium to large green fruits with reddish-orange striping. The sharp flesh sweetens with storage

A mid-season, dessert apple with yellow-green skin strongly flushed and striped with red, and soft, juicy, cream flesh with a sharp flavour. A heavy-cropping, vigorous tree, requiring a group 3, 4 or 5 pollinator. Fruit is ready to pick in early autumn and stores for a few weeks

A small, French dessert cultivar introduced in 1990 up to 6m in height, with a rounded habit and dark green foliage. White flowers in spring are followed by a heavy crop of bright red and green fruits which are ready for harvesting in September to October. Fruits are crisp, sweet and tangy. Pollination group 3 and not self-fertile

Shrub or small tree about 4m tall, with yellowish-green young branchlets becoming reddish-brown with age and softly-hairy, narrow dark green leaves to 20cm long turn yellow in autumn. Small umbels of 4-7 yellow flowers appear just before the leaves in spring, and black berries follow on female plants if pollinated by a male plant

A bulbous perennial to 15cm, with broad, glaucous leaves and solitary nodding white flowers with oval outer segments 2cm in length, and shorter inner ones bearing a green V-shaped mark at the tip, in late winter
An upright, clump-forming, semi-evergreen fern bearing, glossy, green fronds with narrow, widely-spaced leaflets (pinnae) with distinctive forked tips

A low-growing, clump-forming perennial to around 15cm tall with kidney-shaped, lobed, semi-evergreen leaves 3-6cm long. Pale to medium blue flowers up to 3cm across are freely produced in spring, usually appearing before the emergence of new foliage
A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with oval green leaves with silver spots. Clusters of funnel-shaped flowers appear on upright stems in spring, in shades from coral pink to purple

alternative_names: London pride 'Primuloides'|Saxifraga primuloides|Saxifraga umbrosa var. primuloides
description: A mat-forming evergreen perennial with rosettes of spoon-shaped dark green, scalloped leaves and erect stems to 20cm tall, with panicles of starry white flowers, spotted with red, in summer
A perennial, to 10cm in height, with double greenish-yellow flowers, 3cm in width, from late winter, surrounded by divided leafy bracts. Basal leaves are rich green, divided into several lobes

A lax, branching annual with serrated leaves growing to 1.2m tall and wide. Yellow summer flowers with brown centres are followed by rounded edible fruit to 7cm in diameter surrounded by a thin, paper-like husk; fruits ripen from green to yellow or purple

A variable perennial to 40cm, with a fleshy, running rootstock producing rosettes of narrow, lobed, spiny, dark green leaves 8-20cm long. Upright spikes of pink flowers with green bracts are produced from late spring to late summer

primary_name: Viola odorata 'Double Foncée de Madame Dumas' (d)

alternative_names: Ceylon spinach|East Indian spinach|Indian spinach|Malabar nightshade|Malabar spinach|red Malabar nightshade|Basella rubra
description: A climbing or scrambling perennial that is grown as a summer annual in Britain. Edible leaves are used in similar ways to spinach. Small white flowers, sometimes with purplish tints, make this an attractive addition to a vegetable garden
An evergreen shrub with small, dark green wavy foliage and contrasting dark reddish-brown stems. Ideal for hedging

A evergreen shrub to 4m in height with narrow oval, wavy-edged grey-green leaves that are edged with cream, flushed pink, in all seasons. Scented, dark purple star-shaped flowers are borne from early summer

an evergreen coniferous tree with a tall slender crown in its native habitat. Light green new growth in spring darkens with age over the growing season; needles, up to 4cm long, persist on the branches in 2 or 4 ranks. Male and female cones can appear on the same tree; female cones are almost spherical and male cones catkin-like

alternative_names: Yunnan Daimyo oak|Quercus malachotricha|Quercus yunnanensis|Quercus griffithii var. urticifolia|Quercus aliena var. urticifolia

description: A sprawling, evergreen perennial grown as a bedding plant or under glass. It has rounded leaves, dark red-purple on the underside, yellow with green veins and a green central splash on the upperside. Spikes of small, tubular, two-lipped, pale purple flowers can be produced from spring to autumn

alternative_names: Betula tortuosa|Betula toruasa|Betula pumila var. borealis|Betula pubescens subsp. czerepanovii|Betula borealis|Betula pubescens subsp. tortuosa

primary_name: Crataegus pinnatifida var. major 'Big Golden Star'
alternative_names: hawthorn 'Big Golden Star'|Crataegus viridis 'Big Golden Star'|Crataegus pinnatifida 'Big Gold Star'
description: An upright, spreading, deciduous tree with few or no thorns and shredding bark. The lobed, long-stalked leaves are a glossy, bright green. In early summer bears flattened clusters of white flowers followed by large, edible, shiny, orange-red haws 3cm or more across

A large shrub or small tree to about 3m, with dark green, oval foliage developing bronze tints in autumn. Inconspicuous but nectar-rich green and white flowers in summer are followed by bright pink, four-lobed fruit, splitting to reveal orange seeds and lasting well into winter

an upright, bushy, deciduous, shrub rose, to 1.5m tall, with mid-green foliage. Golden-yellow, semi-double, loosely-cupped flowers are held on long, arching stems and this strongly-scented cultivar repeat flowers from summer into autumn
A compact, bushy evergreen shrub to 60cm high, with small, ovate green leaves. Produces clusters of 2-3 double (hose-in-hose), strong purplish-red flowers in spring

alternative_names: Quercus castaneifolia var. algeriensis|Quercus castaneifolia var. incana
green oak|Mohru oak|Moru oak|Tilonj oak|Quercus dilatata Royle|Quercus glauca misapplied|Quercus dilatata Lindl. ex A.DC.
description: A large, fast-growing evergreen or semi-evergreen tree to 30m. Glossy dark green leaves have serrated eges with small bristles. In spring the male catkins are numerous and quite long, making them more visible than most. The bark is an attractive dark red-brown.

Evergreen tree about 25m tall, native to south-east Queensland, tablelands of NSW and upper Snowy Mountains of Victoria, with rough, greyish or white bark shed annually in ribbons, rounded bluish-grey, juvenile leaves to 11.5cm long and broad, pale slate grey to bluish-grey adult leaves to 15cm long. White flowers appear from early autumn to early winter followed by barrel to urn-shaped, woody fruit

Evergreen tree endemic to coastal SE Australia, about 40m tall, shorter in exposed situations, with rough, furrowed, greyish-brown or reddish-brown bark over trunk and larger branches, the smaller branches are smooth and pale grey. Juvenile leaves to 11cm long and adult leaves, to 16cm long, are dark green, paler beneath. White flowers in umbels, midsummer to autumn are followed by cylindrical woody fruits

A leafy, perennial salad vegetable which looks a bit like a dandelion, with clumps of narrow green leaves, which may develop scalloped edges, and bright yellow flowers with heart-shaped bracts appearing in April to August which are loved by bees. The flowers are followed by fluffy seedheads, like dandelion clocks. The leaves can still be harvested whilst the plant is in flower, and both young and older leaves have a mild and slightly sweet flavour. As a bonus it is also slug-resistant
A bulbous perennial to 50cm with green foliage and slim, lily-shaped pink flowers with white edging and a darker purple base. Flowers appear April to May

A vigorous disease-resistant grape vine suitable for outdoor cultivation, and used for wine-making, juice or as a dessert grape, with a sweet refreshing flavour. Bunches of large dark red grapes mature to blue-black in early autumn. Fresh green leaves turn red and purple in autumn

A medium-sized deciduous climber, up to 3 metres high, with divided green leaves and large bell-like flowers of deep blue with a white edge on the outside and white inside, followed by fluffy seedheads

An upright, bushy shrub with variegated cream and green foliage and single, rose pink flowers, with a darker pink corolla, which appear from summer through to autumn. An ideal variety for showing or for pots and containers

A tender, evergreen perennial to about 40-50cm tall, with softly hairy purple-tinged green stems bearing oblong to ovate pale silvery-green leaves, marked with a dark grey-green herringbone pattern, and purple beneath. White flower spikes may be borne intermittently throughout the year
A compact, semi-evergreen, everbearing variety producing deep pink flowers from late spring through to autumn which are followed by tasty red fruits

A marginal, aquatic or semi-aquatic perennial to 90cm in height, spread by long thin segmented rhizomes, often with reddish-purple stems and very aromatic dark green leaves. Rounded terminal spikes of tiny, fragrant pale purple flowers appear in summer
A highly attractive, vigorous, spreading, perennial herb with striking variegated green leaves with cream margins that have a mild, fruity scent. Clusters of cream-white flowers appear in summer

A vigorous perennial herb, with hairy whitish stems, and aromatic, deeply veined grey-green leaves with toothed edges and a citrus flavour. Spikes of small, pale mauve flowers are produced at the tips of the stems in summer

alternative_names: scaly blazing star|American devil's bit|blazing star

description: A small deciduous tree to about 10m tall, broadly conical in outline. The smaller than average, finely cut, narrowly maple-like leaves, reliably turn shades of yellow, red, orange and violet throughout autumn. Insignificant flowers in late spring are followed by spiky fruit capsules in autumn, which remain on the tree into winter. Older branches take on a corky, winged appearance
An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and orange flowers in summer

Classic hybrid tea rose, with upright growth to about 1.65m in height, with glossy mid-green foliage and fragrant, high-centred, fully double, creamy-white blooms to 12cm across, edged pink which darkens and spreads with age, flowering in flushes from summer to autumn

alternative_names: American parsley fern|mountain parsley fern|Oregon rock brake fern

description: A clump-forming, evergreen fern with yellow-green new growth, darkening with age. Fronds are triangular-shaped and the two lowest pinnnae have elongated leaflets that point downwards.

A bushy tree, with a more upright habit than the species, with ascending then spreading branches. Tight clusters of small white flowers are surrounded by four large creamy-white bracts that become blotched pink with age, followed by deep pink fruit in strawberry-like clusters

A medium-sized, upright, conical tree. The five-lobed leaves are bright green, turning rich red in autumn and maintaining the display for longer than average before falling. Inconspicuous flowers are followed by burr-like fruit that stay on the tree through winter

A compact, rounded tree, often grown as a standard pom pom tree. Leaves are alternate, maple-like and dense and take on brilliant and long-lasting autumn colour. Flowers and fruits are inconspicuous, although fruits are a decorative spiky woody capsule.

alternative_names: Primula 'Barnhaven Old Rose Victoria Selected'|Primula 'Barnhaven Victorians'

description: A medium-sized plant with a neat, upright leaf rosette. Flowers are lavender blue with deep purple veining on the lower lobes and in the throat, stems to 4.8cm.
A rosette-forming perennial with oblong, dark green leaves and sprays of white flowers with heavy violet-blue veining on the lower lobes
A rosette-forming perennial with hairy, oblong leaves and sprays of light mauve-blue flowers with deep purple veining
A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m with dark green foliage. Flowers, in late summer and autumn, are pink shading to lemon yellow in the centre, with quilled petals giving a spiky effect

A compact, slow-growing tropical evergreen shrub, with an upright habit and sparsely branching stems. Leaves are long, arching and sword-shaped, with light green centres edged with white, and dark green margins

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and strawberry-rose-pink coloured flowers with a yellow-green throat to 13cm across in summer
A versatile variegated variety providing all year round interest with its oval-shaped dark green leaves that fade to light green with creamy-white margins and tips.
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 70cm in height, forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and green and white flowers with a green throat to 15cm across in summer.

Bushy spreading English shrub rose about 1.2m tall, with healthy mid-green leaves, producing dainty sprays of small, cupped, double yellow blooms with a light musk fragrance, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

A large, bushy 'English' rose with arching stems that can be left to produce a 1.5m high shrub, or trained as a 3.5m high climbing rose. The flowers, produced in summer and autumn, are fragrant, fully-petalled rosettes in apricot-orange

plant_range: C Himalaya to S China and Indo-China

description: May be grown as a tall shrub or short climber. It produces highly-fragrant, fully-double, shallow-cupped, deep purple-red flowers from early to late summer

A spreading shrub rose about 90cm tall, with thorny stems and plentiful semi-glossy dark green leaves. Clusters of deep pink, very double cupped blooms with a strong, old rose fragrance open almost flat and repeat-flower through summer with occasional blooms in autumn. D. Austin 1999

Mounded, spreading rose to about 1.1m tall with glossy, pale green foliage and large clusters of lightly-scented, pale to warm pink rosette-shaped blooms with a button-eye, repeat-flowering through summer to autumn
A tropical, evergreen perennial forming a rosette of strap-shaped, grey leaves with a dense central head of small purple flowers surrounded by spiky pink bracts which may appear all year round
Clump-forming perennial to 60cm, with mid-green leafy stems bearing clusters of rosy-pink flowers, the outer petals with a purple flare, the inner ones marked with yellow, borne in summer and autumn

An evergreen, perennial bromeliad forming a rosette of glossy, dark-green, lance-shaped leaves to 30cm long. In summer an erect stem to 50cm arises from the centre of the rosette, this is topped with a flame-like inflorescence composed of bright red bracts with yellow tips. This showy flower spike will last for several months, after which the leaf rosette will die. However, new, offset plants may be produced around the parent rosette at this time
A bulbous perennial to around 30cm high, with strap-shaped, glossy leaves. In spring, produces a dense cylindrical spike of fragrant, waxy, bell-shaped, vivid violet coloured flowers

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 20cm tall, with green lance-shaped leaves and clusters of red funnel-shaped flowers which have dark brown speckles and a yellow throat, flowering in summer and autumn

A climbing rose about 3.5m tall with fragrant rosette blooms a rich shade of yellow, the outer petals fading to palest yellow, providing a two-tone effect, and repeat-flowering from summer to autumn; D. Austin 1998
A tropical evergreen tree or shrub, often grown as a houseplant, with slender, arching to weeping stems, and glossy, oval-shaped dark green leaves with long pointed tips
A short-lived perennial usually grown as an annual, with dissected grey-green leaves and daisy-like, yellow-centred, white flower-heads from spring to autumn
A hardy and evergreen shrub with a broad and upright habit and bright green foliage. A bud-bloomer, white buds appear in summer through to autumn.
A hardy evergreen shrub with an erect habit approximately 31-45cm tall with an equal spread. It has mid-green foliage and shell pink buds in summer through to autumn.

A compact, upright, rhizomatous perennial to 30cm in height, with slender dark green leaves to 7cm long. Produces abundant bell-shaped, shell-pink flowers to 2.5cm long, spotted with darker pink dots on the lobes, borne singly or in pairs in summer

A spreading perennial to around 30cm high, with trailing to ascending, hairy stems that root at the nodes, and oval-shaped, hairy green leaves with serrated edges. Pendent clusters of white flowers are produced in late summer and early autumn, initially overlapping like a pine cone before opening to long tubular flowers flared at the tips

A compact perennial forming neat clumps of rounded to kidney-shaped mid green basal leaves. Flower spikes, to 35cm high, have dense, hollyhock-like, silky, pale-pink flowers with fringed petals and are borne from early to late summer
A deciduous herbaceous perennial with large, narrow, pale green leaves and upright stems which produce bright orange-red flowers from midsummer until mid autumn
A compact, dwarf cultivar which flowers freely with large plumes of pink flowers
A decorative dahlia to 90cm with dark green leaves and rich lilac-pink blooms

Bushy, upright rose from the Paramount Collection, about 60-90cm tall, with glossy dark green foliage. Fragrant, large, fully double blooms of purple-mauve 10-15cm across, repeat-flower from eary summer to late in autumn
A compact, bushy plant to 75cm tall, with dark green foliage and pointed buds opening to fragrant, full rich crimson blooms, repeat-flowering through summer and autumn
Dainty, compact rose about 30cm tall and wide, with healthy, small, glossy dark green leaves, and bearing fully double rosette blooms of ginger-orange, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

Compact rose about 60cm tall and wide, with glossy green foliage, and bearing masses of small, very full blush pink double blooms, salmon pink towards the centre, produced over a long period during summer into autumn
A late spray cultivar that reaches around 70cm in height and bears anemone-like white flowers tinged a pale yellow at the centre

A tropical, evergreen perennial to 90cm tall, with lance-shaped leaves to 40cm long. The leaves are white to pale green with irregular dark green blotches; grow in a bright position out of direct sun for the best leaf variegation

An evergreen, weeping fig tree to 4m tall (but usually less), with yellow-green leaves that have irregular dark green markings around the midrib. The brightest colour is on young foliage when positioned in good light
A compact and upright shrub with large dark glossy green, veined leaves. Makes an ideal houseplant providing rich, green foliage and filtering unwanted pollutants from the air.
A superb, early June bearing variety producing exquisite and delicious tasting red fruits in late May and June. Noted for its sweet taste and firm texture, it is prized by top restaurants and chefs

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Large, fragrant white flowers, with ruffled edges at the tips of the petals, are produced in mid to late summer

A compact, clump-forming, evergreen perennial, grown as a housplant for its dark green glossy foliage. Small, sweetly-fragranced, white arum-type flowers appear from spring to autumn. An air-purifying plant which improves levels of humidity within your living space
A perennial bulb, up to 60cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are goblet-shaped, with pointed white petals with a cream-coloured flame

A perennial bulb, to around 40cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, slightly wavy grey-green leaves. Flowers are cup-shaped, with petals deep pink in the centre and fading to white at the edges
A perennial bulb to 40cm with green foliage with golden edging, and dark pink goblet-shaped flowers with white edging appearing in the spring

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial with tall, upright, strap-like green leaves. Wrect stems bear elegant flowers in late spring-early summer with pale purple upper petals, known as standards, and dark purple-black lower petals, known as falls, with yellow beards

A perennial bulb, up to 50cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped grey-green leaves. Flowers are cup shaped, with petals that are deep pink in the centre, fading to ivory white with a fine edge of golden yellow
A perennial bulb to 50cm in height with strappy green leaves and fluted purple-red flowers with a golden yellow edge which appear in the spring
A perennial bulb with light green, lance-shaped leaves. The flowers are creamy-yellow with narrow, red flaming, grow to around 55cm and open in late spring
A perennial bulb, up to 55cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are deep red, with a broad green flame and ruffled orange edges

A bulbous perennial to 45cm with green foliage and goblet-shaped white flowers with splashes of pink which darken as they mature until the whole flower becomes pink. Flowers appear from late April to early May

A perennial bulb, with broadly lance-shaped green leaves with a fine cream margin. This tulip has cup-shaped flowers, sometimes 2 or 3 to a stem, opening primrose yellow with cream margins that are increasingly streaked raspberry pink as the flower matures. Flowers are produced in late spring, and stand to around 60cm high

alternative_names: tulip 'Prinses Irene Parkiet'|Tulipa 'Irene Parrot'|Tulipa 'Princess Irene Parrot'
description: An upright perennial bulb to 35cm in height, with lance-shaped dark green leaves. Vivid orange, strong, ruffled flowers flamed with purple and with a splash of green on the outer petals, appear in April. A sport and parrot tulip version of T. 'Prinses Irene'

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This tulip has large, vibrant orange flowers with reddish pink flaming on the outer petals. Flowers are produced in mid-spring, and stand to around 55cm high
A perennial bulb, to 70cm in height, with grey-green leaves. Flowers, orange with a pink-red flame, appear in late spring
A strong, upright tulip, to 45cm, with long-lasting flowers. The colour is predominantly a clear red, with well-defined yellow edges to the outer tepals. Mid to late spring

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This tulip has fully double, bowl-shaped, pure white flowers that are lightly scented. Flowers are produced in mid-spring, and stand to around 55cm high

A rhizomatous perennial, to 1m high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Late flowering and lightly scented, with pale, smoky purple standards, mauve to violet falls touched with gold at the shoulders, and a yellow-orange beard

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which unlike the typical species, produces a compact, flattened, globe-shaped bush, only reaching 45cm (18in) high and 60cm (2ft) across when mature. It has a neat, densely branching habit. The dark-green needles are shorter and thinner than in the typical species. Its small size means it is an ideal choice for a small, city or courtyard garden, where an architectural, or evergreen focal point is needed, as well as for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery
A tuberous-rooted perennial to 1.2m tall, with green serrated leaves and bearing Fimbriated form, creamy-white flowers in summer and early autumn. When disbudded, flowers can reach 25cm across
A deciduous, large upright tree with mid-green, elliptical leaves. The lemon yellow, tulip shaped flowers are lightly fragrant, and can be prolific as the tree matures.

A tender perennial to 60cm tall, forming an upright clump of slender, white-spotted leaves. In summer it produces striking flowers composed of very dark, black-purple spathes wrapped round a purple spadix; the flowers are held on stout stems above the foliage. Grow as a houseplant, for summer bedding or cut flowers

This medium-sized crisphead lettuce produces large round heads with tasty, crunchy, green leaves. It also shows good pest and disease resistance, along with resistance to unfavourable growing conditions, making this a popular variety to grow, especially with organic gardeners. Sow seeds from April (undercover from February) - June, harvest from July until October.
An early maturing, red-skinned onion cultivar producing semi-round bulbs with red-ringed flesh. Excellent flavour, great for salads as well as cooking. Suitable for autumn planting
An annual dwarf french bean with green leaves and white flowers, producing a heavy crop of dark green beans even in very hot weather.
A clump-forming, perennial grass, to 60cm in height, with arching, linear leaves and hairy, narrow, silvery rose-pink panicles, 10-14cm in length, like soft bottle-brushes

An aquatic perennial with rounded leaves which are bronze when young, later dark green, deep red double flowers to 20cm across Dwarf/small cultivars reach 30–60cm (1–2ft) wide, and need water 30–45cm (12–18in) deep Medium cultivars reach 60–120cm (2–4ft) wide, and need water 45–75cm (18–30in) deep Large cultivars reach up to 2.4m (8ft) wide, and need water 75–120cm (30in–4ft) deep For a suitable planting depth in your pond, please follow the plant label guidelines
Clump-forming evergreen perennial about 30cm tall, with large rounded mid-green leaves, red flushed in winter. Pinkish-green stems to 30cm tall bearing pink, bell-shaped flowers in early spring

A clump-forming perennial to 80cm in flower, erect, strap-like green leaves with a prominent midrib rise beneath upright stems bearing stately, large purple, single flowers with contrasting yellow centres, in summer
A perennial with long, narrow, upright, mid-green clasping leaves, and reaches about 40cm tall. The flowers are pale yellow flushed with darker yellow and appear from late spring to midsummer
A clump-forming perennial growing to 25cm tall. Clusters of pink flowers are borne from late summer to autumn above glossy, green leaves

alternative_names: Salvia azurea subsp. pitcheri var. grandiflora|Salvia azurea 'Grandiflora'|Salvia azurea subsp. pitcheri

description: Vigorous, thorny rose about 1m tall, with healthy glossy, dark green leaves, and bearing long pointed buds opening to fully double, bright yellow, high centred blooms usually appearing singly, with a fruity fragrance, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn

Bushy upright rose to about 90cm tall, with plentiful dark green foliage and bearing exceptionally fragrant, fully double blooms in a colour mix of creamy-white and burgundy-red stripes, repeat-flowering through summer and into autumn

A deciduous shrub, with slender upright stems that are reddish when young, and mature to dark purple-brown. Leaves are narrow, and dark green with a paler midrib, and slender green catkins, the male with purple anthers, in early and mid spring. This cultivar is often used for weaving and basketry

A dwarf pea to 50cm. It has green leaves, though is described as semi-leafless and climbs using extra tendrils. Due to its compact size and tendrils, it does not need support. The flowers are white and develop into edible 'mange-tout' peas. It is an annual which lives for one summer.

An early maincrop, annual climbing pea, to about 70cm high at picking. Heavy cropping, producing double pods with an average of 8 peas each, with good flavour. Ready for harvesting from June depending on sowing date, suitable for eating fresh or freezing

Tuberous-rooted, clump-forming perennial to about 1m tall, with mid-green foliage. Fully double flowers 10cm across, produced from midsummer until the first frosts, have narrow, quilled, soft creamy-yellow petals, bright yellow in the centre, with long, divided tips giving a fringed effect

A large-flowered gladiolus, 1m high, with green leaves and spikes with over 10 flower buds, the flowers deep yellow with red throats, cheerful and bright, long lasting blooms from early summer to late summer

A climbing annual which reaches 60cm. The leaves are narrow and green but there are few of them, however there are plenty of tendrils so that, if grown as a block, they support one another - meaning no sticks or string needed. White flowers become green pods, with dark green peas which freeze well.

An easy to grow and high-yielding variety that may be lifted for baby potatoes or left in the ground longer for larger, early maincrop potatoes. Pale golden tubers are good boiled, baked, mashed or roasted. Can be grown in containers

A recently introduced maincrop variety which has good yields and is great for chipping. Viewed as a good all rounder in the kitchen, the oval tubers have cream skin and a slightly yellow flesh. This cultivar shows a high tolerance to drought and good general disease resistance
A bushy perennial grown as an annual vegetable for its edible tubers. A second early potato with a slightly nutty flavour. The long, narrow tubers are ideal for steaming, boiling and roasting

A bulbous perennial grown as a vegetable with long strappy grey-green leaves. These elongated edible French shallots have a purple-brown outer skin and pink flesh ready for harvest from summer well into autumn.
A dwarf bean with green leaves, white flowers and a heavy crop of green fruit. Good disease resistance
A shallot with a distinctive reddish brown skin and white flesh with good flavour. Stores well

A first early, which can be left to bulk up as a second early or even maincrop, with a great taste that's best suited to boiling. Skins are thin and light brown, getting tougher the longer it's in the ground and the flesh is yellow and slightly waxy, although again, if left in the ground it increases in size and becomes more floury. Shows excellent resistance to potato virus, late potato blight on tubers and bruising and drought-tolerant
A bushy perennial grown as an annual vegetable for its edible tubers. An early potato with red skin and yellow flesh. Produces high yields of large, oval-shaped tubers

A versatile, maincrop potato, especially good for baking, boiling and for salads, with red-marked, golden skins. Shows all-round disease resistance. Particularly suitable as a variety for showing, due to its uniform size. Available for harvesting from June to July if planted from March to April

alternative_names: Japanese laurel|blotch-leaved laurel|gold-leaf plant|Japan laurel|spotted laurel|variegated laurel|Aucuba concolor|Aucuba japonica var. viridis|Aucuba japonica 'Concolor'|Aucuba japonica 'Viridis'
description: A bushy, rounded, evergreen shrub up to 3m high and wide, with thick, oval, glossy leaves. Small, red-purple flowers in spring are followed, on female plants, by clusters of red autumn berries provided there is a male plant nearby to provide pollen

primary_name: Lilium × phildauricum hort. F.L.Skinner ex Gard.Chron. (VIIIa/b)

description: A bushy, deciduous rose, to 90cm tall, with glossy, dark green foliage. Clusters of scented, double, cream flowers with a darker centre are borne from summer into autumn

alternative_names: rose [Peter Cottrell]|rose [Sunshine Abundance]|Rosa 'Sunny Abundance'|Rosa [Sunshine Abundance]|Rosa 'Sunshine Abundance'|Rosa [Peter Cotrill]|Rosa 'Harentente'|Rosa [Sunny Abundance] (Abundance Series)
description: Bushy rose to 90cm tall, with dark green leaves and producing fragrant, double yellow blooms, flushed pink on the outer petals, repeat-flowering in summer and autumn
A floribunda rose about 90cm high with glossy, dark green leaves and clusters of five to thirteen fragrant, repeat-flowering, semi-double, mid-pink flowers, 8cm across, from summer to autumn
A giant, clump-forming deciduous perennial with large, blue-green foliage. Upright stems of white flowers appear in summer

A compact, clump-forming, deciduous perennial with broadly ovate creamy white leaves with green margins, some jettings into the white centre with pink scapes and petioles. Center is pale yellow in very low light. Upright stems of pale purple, stripped flowers with redish-pink scapes appear in midsummer. Pinkish seedpods appear in autumn.

A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with blue foliage changing to variegated yellow and green with a blue margin as the season progresses. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium-sized, clump-forming, deciduous perennial with thick, heart-shaped blue-green leaves with streaks of white. Upright stems produce clusters of pale lavender-purple flowers in summer

A robust, upright bulbous perennial plant with long, basal, strap-like leaves. The flower is a dense round globe, approximately 10cm across, made up of little starry, mid to pale-purple individual blooms which are produced in late spring and early summer, with seeds that ripen by late summer

A bushy, clump-forming perennial to 80cm high, with bright green, palmate leaves divided into narrow leaflets. Dense spikes of bicoloured flowers, with pale ivory upper petals and rich violet wings, are produced in early to mid summer
An upright, clump-forming perennial, to 80cm tall, with palmately-divided green leaves and, in summer, spikes of creamy-white buds opening to scented, yellow flowers
An erect, bushy annual with finely dissected leaves and single, purplish-pink flowers

An evergreen shrub or small tree to around 8m in height and width. The leaves are short and needle-like, almost like a Christmas tree. The flowers in spring, are pale yellow fluffy candles that look like fuzzy caterpillars

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 53cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and a blend of pink, orange and lavender coloured flowers that have a purple eye-zone and green throat to 10cm across in early summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 64cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and rose-pink flowers with a greenish yellow throat to 14cm across in summer and the flowers remain open for over 16 hours

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and pale ivory-cream flowers with a strong, green throat to 11cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and pinkish claret-red coloured flowers that have a pale pink eye-zone above a yellow-green throat to 13cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 86cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and spider-type, melon-pink coloured flowers that have a burgundy-purple eye-zone to 13cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 46cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and ivory-cream flowers with a dark purple eyezone and lime green throat to 8cm across in summer
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-like, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of semi-double deep red flowers with a yellow throat
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are slightly fragranced and are pale yellow with a slightly darker yellow throat
Upright, clump-forming perennial to around 1.2m tall with deeply divided, dark green leaves. Branching stems bear heads of hooded, pale yellow flowers in summer
A herbaceous perennial 1.5m high with deciduous strap-shaped green leaves and flowerheads of long, tubular, sky-blue flowers, darker near the tips, which hang down as they open in late summer

A slow-growing, dwarf style, herbaceous perennial reaching between 30 to 60cm in height, when in flower. Above a neat clump of narrow strap-like, green, deciduous leaves, numerous flowering stems bear purplish blue funnel-shaped flowers in rounds heads, in late summer and early autumn
An erect, vigorous perennial, branching and floriferous. Flowers are bright mid-blue, with large white eyes which may show a blue splash

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial, to around 75cm high, with an upright habit and lobed green leaves. Tall, branching stems bear lilac-pink flowers with white centres in late spring to early summer and often again in early autumn

alternative_names: broad-leaved thyme 'Archer's Gold'|Thymus 'Archers Gold'|Thymus citriodorus (Pers.) Schreb. 'Archer's Gold' [1]
description: A bushy, evergreen subshrub, to 20cm in height, with small, lime-green, lemon-scented leaves and erect spikes of tiny, pale lilac flowers in late spring and early summer

alternative_names: golden broad-leaved thyme|Thymus 'Golden Lemon' misapplied [1]|Thymus citriodorus (Pers.) Schreb. 'Aureus' [1]
description: A bushy evergreen shrublet to 20cm in height, becoming spreading and more open with age, with small, bright yellow, lemon-scented leaves and erect, interrupted spikes of tiny pale lilac flowers

alternative_names: broad-leaved thyme 'Bertram Anderson'|Thymus 'Anderson's Gold'|Thymus citriodorus (Pers.) Schreb. 'Bertram Anderson' [1]|Thymus citriodorus 'Andersons Gold'|Thymus 'E.B. Anderson'
description: A compact, spreading evergreen shrublet to 10cm in height, with aromatic, bright golden-yellow, ovate leaves and terminal clusters of small, pink to pale mauve flowers appearing from May to July. A good choice for edging or for planting as a fragrant lawn. Although not as strongly scented as some varieties, it can still be used in cooking
An eye-catching, mat-forming, evergreen sub-shrub with bright golden yellow-green, aromatic foliage and attractive clusters of pink flowers in summer

A compact, rosette-forming, semi-evergreen perennial cowslip with green, veined foliage and tubular semi-double golden yellow rosette-shaped flowers with one growing inside the other, appearing in the spring

This second early cultivar is high yielding, has a lovely flavour and maintains a good texture when boiled or baked. The tubers are attractive, oval-shaped with white skin and cream flesh and suitable for all kitchen uses. Good disease resistance and the ability to store long term make this potato a great all rounder

A tender, upright, branching perennial first early variety with dark green foliage, purple flowers and short, oval tubers with white skin and some resistance to blight. Good for all cooking methods and high yielding. Available to harvest June to July

This maincrop is hugely popular due to its beautiful taste, good yields and versatility. It is easily recognisable by its red skin and creamy yellow flesh and makes excellent chips, mash, roasties and jacket potatoes! Shows some resistance to blackleg and leafroll virus

A versatile, maincrop potato to around 75cm in height, producing high yields of oval-shaped tubers with white skins and creamy flesh. Plant from March to May for harvesting July to September. Shows good resistance to tuber blight, potato leaf roll virus and potato cyst nematode and copes well with drought

A fairly recent introduction to the market which is fast becoming a household favourite due to its delicious flavour. This second early potato has smooth skin with attractive with purple blue tints in places and is a great all rounder in the kitchen. It is a high yielding variety which grows well in heavy soils and tolerates dry conditions. Shows good resistance to potato blackleg, as well as potato virus, slugs and bruising

A carnivorous perennial forming rosettes to 20cm across of yellow-green leaves. Both the upper and lower leaf surfaces are sticky to trap and digest insects. Solitary purple flowers are produced on 15cm tall stems in summer. In winter this species has a period of semi-dormancy when it should be kept drier; during this time it may produce non-carnivorous leaves
An evergreen perennial alpine forming a compact cushion of rosettes of narrowly oblong leaves, with fragrant, slender-tubed, pale yellow primrose-like flowers borne just above the foliage
