A large, rather spreading shrub with broad, rounded leaves flushed purple in spring and turning yellow in autumn. The flowers, produced in late winter, have straight, egg-yolkyellow petals but lack fragrance

An upright, rounded deciduous shrub or small tree with broadly oval, wrinkled green leaves that turn shades of yellow and orange in autumn. Slightly scented, ruby-red flowers with narrow, crimped petals are borne on bare branches in late winter and early spring

A medium to large, upright deciduous, often vase-shaped, shrub to a height of around 3 to 4.5m, with oval green leaves that turn an attractive shade of golden yellow in autumn. Slightly fragranced golden-yellow flowers with narrow crimped petals are borne on the bare branches early to mid-winter, earlier than other cultivars
A slow-growing, tropical evergreen shrub, with upright, sparsely branching stems and long, narrow, glossy dark green leaves streaked with pale green and white

Deciduous, large tree with mid-green, ovate leaves, softly hairy on the underside, reaching over 20m in height. Goblet-shaped, reddish-rose pink flowers with a pale central band to each tepal, open to a waterlily shape to 10cm across with 9-12 tepals, usually flowering in early spring before the leaves; seedling originated at Lanhydrock Gardens, Cornwall, selected by Peter Borlase, Head Gardener

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and dark orange-red flowers with a bright green throat to 14cm across in summer

A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 30cm high, with lance-shaped dark green leaves. Daisy-like flowers, with very pale lavender-coloured petals and yellow centres, are borne on wiry stems from early summer to early autumn

A low-growing perennial, to around 25cm high, with narrowly heart-shaped, yellow-green leaves that are edged and speckled with bronze. A somewhat variable cultivar, with spidery flowers, usually white but sometimes tinted pink or yellow, held on delicate stems above the leaves in spring.

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. White flowers, turning to pale pink as they mature and with yellow stamens, appear in the spring

A neat and compact, spreading, evergreen perennial with dark green, oval-shaped, toothed leaves. Fragrant, bi-coloured flowers are a streaky grey-blue and creamy lemon-yellow to begin the season, changing to completely yellow as the temperatures rise, and appear from spring through to the autumn

A neat and compact, spreading, evergreen perennial with oval, toothed, dark green leaves. Fragrant, star-shaped purple-pink to dark lavender-purple flowers with narrow and twisted petals, are produced from spring through until autumn

A bright large-flowered gladiolus, height around 1-1.5m, with green sword like leaves and an erect upright flower spike with 10-15 flower buds. The flower petals have a satin appearance and are a rich, clear yellow. Imposing blooms for the summer garden

A robust, upright, open deciduous shrub about 2m or more tall, with dark green leaves, and compact flower panicles forming a dense cone of sterile florets opening pale lime green, becoming creamy-white, a slight pink flush gradually deepens to give a pink and green colour mix at maturity in summer and autumn

A deciduous shrub to 1.5m high with broadly oval, serrated green leaves. Dome-shaped clusters of flowers are produced in summer, in pastel shades of pink and lilac purple depending on the pH of the soil, with tints of green later in the season

A bulbous perennial grows to 50cm tall, and has striking colouration. The outer tepals are ochre yellow, almost covered by a broad maroon-purple triangle running from the base up to the pointed tip. Inside the flower is yellow with just a purple flush towards the base

A perennial bulb with pale green, broadly lance-shaped leaves. This Parrot Group tulip has cup-shaped flowers, and heavily fringed petals with a strong green midrib, and creamy white and lilac pink margins. Flowers are approximately 55cm high, and produced in late spring
A perennial bulb with light green, lance-shaped leaves. The flowers, produced in late spring, are white flushed with gold at the base with narrow, pinkish-red flaming
Grows to 40cm, with rounded flowers, soft flesh-pink outside, shading to cream at the margins, and cream within
A perennial bulb, to around 40cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are creamy white, with ruffled petals with a faint purple flame

A small hybrid tulip; slender plants with pointed flowers grow 20-25cm tall. Outer tepals have a broad, strongly red triangle, covering most of the space, with narrow yellow borders. Inside the flowers are yellow with dark purple stamens. Mid to late spring

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This tulip has goblet-shaped white flowers, with a yellow base and sometimes pale yellow streaks up the centre of the outer petals. Flowers are produced in mid-spring, and stand to around 35cm high
An herbaceous perennial with mound-forming mid-green leaves. Flowers are a strong pink, surrounded by a ruff of triangular bracts that are slightly paler pink.
A clump-forming perennial reaching 120cm with coarsely toothed dark green leaves, and erect, rigid stems topped with single white flowers 10-12 cm across, with a yellow centre.
A spreading, evergreen perennial to about 20cm with bright green, heart-shaped leaves. Small, white, viola-shaped flowers are produced from late spring to early autumn

A perennial bulb, to around 50cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Late flowering, with cup-shaped white flowers, edged and streaked with deep pink. Multi-flowering, sometimes producing two or three flowers from each bulb
A perennial bulb, up to 50cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped grey-green leaves. Flowers are cup shaped, with ivory white petals flamed with bright red, and a touch of yellow at the base
A Double Early Group tulip to about 40cm in height with fully double, bowl-shaped, bright, butter yellow flowers flecked and overlaid with red flames, flowering in mid-spring

A perennial bulb with light green, lance-shaped foliage. The fully double flowers are orange with some yellow shading on the inner petals, and red and green feathering on the outer petals. They grow to about 30cm and open in late spring

Small, deciduous, rounded tree or large shrub reaching around 4m in height, with ovate mid-green leaves. The golden-yellow flowers to 10cm wide with thick tepals, open before the leaves in spring and as the foliage develops
Densely foliaged, symetrical, pyramidal tree about 8m in height, with dark green leaves. Tulip-shaped, upright, pure pink flowers are produced before the leaves unfurl in spring
A large-cupped daffodil to around 50cm high, with straplike grey-green leaves. Flowers have broad, ribbed white outer petals and a bowl-shaped, deep orange cup with a frilled rim
A trumpet daffodil, to around 60cm high, with straplike, grey-green leaves. Flowers have white outer petals and a bright yellow corona with a widely flared and ruffled rim
A clump-forming, bulbous perennial up to 65 cm tall, with strappy green foliage. Small, fragrant, creamy-white flowers appear in clusters of up to 10 blooms in the spring
A large-cupped daffodil, to around 60cm high, with straplike grey-green leaves. Flowers have broad white outer petals, and a flared salmon pink cup

Small, upright, deciduous tree or large shrub reaching up to 8m in height with ovate mid-green leaves. The abundant, tulip-shaped flowers are pale to golden-yellow emerging in spring before the leaves

Compact, deciduous small tree or large shrub with mid-green leaves. The cup-shaped flowers, opening in late spring together with the leaves, have six, pale greenish-yellow petals and are very freely-produced

Fast-growing, deciduous tree or large shrub reaching around 8m in height with ovate mid-green. Scented, upright, deep-yellow flowers have a pink flush at the base of the narrow tepals, appear in spring with the leaves

Small, deciduous, conical tree reaching approximately 8m in heigh, with ovate mid-green leaves. The large, tulip-shaped, white flowers with pointed tepals, with dark ered tipped stamens, are produced in spring before the leaves

Large, deciduous shrub, to 8m tall, with ovate leaves, green and bronze when young maturing to mid-green in the summer. Large, scented, very double flowers open in spring before the leaves and are white to very pale pink, approximately 12cm in diameter and made up of around 50 tepals

Rounded, deciduous thorny shrub to 1.5m in height, with mid-green, rounded, glossy leaves. Clusters of single orange-pink, cup-shaped flowers are produced in spring on bare branches, followed, in autumn, by aromatic green fruits that ripen to yellow. These can be used to make jams and jellies but please see notes on toxicity for further advice

A low-growing, spreading evergreen shrub to around 25cm in height with a lush habit and mid-green linear leaves. Delicate-looking, single, ivory-white flowers with yellow centres appear in late spring to summer
A low spreading, evergreen perennial with dark green leaves. Rose pink flowers with red markings near the centre with a yellow middle are produced in spring and summer
A clump-forming, upright perennial up to 1m tall with long, strap-shaped green leaves. Tubular, drooping dark violet-blue flowers are borne in clusters from mid-summer to autumn on erect stems

A perennial poppy, to 90cm high, with bristly stems and finely divided, hairy green leaves. In late spring to early summer, large, cup-shaped flowers are produced, with glossy, crinkled, reddish petals fading to pink, and with dark blotches at the base

A perennial poppy, to 90cm high, with bristly stems and finely divided, hairy green leaves. In late spring to early summer, large, cup-shaped flowers are produced, with ruffled, near white petals flushed with pale rose at the base, and a striking dark purple centre
A small herbaceous perennial with silvery-green fern-like, finely toothed leaves. Has white cup-shaped flowers and yellow stamens in late spring and early summer.
An herbaceous perennial making a clump to 1.5m tall, with rough, ovate leaves to 20cm long and flower-heads with bright yellow semi-double ray-florets and large deep yellow disks

A rosette-forming, evergreen, perennial succulent to about 1.5m. The leaves are light greyish-green, edged and tipped with reddish spines. Plant have not been in cultivation long enough to assess flowering, but in the wild it produces huge, club-shaped inflorescences made up of tightly clustered yellow flowers on short branches supported by a scaly, 5m high trunk
A slowly-spreading, compact perennial to 15cm tall and wide with green, hairy, three-lobedleaves and bowl-shaped, deep blueflowers up to 4cm across borne in spring
A dwarf herbaceous perennial with narrow, mid-green leaves and large, star-shaped, violet-blue flowers opening from inflated, balloon-like buds all summer

Densely-tufted, deciduous, perennial grass about 1m tall, producing a mound of sturdy, fine-textured, glaucous blue leaves. Upright, silvery grey-blue flowers appear in late summer and early autumn. The whole plant usually turns red, orange and copper in autumn and winter

A bulbous perennial to 60cm tall with narrow, strap-shaped, greyish-green leaves and erect stems bearing flowers up to 10cm across in shades of blue, yellow and white from late spring into early summer
A bushy perennial, to 75cm tall, with deeply-lobed, downy, grey-green leaves. In summer to autumn it bears saucer-shaped, soft apricot flowers 2.5cm across

An herbaceous perennial with upright stems of blue-green leaves in three's. Flowers are creamy white in bud opening to a dusky pink, followed by black seed pods

An upright, deciduous, bushy shrub with oval-shaped dark green foliage. Small, tubular, single dark rose-red flowers with white corollas appear in summer. Ideal for pots, hanging baskets and containers

A shrub rose to 1.2m tall, which also makes a useful small climber, with coppery-tinted, glossy, dark green leaves on strong stems and free-flowering, fragrant, fully-petalled amber blooms that repeat-flower from summer to autumn
Has dark green, lime-scented leaves which may take on bronze tints in autumn. It bears bright pink flowers for quite a long season from early to mid summer

Evergreen shrub with an upright habit, to 1.5m high and wide, and variegated glossy, green leaves with a broad green central blotch and lime-yellow margins. Blue flowers are produced in late spring and early summer and contrast with the bright foliage
An upright, deciduous rose, to 1.2m tall, with glossy, dark green foliage and, from summer into autumn, clusters of lightly-scented, double, yellow and red-striped flowers that fade to cream and pink
Bushy rose about 80-90cm tall and wide, with glossy dark green foliage, and well-formed strongly fragrant, fully double, dark lilac-pink blooms, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn

A robust, bushy rose about 75-90m tall, with healthy, glossy mid-green foliage, and bearing large, fully double, bicolored blooms to 10.5cm across, striped and streaked pink, red and white with a strong fruity fragrance, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

Vigorous, upright, bushy rose reaching around 1.2m in height with glossy mid-green foliage, and large, lightly scented, shapely, fully double, creamy-white blooms edged with bright red to the petals, borne from summer through until autumn

A seedless, red dessert grape, producing large bunches of soft-skinned, juicy red fruit with a sweet flavour, ready for eating from the vine. Upright, deciduous tree, often mutli-stemmed, to about 8m in height and freely-branching with mid-green leaves. Large, pure white, goblet-shaped flowers up to 25cm across are produced on bare stems in early to mid-spring
An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 90cm in height when in flower with green, linear strap-like leaves and spikes of yellow, orange and red tubular flowers in summer and autumn.

An upright-growing large, dense shrub or small tree. Abundant, pure white, scented flowers are produces in small clusters in spring just ahead of the bronze-tinted young leaves. Edible, dark bluish-purple berries follow, with red and orange autumn leaf colour

An upright, white-barked birch to a height of 10m. A relatively recent cross between B. albosinsinensis and B. utilis offering a neat canopy of dark green serrated foliage and white to pinkish peeling bark

A rounded, deciduous, small shrub to 1m in height, with glossy mid-green leaves, and bearing clusters of bright orange cup-shaped flowers in spring borne on leafless branches, then aromatic greenish fruits ripening to yellow follow in autumn. A medium, spreading, deciduous tree with double, pale pink flowers on long stems hanging below the branches in mid- to late spring. The leaves turn dark orange in autumn

Very free-flowering, spreading, deciduous tree about 5m tall. A round-headed deciduous tree to 15m. The new foliage is red-flushed as it emerges, then green in summer, and turns bright red before falling in autumn. A profusion of pale pink flowers are produced in spring; these are followed by small dark red fruits

Upright deciduous tree about 6-8m tall, with mid-green leaves to 15cm long. In mid-spring it bears very large, scented, goblet-shaped flowers to 23cm wide, with unfurling 8-10 tepals, pinkish-white with a red base outside and a white interior, from a distance the flower appears pale pink

A compact, deciduous tree to around 5m tall with spreading branches bearing mid- to deep green leaves divided into pairs of toothed leaflets that turn shades of orange and red in autumn. A deciduous herbaceous perennial with strap-like mid green leaves and erect stems that hold rounded heads of pale blue, trumpet-shaped flowers with a darker rib down the centre of each petal, in summer
A rhizomatous, clump-forming iris to 75cm tall with slender, strap-shaped leaves and purple flowers with yellow markings on the falls borne on upright stems in summer
A tuberous perennial that grows to about 75cm, with double flowerheads to 9cm across, the florets bright crimson

Lithops lesliei subsp. lesliei var. rubrobrunnea

description: A warm to hot growing epiphytic orchid which is a hybrid of Bulbophyllum longissimum and Bulbophyllum rothschildianum. The plant produces short, angled, egg-shaped green stems called pseudobulbs, which are adapted to store water and nutrients. The pseudobulbs arise from a creeping, rooting stem, and each are topped with a single, green, oblong to lance-shaped, leaf. Flowers are produced from autumn to spring, in clusters at the end of thin stems and are pale pink with darker pink fine stripes. The upper sepal is somewhat hairy, and pale green with darker stripes, while the lower sepals are up to 30cm long. The hinged lip, an adapted petal evolved to attract pollinators, moves in the slightest breeze, is tongue-shaped and pink. The flowers are scented and appear from autumn to spring

Long, adventurous roots, attaching to anything in their surroundings emerge directly frm the stem, following the ascending growing trend. The plant flowers in spring or early summer on 15 - 30cm long, erect racemes, carrying approximately 6 large, long-lasting, fragrant flowers. Each flowers is 5 - 6cm large, with prominent, wide lip. Cultivar 'John Lacock' is almost pure white, with yellowish centre at the back of the lip.

A medium-sized tropical orchid with long, upright, cane-like stems (pseudobulbs), 30-50cm tall, covered with thin, papery sheaths that turn silvery/grey as the stems mature. Dark green, firm, lance-shaped leaves, 10-12cm long and 3cm wide are alternately arranged near the tips of the stems. Short, arching flowering stems appear from axils of leaves and mature canes in spring. Each stem carries up to twenty yellow, occasionaly pale cream flowers with dark brown or red spots

An epiphytic, semi-evergreen orchid with long, noded, fleshy, green cane-like pseudobulbs. The stems are covered with thin, leaf-bearing sheaths along the nodes of each cane. The leaves may last one or more seasons. Each oblong, bright, or dark green leaf is 5-8cm long. Short flowering stems carrying one to three flowers emerging from the upper nodes of mature stems. Each flower is approximately 7cm large, white or pale pink, with darker centre.

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid hybrid with long, upright, cane-like stems (pseudobulbs). Four to six dark green, leathery leaves are alternately arranged on the upper half or near the top of each pseudobulb. Each lance-shaped leaf is 8-14cm long and 3cm wide. Upright flowering stems up to 30cm long appear from the upper nodes and tips of mature canes and bear up to fifteen, dark pink/magenta flowers. The flowers open in succession and last on a plant for a long time.
A perennial bulb, to around 25cm high, with broadly strap-shaped, upright green leaves. Dense, cylindrical clusters of fragrant, waxy, lilac pink flowers with paler edges are produced in spring
A Jonquilla daffodil with sturdy stems to 70cm, bearing several fragrant flowers over a long period, the perianth segments light yellow, the corona orange

A clump-forming perennial to around 1.8m high, with ovate, slightly hairy, toothed dark green leaves. Bright yellow flowers to 7.5cm across are produced in late summer, with a mass of enlarged disc florets in the centre giving an anemone-form appearance

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 1m, with mid-green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The semi-cactus form blooms have neat rows of tightly inrolled, wine-red petals, forming a flattened ball 10cm across

A clockwise-twining, woody climber with leaves made up of up to 15 leaflets. Very fragrant flowers in shadesof soft lilac-blue with slightly darker edges and aging to whiteare borne in summer on racemes up to 45cm long.

An attractive perennial marigold species native to the Canary Islands and N.W. Africa with stunning, pure yellow flowers held atop green stems and mid-green, lanceolate foliage in spring and summer
A hybrid tea rose to about 90cm tall with glossy, dark green leaves and bearing large, very fragrant, double, bright to deep magenta pink blooms repeat flowering through summer until autumn

A low-growing perennial with a dense, mounding habit growing to 30cm tall. The leaves are a bright green dappled with grey-green spots. Saucer-shaped, open flowers up to 2cm in length and diameter are coloured clear pink tinted with violet-blue and appear in spring

A medium to large-sized, epiphytic orchid with long, cane-like stems. Glossy, oval-shaped leaves are alternately arranged along the nodes of the stems. Each leaf is 8-12cm long and 3cm wide. A compact, deciduous perennial often grown as an annual/biennial with green foliage and large, bright golden-yellow daisy-like flowers with a mahogany-brown central eyezone and a dark brown button-shaped centre, appearing from summer through until the first frosts

A deciduous tree about 10m in height, initially narrow pyramidal, then forming an oval crown, but remaining fairly narrow, with palmate, 5-lobed, dark green leaves turning a deep golden-yellow in autumn. Green spring flowers are followed by winged fruits ripening to red; ideal landscape tree

A small bushy tree with lightly veined, ovate pointed leaves that turn reddish-purple in autumn. Flowers are followed by reddish pink strawberry-like fruits in autumn

An upright, evergreen shrub with small, dark green leaves edged with creamy-white. New leaves are bright red in spring, with pink edges. Creamy-white flower buds are decorative in winter and open to sprays of small, clear white, urn-shaped flowers in spring
A compact, slow-growing variety with a wide spread of upright stems and dark green needle-like foliage. Brown, oval-shaped cones appear in the autumn
A narrow, upright, slow-growing conifer with compacted dark green needles that grow in pairs. Large white buds appear through the winter months. Tolerates high winds and cold weather

A relatively slow-growing, broadly pyramidal pine, ultimately reaching up to 25m. Long, soft needles, arranged in fives, are yellow-green in spring and summer, golden-yellow in autumn and winter. Long, resinous, grey-brown cones remain on the tree all year

A compact, evergreen, bushy shrub with spiny stems and narrow, oblong, glossy dark green foliage. Clusters of flat, white flowers in early summer are followed by orange berries in autumn and winter. This variety has a prostrate habit and can be grown against walls or as a stand-alone hedge or shrub
A compact, slow-growing, coniferous tree to around 1.2m tall. This many-branched cultivar bears whorls of dark green, needle-like leaves and is rounded when young before maturing to a pyramidal shape
A flattened rounded semi-dwarf evergreen conifer. The foliage is grey-green in colour
A short-lived, rosette-forming perennial to 70cm tall, the stems and rough-textured leaves are sparsely covered with stiff hairs. In summer it bears a profusion of deep pink, funnel-shaped flowers
A hardy, evergreen shrub with a compact, bushy habit approximately 21-25cm tall with a spread to 31-45cm. It has dark green foliage and crimson coloured buds from summer through to autumn.

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a bushy, slightly weeping habit, up to 2.5 metres in height. It has distinctive, mid-green, fan-shaped, bilobed leaves and excellent autumn colour. Ideal for use in large containers
A small, slow-growing, deciduous conifer, of columnar to pyramidal form, up to 2m tall. Soft, flat green leaves are held on ascending branchlets and turn shades of yellow and brown in the autumn
A compact and bushy, decidous shrub with oval, toothed dark green leaves. It produces strongly fragrant pink flowers from winter right through until spring

A clump-forming perennial with semi-evergreen, strap-shaped foliage. Flower stems to 1.5m tall bear large spheres of deep purple-blue flowers in summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous perennial to around 60cm in height, with toothed, mid-green foliage at the base. Self-seeds in the right conditions

An erect, clump-forming perennial to 1.8m with large, slightly greyish, mid-green leaves. Creamy-white flowers, the lower petals and throat initially with orange to pale pink markings, then becoming pure ivory, are produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn
A clump-forming perennial to about 1.8m tall, with broad, paddle-shaped bronze-purple leaves margined dark red, and soft apricot flowers blushed rose pink appear from midsummer to mid-autumn
Striking perennial about 2m tall, forming a large, open clump with handsome, large, slender blue-green leaves, and bearing graceful, pale peachy-orange flowers from midsummer to autumn

Upright, clump-forming perennial about 1.1m tall, with large mid-green paddle-shaped leaves with a fine dark margin, and upright panicles of cerise-pink flowers with a pink-speckled, yellow throat, produced from midsummer to autumn
Upright perennial, to 1m tall, forming clumps of large, bronze-tinted green leaves, and bright orange-red flowers with yellow-flushed throats, on sturdy stems, from summer to early autumn
A clump-forming perennial to 1.5m tall with paddle-shaped, lush green leaves and stems. Bright orange flowers above the foliage are borne on tall stems, and appear from early summer to mid-autumn

A clump-forming perennial to 1.5m tall with large, paddle-shaped green leaves, and bearing rounded heads of distinctive, iris-like flowers, sunflower yellow with lines of red dots along the petals, from early summer to mid-autumn

A medium to large-sized, epiphytic orchid with upright, up to 75cm tall pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb carries a single, strap-shaped, dark green, leathery leaf up to 60cm long and 3-4cm wide. The orchid flowers in late spring with upright, dense raceme up to 40cm tall, carrying a large number of small, spirally arranged flowers. Upside-down flowers measuring 0.8cm are pink-purple with darker lip.

A compact evergreen perennial, to 10cm high, with spreading rhizomes and basal rosettes of oval to broadly lance-shaped, leathery green leaves with serrated edges. Slender stems bear sprays of tiny, densely packed star-shaped white flowers in late spring and early summer

A cultivar of hybrid origin with slow and compact growth, eventually reaching around 2-2.5m in height. Pale pink, double flowers, with a central display of yellow stamens, appear over 5-6 weeks in spring
A bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Spikes of fragrant, rich purple-blue flowers to 8cm long are borne on slender stems in summer

A herbaceous perennial, 60cm high, with reddish stems and serrated, pinnate leaves randomly-spotted and splashed with yellow. Deep maroon flowerheads, like small bottlebrushes, appear from late summer to late autumn

A small, deciduous, bushy and trailing shrub with dark green foliage, and abundant pendent double flowers which have a pale powdery pink corolla and pink sepals borne from summer through to autumn. Very suitable for containers and hanging baskets
A rhizomatous perennial to 85cm high with greyish-green sword-like foliage. Flowers produced in early summer have standards, falls and beard an unusual raspberry or rosy mulberry colour
A bushy, evergreen shrub with aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves. In spring it bears fragrant spikes of dark, purple-violet flowers topped with dark purple bracts.

A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Spikes of small fragrant flowers, opening rich purple blue and paling as they age, are borne on short, slender stems from early to late summer
A free-flowering, shortly trailing annual to 40cm tall, with fragrant white flowers 6cm wide, with greenish-yellow mid-vein to each lobe

An erect, tuberous perennial with green, strap-like leaves, purplish stems and large pink to purple flowers with crinkled lips which appear during the summer

A deciduous perennial to around 10cm high producing compact clumps of hairy,-grass-like leaves and short stems bearing star-shaped white to pale pink flowers in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with narrow, glossy green foliage and spotted red stems. Upright stems of violet-purple flowers appear in summer
A compact, clump-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial with green foliage with silver marbling. Panicles of small bell shaped red flowers appear above the foliage in the summer

alternative_names: American alum root 'Ring of Fire'|Heuchera 'Ring of Fire'
description: A compact, clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial producing silvery-green ruffled foliage with darker veining and coral-pink edges which become more prominent during the winter. Small, pale-pink flowers appear on tall, thin, upright stems above the foliage in early summer
A tropical, tuberous perennial grown mainly as a foliage houseplant but can also be used for bedding. It has very large heart-shaped green leaves with pink blotches, held on slender, upright stalks

A perennial bulb to around 25cm in height, with grey-green leaves and slender stems. Nodding, fragrant double white flowers, with a dark green mark running the full length of the outside of the inner petals, appear from February to April

A bushy, deciduous perennial forming a clump of upright, reddish stems to around 1m tall clothed with lance-shaped, dark green leaves each with a prominent white midrib.Yellow-green flowers are borne in flat, terminal clusters from late spring into summer

alternative_names: Paris polyphylla tibetica|Paris polyphylla var. appendiculata|Paris polyphylla var. thibetica

description: Bushy semi-evergreen shrub about 1.5-2m tall, with silky stems and palmate grey-green leaves composed of leaflets 6cm long. In late spring and summer produces dense racemes to 30cm long of fragrant, pea-like blue flowers

A vigorous, clump-forming perennial to 40cm high, with ovate, slightly glossy dark green leaves with a narrow creamy-white margin and deeply impressed veins. Produces loose clusters of fragrant, tubular, near white flowers on upright stems in summer

alternative_names: Anthemis cretica subsp. pyrethriformis|Anthemis carpatica subsp. pyrethrifolia
Chinese elephant's ears|she yan bai cai|Bergenia himalaica|Bergenia ciliata f. ligulata
description: A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to around 20cm high. The smooth, green, rounded to ovate leaves, 10-15cm long, have hairy, serrated margins. In spring, short stout stems bear white to pink flowers

An upright evergreen shrub, with a dense, bushy habit and glossy green leaves with finely serrated edges. Bright red formal double flowers, with high centres like a rose, are produced in mid to late spring
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height, forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and nearly white flowers with a green throat to 13cm across in summer.

Upright, deciduous shrub about 3m tall, with 3-lobed dark green leaves to 10cm long, and very large, deep pink flowers to 13cm across, with prominent red-feathered centres are produced from mid to late summer

A slender-stemmed, trailing or low-climbing, evergreen shrub to 1.25m high and wide with dark green, finely-cut leaves. Profuse creamy-white, fragrant flowers 3.5-5.0cm in diameter with brown anthers on yellow-green filaments are borne in spring
A small bushy evergreen sub-shrub to 60 in height with thin, silvery, almost white, curry-scented leaves, and small yellow flowers in domed clusters in summer

alternative_names: Siskiyou lewisia 'Ashwood Ruby'|Lewisia cotyledon Ashwood Ruby Group [1]

description: A small tree to about 5m with glossy, dark green leaves turning yellow in autumn. Scented, pink-tinged, single white flowers are carried abundantly in mid- to late spring, followed by oval, red fruit up to 2cm across

Tall, upright, bushy rose about 1.2m in height, with dark green foliage. Clusters of orange-yellow buds open to lightly scented, high-centred, fully double, blooms to 11cm across, golden-yellow edged in coral-pink that fade to almost white with age, and produced above long stems and repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

A clump-forming, rhizomatous perennial 30cm high, with deciduous, pinnate leaves, 30cm long, formed of usually nine ovate to heart-shaped, spiny-edged leaflets which open purple and mature to mid-green, and deep pink buds which open to large flowers, of deep pink sepals and pale pink petals with long white spurs, in spring; Epimedium leaves may be used for their nests by leaf-cutting bees

A clump-forming perennial, to around 35cm high, with leaves divided into oval or narrowly heart-shaped green leaflets, tinted with red in spring and autumn. Sprays of small white or pale pink flowers are borne on delicate stems above the leaves in late spring

A compact, mound-forming, evergreen perennial, to 45cm high and around 60cm wide, with upright or sprawling stems bearing blue-grey, narrow, lance-shaped leaves. Clusters of tiny yellow flowers, surrounded by yellow-green bracts, are borne from spring to midsummer

Marion White Group are a group of evergreen, clump-forming perennials with deep green leaves and flowers from late winter to spring with pale yellow petals marked to varying degrees with crimson-red speckles
An upright, perennial with ovate, light green aromatic leaves and whorls of white, long-tubed flowers, forming long, lax spikes in mid and late summer and early autumn
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall, with dark green leaves and erect spikes of pink flowers throughout summer

A large, spreading, deciduous shrub to 3m with narrowly oval, dark green leaves, turning brilliant scarlet-red in autumn. Inconspicuous but nectar-rich, green and white flowers in summer are followed by pink, four-lobed fruit, splitting to reveal orange seeds, and lasting well into winter

primary_name: Euonymus hamiltonianus subsp. sieboldianus var. yedoensis f. koehneanus

alternative_names: dwarf soft shield fern Plumosum Group
description: A clump-forming, dwarf, evergreen fern with soft, overlapping fronds with a very lacy, graceful, multi-layered appearance

A compact, evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet-shaped blue flowers in the summer, flushed with white when fully open
A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to 1.2m tall and wide. The dark-green, silvery-bronze, arching, sword-like leaves can take on a red tint in cold weather
a succulent perennial to 4cm in height, forming a clump of rosettes of thick blue-green leaves with brownish tubercles, and daisy-like bright yellow to orange flowers 2cm across in autumn
A bushy, spreading shrub to about 1.5m. Dull green, oval leaves turn brilliant pinkish-red in autumn. Small, green flowers are followed by pink, lobed fruit splitting to reveal orange seeds

A dense, rounded, relatively compact shrub to about 2.5m, with corky wings on the branches, and narrowly oval, dark green foliage, turning bright scarlet-red in autumn. Small, inconspicuous, yellowish flowers in summer are followed by pink, four-lobed fruit, splitting to reveal orange seeds

A deciduous large shrub or small tree, with an upright spreading habit. Mid green papery long oval leaves, turn reddy pink in autumn. Flowering in mid-summer with small white flowers, followed by pink fruits that can still be on display into winter

primary_name: Euonymus grandiflorus f. salicifolius Stapf. & F. Ballard

description: An historic (17th century) late-season dessert apple with crisp flesh and a sweet, fruity flavour. It is not very vigorous, and forms an upright, compact tree. Prolific pinkish-red flowers are followed by fruit somewhat flattened in shape, yellow flushed with red, ripening in mid-autumn and storing to mid-spring. It is self-sterile, pollination group 3, and can be slow to reach cropping age

A woody, evergreen, twining climber about 2m in height, with oval, glossy, golden-yellow to yellow-green leaves and sweetly-scented, creamy-white flowers in mid and late summer that fade to pale yellow with age

alternative_names: apple 'Red Windsor'|Malus domestica 'Sweet Lilibet'|Malus domestica 'Red Alkmene'
description: A dessert cultivar perfect for smaller gardens; heavy crops of deep red fruits, ready to eat in September, which keep for up to a month. Crisp juicy flesh with aromatic flavour. Happy grown in a large pot; good resistance to many common diseases. Flowers have some frost resistance at blossom time. Pollination Group 2; partially self-fertile
An encrusted saxifrage producing evergreen mats of blue-green leaf rosettes with grey lime deposits. In early summer, sprays of small, pink flowers are produced on 20cm stems

A bushy dwarf plant to 40-50cm tall, branching mainly from the base and evergreen if not cut back by frosts, with aromatic, small, ovate, downy, mid green leaves with a narrow white margin. Bright crimson flowers with purple calyx are borne in terminal racemes from summer to autumn continuing to the first frosts

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to around 35cm high and 75cm across. Leaves are rounded to heart-shaped with pointed tips, dark green with broad margins of golden and pale lemon yellows. Produces loose clusters of tubular, pale purple flowers on upright stems in late summer

Herbaceous perennial variety for full or dappled shade capabable to resist leaf scorching in direct sunlight, has fine large deeply corrugated textured sea-green foliage with wavy golden margins. Slow to grow, will reach its full potential in shade, blossoming in summer with tall white bell-shaped flowers. Exposure to sunlight can alter varigation and colour.

primary_name: Saxifraga from Jiri Kovak's rock garden

description: A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, wavy-edged green foliage and white, waxy undersides. Upright red-purple stems of pale lavender-purple to almost white flowers appear in the summer

A giant, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated yellow foliage and irregular, green wavy margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer. A sport of Hosta 'Piedmont Gold'
A bulbous perennial to 20cm, with grey-green leaves and solitary, nodding, white flowers; the inner petals marked with a green, scissor-shaped mark

An evergreen fern with short creeping rhizomes bearing large bright green, wavy leaflets on pendulous sterile fronds. Young growth is often orange to deep red. The erect, fertile fronds have leaflets greatly reduced in width which curl and turn black as the spores ripen
plant_range: New Zealand, Chatham Is., Kermadec Is.

description: A perennial to 80cm tall, with pinnate leaves divided into many narrowly lance-shaped leaflets, and compact sprays of open bell-shaped light violet-blueflowers throughout the summer

primary_name: Plectranthus saccatus subsp. saccatus var. saccatus

description: An evergreen perennial, angel pelargonium, compact and bushy with small rounded green leaves and magenta-pink with pale pink edged flowers and dark pink upper petals in summer.

alternative_names: Agropyron spicatum var. inerme|Pseudoroegneria spicata subsp. inermis|Agropyron inerme

description: An annual with stems trailing to 90cm long. Fragrant, double, lilac-purple flowers with heavy veining are borne from summer into autumn

An upright, clump-forming perennial varying between 1-2m tall, with dissected, dark green leaves with good autumn tints, and pale to mid purple flowers from late summer into autumn that darken as the season progresses

A clump-forming, rhizomatous, evergreen perennial about 1m tall, with long, broadly lance-shaped glossy dark green leaves, sometimes with pale yellow spots. Yellow-tinted, purple-pink, star-shaped flowers may appear at the base of the plant in summer, followed by green berries. Although grown as a houseplant, it is a useful garden plant in mild areas, and is tolerant of shade and dry conditions

A deciduous shrub, reaching 1.5-1.8m (5-6ft) high. Bears green, simple, opposite, oval to lance-shaped, serrated leaves that are covered on the undersides with white, silky down. Slender panicles of white flowers are borne in May

A clump-forming perennial to around 1m tall and wide forming a mound of bronze-tinged, toothed and divided leaves. Stout plumes of deep pink flowers that darken to red are borne above the foliage in summer and autumn

alternative_names: Wallich's sweet box|Sarcococca coriacea ambig. [2]|Sarcococca coriacea Müll.Arg. [4]|Sarcococca pruniformis misapplied
description: A loosely-clumping evergreen shrub, up to 2m tall, with glossy, lanceolate leaves, to 10cm long, on tall, arching stems. The small, scented, white winter flowers are followed by black fruits

An evergreen, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, mid-green leaves and sturdy stems that hold rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped white to pale pink flowers that emerge from green-white buds in summer
A compact, evergreen herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet-shaped pure white flowers in the summer
Has large tussocks of drooping, arching, glaucous foliage and upright silvery flower panicles. It flowers late, looking good well into early winter

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, fragrant, pale lavender coloured flowers with a green throat to 18cm across in summer. This cultivar also flowers at night

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, lavender coloured flowers that have a green throat to 9cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for over 16 hours a day

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 91cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and very large, very fragrant, deep yellow, spider-type flowers that have a green throat to 25cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 102cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant greenish-yellow flowers with a green throat to 17cm across in summer

An evergreen shrub to about 80cm high, with a spreading habit, and ovate, slightly glossy green leaves that are flushed bronze when young. Produces rounded clusters of 6-8 broadly funnel-shaped, bright red flowers in late spring
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce small, open panicles of trumpet-shaped blue to pale mauve flowers in summer

A small, spreadying, semi-evergreen, trailing alpine perennial with green, lance-shaped foliage. Outward facing, deep violet-blue star-shaped single flowers provide a long flowering display in summer. Easy to grow in containers and ideal as ground cover

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Large, semi-cactus form flowers up to 20cm across, produced from mid-summer until the first frost, are bright coral-pink, shading to yellow in the centre. The edges of the long, pointed petals are tightly rolled under, and slightly twisted, creating a sea-anemone look

Tall, clump-forming, tuberous perennial about 90cm in height with toothed, dark green leaves. This semi-cactus form has a profusion of striking, fully double, bright red flowers with long, pointed petals creating a spiky effect, that bloom from midsummer until autumn

Dwarf, bedding dahlia to about 30-50cm tall, with dark stems and mid-green leaves. Fully double, bright pink flowers to 10cm across, with slightly incurved petals, are produced from mid-summer until frosted in autumn

Tuberous-rooted perennial about 60-90cm tall, with mid-green leaves, flowering from midsummer until the first frosts. The cherry-red blooms, boldly tipped and edged white, have neat rows of tightly inrolled petals, forming a flattened ball to 10cm across
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Salmon pink and yellow, spiky cactus-form flowers appear from summer until the first frosts
A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with dark stems and dark green foliage. The substantial-looking flowers, 15-20cm across, are pure, rich red and produced from mid-summer to the first frost
A dwarf, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Pure white flowers with a yellow centre appear from summer until the first frosts
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Very large purple decorative form flowers, edged with white, appear from summer until the first frosts

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Large, light orange flowers up to 20cm across are produced from mid-summer until the first frost. As the outer petals open the edges roll under, creating a sunburst effect
A fairly short, tuberous-rooted perennial to 60cm, with mid-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frosts bears white flowers, 10cm across, with strongly quilled petals giving a spiky effect

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to 1.1m, with mid-green foliage, blooming from mid-summer to the first frosts. Flowers are white, 20cm across, shading to lemon yellow in the centre. The petals are narrowly quilled, with gentle curves and twists, giving a swirly, spidery effect
A bushy, evergreen perennial, to 45cm tall, with narrow, dark green leaves and short, upright spikes of fragrant, bright yellow flowers opening from dark buds in late spring through to late summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 80cm in height when in flower. It forms clumps of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, fragrant, pale cream-yellow flowers that have a yellow eye zone to 11cm across in summer.
Dwarf evergreen conifer to about 50cm in height and spread and of globose or conical habit with slightly contorted silver-blue needles
A highly attractive, compact, mult-stemmed, deciduous shrub with arching branches of dark green foliage and fragrant, four petalled, semi-double, white flowers in early summer

A short-lived perennial with lobed rounded leaves and long, erect pyramids of open funnel-shaped flowers that can be single, semi-double and double all at once in one stem. Petals are dark burgundy edged pale pink with intricate dark red veins in summer.

A compact herbaceous perennial to 60cm with narrow, upright leaves. Small flowers, 6cm across, have yellow outer petals, orange-red inner petals with a broad yellow stripe, and a yellow throat and are produced from early summer to early autumn

A deciduous, clump-forming perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and erect stems of large, trumpet shaped flowers, pale lavender to darker lavender on the edges of the petals with a yellow-green throat

A slow-growing evergreen shrub, with an open, upright habit and glossy dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Formal double, pale creamy yellow flowers to around 7cm across are produced in mid spring

A compact, evergreen, mat-forming perennial with rosettes of green leaves, sometimes flushed red at the tip and edge. In late spring and summer, small scented white flowers with red spots are borne on arching stems up to 48cm long

alternative_names: cranesbill 'Spring Fling'|Geranium 'Spring Fling'|Geranium × oxonianum 'Kurt's Variegated'|Geranium × oxonianum 'Jester'

Leaves become more green over summer. Pink flowers with dark pink veins and pale near-white centres are produced in summer

A small, deciduous shrub to 1.5m tall and wide with a greyish,felt-like covering andweeping branches. Ovate, aromatic leaves to 7.5cm long are coarsely toothed; violet-blue flowers borne in dense cymes extending from the upper leaf axils appear from midsummer to early autumn

A rhizomatous perennial, to 90cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have a musky scent, ruffled rose and buff-coloured standards, cream falls with a mauve border, and an orange beard. Early midseason
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial producing upright sprays of rich yellow flowers, each 3-4cm across, on stems to 60cm tall from midsummer into autumn

Dense, clump-forming, evergreen perennial sedge, 60cm tall, with slightly arching, rich, warm bronze to chocolate-brown foliage. Produces semi-trailing, brown flower spikes within the foliage, late spring to early summer

A bulbous perennial to 25cmwith relatively large, broad, pleated leaves that are a feature in themselves. Large, solitary, nodding, white flowers with a small, green, inverted V on the inner petals, are produced in mid- to late winter

An upright, clump-forming perennial to 1.2m high, with branching stems and ovate to lance-shaped green leaves. Daisy-like flowers are produced at the tips of wiry stems from late summer to autumn, with dome-shaped dark brown central discs surrounded by fiery orange-red petals

A herbaceous perennial to about 70cm high with dark green foliage. Double flowers to 10cm across are borne from mid-summer into autumn and comprise creamy-white petals flushed with pink and marked with yellow at the base

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Semi-double white flowers surrounded by green and white bracts and with yellow stamens, appear in the spring

alternative_names: narrow-leaved bird of paradise|Strelitzia reginae var. juncea

Bushy upright shrub rose about 1.2m tall, with healthy glossy dark green foliage. The large, very double, lavender-pink quartered blooms produced singly and in clusters, have a strong fragrance and repeat-flower from summer to autumn
A semi-evergreen perennial, to about 20cm, producing a rosette of spoon-shaped leaves. The spring flowers have a golden centre, and gold-rimmed, mahogany petals

Bushy, upright rose from the Paramount Collection, to about 80cm in height, with semi-glossy dark green foliage. Large, lightly scented, very double, creamy-white blooms flushed palest pink, open from ovoid buds, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

alternative_names: hydrangea 'Merveille Sanguine'|Hydrangea macrophylla 'Colour Fantasy'|Hydrangea macrophylla 'Folis Purpureus'|Hydrangea macrophylla [Color Fantasy]|Hydrangea macrophylla 'Brunette'

Compact, bushy rose to 2m tall, with healthy, glossy mid-green leaves and lightly scented, semi-double, mid-yellow blooms to 9cm across, that fade to cream then white, and appear repeatedly in summer and autumn

Bushy, upright rose to 1.2m tall, with semi-glossy dark green foliage and bearing well-formed, fragrant, yellow blooms, fading to creamy-lemon on the outer petals and repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

A large, bushy rose to about 1.2m tall, with semi-glossy, mid-green foliage. Small clusters of rounded buds open to strongly fragrant, fully double yellow blooms become pale yellow with age, and repeat-flower in flushes from early summer to autumn

A small, neat climbing rose with upright growth to about 2m tall, with very glossy dark green leaves, and bearing masses of lightly scented, deep pink double blooms flecked and streaked white, repeat-flowering from midsummer to autumn
Compact, bushy Patio climber to 2m tall, with healthy, dark green, matt foliage on flexible stems, and bearing a profusion of small, fully-double, pure-white blooms through summer and into autumn
A deciduous perennial with broad, green leaves and a branching habit. In summer, ruffled golden yellow flowers emerge which are attractive to butterflies

An erect, tuberous perennial which would normally have yellow flowers. White and mauve flowers are less common. The mauve-flowered variety has green, lance-shaped leaves and three-petalled, crinkly mauve flowers in the spring

Bushy rose to about 1.5m tall, with matt green foliage and bearing lightly scented, double, high-centred, pale-yellow blooms, produced singly or in small clusters from long pointed buds, and repeat-flowering through summer and autumn
Compact, bushy rose to 50cm tall, with mid-green foliage and lightly-scented, bright yellow blooms, continuously borne through summer and autumn

A medium-sized, deciduous to semi-evergreen shrub with narrowly-ovate leaves which are bronze when young before turning dark green as they mature. The small, sweetly-scented pink-cream flowers appear on bare stems in winter to early spring and may be followed by red berries in summer

A spreading tree to 10m tall with narowly ovate, toothed leaves to 10cm long, green above with white undersides and turning rich orange and red shades in autumn. Clusters of small, white, spring flowers are followed by hanging orange to red fruits in autumn
A semi-evergreen perennial to 15cm, with a rosette of dark green leaves flushed with purple, and purplish-pink flowers with pale pink stripes and yellow eyes
An evergreen shrub up to 1.1m high, with an upright to slightly spreading habit and aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves 5-6cm long. Spikes of fragrant, violet-blue flowers appear in late summer

alternative_names: English lavender 'Peter Pan'|Lavandula 'Peter Pan'|Lavandula angustifolia 'Hidcote B'
description: A shrub up to 45cm high, occasionally up to 65cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves 3-5cm long, and flowering stems up to 25cm long topped by spikes 3-3.5cm long of fragrant, vibrant violet flowers in midsummer
A compact, evergreen shrub to around 60cm in height, with glossy, dark green leathery oval-shaped leaves. Trusses of trumpet-shaped pale yellow flowers appear in April to May

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 74cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and very large, fragrant, spider-type, pale yellow flowers that have a green throat to 20cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 102cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, fragrant, spider-type greenish-yellow flowers that have a faint bronze eye-zone above a green throat to 20cm across in summer

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 81cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and orchid-like, medium blue flowers with a green star-shaped throat to 18cm across in summer. Flowers last no more than 24 hours, opening late in the day and remaining open during the night

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and fragrant, crimson-red flowers, with a yellow throat to 24cm across in summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with narrow, upright leaves to around 60cm tall. The fragrant flowers, 15cm across, are deep red with black shading and golden-yellow throat

A densely tufted, perennial evergreen grass, forming a mound of linear, dark green leaves to 30cm long. From midsummer to late autumn it produces airy, open clusters of pink spikelets held on slender stems above the foliage; these are good for cutting. Drought tolerant once established and suitable for coastal sites or containers

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 84cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and large, unusual wavy-edged maroon and yellow flowers to 19cm across in summer

An upright, clump-forming perennial to 65cm high, with semi-evergreen, strap-shaped foliage. Large flowers to 14cm across are borne in summer on branching stems, with creamy, frilly-edged petals with deep maroon eyes and lime green throats
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 70cm in height, with arching, strap-like green foliage. Red-dark orange flowers with a golden orange throat appear from summer to early autumn

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, creamy-white flowers that have a violet eye-zone above a green throat to 11cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves, and lavender-pink coloured flowers that have a yellow-gold frilly edge above a green throat to 14cm across in summer

A deciduous herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant creamy-white flowers with a dark red eyezone and green throat to 11cm across in summer
A clump-forming perennial, to around 1m high in flower, with narrow, grass-like leaves. Flowers have white petals, with purple-flushed standards and fine purple veining on the falls
Bushy, upright rose to about 1.5m tall, with long sturdy, thorny stems clothed in glossy dark green leaves. Prolific, large, double, butter-yellow blooms repeat-flower through summer into autumn

A very tall bamboo forming slowly-spreading clumps to 4m wide and upright canes to 15m or more in ideal conditions. The solid canes up to 6cm in diameter have a striped appearance with a green band around the nodes and yellow-green colouring between the nodes; leaves are mid-green, up to 12cm long and narrowly lances-shaped

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent with rosettes of pointed, fleshy leaves to 3cm across. The foliage is red in summer, taking on green hues in autumn. Starry pink flowers are held in clusters on leafy stems to 15cm tall in summer. The rosettes die after flowering but are replaced by offsets on lateral runners

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing large, fleshy rosettes, the spoon-shaped leaves vary from glowing red in spring, to dark brown in summer, then fading to green and brown in autumn and winter. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes, in clusters, the fairly upright, pointed, silvery-grey leaves, blushed soft pink, are flushed vibrant dark pink in winter. Tall stems of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A clump-forming perennial to 30cm tall, with narrowly linear, rosemary-like leaves. In midsummer it produces tubular, deep violet-blue flowers with a lighter margin; these are held in whorls on softly hairy flowerspikes

alternative_names: soap aloe|Aloe picta|Aloe latifolia|Aloe macracantha|Aloe saponaria
description: A stemless or short-stemmed succulent about 70cm tall, with thorny blue-green leaves which are strongly speckled white and form a neat, fleshy rosette. In early spring, spires of light orange flowers are held on tall branched stems, forming a flat-topped flowerhead

A perennial bulb, to around 18cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with a long olive green ovary, long, curving outer petals, and inner petals almost entirely green, with markings darker towards the tips. Each bulb can produce two flowers in good conditions once established

A large, broadly conicaltree with smooth grey bark. The narrowly oval, double-toothed leaves have prominent veins and are up to 27cm long. They emerge purple-bronze in spring, becoming olive-green. Pale green, papery catkins up to 30cm long appear in spring, gradually fading to tawny brown

primary_name: Corydalis solida subsp. solida Munich form
alternative_names: Corydalis solida subsp. solida from Munich Botanic Garden|Corydalis solida subsp. solida 'Nymphenburg'|Corydalis solida f. transsylvanica 'Nymphenburg'
