description: A small, compact, mound-forming evergreen shrub to about 1-1.2m in height, with arching branches and glossy yellow-green leaves. Pairs of tubular white flowers 1cm long are produced from the leaf axils in spring, and may be followed by glossy, blue-purple berries
A compact, bushy deciduous shrub with small pinnate green leaves reaching a height and spread of 60cm, covered in open, saucer-shaped creamy white flowers from May to September

A slow-growing evergreen conifer cultivar with an elegant, upright pyramid habit, proudly displaying very dreamy blue upcurved needles. The annual growth is 3-5 cm so it will take a while to grow into a kingly size

A compact, evergreen, variegated shrub with upright, bushy growth to around 70cm high and wide. Young foliage emerges white with pale green markings before maturing to dark green with creamy-white blotches. Small, pale green flowers in summer may be followed by autumn fruits

A clump-forming, vigorous deciduous perennial with strap-shaped, variegated foliage which emerges creamy-white with dark green stripes, fading to pale yellow-green as the season progresses. Inconspicuous yellow-brown flower spikes appear in the summer
A dwarf, slow-growing evergreen conifer with an irregular pyramid-shaped habit and pale golden yellow to green foliage. An ideal variety for pots and containers

alternative_names: smoke tree [Green Fountain]|smoke bush [Green Fountain]|Cotinus coggygria 'Kolcot'
description: A neat and compact, bushy deciduous shrub with rounded dark green foliage turning to shades of bright red and orange in the autumn. Large, greenish-pink feathery plumes of flowers, which look like smoke, appear in summer
Produces bright red stems in spring, with leaves that start pinky-red, then turn orange before fading to light, yellowy-green
An evergreen sub-shrub forming a mat to 15cm in height, of very glossy, dark green, coarsely toothed, obovate leaves to 7cm in length, with erect spikes of small, white flowers in early summer

alternative_names: giant viper's bugloss 'Snow Tower'|Echium pininana alba 'Snow Tower'
description: A triennial plant that in its first and second year forms a rosette to 60cm across, composed of rough, lance-shaped leaves. In its third summer it throws up a huge (3m) flower spike, densely packed with thousands of small white flowers; these are irresistible to bees

A short-lived perennial to around 70cm in height, producing large, flat, open rosettes of woolly, grey-green leaves with a rusty tinge in spring. Strong racemes of yellow flowers with orange anthers open on dense spikes over a long flowering period in summer. Makes a great architectural plant, even with just the leaves and no flowers

A vigorous upright, deciduous shrub about 1.5m tall, with spiny stems and glossy dark green leaves. Single, salmon-pink flowers edged and splashed white with pale yellow anthers, appear in mid-spring, followed by large yellow-green fruits. These can be used to make jams and jellies but please see notes on toxicity for further advice
A vigorous, deciduous climber with oval leaves and abundant, exceptionally fragrant, creamy-white to yellow flowers from summer to autumn, followed by red berries

alternative_names: spring gentian 'Angulosa' of gardens|Gentiana angulosa misapplied|Gentiana verna subsp. angulosa hort.
description: A compact perennial forming a mat of small, lance-shaped, evergreen leaves, with erect stems carrying solitary deep sky-blue flowers 3.5cm across in spring and early summer
A compact, almost stemless plant with ovate creamy-green leaves with darker green margins and midrib
A shrubby, evergreen perennial with ovate, dark green leaves to 25cm in length, boldly splashed and marbled with white

Slow-growing, upright, pyramidal conifer to 80cm tall after 10 years, growing up to 8cm annually, with dense branching and exceptionally, light blue foliage; one of several seedlings treated with radioactive cobalt, resulting in intensely blue growth
A free-flowering cultivar that is slow growing and compact in habit. In early spring the branches are smothered in rosy-mauve flowers before the heart-shaped leaves appear
An evergreen shrub (herbaceous in cold areas) with ovate leaves and loose panicles of nodding, dusky pink flowers in summer, marked with yellow and red in the throat

A bushy, clump-forming perennial up to 90cm high, with bright green, palmate leaves divided into narrow leaflets. Upright spikes of lightly scented, creamy white flowers touched with pale yellow are produced from early to mid summer

alternative_names: sweet pea 'High Scent'|Lathyrus odoratus 'April in Paris'|Lathyrus odoratus 'Kings High Scent'|Lathyrus odoratus 'Brilliant Fragrance'|Lathyrus odoratus 'Hiscent'
description: A free-flowering sweet pea, growing to 1.8m high. Flower stems to 20cm long, bearing 3-4 flowers, 4cm in diameter, creamy white with a dark violet picotee edge. Highly scented as per its name

primary_name: Ixora coccinea var. coccinea f. coccinea
Ixora coccinea var. coccinea f. lutea

description: A vigorous sweet pea to 2m. The strongly scented flowers have reflexed, wavy standards and spreading, wavy wings which are silvery white, with deep purple-pink flushing on the reverse, creating a picotee edge
A large-flowered, Spencer type most notable for its long flowering stems and many wavy-edged, white flowers per stem. Height 1.5-2.5m
A large bushy deciduous shrub with leaves composed of narrow dark green leaflets, and masses of small white flowers over a long period from late spring to autumn

A semi-evergreen shrub reaching around 1m tall and wide. It has green leaves in pairs and clusters of yellow flowers. These develop into tall red berries and retain their yellow-green calyx below. Used by florists for flower arrangements

alternative_names: clematis 'Plena'|Clematis florida 'Plena'|Clematis florida 'Alba Plena'|Clematis florida var. plena|Clematis florida 'Flore Pleno'
description: A double-flowered selection, growing to 2.5m or more in height. The greenish-white flowers are borne from summer to autumn on the current year's growth
A compact deciduous shrub with lace-cap flower-heads with mauve-pink to blue sterile flowers surrounding blue fertile flowers, in late summer

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm, with mid-green foliage. Pure vibrant yellow flowers about 12cm across are produced from mid-summer until the first frost. The petals are slightly curved inwards, the edges rolled under, and some twisted, creating a swirling effect

A bulbous perennial, to around 80cm high with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Upward-facing, fragrant, compact clear white flowers, pale green near the centre, appear in summer
A tuberous perennial producing 10cm wide, double flowers with densely packed purple-pink florets, each with a paler pink edge. It grows to 130cm

A bamboo-like, evergreen perennial to 2m, with stiff, smooth, bright green stems banded with brown bracts. The upper part of the plant produces dense clusters of fine, feathery, leaf-like, modified stems, topped with loose, upright spikes of small, red-brown, grass-like flowers

alternative_names: Californian May bush|Christmas berry|red chokeberry|tollon|toyon|Photinia arbutifolia|Heteromeles arbutifolia

description: A compact tuberous perennial to around 20cm high, with long, heart-shaped dark green leaves, with paler silvery green markings on the veins and a purple flush on the undersides. In ideal conditions leaves can be up to 25cm long. Solitary, small greenish spathes, surrounding a cream-coloured spadix with a long protruding 'tail', are produced sporadically from spring to late summer in cultivation; flowers are strongly fragrant and followed by small oval-shaped green berries

A medium-sized weeping tree to 6m tall, with cascading branches creating a waterfall effect. The rounded leaves are bronzy in spring, turning red, orange and yellow in autumn and smelling strongly of toffee apples when opening and at leaf fall
A rare, vigorous variety of cider apple tree to around 7m in height, with a sharp flavour. The fruit is ready to press by mid October. Pollination group 3

A mid-season, dual-purpose apple with very greasy, green then yellow skin and crisp, refreshing, cream flesh. A tip-bearing tree, cropping in early autumn, fruit storing to mid-autumn. Requires a group 4 or 5 pollinator
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Fragrant flowers are pink with a darker pink eye and a yellow-green throat

Large, vigorous, deciduous climber about 6-8m tall, with mid to dark green leaves and large, scented. white flowers to about 10cm across, some with a faint pink tinge to the base of the tepals, and creamy-yellow stamens, flowering from mid to late spring

primary_name: Artemisia campestris subsp. borealis var. borealis
alternative_names: Artemisia campestris subsp. borealis var. purshii

primary_name: Herbertia platensis hort. ex L. H. Bailey

description: A bushy perennial, to around 60cm high, with a spreading habit, strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Yellow flowers, with paler tips to the petals and red flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

An intersectional hybrid between a tree peony and a herbaceous peony forming a plant about 80cm high with a woody base. It has deeply divided, mid-green leaves with pointed segments, and large, scented, semi-double to double, lemon-yellow flowers in early to mid-summer

A bushy perennial, to around 90cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Fragrant, semi-double yellow flowers, with toothed petals and red flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 80cm high, with strong stems and divided green leaves. In late spring and early summer produces large, semi-double, light yellow flowers with touches of red in the base

A bushy perennial, to around 90cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Semi-double white flowers, sometimes with faint purple-pink flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

A clump-forming perennial, to 1.5m high in flower, with fleshy roots and narrowly lance-shaped, mid green leaves that die back after flowering. Tall spikes of small, densely packed white flowers, with pale green midribs on the outer petals and conspicuous anthers, are produced in early summer. Flower heads can be 60cm long or more

A compact, deciduous shrub to 1.5m high, with ovate, toothed leaves. In summer produces flattened, lace-cap flower-heads of large, dark blue or violet (pink on chalky soils) sterile flowers surrounding clusters of tiny pale budded fertile flowers

A compact, deciduous shrub up to 1m high and wide, with flowerheads consisting of small fertile white flowers, surrounded by large sterile florets with three sepals, varying from white to pink and rosy red, becoming deeper red in full sun, in early summer

A large, deciduous shrub or spreading, small tree to 8m tall, the dark green leaves are up to 30cm long and 15cm wide, and the flowers, up to 15cm across, appear in late spring and early into midsummer. These are strongly scented, bowl-shaped, with 10-15 white petals and a large boss of deep red stamens in the centre. Ornamental fruits turn pink in autumn

A large, deciduous shrub or spreading, small tree to 8m tall, with dark green leaves to 15cm long. Strongly scented, cup-shaped flowers appear in late spring and early into midsummer, with 12 white tepals and a very large and prominent boss of deep red stamens in the centre. Ornamental fruits with very large seeds, turn crimson-pink in autumn

A spreading, deciduous shrub or small tree to 5m in height with large, leathery, bright green leaves to 20cm long, glaucous beneath. In early and mid-summer, the spherical white flower buds open to deeply cup-shaped, strongly fragrant flowers to 15cm across with prominent red anthers. A more compact form than Magnolia x wieseneri.

A woody, evergreen, twining climber about 7-9m in height, with narrow, glossy, grey-green to mid-green leaves, 8cm long with silvery veins, turning bronze-purple in winter, and sweetly-scented, creamy-white flowers in mid and late summer that fade to pale yellow with age
A clump-forming, bulbous perennial to 20cm high with linear, semi-upright leaves. In spring, leafless stems bear dense heads of small, urn-shaped, deep sky blue flowers rimmed with white

An unusual hardy shrub, with small variegated pale green leaves with irregular white margins, to around 30cm in height. Small, upward-facing yellow, red and blue flowers appear from spring through to autumn and are followed by red berries. Ideal when planted as ground cover in cooler areas of the garden or in containers and hanging baskets

A shrub up to 80cm high, with an open sprawling habit, evergreen, aromatic, silver-grey leaves 3-4.5cm long, and flowering stems up to 40cm long topped by spikes up to 13cm long of sweetly fragrant dark purple flowers in summer
A compact, clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial producing large, velvety green foliage. Creamy flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage from summer through until the autumn
An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall with grey-green, strap-like, arching foliage. Short, fat spikes of coral-red flowers fading to yellow are borne on stout stems in summer

A low-growing evergreen shrub with a dense, spreading habit and needle-like green leaves. Produces clusters of honeysuckle-like flowers, with long styles and curving sepals, in shades from pale pink to deep rose. Flowers over a long period from winter to late spring or summer

A neat, upright, evergreen shrub that grows to about 2.5m high, with narrow-elliptical, dark green leaves to 3.5 cm long. Saucer-shaped, 5-petalled brilliant red flowers to 2.5cm across, with a prominent central ring of stamens, appear in late spring

An evergreen shrub, up to 2m in height, with peachy-pink flowers in early summer and then sporadically in autumn. The stamens have an evolving colouration, changing from pink to white, with rich golden anthers at their tips and great for pollinators. Broad new leaves emerge in a silvery flourish with a pink flush before maturing to olive green, borne on a rounded bushy branching frame

An upright shrub up to 3m in height, with lanceolate grey-green, aromatic and fairly stiff leaves. The decorative feature of this cultivar are the large, soft-pink inflorescences with yellow anthers that appear from summer to autumn, the blooms fading to white as they age

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial, to around 60cm high, with an upright habit and lobed green leaves. Tall, branching stems bear small dark purple flowers, with reflexed petals and white centres, in late spring to early summer
A compact perennial, to 30cm tall, with aromatic, lance-shaped, grey-green leaves and spikes of deep violet flowers held on upright stems in summer
An annual climber, up to around 2.4m high, with curling tendrils and pairs of green leaves. Strongly scented, bright mauve-purple flowers are produced in summer

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, single saucer-shaped red flowers with a larger centre of edged cream, red petaloids appear in summer.

An erect herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular raspberry-red flowers with buds that never fully open upover a long period of time in summer.
A bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic, slightly grey-green leaves. Spikes of fragrant, very pale pink flowers are borne on slender stems from early to mid summer

A bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Long spikes of fragrant purple flowers, opening from dark purple buds, are borne on tall slender stems in summer. This cultivar holds its colour well when cut for drying

A medium-sized, evergreen shrub to around 4m in height, with a conical shape and leathery, glossy, dark green, mostly spineless leaves which take on a blue-purple tint during colder weather. White flowers appear in spring followed by bright red berries if pollinated by a male variety nearby

A deciduous shrub with green, arching, cane-like stems and soft, pointed leaves. Small white flowers, with deep purply-red bracts, appear in hanging clusters in summer and autumn, followed by shiny, deep purple berries

alternative_names: thyme Coccineus Group|Thymus 'Coccineus'|Thymus 'Creeping Red'|Thymus serpyllum f. coccineus|Thymus serpyllum coccineus|Thymus praecox 'Coccineus'|Thymus serpyllum coccineus 'Minor' misapplied [1]
description: A creeping evergreen subshrub, forming a wide mat to 5cm tall, with very small, aromatic dark green leaves. Two-lipped, dark pink to magenta tubular-shaped flowers appear in the summer. Great for ground cover, with edible flowers

alternative_names: wild thyme|Breckland thyme|creeping thyme|mother of thyme
description: A dwarf, aromatic, evergreen shrub forming a low, wide mat to 5cm in height. It has tiny, pointed, dark green leaves and tight clusters of purple flowers in summer

alternative_names: thyme 'Purple Beauty'|Thymus (Coccineus Group) 'Atropurpureus' Schleipfer [1]|Thymus serpyllum 'Purple Beauty'|Thymus atropurpureus|Thymus serpyllum 'Atropurpureus'
description: A dense, mat forming, evergreen sub-shrub with small, ovate, highly aromatic, dark green leaves and dense whorls of small, purple-pink flowers appearing in early summer

alternative_names: Thymus serpyllum f. coccineus 'Hardstoft Red'|Thymus serpyllum coccineus variegated|Thymus 'Hardstoft Red'
Himalayan blue poppy 'Bobby Masterton'|Meconopsis grandis 'Betty Sherriff's Dream Poppy'
description: A short-lived perennial about 1m tall, forming a rosette of oval leaves suffused with red-purple when young. In summer, erect, leafy stems bear a cluster of sky blue poppies with contrasting yellow stamens. The seed capsules, covered in bristly hairs, are decorative but contain no viable seed

A bushy, half-hardy deciduous perennial to around 250cm in height, with mid-green, ovate, melon-scented aromatic foliage. Narrow, bright scarlet-red flowers appear freely from June to November. The flowers can be used to flavour cakes, drinks or cocktails and in salads

alternative_names: Cerinthe major 'Bouquet Gold'|Cerinthe minor subsp. aurantiaca 'Bouquet Gold'

description: A compact, clump-forming, half-hardy annual growing to 30cm (12in) high with mid-green ovate leaves and clusters of fluffy light blue-purple flowers from late spring through to autumn. Its compact form and long flowering period, make it ideal for using at the front of borders, in bedding schemes and in containers.

primary_name: Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. albiflorum 'Linnett Longbow'
Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. albiflorum 'Linnett Stargazer'
Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. hederifolium 'Fairy Longbow'
Cyclamen hederifolium var. hederifolium f. hederifolium 'Oliver Twist'

description: A large-flowered gladiolus, height around 1-1.2m high, with green sword like leaves and an erect flower spike with around 10 - 12 flower buds. The bold and blousy flowers are a flame orange-red with palest yellow to white throats and flecks of orange-red. Dramatic, eye-catching blooms for the summer garden.

A large-flowered gladiolus, height around 1m, with green sword like leaves and an erect flower spike with around 10 flower buds. The large flowers have a velvety appearance and are a rich raspberry magenta with a very fine white edge bordering the outer petals of each bloom. Sumptous and dramatic blooms for the summer garden.

A branching annual to around 60cm high, with grey-green leaves that are toothed at the base of the plant and pinnately divided on the stems. Sweetly scented, thistle-like, creamy white flowers are produced on upright stems from late spring to summer

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent perennial producing rosettes of fleshy, oval to strap-shaped, dark purple-black leaves with green bases. Flower spikes of pink flowers from mature rosettes die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, lightly fragrant, ruffled, lavender-blue flowers with dark navy blue falls with white markings and tangerine orange beards, appear from late spring to early summer
Grows to 60cm high, with a 60cm spread. Leaves are bronze-coloured, contrasting with pale purplish-pink flowers borne over a relatively long season from late spring to summer
A compact, bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green foliage and red and pale yellow flowers with yellow centres which appear from July through until September

A large deciduous shrub or small tree to 5m in height. New branches are purple, young leaves purple until flowering, changing to green. Slender stellate bracts start greenish and slightly pink and lighten to pure white, surrounding a small green flowerhead, in June. These are followed by strawberry like fruits in late summer.

Sturdy, spreading, deciduous small tree about 6-8m tall, a hybrid between M. soulangeana 'Burgundy' and M. 'Vulcan' with dark green leaves, and clear lilac-purple, goblet-shaped blooms produced in mid-spring

Multi-branched, deciduous tree or large shrub reaching over 5m in height with mid-green leaves. Large, bowl-shaped flowers of purplish-red, are produced freely over a long period in spring, from a young age

A bulbous perennial with narrow, grey-green leaves and white, nodding flowers held on slender stems to around 15cm tall. Outer flower segments are occasionally marked with green at the apex whilst the inner segments have variable green markings at their tips

A spreading deciduous tree, to 10m in height, with ovate, purple-green leaves, and clusters of very large, dark pink flowers in spring. Dark red-purple fruits, 4cm wide, are produced in autumn and one of the best for making crab apple jelly
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, purple-blue flowers, with a white centre, appearing in the spring
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, reddish-brown flowers with a gold centre, appearing in the spring

An upright, mounded cultivar forming a compact dome to around 18cm high. It produces single, daisy-like flowers in autumn with white ray florets, sometimes splashed with pink, surrounding a yellow centre
A compact herbaceous perennial to around 30cm tall bearing semi-double pale yellow flowerheads from early autumn
A cultivar that has bright yellow, double blooms in early autumn and a neat, globular habit . Height around 30cm when grown pinched out
Reaches around 30cm in height and is covered by yellow, double flowers in late summer to early autumn
A cultivar that, grown as a cushion mum, has a domed habit up to 30cm in height. It produces deep pink single flowers with a yellow centre in early autumn
A free-flowering spray chrysanthemum with anemone-centred flowers, the florets dull gold, paler on the reverse
A spray chrysanthemum flowering in late autumn, with light dusky purple rays, the inner ones tinged with yellow, around an anemone centre
A cultivar that reaches around 120cm in height. Grown as a late spray, it bears white double flowers, tinged green in the centre as they open
A compact, evergreen hardy perennial with a mat of narrow, grey-green foliage. Fragrant, single white flowers with a dark magenta-red eye and fringed petals appear throughout the summer

A deciduous, upright, bushy shrub with dark green foliage, and abundant pendent double flowers which have a purple corolla and red sepals and stamens from summer through to autumn. Very suitable for containers and hanging baskets

Large, suckering, deciduous shrub, about 2m tall, with bright green, oval to lance-shaped, toothed leaves, turning yellow in autumn. Clusters of small white flowers in mid-spring, are followed by masses of very long-lasting, large red berries if pollinated by a male plant; berries persisting well into winter
An evergreen, mat-forming perennial to 10cm tall with small rounded leaves. Relatively large, deep violet-purple flowers with small yellow eyes are borne in spring

An elegant variety, characterised by tall spires densely populated with unique flowers edged in pale purple, fading to a white centre. Adds height and structure to a border and helps to enhance biodiversity by attracting bees and other pollinating insects

An evergreen, perennial, alpine auricula, up to 20cm tall, with rosettes of light green leaves. Clusters of red-purple flowers with paler edges and white centres, are produced on short stems in mid- to late spring
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage and fragrant, very pale pink flowers with wavy edges and a pale yellow centre, appearing in the spring

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, double dark velvety-red flowers, with a barely visible gold centre, appearing in the spring
An evergreen, perennial, alpine auricula to 15cm tall, with rosettes of light green leaves. Clusters of rich purple-red flowers with white centres and white eyes are produced in spring

A strong-growing tender, upright or spreading evergreen small tree or shrub with narrow, oval, wavy-edged yellow to green leaves. Reaches a height of 1-5m. Insignificant flowers are yellow greenish-red, and borne in clusters, in summer

A strong-growing tender, upright or spreading evergreen small tree or shrub with narrow, oval, wavy-edged yellw to green leaves. Reaches a height of 1-5m. Insignificant flowers are greenish-red, and borne in clusters, in summer, sometimes followed by impressive winged fruit capsules on female plants that turn from green to vivid red over the season
An evergreen, upright to spreading shrub or small tree to 5m tall with glossy, wavy-margined, deep red to purple foliage and tiny, inconspicuous clusters of flowers in summer

A low-growing, semi-evergreen perennial to about 15cm, forming a mat of dark green, heart-shaped leaves. In late winter and early spring produces small, fragrant, pale pink flowers with darker pink centres

A neat and compact, vigorous, evergreen perennial with dark green, oval-shaped, toothed leaves. Fragrant white flowers with dark purple streaks and a yellow centre appear from spring through to the autumn
A compact, evergreen perennial to around 20cm tall with green, toothed leaves and double, scented, white flowers edged with blue
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, dark-red flowers with a white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring

An evergreen, perennial, double auricula to 15cm with rosettes of pale, grey-green leaves. The large, double flowers, produced in clusters on short stems in spring, are cream with a grey or very pale purple tinge

An evergreen perennial, to 20cm tall, with spreading rosettes of mealy, grey-green leaves. In spring, short stems, held above the foliage, are topped with clusters of flowers in a mix of pale pink, pale green, and pale yellow, with pale yellow eyes
An evergreen, perennial, double auricula up to 20cm tall with rosettes of pale green leaves. Dark red, double flowers are produced in clusters on short stems in spring

primary_name: Alcea rosea Chater's Double Group violet-flowered (d)
description: A vigorous short-lived perennial with lobed rounded leaves and long, erect pyramids of open funnel-shaped large violet double flowers in summer.

A vigorous upright annual or biennial with finely dissected, aromatic blue-green leaves, and large flat umbels of tiny yellow flowers in summer. This compact variety has a good leaf and seed yield. Dill is grown popularly each year as an annual for fresh leaves and used as a herb in cooking - particulalry fish eggs and potatoes, and also grown as a cut flower and for cut scented foliage. Dill will often flower and go to seed in its second year. The leaves, the flowers and the aromatic seeds are all edible. Dill seeds are important culinary additions, and their flavour can provide a more subdued flavour. Dill seed is used in pickling, and features in vinaigrettes and marinades.
An exceptional, everbearing variety producing large, juicy red fruits with a sweet flavour. Very few runners which makes it perfect for hanging baskets and container displays

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage coated with a silvery powder, and fragrant, bright red flowers with a white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring

A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced pale lavender-blue flowers with white centres appear from summer through until the autumn
A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced pink flowers with yellow centres appear from summer through until the autumn
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, orange-brown flowers, with a gold centre, appearing in the spring

A compact, mounding, trailing, floriferous tender annual with oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid- to light-green leaves. Lightly fragrant, ruffled, fully double, pink flowers with darker magenta-pink veining appear from May through to the autumn. Ideal for hanging baskets and containers
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, pale yellow flowers, with a white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring

Compact, semi-evergreen, woody, twining climber about 2.5-3m tall, with paired, oval, dark green leaves, downy blue-green beneath. Very floriferous, tubular, 2-lipped pale yellow flowers are produced towards the ends of the stems in summer, followed by red berries

A tough, evergreen perennial with clusters of rosettes of silvery, encrusted, grey-green leaves with dainty sprays of crisp white flowers on fine stalks to 15cm in height, in late spring and early summer
Forms evergreen mounds of tiny leaves. In late spring these are smothered in reddish-pink flowers

A bushy, suckering, deciduous upright shrub, this dwarf cultivar is grown primarily for its small, compact and multi-stemmed habit, and its slightly larger flowers. Bronze-tinged young leaves that are oval or circular in shape turn mid-to dark-green in summer, and then yellow, orange, red and pink-purple in autumn. Clusters of self-fertile five-petalled white flowers emerge in spring about 4-5cm across as the young leaves unfurl and expand. The edible fruits are enjoyed by wildlife and can be made into jams and pies.

An upright-growing large, dense shrub or small tree. Scented, white flowers are produces in drooping clusters in spring just ahead of the bronze-tinted young leaves. Edible purple-black berries follow, with showy, red and orange autumn leaf colour

An upright shrub or tree, up to 8m high, with oblong, hairless leaves which are coppery pink when they emerge, become mid-green in summer, then turn yellow flushed with red in autumn. Hanging, nodding clusters of large, fragrant, starry-white flowers in spring are followed in summer by edible, sweet, blue-black fruits, up to 1.5cm long

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 58cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, creamy yellow flowers with a burgundy red eyezone and a green throat to 13cm across in summer

A compact, upright deciduous shrub with pointed mid-green leaves flushed crimson when young and in autumn. A Japanese cultivar with flattened lacecap flowerheads of lilac fertile flowers and bright red ray florets, with white at the centre. Flowers are borne from summer to autumn

A compact and tender evergreen perennial, zonal pelargonium with lobed rounded golden-green leaves and large clusters of bright red flowers in summer.

A slender perennial, to 60cm tall, with downy, lance-shaped leaves in a basal rosette, and towers of densely-packed light bronze, tubular flowers, in summer

A semi-evergreen rounded shrub reaching 3m in height, with an arching habit and dark green, deeply-veined glossy leaves. In late spring, small, creamy white flowers arranged in flattened clusters appear, followed by oval-shaped red fruit that turns black as they mature

A bulbous perennial, to 20cm in height, with broad, grey-bloomed, dark green, pleated leaves. The solitary, white, bowl-shaped flowers appear from late winter, with large, puckered outer segments and green-flushed inner segments

A vigorous evergreen sub-shrub or woody-based perennial, with aromatic, wrinkled, slightly grey-green leaves. Spikes of light blue flowers are produced in early summer

A semi-evergreen, very vigorous, trailing herbaceous perennial to 30cm tall. It makes a wide mat of neat, rounded, lobed grey-green leaves and produces pink flowers with darker pink veins in summer
A bulbous, clump-forming perennial with glaucous, strap-shaped leaves and flowers borne in early winter with white outer segments and inner segments with a green, V-shaped mark at the tip

A clump-forming perennial with strap-shaped foliage and rounded heads of clustered, white flowers borne on sturdy stems to 70cm tall in summer
An evergreen, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped, dark blue flowers in summer

A summer-dormant bulb with narrow, grass-like green leaves. In early spring, it bears a flower spike of hanging yellow flowers with a green base

A spreading, bushy, evergreen shrub to 30cm high and 45 wide, with yellow foliage, taking on orange tints in winter. Upright spikes of small, dark pink flowers with protruding black anthers appear in early winter to mid-spring, though it is not free flowering
A hardy, evergreen shrub with a broad, bushy growing habit with mid-green foliage. Classified as a bud-bloomer, grey-white buds appear in summer and autumn.

A compact, evergreen perennial shrub with grey-green stems and small, velvety silver-grey leaves which have a pineapple fragrance when crushed. Fragrant, tubular-shaped, dark violet-purple flowers appear from summer through to autumn

A compact, early-fruiting cultivar which produces smooth-skinned, golden-yellow courgettes, which are ready to harvest when approximately 15-20cm (6-8in) in length. These are produced over a long period from July to October. Its relatively compact habit makes it suitable for growing in containers on the patio where border space is limited. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking

A compact Italian heirloom cultivar producing pale green and dark green striped courgettes which are renowned for their excellent nutty flavour. They are ready to harvest when approximately 15-20cm (6-8in) in length. These are produced over a long period from July to October, as long as the developing fruits are regularly picked. Its relatively compact habit makes it suitable for growing in containers on the patio, where border space is limited. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking.

Annual vegetable with finely divided, feathery, bright green foliage that is grown for its swollen, aniseed-flavoured stems. Yellow umbel flowers are produced if the bulb is not harvested, or if stressed by dry hot weather. Height 1-1.5m (3-5ft).

A reliable, mid-season leek with thick, sturdy stems to 45cm, with a mild flavour and stands well in cold weather. Leeks, Allium porrum are herbaceous perennials usually grown as annual vegetables, with upright stems which can be blanched white, and green or blue-green leaves about 30-50cm long; plants may flower by bolting in their first year, or the following year if left overwinter, with stems up to 1.5m high topped by rounded flowerheads 5-9cm across of hundreds of star-like pale pink to white flowers which are visited by bees, in summer.

A leek with thick white stems up to 5cm thick and 15cm long, with a delicate, mild flavour and buttery texture. Leeks, Allium porrum are herbaceous perennials usually grown as annual vegetables, with upright stems which can be blanched white, and green or blue-green leaves about 30-50cm long; plants may flower by bolting in their first year, or the following year if left overwinter, with stems up to 1.5m high topped by rounded flowerheads 5-9cm across of hundreds of star-like pale pink to white flowers which are visited by bees, in summer.

A fairly compact, dual-purpose cultivar to 60cm (2ft) high and a spread of 1.8m (6ft), producing dark green courgettes which are striped in cream. They are ready to harvest when approximately 15-20cm (6-8in) in length. The fruits can also be left on the plant to mature into marrows which can be stored for several weeks in the autumn after ripening on the plant fully. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking.

A climbing variety of courgette reaching a height of around 1.8m, producing long, slim dark green fruits with pale greens stripes. Sow in March to June for harvesting July to September. Sometimes a tricky variety to germinate, but with success is suitable for smaller spaces, where it can be grown upwards, against a frame
An 'heirloom' variety with a long known history, this evergreen annual/biennial vegetable lasts a long time and can be kept in the ground through the winter and harvested right through to March

An heirloom first early variety introduced in 1900, slightly pear shaped with bright white flesh, smooth skin and a superb 'new potato' flavour. Best boiled or steamed whole in skins or cold in salads and it’s floury texture also makes it ideal for roasting

A heritage potato bred in 1891. This potato is much valued for its pale yellow tubers that have a super rich flavour. A classic first early which is low growing so ideal for a windy garden. Perfect for new potatoes but can be left to develop into a quality general purpose potato

A winter squash producing some of the largest of all pumpkins on trailing vines up to 5m (17ft) in length. The fruits can vary somewhat from a basic egg shape and exceed 1.8m (6ft in diameter. They have orange skins and bright orange flesh. In 2016, this cultivar produced a pumpkin 782kg (2,624.6 lbs) in weight, which was an official record at the time. Primarily grown for competitions as the flesh is somewhat watery, but it can be used in stocks and soups

A tall, high-yielding, long-leaved radicchio-type chicory which may be forced if required, with long, pointed green leaves which turn to red as the temperatures drop. Sow in June to July for harvesting in autumn to early spring. Brings a tangy taste and colour to winter salads. Although a biennial, it is generally grown as an annual and harvested in its first year of growth
An annual bunching radish with elongated red roots with a white tip. Great for eating raw, pickling or cooking with butter and garlic
A dark red-purple round cabbage, ready to harvest in autumn

A twining climber reaching 3m with green leaves. This heritage variety has white flowers which develop into runner beans. These can either be eaten fresh or the pods can be left to mature and the seeds inside stored as dried beans for the winter. In the UK it is grown as a summer annual, lasting only one year.

A medium-height pea to 150cm. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils. The flowers are purple and develop into large, flat, purple 'mange tout' pods in summer. It is an annual which lives for one summer.

A very large winter squash producing rounded, orange fruits which have the potential to reach up to 45kg in weight on trailing vines. The rich, firm flesh is versatile for dishes such as stews and pies and the large seeds are excellent roasted. An ideal variety for exhibiting

A popular variety producing ball-shaped pumpkins with a thick, dark orange skin from 16-40cm (6-16in) in diameter, and 7-11 kg (15-24 lbs) in weight which store well. The flesh is bright orange and very sweet. Its regular shape makes it a good choice for halloween carving.

A relatively new cultivar introduced in 1997, producing large, dark-orange pumpkins in excess of 14kg (30lbs). Time from seed to harvest is around 120 days or approximately 3 months, meaning it is ready for harvest in autumn.

A very old french heirloom, producing compact plants and flattened, round, orange-red pumpkins, to around 25cm (10in) in diameter and 11kg (25lbs) in weight. These are reminiscent of the pumpkin-shaped carriage in Cinderella to which the name refers. Two fruits are usually produced per plant. Its relatively compact habit makes it suitable for growing in containers on the patio where border space is limited. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking

A medium sized pumpkin, producing plants with stems up to 90cm (3ft) high and 2.4m (8ft) across. Bright orange, ribbed pumpkins, three or four to a plant, are produced late in the season and can weigh from 5-9 kg (12-20 lbs) The pumpkins store well over winter after being fully ripened on the plant before harvesting.

A reasonably compact pumpkin cultivar, producing stems to 60cm (24in) high and 1.8m (6ft) across. Dark orange-skinned fruits are produced from late summer into autumn which are approximately 20cm (8in) in diameter and have very sweet tasting flesh, making them eminently suitable for using in pies, muffins and for stuffing and baking. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects and can also be picked and used in cooking.
A scrambling annual which reaches 2m along the ground. It has green leaves and yellow flowers which develop into small round orange pumpkins with orange flesh. They store well into winter

A cultivar producing one of the smallest pumpkins which are attractively ribbed, round and flattened and roughly palm sized, with a bright orange skin. These are perfect for stuffing and baking whole, or for using as miniature lanterns for halloween decorations. One plant will produce around ten fruits. When fully ripened the fruits can store for up to 12 months

primary_name: Cucurbita maxima 'Acorn, Cream of the Crop'

description: A high yielding cultivar of butternut squash, producing cylindrical fruits with a bulbous end furthest from the stalk, roughly 37cm (15in) long and 10 cm (4in) in diameter. These appear on trailing vines up to 2.5m (8ft) long. The smooth, pale orange, hard-skinned fruits, are ready to harvest in autumn and store well over winter once ripe. They have bright orange flesh, with a sweet, nutty taste and can reach around 4kg (approximately 9lbs) in weight
A winter squash bearing large, elongated, banana-shaped fruit up to around 60cm long on trailing vines. Fruits weighing 4-8kg have smooth pink-orange skins and dry, sweet, yellow to orange flesh

A large scrambling plant requiring ample space in which to grow. Very large pumpkins can be produced if required, if each plant is restricted to developing just one fruit, by pinching out all others that subsequently begin to develop. The fruits have a thick bright orange skin and are ready to harvest in autumn

A popular cultivar of butternut squash, producing roughly bell-shaped fruits on trailing vines up to 2.5m (8ft) long. The smooth, pale orange, hard-skinned fruits, are ready to harvest in autumn and can reach around 1.8-2.3kg (approximately 4-5lbs) in weight. They store well over winter once ripe and have bright, orange flesh, with a sweet, nutty taste.

A winter squash, producing cylindrical fruits with a bulbous end furthest from the stalk. These are produced on trailing vines in excess of 1.8m (6ft) long. The smooth, pale orange, hard-skinned fruits, 12.5cm (5in) in diameter and 27.5cm (11in) in length, can be ready to harvest from late summer into autumn. They store well once ripe and have sweet, bright orange flesh with a nutty taste. They can reach around 2.3kg (approximately 5lbs) in weight.
A winter squash bearing 3-4 teardrop-shaped fruits per plant on trailing stems, each weighing from one to two kilogrammes. Fruits have smooth, blue-grey skins and bright orange, sweet-flavoured flesh

A heavy-cropping, early-maturing winter squash bearing small, round, dark green fruit weighing 1.3kg-2.2kg on trailing vines. The fruit have fine-grained, thick, pale yellow flesh and store well. Easy to train up against a trellis or other support

A medium to large heritage variety of squash from Northern Italy which can spread to around 250cm. The fruits are large with thick, knobbly blue-green to grey skin which looks like giant bubble wrap, and the flesh is bright yellow with a sweet and nutty flavour. Sow in spring for harvesting in the autumn

A famous winter squash cultivar producing stems to approximately 60cm (2ft) high and 1.8m (6ft) across. Each plant is able to produce up to six rugby ball-shaped fruits weighing around 1.5 kg (3 lbs), each which when ripe are a pale orange colour. When harvested and baked, the flesh can be forked out and forms spaghetti-like strands which can be used in exactly the same way as the pasta version, but is considerably less calorific!

A winter squash producing distinctive, rounded-shaped fruits, mottled in shades of orange, red, white and green and topped with a knobbly green cap. The fruit is quite ornamental, but it is good for eating, the flesh golden-orange, very moist, sweet and nutty. Harvest October and November - stores well, often to Feburary
A beautiful patty pan Summer squash variety with a bright yellow, glossy skin and tender, nutty flavour flesh. When cooking, steam to retain the buttery, melt in the mouth texture

An annual which scrambles along the ground and over low shrubs, reaching 3+m if unchecked. It has large green palmate leaves and yellow flowers. These develop into a large blue-green deeply-ridged fruits with light orange flesh. They can be stored in the cool and dark over the winter

An old cultivar of butternut squash, producing roughly cylindrical shaped fruits which have a narrower waist, on trailing vines up to 2.5m (8ft) long. The textured, pale orange, hard-skinned fruits, are ready to harvest in autumn and can reach around 4kg (approximately 9lbs) in weight. They store well over winter once ripe and have bright orange flesh, with a sweet, nutty taste.

The smooth, oval tubers of this second early make one of the tastiest salad potatoes. They have a firm, waxy texture and are great for boiling or sautéing. Easy to grow in pots, bags or borders, they produce a generous number of tubers per plant, and as they store well, you will usually be able to enjoy them over a couple of months. Shows resistance to potato leafroll virus and some potato cyst nematodes

A vigorous, upright, annual variety with aromatic, mid-green foliage that has an excellent flavour. Umbels of small, white flowers appear in summer. Noted for being the benchmark of field grown coriander and being slow to bolt
A vigorous greenhouse melon cultivar producing round, yellow fruit with attractive ‘netting’ and sweet, pale green to creamy white flesh. Shows resistance to powdery mildews

alternative_names: California poppy 'Apricot Chiffon'|Eschscholzia californica 'Apricot Flambeau' (Thai Silk Series)
description: A compact annual to 30cm with finely-divided, blue-green foliage and yellow, semi-double flowers with fluted petals, flushed with pink and orange
A compact annual to 30cm, with dissected blue-green leaves and semi-double light lemon-yellow flowers 5cm wide, the fluted petals paler on the reverse
An annual to 30cm tall, with finely divided, blue-green foliage and semi-double cream flowers heavily flushed with pink and streaked with red

An annual vegetable with large, lobed, oblong, blue-green leaves and a central head of densely packed, blue-green flowers which is harvested as calabrese or broccoli while still in bud. This is a compact, quick-maturing cultivar, producing tight, domed heads, and good for growing at close spacing

A biennial grown as an annual vegetable. A cultivar producing a stout rosette of triangular, lobed, grey-green basal leaves and short, sturdy stalks bearing densely packed, edible heads of crisp, blue-green florets. It has an excellent flavour and remains in good condition for a long time. Successional sowing will provide a harvest throughout Summer and Autumn

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, grape-red flowers with a creamy-gold throat to 15cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves, and creamy coloured flowers that are tinted pale pink with a plum-coloured eye-zone and edge above a green throat to 13cm across in summer

A deciduous herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 58cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and very fragrant dark lavender-purple flowers with a purple eyezone and yellow throat to 17cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and creamy-yellow flowers to around 14cm across with a pale pink eyezone and green throat in summer
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are dark purple with a light purple white edge and a green-yellow eye

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms clumps of arching, strap-like, green leaves and large creamy-white flowers that have a frilly, gold braid around the edge of the petals and a green throat to 14cm across in summer.
A variable species with upright, grey-green leaves, up to 50cm long, and nodding flowers, up to 7cm across, with yellow trumpets and narrow, twisted, cream petals, produced in early spring

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 46cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and rose-lavender pink flowers with a washed rose-lavender eyezone edged with dark purple and a green throat to 8cm across in summer
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching green leaves and sturdy stems of showy, coral-orange coloured flowers with a bright yellow-green eye and reflexed petals

An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped arching green leaves and sturdy stems of mango-orange, reflexed flowers, mango-orange which change to darker orange towards a green-orange eye
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are dark red-purple with a yellow green throat and have reflexed petals
A bushy, evergreen perennial, regal pelargonium, with rounded mid-green deeply serrated leaves and frilly trumpet-shaped single pink and white flowers in summer.

Bushy evergreen shrub about 4m tall, with small, glossy toothed dark and pale green leaves with golden-yellow edges. New stems emerge bright burgundy red. Small white flowers appear in spring, with sometimes a second flush in the autumn. This variety is male so does not produce berries but is a good pollinator
A clump-forming perennial to about 60cm producing a mound of foliage topped with very pale purple daisies with gold centres, borne over a long period from mid-summer to mid-autumn

A semi-evergreen clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, mid-green foliage and branched stems rising above with dangling cup-shaped white double flowers which are maroon spotted in late winter and early spring.

A clump-forming perennial about 45cm high, with leathery, deeply lobed, dark green leaves to 40cm long, that usually persist through winter. Stout stems bearing saucer-shaped double, rich red flowers with creamy stamens, appear from late winter to mid spring
A rhizomatous perennial forming a clump of erect, greyish-green, sword-shaped leaves and, in early summer, upright flowering stems bearing pale cream to white flowers with purple-veined falls

This plant is listed as an invasive non-native species in the UK – see Cultivation section for details. A climbing woody vine with stems that can reach 8m long. Clusters of white flowers are followed by balloon-like capsules that contain seed

A herbaceous perennial, to about 50cm tall, with marbled green and white leaves and very stiff, branching stems, flushed with blue and dark red, that bear tight clusters of tiny blue flowers surrounded by deep blue, spiny bracts

A clump-forming, ornamental evergreen perennial with very broad, arching, strap-shaped, veined green foliage and cherry-pink flowers which appear on upright stems in the summer and flower over a long period
A semi-trailing deciduous shrub to 50cm tall, with dark green leaves, and large double flowers with dark reddish-purple tubes and sepals and dark purple corollas, flowering in summer
Upright, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial 1.2-1.5m high with rounded 5 to 7-lobed, divided, deep green leaves, and dense racemes of hooded white flowers in summer

alternative_names: Geranium traversii 'Sea Spray'|Geranium sessiliflorum 'Sea Spray'|Geranium 'Sea Spray'

description: A genus of subtropical, fast-growing, evergreen shrubs with textured, thick, greyish-brown trunks and glossy, lobed dark green foliage which in its natural habitat can reach a height or around 3m. Small, fragrant white flowers appear all year round followed by small, green, red or black fruits. Cultivated as indoor bonsai trees due to their small stature and interesting features

primary_name: Geranium × antipodeum (_G. sessiliflorum_ subsp. _novae-zelandiae_ 'Nigricans' × _G. traversii_ var. _elegans_)

description: An elegant, medium to large, deciduous tree with grey bark on the trunk and dark-brown to grey bark on the branches, which weep at their tips. Rare in cultivation, the tree can reach 20m (66ft) high when mature. It bears attractive, bronze-purple and green new leaves in spring, maturing to green in summer and turning a rich orange-red in autumn. The green, male and female catkins are produced separately on the same tree in April. After fertilisation, the female flowers develop into hop-like clusters in late summer to autumn, containing winged seeds that disperse on the wind when ripe

A medium-sized deciduous tree, with dark grey older bark and brownish-grey younger branches and reaching a height of 9m (30ft) when mature. In very mild gardens in the south-west of England it can sometimes remain in leaf through the year. Foliage emerges reddish-green in spring, maturing to green in summer and then turning bright orange red in autumn. . The green, male and female catkins are produced separately on the same tree in May to June. After fertilisation, the female flowers develop into hop-like clusters in late summer to autumn, containing winged seeds that disperse on the wind when ripe

alternative_names: coneflower 'Rocky Top'|Echinacea tennesseensis 'Rocky Top Hybrids'|Echinacea 'Rocky Top Hybrids'|Echinacea purpurea 'Rocky Top'|Echinacea 'Rocky Top'
description: A clump-forming perennial to 70cm tall with narrow, dark green leaves up to 12cm long. In summer, flowerheads comprising upwardly-curved pink ray florets surrounding a dark central cone are held on erect stems

alternative_names: North American showy orchid|parson in the pulpit|preachers in the pulpit|showy orchid|Orchis spectabilis

description: A slow-growing, deciduous tree up to a height of 8m (much more than this in its native China), with a slender, upright habit and large, pinnate green leaves which turn to bright yellow into the autumn. Male plants produce yellow catkins in the spring, whilst females produce insignificant spikes, which are followed by sweet, edible hickory nuts from late summer to autumn. These are used commercially in China as an ingredient in sweets and snacks as well as for extracting cooking oil. It can take up to 18 to 24 years before a speciment starts to produce fruit. Best used as a specimen tree in large parkland settings or as part of a botanical collection. Specimens can be found at the RHS, Kew, Savill Gardens and Westonbirt Arboretum

A tender annual or short-lived perennial, to around 45cm high, with a branching habit and lance-shaped green leaves. Open clusters of fragrant, lime green flowers, with long tubes and flaring petals to 4cm across, are produced in summer

A dwarf, clump-forming, half-hardy annual around 45cm high, with ovate basal leaves, and branching stems with narrow, serrated stem leaves. Double, dark mahogany-red flowers fading to orange at the tips with a black central cone appear from late summer to early autumn
A compact annual to 25cm high with finely-divided, grey-green leaves and semi-double, papery flowers shaded reddish-pink to orange with paler yellow centres
A low growing, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with shorter stalks formed with divided green leaves and spikes packed with sky-blue flowers in summer.
A compact, semi-evergreen marginal aquatic perennial, comprising fans of leaves making clumps to 40cm in height, with narrow, bright yellow leaves, very lightly striped with yellowish-green
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce large umbels of trumpet-shaped pure white flowers in the summer

An evergreen, compact herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers from summer to autumn. These are dark blue in bud, opening a paler blue with darker midrib down each petal

Fast-growing annual grass to about 1.5m tall, forming a large clump of broadly strap-shaped, dark green leaves with purple midribs, maturing to purple-black. Stout, upright, dark purple bottlebrush-like flower panicles produced on leafy stems in summer are followed by shiny purple seedheads, the seeds are very attractive to birds
A spreading herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall with grey-green foliage. From late spring to early summer, deep purple-red, thistle-like flowers with linear, fringed petals are held on upright stems

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 60cm high, with slightly glaucous, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers over a long period from early spring, producing up to 5 fragrant, double flowers per stem. Flowers are small, to 5cm across, with white petals, the outer sections rounded with slightly wavy margins, and inner sections shorter and incurved, intermingled with sections of orange corona

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 65cm high, with slightly glaucous, strap-shaped leaves. Very early to flower in spring, producing solitary, double triangle shaped flowers to 11cm across, with ovate, lemon yellow outer petals and a large, golden yellow cup with a ruffled, slightly flared rim

plant_range: S China to Thailand & W Malesia

description: A clump-forming tazetta daffodil with slightly grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are 4cm across, with broad yellow outer petals and a cup-shaped, frilly orange corona. Very early flowering, with up to nine flowers per stem
A large-cupped variety flowering from mid-February. Bright golden yellow incurved blooms surrounding a pleated corona
A bulbous perennial to 40cm tall, with broad, deep lemon yellow perianth segments, and a near-white cup that bleaches with age

alternative_names: Cassia sieberiana hort.|Cassia bearana hort.|Cassia abbreviata hort.

description: An easy to grow, compact Chinese cabbage with edible dark-green leaves and prominent white ribs. It has a delicate flavour and can be eaten raw or cooked like ordinary cabbage. Suitable for container growing and small raised beds. Shows good disease resistance

primary_name: Galanthus nivalis f. pleniflorus 'Doncaster's Double Scharlock' (d)
Galanthus nivalis f. pleniflorus 'Doncaster's Double Charmer' (d)
description: A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, arching grey-green leaves. Double white flowers are borne nodding on slender stems in late winter or early spring. Flowers have long, narrow outer petals marked green at the tips, and whorls of smaller petals in the centre

primary_name: Galanthus elwesii var. monostictus from Cassaba, Turkey

description: This plant is listed on Schedule 9 of the UK Wildlife & Countryside Act as an invasive, non-native species and is banned from sale. See cultivation notes for further details
A creeping, low-growing, evergreen subshrub. In summer, purple-pink flowers are held above small, aromatic green leaves

A bulbous, clump-forming perennial with strap-shaped, grey-green foliage. Large flowers with long, white outer segments and inner segments with a broad, green X-shaped marking are borne on arching stems; when established, plants often produce two flowers per stem

An evergreen coniferous tree capable of reaching 10-15m (33-50ft) high and as much across. when mature. The trees have a densely conical profile when young, but as they mature their shape becomes more spreading. The bark is smooth and greyish-black when young but becomes fissured on older trees. The silvery blue-green needles are stiff and produced in groups of five at the tips of new stems. They are approximately 7.5cm (3in) long and somewhat twisted, giving the trees canopy a ruffled texture. The cones are oval and reddish brown, and produced either singly, or in small clusters and can persist on the tree for around six or seven years, so that over the years, the accumulated numbers of cones remaining on older trees can be very noticeable.

alternative_names: snowdrop 'Ginns'|Galanthus 'Ginn's Imperati'|Galanthus nivalis subsp. imperati 'Ginns'|Galanthus imperati 'Ginns' Form'|Galanthus nivalis subsp. imperati 'Ginns' Form'
description: A perennial bulb, up to 20cm high, with pairs of narrow, grey-green leaves slightly folded back at the base. Solitary, nodding white flowers are produced in late winter; flowers are scented, with spoon-shaped outer petals and a thin green mark at the tip of the inner petals

Sandersii Group are bulbous perennials, to 15cm tall, with narrow, grey-green leaves and solitary, single white flowers with a yellow ovary and inner markings. They are selections from a population of yellow snowdrops in Northumberland

A bulbous perennial with grey-green leaves and white flowers on stems around 20cm tall. An elegant bloom with a long ovary and outer segments that curve to a point. This late-flowering cultivar will bloom late into April. For longer lasting flowers, plant in a cooler shady part of the garden to avoid the warmer rays of the mid-spring sun

A large deciduous fast growing tropical or subtropical tree, often multi-stemmed with a flat spreading crown and delicate mimosa-like divided leaves composed of many tiny leaflets. Roundish fluffy creamy white powder-puff flowers are produced in wide open panicles at the top of the tree, followed by clusters of long, narrow, pale brown pods that can hang on into winter.
A subshrub with bare, upright branches to 2m topped with rosettes of somewhat shiny, dandelion-like leaves up to 50cm long, and producing well-branched clusters of yellow, dandelion flowers in summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 90cm high, with finely divided deep green leaves. In late spring and early summer, cup-shaped semi-double flowers open coral pink, fading to apricot and then pale yellow

An upright, hardy, drought-tolerant, clump-forming deciduous to semi-evergreen perennial with lance-shaped dark green foliage and long-lasting, flared, tubular pink-red flowers with striped white throats appearing from June to September. Good for the edge of flower borders or in a large rock garden

alternative_names: Pereskia aculeata var. godseffiana (hort.) Knuth|Pereskia aculeata 'Godseffiana Variegated'|Pereskia godseffiana hort.

description: A climbing shrub with semi-evergreen, ovate, variegated leaves. The yellow variegation on leaves is not uniform, appearing as marbling and splashes of yellow. Flowers, borne in large clusters from summer into autumn, are a rich purple-blue with bright yellow anthers closely-packed at the centre of each flower

A summer-dormant, tuberous, perennial climber to about 1m with small, deeply six-lobed, bright green leaves. The small, yellow, funnel-shaped flowers have a pale green calyx and spur, and appear in spring
A compact, evergreen shrub to around 75cm tall with blue-green foliage and bright yellow, fragrant, pea-like flowers produced from late winter into spring

Vigorous, evergreen twining climber about 3m tall, with purple-flushed dark green leaves composed of leaflets with slender points, and bearing dark pink buds opening to very fragrant, often pale pink flushed white flowers to 2cm across, in late winter or early spring in a warm greenhouse or conservatory; from spring to early summer in warm climates

alternative_names: Crocosmia × crocosmiiflora 'Golden Glory' misapplied [2]|Crocosmia × crocosmiiflora 'Rheingold' misapplied [1]

description: An annual climber to 2m, with fragrant, reddish-purple flowers in short racemes on long stalks in summer and early autumn
Annual climber with greyish-green foliage and long-stalked racemes of fragrant, cream flowers, flushed with light pink

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 1m, with mid-green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The blooms have neat rows of tightly inrolled, light orange petals, forming a flattened ball 7-9cm across

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Large, fully double flowers 20cm across, produced from mid-summer until the first frosts, have narrow, quilled, white to pale greenish-yellow petals with long, divided tips giving a frizzy effect

A neat, compact, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial, to 65cm tall, with a rosette of very divided, toothed and prickly, lance-shaped, dark green leaves emerging from pointed buds. In summer, short spikes bear masses of silvery-white flowers hooded with purple bracts. The leaves, stems and flower spikes are covered with silky hairs

An evergreen perennial forming a clump of large, glossy, green leaves that turn deep red in autumn and winter. Tall, upright stems bear dense clusters of open, white flowers flushed baby pink in spring
An evergreen perennial to 1.5m tall forming a clump of grass-like, linear, dark green leaves. Erect to arching flower stems produced in summer bear nodding, dark pink to purple flowers

Clump-forming perennial with linear, grass-like mid-green leaves. Produces tall flower spikes about 90cm in height, wth pale-greenish cream flowers opening from apricot buds, flowering from late summer to autumn

A bulbous perennial, up to 30cm high, growing from autumn to spring, with long fleshy green leaves, spotted above with maroon-brown. From late winter to spring, spotted stems with spikes of tubular, pale blue-lilac flowers with pale pink-purple tips appear

An evergreen shrub with an upright habit and spreading branches. Leaves are fragrant, narrowly elliptic, and deep green, sometimes tinged with red. From late spring to early summer, abundant double flowers are produced along the stems, with ruffled pale pink petals fading to white around dark pink centres

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 86cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and rich ruby-red flowers with a pale yellow throat to 13cm across in summer
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and yellowish-pink flowers to 12cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and fragrant, double, golden-yellow flowers with a green throat to 14cm across in summer

A distinctive attractive semi-cos due to its red flecks on wavy-edged green leaves. Leaves can be cropped individually or you can crop the loose heads whole. This variety has good mildew resistance and is slow to bolt. Sow April to July, harvest May to October.
A red-leaved cos suited to cut-and-come-again baby-leaf salad. Good resistance to downy mildew
A small cos type lettuce, to just over 20cm high, with wavy, glossy dark red leaves that are green at the base, and a crisp green heart. Slow to bolt. Can be sown at closer spacing for baby leaves

A leafy biennial usually grown as an annual. This robust crisphead (iceberg type) lettuce has smooth, crisp, red-tinted leaves and a green heart. This cultivar is slow to bolt. Ready to harvest from June depending on sowing date

plant_range: S US, Mex., W Ind., N S Am.

description: A clump-forming, deciduous fern bearing arching, triangular, crested, silvery grey-green fronds with reddish / purple stems and midribs

A small to medium sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid, with spindle-shaped, upright stems growing from a short, creeping rhizome. The stems (pseudobulbs), wider in the middle part, carry one or two firm leaves at the top. The leaves are oval, elliptic, 10cm long and 4cm wide. Flowers are large, compared to size of the plant - 10cm across, held on short, terminal stems arising from new, mature growth in spring and summer. Colour of flowers may vary, depending on cultivar. Flowers are long-lasting, often scented, white, pink or pale purple, with a typical three-lobed lip.

A small to medium-sized, tropical orchid, producing a clump of short, cylindrical, spindle-shaped stems - pseudobulbs. Each noded stem is covered with thin, papery sheaths, carrying a pair of rigid, dark green leaves at the top. Each leathery, lance-shaped leaf is up to 20cm long. Numerous bright red, orange or gold yellow flowers up to 4cm across, are borne in racemes in summer.
A dwarf, female hop, climbing to around 2.5m, with golden leaves, scented, pale green flowers in summer and bronzy-yellow, papery cones in autumn
A reliable, old variety with long, reddish-pink stems and a sweet flavour. This is an early to mid-season cultivar, ready to harvest from May. Suitable for forcing

A bushy, densely branched, semi-evergreen shrub to 90cm, bearing bright yellow leaves with green margins. In late spring, and sometimes again in autumn, it produces clusters of fragrant white flowers at the stem tips; the petals are flushed pink

alternative_names: Californian lilac 'Gloire de Plantières'|Ceanothus 'Gloire de Plantières'

description: An exceptionally hardy, narrow-growing conifer reaching 8m. It has sparce branches of blue-green needles making a tall, airy accent plant

A fast-growing, deciduous climber between 4 to 5m in height, with simple, alternate leaves which can be oval, serrated and petiolate. Clusters of bright greenish-yellow, star-shaped flowers appear from April through to September

A bushy shrub to around 3m tall with arching, spiny stems clothed in elliptic to oval, dark green, leathery leaves up to 3cm long. Loose heads of small, creamy-white flowers are followed by cream, woody fruits ripening to a pinkish-red colour
A mat-forming, evergreen sub-shrub with finely hairy, trailing stems that bear small, aromatic, mid-dark green leaves. Whorls of tiny reddish-pink flowers appear in summer

Produces vigorous, bushy plants with thick stems. Plants are relatively dwarf reaching 60cm in height. Half-hardy/tender perennials, they flower in mid to late autumn. The double blooms of this white -lowered cultivar are incurved and, when disbudded, reach 14cm across. Florets are long and broad, overlapping, pointed and curled

A vigorous, mounding and trailing, floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid- to light-green leaves and produces striking, gramophone-trumpet-shaped, fully-double white ruffled flowers with layer upon layer of petals. It blooms from late spring or early summer into autumn. It trails or gently mounds and spreads around 30 cm to 40 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and containers.

Celosia argentea var. cristata Cristata Group
Celosia argentea var. cristata Cristata Group Big Chef Series

Upright, bushy rose to 90cm tall, with glossy mid to dark green foliage, and fragrant, fully-double, high-centred blooms in a combination of peach and pink with frilly petals, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn

Bushy, upright hybrid tea rose to about 1m high, with glossy, dark green leaves and bearing slightly scented, double, well-formed yellow blooms, in large open clusters, produced repeatedly over the summer and into autumn
A dense, slow-growing evergreen dwarf conifer with an upright habit and buttery yellow needles in spring which turn to golden green throughout the season

Celosia argentea var. cristata (Plumosa Group) 'Pink Castle' (Castle Series)
Celosia argentea var. cristata Spicata Group

description: A vigorous, bulbous perennial with broad, grey-green leaves 2.5cm across, and white flowers on stems up to 40cm tall. The inner petals have a large, green mark and the outer petals have fine green streaks at the tips

A small gladiolus, maximum height around 40cm, with green sword like leaves and an upright erect flower spike with around 10 to 12 flower buds. The raspberry ripple flowers are striking with a mix of cream petals with both deep and pale red-pink markings. Perfect for pots and sunny summer borders
A perennial corm, up to 120cm tall, with green, sword like leaves. Upright spikes of large, ruffled, peachy-cream flowers with a salmon-pink throat appear from July to October

An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 1m tall with erect stems clothed in glossy, blue-green leaves divided into three lobed leaflets. In summer, white-tipped, pink-pale purple flowers are borne in loose, branching panicles

primary_name: Thalictrum filamentosum var. tenerum Heronswood form

description: A short-lived, deciduous, clump-forming perennial with mid-green, almost lily-pad shaped leaves and upright stems which produce spicily-fragrant red, orange and yellow drooping flowers in early to late summer. Although this variety should not have their crowns submerged in water, they can cope with wet ground so are idea for waterside and boggy areas. They make an excellent cut flower

alternative_names: sage 'Hot Lips'|Salvia × jamensis 'Hot Lips'|Salvia microphylla 'Hot Lips'
description: A bushy plant, about 100 x 100cm, evergreen if not cut back by frost, with small, ovate, aromatic green leaves. Flowers are borne in loose terminal racemes, red in midsummer, bicolored red and white in July and August, sometimes completely white when the days shorten. Very floriferous in all its colour stages, continuing to the first frost
A bushy sub-shrub to 90cm tall, evergreen in mild localities, with small, aromatic, mid-green leaves. Salmon and cream flowers are borne in terminal spikes over a long period in summer and autumn

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to about 45cm, with deeply divided, leathery, dark green leaves. Saucer-shaped, creamy white flowers, flushed with light green and pale pink, are borne on dark red stems from mid-winter to early spring
A small, mounded perennial with smooth, neat, blue-green leaves with a dull surface. The bell-shaped, 2cm-long flowers are pale purple with darker stripes

A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated, bright yellow foliage and dark green margins. The foliage becomes wavy as it matures. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A small, fast-growing, clump-forming deciduous perennial with heart-shaped, variegated, bright yellow foliage which turns a more coppery colour as the season progresses. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated bright yellow foliage and dark green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming perennial to 80cm tall with deeply divided, coarsely-toothed dark green leaves. Upright, dark coloured stems bear umbels of deep reddish-purple flowers with white bases and surrounded by prominent bracts in summer

A compact, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial with rounded, lobed, glossy dark green leaves. Single, delicate, pink flowers with white centres and darker veining appear from June through to September. An ideal choice for rock gardens

A clump-forming, deciduous grass, to about 2m tall, with a loose, mounding habit and narrow, arching blue-green leaves, which turn yellow in autumn, fading to pale brown in winter. Feathery flower panicles are held well above the foliage and open deep pinkish-red in late summer and early autumn, fading to silver and remaining on the plant over winter
An evergreen, trailing shrub which roots as it spreads. The foliage is dark green with a narrow white border and the large flowers are vivid, deep violet

A large-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with long, upright, club-shaped stems (pseudobulbs) growing from a short creeping rhizome. Each mature stem carries single, apical leaf up to 30cm long and 6cm wide. The leaves are mid or dark-green, oblong, firm and leathery. Flowering stems emerge from the young mature growth in winter and early spring. The buds are enfolded in protecting, thin, pale green sheaths. Large fragrant flowers are carried on terminal flowering stems up to 30cm long. The colour of this species is highly variable from pure white, pale pink, pale lilac to dark magenta flowers with a darker lip and yellow centre. Each flower measures up to 20cm across. It is historically the most awarded species, as well as the national flower of Colombia.

A collection of annual cornflowers, to around 50cm high in flower, with lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Showy flower heads, in a wide range of colours from white to pinks, reds, purples and blues, are produced all through the summer
