description: A vigorous, open, upright shrub to 1.5m, with small, oval, dark green leaves turning crimson in autumn. Clusters of small, globular, white flowers in mid-to late spring are followed by dark blue berries with a silvery-grey bloom in late summer. A partially self-fertile variety which will still crop better with a pollination partner

A popular, compact, bushy, deciduous shrub with dark green foliage that turns a brilliant scarlet red in autumn. Clusters of white blooms appear in spring and are followed by edible, sweet tasting, blue fruits in summer. A half high bush variety that is perfectly suited to colder climates and for container growing

A compact, upright decidous shrub, with elliptic green leaves which turn to golden-orange in autumn. Bell-shaped white flowers appear in late spring, followed by pale blue berries in early to mid-summer. The berries have a sweet taste and juicy texture and are good for eating fresh, baking, cooking or preserves. Perfect for small gardens or containers
A compact, rounded, evergreen shrub with blue-green foliage. Clusters of bell-shaped, white flowers appear in spring and are followed by edible, dark blue fruits in summer

A compact, bushy, semi-evergreen shrub with dark green leaves that fade to purple-red in autumn, producing clusters of bright pink flowers that fade to white in spring and are followed by dark blue fruits in mid-summer

A low-growing, evergreen shrub, with almost thornless stems that root as they spread, and rounded, three-lobed, textured dark green leaves that can turn reddish bronze in cold winters. Bears single white flowers in summer, sometimes followed by rounded orange fruits
This is a bushy annual vegetable which will reach 1m. It has green leaves and purple flowers, which develop early, into a crop of large egg-shaped purple-black fruits.

A compact, semi-evergreen variegated prostrate alpine perennial with dark green leaves and golden yellow margins, flushed red in winter. Erect spikes of small saucer-shaped blue flowers appear in the spring and summer
A herbaceous perennial of a small to medium size with wavy yellow-green pointy leaves and is fast to grow. Has spikes of lavender coloured flowers in summer.

alternative_names: Siberian bugloss 'Looking Glass'|Brunnera 'Looking Glass'|Brunnera macrophylla 'Silver All Over'
description: A herbaceus perennial with mostly silvery foliage without a green trim, sparse green veining, and floriferous delicate 5-petaled flower sprays from February to June. An excellent plant for ground cover
Bushy rose to 1.2m tall with leathery, mid-green leaves and profuse, fragrant, loosly-cupped blooms of bright, buttercup-yellow to 8cm across, flowering through summer

A tender perennial, often grown as an annual, to around 30cm in height, with oval-shaped, dark green foliage. Pale pink and white flowers appear from midsummer onwards. Works well in pots and containers or for bedding displays. Protect from frost

alternative_names: purple coneflower 'Doubledecker'|Echinacea purpurea 'Double Decker'|Echinacea 'Double Decker'|Echinacea purpurea 'Indianer'|Echinacea purpurea 'Doppeldecker'|Echinacea purpurea [Doppelganger]|Echinacea purpurea 'Indiaca'
description: Unusual, double perennial coneflower about 1m tall, producing unique two-tiered flowers with long, reflexed, deep rose-pink ray petals surrounding a orange-brown central cone and topped with a small tuft of shorter petals shooting upwards

primary_name: Hepatica nobilis var. japonica Herashibe Choji Group
Hepatica nobilis var. japonica Sen-e Group
Catharanthus roseus (Albus Group) 'Pretty in Soft Pink'
Catharanthus roseus (Ocellatus Group) 'Sahara Madness Bright Eye'

description: A bulbous perennial to 20cm in height, with narrow, grey-green leaves and solitary, nodding, double, white flowers, the inner petals very neat and symmetrical, marked with an inverted V sometimes with one or two spots above

A perennial bulb, up to 30cm high, with pairs of broad, linear grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter or early spring, usually singly but sometimes two flower stems to a bulb. Flowers are rounded, with inner petals almost completely green

A bulbous perennial to 20cm with narrow, grey-green leaves and solitary, nodding, double, white flowers with fine green lines on the outer petals, the inner petals marked with a broad, inverted, green V in mid- to late winter

A perennial bulb, to 20cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves slightly folded back at the base. Solitary, nodding white flowers are produced in late winter or early spring, with inner petals marked with an inverted u-shape near the tip, and two faint curving green lines up to the base

A compact, mound-forming perennial, often grown as a summer annual, reaching 15cm in height. In summer it bears a profusion of tiny, cross-shaped, scented white flowers in rounded clusters. A good plant for coastal gardens, rockeries or containers
An Old-English variety, with long stalks and a sweet flavour. Ready for harvest in early spring as baby stems or left to mature. Suitable for forcing

Large, conical then spreading deciduous tree to 15m in height, with mid-green leaves up to 25cm long. The rich, red-purple, cup-and-saucer shaped flowers are paler within and to 23cm across, appear in late winter to early spring, before the leaves open
A compact green cabbage with a pointed shape, it is ready in to harvest in spring but resists bolting so can stand though to early autumn
A spring to autumn harvest of 'spring' greens or given more room, forms a pointed heart the following spring
A compact deciduous shrub up to 1.2m high, with mid-green leaves and purple stems, producing lacecap heads of pale blue to mauve flowers, in early summer

A compact, deciduous shrub, to 1m high and wide, with ovate, pointed and serrated green leaves that are tinged with orange in the autumn. The open flowerheads, borne from summer into autumn, are characterised by double lavender-lilac or pink, narrow-sepalled sterile flowers carried on long stalks surrounding the fertile florets

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Flowers, produced from mid-summer until the first frost, are up to 15cm across with white petals shading to yellow at the base and variable amounts of red streaking, giving each bloom a different colour balance

A short-lived herbaceous perennial with a basal cluster of dark, narrow, glossy leaves. The highly-branched flower spikes, to 80cm tall, carry coppery-yellow, bell-shaped to tubular flowers, with darker veining and a long lower lip, produced from early summer
An upright, dense evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves with serrated edges. Double, intense red flowers appear late from April to May, but this variety may continue to flower into June

alternative_names: St Bernard's lily 'Major'|St Bernard's lily|Phalangium liliago var. major|Anthericum liliago var. major
description: An erect herbaceous perennial with clumps of narrow grey-green leaves and trumpet-shaped white flowers 2-3cm in width, in narrow racemes

alternative_names: French tarragon|Artemisia dracunculus var. sativa|Artemisia dracunculus 'Sativa'
description: A woody-based, upright perennial with narrowly lance-shaped, aromatic green leaves and small, nodding, pale yellow flowerheads in late summer.

alternative_names: Russian tarragon|Artemisia dracunculus var. inodora|Artemisia dracunculus dracunculoides|Artemisia dracunculus 'Inodora'
description: An attractive, bushy perennial herb producing branching stems of lance shaped, highly aromatic, mid-green foliage and loose panicles of insignificant, yellow-white flowers in late Summer. Much more vigorous than French Tarragon but equally deserving of growing in the garden for its culinary use
A deciduous perennial to 30cm tall, forming a clump of lance-shaped, unspotted green leaves. Pink buds open to bright blue flowers in spring
A green globe cabbage, ready to harvest as early as midsummer or left until autumn

primary_name: Zinnia elegans 'Swizzle Cherry and Ivory' (Swizzle Series) (d)

description: A dwarf, hardy annual variety mix with bushy, mid-green foliage. Double, daisy-like flowers in shades of bronze, cream, yellow and orange appear from summer to autumn. Petals of flowers are edible and are a great addition to salads

An attractive, colourful, hardy annual variety with bushy, dark green foliage. Bright, fragrant, double yellow flowers appear from late spring to mid-autumn. Easy to grow from seed, excellent for container displays
A highly attractive, hardy annual variety producing charming, orange and yellow, fully double blooms throughout summer into autumn with bright green foliage

A bushy plant to 90cm tall, evergreen if not cut back by frosts, with small, ovate mid to dark green aromatic leaves. Profuse flowers borne in terminal racemes have dark red-purple calyces; flowers are wine purple in bud, opening to rich crimson, then maturing to a deep pinkish-red over a long flowering period from late spring to autumn
A compact, dwarf, hardy annual with bright green foliage and large, cream to deep orange flowers from May to September. Excellent for container displays or the border edge
A highly attractive, upright, hardy annual producing bright golden-yellow blooms held on bright, mid-green foliage in summer and autumn
An attractive annual marigold variety with bright, mid-green foliage and large, deep orange, double flowers from May to October. Perfect for container growing and flower beds and borders
A highly attractive, hardy annual with dark green foliage and double to semi-double cream-apricot flowers in summer and autumn. Excellent for the border or a container display
An attractive annual marigold variety with mid-green foliage. Pretty, cream-yellow, double to semi-double flowers have a dark red centre and last from summer through to autumn
An attractive annual marigold variety with bright, mid-green foliage and strongly coloured, deep orange and flame red flowers from June to October
A stunning, upright annual marigold with mid-green foliage. Bright, double to semi-double, yellow flowers appear from summer through to autumn
A low growing annual with bright, mid-green foliage and fully double, yellow blooms in summer and autumn. Excellent for the border edge or containers
A short-lived, evergreen perennial to 50cm, normally grown as a biennial. The richly-fragrant flowers are a creamy, yellow-apricot, opening from pink buds in mid-spring
Compact clump-forming perennial about 60cm tall, with dark green, deeply dissected leaves, and dark pink flower plumes fading to silvery-pink held on strong stems, above the foliage, in midsummer
A cultivar with deep red pincushion flowers surrounded by a ruff of red bracts that appear from early to late summer. The leaves are deeply lobed and dark green
A tall, herbaceous perennial with soft green, lance-shaped foliage on red stems and pendulous purple, bell-shaped flowers providing a long flowering display in summer

A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with upright to arching stems clothed with lance-shaped green leaves which are attached without a stalk. Upright, tubular, violet blue flowers are produced from mid summer to early autumn
A compact, clump-forming, deciduous perennial with large green leaves and a wavy cream yellow margin. Upright stems with lavender flowers appear in summer. Sport of Hosta 'Sagae'

A compact, clump-forming, upright open-mounded deciduous perennial with long, pointed, blue-green leaves and narrow, wavy, creamy white margins. Upright stems of pale lavender flowers appear in midsummer, the petioles having a slight tint of red at the base

A very small, clump-forming perennial to about 15cm high by 25cm across, with narrow, slightly rippled, satiny, mid- to dark green leaves and tubular, light purple flowers in late summer. Both leaf and flower stems are flushed with dark red

alternative_names: Jacob's ladder 'Stairway to Heaven'|Polemonium 'Stairway to Heaven'
description: A variegated, clump-forming, spreading deciduous perennial. Pinnate mid-green leaves have creamy-white margins, flushed pink in cooler spring weather. Small bell-shaped flowers, are light blue to white, and are slightly fragrant.

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 1.5m, with palmate leaves composed of large, toothed, deeply veined leaflets. In mid and late summer it produces 50cm tall, conical clusters of tiny white flowers
A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with glaucous green, scalloped foliage and tall, slender stems forming a dense mass of bottlebrush dark maroon flower spikes in summer and early autumn
An upright, bushy zonal pelargonium with dark foliage, leaves have maroon, almost black centres and green margins. Produces clusters of bright red flowers in summer.

alternative_names: rat tail radish|Raphanus sativus 'Rat's Tail'|Raphanus caudatus

description: An annual climber growing to about 1.8m with the help of tendrils, and producing very strongly scented, deep blue-purple flowers, in summer and early autumn
An annual climber to about 2m with scented, waved, deep maroon flowers over a long period in summer and autumn

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit up to 90cm tall when in flower. It has healthy, mid-green, blade-like leaves and strong, arching flower stems that bear orange-red tubular flowers with yellow centres, from mid-summer to autumn

A compact, clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, slightly fragrant, ruffled pale pink to lavender purple flowers with greyish-orange falls and lavender beards appear from late spring to early summer

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial with upright, strap-like, green leaves and erect stems bearing large, ruffled flowers with pale yellow upper petals, known as standards, and veined, dark yellow lower petals, known as falls, in late spring and early summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-like grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled, white and golden yellow flowers, yellow throats and orange beards appear from late spring to early summer

A smaller species, clump-forming perennial with rough-textured, heart-shaped and long, dark green leaves which are hairy and silvery green on the underside. Whorls of mauve flowers shoot up in spring flowering all through summer. Seedheads can offer structural interest in winter and also attract wildlife

A repeat-flowering shrub rose to 1.2m tall with mid-green, slightly bluish, matt foliage. In summer and autumn it produces small clusters of lightly scented, fully double, cup-shaped blooms, initially pale apricot then gradually becoming light pink

A succulent, fleshy evergreen perennial to 40cm, with weak, pendent stems bearing thick, dark green, toothed leaves. Panicles of large, long-lasting, nodding, tubular yellow to red flowers 2cm in length appear from late winter

Upright annual to 50cm tall, with fern-like light-green leaves to 12cm long and tubular flowers of white, yelllow, pink, purple or red to 8cm across with violet markings, streaked and spotted in contrasting colours, and produced from spring to autumn

A perennial bulb with broadly ovate green leaves. This tulip has goblet-shaped flowers, with pointed petals that are red with a narrow yellow margin. Flowers are produced in mid to late spring, and stand to around 55cm high
A summer-flowering annual to 60 cm tall producing double to semi-double picotee, or bicolour, flowers on erect stems in shades ranging from deep red to soft pink
A bushy annual to around 35cm high, with finely divided, feathery blue-green foliage. Produces delicate, poppy-like flowers all through the summer, which open pale yellow and fade to creamy white
A bushy annual to about 20cm with feathery, blue green foliage. The single, fluted flowers are bright red with a yellow eye

A bushy annual to around 25cm with feathery, blue-green foliage. The flowers are strongly fluted, with yellow eyes, and petals that are deep pink on the reverse, and may be cream, pale pink, or deep pink inside
A compact, erect annual to 25cm tallwith feathery foliage and single or semi-double summer blooms in shades of pink, red, orange and yellow
A perennial bulb to 40cm with pale green, lance-shaped leaves. Double, purple flowers, developing grey-silver tones with age, are produced in late spring
A dwarf perennial bulb, to 25cm tall, with narrow grey-green foliage. Flowers, red with a black centre and yellow ring at the base, appear in late spring
A bushy, deciduous, floribunda variety with toothed, dark green leaves. Lightly-scented, apricot to pale yellow double flowers are produced from late spring/early summer through until the autumn.
A vigorous but compact plant to 30cm tall, with glaucous leaves and light violet-blue flowers in spring, the falls with darker veining and a white beard

alternative_names: confetti bush|Coleonema pulchrum misapplied|Diosma ericoides misapplied
description: A free-branching shrub, upright then spreading with linear bright green leaves 2-4cm long. It bears red or pink flowers around 1cm across with reflexed petals and darker eyes, from late spring to summer

An annual poppy, to 90cm high, with deeply toothed, pale green-grey leaves. From June to August, large, showy, glossy dark crimson-red flowers with feathery, deeply cut petals appear followed by large, barrel-shaped blue-green seed pods

An annual poppy, to 1.2m high, with deeply toothed, pale blue-green leaves. In late spring and early summer, produces fully double, peony-like white flowers on leafy stems, followed by large, blue-green seed pods

An annual poppy, to 100cm high, with deeply toothed, pale green-grey leaves. From May to July, red and white fringed flowers appear, (the same colours that appear on the Danish flag), followed by large, barrel-shaped blue-green seed pods

A small-sized, clump-forming evergreen orchid with linear, glossy, dark green leaves, 10-17 cm long. Solitary flowers, 4-6 cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 12-15 cm long, upright stems. The pouch (or slipper) is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. Lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. Petals are lime green, pinkish or bronze, sometimes with dark brown spots. Dorsal sepal is bright lime-green with very dark spots. The pouch is bright pink on outside and yellow inside. Flowers are waxy and long-lasting.
A clump-forming perennial about 40-80cm tall, with palmate, deeply divided 7-lobed green leaves, and bearing panicles of blue hooded flowers with yellowish anthers, from early to late summer
Produces blue-green leaves composed of leaflets and in early summer large nodding, purpleflowers in loose sprays on vigorous upright stems

A short-lived, herbaceous perennial producing a neat mound of deeply divided foliage, strongly golden in spring, light green in summer. Tall, fine, upright stems to 60cm support nodding, short-spurred, greenish- or bluish-white flowers from late spring to mid-summer

Compact, clump-forming, short-lived, herbaceous perennials to 40cm producing a basal mound of divided, blue-green leaves. Nodding, short-spurred flowers appear in late spring and early summer in a range of colours including yellow, white and bicolours with shades of purple, pink and red
An upright plant to 60cm with large bicoloured flowers facing upward; very floriferous

A short-lived, herbaceous perennial to 60cm, with bright green, divided leaves with rounded leaflets. Nodding, spurless, double, pompom-like flowers with narrow, very dark purple petals appear in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Aquilegia vulgaris var. flore-pleno 'Tower Light Pink' (Tower Series)
Aquilegia vulgaris var. stellata Barlow Series, mixed (d)

description: A perennial, clump-forming grass, to 1m tall, with variegated foliage comprising white-edged linear green leaves. In summer, panicles of loosely-arranged pale green to white flowers, which age to a rich golden brown, are borne on slender upright stems
A bushy, clump-forming perennial to 75cm tall, with palm-like divided leaves and erect spikes of scented flowers in shades of peachy orange and pink, from late spring to early summer

A medium-sized, clump-forming orchid with narrowly-oval, evergreen leaves. Dark green leaves are mottled with pale green, approximately 15cm long and 3cm wide. One or two (rarely more) flowers are carried on 15-20cm long, upright stems emerging from the centre of the leaf rosettes. Flowering stems are covered in tiny short hairs. White, cream or pink flowers are also often pubescens. Shape and colour of flowers depends on cultivar.

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 50cm, with straplike, glaucous green leaves. Flowers are 6cm across, with white outer petals and a fully split, white corona with a pale lemon yellow throat. Produces 3-5 flowers per stem from mid to late spring
A large-cupped daffodil to 50cm, flowering in mid- to late spring. The 10cm blooms have broad, creamy-white outer petals and an orange cup

Neat, compact rose about 80cm tall, with glossy, dark coppery green foliage, and bearing small clusters of lightly scented, fully double, frilled orange blooms, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn

alternative_names: chilli pepper Habanero Group|sweet pepper habanero|Capsicum chinense 'Habanero'|Capsicum annuum var. annuum Longum Group habanero
description: A group of very hot chilli peppers originating from the Amazon region. The bushy plants typically produce fruit about 2-6cm long, ripening from green to a number of colours including orange, red as well as white, brown, yellow and purple

A very hot Habanero type chilli pepper cultivar growing around 70cm tall producing fruit typically 2.5-4cm long ripening from green to red. The fruit shape resembles tam o’ shanter flat bonnet. Wear gloves when handling the fruit

A half-hardy perennial that produces vigorous, bushy plants with thick stems and flowers in mid to late autumn. Plants are relatively dwarf reaching 60cm in height. It bears double, incurved blooms in a warm yellow. Disbudded, these reach 14cm across. Florets are long and broad, overlapping, pointed and curled

A tender/half-hardy perennial that produces vigorous, bushy plants with thick stems. Plants are relatively dwarf reaching 60cm in height and flower in mid to late autumn. Blooms are double, incurved and brown-bronze in colour. Disbudded, they reach 14cm across. Florets are long and broad, overlapping, pointed and curled

A half-hardy/tender perennial that produces vigorous, bushy plants with thick stems. Plants are relatively dwarf reaching 60cm in height and flower in mid to late autumn. The double, lilac-pink blooms are incurved and, when disbudded, reach 14cm across. Florets are long and broad, overlapping, pointed and curled.
A truly miniature conifer, taking 10 years to form a neat, conical tree to 0.8m tall. It bears short, bright green needles. Ideal for a container or rock garden

An upright clump-forming herbaceous perennial, up to 1.2m high, with deciduous, seven-lobed, mid-green leaves, and large, shallowly bowl-shaped flowers, 5-6cm across, of deep magenta-pink petals with black centres and veins, from early to late summer

A low, spreading shrub with pale green foliage that becomes mottled white and tinged pink in summer before turning brilliant shades of orange and red in autumn. Yellow flowers are borne in racemes along the branches in mid-spring and followed by glossy red fruit

A rhizomatous, evergreen, mat-forming perennial to around 15cm high with shiny, dark green, heart-shaped leaves. Bell-shaped, solitary flowers are borne beneath the foliage at the base of the plant in late winter or early spring and are pale green to pale yellow with dark purple banding at the base and tips of the petals
A cultivar, that when grown as a cushion mum, produces a plant around 40cm in height with a neat, compact shape. Flowers, produced in early autumn, are single and bronze with a yellow centre

A small, compact selection, to 1.5m, of this thicket-forming shrub. It has many upright stems and a distinctive leaf colouring; yellow-green flushed with bright reddish-pink and bronze in spring. Leaves become greener in summer, but redden in autumn; colouring is best in good light. Flowers are borne in stiff, erect, rather narrow panicles of small white flowers in summer

primary_name: Arum italicum subsp. neglectum 'Miss Janey Hall' (v)

description: A shrub reaching up to 1.2m in height. It bears simple, single white flowers with golden stamens borne in clusters of blooms that continue from early summer through to autumn
An upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with deeply divided mid-green leaves. Branched stems bear compact heads of dark, crimson-red flowers, surrounded by green-tipped white bracts, in summer

primary_name: Primula auricula L. subsp. bauhinii f. marginata

description: Spreading, then conical deciduous tree about 8m in height, with broadly oval mid-green leaves, and large lilac to purple-pink cup-and-saucer shaped flowers to 20cm across, produced in late spring

Deciduous small tree or large shrub to around 5m tall with fresh green ovate to obovate leaves, and cup-and-saucer-shaped, deep pink to reddish flowers 20-30cm across that are borne in spring before the leaves emerge
An evergreen perennial with grey-green foliage and fully double flowers to around 7cm across, with a white background and fine red markings towards the edge of the petals appearing in the summer
A fast-growing, large shrub or multi-stemmed tree. Tulip-shaped, pale to mid-yellow flowers open over several weeks in spring both before and after the foliage emerges

Has narrow, lax green leaves to 110cm on a vigorous, spreading plant. Stems are straight, well-branched, erect to 105cm, usually bearing 3 large flowers. Standards are cupped, white with some yellow veining. Falls are flaring, circular, white slightly flushed with yellow. Signal yellow;mid season

Vigorous, bushy old-fashioned rose, rare in cultivation, about 1.5-1.8m tall, with an upright habit and healthy, grey-green foliage. Very fragrant, pure white, semi-double blooms of good shape and size, with a hint of gold towards the centre, once-flowering in midsummer, suited to part shade; introduced in 1817
A tender perennial with mid-green, hairy and wrinkled leaves. Flowers freely borne over a long season haverose-pink lower lobes edged with the same paler pink shade that colours the upper lobes
An evergreen purple-sprouting broccoli which is quick to produce a harvest and if continually picked, can keep producing for many months into winter

An upright, branching, biennial with oblong, wavy-edged, blue-green leaves. The sideshoots, or spears, are topped with purple-flushed buds and harvested as sprouting broccoli from autumn to spring. This cultivar produces high quality spears, of good flavour and texture, and can crop for up to two months

A hardy biennial purple sprouting broccoli variety grown as an annual. It is one of the earliest varieties, producing well coloured, good sized purple spears from November to March when fresh vegetables in the garden tend to be scarce. If growing in colder climates, the crop will be ready to harvest from February
A very hardy evergreen annual/biennial vegetable with large flowerheads, which is harvested in March

An evergreen short-lived perennial usually grown as a biennial. To around 60cm high in flower, with a bushy, upright habit and narrow, dark green leaves. Fragrant, deep crimson flowers are produced from spring into summer
Purple-sprouting broccoli to 60cm tall producing medium to large dark purple spears ready to harvest from spring into early summer

An upright, deciduous ornamental tree reaching a potential height of up to 10m, with a rounded habit and toothed green foliage changing to crimson-red in the autumn. Large, single, fragrant wine-red flowers appear in the summer followed by small, purple-red fruits

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 45cm high, with slightly glaucous, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers from mid spring, producing solitary flowers to 7.5cm across, with rounded, white outer petals and a large, salmon pink cup with a lightly ruffled rim

Fast-growing tree about 25m tall, with a broad crown and pink-tinged, grey-white bark, orange-brown when young, and peeling in narrow strips, coppery on the branches. Dark green heart-shaped leaves to 15cm long turn yellow in autumn; yellow brown male catkins are produced in early spring

primary_name: Lavandula stoechas subsp. stoechas f. leucantha 'Snowball'

description: A clump-forming perennial up to 50cm tall and wide, with thick erect stems bearing shallowly scalloped, broadly elliptic, grey-green leaves and starry bright magenta pink flowers, in flat terminal clusters in late summer

An evergreen perennial, normally grown as an indoor plant, producing a 40cm clump of lance-shaped, dark green leaves with finely tapered points and pale pinkish-orange stems. Short, almost stemless, spikes of greenish-white, star-shaped flowers appear in the centre of the clump in spring and summer

primary_name: Camassia leichtlinii subsp. suksdorfii 'Lady Eve Price'
description: A deciduous, clump-forming perennial bulb with long, narrow, erect green foliage and from late spring into early summer, spikes of compact, dark, violet-blue star-shaped flowers to around 60cm tall

A hardy perennial usually grown as an annual vegetable, with thick, upright blue green leaves. This F1 hybrid leek produces a good yield of uniform, straight smooth stems. Ready to harvest from October depending on sowing time, keeps well in the ground
A compact, deciduous shrub up to 1.5m high and 1.2m wide, producing a profusion of small, deep yellow flowers with broad lobes, in early to mid-spring before the leaves appear

A compact, mound-forming herbaceous perennial producing stems to 40cm (16in) high. Bright purple-blue saucer-shaped flowers with darker purple veining, appear from April to May and a second flush can often occur in summer.

alternative_names: panicled hydrangea [Perle d'Automne]|Hydrangea paniculata 'Starlight Fantasy'|Hydrangea paniculata [Magical Starlight]|Hydrangea paniculata 'Degustar'
description: A branching, deciduous shrub, to 1.8m tall, with ovate green leaves that turn shades of orange and red in autumn. Large, conical flower panicles are borne from summer into autumn and open pure white before maturing to a pale pink colour

alternative_names: Chinese hawthorn [Curly Fantasy]|Photinia fraseri 'Curly Fantasy'|Photinia serratifolia 'Kolcurl'
description: An evergreen shrub or small tree around 2m high with red stems and coarsely toothed, glossy, leathery, oblong leaves which have wavy undulating edges. The leaves are up to 15cm long, and bright coppery red when young, becoming dark green when mature. Clusters of small cream to white flowers appear in late spring, followed by small red fruits the size of hawthorne berries. A lime-tolerant Photinia.
A sweetly scented cultivar with striking dark red flowers against grey-green foliage

A very compact, mound-forming, herbaceous perennial, with reddish-green, lobed foliage in spring, turning to a dark, olive green in summer, on stems to 15cm (6in) high and 30cm (12in) across. In summer to autumn, saucer shaped, reddish-pink flowers with a white eye and veins appear in profusion above the foliage.
A clump-forming, deciduous perennial herb with upright stems and a tuft of dark green lance-shaped foliage at the base. White, daisy-like flowers with yellow centres appear from July to August

Bushy, upright rose about 80cm tall, bearing glossy mid-green leaves, with masses of fragrant, fully double, large, lemon-yellow blooms, produced in small clusters and repeat flowering through summer and autumn

An upright, bushy annual legume bred specifically for the British climate and self-pollinating. It has green foliage and small, insignificant sweet-pea like white to purple-pink flowers which appear from July through to September, followed by clusters of green, hairy fruit pods containing around 3 to 4 soyabeans per pod. Ready to harvest July through to November, when the pods turn yellow and leaves begin to drop

A tender perennial with a bushy, clump-forming habit. In spring, upright stems with mid-green, arrowhead shaped aromatic leaves emerge. From mid-summer to mid-autumn, a succession of azure blue flowers are held above the foliage on thin stems.

An excellent variety that produces smooth-skinned, wedge-shaped roots with a delicious, sweet taste. Growth is uniform and vigorous with some resistance to canker. Sow: February to May, Harvest: October to February

An unusual, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, daisy-like blooms with narrow, drooping yellow petals surrounding a prominent central brown cone through Summer and Autumn. Excellent for prairie style planting and as a cut flower

Distinctive, upright, perennial coneflower to about 75cm tall, producing unusual blooms with slightly quilled, white ray petals, evenly tinged green, surrounding a large dark green central cone, flowering from midsummer to autumn

alternative_names: Martin's spurge 'Aperitif'|Euphorbia 'Mini Martinii'|Euphorbia × martinii 'Little Martinii'|Euphorbia 'Little Martinii'

description: A compact, clump-forming perennial forming a mound of lance-shaped, glossy green leaves with wavy, creamy-white margins speckled with green. Spikes of pale lavender, tubular flowers to around 20cm high appear above the foliage in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated bright yellow foliage and wide green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A compact, clump-forming dwarf herbaceous perennial with ovate, pointed, slightly wavy leaves which have a yellow center that lightens to cream, a dark green edge, and chartreuse jetting towards the midrib. It is a sport of 'Island Charm' with wider margins. Bright, pinkish-red flower stems carry vibrant lavender flowers which appear in midsummer

An upright, compact, clump-forming perennial with slightly 'twisted' white leaves with a dark green margin. Tall, pale lavender flowers appear in July. Needs plenty of light (not hot sun) and regular feeding to perform at its best, and should not be restricted to small pots or containers

A herbaceous perennial producing a mound of foliage about 40cm high and 90cm across. The leaves are intensely blue-green, with a glaucous bloom; opening with creamy-white margins. Tubular flowers on blue-green stems appear in mid to late summer

A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 60cm high, with broad, thick, slightly wavy leaves that are pale creamy yellow in the centre and dark blue-green at the margins. Produces loose clusters of bell-shaped, near white flowers on upright stems in summer

A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial with broadly ovate to heart-shaped, veined, blue leaves with a strong yellow centre. By late summer the leaves become more blue-green and the center is more cream. Upright stems of lavender flowers appear in mid-summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to around 30cm high and 50cm wide. Leaves are broadly ovate, dark green in the centre with a broad, irregular pale yellow marking sometimes speckled with green. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems to 50cm high in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and creamy-yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with green foliage and wavy margins. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in the summer

A small, clump-forming, deciduous perennial with rounded leaves with emerge gold with blue-green margins. The leaves become cupped as they mature and the centres turn to creamy white. Upright stems produce clusters of pale lavender-purple flowers in summer. A good choice for pots and containers due to its compact nature

A vigorous, clump-forming perennial to 40cm high, forming a mound of narrow, lance-shaped, blue-green leaves with broad creamy yellow margins. Produces loose clusters of tubular, pale purple flowers on tall, upright stems in summer

A small, clump-forming perennial to 20cm high, with ovate, slightly cupped, glossy dark green leaves with a broad creamy yellow streak in the centre. Produces loose clusters of purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated white foliage and very wide green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A clump-forming, deciduous perennial with green leaves and thin, creamy-yellow margins. Upright stems produce clusters of lavender-purple flowers in summer

A medium, clump-forming perennial with thick, variegated green foliage with yellow margins in spring, turning more creamy-white as the season progresses. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated dark green, glossy foliage with white margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and creamy-white margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and yellow-white margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated white foliage and dark green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with unusual puckered, creamy-white foliage with bicolor pale and dark green margins Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with dark green foliage. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in the summer. An all-green sport of H. 'Cracker Crumbs'

alternative_names: plantain lily 'June Fever'|Hosta × tardiana 'June Fever'|Hosta 'June Fever'
description: A clump-forming, slow-growing perennial with bright yellow-green leaves and a thinner, dark green margin around the edges Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in July. A variety that seems to have good slug and sun resistance although some protection from these is still recommended
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with small, rounded pale green foliage. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with yellow, variegated foliage and dark green-blue margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A compact, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial with heart-shaped gold leaves. Upright stems of mauve/lilac flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 40cm high, with broadly ovate to heart-shaped, muted yellow-green leaves with a blue-green streak in the centre. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

A compact perennial forming a tight mound of ovate to heart-shaped green leaves with creamy-white margins to 25cm high. In summer, erect stems to 45cm high bear pale lavender flowers above the foliage
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated, thick blue-green foliage and creamy-yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A small, slow-growing tree with palmate, prominently dark-veined leaves, emerging pink, turning red and then purple and finally becoming orange, red and purple in autumn

A round-headed, large, deciduous tree, about 15m in height selected for its early and intense autumn leaf colour. Palmate, 3 to 5-lobed, dark green leaves, grey-green and covered in dense, woolly, soft down beneath, turn brilliant red in September. A male clone that produces dense, upright clusters of tiny red flowers in spring before the leaves, but does not produce fruit

An oval to round-headed, deciduous tree about 10m tall. The 3-5 lobed palmate are leaves to 10cm long. The new spring growth is reddish-green, maturing to bright green in summer, then turning brilliant, fiery red in autumn if the weather is reliably cold. Upright clusters of tiny red flowers are borne in spring followed by dark red winged fruits in autumn. This selection keep its autumn tones for longer than other cultivars and its canopy especially symmetrical in shape

A deciduous shrub to around 2.4m tall with slender, upright deep red stems. Ovate leaves may turn shades of red, orange and yellow in autumn and creamy-white flowers in late spring and early summer are followed by small clusters of white fruit

A large, vigorous, spreading deciduous shrub with dull, purple-red stems and dark green leaves turning orange, red or purple in autumn. Arched sprays of white flowers in late spring and early summer are followed by metallic blue berries

A vigorous small tree reaching up to 7m, with large, glossy, pointed, dark green leaves producing red and purple tints in autumn. In early summer, tight clusters of small, greenish flowers are surrounded by large, broad, pointed white bracts with a hint of green, followed by edible, deep pink, strawberry-like fruit

A shrub or small tree, up to 3m high, with variegated grey-green leaves with broad pale cream margins, which become flushed with pink and soft orange in autumn. The flowers, with showy white bracts, in early summer are followed by red fruits which are edible raw or cooked

A multi-stemmed, fast-growing, suckering deciduous shrub with dark green, ovate foliage and bright red stems which are at their brightest in the winter months. White flowers appear in the spring and summer, followed by bluish-white fruit
A medium-sized branching tree growing to 15m tall. The three-lobed leaves, up to 15cm across, emerge a burgundy-purple in spring, darken to green in summer and are a burgundy-red colour in the autumn

A deciduous shrub with toothed, deep-veined, dark green foliage which changes to red-purple in the autumn. Branches are tiered horizontally and white lace-cap flowers appear in the spring, becoming pink as they mature. A suitable shrub for Japanese-style gardens

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 43cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and double, fragrant pale-lemon coloured flowers that have a green throat to 12cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 69cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and pale apricot coloured flowers to 15cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of light purple-dark pink flowers with a cream edge around each petal and a yellow green centre

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and slightly ruffled purple flowers, to around 15cm across above a chartreuse throat in summer
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are bright yellow with slightly ruffled petals, a yellow throat and are very late flowering
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, green foliage. and wavy edges. Upright, dark red stems of dark purple striped flowers appear in the summer

A vigorous upright evergreen shrub, with glossy dark green, elliptic leaves with finely serrated edges. Flowers are anemone-form to 9cm across, and a deep plum red with a mass of upright frilly petals in the centre, and a silvery sheen on the outer petals. Flowers over a long period from early to late spring

A dwarf evergreen sub-shrub forming a bushy mound to 50cm. The narrow leaves are green flushed with dark reddish purple, the colour deepest in good light. The flower bracts are bright yellowish green, present from early to late spring
A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 30cm high, with lance-shaped, ribbed glossy green leaves. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated lime green foliage and creamy-white margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 40cm high, with ovate, deep green leaves with a glaucous bloom and broad, pale green to creamy yellow marking in the centres. Produces loose clusters of white flowers from pale purple buds, on upright stems in summer
A small to medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with narrow, yellow foliage and wavy green margins which turn darker later in the season. Upright stems of white flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with green foliage and red-purple stems. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in the summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 60cm high, with large, broadly ovate to heart-shaped leaves, blue-green with deep veining and wide, irregular creamy yellow margins. Produces loose clusters of almost pure white flowers on upright stems in summer
A dwarf cultivar, making a low rounded mound with a flattish top and distinctively arranged dark green needle-like leaves, to 1.5cm long. are whiteish beneath. No cones are produced

A large erect deciduous shrub or small tree to 6m in height, of open habit, with oval, green-bronze leaves when young which turn shades of orange and red in autumn. Clusters of small, star-shaped white flowers are produced in spring followed by edible dark purple to black berries

Majestic deciduous tree about 30m tall having a straight smooth trunk, with pale orange-brown or creamy-pink bark when young, aging to rough greyish-brown. Slender, pointed dark green leaves on downy shoots emerge early in the season with the long, yellow-brown male catkins
A spreading, evergreen shrub up to 2m tall with hairy, grey-green leaves that turn glossy green with age and bright yellow, daisy-like flowerheads from summer to early autumn
A hardy evergreen shrub approximately 31-45cm tall with a spread to 46-60cm. It has bright green foliage and tapering stems of pink flowers in summer through to autumn.

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with green, lance-shaped foliage. Tall, upright stems of large, outward facing, powdery-blue, bell-shaped, single flowers providing a long flowering display in summer

A compact evergreen shrub to 1m high, with a rounded habit, and ovate to oblong leaves with blunt, rounded tips. Produces white flowers to 5cm across, with yellow marks at the base of the petals and yellow stamens, in early to mid summer

A deciduous, upright, and compact tree to a height of just 3m. Four-petalled flower bracts appear in April and May. Its leaves are green with bold yellow variegation. In autumn the foliage takes on red and purple tints

A compact, rounded, evergreen shrub with rigid branches and very small leaves, dark glossy green above, greyish below. Small, white flowers open from pink buds in early summer, followed by dark red, spherical fruit

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit up to 60cm tall when in flower. It has healthy, mid-green, blade-like leaves and strong, arching flower stems that bear orange-red tubular flowers, from summer to autumn

A small, perennial corm growing to around 7cm high, with long, narrow, dark green leaves with a paler central stripe. In early spring, produces goblet-shaped white flowers, with outer petals heavily streaked with violet on the outside

A variety of quince up to 5m in height, which is highly productive. Green leaves with pale undersides appear before fragrant, white to pale rose-pink flowers in spring, followed by pear-shaped, fragrant golden-yellow fruits from October which can be used for jams and jellies or adding sparingly to apple pies and crumbles for extra tartness. As quince fruits are very fragrant, they are best stored away from other fruits to avoid tainting them
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with a range of blue and pink flowers in summer.

primary_name: Dryopteris affinis subsp. affinis var. disjuncta

alternative_names: scaly male fern 'Crispa Barnes'|Dryopteris cambrensis 'Crispa Barnes'|Dryopteris affinis 'Crispa Barnes'

description: A clump-forming, semi-evergreen fern producing an erect rhizome bearing shuttlecock-like rosettes of tightly packed, triangular to lance-shaped, dark green fronds, with finely divided, crested segments

A fast-growing, clump-forming perennial, producing stems to 60cm high and a spread of 50cm. Leaves are dark-green with a white central vein. Small inconspicuous flowers surrounded by showy, bright, lime-yellow floral bracts, are produced in terminal clusters in summer

primary_name: Galanthus ikariae subsp. ikariae Latifolius Group
Galanthus ikariae subsp. latifolius Latifolius Group

description: Rare in cultivation, this evergreen, self-clinging climber about 2m tall, bears arrow-shaped, 3-lobed mid to dark green leaves. Mature foliage may produce small flowers in greenish umbels during autumn followed by black berries. Ideal for walls

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and peach-pink flowers with a peach-pink eyezone and a gold throat to 14cm across in summer
A compact, clump-forming perennial with blue-green leaves. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in early summer

A deciduous perennial to around 15cm tall with trailing stems of grey-green, rounded, fleshy leaves to 2cm across. In late summer, dome-shaped flowerheads up to 10cm across, comprising clusters of star-shaped pink flowers to 1cm, are held on short stems above the foliage

A dense, evergreen shrub or tree with spiny, dark green foliage with narrow, irregular creamy-white margins. Young stems emerge purple, and white flowers appear in the spring. This male clone does not produce berries but makes a good pollinator for female I. aquifolium cultivars

Vigorous woody, evergreen climber, deciduous in cooler areas, about 3.5m or more tall with opposite, tapered, dark green leaves. Small, fragrant, deep ruby-red flowers appear during summer, followed by shining black berries, often lasting well into winter
A deciduous, suckering shrub, to around 2m high, with arching, bright green stems and oval-shaped, serrated green leaves up to 10cm long. Golden yellow flowers are produced in mid to late spring

A bulbous perennial to around 1.2m high, with upright stems and lanced-shaped glossy dark green leaves. Large, highly fragranced white flowers with yellow markings down each petal are produced in early summer
A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large upward-facing, orange to dark orange with dark red stamens appear in summer

A vigorous, deciduous or semi-evergreen, twining climber about 5m tall, with paired, oval, dark green leaves to 6cm long, blue-green beneath, and tubular 2-lipped fragrant flowers in brightly coloured shades of pink outside and orange-yellow inside, produced in summer, and occasionally followed by red berries

A deciduous crab apple tree, with a narrowly upright habit, and oval-shaped green leaves that are tinted red when young, and turn dark red before dropping in autumn. Masses of fragrant pink flowers are produced in spring, followed in early autumn by small red fruits

A semi-evergreen bulbous perennial to 45cm high, with narrow, strap-shaped green leaves. Flowers are large and lily-like, with wavy, recurved petals in mid pink with deeper pink centres, and are borne in clusters around the tips of upright stems in autumn

A slow-growing evergreen shrub, to around 1.8m high, with a bushy habit and elliptic, glossy green leaves with irregular pale cream margins, that are tinted reddish-pink when young. Pendent clusters of small, scented, urn-shaped white flowers are borne at the tips of the stems in spring

A slow-growing pine able to reach 15m (50ft) when mature, although usually smaller, with a strongly tapering trunk, often twisted with age bearing grey to reddish-brown strongly fissured bark and a flat, irregularly shaped canopy. The trees are capable of reaching a very great age in habitat and can be among the oldest living things on earth. The evergreen, deep blue-green needles are produced in groups of five and up to 4cm (1½in) long. They are persistent and can live up to 17 years. The purple to brown roughly cylindrical cones take two years to mature and are soon shed after dispersing their seeds
A slow growing evergreen tree, with needles 5-7cm long and borne in pairs. Foliage is dark green in summer and turns golden yellow in winter.
A clump-forming perennial with finely divided green leaves and masses of lilac-pink, 5-petalled flowers with a dark red 'eye', produced in masses through the summer
A compact, vigorous rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with neat, pale green, toothed foliage with a silvery coating, and short stems of creamy-white fragrant flowers which appear in late spring
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, coated with a silvery powder, and fragrant, double, dark velvety-red flowers, appearing in the spring

primary_name: Pyrus communis 'Max Red Bartlett' dwarf pyramid

description: A rhubarb producing 'first early' growth. Plants are vigorous and high yielding, with thick, fairly sweet stems and good colour. Good leaf to stem ratio; suitable for showing

primary_name: Rheum × hybridum from Isle of Ely Horticultural Institute

description: An evergreen shrub to about 1.5m high, with ovate, glossy green leaves with fawn-coloured felting on the undersides. Produces loose clusters of bell-shaped, lavender flowers with wavy edges and pale, near white throats, in late spring

primary_name: Rhododendron wardii var. wardii Wardii Group

description: A low-growing perennial to about 10cm with greyish-green leaves and deep pink flowers throughout the summer
Short, spreading bushy rose about 60cm tall, with glossy, mid-green foliage, and bearing large clusters of mildly scented, small double pale pink blooms through summer to autumn

A large, climbing rose about 6m tall, with thorny stems bearing abundant grey-green foliage, and rounded, fully double, pink flowers 12cm in width, with a strong myrrh scent, produced in one flush of flower in midsummer

alternative_names: rose 'Dunwich Rose'|Rosa pimpinellifolia 'Dunwich'|Rosa spinosissima 'Dunwich'|Rosa spinosissima 'Dunwich Rose'|Rosa pimpinellifolia 'Dunwich Rose'
description: A vigorous, twiggy rose with arching stems forming a low hummock of fern-like foliage about 60cm high and twice that across. In early summer it bears a profusion of bowl-shaped, single, slightly-scented, creamy-white flowers, 6cm across, with prominent gold stamens

Vigorous shrub rose about 2m tall, with arching reddish, grey-green, almost thornless stems bearing purple-flushed, greyish-green foliage. Clear mauve-pink, single flowers with pale centres are once-flowering in summer and followed by oval red fruit (hips)

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 80cm in height, with greyish tinted scalloped, mid green leaves, and slender racemes of small rose-pink lipped flowers which have reddish-purple bracts from late spring throughout summer.

An evergreen, mat-forming perennial with rosesttes of fleshy green leaves suffused with red and densely covered in white cobweb-like hairs. Short, upright stems bearing terminal clusters of pink flowers may appear in suumer

alternative_names: Tibetan whitebeam 'John Mitchell'|Sorbus thibetica 'John Mitchell'|Sorbus 'Mitchellii'|Sorbus aria 'Mitchellii'
description: A compact medium-sized deciduous tree with broadly rounded leaves up to 15cm in length, white-hairy when young, later glossy green above, white-hairy beneath. Creamy white flowers followed by brown fruits

alternative_names: thyme 'Golden King'|lemon thyme 'Golden King'|lemon thyme 'Variegatus'|Thymus citriodorus 'Variegatus'|Thymus citriodorus 'Vila Nova'|Thymus citriodorus misapplied 'Golden King' [1]
description: A compact, upright, bushy, evergreen shrub with narrow, lance-shaped, aromatic, mid-green leaves with golden yellow margins. Clusters of pink flowers appear in summer
A low-growing, upright, bushy, evergreen shrub with brilliant lemon scented, yellow and green variegated foliage and pink flowers in summer

alternative_names: thyme 'Silver Queen'|lemon thyme 'Silver Queen'|Thymus vulgaris 'Silver Queen'|Thymus citriodorus misapplied 'Silver Queen' [1]
description: A bushy, dwarf evergreen shrub to 30cm in height, with small, variegated, lemon scented dark green leaves which are edged with creamy-white. Clusters of tiny, pale mauve-pink flowers appear in the summer
A perennial bulb, up to 75cm high, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Tall stems of violet-purple cup-shaped single flowers appear in late spring. A very old breed introduced in 1863

A perennial bulb, to around 40cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. An historic cultivar, bearing cup-shaped flowers with pointed white petals with a purple-pink flame. Early flowering
A compact, bushy, relatively short-lived perennial to 30cm, with bright green foliage. Large, daisy-like, red and yellow flowers are borne on upright stems from early summer to early autumn

alternative_names: lavender 'Goodwin Creek Grey'|Lavandula 'Goodwin Creek'|Lavandula 'Goodwin Creek Grey'
description: A shrub up to 90cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, silvery sage-green-grey leaves which are 4-6cm long and may be toothed. Upright spikes of fragrant, dark violet-blue flowers appear from midsummer; in mild climates it may flower at other times as well
An evergreen shrub to around 60cm tall and wide with greyish-green foliage and spikes of deep purple flowerheads topped with up to five showy purple-blue bracts from late spring into summer
An upright variety which can be short-lived. It produced rosettes of grey-green velvety leaves, followed by long, slim stems of flat, yellow flowers during the summer

alternative_names: French lavender 'Purple Emperor'|Lavandula stoechas subsp. sampaioana 'Purple Emperor'|Lavandula 'Purple Emperor'
description: An aromatic, evergreen shrub to about 75cm with grey-green foliage and upright, dark purple flower spikes on long stalks, topped with rosy-purple bracts, from late spring and throughout summer

An unusual annual herb, known as the large leaved basil, with frilly edged leaves reaching up to 12cm long and having a strong basil flavour. Short spikes of white flowers appear in late summer. Excellent for container growing and adding interest to traditional herb displays

A low-growing, mat-forming, spreading evergreen perennial to around 20cm in height, with soft, velvety, aromatic lance-shaped silvery-green leaves. Clusters of fragranced flowers in shades of white or pink appear from June through until August

A vigorous, twining evergreen perennial to around 3m in height, with heart-shaped green leaves. Large, wide, funnel-shaped pale blue flowers with a white throat open over a long period from late spring to autumn

A woody, evergreen, twining climber to about 6m in height, with oval, glossy, dark green leaves, sometimes flushed dark red in winter and sweetly-scented, creamy-white flowers with yellow centres in mid and late summer, that fade to creamy-yellow with age
A small, slow-growing tree ultimately to 2m in height and spread. The toothed, five-lobed leaves open pale pink, gradually turning green with a white border, then lime green in autumn

A narrow, columnar, upright growing tree, with dense foliage and pale green, often three-lobed leaves, 25cm (10in) long. In summer it bears upright stalks of cream-white flowers with purple and orange markings followed by slender hanging pods. This cultivar is reportedly variable in habit.
An evergreen, slow-growing, dwarf conifer with irregular sprays of mid-to-dark green foliage, giving a fern-like appearance

A slowly-growing, rounded deciduous shrub to 3m tall, with heart-shaped, blue-green leaves with irregular, creamy-white margins. In autumn it produces lightly fragrant, spidery red flowers to 2cm across. Before the leaves fall they take on bright, fiery hues

A spreading, deciduous shrub or small tree to 4m, with finely toothed leaves to 6cm long. In late spring and early summer it bears pendent clusters of 5-15, bell-shaped rose-pink flowers. This cultivar reliably produces good, red autumn colour

A spreading deciduous shrub or small tree to 4m, with ovate leaves to 6cm long. In late spring and early summer it bears pendent clusters of 5-15, bell-shaped rosy-pink flowers. In autumn the foliage takes on fiery red and orange hues

A spreading, deciduous shrub or small tree to 4m, with toothed leaves to 6cm long. In late spring and early summer it bears pendent clusters of 5-15, large, bell-shaped cream flowers flushed and veined red. In autumn the foliage turns fiery orange and red

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high, with a spreading habit and lobed and lighty hairy, mid green leaves. White flowers faintly veined with purple are borne freely over a long period from early summer

A dwarf, slow-growing tree to around 7m in height, with a broad, bushy habit. Fan-shaped yellow-green foliage in spring turns to yellow in summer. A great variety for smaller gardens and spaces where space is limited

A deciduous shrub or small tree to 4m high, with ascending branches creating a vase-shaped form. Leaves are broadly ovate with broadly serrated margins, and coloured from dark green to deep purple-bronze, turning shades of red and yellow in autumn. Produces dense clusters of fragrant flowers on bare stems in late winter and early spring, each with four long, narrow, golden yellow petals, backed by small, recurved rich brown sepals at the base

A compact, rounded deciduous shrub to 1.2m high, with dark green ovate leaves. Dense conical clusters of flowers are produced from mid to late summer, opening white and maturing to a pale pink that holds into early autumn

A sturdy, upright to slightly spreading shrub with a compact habit, to around 140cm in height with yellow-green foliage and dark, purplish-red stems, maturing to brown. Dense, conical, tapered panicles of cream fertile flower buds with pink tips and sterile lime-green flowers turning to pale green, white then dark pink as they mature, appear in summer. The flowers have a spicy fragrance

This large species can reach up to 4m high with large, dark green leathery leaves to 75cm long, yellow-green beneath, with 8-13 pairs of leaflets on pale, corky stems. Racemes of long, bright yellow flowers appear in early autumn, followed by purplish-black fruits

A bushy, upright, deciduous shrub with golden juvenile foliage in spring that slowly develops to green-yellow through the season. Pure white, double to semi-double flowers appear in summer carrying a rich, sweet orange blossom fragrance
A slow-growing, dense and shrubby dwarf conifer, ultimately making a conical tree to 2m tall. The needles are blue-green beneath and yellow-green on the upper surface
An upright rocket-shaped conifer with medium length dark green needles. Pale brown candle-shaped cones appear in the spring

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which unlike the typical species, produces a compact, flattened spherical bush, eventually reaching up to 1.5m (5ft) high and 2m (6½ft) across after around ten years. The dark-green needles are soft, and up to 12cm (5in) long and slightly twisted, giving the bush a ruffled texture. They are very densely produced, so that the stems and basal branches are concealed by them. It is an ideal choice for a small city, or courtyard garden, where an architectural, or evergreen focal point is needed

A deciduous shrub to around 2m high with a spreading habit. Ovate to oblong leaves that taper to a point emerge in spring a rich golden-yellow becoming greener with age. Hanging racemes of pale yellow flowers are borne from late winter into early spring

An upright, deciduous shrub or spreading tree to 8m tall, with leaves divided into 3 lance-shaped leaflets. In mid-and late spring, before the leaves emerge, it bears pendent clusters of bell-shaped, 1.5cm long white flowers with a pink tint. These later develop into bladder-like, green seed pods which turn pink and red in autumn. Grow in a shrub border or woodland garden

A large shrub or small tree to around 4m high, with an upright, bushy habit and broadly oval, slightly glossy deep green leaves. New leaves emerge deep purple and retain a purplish tint when grown in full sun. Clusters of pendent, bell-shaped pale pink flowers are produced along the undersides of the branches in early summer. Leaves turn yellow and orange in autumn

A bulbous perennial producing a rosette of long, strap-shaped, dark green leaves, heavily blotched with dark purple-red. The star-shaped, dark red-purple flowers are produced in late summer in cylindrical spikes 15cm high, with a cluster of purple-edged and spotted, dark green bracts at the top

Dense, clump-forming, evergreen perennial 60-75cm tall, with foliage in shades of bronze and olive-green, tinted pink and becoming darker, flushed deep bronze-red, in winter. Carries semi-trailing black flower spikes within the foliage, during summer
Clump-forming perennial about 30-60cm high, with finely divided dark green leaves with toothed margins. Produces tall, fluffy plumes of pale salmon-pink flowers, to 45cm tall, in midsummer
