Flowers can be produced in spring; a pale yellow flower spike emerging from the centre of a rosette. This rosette will then die, but will have formed offsets at its base to grow on

Bulbous perennial producing short-lived, strap-shaped, mid-green leaves and large, densely-packed, spherical heads of purple-pink, star-shaped flowers, on straight stems to 1.2m tall in June. The foliage is often wilting and turning brown when the flowers appear, and for best visual effect the bulbs should be sited so that adjacent plants can grow to conceal the leaves as they die back. The flowers are extremely attractive to bees and other pollinating insects, making the plant a wonderful addition to a wildlife garden.

A spreading, moderately vigorous shrub up to 2.5m high and 3.5m wide, with ovate-rounded green leaves 10cm long and 6.5cm wide which are flushed with maroon-purple for a few weeks after they emerge before becoming dark green, then turning yellow in autumn, and slightly scented flowers with deep purplish red calyces and deep burnt orange petals about 2cm long, redder at the base, in late winter
A vigorous, evergreen climber to 4m in height and spread, the three-lobed leaves show a variable mix of grey-green, mid-green, dark green and cream

A deciduous herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and cream-purple flowers with a darker burgundy eyezone above a green throat to 11cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 51cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and small, fragrant, pale lavender coloured flowers that have a washed grey-blue eye-zone and edge with a fuchsia line above a green throat to 6cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for 16 hours or more in a day

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and deep red-black flowers that have a chartreuse-green throat to 14cm across in summer - the flowers remain open for over 16 hours a day

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and burnt orange coloured flowers with a plum-black eye-zone above a green throat to 15cm across in summer

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, and fragrant, double pale pink flowers with a barely visible pale creamy-yellow centre, appearing in the spring

A medium-sized, upright tree with ovate, lobed leaves which are dark green above, glaucous-green beneath, turning long-lasting bright red to purple-red in autumn. Small, red, male flowers are borne in spring
A rosette-forming perennial with spiny, lobed leaves up to 45cm long, with woolly, white undersides. Upright stems to 75cm carry sprays of whiteish-purple, daisy-like flowers in mid-summer

A deciduous shrub or small tree to 4m tall, with ovate leaves to 20cm long, purple-flushed when young. In late summer it bears fragrant, white, star-shaped flowers that emerge from pink buds, these are followed by bright blue berries that form within the persistent pink buds (calyces)
Robust, evergreen, clump-forming bamboo with vigorous, arching yellow-green canes about 4m high that turn shades of red in late summer, with bright green, slender leaves to 10cm long

A deciduous shrub, up to 2.5m tall, with mid-green, lance-shaped leaves. Bright yellow flowers are borne on bare stems in spring; the flowers are larger than average and appear slightly later in spring than other cultivars

A deciduous shrub to 1.5m high, with ovate, serrated green leaves that are tinted with red and bronze. From summer into early autumn, broad lace-cap flower heads bear clusters of tiny fertile flowers, surrounded by large, showy florets with pale centres and a fine edge of rich colour. Flower colour varies depending on the pH of the soil, from deep pink to lavender to baby blue
A dwarf, bushy evergreen conifer with yellow-green needles with bright orange tips appearing in the winter

primary_name: Erythronium revolutum from God's Valley, Oregon
alternative_names: mahogany fawn lily from God's Valley, Oregon

description: A clump-forming perennial to around 60cm high, with upright stems and elliptic, bright green leaves. Long, slender, curving spikes of star-shaped white flowers are produced from early to late summer

A low-growing, compact perennial forming a mat of grey-green, semi-evergreen foliage. Small, pale yellow flowers are held in clusters above the foliage on short stems to 10cm tall in late spring and early summer
This selection bears purplish-pink flowers with white throats. Height to around 90cm

An upright, semi-evergreen perennial to 70cm tall, with mid-green, narrow leaves, stout stems and bell-shaped flowers produced from midsummer into autumn. These are bright purple outside and around the lips, with a solid white throat
This selection bears wine-purple flowers that have white and purple throats. Height to 1m
Has attractive two-tone white and pink flowers. Upright growth, reaching about 70cm
This selection bears purple-pink flowers with white throats that have pink markings. Height to around 80cm
A bushy, semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial. Upright stems produce pure white flowers, with a height to around 80cm, from summer until autumn.

A compact, half-hardy evergreen perennial to 40cm high, with dense clumps of narrow, stiff, grass-like blue-green leaves. In early to mid summer, produces sprays of nodding light blue flowers with conspicuous yellow anthers, held on branched stems high above the foliage. These are sometimes followed by round blue-purple berries
A compact rosette-forming semi-evergreen perennial with toothed, hairy green leaves. Strong stems produce saucer-shaped lavender flowers with deep pink centres during the summer
An upright to spreading, deciduous shrub with dark green leaves that show good autumnal colour. This early-ripening cultivar produces heavy yields of large, light blue berries in midsummer

A late season blueberry forming an upright shrub eventually reaching up to 2m tall with leaves that turn shades of yellow and red in autumn. White spring flowers are followed by clusters of edible, light blue berries in late summer. Suitable for areas with hotter summers

Deciduous climber with slender stems 2-3m tall, with mid-green, serrated leaflets, and single, nodding pink flowers to 5cm long produced from mid to late spring, and occasionally early summer, on the previous seasons old wood, followed by fluffy, decorative seedheads
Compact, dwarf evergreen shrub, about 1m tall, with dense, oblong, glossy dark green leaves, grey-green beneath. Fragrant, saucer-shaped white flowers to 5cm across are produced in early to midsummer

An upright, robust, evergreen shrub to around 1m tall and 1.75m across. The foliage is yellow-green with a pale midrib, and often produces vivid red tones in autumn and winter. Honey-scented, yellow-green flowers are produced from late spring to late summer, turning pale brown as they age, followed by yellow-green, berry-like fruit

alternative_names: dark-calyx Delavay's mock orange|Philadelphus delavayi var. melanocalyx
description: A large, upright, deciduous shrub to 3m tall with arching branches bearing dark green leaves and dense racemes of heavily scented white flowers with purple sepals borne from early to mid-summer
An upright, deciduous shrub with small, widely spaced leaves and very sweet scented, downward facing, white flowers with a purple stain at the base of each petal, produced in early to mid-summer

A potentially large, evergreen shrub, normally grown as an indoor plant. The broad, almost circular leaves, 15cm in diameter, open mid-green, then become bronzy with a narrow, pale pink margin. Catkin-like clusters of tiny red flowers may appear from spring to autumn, but are not showy

alternative_names: white ginger lily 'Gold Spot'|Hedychium gold spot|Hedychium coronarium gold-spotted
description: An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.5m with large, broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Creamy-yellow flowers with yellow centres, fragrant both day and evening, appear from late summer through to October. A hardier variety than others

primary_name: Hedychium spicatum from Salween Valley, China
alternative_names: spiked ginger lily from Salween Valley, China

description: A rhizomatous perennial with upright, arching stems and large, lance-shaped leaves to 80cm. In late summer and autumn it produces a spike of fragrant yellow flowers

An upright, suckering perennial to 4m tall with large, glossy leaves with a maroon-red midrib, dark purple-red striping across the leaves on the upper surface and purple shading beneath. Mature plants may bear long-lasting, yellow-brown flowers enclosed in purple bracts from summer into autumn followed by yellowish fruits

A fan palm with large, evergreen leaves up to 60cm across, waxy-white underneath, and divided into as many as 48 narrow segments. The trunk may retain a loose, fibrous covering of old leaf bases, or these may fall away. Flowering is sparse but mature specimens produce large, branched, yellow-brown clusters of small flowers followed by small, yellow fruit
A bulbous perennial to 50cm tall with grey-green foliage and deep pink to purple flowers with darker purple flames on the outer petals in mid to late spring

A spreading, deciduous tree, to around 10m high, with attractive flaking bark when mature. Leaves are glossy and broadly oval, turning vibrant shades of yellow, red and purple in autumn. Small crimson flowers are produced on bare stems in late winter

A large, deciduous shrub to about 2.5m with corky ridges along the stems. Foliage is oval, pointed, mid-green with fine cream speckles, and turns dark red in autumn. Small, green flowers in spring are followed by dark red, spherical fruit, splitting to reveal orange seeds
An upright, evergreen shrub, with tightly packed dark green glossy leaves which are brighter green when young. Pale green inconspicuous flowers are produced in spring.

A compact and spreading, deciduous shrub, the branches often developing conspicuous corky wings. The oval leaves are variegated, a sliver green centre with a narrow white border, turning rosy-crimson in autumn. Flowers small, greenish, followed by purplish-red fruits splitting to reveal orange seeds

A mid-sized deciduous tree with a spreading habit, long thorns on the branches, and shallowly lobed, toothed green leaves. In late spring, clusters of small white flowers with yellow anthers are produced, followed by red berries

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with relatively shallowly lobed, glossy dark-green leaves. Single, bowl-shaped white flowers, sometimes green-flushed, with pale yellow centres, appear on upright stems in late winter or spring
A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic, slightly grey-green leaves. Spikes of small, violet-coloured fragrant flowers are borne on slender stems in summer

A spreading, medium-sized tree, with heart-shaped, serrated, mid-green leaves turning yellow in autumn. Small, fluffy, catkin-like, green flowers, in late spring or early summer, are followed in late summer by large, succulent, dark red to black fruit ripening in late summer. Self-fertile. It has fruit and foliage larger than other cultivars. Propagated from an old tree growing in Jerusalem

primary_name: Phygelius × rectus [Somerford Funfair Apricot] ('Yapapr') (Somerford Funfair Series)

description: An evergreen shrub, to about 1.2m high, with oval-shaped, dull dark green leaves. Produces dense clusters of up to 9 funnel-shaped, cherry red flowers, in mid to late spring

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark grey-green foliage and branched stems bearing cup-shaped, white to yellow-green single flowers which are slightly green spotted, in late winter and early spring
A hardy, rhizomatous begonia to 50cm tall, with rounded to heart-shaped, mid-green leaves held on long, succulent leafstalks. In autumn it produces pale pink flowers to 4cm across

A clump-forming, deciduous, herbaceous perennial, producing narrow, strap-shaped, mid-green foliage, to a height of around 40cm (16in) and spreading to around 40cm (16in). Hemisperical heads of pendulous, funnel-shaped flowers in very deep purple, are produced in late summer, on straight, green stems, to approximately 80cm (32in) high.

alternative_names: hybrid tulip tree 'Doc Deforce's Delight'|hybrid yellow poplar 'Doc Deforce's Delight'
description: A beautiful, fast-growing tree which has not yet revealed its full height in the UK, but is likely to reach 30m. In spring it has large cup-shaped yellow and red flowers from a very young age. Its large leaves emerge slighty coppery, before turning green. They become bright yellow in autumn before falling

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled, lightly fragrant pale lemon yellow flowers, bright yellow and white falls with pale yellow edges and yellow beards appear from late spring to early summer

Evergreen, creeping perennial to about 15cm tall, producing green foliage edged and blotched gold and cream, the spoon-shaped leaves tinged pink when young, with short spikes of blue flowers appearing in early spring

Strong growing bulbous perennial with broad, poined mid-green basal leaves, Flower stems up to 1.2m tall, bear very large flowerheads 15cm across, made up of starry, silvery-lilac flowers in early summer

An elegant, slow-spreading, semi-evergreen perennial to around 50-70cm in height, forming a compact mound of narrow, dark green, lance-shaped foliage. Fully double, pure-white, bell-shaped flowers appear on upright stems from June to August. Great for bees and for cutting

A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial with medium to large spirally-formed leaves. These have a browny-red edge, with dark green in the central spiral and a mid-green filler with white spots. The reverse of the leaf is red. Compact but vigorous plants reach 25cm in height
A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial with a bold, jagged leaf shape; deep metallic pink overlaid silver-grey and with a dark brown wide margin

A bulbous perennial, to 90cm tall, with a dark sturdy stem bearing whorls of lance-shaped leaves. A large head of bright orange-red, nodding, bell-shaped flowers, topped by leaf-like bracts, is borne in late spring or early summer

A clump-forming, softly hairy,herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall producing low mounds of divided leaves. Scarlet, double flowers to 4cm across are borne on wiry, branched stems from late spring into summer

A tough, tufted, evergreen perennial to 35cm tall, forming dense clumps of linear, glossy green leaves. In late summer it freely produces dense spikes of purple flowers on erect stems. A useful plant for dry shade

A clump-forming perennial with strongly upright, branching stems to 90cm tall, clad with narrowly lance-shaped leaves. Spikes of deep pink to purple-pink star-shaped flowers are produced over a long period during the summer

A small, vigorous, spreading crab apple tree to about 5m, with broadly oval, glossy leaves about 10cm long, opening purplish-red in spring, maturing to dark green, with reddish undersides. Bright pinkish-red flowers appear in early spring, followed by small, round, purple fruit

Compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial, to 25cm tall and 35cm wide, with lance-shaped mid-green foliage. The funnel-shaped white flowers with pale pink flares, yellow throats and maroon-red streaks are borne from summer into autumn

Clump-forming herbaceous perennial with mid-green, lance-shaped leaves and terminal clusters of purple-violet flowers on 1m stems. The inner petals have dark red streaks and the upper two a pale yellow blotch

A fast-growing, bushy perennial to around 30cm in height, with rough-textured, toothed, oblong-shaped dark green foliage. Dense clusters of small, lavender-purple flowers appear on branching stems from summer through to the autumn

A tall, upright, herbaceous perennial to 1.2m with narrow, pointed leaves arranged in whorls around the stems. Stems are topped with long flowering spikes, with deep pink buds opening to tiny, pale pink flowers in late summer and early autumn

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 91cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and velvety, dark red to black coloured flowers with a yellow-green throat to 13cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours
A bulbous herbaceous perennial with upright, lance-shaped green leaves and arching purplish stems. Tubular orange and yellow flowers appear from summer into autumn

A tender, upright, bushy perennial, grown as an annual, with purple flushed dark green leaves that have a classic basil flavour. Dense spikes of whorled, small, tubular, purple flowers appear in summer
A woody-based perennial with hairy, aromatic, ovate leaves and spikes of deep pink, tubular flowers, with dark purple calyces, in summer and autumn

A tall herbaceous perennial, to 1.3m in height, with lanceolate to ovate leaves 7-22cm long. Spikes of cerise pink to cherry red flowers, each up to 4cm long and covered in fine hairs, are borne from summer into autumn

A vigorous, rhizomatous, clump-forming compact perennial with grassy green upright foliage to 80cm high. Flowers are composed of white drooping standards with yellow-green signals wit typically three large flowers on a stem to 65cm high, flowering early to midsummer
A tall iris, to around 105cm, with erect, glaucous foliage to 60cm. Flowers are ruffled, white tinged lavender, with orange-yellow beards. Scented; late season

A rhizomatous perennial to 70cm with fans of bluish-green, sword-shaped leaves that may overwinter. The late-spring to early-summer flowers, on stout, upright stems, have ruffled, very pale pink petals with some greenish shading and violet-blue beards

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, lightly fragrant, ruffled, dark purple-black flowers with buff falls with dark purple and dark wine red veining and rust-orange beards, appearing from late spring to early summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, fragrant, ruffled gold flowers, splashed with plum-red, caramel-brown falls and gold beards appear from late spring to early summer

A rhizomatous perennial, to 90cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have velvety, very dark purple standards and falls, sometimes appearing almost black, and a deep bluish purple beard. Mid season
Reaches 1.1-1.3m, and has bright golden yellow flowers, the falls slightly deeper toned than the standards

A herbaceous, rhizomatous perennial with arching green leaves to 70cm, and flower stems to 90cm with up to 9 flowers per stem. Flowers are large and ruffled, the standards pinkish tan, the falls pinkish tan paling a little in the centre. Beards conspicuous, orange yellow. Mid season

A large, vigorous plant, with spreading green leaves 100-120cm tall. Flower stems are straight and erect, to 140cm, with 3-4 medium-large flowers per stem. Standards and falls rich orange-yellow. Mid-summer

A rhizomatous perennial, to around 90cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are very dark purple, with ruffled petals almost black at the edges, and a violet purple beard

A very tall, clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, fragrant ruffled rich dark purple flowers with bright orange beards appearing May to June, sometimes into July

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, ruffled, dark ruby-red flowers with red to yellow beards and throats, appearing from late spring to early summer
A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial with grey-green strap-like leaves and large, fragrant purple flowers with ruffled edges appearing on strong stems in late spring to early summer

A vigorous plant with lax, slender green foliage to 107cm long. The straight stems, to 105cm, bear up to 5 shapely, smallish flowers, held well above the leaves. Standards are violet-blue, the falls primrose to white with complex deep violet-blue veining

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled, white flowers with a golden edge, violet, magenta and white falls edged with yellow, and yellow beards appear from late spring to early summer

A bushy, deciduous shrub to around 4m tall with deeply lobed green leaves. Medium sized, dark purple-black fruits with sweet red flesh and a good flavour appear in summer and ripen from September. A high yielding cultivar with good cold tolerance
A large evergreen shrub with a dense, upright habit and glossy, lance-shaped green leaves with serrated edges. Produces formal double, rose pink flowers to 8cm across in mid to late spring
A vigorous upright evergreen shrub, with glossy dark green, elliptic leaves with finely serrated edges. Large, rich red, full peony-form flowers are produced in mid spring

A vigorous evergreen shrub with an upright, open habit and small green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces bright pink buds that open to clusters of single, lightly scented flowers, white flushed with blossom pink, over a long period from late winter to early spring
An upright, evergreen shrub with glossy, dark green foliage with serrated edges. Strongly fragranced, semi-double, frilled pale salmon pink flowers appear from February through to April

A vigorous evergreen shrub with narrow, glossy dark green leaves, sometimes forked at the tips like a fish tail. Large, deep pink to carmine, semi-double flowers to 10cm across are produced in mid spring
An upright, evergreen shrub with dark green glossy foliage. Medium to large peony or anemone-shaped, semi-double blush pink flowers appear from winter through until the spring

A large evergreen shrub with an upright habit and glossy, ovate dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces small, single white flowers from pink buds all along the stems, over a long period from late winter into spring

An upright, bushy, deciduous shrub to around 1m high with ovate, toothed dark green leaves and reddish young stems. Produces large, semi-double flowers with white sepals and violet-blue petals in summer and early autumn

A mid-sized deciduous tree with a spreading habit, thorny branches and leathery, lobed and toothed green leaves. In late spring, loose clusters of small white flowers with purple anthers are produced, followed by red berries that mature to dark purple

A mat-forming perennial with small green leaves forming a low mound. Large, upward-facing cup-shaped violet-blue flowers with white centres appear in succession over a long flowering period, and are amazingly fragrant. Because this variety is sterile, flowering continues for many weeks with no deadheading required

A rhizomatous perennial with variegated hexagonal or star-shaped leaves, symmetrically marbled and spotted in a mix of dark, mid- and pale, silvery green. Narrow, hanging, dark red flowers appear in clusters under the leaves in early summer, followed by yellow fruit

A shrub up to 15cm high, forming a very small mound, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves 2-3cm long, and flowering stems up to 10cm long topped by spikes 1-2cm long of fragrant, pale dusky pink flowers around midsummer

A mid-sized deciduous shrub, to around 3m high, with elliptic, papery bright green leaves that are slightly serrated at the tips. Produces pendent white flowers, singly or in small clusters in late spring and early summer, followed by round, hairy seed pods

alternative_names: English lavender Pink-flowered Group|Lavandula angustifolia Rosea Group

description: An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 64cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, yellow flowers that have a cherry-red eye-zone and edge above a green throat to 9cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and cream flowers with a black-purple eye-zone and a green throat to 15cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, lavender coloured flowers with a green throat to 17cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and cream flowers that have a purple eye-zone and edge above a green throat to 17cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves, and fragrant lavender-purple coloured flowers that have a gold frilly edge above a green throat to 17cm across in summer

A deciduous herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 58cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, purple flowers with a blue-grey eyezone and a green throat to 18cm across in summer

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 64cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and fragrant, ruffled, golden-edged coral pink flowers with a yellow throat to 17cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant cherry-red flowers with white edges to around 13cm across, above a green throat in summer
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Semi-double flowers are red to dark red with a yellow eye and ruffle-edged petals
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are pink to pale orange with a darker pink eye, green throat and ruffled edges

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with green, lance-shaped foliage. Upright stems produce masses of large, outward facing, white, bell-shaped double flowers providing a long flowering display in summer. An evergreen, easy to grow plant but dislikes wet winters

A compact, hardy, deciduous shrub with strong, upright stems and long, aromatic toothed dark green foliage which is grey-silver underneath. Dark blue flowers appear from late summer through until the autumn

A hardy, vigorous, reliable French variety to around 25cm in height, with green foliage. White flowers in spring and summer develop into medium-sized, heart-shaped red fruits with firm flesh and a slightly acidic, woody, musky flavour. Shows good resistance to disease
A compact, upright perennial, to about 25cm, with small, narrowly-oval leaves and large, rich blue, upward-facing, trumpet-shaped flowers in late summer and early autumn
A winter or spring bulbous perennial to 40cm tall, producing at least two stout stems, each bearing 3-4 dark, velvety red, funnel-shaped flowers

A robust deciduous shrub with glossy dark green red-flushed leaves to 20cm long with good autumn tints and bearing large, distinctive flattened lacecap flowerheads of strongly red-margined white ray florets in mid and late summer that gradually turn pink
A deciduous shrub to around 200cm in height, with coarsley toothed dark green foliage and white mophead flower heads with a rose-red edge on the petals which appear in the summer

A vigorous rounded but upright deciduous shrub with deep purple-black stems, dark green leaves that colour well in autumn and flattened lacecap flowerheads bearing ultramarine ray florets with occasional white centres

An evergreen, mound-forming, woody-based perennial or sub-shrub to around 20cm high, with narrow, slightly glossy, yellow-green leaves. Dense, flattened clusters of small white flowers are produced from mid to late spring
A dwarf daffodil, to around 20cm high, with straplike, grey-green leaves. Flowers are small, with narrow yellow petals and a long, cylindrical yellow corona
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with bright lime green-yellow foliage with wavy edges. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in summer
A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy green leaves. Upward-facing, fragrant white flowers with a green eye are produced in early summer
A double daffodil to about 40cm, flowering in late spring. The blooms are pure white, with rows of petals getting narrower towards the centre, giving an almost spiky effect

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with lightly bronzed, dark green foliage. Flowers, produced from mid-summer until the first frosts, have a single row of lilac-pink outer petals, flushed with pale orange at the base and orange-red on the reverse, and a broad cushion of shorter inner petals in a mix of red and buff-yellow

alternative_names: Helenium autumnale red and gold hybrids|Helenium 'Rotgold' misapplied [1]|Helenium autumnale 'Helena Red and Yellow'|Helenium autumnale 'Rot-Gold Hybrids'

description: A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, to around 40cm high with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant dark purple flowers, topped with creamy white bracts, are produced over a long period from late spring to late summer

A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, to around 40cm high with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant, dark reddish-purple flowers, topped with pale lilac pink bracts with darker veining, are produced from mid to late summer

A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, to around 40cm high with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant dark purple flowers, topped with long violet bracts, are produced from mid to late summer
A bushy perennial grown as an annual vegetable for its edible tubers. A maincrop potato. Large, oval-shaped tubers have red skin and pale yellow flesh

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high, forming a mound of deeply lobed green leaves feathered with dark bronze. Leaves turn shades of reddish purple in autumn and winter. Tall clusters of flowers are held on slender stems above the foliage in spring, with pink buds opening to small, starry white flowers

alternative_names: lavender 'Bee Cool'|Lavandula stoechas viridis 'Madrid White'|Lavandula 'Madrid White'|Lavandula stoechas 'White Madrid'

description: A bulbous perennial to 50cm with green foliage and pale pink to apricot flowers, turning paler towards the edges, which open in the sunshine and appear in April

primary_name: Lavandula stoechas subsp. stoechas f. leucantha 'Snowman'
description: A compact, evergreen shrub to about 35cm with strongly aromatic, grey-green foliage and dense, terminal spikes of small, white flowers topped by short, white wings in late spring and summer

A compact, evergreen shrub to 20cm tall, with upright stems bearing small, lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Flowers are deep magenta, urn-shaped and held horizontally on upright stems from early summer into autumn
A large, perennial bulb with long, strap-shaped green leaves. Stems of large, creamy-pink flowers with some red veining near the centre and a green yellow eye, appear in the summer through to winter
A tender evergreen perennial, with a compact, trailing habit and lobed, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Produces clusters of semi-double, dark burgundy red flowers from late spring to early autumn

alternative_names: houseleek 'Pacific Blue Ice'|Sempervivum [Berry Blues] (Chick Charms Series)|Sempervivum 'Blue Ice'
description: A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing dense clumps of fleshy rosettes, with pointed, icy blue-green leaves edged with fine white hairs, the leaves flushed pale pink to pale purple in autumn and winter, the blue colour more intense in summer. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets
A dwarf bean with green leaves, pink-purple flowers and a heavy crop of purple fruit

A maincrop potato bred by the Scottish Crop Research Institute and introduced after extensive trials. It has a classic large, oval shape, with red blushes to the pale skin and creamy flesh, a velvety texture, and works well in all general kitchen use. It is resistant to diseases, doesn't bruise easily, with a consistant high yield regardless of weather conditions

A shrub, forming a woody framework with age, suited to being grown as an annual in the UK. White flowers in summer are followed by fruits that are variable in size and colour, generally resembling tomatoes. Fruits are often cooked and used in similar ways to tomatoes or aubergines

plant_range: S. France, Italy, Greece to Israel

description: A bulbous perennial with two strap-shaped, semi-erect, wavy to twisted, hairy basal leaves. Ten to twenty narrowly bell-shaped, deep blue-violet flowers are borne in spring in loose, lax to upright racemes up to 12cm long

An upright, repeat-flowering shrub rose to 1.25m tall with dark green foliage tinged with red when it first emerges in spring. Fragrant, shallow-cupped, pale pink double blooms up to 10cm in diameter are borne from summer into autumn

A rounded, upright shrub to about 1m tall and wide, the glossy foliage emerging dark bronzy-green then turning dark green as the season progresses. Dark red buds streaked orange open to fragrant, fully double, cup-shaped blooms of rich tangerine-orange, from summer to early autumn

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Flowers 10cm across, produced from mid-summer to the first frost, have white petals with purplish-red tips, spreading towards the base as the flowers age. As the outer petals open the edges roll under, creating a sunburst effect

A very hardy, compact, rounded evergreen shrub to around 150cm in height, with long, oval-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Funnel-shaped, wavy white flowers with burgundy-red speckled throats, appear from late May to early June

A compact evergreen shrub to around 80cm high, with elliptic, matt dark green leaves up to 8cm long. Produces clusters of up to 10 broadly funnel-shaped, pale yellow-orange flowers, tinted with soft pink and with dark red speckles on the upper petals, in late spring
A dwarf, compact, hardy evergreen shrub to around 60cm in height, with a neat habit and small, oval-shaped dark green leaves. Clusters of dark, violet-purple flowers appear from March to April

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Rosy-pink flowers, fading to white towards the centres, with yellow stamens, appear in the spring
A compact, neat, evergreen shrub to around 60cm in height, with dense, glossy dark green foliage. Masses of white, ruffled flowers with a hint of yellow-green appear in spring

A shrub rose reaching about 1.5m in height and bearing semi-double flowers through the summer until autumn that are strongly fragrant, elegantly tapered and velvety rich-pink in colour with exposed golden stamens. Fruits (hips) are not usually produced
A very floriferous cultivar of uniform growth, to 40cm, with bright single vivid reddish-orange flowers on red stems and glossy green foliage

primary_name: Eucomis pallidiflora subsp. pole-evansii (N.E. Br.) Reyneke ex J.C. Manning
description: A giant bulbous perennial with strap-shaped leaves, up to 1m long, and a spire of loosely-packed, greenish-white flowers, topped with a cluster of leafy bracts, that can reach 2m tall in late summer and early autumn

primary_name: Tropaeolum majus 'Tip Top Scarlet' (Tip Top Alaska Series)
description: A compact, bushy, trailing annual to around 30cm tall with rounded green leaves, mottled with cream. Masses of large, funnel-shaped scarlet-red flowers are produced freely from June through to September

primary_name: Tropaeolum majus 'Tutti Frutti Mixed' (Tip Top Alaska Series)
description: A bushy, sprawling annual to about 30cm in height, with mid-green, circular leaves splashed and marbled with creamy-white. Single, trumpet-shaped flowers in pale and mid-yellow, pale and mid-orange and red appear from early summer to early autumn

A vigorous, trailing and spreading floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding, seasonal ground cover or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces gramophone-trumpet-shaped, pink-purple flowers around 7 cm across. Blooms from late spring well into autumn if well fed and watered. Its cascading habit means it trails or spreads around 40 to 50 cm so is ideal for large hanging baskets and big balcony containers, and also as ground cover in sunny, warm, well-drained locations.

A vigorous, trailing or gently spreading floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding, or seasonal ground cover. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces gramophone-trumpet-shaped, deepest dark purple flowers around 6 or 7 cm across. Blooms from late spring well into autumn if well fed and watered. Its rambling habit means it can trail and spread well, so good for big hanging baskets, in balcony containers and as colourful ground cover in warm, sunny, well-drained places.

A very compact, rhizomatous alpine perennial to around only 5cm in height, forming a cushion of small, thin, almost pine-needle shaped dark green foliage. Clusters of crimson-red to pale purple, rarely white flowers appear on the tips of the stems from late summer well into autumn
An evergreen, bushy shrub to around 1m tall with small, oval to elliptic, aromatic leaves. Red flowers are borne on dark red stems from late spring to early autumn
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial growing from slender rhizomes, with deeply divided dark green leaves and bright yellow, semi-double flowers appearing in spring
An erect, strong-growing, free-flowering herbaceous perennial, up to 1.7m high, with an equal balance between lobed green leaves and tapering spikes of brown-eyed, mid-blue flowers in midsummer
A bulbous perennial, to around 120cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, pink double flowers with a yellow centre and very fragrant blooms appear in the summe

An evergreen perennial to about 70cm, grown under glass for cutting, and flowering sporadically throughout the year. Foliage is grey-green, relatively broad, and curled; double flowers are white with pink streaks, and strongly scented
A compact, tuberous perennial to about 70cm with dark green, divided foliage. Double, scarlet flowers with narrow, slightly twisted petals are produced from early summer until the first frost
A compact, bushy dahlia to 65cm. The pink, fully double flowers have abundant, interestingly twisted florets, darker coloured on the backs. Flowers consistently for a long season

alternative_names: Persian cyclamen Metis Series|Cyclamen persicum Metis Series, mixed|Cyclamen persicum 'Metis Mixed'
description: A collection of compact, half-hardy tuberous perennials with dark green, heart shaped leaves with silver markings. Flowers are produced in winter and early spring, in a range of colours from white to deep magenta pink

An evergreen, sparingly-branched shrub, to 1.5m in height, with serrated, oval, dark green leaves. Flowers are foxglove-like with a flattened appearance, reddish-orange or apricot in colour and held on upright spikes to 30cm in length

alternative_names: Isabel's foxglove|Callianassa isabelliana|Digitalis canariensis var. isabelliana|Isoplexis isabelliana
description: A half-hardy evergreen shrub to 1.2m high, with upright stems and broadly ovate, serrated dark green leaves. Spikes of rich orange flowers, with long hoods forming a beak-like shape, are produced from the tips of the stems in summer
A tender evergreen shrub, up to 1.8m high, with toothed, ovate to ovate-oblong leaves and racemes up to 13cm long of yellow flowers, netted inside with tawny-brown, in summer

Fast-growing, deciduous tree about 20m tall, with shoots, leaf stalks and flower stalks conspicuously downy. Dark green leaves to 45cm long, composed of up to 7 leaflets are downy beneath, and often turn wine-purple in autumn. Panicles of sweetly-scented creamy petalless flowers in mid-spring are followed by brownish-green winged fruits. Winter buds are a conspicuous grey
A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial with large, red leaves with a wide margin that darkens from deep green to black as the leaf matures, the margin irregularly spotted with red

A biennial usually grown as an annual, with large, shiny, bright green, divided foliage and pale green to white leaf-stems eaten as celery. It is a vigorous cultivar producing good crops of smooth, thick, fleshy stems that are sweet and crunchy
A strong and high-yielding green celery producing tightly-bunched stalks. Shows good disease tolerance

A striking late Summer-Autumn cauliflower variety that produces dense, rich, deep purple curds which become darker the more they are exposed to sunlight. It has an excellent flavour and looks superb in the kitchen garden as well on the plate. Harvest between August and October

A biennial, normally grown as an annual for its swollen, round, edible, dark red root. Foliage is dark green with dark red stems and veins, and is also edible. A robust and reliable beetroot cultivar, suitable for baby beets or growing on to maturity producing smooth-skinned roots to 8cm diameter which store well
A beetroot variety producing sweet, red cylindrical roots that stand proud of the soil. The leaf stalks are ruby red and the leaves are pink-veined. Easy to grow and prepare

An evergreen shrub to about 1.2m high, with elliptic, dark green leaves with a distinctive deep red colouring on the undersides. New growth is flushed bronze. Produces rounded clusters of broadly funnel-shaped, pale pink flowers with rose pink edges, in mid to late spring
A dwarf, compact, hardy evergreen shrub to around 80cm in height, with oval-shaped dark green leaves. Funnel-shaped, dark purple-pink flowers appear from April to May

An evergreen shrub to about 1.2m high. Leaves are elliptic, with a variegated margin that is reddish brown when young, fading to yellow when fully developed. Flowers are red with wavy edges, and produced in clusters of 6-8 in mid to late spring

A tender, rare evergreen shrub to around 4m in height with large, lush green elliptic leaves and pendent panicles of slender-tubed waxy bright red and white flowers in late summer to autumn, followed by edible red fruits, with a flavour similar to kiwi fruit but not as sweet. Grow in a conservatory or greenhouse, providing a tropical feel

A herbaceous perennial with branched stems bearing very large, to 12cm diameter, scented flowers with lemon-yellow petals and orange cones from mid-summer to early autumn; the petals are variously-fluted

A highly attractive, upright, perennial coneflower growing to 1m tall and producing bright orange blooms with a prominent central orange-brown cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators. It looks best when planted in drifts in the border

A deciduous small tree or large bush with mid green oval leaves. Rich burgundy pink, goblet shaped flowers with a paler interior on opening. Flowers can be damaged by late frosts so plant in a sheltered position, in neutral to slightly acid, moist but well-drained soil

Broad, spreading, open tree about 8-10m tall, with mid-green leaves. Fragrant, goblet shaped flowers to 20cm across, appearing with the leaves in mid-spring, are green in bud opening to greenish-yellow, becoming chartreuse yellow then fading to creamy white with age

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 45cm high, with lobed, mid green leaves heavily marked with dark bronze. Flowers over a long period from late spring, with flowers opening near white, and blushing pale pink as they mature

alternative_names: Orobanche cruenta|Orobanche ulicis|Orobanche cruenta var. citrina

description: A scrambling or climbing annual, reaching between 15 to 40cm in height. It has a branching habit and finely divided, blueish-green leaves, giving a delicate, feathery appearance with dull white flowers with purple tips appearing from May to October
A cyclamineus daffodil, 10-15cm high, with green leaves and deep yellow flowers, about 6cm long, with reflexed perianth segments and cylindrical coronas, in early spring

A clump-forming bulbous perennial to around 15cm high, with green, strap-shaped leaves. The elegant flowers are lightly fragranced and upward facing, with slightly swept-back creamy-white petals and a long, creamy yellow cup which turns paler over time. Appears in late winter to early spring and ideal for short, grassy areas or under shrubs and trees
A miniature daffodil producing stems to 15cm bearing 3-5 flowers in mid-spring; flowers are lightly scented with soft yellow cups and swept back petals

An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 80cm in height when in flower with green, linear grass-like leaves and spikes of pale green buds which open to tubular, pale yellow flowers in August to September

Double Click Series Mixed are erect, bushy, half-hardy annuals with finely-divided, feathery foliage and semi-double to double flowers, with ruffled petals in shades of rosy-red, pink or white, borne on stems to1.2m high
A half-hardy perennial to 90cm in height, with divided green leaves and sprays of flowers, 7cm in width, with warm yellowy orange florets, incurved at the centres and reflexed at the edges
A hardy evergreen shrub approximately 30cm tall with a spread to 40cm. It has dark green foliage and double, shell pink flowers on short spikes in summer through to autumn.

A hardy evergreen shrub with a spreading, open habit approximately 35cm tall with an equal spread. It has dark green foliage and tapering stems of double silver rose flowers in summer through to autumn.
A hardy evergreen shrub with a compact, bushy habit with green foliage and spires of pink flowers in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub with an erect, bushy growing habit with dark green foliage. Classified as a bud-bloomer, purple buds appear in summer and autumn.
A compact, spreading, evergreen shrub to 45cm tall and 60cm wide with dark green foliage and reddish-pink flowers borne from winter into spring
A bulbous perennial with leafy stems to around 100cm topped in mid- to late summer with large, scented, outward-facing, bowl-shaped flowers in very deep red with a narrow, white, ruffled edge
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with mid-green, wrinkled, oval leaves and tall spikes of sof-pink lipped flowers in summer.
A vigorous and free-flowering spray chrysanthemum. It reaches around 80cm in height. The reflexed sprays are a deep, clean yellow that retain colour well with aging

A compact, clump-forming perennial to about 25cm high, forming a mound of lobed leaves that emerge purple with a silver sheen, becoming more metallic as the leaves mature. Loose, upright sprays of red flowers are held on slender, dark red stems above the foliage from late spring into summer

A mound-forming perennial spreading to 40cm with large, lobed leaves of varying colours. Leaf colours range from golden-yellow to yellow-brown flushed with pink and green and overlaid with a silvery sheen. In summer, sprays of small pink and yellow flowers are borne above the foliage on dark-pink stems
A deciduous shrub about 1.5m tall if left unpruned. It has green lobed leaves and pale green flowers which develop into strings of light red berries in late July

A deservedly popular rose about 1.2m in height, with healthy dark green leaves, and bearing very fragrant, fully double pale peachy-apricot blooms with flushes of pale pink, flowering from early summer to autumn
An upright, bulbous perennial with strap-like dark grey-green leaves. Strongly scented bell-shaped purple-black flowers appear on strong stems in mid-spring

A large bushy shrub, or small tree, up to 3m high with shoots that are green when young, becoming greenish-brown with age; the large, glossy, elliptic, almost flat leaves, up to 5.5cm long, are lime-green with dark green margins and pale midribs. Scented, dark brown-maroon flowers appear in late spring or early summer

alternative_names: tawhiwhi 'Margaret Turnbull'|Pittosporum 'Margaret Turnbull'|Pittosporum lineare 'Margaret Turnbull'|Pittosporum tenuifolium 'John Flanagan'
description: A bushy, compact, evergreen shrub to about 1.8m with dark brown stems. The shiny, oval foliage is bright yellow-green with mid-green, wavy margins when young, ageing to mid-green with dark green margins. Produces small, deep red, scented flowers in spring

A deciduous shrub, to around 3m high, with an upright to spreading habit and oval to heart-shaped, slightly glossy green leaves. Upright clusters of fragrant, violet-blue flowers are produced in late spring and early summer
An early-maturing, compact pea to about 60cm tall producing pods containing up to eight peas; suitable for eating fresh or freezing

An early-flowering daffodil with slightly grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are almost 6cm across, fragrant, and three or more to a stem, with broad white outer petals and a small, bowl-shaped orange cup with a frilled rim
A hoop petticoat cultivar reaching 20cm in height. It's a strong grower, bearing scented, yellow flowers in late winter and early spring

A clump-forming tazetta daffodil with slightly grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are pure white, to 3.5cm across, with broad outer petals and a small, bowl-shaped corona. Produces many flowers to a stem
A tall, strong,late-flowering variety with large, green inner petals.

A large, slow growing, deciduous tree reaching up to 8m in height with ovate mid-green leaves. The large, showy, tulip shaped flowers, produced in spring, are deeper pink on the outside of the petals fading to pale pink inside.
A spreading, deciduous tree or large shrub reaching approximately 8m in height with ovate mid-green leaves. The globe shaped flowers are purple to mid-pink, produced in early to mid spring.
A bushy, compact, deciduous tree reaching up to 5m in height with ovate mid-green leaves. The deep, reddish purple, goblet shaped flowers are produced in spring, starting before the leaves.

A deciduous shrub to 75cm tall with deeply-divided, dark green leaves. Mildly-fragrant, single flowers open yellow-orange with red flares at the base of each petal and a ring of golden-yellow stamens before fading to a creamy-pale yellow with age

A bushy perennial, to around 70cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves that are flushed red on opening. In late spring and early summer, fragrant semi-double to double flowers open in soft shades of orange, yellow and red, paling slightly in colour as the flowers mature

An intersectional or Itoh peony and an upright and compact herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage green in summer, tinged bronzy-red in spring and autumn. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped brigh crimson-red flowers with a centre of yellow stamens appear in late spring and early summer, with a particularly long flowering period.

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 75cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves that are tinted red in spring and autumn. In late spring and early summer produces large, single or semi-double bright yellow flowers

A clump-forming, compact, deciduous perennial, with lance-shaped, dark green leaves with a paler mid-vein, fading to yellow orange and gold in the autumn. In late spring and early summer, terminal panicles of starry-shaped, periwinkle blue flowers appear

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 75cm high, with strong stems and divided dark green leaves. In early summer produces large, semi-double, raspberry pink flowers fading to pale pink and cream

A large, and fast growing tree, to a height of 15m, with large, oval, long serrated vibrant green leaves and a profusion of yellow catkins. These are up to 10cm in length and are borne from winter to spring
An evergreen tree reaching around 15m, the leaves are long and narrow in shape, shiny green on top and downy white beneath. The acorns become glossy red-brown in a cup with rings of short bristles
An attractive, mat forming, evergreen sub-shrub with upright stems bearing, small, ovate to lance-shaped, aromatic, mid-green leaves and dense clusters of pink flowers in summer

primary_name: Ilex perado subsp. platyphylla var. platyphylla

description: A small evergreen tree to about 8m tall, from the temperate forests of central Chile. Very rare in cultivation with attractive reddish-brown, peeling bark and aromatic, leathery, dark green leaves to 3cm long, deep red as they emerge. Produces large, fragrant, white myrtle-like flowers with long stamens, during early to midsummer followed by red fruit

An evergreen tree or erect shrub reaching about 4m (13ft) in cultivation (20m or 65ft in the wild), with smooth, whitish or light reddish-brown bark. It has stiff, leathery, dark green ovate leaves that are strongly aromatic. Bears cream-coloured flowers profusely in late summer.

primary_name: Myosotis from Eyre Mountains, New Zealand

description: An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 70cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching and strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, white flowers from mid-summer to autumn.

alternative_names: Notocactus magnificus var. warasii|Eriocactus warasii|Notocactus warasii
Erman's birch 'Mount Zao'|Betula ermanii 'Mount Zao Purple'|Betula ermanii 'Zao Purple'
description: A large elegant but strong growing tree to a height of 10m or more eventually, with glossy green, leaves turning yellow in autumn before falling. Its main feature is its unusually coloured bark - brown purple with copper-orange markings and creamy tones emphasising the lenticels
A dual purpose apple, with large, ribbed green fruits ripening to yellow, with a red flush and spots of russet. Flesh is white with a green tint, and sweet with some acidity
A cactus with usually solitary, globose to cylindrical stems to 15cm tall, bearing bristly yellow spines and funnel-shaped sulphur-yellow flowers to 5cm across in summer

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high, with lobed, mid green leaves tinted with dark reddish bronze. Vivid pink flowers, with narrow, spreading petals marked with dark pink veins, are produced over a long period from late spring

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, up to 50cm high, with an upright habit and lobed, mid green leaves. Soft pink flowers, with narrow petals marked with darker pink veins, are produced over a long period from late spring

A clump-forming evergreen perennial with five-lobed leaves and strap-shaped flowers, mauve pink at the tip, with deeper veins, and white at the base, with five or 10 very narrow petals flowering from late spring

A vigorous, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage with a hint of red and slight bronze edge. Masses of buds open to rich, velvety dark red flowers with a yellow eye and appear from March to May

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial with glossy, dark green leaves divided into two or three, ovate or diamond-shaped, toothed, sometimes lobed leaflets. Racemes of nodding white flowers bloom in mid- to late summer.

A rhizomatous perennial, with thick, creeping rhizomes and upright stems, usually to around 40cm high but can reach almost 1m in ideal conditions. Leaves are asymmetric, slightly glossy and deep green. Loose clusters of pink flowers are produced from summer to early autumn

A small to medium-sized spiny leaved evergreen shrub with glossy green elliptical leaves up to 5cm long that are white to silvery white or pale green underneath. Clusters of approximately 10-25 orange-yellow flowers erupt from tight red-orange buds, and these develop into black roundish fruits in autumn

A striking half-hardy gently spreading or mounding short-lived perennial grown mostly as an annual and used in seasonal summer displays. Bright orange starry blooms have a bold splash of yellow-gold at the base of each petal. The flowers are borne in profusion, covering the feathery mid-green to dark green foliage throughout summer and into early autumn. This modern cultivar is vigorous but stays compact if pinched out well when young.

A tall, clump-forming, rhizomatous perennial to 1.8m with glossy, lance-shaped, dark green leaves. In late spring and early summer produces small clusters of tubular, purplish- or brownish-red, or white, flowers with protruding style and stamens, followed by red-black berries

alternative_names: Tricyrtis formosana aff. f. glandosa 'Blu-Shing Toad'
heather 'Leonie'|Calluna vulgaris [Beauty Ladies Leonie] (Beauty Ladies Series)
description: A compact, hardy evergreen shrub to around 50cm in height, with mid-green, needle-like foliage and reddish-pink flowers which appear from August through to November. The flower buds don't fully open so the colour fades slowly

A hardy, evergreen shrub to around 30cm in height, with dark bronze-green and white variegated foliage which is particularly vibrant in early summer. Magenta-pink flowers appear from summer to autumn. A true variegated heather and a sport of C. 'Kramer's Rote'

primary_name: Prunus domestica 'Grove's Late Victoria' early sport (D)

description: Bushy rose to about 90cm tall, with glossy dark green foliage and bearing clusters of large, very fragrant, fully-double lilac to magenta-pink blooms throughout summer and autumn
a floribunda rose of upright habit reaching about 1.2m in height. Flowers are borne in clusters from summer through to autumn. These are a soft, rather old-fashioned, shade of pink
An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing fragrant, reflexed, dark pink petals surrounding a unique red central cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A cultivar related to G. sanguineum, a low-growing bushy, spreading perennial to 20cm tall, with semi-procumbent stems bearing deeply divided dark green leaves. The upward-facing flowers are soft lilac-pink or mauve, each petal with a distinctive white edge, and borne during a long flowering season

Deciduous, woody-based, herbaceous (non-climbing) clematis about 1m tall, with dark green leaves divided into leaflets, and fragrant, nodding, tubular dark blue flowers to 2cm across, recurved at the tips, with prominent pale yellow stamens, flowering early summer to early autumn

Large, vigorous, deciduous climber about 8m tall, with mid to dark green leaves and scented. semi-double or single, pale primrose-yellow flowers to about 6cm across, with creamy-yellow stamens, flowering from mid to late spring

An erect, robust, evergreen shrub to 1m tall and 1.65m across. The foliage is yellow-green with a pale midrib, and often produces vivid red tones in autumn and winter. Honey-scented, yellow-green flowers are produced from late spring to late summer, turning pale brown as they age, followed by yellow-green, berry-like fruit
A rhizomatous perennial, to 1m high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have rich violet standards, velvety dark purple falls, and a bright orange beard. Mid season

A bushy sub-shrub to about 90cm tall, evergreen in mild locations, with small, aromatic leaves. Vivid, pinkish-red flowers in short spikes are borne from summer to late autumn. This plant was shortlisted for the Plant Heritage Threatened Plant of the Year 2025
A frost-tender fern that forms a slender trunk as it matures and produces stiff, upright to arching fronds up to 90cm tall and wide

A compact, clump-forming, slow-growing evergreen fern with a trailing habit and masses of dark green, dense, sword-shaped, tripinnate fronds which are ruffled around the edges. A good air-purifying plant and ideal for terrariums and bottle gardens

alternative_names: blue eryngo 'Jade Frost'|Eryngium × tripartitum 'Jade Frost'|Eryngium 'Jade Frost'|Eryngium tripartitum 'Jade Frost'
description: A more compact variety of Sea Holly. It's green leaves have creamy edges to them and thistle-like flowers which turn from white to indigo are produced from July to August

Rex-cultorum begonia, 40-60cm high, with a compact habit, dark red stems and leaf stalks, obliquely heart-shaped leaves which are dark red below, and dark green above but so heavily spotted with white that they appear silver, and small pink flowers

A bushy annual to around 60cm tall with lance-shaped leaves and white flowers that are followed by conical fruits to 10cm long that ripen from yellow through orange to red producing medium to hot chilli peppers
A compact, bushy, annual plant bearing many white summer flowers followed by green fruits up to 7cm long that ripen to brght red, medium to hot chilli peppers
A perpetual-flowering perennial producing double pink flowers with petals edged a paler pink to white

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial, to around 75cm high, with an upright habit and lobed, bronze and green leaves that are creamy yellow in the centre when young. Tall, branching stems bear small purple flowers, with reflexed petals and white centres, in late spring to early summer
An annual climber, to around 1.8m high, with curling tendrils and pairs of green leaves. Scented flowers are produced in summer, with deep pink upper petals and white wings edged with purple

A bushy, upright rose 1-1.2m in height, with healthy, glossy, dark green leaves, and bearing masses of strongly fragrant, fully double, rich pink blooms, almost continuously in flower from early summer to autumn

alternative_names: fan-leaved water crowfoot|egyllt cylchol-ddail|Ranunculus divaricatus misapplied

description: A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of red flowers, edged with ivory, and a mid green-yellow throat

An evergreen perennial to about 1m, with strap-shaped, glossy leaves, purple at the base. Large rounded umbels of very pale blue flower are produced on strong, upright stems from mid-summer to early autumn
A compact perennial, to 25cm tall, with narrow, strap-like leaves and erect stems bearing a rounded cluster of funnel-shaped, white flowers in late summer
A vigorous, annual climber, up to around 1.8m high, with curling tendrils and pairs of green leaves. Bright, scarlet-red flowers with an old-fashioned fragrance are produced in summer to early autumn
A compact, bushy perennial to about 30cm tall usually grown as an annual bedding plan. Fragrant flowers are purple and white with yellow eyes and borne from late spring into early autumn

A bushy, evergreen shrub about 2m tall, with finely toothed, glossy, dark green leaves to 5cm long. Open panicles of deep blue flowers to 8cm long appear over a long period from late spring to early summer

alternative_names: hot water plant 'Tetra Wine Red Charm'

description: Deciduous climber to about 2.5m tall, with mid-green leaves and bearing large pale lilac flowers to 18cm across, with reddish-purple central bars and reddish-purple stamens, flowering from late spring to early summer and late summer to autumn

Compact, deciduous climber about 2m tall, with mid-green leaves and pale pink flowers to 14cm across with a red-purple central bar and crimped, wavy petal margins, flowering from early to mid summer then late summer to autumn
A deciduous climber with bright, golden-green foliage. Single, nodding lavender-blue flowers appear in spring to early summer

A striking, deciduous Japanese maple, cultivated from the original tree at Westonbirt Arboretum, reaching about 4m in height. Long, pointed 5 to 7-lobed rich green leaves emerge in spring with red tints, turning to brilliant shades of red and crimson in autumn

Deciduous spreading tree about 4m tall, with palmate 4-6 lobed leaves that have rich green spring and summer colour followed by a display in glowing shades of orange, flushed red and gold in autumn. Inconspicuous hanging clusters of small, purple-red flowers in spring are followed by red-flushed, winged fruits

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit up to 75cm tall when in flower. It has healthy, mid-green, blade-like leaves and strong, arching flower stems that bear orange and salmon-pink tubular flowers, with apricot throats, over a long period from mid to late summer
A clump-forming perennial growing up to 90cm tall with erect, green leaves. This cultivar flowers over a long period from summer into autumn, producing orange-peach coloured flowers on arching stems

A vigorous, clump-forming perennial, to 1m tall, with upright, narrow leaves and arching flower stems. The upward-facing orange flowers, with darker orange centres, are borne from late summer into autumn

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial, to around 70cm high, with an upright habit and lobed green leaves lightly marked with bronze. Tall, branching stems bear masses of small, very dark reddish purple flowers in late spring and early summer

A reasonably compact, deciduous, herbaceous perennial, producing deeply lobed, bright green leaves marbled in light green, on stems to 70cm (28in) high. Single slightly reflexed smokey purple flowers appear in spring. While best in sun to partial shade, it is also able to tolerate full shade, making it useful for using in the shady border

Upright, evergreen shrub with lance-shaped, deeply serrated, silver-grey leaves and clusters of very fragrant small yellow flowers in summer. The scent is clove like. Only hardy in milder areas.

primary_name: Lonicera sempervirens Eco flowers all summer

alternative_names: fish bone spurge|fish bone cactus|fish bone thistle|Euphorbia thi

description: A deciduous tree to 12m tall, with rich pink flowers to 20cm across, in spring, the tepals paler to white within
A miniature, quick-growing, clump-forming deciduous perennial with small, green-yellow foliage. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 30cm high, with ovate, rich green leaves with a slight satiny sheen and strongly rippled edges. Produces loose clusters of tubular purple flowers on tall, upright stems in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 60cm high, with an upright, arching habit and large, heart-shaped lime green leaves with creamy white margins. Leaves have lightly rippled edges and a puckered texture. Produces loose clusters of pale lavender flowers on upright stems in summer
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 25cm high, with narrowly ovate, tapered, matt blue-green leaves. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

An upright herbaceous perennial 1.2m high with divided green leaves and strong stems, especially suitable for cutting, of lavender-blue flowers with white centres in early summer; delphiniums may be visited by bumblebees, especially long-tongued bumblebees

alternative_names: Oxalis hedysaroides 'Rubra' misapplied [1]|Oxalis 'Burgundy'|Oxalis spiralis subsp. vulcanicola 'Burgundy'
