description: This plant is listed on Schedule 9 of the UK Wildlife & Countryside Act as an invasive, non-native species and is banned from sale. See cultivation notes for further details

A small tree or shrub to 8m tall with elliptic , mid- to dark green leaves that turn shades of red and yellow in autumn. Inconspicuous, greenish-yellow flowers in thin catkins are followed by three-lobed, hanging seed capsules

alternative_names: Japan wood oil plant|tung oil plant|Aleurites cordata
China wood oil plant|tung nut|Aleurites fordii

primary_name: Dahlia [Happy Single Kiss] ('HS Kiss') (Happy Single Series) (Sin)
description: A fairly short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 60cm, with dark bronze foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers are pale salmon pink, with a narrow, red central ring and a dark brown disc opening to dark yellow

A dwarf, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing a profusion of mildly fragrant, bright pink blooms from early to late Summer. Flowers have a large, prominent, central copper-orange cone surrounded by flat pink ray florets, held on well branched and sturdy stems. Extremely attractive to pollinators and excellent as a cut flower

A compact, hardy, clump-forming, evergreen herbaceous perennial with deeply-lobed dark green foliage. Single, cup-shaped purple-pink flowers with darker veining and eye and a satin sheen, appear over a long period from May through to October
A vigorous, all male asparagus variety producing heavy yields of purple tipped, green spears between April and June. Bred in Canada, it is particularly cold tolerant and suitable for most soil types

A high yielding, colourful variety producing stringless, dark-green purple spears between April and June. The spears are more tender and sweeter than many other green varieties. Steam or eat raw as colour can be lost when cooked

alternative_names: cat tails euphorbia|Alluaud's euphorbia|Madagascan fire plant
flowering spurge|garden spurge|purging root|snake milk|tramp's spurge|white purslane|wild hippo|wild spurge|Euphorbia marilandica

description: A large shrub or with delicate, mimosa-like, green bipinnate leaves which turn to purple-red in the autumn, and a spreading, umbrella habit. Fluffy bright red flower-heads, with prominent stamens, open in summer. An exotic-looking plant which is ideal for smaller gardens where space is limited, or in pots and containers

A vigorous, evergreen shrub of rounded habit, up to 2m (6½ft) high, having long, narrow, bright green leaves, with toothed margins. Plants can be either male or female. The males produce dark purple flowers in spring, with four yellow stamens, while the females produce small, stamenless, dark purple flowers in spring, followed by clusters of bright red, oval berries in autumn, if a male aucuba is flowering nearby to fertilise the flowers.
An everbearing variety producing very heavy yields of large, attractive, sweet, bright red fruits that have a juicy texture throughout summer and early autumn
An everbearing variety producing high yields of sweet and juicy red fruits from early summer through to late autumn
A shrub to 3m tall with upright stems bearing double, purplish-pink flowers from late summer into autumn

A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant, dark purple flowers, topped with frilly, lilac-pink bracts, are borne on short stems from late spring through to late summer

alternative_names: French lavender [Coco Deep Pink]|Lavandula stoechas 'Coco Dark Pink'
description: A compact, aromatic evergreen shrub with linear silvery-grey green leaves. In late spring and midsummer produces abundant slender, upright stems with oval spikes of densely clustered rosy-purple flowers topped with pink bracts

primary_name: Lavandula stoechas [Coco Deep White on Blue] (Coco Series)
alternative_names: French lavender [Coco Deep White on Blue]

description: An evergreen perennial to 1m, forming a clump of arching, sword-shaped, bright pink leaves with green margins. Makes an eye-catching accent plant and is good in a container

An upright, fast-growing shrub with prickly canes and oval-shaped, toothed and wrinkly dark green leaves. Small white flowers appear in late spring to early summer, followed by large and glossy bright red fruit in the late summer to early autumn

A small, spreading tree to 10m tall and wide with leaves made up of 21-33 narrowly oblong, glossy green to dark green leaflets that are downy beneath and turn attractive shades of orange, red and purple in the autumn. Flattened heads of small white flowers borne in spring are followed by rounded red fruits

A vigorous deciduous tree, with channelled bark and brittle, glossy brown shoots. Leaves are lance-shaped, coarsely serrated, and glossy deep green. Slender catkins are produced in early spring, and male catkins are often distinctively forked at the tips

A robust, compact, free-branching evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy deep green, wavy-edged leathery, oblong-elliptic leaves which are a rich rusty-brown on the undersides Plentiful, highly fragrant, large, cup-shaped creamy-white flowers are produced from summer to autumn

Low-growing, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Creamy peach-pink flowers with an orange flush are held on stems above the foliage from spring to early summer

A rare, evergreen flowering shrub endemic to sub-alpine parts of Australia growing to around 30cm in height with elliptic, glossy dark green foliage on woody stems. Dense spikes of maroon-red flowers, greenish towards the base, are produced in summer and followed by round, blue-purple berries favoured as a food source by birds and small mammals. Prefers a woodland setting
A tuberous perennial to 30cm, more compact than the species and with a stronger chocolate scent. Foliage is narrow, rather bluish green, and the bowl-shaped, late-summer flowers are dark brownish-red

An upright biennial bearing ovate to heart-shaped, toothed, dark grey-green leaves and violet-blue flowers in late spring and early summer, followed by flat, green seed pods. When ripe, the outer covers peel away to expose silvery, paper-like discs.

A bushy, upright annual to about 70cm with very finely divided foliage.In spring or summer, depending on sowing date, produces white, single flowerswith a central, deep purple boss, followed by inflated seed pods that start pale green and turn dark purple

A reliable, hybrid, large white grape, suitable for growing outdoors, with deciduous, lobed green leaves, tiny green flowers in summer, producing heavy crops of disease-resistant, large bunches of fruit in autumn, suited to wine making

Multi-stemmed, evergreen shrubby tree about 6m tall, restricted to a small area near Sydney and the Blue Mountains area of New South Wales. Smooth bark with white, cream or green patches is shed in long thin strips. Glossy green juvenile broadly lance-shaped leaves, and adult leaves linear to slender, aromatic, lance-shaped, often held vertically. White or cream flowers in clusters of 7 flowers, between summer and autumn are followed by barrel or urn-shaped woody fruit

alternative_names: paulownia [Fast Blue]|Paulownia fortunei 'Minfast'|Paulownia fortunei 'Fast Blue'|Paulownia tomentosa 'Fast Blue'
description: A fast-growing tree with a pyramidal habit reaching to 8m tall. Large, ovate to heart-shaped leaves have hairy undersides and are up to 20cm across. Upright panicles of fragrant, funnel-shaped flowers are borne in spring and are lilac-blue outside and creamy-white inside with a yellow throat

Bushy, spreading shrub rose, about 1m or more in height, with glossy mid-green foliage, and producing clusters of large, cupped, very full-petalled delicate carmine-pink blooms to 12.5cm across with a strong, old rose, fruity fragrance. Repeat-flowering through summer into autumn
Bushy shrub rose about 1.2m tall, with glossy dark green leaves, and lightly scented, very full-petalled, cupped and quartered glowing apricot-pink blooms, repeat-flowering through summer to autumn

A vigorous deciduous shrub, to around 3m high, with a spreading habit and elliptic to oval, slightly glossy green leaves that often tint purple in autumn. Hanging clusters of small, scented, tubular white flowers are produced in summer, followed by round, blue-black berries

A large, tender perennial bulb grown as a houseplant, with long, strap-shaped green leaves. Clusters of large, lily-like white flowers, touched with green in the throat, are produced on upright stems in winter or early spring

alternative_names: meadow saffron 'Giant'|Colchicum speciosum 'Leith Vale Seedling'|Colchicum 'The Giant'
description: A robust cormous perennial 20cm high with semi-erect, narrowly ovate leaves, 18-25cm long, from winter to spring, and a succession of up to 5 somewhat goblet-shaped flowers, up to 8cm long, with lightly tessellated tepals which are purple-violet with white bases, in autumn; colchicums are a useful late-season source of pollen for honeybees
An upright, clump-forming, semi-evergreen to evergreen fern with erect to arching, glossy, triangular, mid- to dark green fronds divided into pointed, lance-shaped, deeply lobed leaflets or pinnae.

A vigorous, evergreen fern forming clumps up to 60cm high and 120cm wide. The fronds are slightly arching, shiny green and twice-divided. This sterile hybrid produces one, or occasionally more, bulbils at the frond tips

alternative_names: white-striped Cretan brake|Pteris albolineata|Pteris cretica var. albolineata
description: An evergreen fern with erect or arching fronds to 45cm in length, pinnately divided into 3-5 pairs of linear pinnae, each with a broad central creamy-white stripe

primary_name: Acer sterculiaceum subsp. franchetii f. megalocarpum
alternative_names: Acer franchetii f. megalocarpum|Acer franchetii var. megalocarpa

primary_name: Alcea rosea Chater's Double Group purple-flowered (d)
description: An upright biennial or short-lived perennial, to just over 2m high, with rounded, lobed, slightly hairy green leaves. Tall spikes of fully double, deep pinkish purple flowers are produced in summer

primary_name: Alcea rosea Chater's Double Group scarlet-flowered (d)
description: A vigorous short-lived perennial with lobed rounded leaves and long, erect pyramids of open funnel-shaped large scarlet red double flowers in summer.

primary_name: Petrocosmea rosettifolia C.Y. Wu ex H.W.L.

description: An alpine herbaceous perennial up to 8cm high with an almost flat rosette of spoon-shaped succulent green leaves covered in silky silvery hairs and with upturned margins, and blueish-lavender flowers, about 1.5cm across; they usually have one flower per stem, the upper two petals are fused into a shorter two-lobed hood, and there is a darker purple spot at the base of the tube

A compact, slow-growing evergreen alpine perennial to around 10cm in height, forming a dense cushion of rosette-forming, silvery dark green foliage. Masses of small pale, primrose-yellow flowers with greenish-yellow centres appear in spring
A compact, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Magenta-pink, ball-shaped flowers appear from summer until the first frosts
A large, vigorous deciduous shrub to around 150cm in height with a rounded habit and dark green foliage. White lacecap flowers appear during the summer
A bushy, repeat-flowering rose to about 1m in height, with healthy glossy dark green leaves, the fully double, quartered blooms are deep pink, very fragrant, and appear from summer into autumn
A species of deciduous shrub to around 90cm with variegated green and white foliage and clusters of blue flowers surrounds by white bracts appearing in the summer

A vigorous, arching, repeat-flowering rose, to 4m tall, with glossy, dark green foliage. Large heads of small, lightly-scented, single to semi-double, bright red flowers, with a white eye, are borne in summer and autumn

Bushy, upright hybrid tea rose to 1m high or more, with healthy, glossy, dark green leaves, tinted red when young. High-centred, shapely creamy-white blooms, tinted palest pink, are very fragrant and produced almost continuously during summer and into autumn
A vigorous, bushy rose to 75cm tall, with dark green foliage and fragrant, shapely, dark-red, high-centred blooms opening from well-formed buds and flowering repeatedly through summer

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 1.2m to 1.8m in height when in flower. It forms a compact, dense mound of dark green leaves, and strong stems of mid sky-blue flowers that have a contrasting white centre from early summer to early autumn

primary_name: Primula 'Gold-laced Jack in the Green' Barnhaven (Pr/Poly)

description: A medium-sized deciduous tree to 12m. It has glossy deep green leaves which emerge red then return to dark red in autumn. The fruits, if they form, are dark purple-black
A tender perennial, species pelargonium with grey-green scented leaves smelling of pine and small clusters of delicate-looking single white flowers from spring to late summer.

A tender, upright, bushy, trailing shrub with dark green leaves and single, narrow, tubular magenta-pink flowers with a rose-pink corolla, appearing from summer through until the autumn. Tends to be more tolerant of full sun than other varieties and good for hanging baskets due to its trailing habit

An early, heavy cropping, dessert apple ready for picking from late summer; the large, pale yellow-green fruits are overlaid with dense red stripes on the sides that are exposed to the sun. Care should be taken when harvesting as the fruits bruise easily. Requires a pollinator from groups 2, 3 or 4
A deciduous climber, 2-3m tall, flowering from mid-summer to early autumn. The single flowers, 5-8cm across, are deep purple with lemon-yellow stamens

A small to medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with egg-shaped, slightly flattened pseudobulbs, covered with basal leaf sheaths, carrying five or six, linear leaves up to 50cm long and 1-2cm wide. In spring, upright or arching flowering stems emerge from base of mature pseudobulbs. Each, 15-35cm long stems carries ten to forty, 3-4cm large flowers. Sepals and petals are maroon, often with pale yellowish edge. Lip is small, white with dark red markings and yellow crest in the middle.

A low-growing, evergreen succulent forming a rosette to 30cm across. The fleshy, incurved leaves are glaucous blue-green and flushed pink at the tips. Pink, lantern-shaped flowers are carried on slender, arching stems above the leaf rosettes in early summer
An upright, deciduous, columnar shrub, to 1.5m tall and 0.6m wide, with bright green-yellow foliage. Small, pale yellow spring flowers are followed by scarlet berries
A tall cultivar with evenly produced spikes of creamy-yellow flowers on green stems, to 30cm. The green foliage is semi-erect

A perennial bulb with broadly ovate green leaves. This tulip has goblet-shaped flowers, with pointed petals that are beetroot purple, with a dark purple flush at the base and a narrow white margin. Flowers are produced in mid to late spring, and stand to around 55cm high
A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, ruffled, velvety magenta-purple flowers appearing May to June
A clump-forming perennial to about 1.5m tall, with large, dark green, deeply divided, palmate leaves and in mid and late summer produces tall panicles of grey-blue hooded flowers

A sturdy perennial to 70cm tall, with dark green leaves. Intense purple-pink flowers with rather narrow, pointed rays held flat or slightly up-curved surround an orange-brown cone, and appear from midsummer to autumn

A dense, upright, spreading, evergreen perennial to 80cm tall. The neat, green leaf rosettes are covered in thick, soft hairs when young and the flowers, produced from mid-spring, are yellow-green with a red eye

A clump-forming plant with rather low upright to spreading foliage; to 120cm high, clump 120cm wide. The compact, oblong flower heads, a rich, warm orange fading to yellow, are borne well above the foliage on dark stems. May have two flushes of flowers, in early summer and autumn

alternative_names: Linaria striata subsp. ochroleuca|Linaria striata var. grandiflora

description: A low-growing, evergreen shrub to about 20cm tall, with rounded, leathery dark green leaves to 4cm long. White flowers produced in the leaf axils in midsummer, become yellow with age, and are followed by lustrous, rounded black fruit

A herbaceous perennial to 1m with large, dark green, highly divided leaves. The blooms are made up of jade-green bracts surrounding small, black flowers. They appear in late spring and last to autumn, gradually maturing to pink
A triumph group daffodil with green, strap-like leaves. Small, single, cup-shaped flowers which are yellow with red stripes are produced in the spring.

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This Triumph group tulip has single, cup-shaped flowers, that are very pale grey, almost white. Flowers in mid-spring, and stands to around 40cm high

Multi-stemmed evergreen shrub or small tree, native to south west of Western Australia, about 3-4m tall, with smooth, white or greyish-brown bark. Oval, white waxy juvenile leaves densely packed along the branches become narrow, glossy green adult leaves. Creamy-white flowers in clusters of 7-9 flowers appear from late spring to midsummer, followed by cone-shaped to rounded, woody fruits

Fast-growing annual grass about 1.5m tall, forming a large clump of broadly strap-shaped, dark green leaves maturing to dark mahogany-purple in summer. Stout, upright, tan to gold bottlebrush-like flower panicles produced on leafy stems in summer, followed by shiny purple seedheads, the seeds are very attractive to birds

A very floriferous, clump-forming, bushy perennial about 1m tall, with mid-green foliage, and bearing semi-double, soft yellow flowerheads with several rows of petals and a central yellow disk, opening from coppery buds, flowering in mid to late autumn
A Rembrandt Group tulip about 60cm in height, with burgundy-red to chocolate-brown cup-shaped flowers overlaid with a yellow flame pattern produced in late spring. A heirloom tulip dating from 1780

A short-lived perennial about 1m tall, forming an upright rosette of long, oval, hairy leaves suffused with red-purple when young. In summer, erect, leafy stems bear a cluster of deep blue poppies, sometimes suffused with mauve or purple tones with contrasting yellow stamens. The seed capsules, covered in bristly hairs, are decorative but contain no viable seed

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 20cm high and wide producing upright, sword-shaped, greyish-green leaves with cream-striped margins. Clusters of star-shaped flowers borne from late spring into summer are a pale brown-orange colour with bright yellow centres and purple stripes and streaks at the base of each petal

An upright, clump-forming perennial to 1.5m high, with long, toothed dark green leaves with cream margins, that are tinted pinky-red when young. Flat-topped, branching clusters of pink flowers are produced at the tips of the stems in late summer and early autumn

A perennial bulb, up to 50cm high, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Tall stems produce single, rose-red, cup-shaped flowers with streaks of white and pink from April to May. An historical variety, introduced around 1900

A perennial bulb to 30cm with broad, grey-green foliage, edged with pink, and double, goblet-shaped red to pink flowers with a green 'flame' shape on the underside of the petals, appearing in April to May

A deciduous azalea to about 1.5m high, with an upright to spreading habit and ovate green leaves that turn orange-red in autumn. Produces clusters of 8-9 deep reddish-orange flowers in late spring to early summer

A small, tough, hardy cormous perennial with narrow, grass-like linear green leaves which appear at the same time as the flowers. Fragrant white to very pale pink flowers with purple feathering and yellow throats, appear from late winter to early spring. Great for troughs, raised beds or a rockery and provides nectar for early pollinators

A short-lived, deciduous, dwarf perennial up to 40cm when in flower. Plants form a mound of finely dissected, green leaves with airy spikes of soft rose pink double flowers with dark spurs, from summer to early autumn

A mat-forming, succulent perennial with rosettes of fleshy, pointed leaves. The foliage is red in winter, developing a greener centre to the rosette later in the year. In summer it produces a 15cm tall flowerspike bearing starry pink flowers. The rosettes die after flowering but are replaced by offsets on lateral runners

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 46cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and pinky-red flowers with a yellow throat to 6cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms clumps of arching, strap-like, green leaves and pink flowers that have a scarlet-red eye zone above a green throat to 11cm across in summer.

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms clumps of arching, strap-like, green leaves and purple-blue flowers that have a yellow throat to 15cm across in summer.

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, semi-double, saucer-shaped raspberry pink flowers with a tufted centre of creamy pink petaloids appear in summer.
A strong, deciduous climber with dark-green leaves. Masses of small, white, nodding flowers with greenish anthers appear from July through to September
A compact and bushy, miniature, zonal evergreen perennial with dark-green leaves zoned maroon and clusters of pale pink to bright pink double flowers borne on strong upright stems in summer.

A deciduous shrub about 1.2m tall and 60cm wide, one of the best columnar golden-leaved cultivars, which keeps its colour and shape well all season; red-tinged, pale yellow flowers in spring are followed by red autumn fruits

A compact, dwarf shrub with distinctive colouring. Flowers are pale yellow and relatively insignificant, but the leaves are variegated cream/green, contrasting with red stems. New shoots may be pink-flushed in all parts. Scarlet berries develop in autumn when the leaves also turn orange-red

A deciduous, dome-shaped, low-growing shrub to 45cm tall and wide, with dark velvety purple foliage, turning scarlet in autumn, and red tinged, pale yellow flowers in spring followed by red berries in autumn

A deciduous, upright shrub, to 1.2m high, with spiny, dark red-brown stems. Leaves which are rusty orange when young, become green in summer and turn orange-red in autumn. Scented yellow flowers in spring are followed by bright red fruits in late summer and autumn

A low-growing, compact, dense deciduous shrub with oval-shaped, dark red foliage emerging in spring turning to a darker reddish-black. Small yellow flowers appear in the spring, followed by red berries in the autumn which may persist into winter

alternative_names: hellebore 'HGC Silvermoon'|Winter's song hybrid Christmas rose 'HGC Silvermoon'|Helleborus 'Silver Moon'
description: Has a clump-forming habit and leathery, toothed grey to green leaves. Upright stems produce pink to green to creamy white flowers from mid-winter until mid-spring
A clump-forming evergreen perennial, with glossy dark green lobed leaves. Flowers are white with deep red speckling and saucer-shaped, nodding on short stems.

A very robust, semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, mid-green foliage. Branched stems bear flattish, creamy-white single flowers with a central boss of yellow stamens, in late winter and early spring

A deciduous climber, 1-1.5m high, with green leaves and nodding flowers, 10-13cm across, composed of four to six deeply ribbed blue-purple sepals, fading to mid-blue and opening into a wide star shape, and pale yellow anthers on pale purple filaments, from late summer to early autumn; many clematis are visited by bees for pollen, and some also provide nectar

A deciduous climber to about 3m, with bright green foliage, flowering in late spring to early summer on last year’s growth, and again in late summer on new growth. Flowers are 18-20cm across, with bright purple, wavy-edged petals and cream and dark red stamens

A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Funnel-shaped orange-red flowers, with a streak of bright yellow towards the centre of the petals, are borne over a long period from late spring into autumn

A bushy and upright herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall, and wrinkled, scalloped leaves to 7cm long; these have a strong citrus scent when crushed. Throughout summer it produces spikes of white to purple-tinted flowers that are attractive to bees
A widely spreading, low-growing, well-branched, evergreeen shrub with grey-green needle-like foliage to 30cm (1ft). May produce small dark-blue fruits.

alternative_names: dawn redwood 'Miss Grace'|Metasequoia glyptostroboides 'Semi Prostrata W.B.'

description: A compact, slow-growing conifer forming a narrow column up to 9m tall with twisted sprays of scale-like green foliage that may be tinged purple in winter; leaves have a fruity fragrance when crushed

A compact, clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled silvery lilac-blue flowers with dark burgundy red signals and bronze beards appear from late spring to early summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 80cm high, with divided, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Fragrant, double pink flowers are produced in late spring and early summer

alternative_names: purple moor-grass 'Poul Petersen'|Molinia caerulea 'Poul Petersen'|Molinia caerulea subsp. arundinacea 'Poul Petersen'
description: A tufted, vase-shaped, perennial grass up to 90cm high, with strong clumps of green leaves which turn burnished golden-brown in autumn. Fairly upright stems of purplish flowers are held well above the leaves in summer and autumn, followed by seedheads which remain attractive in winter

A tuberous perennial to 50cm in height with semi-double, orange-tipped flowers, yellow across the petal mid-sections and base, are held on purple stems from summer through to early autumn. The inner petals are variable in their length

A broad deciduous tree reaching 25m tall by 15m wide. The leaves emerge copper-coloured then become bright green then yellow before they fall. They are very large (up to 50cm long) and have usually 9 or 11 pointed leaflets which are fragranced when bruised. The flowers are insignificant but turn into green fruit in late summer from which edible walnuts can be extracted.
A rhizomatous, tender, evergreen perennial with strikingly-marked, sturdy leaves, predominantly silver-grey and dark green with hints of pale red

A fairly compact, rhizomatous, tender, evergreen perennial cultivar with tightly congested, spiralled leaves, a double spiral developing on some mature leaves; leaves are pale grey-green with a central blotch of dark olive green, flushed with magenta on older leaves, and a narrow red rim at the margin

primary_name: Begonia 'New York Swirl' (Great American Cities Series) (R)

description: A clump-forming perennial to about 45cm producing rosettes of bright green, hairy, spoon-shaped leaves and dusky pink, nodding, four-petalled flowers on upright stems in spring
A tall dahlia of airy habit, to 180cm. Flowers are purple-pink, to 14cm, deep red at base around the disc which is orange-yellow
A single dahlia to about 80cm with very dark purple, deeply dividedfoliage. Bright orange-red flowers with dark centres are produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn
A clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 60cm tall with green, divided foliage. Double flowers borne in summer and autumn on upright stems are rose-pink with white-edged petals
A tuberous perennial to 80cm in height with toothed, pinnate, dark mahogany to purple-black leaves. Single bright yellow flowers with orange centres are borne from summer to autumn

An upright, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m with mid-green, divided foliage. Neat, ball-shaped flowers about 8cm across, with inrolled, white petals flushed with pale purple, are produced from early summer to the first frosts

An upright, narrowly pyramidal, deciduous, small to medium-sized tree up to 12m tall with deeply lobed, glossy green leaves that turn crimson red in autumn. Very pronounced wing-like, corky projections on the stems and bark are a feature of established trees. Inconspicuous greenish flowers may be followed by burr-like fruit, 2-4cm across, that stay on the tree through winter

A small to mid-sized evergreen tree, up to around 12m high in cultivation, with lance-shaped glossy green leaves that are slightly serrated at the tips and flushed reddish-pink when young. Mature bark is peeling and rich reddish brown. Dense clusters of small, bell-shaped, cream to pale yellow flowers, with recurved petals and long stamens are produced in spring

This slow-growing, Mexican species is quite rare in the UK but if you can find it, it is definitely worth a spot in your garden. It does require a bit more shelter than some Mahonias and needs well-drained soil, but it will reward you with racemes of fragrant, yellow flowers from late autumn into winter and whorls of pinnate, glossy green leaves, held on bright red stalks

primary_name: Begonia 'Boston Cherries 'n Chocolate' (Great American Cities Series) (R)

description: A tuberous perennial that grows to about 180cm with mid-green foliage. The flowers are 16cm across and have bright, pinky-red petals, yellow at the base, and are rolled outwards giving a spiky appearance
Grows to 170cm. The flowers are up to 12cm across with broad, velvety-red outer florets narrow, pink inner ones and a bold, yellow, central disc
A compact, bushy shrub with wiry, silvery branches and scale-like leaves. Tiny creamy-white to pale yellow flowers are borne in small clusters in summer
A compact, low-growing deciduous perennial with dark green leaves. Sapphire-blue to dark purple, star-shaped purple flowers appear from mid to late summer. This variety does not climb

Bulbous perennial, to around 80cm tall, with strap-shaped, glossy green foliage, dying back as the flowering beginsand umbels of densely packed violet-pink flowers, forming heads up to 12cm across, in early summer
A mound-forming perennial to around 30cm tall bearing fragrant, double, magenta-pink flowers with red centres and fringed petals

An upright, cormous perennial, to 45cm tall, with semi-erect, narrowly-linear, grey-green basal leaves and, in early summer, loose umbels of up to 25 funnel-shaped white flowers with broad violet-blue stripes down the centre of each petal

A tender evergreen perennial, with a bushy habit and shallowly lobed green leaves with serrated edges. Produces clusters of pale pink flowers, with deep reddish-pink blotches at the base of the petals, from early summer to early autumn

A vigorous deciduous shrub or small tree, with an upright to rounded habit. Leaves are broadly ovate, grey-green and softly hairy, turning yellow in autumn. Small, faintly scented flowers are produced in autumn, with long, narrow, curled petals in shades from cream to bright yellow
An upright, bushy evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green foliage and clusters of small, slightly fragrant, star-shaped pinkish white flowers in spring

alternative_names: large-leaved Japanese witch hazel|Hamamelis megalophylla|Hamamelis japonica subsp. megalophylla
description: A deciduous shrub or small tree with a rounded habit. Leaves are large, broadly ovate to rounded, and dark green with toothed margins, and turn shades of orange and red in autumn. Produces flowers on bare stems in late winter and early spring, with long, narrow, very pale yellow petals and dark red sepals at the base

A clump-forming perennial with mid-green leaves cut deeply into three fine lobes. Has stems bearing umbels of saucer-shaped white flowers with indigo centres and a tinge of blue on the reverse from late spring to early summer.
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with glossy green, twisted foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A miniature, compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial with glossy green foliage. Upright stems of nearly-white flowers appear in summer. It's neat and compact habit make this an ideal variety for hanging baskets

A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 30cm high, with narrowly ovate, long-stemmed, glossy green leaves with wavy edges. Forms a dense mound to approximately 80cm across, and produces masses of pendent, pale purple flowers, on slender upright stems high above the foliage in summer

A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with bright yellow-green foliage variegated with wide, white margins. These white margins make take on a pinkish hue in the summer, depending on light levels. Lavender purple flowers appear on stems above the foliage during the summer

A compact, bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial which is later flowering than other varieties. It produces dark green, lobed foliage and single, strongly fragranced, magenta-pink flowers with a paler pink inner ring and yellow centres during October and November

primary_name: Viola × wittrockiana 'Dynamite White With Blotch Improved'

description: A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and orange-red flowers to 14cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and dark purple flowers to around 13cm across with a pale green to yellow throat in summer
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are slightly fragrant and pink with ruffled petals and a large, green-yellow throat
A strong, evergreen perennial to about 1m, with unusual pale yellowish-green fully double flowers, the petals having shallow-toothed margins; consistently good flowers throughout the year

primary_name: Ipomoea batatas 'Sweet Caroline Light Green' (Sweet Caroline Series)
Ipomoea batatas 'Sweet Caroline Bronze' (Sweet Caroline Series)
description: A tender, trailing perennial, normally grown as an annual, to around 50cm in height with heart-shaped, lobed bronze and lime-green foliage. Grown as an ornamental for its foliage from June to September, it works well in hanging baskets, patio pots and window boxes or covering a trellis to add colour and texture

primary_name: Ipomoea batatas 'Sweet Caroline Purple' (Sweet Caroline Series)
alternative_names: Ipomoea batatas 'Purple' (Sweet Heart Series)|Ipomoea 'Sweet Caroline Purple'

description: A compact, evergreen shrub to around 45cm high, with aromatic, grey-green leaves. Spikes of fragrant pink flowers topped by pale pink bracts appear in summer

A deciduous, bulbous, vigorous herbaceous perennial to around 120cm, with strap-like dark green leaves and white, fragrant flowers with a yellow streak in the centre of each petal. Flowers are upward and outward-facing and appear in the summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 90cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, outward-facing, bowl-shaped lightly fragrant orange flowers, with darker orange streaks along the midveins, are produced in summer, with up to 6 flowers per plant

A compact, upright, bulbous perennial to 40cm high, with dark green leafy stems. Produces upward to outward-facing, bowl-shaped flowers in late spring or early summer. Flowers are large and mid- to deep orange.

A bulbous perennial producing a strong, upright stem to about 75cm clothed in shiny, dark green, lance-shaped leaves and topped in mid-summer with a cluster of egg-yolk yellow, upward-facing, bowl-shaped flowers with tiny, dark red speckles in the throat, and dark red anthers
An upright, epiphytic perennial to approximately 50cm, with glossy dark green leaves. Bright red, heart-shaped spathes with yellow spadices are produced periodically throughout the year.

An evergreen perennial houseplant with glossy dark green foliage and waxy lime green spathes which turn white as they mature between November and May. Lime green spikes protude from the spathes. An exotic but easy to care for plant

alternative_names: red Christmas pride|Ruellia longifolia (Pohl) Griseb.|Ruellia amoena|Ruellia graecizans

description: A hardy biennial grown as an annual vegetable. An easy to grow purple skinned variety with a superior taste which is very Winter hardy and has a long holding ability. It shows high resistance to powdery mildew

A tough, evergreen shrub of rounded habit, up to 2m (6½ft) high, with bright green leaves, toothed at the margins, that are liberally dusted with small yellow spots. A male form, this produces small, purple flowers, with four bright yellow stamens in spring.
A vigorous, upright shrub up to 2.5m high, with deciduous, three-lobed, green leaves, and white or very pale pink flowers with deep red centres and veins, from late summer to mid-autumn
A bushy, medium-sized, evergreen shrub with dark green foliage, flushed red in spring. The urn-shaped flowers in white and dark pink are produced in dense, upright to spreading, clusters in spring

A clump-forming, short-lived perennial to 85cm with blue-green, divided leaves. Long-spurred, outward- to upward-facing flowers, with white inner petals and light blue-purple outer petals and spurs, appear in late spring and early summer

A clump-forming, upright herbaceous perennial with mid-green lance shaped leaves. Bronze red flowers with orange edging and deep brown centres with yellow tips in summer, flowering over a long period if dead-headed regularly.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 90cm high, with rough, ovate leaves and yellow blooms with raised, anemone-like centres on strong stems in summer and early autumn

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 90cm, with dark green, divided foliage which emerges beetroot red in spring and takes on dark red tones again in autumn. The double,deep red blooms are carried on darkstems in late spring and early summer, though it can be shy to bloom
A small-cupped daffodil, with straplike grey-green leaves. Flowers are 13.5cm across, with smooth white outer petals and a bowl-shaped, pale lemon yellow cup with a frilled rim

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to 45cm high, with glossy dark olive-green leaves with pewter-grey veins. The large flowers, appearing from late winter to early spring, have green centres and long creamy stamens, the petals opening creamy-white and becoming pinkish-red with age

A bushy, evergreen to semi-evergreen small tree or shrub with thick, glossy, oval-shaped bright green foliage turning to purple in winter. Clusters of white flowers (bracts) appear in summer followed by red berries in the autumn

A slow-growing, upright, evergreen conifer with a slightly 'twisted' habit. Weeping branches produce blue-green-grey needle-like foliage. Makes an interesting specimen tree for a sunny garden. Tolerates air pollution.

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and black-red flowers that have a yellow-green throat to 13cm across in summer. This variety continues to flower at night
A clump-forming, upright herbaceous perennial with mid-green lance shaped leaves. Bright yellow flowers with dark brown centres appear in summer, flowering over a long period if dead-headed regularly

An aquatic perennial with rounded leaves blotched with purple, and starry flowers to 15cm wide, with red inner petals and pale pink outer petals Dwarf/small cultivars reach 30–60cm (1–2ft) wide, and need water 30–45cm (12–18in) deep Medium cultivars reach 60–120cm (2–4ft) wide, and need water 45–75cm (18–30in) deep Large cultivars reach up to 2.4m (8ft) wide, and need water 75–120cm (30in–4ft) deep For a suitable planting depth in your pond, please follow the plant label guidelines

primary_name: Calibrachoa [Million Bells Trailing Ice] ('Sunbelkuriho') (Million Bells Series)

description: An upright herbaceous perennial 1.2m high with divided green leaves and strong stems, especially suitable for cutting, of deep blue flowers with white centres in early summer; delphiniums may be visited by bumblebees, especially long-tongued bumblebees

A hardy evergreen clump-forming perennial with strap-like green leaves and upright hairy stems. Pink-flushed white daisy-like flowers with thin petals that droop downwards from the orange-brown centre cone, appear from mid to late summer and are lightly fragranced. A good plant for cutting and drought-resistant once established

A semi-trailing to mounding and spreading floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces fragrant, frilly, ruffled, fully-double red and white flowers around 6 cm across. Blooms from early summer well into autumn if dead-headed and well fed. It trails or spreads around 40-50 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and balcony containers and patio pots

alternative_names: rat tail cypress|Crassula lycopodiodes f. acuminata|Crassula pseudolycopodioides
description: A spreading, perennial succulent forming a dense bush to 25cm tall. The scrambling branches are completely covered with neat ranks of tiny, scale-like leaves. Bears minute, tubular, greenish-yellow flowers in spring

A evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and copper-brown coloured flowers with a dark green throat to 15cm across in summer
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial and one of the smallest hemerocallis, with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are small and yellow-orange with a yellow throat

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and large, fragrant, pale yellow flowers with a green throat to 19cm across in summer

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and fragrant dark violet pink flowers with a green throat to 13cm across in summer

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 94cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, creamy-yellow flowers to around 18cm across with a purple-black halo and a yellow-green throat in summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

alternative_names: silver crown|oblong round-leafed navel-wort|silver ruffles|Cotyledon undulata
description: An upright, evergreen, succulent subshrub branching from ground level and grows to around 50cm tall. Fleshy leaves, 5-10cm long, are obovate, wedge-shaped to oblong-linear, grey-green in colour with a powdery waxy coating and margins that may be edged deep red. Flower stems to 70cm high bear clusters of bell-shaped to tubular, pendulous, pinkish-orange flowers
An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 157cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and orange-red flowers in summer

A spreading, medium-sized tree with arching branches and deep green leaves about 10cm long. In early spring, before the leaves open, it produces a profusion of very pale pink to white, bowl-shaped, single flowers about 4cm across

A compact, free-flowering rose to around 60-90cm in heightwith healthy, glossy foliage, and bearing scrolled buds opening to the palest of pink double blooms with a strong scent, flowering through summer and autumn

A small, bushy floribunda rose with rich green foliage. Clusters of sweetly scented semi-double blooms in a rich purple-mauve appear in the summer which then fade to a slatey blue. Becoming more open with age, great for passing pollinators. Freely flowering from July to September

primary_name: Petrocosmea begoniifolia C.Y. Wu ex H.W. Li
description: An alpine herbaceous perennial up to 10cm high, with an almost flat rosette of glossy, succulent dark green leaves with a dimpled texture, and dark red stems carrying white flowers with yellow throats in spring

An alpine herbaceous perennial up to 6cm high, with an almost flat rosette of rounded, felted succulent green leaves, and many white, lavender-tinged or lavender-blue flowers 2-3cm across in late winter or spring

An evergreen succulent, forming a spreading rosette of lance-shaped green leaves with a slight glaucous bloom. Leaves have small, sharp teeth along the edges and grey spines to 5cm long at the tip. Slow growing, but can reach up to 1.2m high at maturity. Mature plants may produce a tall spike of yellow flowers, after which the central rosette dies off

alternative_names: castor oil plant 'New Zealand Black'|Ricinus 'New Zealand Purple'
description: A large, tender, evergreen shrub grown as an annual in temperate climates. It has large, dark red-purple, palmately lobed leaves and showy red female flower spikes in summer, followed by dark red fruits with soft spines

alternative_names: blackberry lily|Chinese blackberry lily|Chinese leopard flower|dwarf tiger lily|leopard lily|Belamcanda chinensis 'Leopard Lily'|Belamcanda flabellata|Belamcanda chinensis var. curtata|Belamcanda mixed|Belamcanda chinensis
description: Has narrow leaves to 20cm long, and yellow of reddish-orange flowers 4cm wide, heavily spotted with deep red, and followed by green seed pods splitting to reveal several conspicuous, glossy black seeds
A spreading perennial to 30cm tall, with finely divided, vividly glaucous leaves and arching sprays of pink-flushed creamy-white flowers in late spring and early summer

Upright, relatively compact coneflower cultivar reaching around 60cm tall with dark green, toothed leaves. Double flowers comprise rings of drooping, white ray florets surrounding the pompon-like lime green inner florets and orange centre
A Triumph cultivar, to 50cm in height, with grey-green foliage. Flowers, pastel-pink turning white at tips, appear in mid spring
A selection with lavender-purple flowers and clear, white throats. Height to around 60cm
A semi-evergreen perennial up to 50cm high with oval green leaves and scarlet flowers with white throats in summer and autumn
a semi-evergreen perennial to 80cm tall with slender mid-green leaves and large cerise-pink to purple tubular to bell-shaped flowers with a pale throat from summer to autumn
A bushy, semi-evergreen perennial to 80cm tall, with slender mid-green leaves and from summer to autumn, large, bright-pink tubular flowers with a white throat
A semi-evergreen perennial to 60cm tall with slender dark green leaves and from summer to autumn pale pink tubular flowershave fine red stripes and a red throat are borne over a long period

A tender shrub with an open, erect and branched habit. This free-flowering cultivar produces double, trumpet-shaped flowers in spring and autumn. The apricot-coloured flowers are 30cm long and highly fragrant

A branching, dense, evergreen shrub to around 2.4m high and wide with prominently-veined, oval leaves up to 40cm long. Erect flower spikes are borne from late summer into winter and sporadically throughout the rest of the year with the white, two-lipped flowers surrounded by showy red bracts

A dense, compact, evergreen succulent with neat rosettes of thick, fleshy blue-green leaves edged with fine tufts of hair. The leaves turn a more turquoise colour and develop red and yellow tints in strong sunlight. Beautiful, bell-shaped yellow and red flowers appear on stems above the foliage in summer

primary_name: Tulipa 'Duc van Tol Red and Yellow' (1)
alternative_names: tulip 'Duc van Tol Red and Yellow'
description: A perennial bulb, to around 30cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. This is one of the earliest known cultivars, with bright red petals finely edged with yellow

A slow-growing, evergreen, long-lived indoor plant, which is more compact than other varieties. Produces a rosette of stiff, very upright, wide, lance-shaped leaves with a variegated green and yellow snake-like pattern and yellow edge

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes to 5cm across, the spoon-shaped, pale green leaves flushed pale pink are covered with silvery white hairs, giving a misty appearance. Tall spikes of starry pale pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant, dark purple flowers, topped with long, frilly pink bracts, are borne on short stems from early to late summer
A dwarf, sprawling succulent to 15cm tall, producing ranks of fleshy leaves that emerge light green, before the tips age to bright red. Best colour is achieved if grown in a sunny position

alternative_names: blackberry lily 'Freckle Face'|Belamcanda 'Freckle Face'|Belamcanda chinensis 'Freckle Face'

description: A rhizomatous perennial, to around 45cm high in flower, with fans of upright sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Small, clear yellow flowers are borne on branching stems above the foliage, opening in succession from mid to late summer, and followed by papery seed pods containing clusters of shiny black seeds

A twining climber reaching 3m with green leaves. Scarlet flowers develop into long, smooth runner beans. This variety is slow to 'go over' and become tough. In the UK it is grown as a summer annual, lasting only one year.
An annual dwarf french bean with green leaves and white flowers, producing a heavy crop of beans over a long period

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm, with mid-green foliage. Flowers 10cm across, produced from mid-summer until the first frosts, have one or two rows of broad, rose-pink, outer petals and a central cluster of numerous, short, rose-pink petals with toothed, cream tips

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with dark green foliage. Flowers 10cm across, produced from mid-summer until the first frosts, have creamy-white outer petals suffused with pink and with a fine pink rim, and a central powder-puff of short, toothed, yellow petals

An attractive, spreading, upright, perennial herb with purple stems bearing mid-green, lance shaped leaves that have a good spearmint scent and flavour. Small, mauve-pink flowers appears in terminal, cylindrical spikes in summer

A compact tuberous perennial with heart-shaped dark green leaves with silver markings. Flowers are produced in late winter and early spring in a range of colours from white to purple, and are distinctive for their fringed and ruffled petals

An vigorous, upright, annual variety with aromatic, bright green leaves and umbels of small, white flowers in summer. Very slow to bolt, as the name suggests, therefore reduces successional sowing throughout the season
An evergreen shrub, up to 45cm high, with aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and long spikes of fragrant, deep blue-purple flowers in summer

A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial with spirally arranged ovate leaves, outlined and veined dark green, deeply edged silvery white and suffused purplish-pink , darker at the centres. Small pink flowers in panicles appear in winter

A vigorous, evergreen shrub with a distinctly upright habit, to 1.2m tall. It bears glossy leaves and in early spring produces clusters of fragrant pale pink flowers opening from darker pink buds; these are followed by spherical red fruits
An evergreen, perennial alpine with narrow, blue-grey foliage and trumpet-shaped lavender blue flowers, which appear on tall spikes in summer

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to about 30cm high, with lobed, deep purple leaves with a silver sheen on the upper surface, and dark purple veining. Loose sprays of small cream flowers appear from late spring to mid-summer

alternative_names: Veronicastrum sibiricum subsp. japonicum var. australe

description: A vigorous, trailing and mounding, floriferous tender perennial usually grown as an annual for seasonal bedding displays or as a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces trumpet-shaped, ruffled and fully double pale lilac flowers. It blooms from early summer into autumn. It trails or gently mounds and spreads around 30 cm to 40 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and containers and as ground cover in warm, well-drained, sunny spots.

alternative_names: petunia [Surfinia Hot Red]|Petunia 'Sunhore'|Petunia [Surfinia Hot Salmon] (Surfinia Series)
description: A vigorous, mounding or trailing floriferous tender perennial with a mature height of 20 to 30cm, and usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces striking, gramophone-trumpet-shaped, pale salmon-red flowers with red veining. It blooms from late spring or early summer into autumn. It trails or spreads around 30 cm to 40 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and containers.

An erect, woody-based, deciduous perennial, producing stems to 90cm high and a spread of 50cm, with deeply divided, aromatic green leaves. In late summer and autumn, the plants produce many sprays of fully-double, rich red flowers, the petals are slightly incurved and have a pale orange reverse, creating a two-toned effect to the flower

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches to approximately 90cm in height when in flower. It forms a mound of green, deeply lobed leaves and flower stems of pale lilac flowers with contrasting dark centres, in summer

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which unlike the typical species, produces a compact, flattened spherical bush up to 25cm (10in) high and 50cm (20in) across after ten years. The mid-green needles are small, stiff, and very densely produced, so that the stems and basal branches are completely covered. It is an ideal choice for a small city, or courtyard garden, where an architectural or evergreen focal point is needed; for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which produces a compact, flattened, irregular globe to dome-shaped bush, reaching about 1-1.5m (3-5ft) high and 1.5m (5ft) across after ten years. It has an open horizontally branching habit. The needles are produced in bunches of two at the tips of the stems and are around 7.5-12cm (3-5in) long. They are stiff to the touch and are dark grey-green in colour. It can produce oval-shaped, brown cones, that taper to a point at the tips and are up to 7.5cm (3in) long. It withstands exposed, coastal positions exteremely well and its relatively small size, means it is an excellent choice for a small, city or courtyard garden, where an architectural, or evergreen focal point is needed, as well as for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery

A spreading, semi-evergreen shrub or small tree to 4m tall and 6m wide. Oblong to elliptic leaves up to 8cm long are semi-evergreen with some turning shades of yellow, orange and reddish-purple before falling in autumn; new growth emerges tinted deep reddish-purple in spring before turning glossy green. In late winter to early spring, dense clusters of flowers open from brown buds with yellow anthers tinged red surrounded by purple-brown bracts

A clump-forming, upright perennial, to around 90cm high in flower, with narrowly sword-shaped, slightly grey-green leaves. Flowers are large and double, with white petals marked with a vivid yellow-green signal at the base

primary_name: Petunia [Surfinia Baby Red with Eye] ('Keiresam') (Surfinia Series)

description: A less vigorous selection of the species, to around 1.5m in height. Leaves are dark green with white splashes and with touches of yellow when newly-emerged. Flower spikes, in the summer months, have white and pink bracts
A bushy plant with grey-green leaves and white fully-double flowers, where the outer ray florets are multiplied row upon row so that no central disc is visible

A compact, evergreen subshrub to about 40cm with whorls of narrow, dark green leaves on red-flushed stems. Sprays of long-lasting, lime-green flowers with red eyes are produced in spring and early summer

Forms a clump to 50cm in height, with narrow, dark green glossy leaves and semi-double flowers 10-12cm in width. The narrow outer ray florets open butter yellow, maturing almost to white, and surround a yellow disc. A compact, shapely plant with a long flowering season

A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced white flowers with yellow centres appear from summer through until the autumn

A compact perennial, to 35cm high, with dissected, lobed to palmate, tiered, mid-green leaves with striking, dark-brown, central markings. Small, pale-pink flowers are clustered along each flower stem giving a frothy, wand-like appearance. Flowers appear from spring to early summer

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Pale pink daisy-like flowers, turning a darker shade of pink as they mature and with yellow stamens, appear in the spring

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Single flowers open white then fade to light pink to lavender in the spring. An old-fashioned variety

An evergreen, frost-tender sub-shrub, often grown as an annual, forming a compact mound of finely-divided, mid-green foliage to around 30cm tall. A mass of single flowers, lemon-yellow with a darker yellow centre, are borne above the foliage from late spring until the first frosts.

A tender evergreen perennial usually grown as an annual, with trailing stems and small, narrow leaves. Bright reddish-pink trumpet-shaped flowers, with fine red veins and a yellow throat, are produced over a long period in summer and autumn

A fast-growing, frost-tender perennial usually grown as an annual with rigid, thornless, upright stems bearing palmate, dark green leaves. Open, terminal clusters of four-petalled, spider-like, lavender-pink flowers with long, protruding stamens are borne from early summer into autumn

A spreading evergreen tree, with peeling grey and red-brown bark when mature. Leaves are sharply serrated, and emerge bright orange-red, maturing to glossy dark green. Small white flowers are produced in large, flattened clusters in late spring and early summer, followed by red fruit

A deciduous herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 41cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and double creamy-white to pale pink flowers above a green throat to 13cm across in summer
A vigorous, annual climber, up to around 2.4m high, with curling tendrils and pairs of green leaves. Fragrant, dark burgundy red flowers with a pink and cream blush, appear from May to September

A clump-forming, spreading perennial to 60cm tall, with a basal rosette of slender, egg-shaped, green leaves, the branched stems bearing solitary bright purple-blue, pincushion-like flowerheads 2cm across, in summer and autumn

A perennial grown as a houseplant, forming a clump of evergreen, strap-like leaves to 60cm in length, with erect stems bearing a terminal umbel of slender, tubular, yellow-throated, orange-red flowers up to 7cm in length, from spring to summer

A clump-forming succulent producing 4- or 5-angled, grey-green stems to 6cm long, edged with conical spines. In late summer it bears succulent yellow flowers marked with burgundy dots and stripes; these emerge from star-shaped buds. Huernia flowers have an unpleasant smell to attract pollinating flies

A succulent, evergreen perennial to 30cm tall, forming a clump of upright to curving, 4-angled stems. In late summer, dark maroon, inflated flower buds are formed; these open into bell-shaped blooms 8cm across, emitting a foul smell to attract pollinating flies
A low-growing, mat-forming evergreen perennial to around 20cm in height, with green foliage. Bell-shaped, lilac-blue flowers, 2cm in length, appear on branching stems in the summer

A hardy biennial, with toothed, heart-shaped leaves in shades from dark green to deep purple. Large, open clusters of pinkish-purple flowers are produced on purple-flushed stems in late spring and early summer, followed by flat, round seed pods that dry to translucent silvery white

A rhizomatous, tender perennial to around 30cm in height, with soft, pale green foliage with brownish-black markings, prominent green veins and red undersides. Pink flowers appear on short stalks from January to April

A deciduous, compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce large panicles of trumpet-shaped, pale blue-mauve flowers with a darker blue mid-rib, in the summer

Fast-growing, deciduous spreading tree, narrow in habit when young, to about 18m tall, with downy shoots and green leaves borne late in spring that turn yellow, red and burgundy in autumn and are held on the tree longer than other selections. Inconspicuous, pale, petalless flowers in spring, but no fruit is produced

A clump-forming, bushy perennial about 65cm tall, with deeply dissected dark green leaves, silvery on the reverse, and bearing quill-shaped, double, creamy-yellow flowerheads 8cm across, in mid to late autumn

A bushy, compact herbaceous perennial with divided dark green leaves to around 60cm in height. Dense clusters of very small, fragrant, fully double, intense magenta-pink flowers appear from September through to November

alternative_names: afal pig aderyn|Malus domestica 'Afal Pig Aderyn'

description: An evergreen succulent with rosettes of spoon-shaped, succulent, cabbage-like leaves, warty towards the tops with crinkled edges. These emerge pale grey-green turning to pinkish-orange as they mature. It may produce tube-shaped peachy pink-orange flowers in spring to summer

A deciduous, compact or branching, large shrub or small tree with mid-green, oval-shaped leaves, narrower at the base. Goblet shaped flowers are purple fading to pink and lightly scented. Flowers in early spring so flowers can be damaged by frosts.

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial, up to 40cm high, with dark green serrated leaves, flushed with pewter-grey. Large, outward-facing, pink-flushed white flowers appear from midwinter until late spring

A vigorous small tree, about 10-15m tall, with a conical habit, and 3-lobed leaves emerging deep wine red in spring, fading to dark green in summer then turning to rich burgundy in autumn
A tender evergreen perennial, with a compact, trailing habit and lobed, slightly glossy, ivy-like green leaves. Produces clusters of mid pink flowers from late spring to early autumn

A large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for its unusual, bright-coloured flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a central tip on a long, stem-like rhizome, covered in leaf-bearing, green, alternate sheaths. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves grow from the top of the plant, older lower leaves gradually drop off. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system, that hangs downwards at the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Multiple inflorescences appear from the axils of leaves and the stem and carry 8 or more large, waxy, round-shaped flowers. Petals and sepals are white, covered in a distinctive mosaic, square pattern of blue or purple lines. Each flower measures over 10cm in diameter.

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, tropical orchid hybrid. As a typical example of a monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from the central tip of the long, stem-like rhizome. Alternate, leaf-bearing, green sheaths cover the whole rhizome. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves angle out from the central stem. While new leaves appear from the top, older, lower leaves gradually drop off. Large root system of pale silvery roots hangs from the base of the plant. New roots grow directly from the stem, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from axils of leaf sheaths, and carry 8 or more large, brightly colured, flat, round-shaped flowers. All petals are round, uniform in size, colour and shape. Petals and upper sepal are marked with darker spotted pattern, while lower sepals are covered in darker, thick tesselation, resulting in overall darker appearance. Each flower measures up to 10cm across. This hybrid is one on the 'modern' flat-shaped hybrids, which are so valued for their large, bright, long-lasting flowers, often used by florists.

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid hybrid, valued for its large, bright-coloured, long-lasting flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from the central tip on a long, stem-like rhizome. The stem is tightly covered with leaf-bearing, green, alternate bracts. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves angle out from the stem. A characteristic feature is an impressive roots system, hanging downwards from the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the main stem, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from axils of leaf sheaths, and carry 8 or more large, waxy, round-shaped flowers. All petals and sepal are round, uniform in shape and size. Flowers are heavily spotted with darker pattern, and mosaic tesselation on the lower sepals. Colour may vary from pink to purple, depending on the cultivar. This hybrid, bred in Florida in 1982 has given progeny to many bright-coloured modern hybrids, valued for the longevity and size of their flowers.

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for its large, bright-coloured, long-lasting flowers. Inflorescences emerge from the axils of leaves, bearing approximately 6 large, waxy, round-shaped flowers. 'Robert's Delight' is a hybrid with large, flat, long-lasting, flowers, measuring 10cm or more in diameter. Petals and sepals are round-shaped, with spotted and tesselated pattern, heavier on two lower sepals, giving them a darker appearance. Colour of the hybrid varies depending on cultivar.
