Bulbous perennial about 90cm high, with green strap-shaped, basal leaves which die back before the airy, sparkler-like, rich pinkish-purple flowerheads to15cm across, open in early summer
A cultivar with gold and green variegated foliage that is tinged pink in colder weather. Flowerheads of green bracts with central red flowers are borne in March to July; often a short-lived plant

A bulbous perennial, forming clumps of narrow grass-like blue green foliage up to 38cm tall, with loose umbels of white star-like flowers, from late spring to early summer. The foliages dies down by late summer and regrows in late autumn
A bulbous perennial, native to Central Asia with narrow basal mid-green leaves and producing compact umbels, of purplish-violet star-shaped flowers on stems up to 1m tall in summer
A mound forming perennial, leaves are palmate glossy rich purple, can turn silver with purple tint in winter. Panicles of white-pink flowers on dark stems

A deciduous shrub to 1.5m high, with reddish, branching stems and ovate, serrated green leaves that turn deep red in autumn. Broad lace-cap flower heads are produced on both new and old wood, extending the season to provide flowers all summer. Clusters of tiny fertile flowers are surrounded by large, showy florets in shades of pink, purple or blue depending on the soil

A compact, spreading evergreen shrub with mid-green, lance shaped leaves with cream edges. Leaves flushed with darker red in the autumn and winter. Sprays of small white, bell-shaped flowers in spring.
A bulbous perennial with leafy stems up to 2.5m. Large, open flowers with recurved, rich-pink petals, darker in the centre, with pale edges, and a strong, spicy scent, open in mid-summer

A deciduous, bulbous herbaceous perennial to around 120cm, with strap-like green leaves and dark, crimson-red, fragranced flowers with darker red speckles. Flowers are outward-facing and flat with only the tepal tips recurved, and appear in July and August
A perennial bulb, to around 35cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are red with white edges, with pointed petals that open wide in the sun

Deciduous, clump-forming, perennial grass, about 1m tall with an upright vase-shaped habit, and flat, linear, blue-green leaves, turning deep red-purple in late summer and autumn. Airy sprays of tiny, red-purple flowers are produced from mid-summer to early autum
A Single Late Group tulip to around 10-20cm tall, the petite, single, cup-shaped purplish-pink flowers edged white, open in late April. A historical tulip dating from 1700

primary_name: Vincetoxicum nigrum [I am a Tiny Star] ('Zotista')

description: An erect, woody-based, half-hardy, deciduous perennial, producing stems to 1.2m (4ft) high and a spread of 50cm (20in), with deeply divided, aromatic leaves, dark-green above and greyish-green on the reverse. In late summer and autumn, fully double flowers are produced with incurving petals pink on the upper sides and pale pink on the undersides, creating a two-tone effect. Flowers are long lasting in water and are ideal for growing for cutting. Plants are best lifted after flowering or grown in containers and moved into cold, but frost free conditions over winter.
A tender perennial to 1.5m tall with aromatic, dark green, divided leaves. Fully double flowerheads with incurved, creamy-white florets are borne in autumn
An upright perennial with dark green, lobed foliage and large, fully double, pure golden-yellow flowers in early autumn
An evergreen perennial with glossy, toothed leaves forming a low mound and scented, double flowers borne in late winter and spring with ruffled white petals speckled with lilac-blue

primary_name: Pyrus communis ['Conference', 'Doyenné du Comice', 'Williams' Bon Chrétien']

description: A bushy, aromatic, short-lived herbaceous perennial 60cm high with ovate to lance-shaped dark green leaves, 4-6cm long, and spikes up to 30cm long of dark raspberry-pink flowers from midsummer to autumn.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with lance-shaped, mid-green leaves turning golden in autumn. Bears clusters of lilac-blue starry flowers in summer.

A small and compact, bushy, clump-forming perennial with elongated lance-shaped green leaves and abundant large, double, golden yellow flowers with frilly petals held on stalks just above its foliage flowering for a long period of time over summer.

primary_name: Corydalis solida subsp. solida dark pink-flowered
Corydalis solida subsp. solida pale pink-flowered

description: Upright, perennial coneflower about 75-90cm tall, the daisy-like flowers with a central orange-brown cone surrounded by narrow, overlapping, recurved, pale pink ray petals, flowering from midsummer to autumn

A clump-forming perennial about 1-1.2m high, with upright, branching stems and deeply divided, stalked mid-green leaves. Clusters of small daisy-like mauve flowers with yellow centres, are produced from mid to late summer and well into autumn

A low-growing, clump-forming perennial about 30cm tall, producing leafy, branching stems bearing pale blue daisy-like flowerheads, with golden yellow centres, appearing over a long period from early summer to autumn
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with aromatic green foliage and whorls of violet-blue flowers in late summer and autumn.
A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial with flat, blue-grey leaves and slim spikes of fluffy, dark red to pink flowers which appear from summer through to autumn
A tall, airy, clump-forming perennial to 2m, producing a mound of light green, divided leaves. Tall, slender, branched stems support small, cylindrical, dark red flowerheads in mid to late summer

A short-lived perennial, often grown as an annual, up to 20cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves, and racemes of bicoloured flowers in shades of white, yellow, bronze, pink, and red, from early summer to autumn
A compact, semi-trailing variety with loose-cascading white flowers from summer until early autumn

A compact, rounded shrub to about 1.2m with shiny, thick, oval leaves 2-3cm long, lime green with a central yellow splash. Leaf colour intensifies in winter and may develop orange tints. This is a male cultivar with insignificant flowers and no fruit
Bushy, deciduous rose to around 1m tall, with glossy, mid-green leaves and bearing clusters of lightly scented, double, pale to mid-pink blooms, repeat-flowering from summer into autumn
An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 1.2m tall with lance-shaped leaves. Branching, candelabra-like stems bear long spires of small, white flowers from early summer into autumn

A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 60cm high with wavy-edged, upright, green leaves and dark purple flowers which appear from summer to early autumn. May be grown as a house or conservatory plant or as a summer patio plant

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and mid-yellow flowers that have a frilly edge and green throat to 15cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours

A clump-forming, deciduous, herbaceous perennial, producing narrow, strap-shaped, mid-green foliage, to a height of around 90cm (3ft) and spreading to around 1m (39in). Hemisperical heads of pendulous, funnel-shaped flowers in deep blue with pale-blue bases, are produced in late summer, on straight, green stems, to approximately 1.5m (5ft) high.

alternative_names: Mount Omei busy lizzie 'Ice Storm'|Impatiens omeiana silver-leaved|Impatiens from China
description: A hardy rhizomatous cultivar that has a silvery frosting on the leaves and almost orchid-like, creamy yellow flowers in early autumn. The species is endemic to Sichuan in China. It looks great in a jungle or exotic scheme and is ideal for growing in a container too. Grow in moist, well-drained soil that doesn't dry out. It grows to 50-60cm in height and enjoys semi-shade best but will grow in sun too if kept moist and well watered.

Robust, clump-forming, gradually spreading, evergreen perennial sedge, about 30cm tall, with intense, glaucous-blue foliage. Carries purplish-black flower spikes to 30cm long within the foliage, in late spring

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial grass to 1.5m in height. Leaves are narrow and mid-green in colour. In late summer to early autumn, pale brown spikes of flowers are borne. This is a specific seedling (amed by Neil Lucas at Knoll Gardens) that used to be part of a larger group known as 'M. 'Yakushima Dwarf'

A hybrid between P. macrostachyum and P. setaceum. Strappy, dark-red foliage emerges in spring, initially flushed green. Arching stems bear bottlebrush-shaped flowers in late summer to autumn, their silver and red plumes eventually becoming brown

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 58cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, double, fragrant beige-cream flowers that have pale orange veins and a green-yellow throat to 17cm across in summer

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, black-red flowers with a green throat to 11cm across in summer

Densely tufted, spreading evergreen perennial grass about 1.5m tall, with narrow, mid-green leaves and tall, upright, panicles of pinkish-beige spikelets, to 30cm long, produced in late summer and early autumn
A rhizomatous perennial to 50cm in height, with grey-green basal leaves and fragrant pale pink flowers with lemon centres in terminal umbels in late summer and early autumn

A colour mix of tender flowering perennials which grow from bulb-like structures known as corms. In late winter, spring or summer (depending on time of planting), funnel-shaped, scented flowers in red, orange, magenta, lilac, purple, yellow and cream bloom sequentially on thin arching stems above sword-shaped, mid-green leaves. Height around 45cm (18in).

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and creamy-white coloured flowers with a blueish-purple eye-zone above a green throat to14cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and purple flowers with a washed lavender eyezone and green throat to 9cm across in summer
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems producing panicles of trumpet-shaped mid-blue flowers in summer
A bulbous herbaceous perennial 0.8-1.1m high, with evergreen, wide green leaves, and flowerheads, about 12-13cm across, composed of about 70 violet-blue flowers, in late summer

An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems with rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped flowers in the summer. These are almost white, tinged with pale purple on darker stems
A tender perennial with pale yellow quilled flowers, darker towards the centre, produced in late autumn
A compact, upright perennial, to around 40cm high, with thin, lance-shaped deep green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant, pale pink flowers with dark pink eyes are produced in summer

A deciduous climber with mid to dark green leaves, reaching a height of around 2m. Semi-double or double pale lavender pink flowers appear in late spring until early summer and then again in early autumn.

An upright, clump-forming perennial grown for its edible, rich dark purple shoots, known as spears, harvested from mid-spring to early summer. Once cropping has stopped, tall, branching stems develop with airy, feathery, mid-green foliage, 1.5 x 1.5m. Small, inconspicuous, green and white flowers may be followed by sparse red berries
A compact, bushy shrub to 1m tall with silvery-green aromatic foliage and deep violet-blue flowers in late summer

Deciduous climber or scrambler about 2.5-3m in height, with sharply serrated, mid-green leaves divided into 9 leaflets and double, nodding, bell-shaped, white flowers to 5cm long with an inner skirt of the same colour petals and bluish-white stamens, flowering early to mid spring
A clump-forming perennial about 45cm tall, with finely divided, fern-like, grey-green foliage, and sprays of cherry-red flowers produced in spring then intermittently through summer

A deciduous, slow growing small tree or shrub with mid-green, distinctive fan-shaped, bilobed leaves, up to 2 meters in height. Leaves are about half the size of other cultivars, ideal for containers and excellent autumn colour.

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial, growing to 40cm tall, with dark green leaves. Flowers are produced abundantly from mid-winter to mid-spring, opening from pink buds, flowers emerge white tinged with pink and darken to a deeper pink as they age

alternative_names: hellebore 'Ivory Prince'|Helleborus 'Ivory Prince'|Helleborus [Ivory Prince]|Helleborus 'Walberton's Ivory Prince'|Helleborus 'Walhelivor'|Helleborus niger 'Ivory Prince'
description: A clump-forming, evergreen perennial, to 40cm tall, with five-lobed, dark green leaves with silvery veining. The ivory-white, bowl-shaped flowers open from dark pink buds in late winter to mid-spring, developing pale green and pink flushing as they age

A clump-forming perennial to about 25cm high, forming a mound of lobed, dark purple, almost black leaves with lightly ruffled edges. Loose sprays of small white flowers emerge from pink buds, held on slender stems above the foliage in summer
An evergreen, tuftedperennial to 25cm tall with dense, arching, grass-like black leaves. Spikes of small, purple-flushed white flowers in summer are followed by shiny, blue-black berries in autumn

A ground-cover rose, 50-60cm high, with glossy dark green leaves and clusters of slightly scented semi-double flowers, 4-5cm across, with bright pink-red petals and golden stamens, repeat-flowering from midsummer to autumn; leaf-cutting bees may use rose leaves to make nests for their larvae

A clump-forming perennial to around 25cm tall with deeply-lobed, bright green leaves with white speckled variegation and prominent red veins. Leaves take on pink tones in the autumn. Whorls of pale pink-white flowers are borne on upright stems in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Rhododendron fortunei subsp. discolor var. kwangfuense

description: A prostrate, mat-forming evergreen alpine with fine, green needle-like leaves and star-shaped pure white flowers in spring and summer

A short-lived, perennial about 1m tall, forming an upright rosette of long, oval leaves with ginger hairs. In summer, erect leafy stems bear a small number of large, deep blue poppies with contrasting yellow stamens. The seed capsules, covered in bristly hairs, are decorative but contain little seed

A clump-forming perennial to around 1.5m in height, forming a rosette of upright, elliptic green leaves that are covered with dark brown hairs when young. In early to mid summer, tall leafy stems bear a succession of large clear blue flowers

A dense, dwarf, clump-forming, deciduous perennial to around 30cm in height, forming rosettes of lance-shaped, dark green bristly foliage. Lavender-purple, pincushion flowers appear on short stems above the foliage from July through to October, sometimes beyond if conditions are favourable
A compact, tufted, evergreen perennial to 20cm tall with grass-like, dark green leaves and erect stems topped with round clusters of rose pink flowers in spring and summer
A low-growing, evergreen perennial, forming a mound of lightly scented foliage to 15cm in height, with soft, silvery, finely-divided leaves. Small yellow flowers are sometimes produced in summer

A compact, mound-forming rhizomatous perennial, mid-green-lance-shaped leaves, branching stems bearing clusters of numerous multi-rayed vibrant violet-blue flowers with reddish-yellow centres from August to October. A naturally dwarf variety with good mildew resistance.

An upright, evergreen shrub to 3.5m tall. Glossy, oval leaves emerge bronze-red in colour and mature to dark green. Small to medium-sized, single, rose-red flowers appear in late winter to early spring. The candle-like red buds are a striking winter feature

A vigorous upright evergreen shrub, with glossy dark green, ovate leaves with serrated edges. Flowers are formal double, bright cerise pink with white streaks in the centres of the petals, and are produced in mid to late spring

primary_name: Calibrachoa [Dream Kisses Orange Sunset] ('Wescaosu') (Dream Kisses Series)
Lobelia erinus 'Waterfall Deep Blue With Eye' (Waterfall Series)
alternative_names: Lobelia erinus [Waterfall Deep Blue with Eye] (Waterfall Series)

primary_name: Lobelia erinus 'Waterfall Light Blue With Eye' (Waterfall Series)
description: A vigorous, branching annual up to 15cm x 30cm with semi-trailing stems and tiny, dark green leaves. Mid-blue flowers with a large, white eye are carried profusely in summer and autumn

A robust and compact, bushy, half-hardy perennial. Has small lance-shaped, toothed dark green leaves and terminal racemes of scented two-lipped tubular mid-purple and soft lilac flowers with a yellow protuberance in the centre from late spring to early autumn.

primary_name: Petunia 'Mini Me Pink Star' (Mini Me Series)

description: An upright, herbaceous perennial that produces green foliage with purple stems and leaf undersides. Striking racemes of pink flowers bloom from midsummer to early autumn, followed by purple-black fruit

primary_name: Aquilegia vulgaris var. stellata (Vervaeneana Group) 'Sweet Dreams' (d/v)
Aquilegia [Spring Magic Rose and Ivory] (Spring Magic Series)
alternative_names: columbine [Spring Magic Rose and Ivory]|Aquilegia 'Roses and Ivory'
description: Compact, clump-forming, short-lived herbaceous perennial to 40cm producing a basal mound of divided, blue-green leaves. Nodding, short-spurred flowers appear in late spring and early summer with light rose-pink outer petals and spurs and pale yellow inner petals

primary_name: Aquilegia vulgaris var. stellata 'Bordeaux Barlow' (Barlow Series) (d)
description: A short-lived perennial to 80cm with divided, dark green leaves. Nodding, spurless, double, pompom-like flowers with narrow, very dark red petals appear in late spring and early summer

A biennial or short-lived perennial to 1.2m high, with a basal rosette of green leaves. An 'orchid-flowered' cultivar, producing tall spikes of pendent, tubular flowers that are divided into fluted petals. Flowers are white flushed with lilac, with dark maroon markings in the throat

A biennial or short-lived clump-forming perennial to around 35cm in height, with semi-evergreen, lance-shaped grey-green divided leaves. Pale to dark blue flowers appear on stems above the foliage from mid-summer through to early autumn

alternative_names: blanketflower [Sunburst Burgundy Picotee]|Gaillardia × grandiflora 'Granretip'|Gaillardia aristata [Sunburst Red With Yellow Tip]
description: A compact, bushy, relatively short-lived perennial to 20cm, with bright green foliage. Large, daisy-like, dark red flowers, with a fine gold line round the petal tips, are borne on upright stems from early summer to early autumn
A peachy-orange flowered cultivar noted for its long flowering season from late spring to autumn. It reaches a height of 90cm. As a sterile selection, it will not self-seed

A clump-forming, strongly growing evergreen perennial with leathery, divided, blue-green leaves reaching up to 40cm high. The pale pink flower are carried on reddish-brown stems from mid-winter to spring, turning light green with age.

A vigorous, deciduous shrub, usually to about 1.5m high, though it can reach over 3m if unpruned. Strong dark red stems produce serrated green leaves that turn orange and red in autumn. Loose conical flower heads are produced from mid summer, with flowers opening white and developing to rose pink as they mature
A compact, bushy deciduous shrub with green foliage in spring which turns yellow-orange-red in autumn. Dark rose-pink flowers with crinkled petals are produced in large, terminal clusters in summer

A fast-growing, semi-evergreen shrub to around 2m high, with palmate grey-green leaves divided into 6-9 leaflets and silky-hairy beneath. Fragrant blue flowers are borne in upright spikes at the tips of the stems in late spring and summer

An evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 40cm in height, forming an architectural mound of large, caramel and bronzy leaves, covered in a fine layer of hair to give a shimmery appearance. Tall stems of cream flowers bloom over the summer

A compact, clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with lobed, bright golden leaves with red veins, changing to shades of caramel in winter. It produces white flowers on slender, erect stems in late spring and throughout summer.

A vigorous, mound-forming cultivar with rufffled, bright lime green to chartreuse leaves throughout the growing season. Clump to 45cm spread. Small white flowers on green stems are borne above the leaves in summer, to 40cm
A vigorous, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage and fragrant, soft pink flowers with a yellow eye appearing from spring to early summer
A clump-forming perennial with bright yellow feathery foliage boldly marked with deep red centre. Panicles of small white flowers in spring

A compact perennial forming a clump of maple-like, palmately-lobed burnt orange leaves, the main veins flushed with maroon. Colour deepens toward summer, pales somewhat in autumn and winter. Small white flowers are borne on stems to 50cm tall in spring and early summer

A compact, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 25cm high, forming a mound of deeply lobed, hairy green leaves marked with dark bronze. Long clusters of small, starry white flowers, opening from pale pink buds, are held on upright stems above the foliage in spring
A semi-evergreen perennial with mid green slender leaves and from summer to autumn deep purplish-red flowers with a white throat

A deciduous shrub to about 2m, the branches upright in their first year then arching over in bloom in their second. The flowers are very fragrant with white petals opening from a dark red calyx. The stems are red-brown in winter
A clump-forming, evergreen fern with arching, lance-shaped, bipinnate fronds, divided into glossy, toothed, oblong to ovate, dark green leaflets, yellow-green when young, green when mature.
A very early hybrid raspberry with black fruit. It has deciduous green leaves and small white flowers in late spring producing its harvest early to midsummer
A bushy, clump-forming perennial to around 80cm high, with upright stems and long, narrow, toothed dark green leaves. Tall spikes of soft pink flowers are produced from mid to late summer

A spreading, deciduous shrub to about 2m tall and wide, with oval, tapered dark green leaves variegated yellow or lime green, and funnel-shaped white flowers, produced during late spring and early summer

A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 120cm with mid-green foliage. Semi-double, velvety, fragrant dark raspberry-red flowers with ruffled, asymmetrical petals appear in late spring to early summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 80cm high, with divided green leaves. In early summer produces large, very fragrant, double red flowers to 18cm across, with a single bud on each stem

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 90cm high, with deeply divided, slightly glossy green leaves with wavy edges. Large, reddish pink double flowers, with broad outer petals surrounding a mass of ruffled inner petals, are produced in late spring and early summer. Inner petals are sometimes accented with yellow pollen at the edges

A bushy perennial, to around 75cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Lightly scented flowers open dusky reddish pink with raspberry pink flares at the base, and fade to pale pink and yellow

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 90cm high, with large, divided, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Large, semi-double soft pink flowers, paling slightly as they mature, are produced in late spring and early summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 1m high, with divided, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Rich pink, anemone-form flowers with creamy yellow centres are produced in late spring and early summer

A vigorous, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 90cm with dark green foliage. Single, rich yellow, crushed flowers with a thin red edge to the petals and golden stamens fade to cream and appear in late spring to early summer
A cultivar that produces light blue flowers, with orange stamens and stigma, in early spring

A bushy tender evergreen perennial, with small, rounded, lobed mid-green leaves. Produces abundant small single flowers to 3cm across, with deep pink upper petals and pale pink lower petals with deep pink veins, from late spring to early autumn

A bushy, upright perennial to around 80cm high, with aromatic, lance-shaped green leaves with serrated edges. Spikes of tubular, coral pink flowers open from purple-tinted buds from mid summer into early autumn
A tall perennial to around 90cm high, with aromatic, lance-shaped green leaves with serrated edges. Long spikes of tubular pink flowers open from red buds, from mid summer through to autumn
A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Single, pale lavender-blue flowers with yellow stamens appear in the spring

A herbaceous perennial and rather unusual variety with very rigid upright flower stems. Large clusters of small, pure white daisies are borne among pale green foliage during the late summer and autumn months. Needs no staking and is resistant to powdery mildews

A dense, twiggy, deciduous shrub to 1.5m tall, with slender stems and narrow golden-yellow leaves to 4cm in length. White flowers 6mm in width are borne in abundant small clusters along the branches in mid to late spring

A British-bred butternut squash, producing roughly bell-shaped fruits on trailing vines in excess of 1.8m (6ft) long. The small, smooth, pale orange, hard-skinned fruits, can be ready to harvest from early autumn into late autumn, making it ideally suited for growing in the shorter UK climate. They store well once ripe and have sweet, bright orange flesh with a nutty taste. They can reach around 700g (approximately (1½lbs) in weight.

A compact, clump-forming, summer-dormant bulbous perennial to around 15cm in height, with onion-scented narrow, dark green foliage. Delicate, fragrant star-shaped white flowers, flushed pale violet-blue, appear on upright stems in the spring

A hardy, clump-forming, architectural deciduous perennial with deeply divided blue-green foliage and large umbels of pink to white flowers which appear in early summer. Good for pollinating insects. Seed heads can be left over winter

primary_name: Crocosmia masoniorum from Satan's Nek, South Africa

description: forms clumps of foliage and from midsummer into autumn produces arching, branched flower stems bearing up to 30 large red flowers with orange-yellow throats

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.2m, with dark stems and mid-green foliage. Fully double flowers 12cm across, produced from mid-summer until the first frosts, have broad, very dark red petals with short notches at the tips

Tall, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to about 1m in height with toothed, dark green leaves. This semi-cactus form has a profusion of striking, fully double, pale pink flowers, becoming white at the tips, with long, pointed, dark raspberry flecked and striped petals, that bloom from midsummer until autumn

A bushy, compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 80cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Double, lilac-pink flowers streaked with purple-red, appear from summer through until the first frosts

A compact, clump-forming bulbous perennial heritage daffodil to around 30cm in height, with green strap-like foliage. Fragrant, neat and symmetrical, rose-like double golden yellow flowers appear from March to April. Suitable for naturalising
A viridiflora tulip reaching 40cm, with pale green, lance-shaped leaves and yellow flowers with a central green flare on each petal

An small to medium, evergreen tree or large shrub, reaching around 12m in height. The leaves are green above, emerging pale and downy and remaining so on their lower surface. They have a rounded shape with slightly serrated edges at first, followed by longer, smooth-edged leaves as they mature. Acorns have a cup with long shaggy scales..

Compact, clump-forming perennial to around 30cm tall with lance-shaped leaves. Yellow flowers with a deep rosy-pink blotch at the tips of the petals and dark streaks on the inner petals are borne from summer into autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 30cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of yellow, funnel-shaped flowers, the petals striped and tipped red, with dark brown speckles on the inner petals, appearing in summer and autumn

Compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial, to 30cm tall and wide, with lance-shaped, dark green foliage. Magenta-pink funnel-shaped flowers, with yellow throats and dark red flecks are borne in open, terminal clusters from summer to mid-autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial, to 30cm tall, with lance-shaped dark green leaves. Peach-orange flowers, with yellow throats and dark reddish-brown streaks and flecking on the inner petals, are borne from summer into autumn

An deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers in the summer. These are almost black in bud, opening to dark blue-purple.
A rhizomatous perennial to 1m tall with glaucous leaves; flowers have deep purple-blue falls, white standards and golden-yellow beards

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled, slightly fragrant creamy-white flowers, white and blue falls and yellow beards with a white base appear from late spring to early summer

A dainty, clump-forming, miniature perennial, with small, rounded blue-green leaves that have broad creamy-white margins. Violet-purple, bell-shaped flowers are borne on upright stems, around 20cm high, in summer
A sport of 'Blue Mouse Ears'. A compact Hosta producing thick blue-green leaves with a creamy-white centre. Pale lavender-coloured flowers appear on short, upright stems during the summer

A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 50cm high, with broadly ovate, textured green leaves with a silvery-blue waxy sheen. Produces loose clusters of bell-shaped pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A large, vigorous, clump-forming deciduous perennial with crisp, puckered, thick blue foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with green foliage and yellow margins. Upright stems of fragrant, lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer. A reverse sport of H. 'Guacamole'
A giant, clump-forming deciduous perennial with deeply veined blue-green foliage and wavy margins. Upright stems of pale, lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

primary_name: Gladiolus scullyi from Ceres Karoo, South Africa
Hypoxis obtusa from Harrismith, South Africa
Hypoxis rigidula from Harrismith, South Africa
Lachenalia zebrina f. densiflora from Tanqua

description: A semi-evergreen, upright, tall and bushy perennial which has green, long, lance-shaped leaves and whorls of long tubular velvety pink flowers that are often curved in late summer and autumn.

primary_name: Ornithogalum multifolium from Loeriesfontein, South Africa
Romulea cruciata var. cruciata from Riverlands
Romulea flava var. minor from Dassenberg
Romulea hirsuta var. cuprea from Rawsonville
Romulea hirsuta var. hirsuta from Klipheuwel
Romulea hirsuta var. zeyheri from Malmesbury
Romulea rosea var. rosea from Caledon
Romulea setifolia var. aggregata from Rawsonville

description: A medium-sized epiphytic orchid, producing a clump of pseudobulbs (thickened stem on base of each growth) which serve as a storage organ for water and nutrients. Measuring 10cm across, each flower is white or pale yellow, with two dark spots in the centre. The flowers of this orchid have evolved in a very unique way - to perfectly mimic and deceive their pollinator. Downwards facing flowers are pollinated by male Euglossine bees (also known as Orchid Bees) that confuse the flowers for females. The flowers are short-lived, lasting only 2-4 days, but large plants produce many inflorescences that flower in succession.

A perennial bulb, to around 40cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves and crimson coloured flowers

A vigorous, umbrella-shaped deciduous tree with serrated-edge leaves. Foliage emerges pinkish-green, then changes to lime-green. pale green then finally to bright red during the autumn. An ideal variety for attractive all-year round interest, and best suited to large gardens or parks
A white wine grape variety that is a cross between the French Cabernet Sauvignon grape and a disease-resistant hybrid grape. The grape was developed in 1991 by Swiss grape breeder Valentin Blattner

An evergreen, free-flowering cultivar with a green-grey mat of linear foliage and erect flower stems to 35cm. The highly-scented, double flowers, with fringed petals, are salmon-pink with a darker band of colour near the deep pink eye and are borne from late spring into summer
A fast-maturing annual dwarf french bean with green leaves and white flowers, producing a very heavy crop of slender beans.

A deciduous tree to 20m high, with a compact, conical crown and toothed, rounded green leaves with pointed tips, turning yellow in autumn. Free-flowering, producing clusters of up to 36 scented, pale yellow flowers in midsummer
A green-leaved cultivar to 1.2m tall bearing sugar pink, small double blooms to 10cm across from summer into autumn

Tall, upright, clump-forming, tuberous perennial about 1.2m in height, with serrated dark green leaves. Large, warm apricot, fully double Waterlily form flowers fading to pale peach at the edges of the petals, bloom profusely on upright stems from midsummer until the first frosts of autumn

A dwarf ground cover rose of compact growth, about 45cm tall and 60cm wide, with healthy dark green leaves, and softly cupped, fully double pale peach blooms to 4cm wide, crowding the arching stems from mid-spring to the first frosts of autumn

A medium-sized, free-flowering climber to around 2.5m. The large flowers, up to 15cm across,with six to eight light purple petals, a faint rose-pink bar and white stamens, are produced in late spring to early summer and again from late summer to early autumn

A bulbous perennial to 15cm with narrow, grey-green leaves and slender flowers, the inner petals marked with a green X, paler towards the base, in early to mid-winter
A clump-forming, bulbous perennial with broadly strap-shaped, greyish-green leaves and relatively large flowers with white outer segments and green inner segments with a thin white strip at theedges

A bulbous perennial with grey-green leaves, flowering in winter to 15cm high. Outer petals have green veining along their length and are tipped green. Inner segments are almost completely green with narrow, white edges

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Mature bulbs will usually produce two flowers each once established, though only the larger flower will have markings on the outer petals

A clump-forming, bulbous perennial with grey-green leaves and large, mid-seasonflowers borne on upright stems to 16cm tall. Flowers have white, ridged outer petals and inner petals marked top and bottom with well-defined zones of green

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 80cm, with mid-green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The blooms have neat rows of tightly inrolled, light peach-pink petals, forming a flattened ball 8-10cm across
A bulbous perennial with dark green leafy stems to 2m, bearing large, outward-facing dark red flowers in summer.

A bulbous perennial, to around 110cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, downward-facing, lightly fragrant dark red flowers, with white edges and tips to the petals and brown blotches, are produced in July

A perennial bulb with broadly ovate green leaves. This tulip has goblet-shaped flowers, with pointed petals that are pale primrose yellow, with deeper yellow at the margins. Flowers are produced in mid to late spring, and stand to around 55cm high
A perennial bulb with pale green, lance-shaped leaves. The flowers have narrow, pointed, reflexed petals, golden yellow at the base shading to red, reach about 45cm tall and appear in late spring

A dwarf, bulbous perennial to 40cm tall, with green foliage and flowers which are soft apricot to pink with a hint of lilac, opening in the sunshine to reveal a darker apricot inside with creamy-yellow to white edges and a black base, appearing in early to late April

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 120cm in height, with green serrated leaves. Upward-facing, single very pale pink flowers, with dark red and yellow centres, appear on tall, dark red stems from July through to October

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with dark stems and mid-green foliage. Relatively small (10cm), vivid orange flowers, with slightly incurved petals giving a neat shape, are produced from mid-summer until the first frost

primary_name: Dahlia [Happy Single Date] ('HS Date') (Happy Single Series) (Sin)
alternative_names: dahlia [Happy Single Date]|Dahlia 'Dark Leaf Date'|Dahlia 'HS Date' (Happy Single Series)
description: Grows to 60-70cm high, with dark red-green leaves, dark red stems, and single flowers, 5-10cm across, from summer to autumn; the outer circle of ray florets are pale orange with darker orange-red at their bases, forming an orange-red ring around the dark brown and golden centres
A deciduous, spreading tree or large shrub with large, lbed leaves and producing good crops of edible fruits that ripen to greenish-yellow in autumn with strawberry-red flesh
A trailing, semi-evergreen variety with distinct pink flowers in spring followed by glossy, bright red fruits in summer and autumn

A bright and colourful, perennial coneflower variety producing flowers with a single row of pale pink, reflexed outer petals surrounding shorter, double, deep pink inner petals. Perfect as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A compact, clump-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial producing very ruffled peach to amber foliage. White flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer. A good choice for the front of a border or for pots and containers
A herbaceous perennial, up to 1m high, with red stems, aromatic, pale olive-green leaves and abundant, citrus-scented, rich pink flowers with darker pink calyces from midsummer to autumn

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 64cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and red-cherry-pink coloured flowers with cream mid-ribs above a green throat to 11cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and rose-pink coloured flowers that have a tangerine-orange throat to 9cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and fragrant, salmon-gold coloured flowers with a burgundy eye-zone above a green throat to 17cm across in summer

alternative_names: butterfly bush [Buzz Magenta]|Buddleja davidii 'Tobudpipur'|Buddleja davidii [Buzz Pink Purple] (Buzz Series)

A short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 40cm, with very dark green foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers have one or two rows of yellow petals with darker veins, and a dark yellow central disc
A compact evergreen perennial, to around 20cm high, with narrow, deep green leaves. Produces fragrant, deep red flowers with fine white edges, from late spring to late summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 20cm, with soft hairy, deeply lobed, dark green leaves. New spring leaves have a maroon tint as they open and turn orange-The veined lilac-pink flowers bloom freely through the summer

A semi-evergreen perennial to around 40cm tall and one of the hardier cultivars. Its dark green, lobed and broadly lance-shaped foliage forms a basal rosette; crimson daisy-like flowers are borne above the foliage from spring until the first frosts

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a rounded, spreading habit and oval-shaped, variegated grey-green foliage, turning dark red to purple in the autumn. Luminescent green flowers (bracts) turning to creamy-white, appear early to mid-summer, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn
A compact, mound forming, evergreen sub-shrub with small, narrow, lance shaped, aromatic, mid-green leaves and clusters of whorled pink flowers in summer
A compact bulbous perennial to 20cm tall with erect, narrow, grey-green foliage. Deep purple to blue flowers with white marked purple-black falls are borne from late winter to early spring
An evergreen, perennial forming low, tight mounds or compact mats made up of rosettes of small leaves. In spring, short stems bear an abundance of small white flowers just above the leaf rosettes

A clump-forming deciduous perennial with narrow, glossy, wavy-edged leaves, that are bright mid green in the centres, and cream to yellow along the margins. Produces loose clusters of tubular, pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with rippled, heart-shaped blue-green foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, fast-growing, clump-forming deciduous perennial with green foliage and wavy margins. Upright, dark red stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with glossy, variegated yellow-green foliage and green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer. A sport of Hosta 'Sum and Substance'
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with yellow foliage and green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A clump-forming deciduous perennial to around 60cm in height, with large, rounded, yellow leaves. Tall, elegant stems of white flowers sparkle in July and August
A medium, clump-forming perennial with bright yellow, rippled foliage and purple-red stems. Upright stems of purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with bright, yellow-green foliage. Upright, dark red stems of purple flowers appear in summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with blue foliage and green-yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with dark blue-green foliage and creamy-white centres. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with glossy, dark green, deeply ridged foliage with wavy edges. Upright stems of fragrant, pale lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A medium, clump-forming perennial with thick, chartreuse to yellow foliage with a dark green margin. The colour becomes brighter when exposed to more sunlight. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, narrow, variegated blue-green foliage with a thin, creamy-yellow line in the centre. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 25cm high, with thick, slightly cupped, ovate blue-green leaves with a creamy yellow streak in the centre. Produces loose clusters of tubular pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 35cm high, with thick, broadly ovate, lightly cupped dark green leaves, with a central streak of pale yellow fading to white. Produces loose clusters of tubular, pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with intense blue foliage with wavy edges. Pale lavender-purple flowers appear on upright stems in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with deeply ridged green foliage and wavy edges. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A slow-growing, medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated lime green foliage and white margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer. Performs better if grown in a pot for the first couple of years

A giant, clump-forming deciduous perennial with very large, textured dark green foliage with yellow margins. The leaves turn a lighter shade as the season progresses. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
An ornamental annual pepper with bushy dark green pointed leaves and white flowers which are followed by masses of medium-hot purple fruits with an orange blush which fade to red towards to autumn
A slow-growing, deciduous variety which can be grown as a small tree or shrub. It's featheryleaves are purpleto reddish during the summer, turning to bright orange and red during the autumn.

A slow-growing small tree or shrub, particularly suited to beds and borders or containers and as a specimen plant. Bronze-tinted foliage turns green with red tips in the spring, changing to orangey-red in the autumn.

A New Zealand-bred, very floriferous hybrid to around 2m in height, with dark green, glossy foliage and an upright, columnar habit. Single, miniature flowers to around 4.5cm across are pale pink with darker pink flashes on some petals, and a neat, upright ring of golden anthers inside, appearing from March to April

A large evergreen shrub with glossy, ovate dark green leaves with a fine, delicate texture and serrated edges. Free-flowering, producing large, lightly scented, single pink flowers in late autumn and winter

A woody, evergreen, twining climber about 3m in height, with oval, glossy, yellow leaves, 5cm long, edged green and flushed orange-red in summer on new leaves and in winter, and bearing sweetly-scented, creamy-white flowers in mid and late summer that fade to pale yellow with age

A very hot Habanero type chilli pepper cultivar growing around 70cm tall, producing small tapering fruits generally 2.5-4cm long ripening from green to pale orange. Wear gloves when handling the fruit
A herbaceous perennial to around 60cm tall and 45cm spread. The large daisy flowerheads are orange-yellow and as they mature they gradually develop a pinkish-salmon hue

Bushy upright rose about 90cm tall, with dark green glossy foliage, and bearing fragrant, deep, crimson-red ruffled blooms with a smoky, velvet sheen to the reverse of the petals, flowering repeatedly throughout summer
A herbaceous perennial, up to 60cm high, with green, lance-shaped leaves and scented, white flowers with a green eye in midsummer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 86cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, deep velvety-red flowers that have a green-yellow throat to 18cm across in summer

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to about 45cm with sycamore-shaped leaves that are dark green and silver above, and dark red below with dark red stems. It rarely flowers

A compact, trailing, low-growing variety with loose-cascading white flowers with deep blue edging from summer through until early autumn
A bushy, upright annual producing very dark purple-black flowers up to 5cm across from early summer until the frosts

A low-growing, evergreen perennial about 10cm in height, producing dense mounds of small, hairy grey-green leaves, and deep pink, double flowers with a yellow-green eye, produced in short spikes through spring

Clump-forming, deciduous grass, to 2m tall, with upright stems and narrow, arching mid-green leaves which turn red and gold in autumn, fading to pale reddish-brown in winter. A clump-forming daffodil, to around 25cm high, with grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are scented, to 7cm across, with swept-back yellow petals and a long, narrow yellow cup

Compact perennial to 60cm tall, with semi-evergreen basal rosettes and strong stems holding slender, glossy, mid-green leaves and abundant bright red tubular flowers with white splashed throats, through summer
A slow-growing dwarf tree to approximately 5m. The leaves are green and have symmetrical pointed lobes and they turn orange and red in autumn before falling

A tuberous perennial with long stalked, deeply lobed darl green leaves and branched flowers stems with one to four double deep purple double flowers in spring and early summer.

A deciduous ornamental grass to about 40cm forming mounds of arching, ribbon-like foliage in bright green with fine cream stripes. Flowers are insignificant
An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 70cm high with lance-shaped leaves and fragrant, purple, white-eyed flowers borne in terminal heads from late summer

A herbaceous perennial, up to 60cm high, with green, lance-shaped leaves and scented, vivid dark pink flowers in midsummer
A herbaceous perennial, up to 60cm high, with green, lance-shaped leaves and scented, vivid purple-pink flowers from dark buds in midsummer

Scented pale pink trumpet-shaped flowers are borne in clusters from early summer to mid autumn

A bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with upright stems, woody at the base, and dark green foliage. Very large, white flowers with a large red eye and white stamens, appear from July through to September
A perennial to 70cm tall bearing flattened heads of small orange-red to dark pink flowers with yellow centres in summer and autumn held above the divided silvery-grey to green foliage

Evergreen perennial groundcover plant producing pale green spoon-shaped leaves edged and splashed creamy-yellow, the leaves infused with rose-pink in cooler weather. Short spikes of blue flowers appear in mid to late spring

An erect, herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular soft pale-lilac flowers with a pink-purple eye over a long period of time in summer.

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with frilly deep lilac-blue flowers and a lime-green eye in summer.

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 1m in height, with rosettes of dark green, hairy leaves and tall, well-branched stems bearing apricot-pink flowers from late spring until late summer

An upright, perennial coneflower variety producing attractive double blooms with narrow, recurved, cream-white petals surrounding a green flushed, pale pink central cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An upright perennial, to 1m high, with thin, lance-shaped green leaves. Large, rounded clusters of pale pink flowers with contrasting dark pink eyes are produced in midsummer
A dwarf, evergreen, alpine shrub with a tufted habit and mid-green leaves. Purple and yellow pea shaped flowers are produced in the spring and summer.

A compact, evergreen perennial forming a low mound of finely cut, silvery-green foliage. In spring and summer, it produces daisy-like, pink flowerheads on softly hairy stems to 30cm tall. Grow in a sunny rock garden, raised bed or in a container

A semi-evergreen, bushy perennial with mid-green, small oval fragrant leaves and pale pink lipped flowers from summer to autumn.
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy sub shrub with aromatic green foliage and creamy-yellow lipped flowers from summer through to autumn.

description: A tender evergreen subshrub, often grown as an annual, forming a mound of lobed and divided, grey-green foliage to around 40cm high. Deep crimson daisy-like flowers with yellow centres are borne above the foliage from late spring until early autumn

primary_name: Nemesia [Sunsatia Plus Cherry on Ice] ('Innemcheoi') (Sunsatia Plus Series)

An upright, compact perennial some times grown as an annual, with lance-shaped silvery green foliage, hairy on the reverse, and spikes of dark blue lipped flowers in summer and autumn.
An upright, compact perennial sometimes grown as an annual, with lance-shaped silvery green foliage, hairy on the reverse, and spikes of pale blue lipped flowers in summer and autumn.

A cordon cherry tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces reliable crops of long, cascading fruit trusses with uniform, round, red cherry type fruit

A collection of mound-forming perennials growing to around 15cm tall and 30cm wide with small, toothed leaves. Depending on the mix of cultivars, they may include single, bi or tri-coloured flowers in varying shades of blue, purple, orange and yellow, with or without central dark or white markings and darker veins

primary_name: Viola × wittrockiana [Frizzle Sizzle Mix] (Frizzle Sizzle Series) (P)
description: A compact, clump-forming evergreen perennial often grown as an annual, with dark green, scalloped-edged leaves. Single, fragrant flowers with wavy edges in shades of white, blues, purples, yellows and reds appear from Autumn into Spring

A compact deciduous climber to 1.5m in height. Single flowers, 12cm in width, are bright pink with a darker pink stripe down the middle of the petals and golden stamens. Flowers in early summer to early autumn

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm, with dark stems and unusual, purple-flushed, grey-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frost produces double flowers with pointed, dark red petals fading to pale pink at the tips

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 50cm, with dark bronze foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers have broad, rounded, bright pink petals with a red inner ring and a yellow central disc

A hardy, evergreen shrub with an upright habit and dark green foliage. Double, deep cerise red flowers on long spikes appear from summer through to autumn.
A low-growing, spreading variety with small golden-yellow leaves which change to shades of gold, orange and bronze during the winter. Lavender-pink flowers are produced from mid-winter to mid-spring
A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Funnel-shaped deep pink flowers are borne over a long period from late spring into autumn

A compact, clump-forming perennial, to around 25cm high in flower, with lobed and toothed green leaves. Bright orange-red flowers are borne on leafy stems from late spring to midsummer
A large, fast-growing evergreen shrub with bright mid-green, leathery, broadly oval leaves. Flowers are yellow-green and very small and inconspicuous

A medium-sized, upright tree, with stripey, yellow and green young shoots in winter, white blossom in spring, and shiny, oval leaves. Not self-fertile, in pollination group 3

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and pale pinky-cream flowers with a multi-banded pink eye-zone above a chrartreuse-green throat to 11cm across in summer
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 75cm in height, forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and grey lavender flowers with a purple centre and a green throat 15cm across in summer.
A deciduous herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped arching green leaves and large, near white-cream flowers with a yellow green throat. Some petals are reflexed and curled

alternative_names: eryngo from Roger Grounds|sea holly from Roger Grounds

description: A spreading, clump-forming, floriferous rhizomatous perennial with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Frilly, open, pale pink flowers appear from April to mid May
A slow-growing, spreading, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Single bright orange flowers appear on upright stems in the spring

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 91cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and very large, fragrant, salmon-pink flowers with a pale yellow throat to 25cm across in summer

A terrestrial orchid that has soft, folded bright green leaves 5-20cm long. In summer it bears pale reddish-brown flowers 9cm long with twisted petals and a large, pale yellow pouch-shaped lip, growing singly or in pairs on upright stems to 40cm high.
A solitary, evergreen cactus with glowing, pinkish radial spines curved slightly towards the stem. Large, dark pink flowers with a yellow throat, appear in the spring

A very hot Habanero chilli pepper producing small 2.5-4cm long fruits which mature from pale green to orange to red. The peppers have a delicate smoky and fruity flavour and the heat intensifies as they mature. Harvest July to October

A reasonably compact, climbing cultivar, growing to around 1.8m (6ft) high and producing prolific crops of mini cucumbers which are smooth-skinned, sweet and free of bitterness. It is an all female variety, producing fruits without the need for pollination, which means every flower is capable of producing a fruit. This cultivar is well suited to being grown outdoors in summer in the UK, as well as in the greenhouse.

A disease-resistant courgette with a bushy habit, producing excellent yields of bright yellow round fruit with a thin skin, the flesh described as thick, creamy and meaty. Harvest when the fruit is about 10cm in diameter
A tapered carrot which reaches 25cm long. It has green feathery leaves and a distinctly red root which is retained when cooked
A plant usually grown as an annual for its edible taproot. This cultivar produces tapering roots up to 18cm long with purple skins and bright orange cores

A compact, annual, deciduous vegetable to around 18cm in height, producing golden yellow tender roots with a sweeter flavour than the traditional orange variety. Sow this maincrop variety outdoors from April to June for harvesting from June to November. Great for roasting

A very dwarf pea to 45cm. It has green leaves and climbs using tendrils, because it is so compact, it doesn't need support. The flowers are white and develop into pods containing a good crop of peas in summer. It is an annual which lives for one summer but this variety can be sown in autumn for an earlier start in spring.
A short climbing bean with green leaves and mauve flowers producing an early crop of green fruit with black beans inside
An old facourite, cordon, salad tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces reliable crops of medium sized red salad tomatoes
A cordon beefsteak tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces large, ribbed, beefsteak tomatoes with deep red and purple skin and flesh. Excellent for slicing and grilling
A cordon cherry tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces reliable crops of long, cascading fruit trusses with small, round, red cherry tomatoes which are very sweet

A bushy perennial, grown as an annual vegetable for its edible tubers. A first early potato that has remained popular since the 1940's. Oval tubers have pale skin with firm, creamy white flesh, suitable for boiling, baking, roasting, frying and mashing. An all-rounder with good flavour

First introduced in 1879, these potatoes are still sought after today for their sublime texture, thin skins and rich, buttery flavour. When grown on the island of Jersey these potatoes are better known as 'Jersey Royals'. Traditionally known as an early maincrop, it is usually grown (and sold in the supermarkets) as a new, second early or salad potato. Makes a great all-round variety

These baby sweetcorn are easy to grow and great for a smaller plot. This variety produces about five sweet, crunchy baby sweetcorn per plant. Harvest them as soon as the silks appear and the tassels darken (about 10cm long) to avoid pollination. Delicious steamed or raw and much better than shop bought! Sow indoors: March to May. Sow / plant outdoors: May to June. Harvest: July to October

A clump-forming, spreading deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial to around 15cm. Fern-like, divided leaves are dark green to almost black. Pale, lemon yellow flowers appear in the spring. A hybrid of nemorosa (wood anemone) and ranunculoides (yellow anemone)

primary_name: Salvia fulgens from Mount Popocatépetl, Mexico

description: A smaller cultivar, moisture-loving, upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with mid-green, slightly sticky lance-shaped fragrant leaves and short spikes of sky-blue blue lipped flowers from late summer to autumn.

A clump-forming, rhizomatous perennial to around 45cm high in flower, with a spreading habit and simple, downy green leaves. Flowers from late spring through the summer, with slender stems bearing buds encased in overlapping bracts, which open to large, showy dark reddish-purple flowers, with a ring of fine outer florets surrounding a crowd of tiny, near-black flowers in the centre

A low, spreading herbaceous perennial to 30cm in height, with trailing stems bearing 5-lobed leaves. Flowers are saucer-shaped, rich violet-blue with a large white central zone and dark veins to 3cm in width. They bloom from June to October and gradually fade to magenta
A strongly upright, spreading perennial to about 80cm, with bright green, aromatic foliage and large, blue-violet flowers in short spikes from mid-summer to early autumn

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and red flowers with a yellow-green throat to 15cm across in summer

Deciduous, multi-branched, shrubby tree about 5m tall, bearing red young shoots, and small, 5-7 lobed leaves 3-6cm long, with coarsely-toothed margins. Young leaves are bright pinkish-red, the colour lasting into summer when they mature to green, then orange-red tones of varying intensity in autumn.

A robust, clump-forming perennial with rounded, deeply toothed, grey-green basal leaves, and upright, branched stems bearing deeply-lobed, silvery-green spiny leaves and small, silvery-white terminal flowerheads above narrow, spiny bracts 2.5cm long, in summer and early autumn
A perennial bulb to 20cm in height with prostrate green leaves. The scented flowers are upright and vivid gold-yellow in early spring
A palm-like shrub or small tree with bright green to greyish-green, arching leaves. Mature plants may produce scented, white flowers in rounded clusters followed by berries
A slow-growing dwarf conifer, up to 50cm high in 10 years, with a low, spreading habit and stiff, dark green needles that are bright green when young

A narrow, conical, evergreen conifer with upright branches and glossy dark green, short needles with silver undersides. Has a narrow pyramidal shape when young but becoming more conical with age, reaching a height of 3-4m x 1m wide.
A small, deciduous, vase-shaped tree about 3m tall, with a willow-like appearance, the long, slender, slightly incised 5-lobed purplish-red leaves, turn fiery orange and red in autumn

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial reaching up to 1.2m tall. Its large, compound leaves emerge golden-yellow in spring and maintain their gold colour when exposed to sun for a few hours each day. Tiny white flowers are borne on spikes up to 60cm tall in late summer, forming inedible purple berries in the autumn

A compact, clump-forming, bushy deciduous perennial to around 45cm in height, with rosettes of dark green, veined leaves. Clusters of small, lavender-purple flowerheads with spikey purple bracts appear on strong stems, in mid to late summer. This compact variety is ideal for pots and containers or in a rock or alpine garden

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 30cm tall, with lance-shaped, aromatic, mid- to dark green foliage. From mid-summer to early autumn each upright stem carries a whorl of two-lipped, tubular, light rose-pink flowers with a dark centre

A deciduous clump-forming perennial with upright dark green to bronze stems and leaves divided into numerous oblong to ovate, blue-green leaflets. Panicles of lilac blue to pale purple flowers are displayed in summer.

A vigorous tuberous perennial, up to 50cm high, with asymmetric, bright lime green crinkled leaves with prominent veining, finely toothed edges and pinkish-red undersides. Loose, hanging sprays of slightly fragrant, pale pink flowers are borne on long, reddish stems in late summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled, fragrant dark purple-black flowers, white falls with a purple edge and dark purple-black beards appear from late spring to early summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Dark maroon-red ruffled flowers, veined on the falls, with bright golden yellow beards appear from late spring to early summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, lightly fragrant, ruffled, dark purple to dark purple-black flowers with burnt orange beards, appearing from late spring to early summer

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves. Large, ruffled creamy-white flowers, white, yellow and bright purple falls and bright yellow beards with white tips appear from late spring to early summer

a variegated, evergreen shrub to around 1.2m in height. New foliage is flushed red in spring and is green and yellow-edged the rest of the year. Small, scented, tubular flowers are white with a hint of pink; these are borne over a long season through summer

A tough, tufted, evergreen perennial to 30cm tall, forming dense clumps of linear, dark green leaves. From early to late autumn, purple stems bear long, dense spikes of lavender-purple flowers. A useful plant for dry shade

primary_name: Hydrangea macrophylla 'Black Steel Zambia' (Black Steel Series) (H)
description: A compact, rounded, deciduous shrub to about 1m, with broadly oval, rich green foliage and almost black stems. Domed flower heads bear clusters of flowers emerging lime green, and developing to deep pink over the summer. Colours will vary depending on the pH of the soil.

An upright perennial, to around 70cm high, with thin, lance-shaped green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant flowers are produced in summer, with dark pink tubes and white faces with pink central eyes

A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Funnel-shaped, cerise pink flowers, with darker flecks on the upper petals, are borne over a long period from late spring into autumn
Compact, clump-forming perennial about 30-40cm tall, with dark green, lance shaped leaves, and clusters of white funnel-shaped flowers with a coral-pink throat, appearing in summer and autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 20-30cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of lilac-pink, funnel-shaped flowers which have dark brown speckles and a creamy white throat on the upper petals in summer and autumn.

Clump-forming perennial about 30cm tall, with lance-shaped mid-green leaves, and coral-pink funnel-shaped flowers, the inner petals streaked and speckled crimson, the two uppermost petals marked with golden-yellow at the base, flowering from midsummer to autumn

primary_name: Anemone × hybrida 'Pretty Lady Diana' (Pretty Lady Series)
description: Compact, deciduous perennial, reaching 60cm in height with mid-green foliage and branching stems bearing single flowers in mixed shades of rose-pink, with a central boss of yellow stamens, bloom through summer and early autumn

A clump-forming perennial to around 1.2m high, with branching stems bearing narrow green leaves. Flowers are large, with broad, overlapping golden yellow petals around a brown central cone, and are produced from late summer into autumn

A slow-spreading, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial with bright green fern-like leaves and upright long, slim spikes of dark red bottlebrush flowers which appear from summer through until the autumn
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are mid pink and spider shaped with a darker pink eye and green-yellow throat
A dwarf, evergreen conifer reaching a height and spread of 50cm in ten years with soft, green, spirally-arranged, awl-shaped leaves
A short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 50cm, with mid-green foliage. Neatly rounded flowers, 12cm across, are yellow with a touch of tangerine, and produced from mid-summer to the first frost
An evergreen clump-forming herbaceous perennial with mid-green strap-shaped arching stems. Flowers have ruffled edges, cream green in colour with a green throat

description: An upright, bushy shrub to 3m tall with deep purple to red, double flowers borne from late summer into early autumn
A small, upright tree to about 4m, with single, pink and white flowers in late spring to early summer, followed by large, glossy, bright red fruits with red flesh that are good for jelly-making
A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 65cm tall with dark green divided leaves. Fragrant, rich pink, anemone-type flowers with red-tipped stamens are borne from mid to late spring
A vigorous, clump-forming bulbous perennial daffodil, with green strap-like foliage and broad white petals and frilly orange cup, appearing in mid April

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, lightly fragrant, ruffled, pale to dark beetroot-red flowers with a yellow-orange blush at the sides of the petals and rust beard. Flowers appear from late spring to early summer
A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 80cm with dark green foliage. Strong, upright stems with double, dark pink flowers appear in late spring to early summer

A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 80cm with dark green foliage. Large, double, dark rose-pink flowers with a slight silver flush appearing on the outer edges of the petals, appear in late spring to early summer

An upright, bushy, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with slim, dark green leaves with serrated edges. In summer, strong, upright stems produce masses of large, fragrant, semi-double white flowers with golden-yellow centres
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 90cm high, with divided, deep green leaves. Semi-double, deep reddish pink flowers are produced in late spring and early summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to 80cm tall, with dark green, divided foliage and fragrant, fully double, very pale apricot-pink flowers in early summer
A hardy, evergreen shrub with yellow foliage that is tinted orange in winter and lavender coloured flowers in Summer.
A hardy, evergreen shrub to around 30cm in height with dark green foliage. Mauve-pink flowers appear from August to November

An upright shrub to about 1m, with tiny, needle-like, mid-green leaves in well-spaced whorls of four. Small, terminal clusters of pale pink, urn-shaped flowers with dark red anthers appear between autumn and early spring
A low-growing, evergreen shrub to around 20cm tall with mid-green foliage and clear pink flowers borne from winter into spring

A dwarf shrub with a compact habit, forming a low mound 15cm high, with leaves which are deep golden in summer and lime-green in winter, and lilac-pink flowers which deepen to magenta pink, and dark brown anthers, from early to late spring; most Erica species and cultivars are excellent plants for all types of bees
A compact, evergreen shrub up to 20cm and 30cm wide, with tiny, narrow, dark green leaves. Short sprays of small rose-pink urn-shaped flowers are produced in summer

A dwarf shrub with a broad, spreading, compact habit, forming a low mound 40cm high, with golden-yellow leaves which become yellow-green in winter, and white flowers with brown anthers, from early winter to late spring; most Erica species and cultivars are excellent plants for all types of bees
A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 40cm high, forming a mound of lobed green leaves mottled with dark bronze. Very pale pink flowers are produced over a long period from early summer

A clump-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial producing large, showy, ruffled apricot-orange to dark golden foliage. Creamy flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer
A medium-sized deciduous tree to 10m. Its lower branches hang downwards in a slight weeping form. It has glossy deep green leaves which turn red, orange and yellow in autumn
A medium-sized deciduous tree to 10m. It has glossy green leaves which turn bright orange in autumn

Compact, deciduous tree that can reach a height of 6m, with an upright habit and a narrow, columnar crown. Maple-like, dark green, palmate leaves are 5-lobed and turn yellow-orange to red in autumn. Small yellow-green flowers appear in spring followed by spiky, brown fruits after flowering
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage and fragrant, pale orange to yellow flowers appearing in the spring
Plants produce feathery spikes of flowers in 'earth' colours such as rust-red, orange, brown and cream, in summer and autumn. Some seed mixtures may have a preponderance of pale colours

A frost-tender, tuberous evergreen perennial to 1.2m tall, producing striking, heart-shaped, emerald-green leaves with a paler green centre and midrib. A stunning foliage plant, perfect as a houseplant or can be grown outside in containers in a frost-free, sheltered location
An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.5m with large, broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. White to salmon-pink flowers, fragrant both day and evening, appear from late summer through to October

primary_name: Cypripedium parviflorum subsp. parviflorum var. planipetalum

description: Quite a short tulip, often less than 25cm, with cup-shaped white flowers, the outer tepals with a broad yellow flame and fine yellow spreading lines
A distinctive tulip 40-45cm tall, bright yellow with bright red edges to the outer tepals, which are slightly notched at the apex
An early-flowering variety with huge, silky, bright red flowers. The foliage is mottled with deep red spots and stripes.

A dwarf, early-flowering tulip to 30cm tall, with broad grey-green leaves marked reddish-purple and bearing large, bowl-shaped, white flowers with a deep pink stripe on the middle of each petal and orange-yellow centres, in early spring
A bulbous perennial with grey-green leaves and pale pink, single flowers held erect on stems up to 30cm tall

A striking bulbous perennial with brightly coloured, large flowers held to 30cm above boldly mottled green and purple foliage. Outer tepals are yellow with bold red stripes up the central spine and into the pointed apex. Inside the flower is orange and yellow. Early spring
A short, sturdy tulip, to 20cm, with stiff, grey-green foliage and wide flowers. Tepals are a rich yellow throughout. Mid spring

A low-growing, spreading, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 45cm in height, with basal rosettes of lobed, toothed, unusually crinkly dark green leaves. Large, cup-shaped double peach-yellow flowers flushed with pink appear from April to June and then again for a second flush in the autumn

A herbaceous perennial about 35cm high with mid-green pinnate leaves of lobed and toothed leaflets (the terminal leaflet is larger, while the lower leaflets are much smaller and inconspicuous) and yellow flowers, both single and semi-double, from early summer to early autumn

primary_name: Cypripedium flavum S008-1 from Hengduan Mts, China
Cypripedium shanxiense S015-1 from Hengduan Mts, China
Cypripedium shanxiense S015-2 from Hengduan Mts, China
Cypripedium tibeticum S028-1 from Hengduan Mts, China
Cypripedium tibeticum S028-2 from Hengduan Mts, China

description: A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing lobed, rounded, dark red to maroon leaves and slender, dark red stems bearing open panicles of tiny, white flowers in late sring and early summer.

primary_name: Calibrachoa [Million Bells Trailing Lemon] (Million Bells Series)
Calibrachoa [Million Bells Trailing Plum] ('Sunbelkufepi') (Million Bells Series)
