A clump-forming, rhizomatous deciduous perennial with strap-like green leaves and purple and white flowers with a yellow centre which appear in the summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 80cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of cream-variegated, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, blue flowers from mid-summer to autumn.
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet-shaped pale blue-mauve flowers in the summer
A deciduous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid green leaves and compact, sturdy stems with rounded umbels of trumpet shaped, violet blue flowers in summer

An evergreen perennial forming a rhizomatous clump with large, oval, mid-green leaves with a fine red rim that turn entirely maroon-red in autumn. Tall stems with clusters of pinkish-red flowers on red stems appear in late winter through spring

A slow-growing evergreen perennial, to 1.2m high in flower, with fine clumps of narrow, grass-like leaves. From mid to late summer, produces slender, arching stems bearing a succession of pendent, bell-shaped dusky coral pink flowers with papery white bracts
Compact, upright, perennial coneflower producing single, yellow-orange blooms with downward arching ray petals surrounding a central yellow-green cone, in summer

An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 60cm tall with hairy, dark green leaves. Fragrant flowers up to 10cm across are borne from summer into autumn and change colour as they age; ray florets surrounding the bronze-orange cone emerge red before turning orange and then pink
A compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, downward arching, rose pink rays with a dark cooper orange centre. Perfect for container growing and attracting pollinators

Uright, perennial coneflower about 75cm tall, producing rose-pink daisy-like flowers with flattened ray-petals surrounding a central orange-brown cone, flowering profusely over a long period in summer into autumn

An attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, white blooms with downward arching rays surrounding a prominent central yellow-orange cone. Excellent for container growing and attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing deep orange-pink, fully double flowers with a prominent central pompom surrounded by light pink ray petals that arch downward. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright perennial coneflower variety producing a mix of bright flowers with petals merging from yellow at the centre to orange-red at the end. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A mound-forming, deciduous, herbaceous perennial, bearing mid-green, deeply divided, lobed leaves, which often turn red in autumn, on stems to 90cm (30in) high and across. In summer, many single, dark pink, star-shaped flowers with narrow petals, a black eye and purple veins are produced, that are attractive to bees and other pollinators, making it a good addition to the wildlife garden.

A compact, vigorous, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen herbaceous perennial producing shiny, silvery-brown foliage. Pink flowers appear on upright stems above the foliage from spring to summer

A compact, rhizomatous clump-forming perennial to 40cm with arching, variegated green and cream phormium-like foliage and delicated, orchid-like pale lavender-blue flowers with yellow centres appearing spring and summer. Good for ground cover

A low-growing, mat-forming, semi-evergreen to evergreen perennial bearing oval to triangular, toothed, silver leaves with narrow, mid-green margins and spikes of whorled, bright purple flowers in summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Semi-double white flowers with yellow centres, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly.

A bushy, clump-forming perennial up to 90cm high, with broad, palmate green leaves divided into narrow leaflets. Upright spikes of bicoloured, deep violet and creamy white flowers are produced from early to mid summer
An erect herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular red flowers with a hint of purple over a long period of time in summer.

A vigorous, compact herbaceous perennial to 40cm tall, with ovate green leaves which turn orange-red in the autumn. Nodding, white, bell-shaped flowers 2cm wide appear in summer, followed by inflated, lantern-like deep orange calyces 5cm long, enclosing red berries
A clump-forming perennial, to 1.4m tall, with dark red, egg-shaped flowerheads held above the divided foliage in summer

Densely-tufted, deciduous, perennial grass about 1m tall, producing an upright mound of fine-textured, glaucous, light blue leaves tinted deep pink and burgundy in late summer. Upright, silvery blue flowers appear during late summer and autumn. The whole plant usually turns colours of red, orange and copper in autumn and winter

A vigorous, mat-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to 10cm tall, with fleshy, bright green leaves held on spreading, rooting stems. Star-shaped, pink flowers are produced in rounded clusters in late summer
A cormous perennial, with narrow, strap-shaped basal leaves in spring. Upright stems bear loose clusters of creamy yellow buds, opening to funnel-shaped white flowers with greenish midribs in summer

A dwarf cultivar with a height and spread of 60cm. It is a short-lived perennial with rough stems and leaves, and dense clusters of small, purple flowers in summer and autumn; these are a good nectar source for pollinating insects
A clump-forming perennial to around 75cm with narrow, pleated foliage and, in mid- to late summer,large, coppery-orange flowers with reflexed petals and prominent stamens

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, blended purple flowers with a green throat to 13cm across in summer

A bulbous perennial, to 20cm in height, with erect, narrow, grey-green leaves and, in late winter, solitary, nodding, white flowers with long, narrow, outer segments. The short, inner segments have a large, green mark like a blurred X
A spreading perennial to about 70cm, with grey-green, fern-like foliage. Upright, branching stems are topped with domed flowerheads of small, soft yellow flowers from early summer to early autumn

A fast-growing, upright, deciduous tree that may ultimately reach 30m but can be kept smaller with annual pruning. The glossy, triangular foliage is rich, bronzy red-purple and balsam-scented when young. Red male or green female catkins are produced by mature trees in early spring
A deciduous, dwarf maple about 1.5m tall with a dense, compact habit, the dark green 5 to 7-lobed leaves have red petioles and emerge bright pink-red in spring, turning orange-red in autumn

An upright, branching, deciduous shrub with finely textured, dissected, dark green leaves. Large and showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped flowers borne from late spring into early summer have reddish-purple petals with very dark burgundy flares around a golden yellow centre

A compact, clump-forming perennial bulb with lance shaped green leaves. This dwarf tulip has single, cup-shaped flowers; buds are a delicate greenish grey, and open to show strong yellow flaming and white tips. It flowers in mid spring and stands to about 15cm high. Good for naturalising

description: A type of New Guinea Impatiens native to Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands. They are tender bushy plants mostly grown as annual bedding plants or patio specimens. They can flower throughout the warmer summer months with flowers 3-5cm wide. They have succulent stems and rich bronze-green glossy serrated edged, pointed foliage around 5-7 cm in length . Ideal bedding or patio plants to help brighten up a either a semi-shady or sunny in the garden. They flower until the first real cold and frosts of autumn. Keep them warm, well-watered, and feed and dead-head plants regularly.

alternative_names: Impatiens schlechteri white-flowered|Impatiens New Guinea Group (White)

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 70cm, with dark stems and dark green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The blooms have neat rows of inrolled petals, forming a flattened ball, white with purple tips at first, becoming more purple with age

A compact, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial to around 30cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Large, decorative, double creamy-pink flowers with a cherry-red blush appear from summer through until the first frosts. A fragile variety from the USA

Bears double, reddish-purple flowers, above dark foliage, in summer and early autumn. Height to 80cm

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, ruffled pale apricot to peach orange flowers with bright orange beards appearing May to June
A deciduous, clump-forming perennial bulb with long, narrow, erect green foliage and from late spring into early summer, spikes of compact, mid denim-blue, star-shaped flowers to around 75cm tall

Bulbous perennial to 75cm in height, with long, wavy-margined, pale green leaves to 70cm long, and stout, pale green stems bearing racemes of star-shaped, creamy-white flowers, each with a pink eye, with a terminal rosette of leafy bracts

A bulbous perennial producing stems to 1m tall bearing whorls of glossy green, lance-shaped leaves and hanging clusters of pale orange to pink, red-veined, bell-shaped flowers crowned with small, leaf-like bracts

An evergreen, frost-tender subshrub, often grown as an annual, forming a compact mound of finely-divided, blue-green foliage to around 60cm tall. A mass of single flowers, white with a yellow centre, are borne above the foliage from late spring until the first frosts.
Forms a mound to 50 x 60 cm with silvery glaucous foliage and classic white-rayed, yellow-centred flowers to 4.5cm

Moderately floriferous and forms a spreading mound to 40 x 50 cm with green leaves and singledistinctive flowers to 5cm across. The central disc florets are brownish in bud opening to yellow; the showy, outer ray florets are pale yellow with blotches and speckles of red
A herbaceous annual with fine-texured leaves and masses of white daisy-like flowers with yellow centres
A sub-shrub to about 50cm, with finely-divided, aromatic, blue-green leaves and pink, double flowers from late spring to mid-autumn

A low-growing, bushy, mound-forming evergreen perennial sub-shrub, often grown as an annual, to around 60cm in height with finely-divided, grey-green leaves. Single, dark pinkish-red daisy-like flowers with yellow centres appear in the summer
A vigorous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 30cm, with erect leafy stems and purple, orchid-like flowers appearing in May to August
A tuberous perennial, growing to about 30cm tall, with fairly broad, upright, green, stem-clasping leaves. The deep purple flowers, with white eye, appear in early to midsummer

alternative_names: Viola epipsila|Viola suecica|Viola palustris var. epipsila

description: A vigorous, twining climber with semi-evergreen, lobed leaves. Flowers with reflexed purple petals and deeper purple to blue coronal filaments are borne from summer into early autumn and may be followed by orange-yellow fruits. The pulp in the fruits only can be eaten when they are fully ripe and yellow-orange. Unripe fruit and is toxic
A tender, compact perennial to around 30cm tall with wrinkled, strap-shaped, dark green leaves and clusters of pale salmon-pink flowers borne on short stems from spring into autumn

A compact, evergreen perennial to about 60cm, producing a clump of glossy, strap-shaped leaves. Rounded umbels of funnel-shaped flowers, with rather narrow, mid-blue petals with a dark central stripe, appear from mid-summer to early autumn

A clump-forming, cormous perennial to about 80cm with sword-shaped leaves. In mid- to late summer the vivid orange flowers open wide, revealing prominent yellow stamens and a yellow throat with a ring of red dots. They are followed by decorative seed pods

alternative_names: rose [Pure Poetry]|Rosa [Johann Wolfgang von Goethe Rose]|Rosa 'Tan04179'|Rosa 'Goethe Rose'
description: Robust, bushy rose to 75cm tall, with large dark green leaves and bearing sweetly-scented, fully double, deep magenta blooms held above strong upright stems, repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

Small, upright, vase-shaped deciduous tree about 5-6m tall, with serrated dark green leaves, turning orange and yellow in autumn. Single pale pink flowers are produced in masses, throughout early spring

Modern climbing rose about 3m tall, bearing healthy, glossy dark green leaves with purplish young growth. Peach buds open to semi-double creamy-lemon blooms fading to white, with prominent yellow stamens, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn, followed by orange-red fruits (hips)

Free-flowering shrub rose to 1.2m tall which can be grown as a short climber, with plentiful glossy, mid-green foliage and clusters of semi-double, lightly scented blooms in a colour blend of apricot, peach and yellow, flowering repeatedly from summer to autumn
A bushy, repeat-flowering shrub rose. to 1.2m tall, with matt green foliage. Lightly-scented, rosette-shaped, pink flowers, softening to a paler shade with age, are borne in summer and autumn
An upright shrub rose up to 1.2m high with glossy, dark green leaves and fragrant, double flowers, the petals coral-pink tinged with orange, from early summer to the autumn frosts

alternative_names: Seriphidium maritimum subsp. humifusum|Artemisia camprestris subsp. maritima var. humifusa

description: A bushy, upright, repeat-flowering shrub rose to around 1.2m tall, with sparsely-thorned stems. Fragrant, double, pink blooms are borne in clusters repeat-flowering from summer into autumn

Bushy, deciduous rose to around 90cm tall, with healthy, glossy, dark green leaves and bearing fragrant, semi-double to double, pinkish-purple flowers shaded, blotched and edged silvery white and repeat-flowering over a long season from summer to autumn

Bushy, upright rose to about 1.1m tall, with dense, glossy dark foliage and large clusters of very fragrant, old-fashioned, fully double pure-pink blooms 10cm across, borne in abundance through summer and autumn

A dwarf evergreen shrub, 30-45cm high, with an upright to rounded habit. Young stems are coated in a woolly reddish-brown felt, and the small, ovate, dark green leaves have rust-coloured felting on the undersides. Produces small rounded clusters of tiny white flowers with prominent white stamens, from late spring to early summer

A dwarf evergreen shrub to 60cm high, with an upright to rounded habit. Young stems are coated in a woolly reddish-brown felt. Leaves are small, ovate, aromatic and dark green, with a rust-coloured felting on the undersides. Produces small rounded clusters of tiny white flowers with prominent white stamens, in early summer

Compact climbing rose to 1.8m tall, with dark green foliage and large clusters of sweetly-scented, semi-double, delicate-pink, open blooms, 5cm across, with bright yellow stamens, flowering in flushes from summer to autumn
A climbing annual reaching up to 2m high and bearing apricot-orange fragrant flowers on strong stems from summer into autumn

A vigorous evergreen, perennial of bamboo-like stout clumps rising from rhizomes, with drooping, feathery green to reddish-pink foliage. Male plants have inflorescens of spherical, shiny, plum-brown flowers and female plants have flower heads of large, swollen brown spikelets.

A small, upright, slow-growing tree ultimately to about 3m in height and spread. The leaves have five, toothed, tapering lobes opening lime green, becoming yellow-green in summer with red-flushed edges and yellow-orange in autumn. Inconspicuous red flowers in spring are followed by red and green, winged fruit in autumn
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 40cm tall with upright, narrow, twisted, dark green leaves with yellow margins. Funnel-shaped, lavender flowers are borne on erect stems in summer

A bulbous perennial with leafy stems to around 100cm topped in mid- to late summer with large, scented, upward-facing, bowl-shaped flowers in bright sugar pink, paler towards the ruffled edges and darker along the midribs
Bushy rose to 90cm tall, with plentiful, glossy dark foliage and fragrant, large and shapely, double, deep cerise-pink blooms repeat-flowering from summer to autumn
This shallot produces a cluster of bulbs with a deep red skin and white flesh and stores well

Compact clump-forming perennial 35-45cm tall, with glossy, bronze-tinted, dark green, finely dissected leaves. Rich reddish-purple flowers in short, narrow plumes to 18cm long are produced above the foliage in mid-summer
Compact, bushy annuals to 35cm, with divided, fern-like leaves. Showy, semi-double flowers, in yellow, orange and red, are produced in summer and autumn
A compact, deciduous shrub to around 100cm with coarsley toothed dark green foliage and rounded, bright green mophead flowers, changing to bright pink as they mature, from June through to October

A compact deciduous shrub to 1.2m high, with dark green ovate leaves. Dense conical clusters of flowers are produced from mid to late summer, opening creamy white and rapidly developing to a deep reddish pink that holds into early autumn

An attractive, round, grey–green courgette with white speckles. Habit is more compact than other varieties so a good option for a smaller garden. You should get good yields of courgettes that can be eaten raw or cooked. Shows good resistance to powdery mildew.

An early-fruiting cultivar which produces smooth-skinned, golden-yellow courgettes, which are ready to harvest when approximately 15-20cm (6-8in) in length. These are produced over a long period from July to October, as long as the developing fruits are regularly picked. Its relatively compact habit makes it suitable for growing in containers on the patio where border space is limited. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking
A tender perennial usually cultivated as an annual vegetable. This F1 hybrid courgette produces uniform, dark green stems with few spines. Ideal picked as a baby courgette

A compact, prolifically fruiting cultivar, which produces smooth-skinned, very dark green courgettes, which are ready to harvest when approximately 15-20cm (6-8in) in length. These are produced over a long period from July to October, if the fruits are regularly picked. Its relatively compact habit, makes it suitable for growing in containers where border space is limited. The bright yellow flowers are attractive to pollinating insects. The flowers can also be picked and used in cooking

A robust and compact, bushy, half-hardy perennial. Has small lance-shaped, toothed dark green leaves and terminal racemes of scented two-lipped tubular golden yellow flowers with a small dark purple feathering towards the orange-yellow protuberance in the centre from late spring to early autumn.
An evergreen, trailing perennial with succulent stems and fleshy, rounded leaves to 4cm across. A good foliage houseplant for a hanging basket or shelf, where it can be allowed to trail downwards

A bulbous, clump-forming perennial with slender, erect leaves and rounded flowers comprising spoon-shaped, bluntly-pointed, white outer segments and inner segments with a broad green mark from the apex, paling at the base

Clump-forming perennial, to 1m in height, with lance-shaped, variegated leaves of creamy-white edged with green. In spring, new shoots are yellow. Throughout summer and autumn dark red flowers contrast well with the foliage and the creamy-white flower stems

A slow-growing small, weeping ornamental cherry with 3 seasons of interest. A profusion of white flowers in early spring are followed by dark-green centred foliage with light green margins. In autumn, the leaves turn red, orange, and yellow.

A half-hardy evergreen shrub to 4m high, with glossy green leaves with irregular pale cream margins, the new growth is tinted pink. Produces large clusters of small, daisy-like white flowers in early summer

A vigorous, trailing and mounding tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green and cream-yellow leaves and produces jolly, gramophone-trumpet-shaped, rich pink-purple flowers. A very striking variegated variety that blooms from late spring well into autumn if dead-headed and well fed. It trails or spreads around 30 cm to 40 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and containers.

alternative_names: Syringa reticulata subsp. reticulata 'Bailnce'|Syringa reticulata [First Editions Snowdance]

primary_name: Syringa pubescens subsp. patula 'Colby's Twinkling Little Star'

description: A compact, deciduous shrub to around 1.2m high, with ovate, glossy green leaves. Produces rounded to conical clusters of small, fragrant, tubular lilac-coloured flowers, with the main flush in late spring followed by a second flush in late summer that can last into early autumn

A bulbous, herbaceous perennial, to 45cm in height, with strap-like leaves and double flowers, to 10cm across. The outer petals are ivory-white to cream with the inner petal segments a mix of orange-yellow interspersed with cream

A clump-forming daffodil to around 50cm high, with straplike, grey-green leaves. Flowers are 8.5cm across, scented and slightly nodding, with outer petals fading to cream and a pale primrose yellow corona, split to the base and held flat against the petals. Usually produces two or three flowers to a stem

Spreading, deciduous shrub to 75cm tall with upright shoots and bright green leaves to 15cm long, composed of almost diamond-shaped leaflets, and bearing white flowers in dense racemes 13cm long, in early and midsummer.

alternative_names: long-styled disporum 'Night Heron'|Disporum kawakamii 'Night Heron'|Disporum cantoniense 'Night Heron'
description: A clump-forming, rhizomatous perennial with tall, arching stems, and purple, glossy leaves which gradually turn to green throughout the season. It produces delicate bell-shaped white to yellow flowers in late spring, followed by black-red berries. A good plant for shady areas

primary_name: Ageratum houstonianum [Artist Basso White] ('Agwitto') (Artist Basso Series)

description: A deciduous shrub with finely-branched, upright stems to about 2m, turning rich orange in winter. The mid-green leaves turn greenish-yellow in autumn. Clusters of small, white flowers in summer are followed by black fruits
A deciduous small tree or large multi-stemmed shrub to a height of 10m, with glossy green leaves and shiny green-brown bark that darkens grey, and peels when more mature
A bushy, deciduous shrub to around 150cm, with coarsley toothed dark green foliage and rounded clusters of mophead green flowers turning to dark pink appearing from July through to September

alternative_names: Omphalodes cilicica Hauss.|Omphalodes luciliae var. cilicica

description: A perennial poppy, to 70cm high, with bristly stems and a rosette of divided and toothed green leaves covered with silvery hairs. In early to mid summer, produces up to 10 upright, hairy buds, that open to large, orange-red flowers, often with black blotches at the base of the petals

An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.2m with broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Racemes of delicately fragranced, pale orange flowers with prominent salmon-pink stamens appear from late summer through to October
A spreading deciduous shrub to 2m tall, with aromatic, lobed dark green leaves and dense nodding racemes of small, red and yellow flowers in early summer

A late raspberry with red fruit. It has deciduous green leaves and small white flowers in the summer producing its harvest in late summer into autumn. Although true of many late raspberries, this variety is particularly good at producing another early crop the following year, if the stems are left uncut. It is compact enough to be grown in a large container.
A bushy, upright rose to 90cm tall, with healthy glossy green foliage and long pointed buds opening to lightly fragrant, semi-double, rich red blooms, borne repeatedly through summer and autumn

Very free-flowering, bushy upright rose about 50-70cm tall, with glossy rich green leaves. Lightly scented, single to semi-double, pale salmon-pink blooms open flat to display golden stamens, produced from masses of pointed buds, virtually covering the plant and almost continuously in flower from summer to autumn; shade tolerant

Bushy, compact, upright rose about 70cm tall, with glossy mid-green leaves, and bearing small clusters of fully double, cherry-red blooms with a light fragrance, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn

Large upright rose about 1.2m tall, with very healthy, leathery mid-green leaves, and bearing very fragrant, large, pale pink, well-formed double blooms, with frilled edges, repeat flowering from early summer to autumn

A bushy, upright, compact deciduous shrub to around 70cm, with arching stems of glossy dark green foliage and pale creamy-pink double flowers, repeat flowering from summer through to autumn. Great for cutting and good disease resistance
A semi-evergreen perennial with substantial, dark green, arrow-shaped foliage. Flowers comprising a pastel pink spathe and yellow spadix appear in spring
Large deciduous tree to about 20m tall, with brown bark, leathery, dark green 3-5 lobed leaves,

A bulbous perennial to about 40cm in height, with broadly strap-like green foliage. Peony-like, warm pink, fully double flowers with ruffled petals finely dusted and tipped with palest pink, appear in April to May

alternative_names: Martin's spurge 'Rudolph'|Euphorbia × martini 'Waleuphrud'|Euphorbia × martini [Rudolph]|Euphorbia × martini 'Walberton's Rudolf'
description: A fast-growing, evergreen, perennial sub-shrub, forming a mound of leathery lance-shaped dark green leaves. The tips of the stems develop bright red colouration in the winter and go on to produce heads of lime-green flowers in the following spring and summer. New stems emerge at ground level in spring

A large, tropical evergreen tree, about 30m tall in the wild, but forming a small tree or large shrub in British gardens, and suitable only for the mildest counties. Coppery-red young leaves mature to glossy green, 17cm long and grey-silver beneath, Yellowish flowers from mid summer to early autumn are followed by yellow-brown winged fruits, produced until early winter

primary_name: Acer pictum subsp. pictum f. ambiguum
alternative_names: Acer mono f. ambiguum|Acer pictum var. ambiguum|Acer pictum var. paxii|Acer pictum f. ambiguum|Acer mono var. ambiguum|Acer ambiguum|Acer truncatum var. barbinerve|Acer mono 'Ambiguum'

description: Rounded, deciduous tree about 12m tall, with 3-5 lobed, bright green, heart-shaped leaves that turn yellow in autumn, and bearing upright flower clusters of greenish-yellow flowers in spring, followed by 3-4cm long brown winged fruits with wide-spreading wings

A short-trunked, medium-sized decidiuous tree with glossy deep-green palmate leaves which turn deep red in autumn. Pale yellow 'candle' flowers with yellow then pink throats, become familiar conkers inside a smooth leathery case.

alternative_names: Kniphofia uvaria var. serotina|Kniphofia alooides var. serotina

description: A dioecious plant which needs both sexes to bear fruit. The roots are nitrogen-fixing and also, able to bind loose sandy soils for stabiliasation purposes.

A deciduous tree to 20m with strong green leaves with yellow hairs. The leaves show no autumn colour, dropping to the ground when still green. There are male catkins from autumn, slowly becoming larger then opening in late spring. Female 'cones' are held on single stems and open as round, woody fruits remaining on the tree all winter

alternative_names: Tritoma grandis|Kniphofia alooides var. grandis|Tritoma uvaria var. grandis|Kniphofia grandis

description: A fast-growing deciduous tree to 20m. Leaves are green with an elongated shape, pink when young then shiny green until they fall in autumn. Male catkins hang in large numbers in late summer and female woody 'cones' persist on the branches through the winter in clusters

A hardy, deciduous shrub or small tree which may reach a height of up to 10m in its natural habitat, less within UK gardens, with very large, bipinnate green foliage which turns to yellows, browns and purples in the autumn, and a sharply spiny single dark brown stem. Umbels of fragrant, purplish-white flowers appear from June to August, followed by clusters of small, dark purple to black berries from September to November

Ultimately makes a small, upright tree, but is slow-growing and can remain shrub-like for many years. Red-brown peeling bark and glossy, dark green leaves to 12cm long are bronzed when young. White, urn-shaped flowers flushed with deep pink in large, hanging clusters in late summer and autumn, followed by spherical yellow then red fruit. Whilst the fruits are edible and used to make jams and liqueurs in some countries, they are generally grown for ornamental purposes only in the UK
An evergreen large shrub or small tree with long, narrow leaves that are green above and pale grey on the underside. Pale yellow, cylindrical flowers are produced in summer and autumn
An upright hybrid tea rose to 1.2m with dark green, glossy leaves and lightly-scented, fully double flowers with creamy-yellow petals, darker in the centre of the bloom

A compact, evergreen, clump-forming succulent perennial producing a single rosette of wavy-edged, powdery blue-green foliage. The edges and undersides of the leaves turn pink in cooler conditions but overall colours will depend very much on temperature. Bell-shaped, orange-yellow flowers may appear in the spring
A bulbous perennial to around 1m tall with alternate, dark green leaves. Flowers to 10cm in diameter with deep burgundy petals tipped and edged with orange are borne in early summer
One of the David Austin Wedding Roses Collection of cut flowers with fully double, very frilly, rosette blooms of fragrant, creamy-white to ivory, produced above strong upright stems

An attractive deep purple skinned Spring onion with a mild flavour and crisp texture. Fast maturing, suitable to harvest within 6 weeks from sowing. Suitable for both open ground and container growing

A hardy perennial grown as an annual vegetable. Easy to grow compact, upright leek with a mild flavour, often grown as baby leeks in a late Summer harvest or can be left to mature in Winter. Shows excellent disease resistance

An evergreen shrub or small tree ranging from 1.5–5m tall, with slender, yellow-grey branches when young and small, bright red new foliage which turns papery and leathery dark green. Lightly fragrant, solitary white or pale purplish-red flowers, with 5-7 petals, appear in the axils of the leaves from February to March. Green fruits ripen to purple-red from September to October

A medium to large, deciduous tree with grey bark that is reddish brown on the younger branches. The new growth is initially downy, becoming bare as the stems mature, but the undersides of the leaves retain a covering of silky down-like hairs. The foliage is green in spring and summer and bright orange red in autumn. The green, male and female catkins are produced separately on the same tree in April. After fertilisation, the female flowers develop into hop-like clusters in late summer to autumn, containing winged seeds that disperse on the wind when ripe

A free-flowering, bushy, evergreen shrub. The aromatic leaves, with three to five slender leaflets, open yellow, maturing to green. Clusters of fragrant, white flowers appear in late spring and again in late summer to autumn

An evergreen succulent with large rosettes of olive-green to lavender-rose coloured pointed fleshy leaves and pink edges. The leaves turn more rose coloured the more sunlight they are exposed to. Coral pink flowers appear on tall, upright stems during the summer

A hardy, deciduous, clump-forming perennial to around 80cm in height, with strap-like dark green leaves and upright, hairy stems. Large, double, pom-pom-like flowers with downward-facing petals are bright pink with a greenish central cone, appearing from mid summer and sometimes lasting through until the autumn

A fast-growing, deciduous tree to 20m tall in its native habitat but likely to be smaller in cultivation. The greyish-brown bark exudes a sticky resin and splits to reveal a pink inner layer. Divided leaves up to 40cm long are made up of 4-15 pairs of pointed, papery leaflets, each up to 12.5cm long. Leaves emerge tinged red in the spring, maturing to green before turning red again in the autumn. Small, yellowish or red flowers borne in late spring are followed by fruits to 2.5cm across that ripen to red and are edible with a sour, white flesh

A compact evergreen perennial with shorter and stouter leaves than your average spider plant. Bright green leaves edged with cream margins. Racemes of tiny white flowers are borne on arching stems, with plantlets forming along the branching flower stems

An evergreen, perennial bromeliad forming a rosette of glossy, dark-green, lance-shaped leaves to 30cm long. In summer an erect stem to 50cm arises from the centre of the rosette, this is topped with a striking inflorescence composed of red bracts with white tips. This showy flower spike will last for several months, after which the leaf rosette will die. However, new, offset plants may be produced around the parent rosette at this time
A compact, mound-forming cultivar to approximately 50cm high bearing a profusion of deep pink to purple flowers from early autumn
A large-flowered gladiolus, maximum height 120cm high, with green sword like leaves. Tall spikes of pure white flowers, appear in August to September

A compact, deciduous shrub to 1.2m high, with dark green ovate leaves. Dense conical clusters of flowers are produced from mid to late summer, opening white and rapidly developing to a cherry red that holds its colour into early autumn

Columnar tree to about 10m tall, very narrow when young, with yellow-green young twigs and mid-green leaves to 17cm long, bronze when young. Downy flower buds open to fragrant pure white, star-shaped flowers with 6 tepals, in mid-spring; flowers appear even on young trees

A late primocane blackberry, fruiting on canes in the first year and produces large, 11g sweet black fruit in late summer on compact thorny canes. The fruit are of moderate flavour and are suitable for desserts and cooking

Bushy, deciduous shrub about 2m tall, with sharply-toothed green leaves tinted red in spring, becoming green in summer, then yellow in autumn. Produces bowl-shaped, bright pink flowers in flattened heads during summer that become paler as the season progresses

A lush, clump-forming perennial to 1m with large, lance-shaped leaves, dark green above, paler beneath, on long stems. In summer, stems up to 65cm tall carry clusters of small, pale green flowers with four large, pale green, leaf-like bracts and long, pale green 'whiskers', all suffused with grey

A tuberous perennial with elongated heart-shaped dark to mid-green leaves. In summer,wavy-edged, purple-black hood-shaped flowers or spathes, with ared or mauve border and yellow edging, and a central yellow spadix, are produced on long, upright stems

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to 50cm tall with glossy, dark green leaves sparsely spotted with white. Upright stems borne in summer comprise spathes of pale pink to white surrounding a clusters of tiny yellow flowers

A tender perennial to 50cm tall, forming an upright clump of white-spotted, arrow-shaped, dark green leaves. In summer it produces striking flowers composed of bright yellow spathes wrapped round a yellow spadix; the flowers are good for cutting. Grow as a houseplant or as summer bedding
A compact herbaceous perennial, 25cm high, with green leaves and miniature decorative orange-red flowerheads, 5-10cm across, from summer until the first frosts in autumn

Compact, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 45-50cm in height, with mid-green foliage. Flowers, produced from midsummer until the first frosts, have vibrant yellow slightly incurved petals, creating a neat shape to 10cm across

A climbing rose to 3m in height, producing clusters of lightly-scented, fully double, bowl-shaped, pink blooms with dark pink veining and dark pink on the reverse of the frilly petals, in summer and autumn

A large shrub or small tree to around 5m high, with an upright then spreading habit, thorny branches and lobed and serrated dark green leaves. In late spring, clusters of white flowers with purple anthers are produced, followed by pendent, glossy red berries

A hardy and reliable perennial with long, pointed green, aromatic foliage with toothed edges. Tall, upright spikes of dark violet-purple to dark blue bottlebrush-like flowers appear from July to October

alternative_names: Capsicum baccatum var. pendulum 'Friar's Hat'|Capsicum 'Friar's Hat'

description: A bulbous perennial with whorls of leaves on upright stems, to about 1.2m tall. The buff-yellow flowers have strongly reflexed petals, heavily flushed with coppery pink, dark red spots and prominent orange anthers

A clump-forming perennial with upright stems to about 1.2m bearing whorls of mid-green leaves. The pungently scented, turkscap flowers, produced in summer, are dark pinkish red, with bright orange stamens

A bulbous perennial with whorls of leaves on upright stems to about 1m tall. The yellow flowers, produced in summer, have reflexed petals flushed and spotted with coppery red, and prominent orange anthers

Climbing rose to about 2.5-3m in height with large, glossy dark green leaves. Very large and fragrant, fully double, high centred, cupped red blooms from ovoid buds, borne mostly solitary or in small clusters, repeating in flushes through summer to autumn

A repeat-flowering, climbing rose to 2.5m high with toothed and glossy, dark green foliage. Clusters of double, ruffled flowers in shades of apricot-pink with a strong, fruity fragrance are borne from summer into early autumn
A climbing rose to about 2.5m tall, with glossy mid-green foliage and a profusion of large, fragrant, semi-double, deep red flowers from summer to autumn

A tender, upright perennial, with glossy dark green, arrow-shaped, leaves on tall leaf-stalks, and glossy, heart-shaped, dark purple-burgundy, almost black spathe flowers with yellow spike-like spadices, produced through the year

A hardy, evergreen shrub approximately 30cm tall with a a spread to 25cm. It has dark green foliage and mid-green new growth in spring, followed by blueish pink to violet flower buds in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub approximately 30cm tall with a spread to 25cm, dark green foliage with mid-green new growth in spring. Brilliant violet-blue flower buds appear in summer and autumn.

A compact, low-growing evergreen shrub with upright stems bearing tiny, linear, overlapping, dark-green leaves and spike-like racemes of long-lasting cerise flower buds. These eventually turn brown and remain on the plants overwinter. This variety flowers early from late summer to early winter.
A hardy, evergreen shrub to around 30cm in height, with mid-green foliage. Shell-pink flowers appear from summer through to autumn
A hardy, evergreen shrub with an upright habit, approximately 60cm tall with a spread to 50cm. It has silvery grey foliage and spikes of light pink buds in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub approximately 60cm tall with a spread to 50cm and green foliage. Pinkish-purple buds appear in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub with an upright, bushy habit approximately 50cm tall with an equal spread. It has green foliage and dark red flowers from summer through to autumn.

alternative_names: heather 'Laura'|Calluna vulgaris [Beauty Ladies Laura] (Beauty Ladies Series)
description: An evergreen, semi-upright shrub to around 50cm in height, with green foliage and dark purple flowers appearing from summer through until the autumn
An upright, hardy evergreen shrub to around 60cm in height, with dark green foliage which turns dark purple-green in winter. Lavender pink-purple flowers appear from summer through to early winter

A dwarf, slow-growing, hardy, evergreen shrub reaching a height of around 20 to 50cm in height, with dark green foliage. Dark, raspberry pink to crimson red flowers appear from August through to November

alternative_names: Calluna vulgaris [Beauty Ladies Sissi] (Beauty Ladies Series)
description: A hardy, evergreen shrub with an upright habit and dark green foliage. Bright red flowers appear from summer through until the autumn
A compact, hardy, upright evergreen shrub to around 30 to 50cm in height, with a bushy habit and dark green foliage. Purple-red flowers emerge in October, remaining through the early part of winter
A hardy, evergreen shrub with thin, scaly branches of dark green foliage and reddish-pink flowers, appearing from summer to autumn

A compact, rounded herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall bearing a profusion of double flowers above the mound of foliage in autumn. Flowerheads comprise pale orange outer florets and inner florets tipped with a dark red to bronze colour
A compact herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall with mid green leaves forming a low mound. Double, pink flowers with slightly darker centres are borne in autumn and reach up to 5cm in diameter
An excellent strawberry variety that produces a medium-sized, glossy, orange-red, conical fruits in summer with a firm texture and a sweet and juicy taste
An everbearer, producing good-sized, conical fruit, though of variable quality, from early summer to early autumn.

An evergreen shrub with beautiful, long, leathery, leaves with two to four soft spikes along them - the leaves are slightly narrower than many other Mahonias. Evergreen apart from the absolute coldest winters and bearing the classic bright yellow flowers in autumn

An evergreen shrub to around 2m high, with pinnate leaves to 40cm long, divided into overlapping pairs of thin, curved, dull green leaflets, with tapered tips and finely edged with numerous tiny spines. Small, yellow flowers are borne in upright to spreading clusters to 7cm long in late summer or early autumn
A strongly compact variety producing large, sweet flavoured, bright red berries in summer. It produces very few runners which makes it ideal for container growing or small garden spaces

A clump-forming evergreen perennial to around 15cm high, with a spreading, trailing habit, and lobed and toothed dark green leaves strongly flushed with dark purple. A clump-forming perennial daffodil to 45cm, with straplike, grey-green leaves. Flowers are 9.5cm across and scented, with broad, pale creamy yellow outer petals and a split orange-pink corona. Flowers in mid spring

A clump-forming perennial daffodil to around 40cm high, with straplike, grey-green leaves. Flowers are fragrant, around 9cm across, with light yellow outer petals and a split, pale yellow corona with a frilly yellow-orange rim

A clump-forming, late-flowering bulbous perennial to around 30cm in height with green, strap-like foliage. Bright yellow-green, star-shaped, lightly fragrant flowers with reflexed petals, appear in the autumn and may last until Christmas. Best grown in a heated greenhouse or conservatory

Sturdy, deciduous, clump-forming, perennial grass, to 1.2m tall, with a graceful, upright habit, and flat, linear, bright green leaves, turning yellow in autumn. Airy sprays of tiny, pinkish flowers are produced from summer to early autumn turning gold later in autumn

A compact, deciduous climber to around 1.5m tall with deep green foliage. The flowers reach up to 17cm in diameter, their colour fading as they age

A deciduous climber to 1.5m tall with dark green foliage.Pale pink flowers with a deeper pink central bar and red anthers reach up to 17cm in diameter and are borne from late spring to early summer and again from late summer to early autumn
A compact, deciduous climber to around 1.2m tall with mid- to dark green foliage. Flowers, 10-13cm diameter, are pale blue to purpleand borne from early summer into autumn
A green-leaved cultivar growing to 1.5m tall and bearing pink and white blendedflowerheads, 15-20cm across, from summer into autumn

While easy to grow as a houseplant, despite its provenance, it is still rather rare in cultivation. Mature plants only, produce flowers consisting of a greenish-white, sheath-like spathe, surrounding a white spadix or column

A pyramidal shrub with spreading, layered branches clothed in tapered, deeply-veined dark green leaves which turn red-purple in autumn. A bulbous perennial to 50cm, with broad, strap-shaped green leaves. Upright stems are topped by clusters of lily-like pink flowers with wavy, crisped edges, from early to mid autumn

A clump-forming perennial to around 90cm high, with lance-shaped, grey-green leaves with narrow, creamy white edges. Spikes of small, star-shaped white flowers are produced in summer

Upright perennial coneflower to about 90cm tall, producing deep green, leafy clumps, and large daisy-like flowers, with white, reflexed petals surrounding a prominent, central orange cone, flowering from summer to autumn

A bushy, clump-forming perennial up to 90cm high, with broad, palmate green leaves divided into narrow leaflets. Upright spikes of bicoloured, deep violet and creamy white flowers are produced from early to mid summer

Bred to suit the british climate, this variety is slower to bolt and has a long cropping season. Broad white stems and deep green leaves
