An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and fragrant, nocturnal, creamy, pale apricot-buff coloured flowers with a yellow throat to 17cm across in summer

primary_name: Argyranthemum frutescens subsp. foeniculaceum (Pit. & Proust) Humphries

description: A clump-forming, deciduous perennial grass with a neat habit and mounds of delicate, arching mid to bright green to silvery-white foliage with pendent pink-red flowers appearing in the autumn. The flowers also turn silvery-white as they mature

A very compact and free-flowering, dwarf deciduous perennial grass to 90cm tall, the narrow, arching, silvery-green leaves become golden in autumn; feathery, arching, creamy-white flower heads open in late summer or autumn, soon turning silver

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches to approximately 70cm in height when in flower. It forms a mound of green, deeply lobed leaves and strong flower stems of double, frilly violet flowers with hints of blue green, in summer
Produces eye-catching flowers comprising hot pink petals that surround a broad orange eye. This herbaceous perennial will reach about 60cm in height and 45cm spread

A vigorous, clump-forming evergreen perennial to around 40cm in height, with long dark green leaves which emerge mottled with red. Spidery pale to mid-pink flowers with long narrow spurs are held on delicate stems above the leaves in spring. A great choice for shady areas

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with curving outer petals, and inner petals marked with a vivid green 'x' shape, slightly paler towards the base

alternative_names: aralia Hayata deeply cut leaf|Fatsia polycarpa Needham's form

description: A large evergreen shrub with a spreading habit and glossy, ovate dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces large, fragrant single flowers, white to pale pink with rose-red shading at the margins, in autumn and winter

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with lance-shaped, mid-green leaves. In summer and autumn it produces large, single, golden-yellow flowers that have red undersides on branched stems. The upward, curling petals are arranged loosely around a central boss of dark-red/brown stamens.

A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce panicles of trumpet shaped flowers in summer. These are blue with a darker midrib down the centre of each petal

An eye-catching, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing attractive, double orange-red blooms in Summer with a prominent central reddish-pink pompom surrounded by short, broad, downward arching, orange petals. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators
A vigorous, mound-forming to spreading, herbaceous perennial with finely divided, mid-green leaves. From summer to early autumn it produces an abundance of pink flowers with darker pink veins.

A compact, evergreen perennial forming a low mound of finely cut, silvery-green foliage. In late spring and early summer it produces daisy-like, pink flowerheads on wiry stems to 20cm tall. Grow in a sunny rock garden, front of border or container
A semi-evergreen, upright, tall and bushy perennial which has green, long, lance-shaped leaves and whorls of long tubular deep magenta flowers that are often curved in late summer and autumn.

Compact, clump-forming perennial to about 40cm tall, with mid-green lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of long-lasting purplish-pink, funnel-shaped flowers with creamy-yellow-flushed inner petals that are strongly flecked purple-brown, in summer and autumn

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to about 70cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of large, funnel-shaped white flowers streaked with burgundy-red, and a yellow and pink-purple throat, appearing from June through until November

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to about 90cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of large, funnel-shaped peach-pink flowers with a yellow speckled throat, appearing from June through until November

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 69cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and mauve-pink flowers that have a gold edge and a rose-coloured halo that surrounds a yellow eye-zone above a green throat to 15cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant apricot-orange flowers with a light green throat to 20cm across in summer

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and lemon-yellow flowers with a dark green throat to 13cm across in summer. The flowers remain open at night
A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, with strap-shaped mid-geen leaves and pale yellow to creamy tangerine flowers with a purple eye at the base, and a green yellow throat

A strong, reliable, low-growing, spreading, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 40cm in height, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Large, double and single creamy-lemon yellow flowers fading to creamy-white appear from late April to June then again for a second flush in the autumn

A low-growing, spreading, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 40cm in height, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Dark red buds open to large, double golden apricot-orange flowers tinted with orange appear from June to July then again for a second flush in the autumn. Will tolerate sun or part shade

A compact, spreading, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 18cm in height, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Semi-double, drooping soft pink flowers with a red calyx appear from April through to the end of May. Free-flowering in shadier areas of the garden

A strong, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 45cm in height, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Masses of single, nodding, upward-facing peach-orange flowers on upright stems appear in late June to July and then again for a second flush in autumn

A compact, bulbous perennial to 12cm with strappy green foliage and dark red, star-shaped flowers with pointed petals which open to reveal white, purple and yellow centres, appearing in May. A good variety for rockeries, front of borderes or in pots and containers
A dwarf perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Flowers are pale pink, with pointed petals and a violet-blue centre

A compact rhizomatous perennial to 35cm high, with straplike green leaves. This dwarf iris produces slightly fragrant white flowers, with pale green veins on the standards and a conspicuous violet-blue beard, from mid- to late spring

A clump-forming perennial, to around 40cm high in flower, forming a mound of deeply lobed, wrinkled green leaves with toothed edges. Semi-double flowers, pale apricot yellow with rose-coloured margins, are borne on slender stems above the foliage from late spring to early summer
A compact clump-forming, tuberous perennial with deeply lobed or cut, blue-green leaves up to 25cm long and producing pale pink flushed white flowers in early spring

An upright, clump-forming perennial to 70cm tall with dark green foliage and large, double flowers to 10cm across made up of deep orangey-pink pompom-like central cones surrounded by drooping pink ray florets

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, producing slender, branched, racemes of fragrant, pale-pink, bottle brush like flowers, followed by black berries, on purple-bronze stems to 1.5m high; above dissected, dark bronze foliage

Unusual perennial coneflower about 75cm tall, producing semi-double purplish-pink flowers with slightly quilled, narrow ray petals surrounding a orange-brown central cone and topped with a small tuft of shorter petals shooting upwards, flowering from summer to autumn
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height, forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and rich golden yellow flowers in summer.

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring, and erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped raspberry-pink flowers with a large tufted centre of white and pink petaloids appear in summer.

Spreading, deciduous shrub about 3-4m tall, with long arching stems bearing mid-green, lance-shaped leaves to 20cm long, grey-green when young. Rounded clusters of fragrant, pale mauve-blue flowers with an orange eye, produced in open terminal panicles, in summer and autumn
A deciduous shrub, to 2m tall, with lobed, green leaves. Pale pink, semi-double flowers, to 8cm across, with darker veins at their centre are borne from mid-summer to autumn

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a rounded, spreading habit and oval-shaped, variegated white and pale green foliage, turning pink in the autumn. White flowers (bracts) appear early to mid-summer, followed by strawberry-like pink to red berries in the autumn
Strong, upright rose to 90cm tall, with dark green foliage and small clusters of large, scented, fully-double, cerise-pink blooms repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

A rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial, up to 75cm high in flower, with glaucous, sword-shaped leaves and scented, fall petals lightly marbled violet, standards marbled deep blue-violet, crested beard, light yellow, flowering in May.

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial bred by Sir Cedric Morris, with upright, strap-like, green leaves and erect stems in late spring and early summer bearing elegant white blooms with pale yellow beards

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial bred by Sir Cedric Morris, with upright, strap-like, green leaves and erect stems in late spring and early summer bearing white blooms, flushed pale pink, with yellow beards

A compact, evergreen, perennial plant with small strappy leaves, that are softly hairy and wrinkled, and large blooms borne over a long season. These are a pale bluish-purple above with the lower lobes blotched and veined in dark purple on a yellowish- white background

A compact evergreen perennial to about 20cm producing a rosette of hairy, strap-shaped leaves. Clusters of flowers, 5.5cm across, with purple upper lobes and cream lower lobes streaked with purple, are produced from early spring to late autumn
An evergreen perennial with strap-shaped, wrinkled leaves. This cultivar is free-flowering over a long season, bearing up to ten clear white flowers with a pale yellow throat on each flower stem

A tender, evergreen perennial to 30cm tall with strap-shaped leaves. Sweetly-scented tubular flowers open white with a pale blue flush and edging that turns pale pink with age; the throat is marked with yellow

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 70-90cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, dark blue flowers from mid-summer to autumn.

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 80-90cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, white flowers from mid-summer to autumn.

An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy dark stems which produce open panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers in summer. These are pale purple-blue with a darker midrib down the centre of each petal

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 30cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, white flowers from mid-summer to autumn.

A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves with sturdy stems which produce large panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers in summer. These are very pale blue in bud, opening mid blue, with a darker blue mid-rib down the centre of each petal

A vigorous, semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark green foliage. Branched stems produce cup-shaped, double white flowers with a subtle yellow central boss of stamens, in late winter and early spring

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus Harvington double yellow speckled (d)
description: A bushy, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen perennial with leathery dark green leaves and double, cup-shaped, outward-facing yellow flowers with red speckles, appearing from December through until the end of March
A tender perennial that's often grown as a bedding plant. It has a compact growing habit and purple-blue flowers
A neat and compact, low-growing evergreen perennial with dark green, heart-shaped, toothed leaves. Fragrant white flowers in dark and pale blue, white, red or speckled appear in April to May

A dense, upright, evergreen shrub to around 75cm in height, with glossy, dark green foliage with velvety-beige undersides. Pink buds open to trusses of trumpet-shaped, white to pale pink flowers with red-orange throats in May. Easy-to-grow and perfect for containers or smaller gardens

Dense, clump-forming, evergreen perennial sedge, about 40cm tall, with fine-textured, arching, light green leaves. Produces stems bearing light brown flower spikes which grow to 1m long as the red-brown seedheads mature in late summer

An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.5m with large, broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Spikes of pink flowers with conspicuous stamens, fragrant both day and evening, appear from late summer through to October

A compact and bushy, upright herbaceous perennial with aromatic, dark green to bronze, lance-shaped leaves and slender whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped deep rose pink flowers with a hint of purple which are very attractive to pollinators all through summer to autumn
An uncommon variety,producing large, pale pink flowers with centres like pincushions throughout the summer.

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Single white flowers with yellow centres, sometimes spoon shaped petals, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly.

An upright-growing, herbaceous perennial to about 1m. Maroon flowers resembling upright catkins are produced on branched, wiry stems over a long period in summer and early autumn above a mound of foliage
A compact, clump-forming perennial with semi-evergreen, strap-shaped leaves. Open heads of white, trumpet-shaped flowers are borne on erect stems to 60cm tall in summer
Bushy rose to 60-70cm tall with glossy green foliage and peach-pink double blooms borne in flushes through summer and into autumn
A large, clump-forming deciduous perennial with rippled, grey-green foliage. Upright stems of pale pink to white flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to around 15cm high and 40cm wide. Leaves are narrow and lance-shaped, yellow-green fading to cream, with distinctive rippling and inward folding. Produces loose clusters of lavender flowers striped with purple, on upright stems in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, variegated, dark green foliage and yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A medium, clump-forming perennial with chartreuse-green foliage and dark green margins. The colour becomes more intense as the season progresses. Upright stems of pale, lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A compact clump-forming, deciduous perennial with narrow green-yellow foliage with a thin dark green margin. Lavender purple flowers appear on stems above the foliage during the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated grey-green foliage which becomes more yellow with higher light levels. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and yellow margins which turn white as the season progresses. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 20cm high, with narrow, elliptic green leaves with a fine yellow margin and strongly rippled edges. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

A vigorous deciduous shrub or small tree, up to around 4m high, with an upright to spreading habit, and broadly oval green leaves with long, pointed tips. Slightly later to flower, producing upright clusters of fragrant, violet-coloured flowers in early summer

A slowly spreading, mound or mat-forming, low growing, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, ovate and sometimes toothed variegated mid-green leaves with pale yellow edges. Blue-purple, four-petalled flowers are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

A bright, compact, perennial coneflower variety with double pink flowers through Summer into Autumn. Short, narrow, reflexed pale pink petals surround a darker pink-red pompom. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing bright, sweetly fragrant blooms with soft-yellow, drooping petals surrounding a prominent orange-brown central cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and double, fragrant pastel-peach coloured flowers that have a rose eye-zone to 15cm across in summer.

An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 60cm in height when in flower with green, linear grass-like leaves and spikes of tubular, creamy-white flowers that emerge from pale yellow buds in summer and autumn.

An upright, clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to 75cm, with lance-shaped, mid-green leaves. Spikes of bell-shaped, purple flowers with white throats marked with purple are produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn
An upright, clump-forming cormous perennial with mid-green strappy leaves and long arches of pale lemon-yellow flowers, with paler yellow tips, throughout the summer

A vigorous bulbous herbaceous perennial up to 40cm high with elliptic dark green leaves, up to 13cm long, with dark maroon patches between the veins, which die down in summer, and one to four creamy white flowers, 3-5cm across, with yellow and orange markings near the bases of the tepals, in spring

primary_name: Roscoea humeana from Cruickshank Botanic Garden

description: A tender perennial, to around 1.5m high, with dark red stems and heart-shaped, glossy, dark grey-green leaves with reddish-purple undersides

A dwarf upright and compact deciduous shrub. Striking small red leaves that are more green in colour towards the base of the plant, turn bright red in autumn. Grown very much for its leaf colour but has quite tiny clusters of pale yellow flowers in spring followed by small red berries

A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with narrow, long, twisted green leaves with yellow margins that lighten to creamy-yellow. Mature plants display red speckled petioles. Lavender purple flowers appear on stems above the foliage in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with bright yellow heart to oval-shaped foliage. Upright, slightly purplish stems of pale, lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with thick, variegated, heart-shaped golden yellow foliage with a blue-green centre. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and wide yellow margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
An upright perennial, to 1.2m high, with narrowly oval-shaped, toothed green leaves. Tall stems bear loose clusters of open bell-shaped, violet blue flowers with white centres in summer
A clump-forming perennial with large lime leaves with red-black veining. Leaves go pink in colour in autumn and bear panicles of bright pink flowers through summer.

A mound forming perennial, with large rounded palmate lime-gold foliage with red centre in spring and autumn. In summer leaves change to red veined leaves over lime-gold foliage. small white panicles of flowers in summer.
A clump-forming perennial with bright orange-red glossy palmate leaves, panicles of white flowers tinged with pink in summer

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing rounded, lobed purple/ pink leaves with darker veins and slender, upright stems bearing panicles of small, bell-shaped, pink flowers from late spring into summer.

A clump-forming perennial to about 25cm high, forming a mound of rounded, lightly lobed, dark reddish purple leaves. Loose sprays of bell-shaped, pale yellow flowers are held on dark red stems above the foliage, from late spring into summer

A clump-forming perennial with gently ruffled and attractively veined leaves appearing pink to red in spring before turning shades of orange to burgundy as the seasons progress. Small white flowers are held above the foliage in late spring and early summer.

A compact, clump-forming perennial to about 20cm high, forming a mound of lobed leaves in shades from pale tan and peach to deep red. Loose sprays of small white flowers are held on slender stems above the foliage in summer
A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing lobed, purple / bronze leaves marked with darher veining. Slender stems bear small, bell-shaped, white flowers from late spring into summer.

Perennial bulb with strap-shaped, deciduous foliage. In late spring, globe-shaped flowerheads, up to 7cm across, comprising starry white 6-petalled flowers with lavender stamens and purple anthers, are borne above the foliage
Tall bulbous perennial about 90cm in height, with long, linear mid-green leaves and bearing large globular umbels of pinkish-purple starry flowers to 15cm across, in late spring and early summer
Bulbous perennial, to 1m tall, with glossy, strap-shaped mid-green leaves. Dome-shaped, fairly open flowerheads comprising reddish-purple flowers are borne from late spring into early summer
A curious ornamental cultivar that bears umbels that open in early summer. Each purple flower is held on a long wiry stem. These umbels develop bulbils at their base. Height to around 50cm

This selection, with green foliage,bears single flowers with narrow, incurved petals. Superficially white with a yellow eye, on closer inspection, each petal is outlined in red with red and yellow flashes at the base. Height around 60cm

A clump-forming, bulbous perennial to 20cm high with linear, semi-upright leaves. In spring, leafless stems bear dense heads of small, urn-shaped, soft pink flowers with paler, almost white flowers at the tips
A medium sized, spiny evergreen shrub with glossy green leathery serrated leaves up to 9cm long. Clusters of approximately 2-6 yellow flowers develop into egg-shaped dark black berries in autumn

A fast-growing medium-sized deciduous tree to a height of 7m with attractive pinkish brown and copper bark with white markings (lenticels). Dark green foliage appears in the spring, turning to a buttery yellow colour in the autumn
Short-lived, compact, clump-forming, herbaceous perennials to 40cm producing a basal mound of divided, blue-green leaves. Nodding, short-spurred, yellow flowers appear in late spring and early summer

A short-lived, compact, herbaceous perennial to 40cm, with pale blue-green divided leaves. Upward-facing, spurless, double, pompon-like flowers up to 4cm across, with narrow, light rose pink petals, appear in late spring and early summer

A compact evergreen shrub to around 1m high, with small, glossy green leaves streaked with yellow in the centre and tinted dark bronze at the margins. Leaf colour deepens in autumn and winter to a dark purple-bronze that is almost black, with touches of red and green in the centre. Flowers in spring are green, small and insignificant

an evergreen shrub with a spreading then upright habit. Glossy, slightly wavy green leaves are edged with yellow before turning green and orange in the summer and darkening to burgundy and brown by winter

A vigorous twining climber, with a woody base and pinnately divided, light green leaves. Produces pendent clusters, up to 40cm long, of lightly fragrant, pale violet-blue double flowers in late spring

A compact deciduous shrub to 1m high, with an open habit, dark reddish stems and narrowly ovate, serrated dark green leaves that turn red in autumn. In summer, produces rounded heads of densely packed white flowers, with lightly feathered edges to the petals. Flowers develop a tint of pink or red as they age

A deciduous shrub to 1.2m high, with ovate, serrated green leaves that turn bright red and orange in autumn. In summer, loose lace-cap type flower heads open to clusters of tiny fertile flowers, with larger florets held on short, delicate stems around the edges. Flower colour varies depending on the pH of the soil, from pale pink to soft blue, and deepens as the flowers age

primary_name: Aquilegia vulgaris var. stellata 'Pink Barlow' (Barlow Series)
description: A short-lived perennial to 80cm with divided, dark green leaves. Nodding, spurless, double, pompom-like flowers, with narrow, rich pink petals, appear in late spring and early summer

alternative_names: fringed primrose|Primula auricula subsp. ciliata (Moretti) Lüdi|Primula auricula L. subsp. balbisii

description: A dense, bushy, evergreen shrub to 1m tall with glossy, dark green leaves and clusters of small, white, very fragrant winter flowers followed by red berries

Small, compact ornamental cherry tree or shrub, about 1.2m tall, with small, toothed dark green leaves, to 6cm, bronze-red when young, then with good red and orange autumn colour. Very free-flowering with pink buds opening to white with a dark pink eye, appearing before the leaves in early to mid-spring; suitable for tubs and bonsai

A woody climber to around 4m in height, with pale green foliage which turns to yellow in the autumn. Dense, long, hanging racemes of fragrant, showy blue flowers appear in early summer. More compact and less vigorous than other varieties, it is a good option for smaller gardens and may be grown in a large container

Large, vigorous, deciduous climber about 9m tall, with twining stems, and green leaves divided into leaflets, that turn butter-yellow in autumn. Drooping racemes to 30cm long, of scented, pea-like, mauvish-blue flowers, marked violet-mauve, produced in late spring, often followed by bean-like velvety, blue-grey seed pods 15cm long. Free-flowering from a young age

A slow-growing, upright, deciduous tree about 15m tall, the 3-5 lobed palmate, dark green leaves to 10cm long, greyish-white beneath, turning yellow to deep red in autumn. Upright clusters of tiny red flowers are borne in spring followed by dark red winged fruits in autumn.

An erect, branched, twiggy shrub to 2m in height, with green stems turning to orange-red in winter, bearing green leaves in spring, then yellow in summer, turning to shades of yellow, red and burgundy in autumn. Creamy flowers in late spring to early summer followed by round, white berries ripening to blueish-white

A deciduous large shrub or tree bearing large, furrowed, pear-shaped aromatic fruits in autumn that ripen to yellow. The smooth, pale yellow flesh turns pale pink when cooked but stays firm. The leaves of this cultivar are large when compared to other quinces but retain the characteristic green upper surfaces and downy-silvery-grey undersides

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches to 70cm in height when in flower. It forms a mound of green, deeply divided leaves and strong flower stems of double, frilly, pale lilac flowers with creamy yellow or pale green centres, from early to late summer
A simple yet stunning coneflower variety producing melon-yellow flowers with an orange central cone. Excellent as a cut flower, for growing in containers and for attracting pollinators

A compact, mound-forming perennial to 35cm tall with deeply-lobed mid-green leaves with slight yellowish mottling. Pale lilac-pink, outward-facing flowers with darker veining are borne form summer into autumn

A medium to large, slow-growing deciduous tree to around 4m in height, with an upright, columnar habit. Fan-shaped leaves emerge pale green in spring, turning darker green in the summer then golden in the autumn. Green flowers appear in April, but as this is a male cultivar, it will not produce fruit. Makes an attractive addition to smaller gardens and patios where space is at a premium

An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 60cm in height when in flower with green, linear grass-like leaves and spikes of tubular, pale peach flowers that emerge from deep orange buds in summer and autumn.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial up to 75cm, with narrow grass-like leaves, with narrow spikes with orange buds that open to bright, yellowish orange flowers.

Vigorous, upright, columnar tree to about 10m in height, producing broad, mid-green leaves, and bearing slender, pointed, deep pink buds which open to reveal tulip-shaped, paler pink blooms, darker at the base of the tepals, over a long period in mid to late spring
A dwarf, clump-forming deciduous perennial with aromatic green-yellow foliage and short, upright spikes of lavender-blue flowers appearing in the spring and summer
A spreading perennial up to 20cm high and 50cm wide, with lax stems bearing grey-green leaves and terminal whorls of purple flowers in summer and early autumn

A dense, tussock-forming, evergreen grass to 1m tall in flower, with rough, rigid, linear leaves. From early to late summer it produces airy, arching panicles of brown flower spikelets. The flower spikes can be cut for fresh and dried floral arrangements
A compact climber to around 1.5m tall producing small, white flowers to 8cm across; early flowers are sometimes double

A deciduous climber to about 2m, flowering in late spring to early summer on old wood and again from late summer to early autumn on new wood. The rosette-like, purpleflowers have six to eight large outer petals and a double centre but both the depth of colour and the flower shape can vary from plant to plant

primary_name: Corydalis aff. glaucescens from Ihnachsai Gorge, Uzbeckistan

description: A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 45-50cm in height, with dark green foliage. Single flowers have broad, rounded, bright pink petals and a yellow-banded, dark reddish central disc, blooming from midsummer until the first frosts
A dwarf, bedding dahlia to about 30cm with dark stems and mid-green foliage. Single, clear pink flowers with a yellow centre are produced from mid-summer until frosted in autumn
A dwarf, bedding dahlia to about 30cm with dark stems and mid-green foliage. Single, rich red flowers with a dark yellow centre are produced from mid-summer until frosted in autumn

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, banana-yellow flowers with a green throat to18cm across in summer
A woody-based, bushy perennial with aromatic foliage and two-tone blue flowers in open, upright spikes from early summer into autumn
A bulbous perennial, to around 1.2m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped glossy dark green leaves. Upward-facing, bright yellow flowers with a green throat appear in the summer

A mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Rich deep blue-purple, four-petalled flowers , are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

A mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Bright blueish-purple, four-petalled flowers with a white eye, are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

primary_name: Anemone × hybrida 'Pretty Lady Julia' (Pretty Lady Series)

description: A compact plant, 25-30cm, with pure white double flowers and outstanding, spicy scent in summer. May repeat flower

An upright, palm-like shrub or small tree, to around 3m high in good conditions, with upright to arching, lance-shaped leaves held at the tips of the branches. Leaves are deep pink with dark reddish-purple centres. In late spring and early summer, mature plants produce a mass of tiny, fragrant, creamy-white flowers
An upright perennial bulb to around 40cm with broadly lance-shaped, curled dark green foliage. Yellow, cup-shaped flowers with dark red stripes and fringed edges appear in April to May

A low-growing, tender, spreading perennial with dark green, lobed leaves and large, daisy-like red and yellow flowers with large yellow centres, appearing in summer to autumn. Flowers open in the sunshine and close when cloudy

An upright, clump-forming soft perennial, also grown as an annual, with moderately green ovate-elongated leaves and erect stems bearing terminal spikes of soft pink two-lipped flowers with darker tubes and centres from mid-summer to autumn.

A highly coloured sport of ‘Discovery’, this early, dessert apple has bright red skin, and shows a rosette-shaped, pink stain when cut in half. Straight off the tree it has a crisp, juicy texture with a fresh, sweet/sharp flavour but this soon fades. Compact trees produce a heavy crop in late summer and early autumn. Requires a group 1, 2 or 3 pollinator

A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are golden yellow with a large red eye and a green-yellow throat
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are orange-gold and slightly fragrant
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are red with a green-yellow throat and a frilly edge to the petals

Vigorous, twining, evergreen climber about 10m tall, with elliptic polished dark green leaves to 16cm long. White, cream or yellow long-stalked, scented flowers composed of up to 25 sepals, 2.5cm long are produced in summer and followed by very large clusters of scarlet-red berries in autumn

primary_name: Lilium formosanum short, from high altitude (IXb/a)

description: Slim, elegant, evergreen shrub or small tree about 5m tall bearing long slender, papery bright green leaves to 14cm long with orange bristly hairs along the prominent veins underneath. Yellow flowers are produced singly or in small umbels from the leaf axils mid autumn to early spring followed by black fruit, late spring to late summer, on female plants if pollinated by a male plant

primary_name: Magnolia sieboldii subsp. sieboldii from Korea

description: A species of clump-forming perennial to 30cm, with narrow, lance-shaped green leaves clasping the stems. Violet-pink and white striped 3-petalled orchid or iris-like flowers appear from summer to November

primary_name: Sarcococca aff. vagans from north Thailand

description: A small, rounded, evergreen coniferous shrub with a slightly untidy, tangled appearance. Bears dense, yellow-green sprays of scale-like evergreen foliage.

alternative_names: white cedar [Golden Smaragd]|white cedar 'Janed Gold'|Thuja occidentalis 'Janed Gold'
description: A compact, dense conical-shaped evergreen conifer with golden-yellow needles
a tender perennial with arching, semi-trailing stems and long, narrow, toothed, triangular, mid-green leaves. Bright pinky-red, semi-double flowers are produced from late spring to autumn
Bushy upright rose to about 75cm tall with dark green foliage and clusters of very fragrant, ivory-cream, fully-double blooms repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

A low-growing, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 40cm high, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Large, single, buttercup-yellow flowers are held on stems above the foliage from late April to early June
Flowers emerge snow white in early spring to become light pink, while leaves become greener. Winter foliage is very dark by contrast, compact and glossy with red and purple highlights.
A compact, evergreen, clump-forming sedge forming mounds of variegated, arching, yellow leaves with dark green margins; tiny brown flowers are borne on short spikes in summer
A clump-forming perennial about 55cm tall, with dark green foliage, and bearing glowing, deep red semi-double flowers with yellow disk centres, flowering from mid to late autumn

A clump-forming, rhizomatous, hardy evergreen perennial with tall, narrow dark green leaves. Rarely, white and dark red, star-shaped flowers appear at the base of the plant in spring to summer. Although most often grown as a houseplant, it is also a useful garden plant in mild areas, and is tolerant of shade and drier conditions

A clump-forming, rhizomatous, hardy evergreen perennial with long, narrow, broadly lance-shaped glossy dark green leaves with creamy-white spots. Rarely, small, star-shaped purple flowers appear at the base of the plant in early spring. Although most often grown as a houseplant, it is also a useful garden plant in mild areas, and is tolerant of shade and drier conditions
An upright evergreen shrub to 5m high, with glossy dark green ovate leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces semi-double pink flowers with long, inward folding petals in mid to late spring
A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with glaucous green, scalloped foliage and tall, slender stems forming a dense mass of small, ruby red, oval flower spikes in summer and early autumn

alternative_names: mountain blue vervain 'Lavender Spires'|Verbena 'Lavender Spire'|Verbena 'Lavender Spires'
description: A clump-forming perennial to 1.8m tall with rough, narrow leaves. Branching spikes of small lavender flowers are borne from mid-summer to autumn

A compact bushy deciduous shrub reaching up to 50cm in height. Leaves undivided, ovate to oblong, in pairs, green with a more glaucous underside. Flowers are fragrant, borne in clusters at the ends of the shoots. Flower buds are purple-pink, opening to pink-white becoming orange-yellow as the flowers mature
A bushy, relatively compact perennial to 55cm tall forming mounds of greyish-green, aromatic foliage topped with spikes of intense violet-blue flowers in summer

A summer-dormant perennial autumn-flowering bulb with large terminal umbels of wavy-petalled funnel-shaped pale pink flowers held by a red stem, followed by the growth of rich green long, strappy foliage in autumn once the temperature drops.

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 75cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped variegated green and yellow striped leaves and double orange flowers with carmine red hues in summer

A compact, clump-forming, evergreen perennial, to 25cm tall, with dark red stems and leaves, flushed copper on the upper surface and with lobed edges. Short, compact spikes of pale yellow flowers are produced in large numbers over a long period from late spring to early autumn

primary_name: Canarina canariensis from Los Silos, Tenerife
Canarina canariensis from Anaga Mountains, Tenerife

description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 90cm high, with divided green leaves. Large, scented, densely double white flowers are produced in early summer
An herbaceous perennial to 20cm high, with rosettes of broadly oval, wrinkled green leaves. Produces lacy lilac flowers veined with blue, in loose clusters on upright stems in spring

A hardy evergreen shrub with an upright habit approximately 30cm tall with a spread to 25cm. It has dark green foliage with mid-green new shoots in spring and tapering stems of white buds in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub approximately 30cm tall with a spread to 25cm. It has light green foliage that turns light greenish-yellow in winter and spikes of white buds in summer through to autumn.
A hardy evergreen shrub with a bushy habit approximately 30cm tall with a spread to 25cm. It has dark green foliage with mid-green new growth and lilac-pink buds in summer through to autumn.
A hardy, evergreen shrub approximately 30cm tall and a spread to 25cm. It has dark-green foliage and ruby coloured buds.

Robust, deciduous climber to about 2.5m tall, with mid to dark green leaves and lime green buds that open to lightly scented, semi-double lemon-yellow flowers aging to white, with wavy-margined, slender, pointed tepals and pale lemon anthers, flowering in late spring with later flowers in mid to late summer

An evergreen shrub to about 1.5m high, with a spreading habit, and elliptic green leaves. Produces rounded clusters of up to 23 broadly funnel-shaped, dark reddish-purple flowers, with wavy edges and near black speckles on the upper petals, in late spring

A bushy subshrub to 90cm tall, evergreen if not cut back by the frosts, with aromatic, small, ovate, mid to dark green leaves. Large bright cherry-red flowers are borne in terminal racemes over a long period from late spring to autumn
A large, upright, deciduous shrub or small tree to around 6m in height with rounded, mid-green foliage. Large, goblet-shaped white flowers with a hint of pink appear in March to April
A green-leaved tuberous-rooted perennial to around 1m tall. The giant, fully double blooms, to 30cm in diameter, are pale, peachy-bronze in summer and early autumn
A tuberous-rooting perennial about 1.5m tall, with green serrated leaves and bearing Collerette form yellow flowers around a golden eye in summer and early autumn
A cultivar which bears pale-yellow flowerheads, tinged with pale pink, in summer and early autumn. Height to 1.5m; flowerhead to 25cm wide
A compact and low growing shrub ideal for containers and pots. Small, dark pink rose-form double flowers appear in mid to late winter.

A spreading, decidous tree to about 10m or more in height, with an oval crown and large, mid-green leaves. Produces large, pure white, upright flowers to 30cm across, with 9 tepals and contrasting pink stamens, the flowers occasionally flushed pink at the base, appearing before the leaves in early to mid-spring

primary_name: Achillea [Desert Eve Deep Rose] ('Desderos') (Desert Eve Series)
description: A compact, clump-forming perennial to 30cm high forming mounds of aromatic, finely-divided leaves and bearing flattened heads of small, deep pink flowers in summer on erect stems

A clump-forming perennial to around 70cm tall with lobed and toothed leaves. In summer, erect stems bear small clusters of flower heads made up of tiny white flowers surrounded by pinkish-white bractstipped with green
A vigorous, clump-forming perennial, to around 40cm high, with a spreading habit and glossy, lobed green leaves. Loose clusters of white flowers are produced from late spring to early autumn

primary_name: Geranium platypetalum 'Dark Side of the Moon'

description: A semi-evergreen, mat-forming perennial, to around 20cm high, with spreading runners and rounded, lobed green leaves. Flowers are lilac pink with white edges, and are produced in early and mid-summer

A clump-forming perennial to 30cm tall with lobed, hairy, mid green leaves. Reddish stems bear nodding, single, pale lemon-yellow flowers with lightly ruffled petals tinged pink along the edges, which appear from late spring to summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, nearly white flowers with a green throat to 15cm across in late summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and double orange flowers with a dark lavender-purple eyezone and petal edges to around 15cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of large, fragrant, frilly pale yellow flowers with a red edge, a central red band and bright yellow-green throat

An upright, deciduous tree with a pyramidal crown eventually reaching to 20m tall. Its distinctively lobed and variegated leaves are green with creamy-white margins and turn yellow in autumn. Mature specimens produce tulip-shaped, greenish flowers with orange markings at the base of each petal

alternative_names: Primula × pubescens 'Peggy Fell'|Primula auricula 'Peggy Fell'|Primula 'Peggy Fell'
description: A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage with a silvery coating, and fragrant, purple flowers with a white eye, appearing from late-winter to mid-spring

A biennial to around 90cm tall with finely-divided dark green leaves and, in summer, erect, branching stems bearing umbels of tiny white-pink flowers that darken with age to shades of reddish-purple and dark purple

A relatively compact herbaceous perennial, growing to about 50cm tall, with clumps of strap-shaped green leaves. This cultivar flowers freely in the summer producing loose clusters of rich sky-blue flowers with a darker stripe running through each petal

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 86cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and fragrant, lemon-yellow flowers that have a green throat to 13cm across in summer. The flowers remain open at night
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 157cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and red flowers with a yellow throat to 13cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, white flowers from mid-summer to autumn.
An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 80cm in height, producing a clump of green strap-like leaves and rounded heads of dark blue purple tubular flowers in summer.
An herbaceous perennial that forms clumps of strap-like leaves and rounded heads of indigo-black, pendulous, tubular flowers in summer reaching approximately 80cm in height.

An evergreen perennial cultivar with strappy leaves that are softly hairy and wrinkled. Flowers are double with ruffled blue central petals. Upper lobes are blue, lower ones white with purple and violet-blue blotches and veining

A compact, tender perennial with strap-shaped, dark green leaves and clusters of up to ten flowers per stem borne over a long period from early spring until late autumn. Flowers comprise pale yellow lower petals streaked with purple veining and pure white, ruffled upper petals
A tender perennial with mid green, strap-shaped leaves. Violet blue and pale yellow flowers up to 5.5cm across are borne in loose clusters over a long period from spring into early autumn

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 50cm tall. Its large, rounded leaves are covered in fine hairs and may be deciduous in cold areas. In spring, short spikes of very pale pink flowers, that darken with age, are borne on red stems

Has bright green veining through frosted silver heart-shaped leaves, which are creamier when young, delicate sprays of 5-petaled, blue flowers. A mutation of Brunnera 'Silver Lace'. Good for ground cover.

An evergreen perennial forming a clump of lance-shaped leaves to 20cm long. In summer it produces pinkish red, spherical flowerheads to 4cm across, held on strong stems to 35cm tall. Makes a good cut flower

A bushy, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial with tall, dark stems, aromatic, wrinkled grey-green foliage and upright spikes of pale lilac to white flowers, which are produced throughout the summer
A midseason lactiflora variety with sweet-scented, double pink flowers with silvery edges. Excellent as a cut flower

A mat-forming, creeping perennial which can become invasive. Foliage usually comprises three deep maroon-red leaflets marked with green at the base and clusters of small, light pink flowers are held on short stalks from spring into summer

A bulbous perennial to around 30cm tall with stems bearing 2-3 flowers up to 3.5cm wide. Each flower has white, overlapping perianth segments and a cup-shaped, loosely-ribbed corona that opens orange and may become paler sometimes with yellow at the base

primary_name: Clematis integrifolia from Lake Baikal, Russia
description: A bushy, deciduous perennial with an informal habit, reaching a height of around 60cm, with dark green leaves. Masses of large, lavender-blue bell-shaped flowers with upturned petals, appear from late May through to September

A bulbous perennial, to around 60cm high, with narrow, upright green leaves. Flowers have slender, coppery bronze standards, and orange-brown falls with a yellow centre spot. Flowers from late spring to early summer

A bulbous perennial with whorls of leaves on upright stems, to about 1m tall. Scented, light yellow flowers, flushed pink towards the tips of the reflexed petals, with dark red spots and prominent orange anthers, are produced in summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Small, golden orange-yellow heavily spotted downward-facing flowers with recurved petals appear in the summer
A clump-forming, cormous perennial to 1.25m, with narrowly sword-shaped leaves to 75cm long. In summer it produces branched spikes of up to 20 orange flowers; these are good for cutting
A winter or early spring flowering bulbous perennial to 60cm tall, producing 1 or more stout stems, each bearing 3-4, raspberry red, funnel-shaped flowers to 12cm across

A semi-evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high, forming a spreading clump of deeply lobed, aromatic green leaves. Near white flowers, with prominent stamens and pale pink calyces, are produced in early summer

A large very handsome, medium to fast-growing deciduous tree to 20m. The leaves are green and around 12cm long with very deep lobes, almost to the mid-vein. Each lobe has a few rounded secondary lobes. The grey-brown acorns are at least half enclosed in a scaley cup. No autumn colour

Stately, clump-forming perennial to 2.4m tall with very bold, broad, purple-red leaves to 60cm long, with a contrasting green pattern between the veins. Bright, brilliant red flowers appear above stout stems from midsummer to mid-autumn
A medium-sized, deciduous shrub to 1.5m tall with green to golden-yellow leaves and clusters of white flowers in summer followed by red fruits

A slow growing evergreen conifer with a very distinctive presence. The narrow pyramidal habit is sparsely covered with branches which are covered in short and twisted green needles giving the branches a skinny, tail-like appearance. It will need staking to develop a strong central leader and has an annual growth rate of 10cm per year

Small, spreading deciduous tree about 3m tall, with distinctive foliage colours, purplish pink, edged bright pink in spring, then deepening to purple-red in summer, followed by deep red autumn colour. Inconspicuous hanging clusters of small, purple-red flowers in spring are followed by red-flushed, winged fruits

A compact, clump-forming, semi-evergreen to evergreen perennial bearing lobed, rounded, dark purple to dark red leaves and slender, upright, maroon stems bearing open panicles of pale pink flowers from early summer into autumn.

A compact, clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial producing dark pink foliage with darker veining and lime green edging. Pink-red flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with mounds of mid-green foliage. Flowers are dark pink almost maroon, with lance-shaped dark pink bracts, forming a ruff around the flowers

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a tiered, spreading habit and oval-shaped, glossy, mid-green foliage with pink and white margins, turns to red and purple in the autumn. Small white flowers appear early to mid-summer, followed by red and pink fruit in the autumn

A neat, compact, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen herbaceous perennial producing golden foliage with red veining. Thick stems of small, dark pink flowers appear throughout the spring and summer
A compact mound forming perennial with lemon-lime green palmate leaves, panicles of bicoloured cerise and pale pink flowers

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing attractive, lobed, caramel and pink / purple coloured leaves, marked with darker veining in the centre. Flowers less freely than many other cultivars but can bear slender stems with tiny, bell-shaped, white flowers from late spring into summer.

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with deeply lobed, silver-flushed, purple leaves, darker at the veins and flushed pink to orange in spring and autumn. Slender stems bear open panicles of tiny, bell-shaped, white flowers from late spring into summer.

alternative_names: lungwort 'Pierre's Pure Pink'|Pulmonaria saccharata 'Pierre's Pure Pink'
description: A compact, clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing ovate, green leaves with white or silvery spots. In mid-spring the plant displays clusters of bell-shaped, pale pink flowers
A low-growing, widely spreading, evergreen shrub with bright green foliage and golden-yellow branch tips. Growth rate is slow to moderate, eventually reaching 30cm in height.
A semi-evergreen, climbing, bushy perennial with dark green foliage and abundant pendent flowers which have a dark purple corolla and pink-red sepals and stamens from summer through to autumn

A tuberous perennial to 40cm with long-stalked, deeply lobed, mid-green foliage. In late spring and early summer upright, branching stems bear fully double flowers with many rows of ruffled, satiny, deep red-purple petals

alternative_names: Stokes' aster 'Mel's'|Stokesia laevis 'Mel's Blue'|Stokesia laevis [Mel's Blue]
description: An upright, clump-forming semi-evergreen perennial with leathery, soft spiney dark green leaves. Large fringed violet-blue flowers are produced in the summer

A deciduous shrub which slowly grows to approx 3m tall and wide. It has green heart-shaped leaves and in late spring/early summer, has many clusters of mauve semi-double flowers which are very sweet-smelling

A medium-sized semi-evergreen or deciduous tree to around 15m in height. The leaves emerge coppery red then become green and are around 15cm long with shallow teeth at the tip end. The acorns are large and in a warty cup. The leaves remain a long time on the tree, often only falling just before the new ones emerge

An upright, evergreen shrub with large, arching leaves divided into lance-shaped, dark green leaflets that are tinted reddish-bronze when young. Spreading racemes of bright yellow flowers borne in dense terminal clusters in late winter and early spring are folllowedby blue-black berries

A mid-sized deciduous tree, to around 4m high in 10 years, and up to 10m high at maturity. It has an upright then spreading habit, and broadly oval green leaves. Flowers are pale pink, flushed with soft yellow on the outsides, and are produced just before or alongside the new leaves in spring

A leafy shrub to around 1.2m high, with an open habit and small, compound leaves divided into three narrow leaflets. Leaves are dark reddish purple when young, and mature to deep green, with tints of red in autumn and winter. Produces small white flowers from pink buds in spring; when pollinated these are followed by persistent round red berries

A small, deciduous tree up to 7m tall with elliptic to oblong leaves 10-15cm long with finely serrate margins. Leaves emerge bronze-reddish in colour, maturing to green with hairy, white undersides and contrasting brownish veins. Dense, tight clusters up to 7cm across of small white, spring flowers are followed by rounded, red fruits

An upright, deciduous shrub, to 2m in height and spread, with very glossy, long, oval leaves which turn wine-red in autumn. Flat heads of creamy-white flowers in mid-summer are followed by large clusters of berries maturing from pale green through white, pink and blue to black, and remaining after the leaves have fallen. This cultivar is self-fertile

A very dwarf, slow-growing form which unlike the typical species produces tightly compact, flattened globes up to 20-30cm (8-12in) high. The mid-green needles are small, stiff, and very densely produced, so that the stems and basal branches are completely covered. It is an ideal choice for a small city, or courtyard garden, for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which unlike the typical species, produces a low, compact, spreading bush up to 90cm (3ft) high and 1.2m (4ft) across. The dark green needles are slightly wavy, giving the plant a ruffled texture and are very densely produced, so that the stems and basal branches are completely covered. It is an ideal choice for a small city, or courtyard garden, where an architectural or evergreen focal point is needed; for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery
A compact, slow-growing, dense, mound-forming conifer with upward facing branches producing yellow tipped dark green needles. Small ovoid brown cones are produced in the autumn

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which produces a compact, flattened, globe to dome-shaped bush, reaching about 50cm (20in) high and 75cm (30in) across after ten years. It has a neat, densely branching habit. The thin needles are produced in bunches of five at the tips of the stems and are around 6-8cm (2½-5½in) long. They are curved to twisted and soft to the touch and are a silvery blue-green throughout the year. Their twisting gives the bush a ruffled appearance. It can produce cylindrical brown cones,10-20cm long. Its small size, means it is an excellent choice for a small, city or courtyard garden, where an architectural, or evergreen focal point is needed, as well as for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery
A mat-forming, evergreen perennial to 10cm tall, with fleshy, rounded, shiny green leaves, pink-flushed at the tips in cold weather. Small, starry yellow flowers are produced in summer

An attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large purple-pink blooms with horizontal ray petals, slightly toothed at the ends, surrounding a prominent central brown cone. Excellent for container growing and for attracting pollinators

A bushy, clump-forming deciduous shrub to around 4m in height, with maple-shaped green palmate leaves that turn to yellow, pink and red in the autumn. Flat, white lace-cap flowerheads are produced in late spring, and are followed by glossy red berries in late summer to autumn

A bushy, clump-forming deciduous shrub to around 3m in height, with maple-shaped green palmate leaves that turn to red and purple in the autumn. Flat, lace-cap white flowerheads are produced in late spring, and are followed by glossy red berries in autumn

A clump-forming daffodil to around 40cm high, with slightly grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are scented, around 6cm across, with lemon yellow petals, and a yellow cup that fades to near white. Late flowering, with up to five flowers to a stem
An upright, evergreen shrub with ovate, glossy, leathery, dark green leaves and, from midwinter to early spring, double, reddish-pink flowers with white petal margins

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus Harvington double purple cascade (d)
description: A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark green foliage and branched stems rising above with dangling cup-shaped dark purple double flowers in late winter and early spring.

A bushy, clump-forming semi-evergreen perennial with deeply divided, leathery, dark green leaves up to 45cm high and single, pink speckled, deep purple, pendent or outward facing flowers from late winter to early spring.

primary_name: Primula auricula 'Old Tall Purple Dusty Miller' (Au/B)
description: A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, coated with a silvery powder, and fragrant, dark purple flowers, with a white centre and yellow eye, appearing in the spring

primary_name: Molinia caerulea subsp. arundinacea 'Tears of Joy'

description: A compact, rounded herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall and wide. Bright yellow blooms to 5cm across cover the aromatic foliage in autumn

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 71cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and near white flowers that have a ruffled edge and a green throat to 15cm across in summer
An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 38cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and orange and red flowers with a green throat to 7cm across in summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with slightly cupped, variegated, blue-green foliage and cream margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A deciduous, bulbous, large herbaceous perennial to around 90cm, with strap-like dark green leaves and lightly-fragranced, dark red flowers, outward-facing and bowl-shaped and almost black in the centre, appearing from June to July
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with cup-shaped dark green foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 30cm high, with long, narrow pale yellow leaves with a fine blue-green margin and strongly rippled edges. Produces loose clusters of tubular, pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

An attractive, perennial coneflower variety producing bright flowers with orange-pink, narrow, ray petals, surrounding a dark red central cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A deciduous climber, to around 2.5m high, with mid-green oval-shaped leaves. Large, star-shaped flowers to 20cm across, with white petals feathered to raspberry pink at the edges, are produced in late spring and early summer, often with a second flush in late summer
A bulbous perennial which bears umbels of wine-red flowers opening to white. Those on top of the flowerhead are borne on elongated stems. Height to around 1m
A bushy, spreading evergreen sub-shrub or woody-based perennial, with aromatic, wrinkled grey-green leaves broadly edged with creamy yellow. Spikes of purple flowers are produced in early summer

Tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm in height, with mid-green foliage. Blooming from midsummer until the first frosts, the single, star-shaped flowers about 13cm across, have about 8 narrow, incurved orange petals surrounding a yellow central disc

A rare, semi-evergreen perennial to around 80cm in height, with velvety green, aromatic foliage. Cobalt-blue flowers appear throughout summer into the autumn. May require winter protection in colder parts of the UK
Bears pale pink, double blooms, around 10.5cm across, with a hint of apricot, above green foliage in summer and early autumn. Height 75-90cm
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Large, lavender pink-purple decorative form flowers, with a hint of white, appear from summer until the first frosts

A bulbous perennial, to around 15cm in height, with green, strap-like foliage and delicate pale blue flowers in early spring, with darker, royal-blue tips to the falls around a blue-veined, white and yellow central zone
A compact, bulbous perennial with erect, narrow, grey-green foliage. Rich blue-purple flowers with white and yellow markings appear in late winter to early spring
Vigorous semi-evergreen perennial about 15cm tall, producing attractive, spreading, intense burgundy-red foliage in spring, followed by short spikes of two lipped, deep blue-purple flowers
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with pale green leaves that have silver veining and panicles of small white flowers held above the foliage.

An evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 30cm in height, forming a neat mound of lobed leaves that open mid-pink in spring and change to a dusky pink to caramel, with a pink underside, as the foliage matures. Loose sprays of small, bubblegum pink flowers are held on slender stems above the foliage from late spring into summer
A compact, mound-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial with pink-orange foliage with a dark pink underside and darker veining. Panicles of white flowers appear above the foliage in the summer

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus (Party Dress Group) 'Party Dress Primrose' (d)

description: A low-growing, mound forming perennial. Lobed green leaves have deep red veining and a silvery veil. Produces upright stems to 60cm high of unusually large creamy white flowers above the foliage in summer
A neat mound forming perennial with large shiny brown leaves going orange in colour. Tall panicles of white-pink flowers
A shrub up to about 40cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant, deep purple flowers topped by paler violet bracts in summer
An vigorous, clump-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that has rounded silver leaves with dark green veins, flushed purple. Panicles of cream flowers appear above the foliage.

alternative_names: sage 'Royal Bumble'|Salvia microphylla 'Royal Bumble'|Salvia × jamensis 'Royal Bumble'
description: A bushy, evergreen shrub to 75cm high with aromatic, glossy, deep-green leaves. Large, rich glowing-red flowers with purple-black calyces and stems, appear over a long period from late spring to autumn
A mat-forming, evergreen perennial native to the Mediterranean with prostrate stems that bear ovate, aromatic, dark green leaves. Dense clusters of purple-pink flowers appear in summer

alternative_names: Oregon grape 'Esme'|Mahonia White House Farm hybrid

description: An insectivorous perennial forming rosettes to 30cm wide. The leaves are formed of hinged lobes to 6cm long, with 15-20 stiff spines at the margins; these interlock when the trap closes. The traps are yellow-green on the outside and flushed burgundy on the inside. White flowers to 1cm across are produced on slender stems above the foliage in early summer.

A clump-forming, evergreen epiphyte with green, arching and incurved leaves forming dense rosettes with silvery bases. The tubular violet-blue flowers are borne just above the foliage in spring and summer and the leaves blush red when the plant is in bloom
An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 1m tall with mid-green, divided foliage and sweetly-scented, dusky pink double flowers borne from mid- to late spring

primary_name: Paeonia lactiflora 'Elizabeth Queen of the Belgians'

alternative_names: peony 'Ma Petite Cherie'|Paeonia lactiflora 'My Petite Cherie'
description: An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, semi-double, soft-pink saucer-shaped flowers which have a centre of subtle yellow stamens appear in late spring and early summer

A spreading perennial to about 60cm, with grey-green, fern-like foliage. Upright, branching stems are topped with domed flowerheads of small, pinky-red flowers with gold centres, fading to straw yellow, from early to late summer

A bulbous perennial reaching a height of up to 50cm tall. It has green strap-like leaves and erect stems with dense clusters of star-shaped rose-pink flowers. These open from the bottom of the stems upwards from mid to late summer. Excellent as a cut flower and in containers.

primary_name: Aechmea nudicaulis var. capitata f. albomarginata

description: A vigorous, evergreen tropical vine with large, mid-green leaves that produce carnivorous pitchers from the extended midrib of the leaf. Pitchers are around 15cm long and 8cm wide at maturity, and pale yellow, with speckles and lips that are dark red on younger pitchers, and deepening to dark purple on pitchers lower down the plant

alternative_names: pearlbush 'Niagara'|Exochorda × macrantha [Snow Day Surprise]|Exochorda racemosa [Snow Day Surprise]|Exochorda × macrantha 'Niagara'
description: A fast-growing but compact variety which is a cross between E. racemosa and E. x macrantha 'The Bride'. An abundance of white flowers with yellow centres are produced from April until May. Good for borders or in a pot.

An evergreen, epiphytic bromeliad, with funnel-shaped rosettes of long, strappy leaves. Produces upright flower stems of small yellow flowers surrounded by large, bright, greenish yellow bracts in summer
A compact, evergreen perennial with grey-green foliage. Fragrant, single, fringed, white flowers have a deep maroon centre and are held on sturdy stems
