description: A bushy, upright shrub, to 1.5m tall, with dark green to bronze-coloured oval, toothed leaves. Flattened clusters of purple to red, sterile florets, with cream-coloured centres, surround the inner, purple, fertile florets in summer

A reasonably compact, upright, bushy, deciduous shrub with dark red-brown stems bearing ovate, toothed, dark green leaves, flushed bronze when young, and, in summer, rounded flower heads of red flowers with small cream centres.

A compact deciduous shrub to 1m high, with broadly oval, serrated dark green leaves. Dome-shaped clusters of flowers with strongly ruffled petals are produced in summer. Colours vary depending on the pH of the soil, from rich pink to violet and blue, and the flowers fade to green as they age

alternative_names: Korean feather reed grass 'Mona'|Calamagrostis from Korea
hellebore [HGC Pink Frost]|Helleborus × ballardiae 'HGC Pink Frost'|Helleborus × ericsmithii 'Pink Frost'|Helleborus 'Coseh 710'|Helleborus 'Pink Frost'
description: A clump-forming evergreen perennial, producing a 40cm mound of dark green leaves marbled or veined in silver. Outward-facing flowers are produced from mid-winter to mid-spring. Opening from pink buds, flowers emerge cream tinged with pink and darken to a deeper pink as they age

A semi-evergreen perennial forming a low mound of leathery, divided, dark green leaves with silvery veins and spiny edges. Flowers borne on short, erect, dark stems are creamy-white with pink reverses; pink and green tinges develop as the flowers age

A clump-forming, evergreen herbaceous perennial to about 30-35cm high, with leathery, dark green leaves. Upward-facing, pure white flowers, about 8cm across, with golden stamens, appear from early winter to early spring

alternative_names: leopard plant 'Osiris Café Noir'|Ligularia 'Osiris Café Noir'
description: A clump-forming perennial with a mid-sized mound of large, jagged-edged leaves that emerge deep black-purple, ageing to bronze shades and eventually turning to olive green. Tall stems of golden-yellow daisy flowers appear in summer. Performs best in moist soil

alternative_names: sand couch grass|Agropyron junceum subsp. boreo-atlanticum|Elytrigia juncea subsp. boreoatlantica|Agropyron junceiforme

description: A perennial bulb, up to 65cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Late flowering, with cup shaped, soft purple flowers with coppery brown edges

primary_name: Actinidia chinensis Planch. var. setosa H.L. Li

description: A small, upright, deciduous tree with smooth, grey bark and a tendency to sucker. The white flowers appear in hanging clusters, up to 10cm long, in spring starting before the bronzy young leaves unfurl. Juicy, edible, blue-black berries appear in summer, and the leaves turn to shades of red, yellow and orange in autumn
A compact, tuberous perennial to 50cm tall with wavy, dark green, broadly lance-shaped foliage and white summer flowers with a dark eye

primary_name: Diascia [Flying Colours Deep Salmon Improved] ('Dala Depsam') (Flying Colours Series)
alternative_names: twinspur [Flying Colours Deep Salmon Improved]|Diascia 'Dala Depsam'
description: A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 25cm in height with small, semi-trailing, dark green leaves. Dark salmon-pink flowers with darker centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

primary_name: Diascia [Flying Colours Red Improved] ('Disz0001') (Flying Colours Series)

description: A compact, upright, evergreen shrub to a height and spread of around 1.2m with narrow, spine-free leaflets. Masses of delicate spires of yellow, honey-scented flowers are borne in late summer and autumn, followed by blue-black berries
A compact shrub with purple-tinted oakleaf-shaped leaves. It produces lots of large, semi-double hot pink flowers, darker on the inside, from June until August. Good as a specimen plant or in borders

A compact evergreen shrub to around 1m high, with small, glossy, variegated green and yellow leaves that are flushed bright red in summer, and dark maroon in autumn and winter. Flowers in spring are green, small and insignificant

A relatively compact winter squash cultivar bearing teardrop-shaped fruits up to around 2.2kg on trailing stems up to around 1.2m long. The fruits are smooth skinned, blue-grey in colour with fine-grained, yellow-orange, sweet-flavoured flesh

A compact, clump-forming evergreen perennial with dark green, leathery, lightly marbled, divided leaves growing up to 35-40cm high. The large, white, outward facing flowers open from pink buds from mid-winter to spring.
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark green foliage. Branched stems bear flat, creamy green single flowers in late winter and early spring

A semi-evergreen clump-forming tender perennial with divided, leathery, dark blue-green foliage. Branched stems of flattish pale green to creamy white single flowers appear in late winter and early spring

alternative_names: dog hobble [Twisting Red]|Leucothoe axillaris 'Opstal20'|Leucothoe fontanesiana 'Twisting Red'
description: Compact, evergreen shrub about 1m tall with small, twisted dark green leaves, dark red when young then purplish-red in winter. Small, urn-shaped white flowers are produced in short racemes from the leaf axils, in late spring
An early-flowering deciduous perennial climber with dark green leaves. Large, rounded fully double white to pale blue flowers with yellow anthers, appear from June through to August
A bushy, evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green foliage and clusters of small, fragrant, dusky pink flowers in spring

A tuberous-rooted perennial to 1m, with dark stems and mid-green foliage, flowering from mid-summer until the first frost. The blooms have neat rows of tightly inrolled petals, forming a flattened ball 7-8cm across in a dusky blend of orange and pink
A compact cultivar, to 50cm tall, with green foliage. It bears bright yellow flowers in summer and early autumn
A dwarf cultivar that bears white flowers, with a hint of greenish-yellow at the centre as they open, in summer and early autumn. Height to 40-50cm
A compact decorative cultivar to around 50cm in height. It bears double, pink flowers in summer and autumn
A compact, green-leaved cultivar, bearing apricot blooms suffused with a pale gold in summer and early autumn

alternative_names: dahlia 'Dark Side of the Sun'|Dahlia 'Cindy's Circle'|Dahlia 'Mystic Haze'
description: A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 75cm, with very dark bronze, almost black, foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers have broad, rounded, pinkish-orange petals shading to yellow at the base, with a dark brown central disc opening to dark yellow
A clump-forming, compact perennial to 6cm tall, bearing large multi-layered blooms with white fringed petals a large yellow centre

An evergreen, small, clump-forming shrub up to 50cm high, with undivided, ovate to narrowly-elliptical, finely toothed leaves, 5 cm long. The young leaves, leaf stalks and stems flush bright red when in growth. Clusters of small, urn-shaped flowers appear in the spring.
A bulbous perennial with leafy stems to around 120cm topped in mid- to late summer with large, scented, upward-facing, vivid pink, bowl-shaped flowers

alternative_names: Tibetan cherry 'Dorothy Clive'|Prunus serrula Dorothy Clive form
description: A round-headed small deciduous tree to 10m in height, the trunk with shining coppery-brown young bark. Narrow green leaves turn yellow in autumn. The showy single pink flowers are borne in clusters in late spring

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 70cm, with dark stems and dark green foliage. Flowers, produced from mid-summer until the first frost, have pink petals, darker on the reverse and slightly incurved, creating a neat shape 15cm across, with a dark red centre

alternative_names: water primrose|clove strip|Ludwigia uruguayensis|Jussiaea repens|Ludwigia hexapetala
description: This plant is listed as an invasive non-native species in the UK – see Cultivation section for details A perennial aquatic plant with creeping stems that form dense mats over wet ground or float on the water surface. Bright yellow flowers are followed by cylindrical seed capsules

alternative_names: geranium [Precision Red Ice]|Pelargonium 'Sil Chris'|Pelargonium [Precision Red Bicolour]
description: A trailing plant with fleshy, ivy-shaped leaves and rounded clusters of semi-double, red flowers with pink feathering from late spring to early autumn

This is a short-lived perennial subspecies of Brassica oleracea from which perpetual kale has been bred. It has large waxy, green leaves with wavy to deeply serrated edges and a smooth or wrinkly surface. If left to flower, they will be yellow, becoming long seed pods. Harvest all year round

An evergreen grass, forming a dense clump to around 45cm high of very fine, arching leaves. Airy pale brown flower heads are held on thin wiry stems, upright at first and then arching to trailing, from late spring to mid summer

primary_name: Hydrangea macrophylla 'Black Steel Zaza' (Black Steel Series) (H)
description: A compact deciduous shrub to about 1m high, with broadly oval, rich green foliage and dark red, almost black stems. Dome-shaped clusters of flowers are produced in summer, that open lime green, and develop to pink, lilac or blue depending on the pH of the soil

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, double, saucer-shaped rich red flowers forming a ball of ruffled red petals inside appear in late spring and early summer.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to 90cm tall, with dark green, divided foliage and single, slightly pinkish-red flowers with golden anthers, in late spring and early summer
A biennial, to 75cm tall, with dark purple, divided leaves and pink and grey umbels of flowers in late summer
A perennial that has divided, palmate foliage that has dark tones when young. Flowering stems are tinged red and starry flowers in summer are also dark red
A spreading, upright perennial, to 1m tall, with oval green leaves. Upright spikes of bell-shaped, lilac flowers appear in summer

A semi-evergreen fern with clumps of ribbon-shaped, twice pinnate fronds growing from 60 to 100cm long and 40-60cm wide. The fronds are a glossy green with horizontal yellow bands that aremost pronounced in new growth

Compact growing, medium-sized (30 - 45cm) epiphytic orchid, with upright, 20-30cm long, evergreen leaves. New growth appears from the base of swolled stem - pseudobulb. Oval-shaped, slightly flattened pseudobulbs are partially covered by a pair of green, leafed sheaths. Linear, fleshy, mid-green, evergreen leaves are borne in pair at the tip of pseudobulbs. New flowering stems arise from the axils of young, mature pseudobulbs and the leafed sheaths. Up to 12 flowers approximately 8 cm across are carried on a long, arching stem. Star-shaped, pale pink or cream flowers are marked with deep red irregular spots. Lip is usually white, with frilled edge and darker markings or spots in the centre. A very popular and reliable intergeneric orchid hybrid.

More compact than its parents B. bracdiana and B. rex, with leaves reaching up to 35cm long and flower stems to 1m bearing up to12 tall, yellow-green scented flowers to 28cm long and 8cm wide with long thin petals and chestnut-brown barring and spots on a frilly lip
A highly floriferous cymbidium producing pendent racemes of 25 or more small rich pinkish-brown flowers with a maroon lip produced from winter to spring
A compact-sized, tolerant hybrid, flowering in summer with vibrant yellow, fragrant blooms.

A terrestrial orchid, more compact than its parents D. kingianum and D. Mini Pearl. It grows to 38cm tall, with leathery leaves and sprays to 30cm long of up to 10 long-lasting, dark pinkish-mauve flowers 2cm across, on upright stems from the pseudobulb tips in spring

A compact-growing, medium-sized, epiphytic orchid, producing a clump of small, light-green, ovoid, compressed pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb is covered with three leafy sheaths growing at the base and two leaves growing from the tip. Leaves are green or light-green, up to 35cm long and 3cm wide. Flowering stems up to 35cm long emerge from the base of mature pseudobulbs and carry large number of small, 3cm wide, brilliant yellow flowers.

A small to medium-sized, epiphythic orchid, with upright, narrowly oval, evergreen leaves. New growth appears from the base od swollen stems (pseudobulbs), which serve as a storage for water and nutrients. Each pseudobulb is oval-shaped, slightly flattened, carrying a pair of leaves. The plant typically flowers in autumn, but may produce flowers almost any time of year. New flowering stems arise from the base of the maturing pseudobulbs and carry numerous, small (2cm wide) sweetly scented flowers. Colour of flowers range depending on cultivar from pale cream or pink to a soft red. The plant often produces multiple, pendulous, simultaneously flowering stems for an impressive display.

Nelly Isler gx AGM is a vigorous, free-flowering epiphytic orchid to 25cm tall with ovoid pseudobulbs, each with 2-3 leaves to 20cm long. It bears spikes of fragrant, long-lasting, bright carmine-red flowers with a striking yellow blotch in the centre of the flower, the lip is a light pink colour with bold waterfall markings and attractive carmine spots and blotches; flowers can appear at any time of year and will last for a number of weeks

Medium-sized, sympodially growing epiphytic orchid, producing a clump of large, ovoid, compressed pseudobulbs, covered by two or three distichous leafy sheaths. Linear, fleshy, evergreen leaves up to 40cm long are borne in pair at the tip of each pseudobulb. Flowering stems can reach up to 75cm and emerge at the base of mature pseudobulbs, between the pseudobulb base and leafy sheaths. Branched racemes carry large number of small, approx 3 cm wide flowers. Colour may vary from ruby-red, orange to yellow with darker markings. Large, older plants with two or more mature pseudobulbs can often carry two or more inflorescences.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with ovate, light and dark green mottled, 12cm long leaves. Solitary flowers up to 10cm across, appearfrom the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 15 - 20cm tall erect stems. Apple green pouch (or slipper) is a modification of lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' which results in successfull collection of pollen and flower pollination. Green and white lateral sepals are largely fused and hidden behind the pouch. Petals are apple green and white, upper sepal is white with dark green stripes.

A tender evergreen hybrid slipper orchid to 30cm tall, with oval green leaves. Flowers are borne singly on long stems, usually in winter or early spring, though they may appear year round when grown under glass. Flowers are up to 10cm across and have a dark burgundy pouch, pale green petals with burgundy veining, and a burgundy speckled, pale green hood fading to white

A small, evergreen, upright growing epiphytic orchid. Broadly oval, green, approximately 10cm long leaves emerge from the centre of the plant. New flowering stems appear from the base of older leaves. This hybrid produces up to 15 small, long lasting flowers on cascading branched racemes up to 30cm long. Flowers measuring 4 - 5 cm in diameter are bilaterally symmetrical, white, flushed pink at the centre and with a dark pink or red prominent lip with yellow centre
An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing an arching spike of long-lasting, pale pink flowers with pale orange lips

An evergreen, epiphytic orchid suited for growing in a cool or intermediate greenhouse. It has narrowly oval, ribbed leaves and produces long-lasting sprays of fragrant flowers on long spikes; flowers are mottled a dark reddish-brown and green and have a broad, white, velvety lip heavily marked and streaked with purple

An evergreen, succulent shrub reaching a height of 70cm. The chunky leaves, up to 3.5cm long, are covered in a down of hairs and have 3-10 prominent dark-red "teeth" at their tips. Small, bell-shaped orange-yellow flowers are borne on short stems in summer

A compact, evergreen succulent to 10cm tall, bearing flattened, fleshy, grey-blue leaves which are neatly arranged around the stems, giving the plant the appearance of a pile of pebbles. From winter to spring it produces domed clusters of pink flowers

An erect, perennial epiphytic cactus with flat thin slightly scalloped, fleshy stems, rarely 3-ribbed. The crimson to scarlet, red funnel-shaped flowers to 12cm have contrasting yellow pollen and white stigma lobes
A tender succulent forming rosettes of red-purple coloured water-storing leaves producing multiple pink star shaped flowers over a long period of time

An evergreen succulent with 10cm rosettes of thick, pale green, spoon-shaped leaves densely covered in white hairs. The 10cm flower stems produce red and yellow, urn-shaped flowers in late summer and early autumn
A cactus to 15cm tall, with a dense covering of bristly, light brown to white spines. In spring it produces brilliant pink, funnel-shaped flowers to 3cm across

A tender, succulent perennial which produces a partially underground swollen stem or caudex, with snake-like green cylindrical stems that emerge radially from its centre to approximately 20cm (8in) in length. Narrow, lance-shaped leaves are produced at the tips of the stems as they grow and are approximately 1cm (½in) long, but are soon shed leaving the older parts of the stems bare. Short-stemmed, yellow-green floral bracts, reddish in bud, are produced along short-stems from the centre of the caudex in summer. New plantlets are produced at the tips of older stems and drop to the ground when developed sufficiently to sustain themselves and form new plants

A solitary cactus to 20cm diameter, with a spherical, grey-green stem and about 21 warty ribs. It bears fine, white radial spines and stiff, flattened, brown central spines. In summer funnel-shaped pink flowers are produced

A slow-growing evergreen succulent forming a low rosette of fleshy, triangular, wedge-shaped leaves; these are green with white markings and become pink-flushed in hot, sunny conditions. In late spring, white flowers are borne on an upright flower stem to 30cm tall

A succulent perennial that grows parltly sunken into the ground. Its buried leaves have a translucent area covering the whole of the tip to allow for light to come through for photosyntheisis. Flowers are inconspicous, off- white, held on wiry stems emerging in between the leaves with six tepals, grouped together in threes, one set curling upwards and the other set of three downwards. Flowering in spring and summer

A short-stemmed perennial succulent to 15cm tall, with upright rosettes of bright green, rigid, fleshy, rounded leaves; these become red-flushed in good light. In early summer the rosettes may elongate into a 60cm tall flowerstalk; this is crowded with small, scented, pale yellow flowers. After flowering the rosette dies, but there are usually many small plantlets forming around the base

A bulbous perennial, up to 15cm high, growing from autumn to spring, with narrow green leaves, up to 150mm long and 5mm wide. In autumn and early winter dense clusters of honey-scented, bell-shaped flowers, about 15mm wide, appear. Flowers are lilac-pink, flushed with a darker blue-lilac central stripe along each petal

alternative_names: sword-leaved Cape cowslip|Polyxena ensifolia var. ensifolia|Polyxena odorata
description: A bulbous perennial to 5cm tall, with two grooved leaves to 20cm long. In autumn it produces trumpet-shaped, sweetly-scented white flowers with reflexed petals

A fairly fast-growing, low-growing species of cacti to around 6cm in height, forming large grey-green cylindrical stems, densely covered with soft white spines. Rings of bright pink flowers with yellow centres appear in spring, close to the stems in contrast with the white spines. Easy to grow for those wanting to grow cacti for the first time

A mat-forming succulent to 5cm tall, with erect, 4-angled, toothed stems, the tips tinged red. In summer it bears solitary, pale yellow, star-shaped flowers; these emit an umpleasant smell to attract pollinating flies

A slow-growing, mat-forming succulent to 8cm tall, with one or two pairs of fat, fleshy, almost hemispherical leaves. The leaves are dark purple and speckled with brown dots. In spring, many-petalled bright pink flowers to 6cm across are produced

A cactus to 40cm tall, producing fragile, grey-green, cylindrical stems from a tuberous rootstock. Whitish spines arise from grey areoles and lie flat against the stems. Showy, pale yellow, sometimes copper-tinged flowers are produced in early summer
A clustering cactus with spherical stems to 10cm, bearing bristly spines and bright orange flowers to 3.5cm across in summer
A clustering cactus with spherical stems to 10cm, bearing bristly spines and bright reddish-orange flowers to 3.5cm across in early and mid summer

alternative_names: Marsoner's crown cactus|Rebutia marsoneri vattri|Rebutia krainziana|Rebutia marsoneri var. brevispina|Rebutia marsoneri
description: A freely clustering cactus to 5cm tall, with globose stems and spirally arranged ribs. Short, bristly white spines arise from the prominent white areoles. In spring it produces bright yellow to orange flowers from around the base of the stem
A small, clustering cactus with flattened, globular, warty stems to 4cm tall. Bristly, white spines arise from the spirally arranged areoles. In spring it produces showy, white, funnel-shaped flowers

A small, densely clustering cactus with flattened, globular, warty stems to 4cm tall. Short, white spines arise from the spirally arranged areoles. In spring it produces showy, pink, funnel-shaped flowers

A carnivorous perennial to 40cm tall, with slender, erect pitchers terminating in ruffled hoods. The pitchers emerge green, becoming dark pink with marbled hoods and purple veining. In spring, solitary, nodding, red flowers are produced on tall stems

alternative_names: brain cactus|wave cactus|Stenocactus zacatecasensis|Stenocactus erectocentrus|Echinofossulocactus multicostatus
description: A solitary or clustering cactus to 10cm tall, producing spherical stems with 100 or more wavy ribs. Yellow or grey spines arise from white, felted areoles. In spring it bears funnel-shaped, pink flowers with a darker pink stripe on each petal

Evergreen coniferous tree to 30m or more, with a regular, narrow, conical or columnar crown. Dense, rounded, glossy dark green leaves, notched, with a sunken midrib, are held in distinctive sprays where a proportion of the needles are swept forwards above the shoots, almost obscuring it. Slender, tapered, reddish-brown cones are 15cm long and 5cm wide

A vigorous, tall, evergreen conifer tree, remarkable for its blue foliage. This cultivar is slow-growing from the beginning, but after 7-8 years the growth rate becomes more moderate, eventually reaching the height of up to 20 metres. A very elegant cultivar of Fir with pyramidal crown and blue, upcurved needles, 1 - 3.5 cm long. After 15 years the tree will start producing attractive, up to 20cm long, blue seed cones, turning brown when mature.
A low-growing, branching dwarf conifer to 1.5m high, with rounded clusters of stiff, bright green needles, and numerous pale, whitish buds in spring

alternative_names: Winterocereus colademononis|Hildewintera colademononis|Cleistocactus winteri subsp. colademono
description: A trailing cactus with cylindrical, fleshy stems to 1m long, densely covered with white, hair-like spines. In spring it produces red or pink flowers to 5cm long. Best grown in a hanging basket in a conservatory or temperate greenhouse

alternative_names: daphne [Pink Fragrance]|Daphne × transatlantica 'Blapink'|Daphne × transatlantica 'Pink Fragrance'|Daphne × transatlantica [Spring Pink Eternal Fragrance]|Daphne × transatlantica 'Eternal Fragrance Pink'
description: A compact, rounded shrub, to 90cm tall, with small, semi-evergreen, lance-shaped leaves. Scented pink flowers, flushed white, open from deep pink buds and are borne over a long season from spring until autumn

A compact cultivar to a height of about 40cm, with dark purple foliage, that bears single flowers of lilac pink with a flush of white and a central eye that opens to yellow stamens in summer and autumn
A compact cultivar with dark purple foliage, growing to around 30-50cm. Single, creamy-white flowers with an inner yellow halo and central eye are borne through summer and early autumn

A reliable, versatile, early maincrop potato favoured by growers, to around 60cm in height, particularly recommended for making chips. The long, oval-shaped tubers have creamy-coloured skins, good resistance to disease and store well. Harvest July to October if planted from March to April
A compact cultivar to 70cm tall with deep purple-mahogany foliage. Single flowers borne in summer and early autumn have deep red, velvet-textured petals surrounding a yellow eye
A leafy biennial harvested in its first year, suitable for overwintering. It produces good yields of medium to dark green leaves.

Tuberous-rooted perennial to 1m in height, with mid-green foliage. Flowering from mid-summer until the first frosts, the rounded blooms have neat rows of tightly inrolled orange petals, forming a flattened ball about 7-9cm across

alternative_names: cottonweed|sea cottonweed|sea cudweed|Filago maritima|Diotis candidissima|Otanthus maritimus
description: An evergreen, silvery, woolly perennial subshrub to around 10–50cm tall, with small, oblong leaves and aromatic yellow flower heads 8–10 mm wide, blooming from June to September. The plant emits a strong, herbal scent, particularly from its foliage, which intensifies when crushed

A compact, upright, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with serrated dark green leaves. Pale yellow flowers with rosy-pink edges bloom profusely on upright stems from summer through until the first frosts of autumn

A clump-forming perennial, to 1.2m high in flower, with fleshy roots and narrowly lance-shaped, mid green leaves that die back after flowering. Tall spikes of small, densely packed, pure white flowers with long stamens are produced in early summer

alternative_names: Chrysanthemum montanum var. adustum|Leucanthemum vulgare subsp. montanum

description: A clump-forming deciduous perennial with upright stems and a tuft of dark green lance-shaped foliage at the base. Large, white daisy-like flowers with yellow centres appear from June to September

alternative_names: Ilex aquifolium 'Mutchagara'|Ilex maximowicziana var. kanehirae|Ilex mutchagara
description: A dense, branched evergreen shrub with smooth glossy green foliage. White flowers appear April followed by shiny black berries. Good for creating and evergreen hedge
An old fashioned, cordon salad tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces reliable crops of medium-sized red tomatoes with good flavour
A spreading, perennial succulent, with flat, fleshy grey-green leaves that appear to be threaded onto the stem like beads. Leaves take on a reddish tint at the edges when stressed

An evergreen, trailing succulent to around 30cm in height, forming long, thick layers of fleshy stems of jade green foliage with red edges. Clusters of star-shaped, pinkish-white flowers appear at the end of the stems in the spring. A great choice for cascading out of indoor pots and hanging baskets

description: A shrub or small tree with arching, sword-like, greyish-purple leaves with bright pink margins. Panicles of small, scented white flowers may be produced in summer and followed by rounded, white or blue-tinted berries

A semi-evergreen perennial, to 1cm high in flower, with ovate to lance-shaped, slightly serrated dark green leaves, wider at the base and narrower on the stems. Upright spikes bearing numerous nodding, tubular and slightly flattened, coral pink to apricot coloured flowers with dark spotted throats are produced from mid summer into early autumn

A semi-evergreen biennial or short-lived perennial, to 1.2m high in flower, with ovate to lance-shaped dark green leaves. Tall spikes bear nodding, tubular to bell-shaped pale pink flowers with deep reddish-purple blotches in the throats, from early to late summer

Clump-forming perennial, to 90cm tall, with alternating, strap-like green leaves and terminal clusters of peachy-pink flowers, the inner petals streaked yellow and speckled dark brown. Flowers appear in summer through to autumn

A clump-forming perennial about 80cm tall, with lance-shaped dark green leaves, and terminal clusters of funnel-shaped bright pink flowers, the inner petals streaked yellow with brown speckles and dark pink edges. Flowers appear from summer and into autumn

A clump-forming perennial, to 75cm tall, with lance-shaped mid-green leaves, and terminal clusters of mid-pink funnel-shaped flowers, flushed with dark-pink, the inner petals flushed yellow and cream with brown flecks. Flowers appear from summer to autumn

A compact, clump-forming perennial with dark green lance-shaped leaves and clusters of funnel-shaped magenta-pink flowers which have dark brown speckles and a yellow throat on the upper petals, flowering in summer and autumn

A compact, clump-forming perennial with dark green lance-shaped leaves and clusters of funnel-shaped, creamy-white flowers which have a pink throat and dark brown speckles on the inner petals, flowering in summer and autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial to 35cm tall, with dark-green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of striking bright orange funnel-shaped flowers which have yellow inner petals speckled dark brown, flowering in summer and autumn.

A deciduous tree, to around 6m high, with a branching habit and dark red young bark streaked with silver. Leaves are shallowly lobed, with long tapering tips often curved underneath, emerging pale green flushed with pink in spring, and maturing to green over the summer. Autumn colour is golden yellow

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing small, compact rosettes to 6cm wide, densely packed with small, thick fleshy, yellowish-green leaves, the central leaves flushed dark red in summer. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers may be produced from mature rosettes that die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

primary_name: Sempervivum erythraeum from Mesta Valley, Bulgaria

description: A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes in loose cushions, the spoon-shaped, silvery, pale grey-green leaves, flushed pink in spring, are covered and cobwebbed with silvery white hairs. Tall spikes of starry pale pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets
A cordon cherry tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces plentiful, small, purple/red cherry tomatoes throughout the summer

A clump-forming perennial to 60cm high, forming a mound of lobed and divided green leaves. Large, upward-facing flowers, with rich purple spurs and sepals surrounding bright white inner petals, are held on tall stems above the foliage from late spring to early summer

Short-lived, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall with blue-green, divided foliage forming a basal mound. Large, outward- to upward-facing flowers with pink, mid-length spurs and outer petals, and pale yellow inner petals, are borne on upright stems from early spring into summer

Short-lived, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall with blue-green, divided foliage forming a basal mound. Large, outward- to upward-facing flowers with red, mid-length spurs and outer petals, and white inner petals, are borne on upright stems from early spring into summer

A slowly spreading, mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Mid blue-purple, four-petalled flowers, with yellow-green eyes are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

A slowly-spreading, mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Red-purple and blue-purple, four-petalled flowers are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer
An evergreen, semi-trailing perennial, usually grown as an annual, with small ovate to elliptic dark green leaves and trumpet-shaped dark yellow flowers which appear from summer to early autumn

A tender evergreen perennial usually grown as an annual, with a bushy habit, trailing stems and small, narrow leaves. Trumpet-shaped golden yellow flowers, veined and flushed with red, are produced over a long period in summer and autumn

A small, low-growing perennial that forms neat, compact mounds of small, dark green, toothed round to ovate leaves. Numerous, outward facing, violet blue bell-shaped single flowers are borne on short stalks sitting just above its foliage providing a long flowering display in summer

An upright, spreading, semi-evergreen perennial to around 30cm in height with small, oval, dark green leaves. Reddish-orange flowers with darker centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced flowers which are a blend of reds, oranges and golden yellow with orange centres appear from summer through until the autumn

A tender, mound-forming to semi-trailing perennial, mostly grown as an annual for summer container or bedding displays. It has ovate, sticky and hairy, green to grey-green leaves and, from late spring into autumn, trumpet shaped flowers that are either a rich mauve-purple or magenta-purple colour, with a bold halo of creamy white around the edge of each individual bloom.

A compact, rosette-forming perennial with dark green leaves and large, eye-catching blue and white striped flowers with yellow centres, appearing over a long period from late winter to late spring. An ideal variety for either borders or in pots and containers

A tuberous perennial, to about 45cm tall, with strap-shaped green, veined upright leaves clasping the reddish-brown stems. Terracotta-red orchid or iris-like flowers are produced over a long flowering period in loose clusters from July to October

A semi-evergreen, borderline-hardy tree to 15m tall with elliptic to oblong leaves up to 16cm long. Clusters of 6-8 white flowers in racemes up to 7cm long open in spring and are followed by brown, cylindrical, woody, ribbed fruits to 8cm long

primary_name: Sorbus commixta from Ulleungdo, South Korea

description: A small, evergreen tree to 8m tall with greyish-white bark, purplish-brown branchlets and leathery, oblong to elliptic leaves up to 11cm long that are dark green and shiny on the upper surfaces with pale green undersides. Small, white to pale yellow flowers borne in late spring to early summer are followed by rounded, leathery fruits up to 2cm in diameter
An erect, clumping perennial to around 70cm tall with oval to oblong or lance-shaped leaves and, from early summer into autumn, spikes of nodding, bell-shaped, violet-blue flowers
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 60cm in height, with hairy, dark green, pinnate basal leaves with semi-double flower; each a combination of pale pink, apricot and cream

Clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing rounded, glossy, lobed and heavily ruffled dark red to black leaves and slender, upright stems bearing panicles of small, bell-shaped, pink flowers from mid-spring into summer.

A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial with mid to dark green heart-shaped leaves with irregular creamy-white margins. Lavender purple fragrant flowers appear on stems above the foliage in the summer
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with thick, smooth, rounded gold foliage. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with round, thick, solid golden yellow foliage. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer. One of the larger varieties of 'Mouse' hostas

A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with very thick, variegated yellow foliage and green streaks over the entire leaf area. Upright, yellow stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer. A more compact sport of H. 'Silver Threads and Golden Needles'
A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with blue-green foliage with wavy margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer. A sport of 'Blue Mouse Ears'
A miniature, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, tapered green foliage and wavy edges. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A woody-based herbaceous perennial up to 60cm high with evergreen, aromatic, ovate, mid-green leaves and dark pink flowers from summer to autumn

A semi-evergreen perennial forming a low mound (up to 25cm) of wiry stems bearing bright green leaves. Plants are covered with white daisy-like, yellow-centred flowers in summer. The white petals age to pinkish-purple, giving the plant a two-tone effect. Blooms begin in spring (starting as early as late April or May) and will continue until late autumn. Similar to the parent species, Erigeron karvinskinanus, but is typically slightly taller. In cold areas and frosty winters, the foliage is killed, but plants will regrow from a shoots at the base of the plant in spring.

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 40cm high. Leaves are ovate, slightly twisted at the tips, and matt dark green, with a pale green central streak surrounded by narrow flashes of white. Produces loose clusters of tubular pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A shrub about 40-50cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant purple flowers in early summer
A deciduous, rhizomatous, mound-forming perennial with large, heart-shaped, silver leaves that are veined and edged with green. Airy sprays of blue, forget-me-not-like flowers appear in spring
A clump-forming perennial to 70cm tall with hairy, toothed leaves and flowerheads with pale yellow, rolled-up, spoon-shaped ray florets surrounding a deep yellow cone
A dwarf, spreading, evergreen shrub, to about 60cm tall, with small, yellow leaves in spring turning lime green in summer. Small, tubular, red flowers are produced for most of the summer

A clump-forming perennial to around 30cm high, with deeply lobed, wrinkled green leaves with toothed edges. Semi-double pale yellow flowers, fading to cream at the edges, are borne on slender stems above the foliage, in flushes from late spring to late summer
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height, forms clumps of arching strap-shaped leaves and dark purple-black flowers with a green throat to 14cm across in summer.

An evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 30cm high and spread of 40cm, forming a mound of glossy frilly black cherry coloured leaves, with a sliver frosting. A strong-growing plant which produces pale pink flowers fromsSpring until autumn, great for a sunny location
A compact mound forming perennial, with bright yellow, lime-green leaves which are scorch resistant. Panicles of small white flowers
A neat, clump-forming semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial producing large dark plum-purple foliage. Creamy flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer

Bushy upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennials to 60cm with lance-shaped somewhat toothed dark green hairy leaves. Numerous large flowers often darker towards the base around a brown central cone in shades of yellow, orange and coppery browns produced in summer. This series incorporates the appearance of a rudbeckia and the hardiness of an echinacea, flowering over a long period from summer into autumn

A compact, vigorous deciduous small tree or large shrub with an upright habit and oval-shaped, dark-green foliage turning red-purple in the autumn. large, white flowers appear early to mid-summer, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn. One of the more disease-resistant varieties

An evergreen conifer with luminous, lime-green young foliage that contrasts with dark green colour of older growth. Needles are fairly thin, 1.5-3cm long with two greyish lines underside. It is a medium-sized conifer with approximate growth rate of 30cm per year. 10 year specimen can reach height of 3 metres and width of 1.5m. Crown is narrowly conical, broadening with age.
An evergreen perennial producing a mat of small, grey-green leaves. Masses of pinky-purple flowers appear in mid to late spring

An upright, small, deciduous shrubby tree about 2m in height, a sister seedling of 'Sunglow'. Shallow, 7-9 lobed leaves to 13cm long emerge in spring in shades of apricot which slowly change to light green in summer then bright yellow to orange in autumn. Pendent clusters of wine-red and white early spring flowers are followed by brown winged fruits in late summer
A compact, semi-evergreen perennial forming a low mound of finely-divided, deep green foliage topped in summer with flattened flowerheads made up of small, cream flowers

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 90cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and an abundance of rounded heads of tubular, intense blue flowers on strong stems from mid-summer to autumn

An upright, compact, rhizomatous perennial with palmate toothed dark green leaves and numerous long, erect, branching flower stems bearing a profusion of single rose-pink petalled flowers with yellow centres from mid to late summer.

A compact, erect, rhizomatous perennial with toothed, palmate dark green leaves and erect robust branching stems bearing an abundance of slightly cupped, double rose-pink, sinuate flowers with sinuate margined, slightly frilled petals and golden central boss of stamens from midsummer into autumn, followed by cotton white seed heads providing interest in autumn and winter.

primary_name: Anemone × hybrida [Pretty Lady Maria] ('Aneplaria') (Pretty Lady Series)
description: Compact clump-forming perennial to about 60cm tall, with mid green 3-lobed leaves, and bearing a profusion of single white flowers to 6cm across, with a central boss of yellow stamens, produced from late summer to autumn

An evergreen, frost-tender sub-shrub, often grown as an annual, forming a compact mound of finely-divided, grey-green foliage to around 50cm tall. A mass of single flowers, white with a yellow centre, are borne above the foliage from early summer until the first frosts
A mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Dark red-purple, four-petalled flowers are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

alternative_names: aubrieta [Axcent Light Blue]|Aubrieta [Axcent Glacier Light Blue] (Axcent Series)|Aubrieta 'Abrz0002'
description: A compact, mat-forming, evergreen perennial up to 15cm tall with small, ovate to oblong, grey-green leaves. The mounded foliage is covered from late spring to early summer with pale to mid-blue flowers, each with a tiny yellow eye

A vigorous, early-flowering upright, evergreen hybrid (C. sasanqua × C. reticulata) with an open, spreading habit. Large, semi-double blooms in luminous deep rose-pink, accented by flared golden stamens, appear from December to February, adding vibrant winter colour. Ideal for ornamental use in mild climates

An upright evergreen shrub, with glossy dark green, elliptic leaves with finely serrated edges. Small, anemone-form flowers to 4cm across, with rounded, hot pink outer petals and a mass of pink and white petaloids in the centre, are produced in mid to late spring

A large evergreen shrub with small, elliptic dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces semi-double, deep pink flowers to 12cm across, sometimes splashed with white, in late autumn and winter

A dense, spreading, slow-growing evergreen shrub with dark green, glossy leaves. Tight rose-like buds open to masses of single white flowers, the petals alternately flushed pale pink, and appear from winter to early spring
Dense, tufted, evergreen perennial sedge, about 30cm tall, with cascading mounds of dark green leaves. Carries brown flower spikes on stems to 15cm long, within the foliage, in mid and late spring
an evergreen tree
an open-branched deciduous medium shrub with blue flowers and autumn colour.

An evergreen dwarf conifer with horizontal spreading branches, giving a mounded, broad form. Its flattened sprays of foliage appear yellow-bronze in spring, turning green in summer and coppery-orange in winter.
A cultivar to 1.2m tall with glossy dark purple foliage. It has single, warm yellow flowers with a central darker yellow-orange ring, and faint orange and purple veining on the reverse
A green-leaved cultivar to around 1.2m tall. It bears flowerheads, typically just over 6cm wide, that are peachy-bronze suffused with lemon in summer and early autumn
A green-leaved cultivar that reaches a height ofaround 1.2m. Flowers with magenta-rose petals shading to yellow near the base are borne from summer into autumn

A compact deciduous climber, to around 1.5m high, with deeply veined green leaves. Large pink flowers to 10cm across are produced in late spring and early summer, with broad, overlapping petals and red-tipped anthers

A compact, deciduous climber, to about 1.2m tall, flowering from late spring to early autumn. The single flowers, up to 15cm in width, are purple with red-purple central stripes and purple and white stamens
A climber up to 1.5 m high with many flowers, 10-12cm across, of 6-8 pink tepals with darker pink central bars and brown anthers from early to late summer and early autumn
A deciduous climber to around 1.5m tall bearing in summer pink flowers with deeper pink central bars and brown anthers; each flower up to 12cm in diameter

An upright, deciduous shrub to 2.5m tall developing flaking bark with age. Oval, toothed, dark green leaves turn shades of red and yellow in autumn. Long racemes of fragrant white flowers are borne from late summer into early autumn

A non-branching, columnar tree about 2.5m tall and 50cm wide, producing flowers and fruit from short shoots all along the main trunk. Dull, bluish-purple and green apples have crisp, juicy, sweet-sharp flesh, cropping in late summer and storing for a few weeks. A self-fertile cultivar, but will crop better with a pollination partner

A non-branching, columnar tree about 2.5m tall and 50cm wide, producing flowers and fruit from short shoots all along the main trunk. Bright yellow-orange apples have crisp, quite sharp flesh, cropping in early autumn and storing for a few weeks. A self-fertile cultivar, but will crop better with a pollination partner

A non-branching, columnar tree about 2.5m tall and 50cm wide, producing flowers and fruit from short shoots all along the main trunk. Greenish-yellow apples have a mild flavour, cropping in early autumn and storing for a few weeks. A self-fertile cultivar, but will crop better with a pollination partner

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to around 80cm high, with strong stems and divided green leaves. In early summer produces large, semi-double, lightly scented flowers, with rich cream coloured petals flecked with raspberry pink

An intersectional or Itoh peony and upright and compact herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage green in summer, tinged bronzy-red in spring and autumn. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped creamy, pale apricot-orange flowers with a centre of yellow stamens appear in late spring and early summer, with a particularly long flowering period.

A non-branching, columnar tree about 2m tall and 50cm wide, producing flowers and fruit from short shoots all along the main trunk. Large, green apples have firm, crisp, slightly acid flesh, cropping in early autumn and storing for a few weeks. A self-fertile cultivar, but will crop better with a pollination partner

A vigorous evergreen conifer, to around 5m high in 10 years, with fibrous, red-brown bark and fine, linear leaves arranged in spirals around the stems. Leaves are bright yellow-green in spring and summer, turning gold in late autumn and winter
A short, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with shorter stalks formed with divided green leaves and spikes packed with deep purple flowers with a blue-black bee in summer.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with deep light-blue flowers and a white centre or 'bee' in summer.

primary_name: Delphinium 'Magic Fountains Blue/White Bee' (Magic Fountains Series)
description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with blue flowers with a white centre which appear in the summer

primary_name: Delphinium 'Magic Fountains Deep Rose/White Bee' (Magic Fountains Series)
description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with rose-pink flowers and a white bee in summer.

An evergreen shrub or tree to 4m tall, with stout shoots bearing large, strongly veined, glossy leaves to 30cm long. It produces clusters of small white flowers in late winter but is unlikely to bear edible fruit (loquats) in cool climates
An upright, mound-forming tender evergreen sometimes grown as an annual with aromatic silver-grey leaves. Clusters of dense yellow flower heads are produced in summer

An early flowering, semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with leathery, pewter-green foliage and branched stems with cup-shaped, creamy -pink single flowers turning a darker tone of pink as they mature in late winter and early spring
An evergreen succulent, forming a rounded rosette to 60cm across, with narrowly linear, rigid yellow-green leaves strongly flushed with red

A semi-evergreen clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, mid-green foliage and branched stems bearing cup-shaped, near black, very dark purple flowers with yellow stamens, in late winter and early spring

alternative_names: hellebore [HGC Marlon Cream]|Winter's song hybrid Christmas rose [HGC Marlon Cream]|Helleborus × ericsmithii 'Coseh 980'
description: An early flowering, semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with leathery, dark green foliage and branched stems bearing forward-facing, cup-shaped, cream single flowers turning soft green and purplish as they mature from early winter into spring

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 45cm high, with ovate, mid green leaves that brighten to yellow-green, with a narrow cream margin. Produces loose clusters of pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer

An upright to spreading deciduous shrub to around 2m high, with ovate, lightly toothed leaves that are deep red when young, maturing to greenish purple with deep purple undersides. Produces large, slightly domed flower heads in late summer, with small, purple-pink flowers in the centre and larger pale pink sterile florets around the outside
A deciduous shrub to 1.2m high with broadly oval, toothed dark green leaves. Dome-shaped clusters of double flowers, with pure white petals that are pointed at the tips, are produced in summer

A vigorous deciduous shrub to 1.2m high with broadly oval, serrated green leaves. Compact, dome-shaped clusters of flowers, with clearly separated, diamond shaped petals, are produced in summer. Flower colours vary depending on the pH of the soil, from pale rose pink to lavender and pale blue
A reasonably compact, deciduous shrub with a bushy habit and large blooms emerging in summer, starting green then turning pink to red as it matures

A large, deciduous, woody climber about 6m in height, with pale yellow-green ferny leaves composed of 7-9 leaflets. Very fragrant, white flowers sometimes flushed pale pink are 2cm in width open in terminal clusters of 3 to 10 in summer and early autumn
An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 60cm in height when in flower with green, linear grass-like leaves and spikes of tubular, orange and brick-red flowers that in summer and autumn.

alternative_names: crape myrtle [Rhapsody in Pink]|Lagerstroemia indica 'Whit VIII'
description: An upright, deciduous shrub or small, multi-stemmed tree to 3m tall, with peeling, grey and brown bark and glossy, dark green leaves, purple-flushed when young. In late summer, if the weather has been hot, it produces pink flowers with crinkled petals, held in conical clusters to 20cm long. Grown against a sunny, sheltered wall and protected from frost when young it will make a stunning specimen plant in mild districts
a robust evergreen shrub to 55m tall by 70cm wide. It has linear, grey-green leaves and violet-blue flowers in summer
An evergreen shrub with grey-green aromatic foliage growing to about 50cm tall and 70cm wide. The strongly-scented, purple flowers appear in mid- to late summer
Bushy evergreen shrub about 1.5m tall, with red stems covered in green, flushed red leaves and flowerheads surrounded by yellow and flame-red floral bracts, produced from late spring to late autumn

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Single pale yellow flowers with darker yellow centres, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly.

A bulbous perennial, to around 1.1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped green leaves. This martagon hybrid produces lightly fragrant, hanging flowers, with spreading pale pink petals with white edges and dark purple spots, in early to mid summer

A compact, deciduous, woody-stemmed, twining climber to about 3m in height, with rich, dark green oval to rounded leaves. Fragrant, long, tubular, 2-lipped flowers in shades of apricot-pink appear in whorled clusters at the end of the stems, opening from dark pink buds from midsummer to early autumn. These may be followed by red berries

An annual poppy to 90cm high, with deeply toothed, pale blue-green leaves. In early summer, produces densely double, dark reddish purple flowers on tall leafy stems, followed by large, blue-green seed pods
An annual poppy, to 90cm high, with deeply toothed, pale blue-green leaves. In early summer, produces densely double, dark purple flowers on tall leafy stems, followed by large, blue-green seed pods

A rich evergreen shrub with bright red coppery foliage in early spring maturing to a glossy leathery green. The young bright red foliage will remain well into early summer, longer than other varieties. Ideal for general garden planting or hedging, low maintenance and easy to cultivate. Panicles of creamy-white spring flowers may be followed by red fruits. Approximate mature height of around 2 metres and a spread of 1.5 - 2 metres

A dwarf, slow-growing, evergreen conifer, which produces a compact, flattened, globe to dome-shaped bush, reaching about 75cm (30in) high and 1.5m (5ft) across. It has a neat, densely branching habit. The thin, needles are produced in bunches of five at the tips of the stems and are around 6-8cm (2½-5½in) long. They are soft to the touch and are a silvery blue-green throughout the year. It can produce cylindrical brown cones,10-20cm long. Its small size, means it is an excellent choice for a small, city or courtyard garden, where an architectural, or evergreen focal point is needed, as well as for container growing, or for inclusion in the rockery
A bushy, evergreen shrub to 1.5m tall, with leathery leaves. In summer it bears solitary, ruby red flowerheads with white hairs at the tips
A compact evergreen shrub to 1.5m, with grey-green leaves. In summer it bears flowerheads with cream-coloured, pink-flushed bracts

A compact, slow-growing small tree or shrub, reaching a height of around 1.5m, with a rounded crown which eventually becomes irregular in shape. Fan-shaped pale green leaves turn to golden yellow in the autumn.

Bulbous perennial producing short-lived, strap-shaped mid-green leaves, dying back at flowering time, and large, densely-packed spherical heads of purple-pink star-shaped flowers on straight stems to 75cm tall in late spring and early summer
An upright, evergreen shrub to 2m, with glossy, purple-flushed, toothed leaves divided into 3-5 slender, leathery leaflets

Bulbous perennial producing short-lived, strap-shaped mid-green leaves and large, densely-packed spherical heads of purple-pink, star-shaped flowers on straight stems to 75cm tall in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Phoenix loureiroi var. pedunculata from Kashmir

description: Bulbous herbaceous perennial to 1.4m, bearing dense, globose umbels of pink flowers in summer.

Bulbous perennial about 40cm or more tall, with lance-shaped, grey-green basal leaves to 50cm long. Open, cup-shaped pale lilac-pink flowers, with a central greenish-black ovary, form rounded clusters with a flattened top, up to 7cm across, in early summer

Hybrid group of perennial, bulbous plants, producing densely-packed spherical heads of star-shaped flowers, in shades of pink, purple or white, on straight stems to 70cm tall in May and June, above short-lived, mid-green leaves. The foliage is often wilting and turning brown when the flowers appear, and for best visual effect, the bulbs should be sited so that adjacent plants can grow to conceal the leaves as they die back. The flowers are extremely attractive to bees and other pollinating insects, making the plant a wonderful addition to a wildlife garden.
A bulbous perennial with strap-shaped leaves and umbels of densely packed pink and white flowers with dark red eyes, borne on stems about 60cm tall in late spring and early summer
A bushy shrub to 90cm tall with glossy, mid-green leaves, and abundant, velvety, crimson-red, very fragrant flowers, to 12cm across, borne repeatedly through summer and autumn

Bulbous perennial to around 70cm high with strap-shaped leaves. Large rounded flowerheads comprising irridescent purple, star-shaped flowers to 15cm across, with a silvery, metallic sheen are borne in late spring to early summer
Compact bulbous perennial to 50cm tall with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and rounded umbels of star-shaped, violet-purple flowers from late spring to early summer

A tall, clump-forming herbaceous perennial, up to 1.8m high, with hairy stems and broadly lance-shaped, hairy green leaves. Produces large, daisy-like flowerheads, with a prominent grey-green central cone that turns brown as the flowers mature, and drooping yellow petals. Flowers are held singly on tall stems from mid to late summer

Tall, bulbous perennial to about 1.2m with greyish-green, strap-shaped leaves that die back as the flowers open. Rich purple, star-shaped flowers are carried in dense, spherical heads in late spring and early summer
Bulbous perennial producing narrow strap-shaped, mid-green leaves, and densely packed spherical heads of purple-pink flowers on straight stems to 40cm tall, in late spring and early summer
A large, bulbous perennial with strap-shaped, grey-green leaves. Globe-shaped clusters of starry purple-violet flowers, around 10-15cm across, appear in summer
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy sub-shrub with aromatic green foliage and lavender-blue lipped flowers held on dark purple calyces from summer through to autumn.
Deciduous, bulbous perennial producing strap-shaped mid-green leaves and densely packed, spherical heads of purple-pink flowers on straight stems to 1.25m tall in mid and late summer
Bulbous perennial producing strap-shaped mid-green leaves and densely packed, spherical heads of pale pink flowers on straight stems to 1.2m tall in mid and late summer
Deciduous, bulbous perennial producing strap-shaped mid-green leaves and densely packed, spherical heads of deep purple-pink flowers on straight stems to 1.2m tall in mid and late summer

Bulbous perennial, producing strap-shaped mid-green leaves and densely packed, spherical heads of white flowers on straight stems to 1m tall, in mid and late summer. The flowers are followed by large ornamental greenish seed-heads that age to brown
Bulbous perennial to 20cm tall with strap-shaped leaves and upright stems bearing rounded heads of pale purple star-shaped flowers in spring

A compact evergreen shrub to 80cm high, with elliptic, leathery green leaves that are aromatic when crushed. Clusters of fragrant small white flowers open from deep red buds in spring, and if pollinated, these are followed by bright red berries in autumn that persist well into winter
Bulbous perennial producing strap-shaped green leaves and spherical heads of densely-packed white flowers on straight stems to 1m tall, in mid to late summer

A deciduous tree, to around 6m in 20 years, with an upright to spreading habit, and slightly blue-green leaves divided into pairs of toothed leaflets. Leaves turn shades of red and bronze in autumn. Clusters of creamy white spring flowers are followed by orange berries that persist into the winter months

A compact, spreading tree to 6m tall with leaves divided into glossy green leaflet that may turn shades of purple, red and yellow before falling in autumn. Clusters of creamy-white flowers in spring are followed by drooping clusters of fruit that start red before turning pink
Clump-forming bulbous perennial with strap-shaped, green leaves; in spring, upright stems bear small, star-shaped, deep purple flowers packed into a half-sphere shape
