A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and bright red flowers with a chartreuse throat to 13cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for more than 16 hours a day

An evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 109cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves, and unusual, dark maroon coloured flowers with a purple-black eye-zone to 18cm across in summer

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and pale salmon-pink coloured flowers to 13cm across in summer. The flowers remain open for longer than 16 hours

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 64cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and pale, mauve-pink flowers that have a lavender-pink coloured edge and eye-zone above a yellow-green throat to 15cm across in summer.

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 56cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like, green leaves and peachy-pink coloured flowers with a green throat to 6cm across in summer.

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 86cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and lavender-purple flowers with a purple eyezone and picotee edge to around 18cm across above a green throat in summer

An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Very pale orange flowers, with a darker ruffled edge petals and yellow-green throats appear early in the season

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 102cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and fragrant yellow flowers above a green throat to 20cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and red flowers with an ivory-white edge and chartreuse throat to 16cm across in summer. Flowers appear in the evening and bloom through the night

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 61cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and pale pink, cream and gold flowers with a gold-green throat to 15cm across in summer

A semi-evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 89cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and fuchsia red-purple flowers, with a purple eyezone and a chartreuse throat to 18cm across in summer
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are bright yellow-gold with a pale green throat
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial. A shorter Hemerocallis with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are yellow with a red centre, ruffled edge and a green throat

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of pale purple to lilac flowers, cream towards the centre of the flower with a green-yellow throat and slightly reflexed petals

A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching green leaves and sturdy stems of large, coral-pink flowers with reddish markings towards a yellow green throat and reflexed petals

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped arching, mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of showy fragrant yellow flowers with long, reflexed petals, a white mid rib down the centre of each petal and a green throat
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Flowers are copper orange with a large yellow throat

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and pale yellow flowers with a red-purple middle and a green yellow eye. Petals are slightly ruffled along the edge and flowers are reflexed
A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to 70cm tall with narrow, arching leaves. Fragrant deep red to purple flowers with black veins and yellow-green throats are freely produced in summer

Tuberous-rooted, clump-forming perennial about 1-1.2m tall, with dark green foliage. Fully double flowers to 25cm wide, produced from midsummer until the first frost, are bi-coloured purple with white-tipped slightly incurved petals, creating a neat shape

A fast-growing, bush annual with green foliage to around 50cm in height. Peach-yellow snapdragon flowers appear from mid April until early summer. Great for filling in gaps between hardy perennials in a flower border

An herbaceous perennial grown as an annual to 25cm, flowering in its first year from seed. It has whorls of fine, narrow, grey-green leaves topped from late spring to mid-summer with shorts spikes of small, snapdragon-like purple flowers with dark red throats. With a slightly trailing habit, it is ideal for pots and containers
An erect, branching annual to 50cm high with narrowly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves, and in summer loose clusters of small, rounded white flowers with dark red centres
A deciduous climber to about 2m with yellow-green leaves and nodding, semi-double, bell-shaped flowers with narrow, pale purplish-pink petals in spring
A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial to 60cm tall and wide with deeply divided dark green leaves. Bowl-shaped white flowers spotted with deep red are borne from late winter into early spring

A compact, bushy, herbaceous perennial, to 50cm tall, with lance-shaped, toothed leaves. From late summer to autumn, masses of flowers are borne on sturdy stems and comprise yellow, orange and red ray florets surrounding a brown central disc

A compact, herbaceous perennial to 50cm tall with green, lance-shaped, toothed leaves. Flowers with red to dark orange ray florets and a yellow-brown disc are borne freely on sturdy stems from late summer to autumn

A clump-forming perennial, to around 80cm high, with dark purple, branching stems and aromatic, narrow dull green leaves. Rounded flowerheads of tubular, pale lilac pink flowers are produced from mid to late summer

A clump-forming, compact, bushy deciduous herbaceous perennial with aromatic silvery grey-green foliage and upright spikes of purple-blue flowers from summer through to autumn. Cats are attracted to this plant

A cultivar with a columnar habit forming a relatively compact tree with minimal branching and fruit developing on spurs off the main stem. The mid-season, medium-sized apples are flat to rounded in shape with a smooth green skin that matures to yellow with a faded orange blush on the sun-exposed side

A dessert apple cultivar grown for its natural columnar habit and mid-season fruits. The medium-sized apples have greenish-yellow skins flushed red on sun-exposed surfaces and sweet, juicy, crisp flesh with low acidity. Fruits store well for up to eight weeks

A tree with a compact, columnar habit that is notable for the side shoots it produces that grow only a short distance away from the main stem before turning sharply vertical. Small to medium sized fruits have a yellowish base colour that is flushed bright red on the sun-exposed surface and sweet-sharp, jucy and crisp flesh

A large, late cooking apple with mid-green skin, sometimes flushed with brownish-red, and sharp-tasting, greenish-white, flesh that cooks to a well-flavoured, cream-coloured puree. This triploid, part tip-bearing cultivar is 20 percent less vigorous than ‘Bramley Seedling’ but is still vigorous, cropping in mid-autumn with fruit storing to early spring. Requires a group 2, 3 or 4 pollinator
A conifer slowly reaching a narrow 2.5m cone. It has strong, grey-green scale leaves flecked with cream throughout
A bushy perennial with toothed, mid-green leaves. Very pale lilac flowers, deeper round the edges and with a red-spotted yellow throat, are produced in summer and autumn

A rhizomatous perennial to 50cm, with sharply divided, dark red, almost black leaves with pale green veining at the centres. Produces sprays of small, pale pink flowers, speckled with darker pink, on upright, reddish green stems in spring

A tender perennial to around 30cm tall with hairy, wrinkled, strap-shaped leaves. Clusters of pink flowers to 5cm across are borne from spring into autumn; flower lobes are streaked and speckled with pink over a paler pink to white background

An evergreen tree to 10m tall, with a wide spreading crown and rough, furrowed bark. The large, 2-pinnate leaves are composed of opposite pairs of finely toothed, oval leaflets. Golden yellow flowers are borne in pyramidal clusters to 30cm long in late summer; these are followed by unusual, inflated, pink-flushed fruit capsules. Not hardy in the British Isles
A deciduous climber, up to 4m high, with divided dark green leaves. Small flowers to 6cm across are produced in mid summer, with pale pink petals with darker pink veins, wavy edges and recurved tips
A deciduous climber, to around 2.5m high, with divided green leaves. Large, star-shaped white flowers to 12cm across, with textured petals and recurved tips, are produced in mid to late summer
A rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial, up to 90cm high in flower, with glaucous, sword-shaped leaves and scented, bright yellow flowers with a touch of green on the fall petals, in May.

An attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial bred by Sir Cedric Morris and named after one of his cats. It has upright, strap-like, grey-green leaves and erect stems bearing large, fragrant, bright purple, red-pink flowers with yellow beards

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial with tall, upright, strap-like grey-green leaves and erect stems bearing elegant marmalade flowers in late spring-early summer with orange-yellow upper petals, known as standards, and yellow-flushed cream-orange lower petals, known as falls with orange beards

An evergreen or semi-evergreen, rhizomatous perennial, forming a clump of glossy, arrow-shaped leaves to 45cm long. From late spring to midsummer it freely produces a succession of exotic-looking flowers to 15cm long, composed of white spathes around a yellow spadix; these are borne on stout stems above the foliage. Suitable for constantly moist soil, a bog garden, or pond margin

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 102cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, pale yellow flowers with a green throat to 20cm across in summer

A mid-season, sweet cherry producing white spring blossom, then a good crop of medium to large fruit with black skins and soft, juicy, very dark red flesh with a fair flavour and good resistance to splitting. It is self-sterile and requires a compatible pollination partner

A tender and evergreen perennial, scented-leaved pelargonium with small, lemon-scented, green leaves with a golden crisped edge. Has single mauve flowers from spring to autumn, with mauve and dark purple feathering on upper petals and narrower pale pink lower petals.
An upright, herbaceous perennial with lance-shaped dark green foliage. Clusters of single, fragrant, lavender-mauve flowers with purple centres appear on upright stems from June through to August

A vigorous, spreading perennial herb with small, aromatic, mid-green leaves that have a scent reminiscent of strawberries and clusters of small, pale purple flowers that appear in summer. Perfect as a garnish for desserts

A very large, hardy variety of ornamental rhubarb, reaching a height of around 3m, forming clumps of large, spikey-edged green leaves on tall, thick stems. Clusters of red flowers appear in late spring to summer. Copes well in shade as long as it is planted in soil which doesn't dry out, and can be grown next to a pond or stream
Compact climbing rose about 2.4m tall, with dark green foliage, and abundant, intensely perfumed, fully double, deep pink blooms, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn
A semi-evergreen, upright, tall and bushy perennial with a running rootstock which has green foliage and loose, slender spikes of deep-blue flowers in late summer and autumn.
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy shrub with dark green foliage and vibrant pink lipped flowers which have a near black calyx from summer through to autumn.

A compact, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen herbaceous perennial producing silvery foliage with black veining and pale purple undersides. Masses of fuchsia-pink flowers appear on long stems above the foliage throughout the spring and summer
A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub, up to 1.2m tall with lance-shaped, green leaves. The panicles of scented, deep pink flowers are produced in abundance from summer through to autumn.

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial bearing lobed, coppery leaves, marked dark bronze in the centre. Slender stems bear panicles of tiny, bell-shaped, white flowers from late spring into summer.

A clump-forming, semi-trailing evergreen herbaceous perennial with deeply lobed, soft blue-green leaves, frosted with silver and darker red veins. Slender stems bear open panicles of tiny, bell-shaped, white flowers from late spring into summer. Ideal for ground cover or for cascading over pots and containers

Tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m tall, with mid-green serrated leaves. Large, fully double flowers 15cm across, produced from midsummer until the first autumn frosts, have narrow, quilled, pale apricot petals flushed lemon-yellow in the cente, with long, divided tips giving a fringed effect

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 25cm high, with lobed leaves in shades of pale pink and orange with a silvery overlay. Slender stems bear clusters of tiny, bell-shaped white flowers from late spring into summer
A hardy, evergreen shrub with an erect, bushy habit with green foliage and white flowers in summer through to autumn.

A compact, evergreen shrub to 40cm tall with stiffly upright stems bearing small, lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Flowers are deep magenta, urn-shaped and pendent, and produced from early summer into autumn
A compact, dwarf, evergreen shrub to about 20cm with needle-like, dark green foliage. Spikes of tiny, vivid sugar-pink flowers appear from late winter to mid-spring

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. White, semi-double flowers surrounded by greenish bracts and with greenish-yellow stamens, appear in the spring

A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high with hairy, lobed and toothed, semi-evergreen foliage. Slender stems bear double flowers with ruffled yellow petals suffused with orange from late spring into summer
A compact, neat, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green leaves and slim spikes of dark red flowers which appear from summer through to autumn. Similar to 'Tanna' but taller

An upright, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 120cm in height, with dark green leaves and slim, dark-coloured stems which produce spikes of white flowers, with a flush of strawberry-pink, which appear from summer through to autumn

A dense, compact, clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial species producing bright green, multi-lobed foliage with hairy edges. Cream and pale pink flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer. A good option for planting under trees

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, with a trailing habit and masses of small, shallowly lobed yellow-green leaves with red veining and scalloped edges. Slender stems bear clusters of tiny, bell-shaped pale pink flowers from late spring into summer

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, double saucer-shaped pale pink flowers, turning a darker shade of pink towards the centre, appear in late spring and early summer

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, saucer-shaped dark red flowers which have a small centre of prominent yellow stamens appear in late spring and early summer

An upright and bushy herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, semi-double saucer-shaped soft lemony-yellow flowers and golden stamens appear in late spring.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen dwarf shrub to a height of around 1m, with variegated foliage which turns from green in the spring and summer to yellows, oranges and reds in the autumn and winter. Single, delicate star-shaped pink and white fragrant flowers appear in the summer

alternative_names: long-leaved bear's breech 'White Lips'|Hungarian bear’s breech 'White Lips’
description: A clump-forming perennial, to 70cm high in flower, with long, deeply cut basal leaves. Tall, spiny spikes of white flowers with purple hoods are produced from early to late summer

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with dark bronze to purple-black dissected foliage. Tall, bronze, slender stems of pendant, sweetly fragranced, white, bottle-brush like flowers appear in late summer, followed by black berries

A compact and bushy, upright herbaceous perennial with aromatic, dark green lance-shaped leaves on dark purple stems and slender whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped lavender-rose pink flowers which are very attractive to pollinators all through summer to autumn. Has a particularly long flowering period

Clump-forming, tuberous perennial about 30cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves. From midsummer to autumn it bears clusters of bright red, funnel-shaped flowers, blotched yellow in the throat, with dark crimson speckles and streaks on inner petals

A compact, clump-forming deciduous woodland herbaceous perennial. Leaves are green and divided into 3 'fingers'. Single, pale pink flowers, becoming darker with age, and with yellow stamens appear in the spring

A handsome herbaceous perennial grown for its lush foliage. It has pairs of light green leaves which are atttractively veined and have crisply serrated margins and pointed tips. In midsummer, strings of long pale flowers develop looking like pipecleaners.
A compact, low-growing mound-forming evergreen clematis with glossy dark green leaves and masses of creamy-white flowers with separated petals, tinged with green appearing from March to April

Tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m tall, with dark stems and dark green leaves. Very large flowers, 22-25cm across, produced from midsummer until the first frost, are very dark red, almost black, with a velvety sheen to the long, pointed petals, rolled under at the edges, creating a spiky effect

A clump-forming biennial or short-lived perennial, to 1m high in flower, with soft, silvery leaves irregularly toothed at the edges. Loose spikes of pale creamy yellow buds open to white flowers in late spring and early summer

A semi-evergreen biennial or short-lived perennial, to 1.2m high in flower, with a basal rosette of hairy green leaves. Tall spikes of tubular pendent flowers, in warm shades of peach and orange-pink, are produced in late spring and early summer

A succulent, evergreen sub-shrub forming a compact mound of closely-packed leaf rosettes. The leaves are are green at the centre of the rosette, darkening to deep purple-red on the outer whorls. Domed clusters of small, starry yellow flowers are sometimes produced in summer. A good patio plant, but is best moved under glass where winters are not reliably mild

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing showy, double flowers with a central pompom fading from green to yellow surrounded by slightly drooping, toothed, pale yellow ray petals. Excellent as a cut flower

An upright, compact, clump-forming perennial to 50cm tall with toothed, dark green leaves. Fragrant, double flowers to 7.5cm in diameter are borne on sturdy, branched stems from summer into autumn and comprise a dark pink, pompom-like central cone surrounded by pale pink ray florets

A highly unusual, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing unique, bi-color blooms with a large, reddish-brown central cone surrounded by narrow, recurved, purple ray petals brushed green at the ends. Excellent as an interesting feature in any border and as a cut flower

A luminous, perennial coneflower variety named after the Cleopatra Butterfly, producing large, fragrant, vibrant golden-yellow flowers with a prominent central orange cone. The flowers turn to a creamy yellow as they mature. It will bloom prolifically between June and September. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing creamy-white blooms with a pale yellow pompom surrounded by narrow, downward arching, recurved ray petals from mid-summmer through to autumn. Excellent planted en masse in the border and as a cut flower

A stunning, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, double, cream-white flowers, up to 15cm wide, with drooping white petals surrounding a prominent creamy pompom. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing bright orange blooms flushed pink with narrow petals surrounding a central dark brown-orange cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, double red blooms with hints of orange. A prominent central pompom is surrounded by drooping rays of lighter red and orange. Slightly scented. Excellent for cutting and attracting pollinators
A spreading perennial to 20cm in height, with divided mid-green leaves, and single pale pink flowers with darker pink veins throughout summer
An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with thick, green leathery leaves marbled with white and pink stems of showy, cup-shaped pink to pale purple flowers with a hint of green

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, green, marbled foliage and branched stems bearing cup-shaped, creamy green single flowers soflty flushed pale purple in late winter and early spring

A compact, deciduous, rounded shrub, semi-evergreen in mild winters, to 1m tall, with ovate dark green leaves and shallow, cup-shaped, rich golden-yellow flowers with prominent central yellow stamens, from early summer into autumn; profuse white fruits follow

An early-flowering, low-growing, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial with aromatic grey-green foliage and upright stems which produce lavender-blue flowers from late spring throughout the summer. An attractive plant to cats

An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall with narrow bluish-green glossy leaves and masses of tubular flowers in long spikes, yellow-tinged in bud then opening to violet-blue flowers becoming reddish-purple with age
An erect herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular white flowers with a lime-green eye over a long period of time in summer.
A dwarf, upright, spreading herbaceous perennial to 40cm tall, with lance-shaped, mid-green leaves and dense, spike-like racemes of tubular, white flowers from midsummer to early autumn
A marginal, aquatic perennial to around 90cm with upright, green spear-shaped leaves, tinged with red, 1-2.5 cm long and bearing bright yellow, cup-shaped flowers, 2cm across in early summer.
A vigorous and bushy, trailing perennial shrub, to 35cm tall. From early summer to autumn it produces slender, pendent single flowers with a red tube and reflexed corolla, and dark pink petals
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with dark, aromatic green foliage and butter-yellow lipped flowers blushed orange from summer through to autumn.
A spreading, clump-forming perennial up to 1.5m high with finely divided leaves and wiry, branching stems bearing bottlebrush-like heads of dark red to purple flowers in summer and early autumn

A rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with grey-green powdery foliage, silvery-grey on the underside. Upright silver stems produce powdery pom-pom clusters of violet-blue purple flowers from late spring to early summer
An upright, bushy evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green foliage and clusters of small, fragrant, star-shaped white flowers in spring, followed by bright red berries

A deciduous shrub to around 2m high, with a compact, bushy habit and ovate, slightly glossy green leaves. Produces loose, conical clusters of fragrant, tubular pale pink flowers from deep pink buds in early summer

A vigorous, evergreen, twining, woody climber about 7-9m tall, with glossy dark green, oval leaves 5-8cm in length, often turning deep red in winter, and profuse clusters of very fragrant, pure white flowers, 2.5cm in width, produced through summer
A vigorous, evergreen perennial forming a rhizomatous clump with glossy, dark green foliage that turns a reddish-brown in winter. Good sized purple-pink flowers are held atop sturdy stems in spring

An unusual, hardy, deciduous rhizomatous perennial to around 40cm in height with variegated, serrated-edge green foliage with pink veining and white to pink midribs and almost orchid-like, peachy-yellow flowers in late summer. It looks great in a jungle or exotic scheme and is ideal for growing in a container too

primary_name: Oxalis obtusa lilac-pink-flowered, from Namaqualand, southern Africa

alternative_names: peony 'Magical Mystery Tour'|Paeonia [Magical Mystery Ride] (Garden Candy Series)
description: A deciduous shrub to around 70cm tall with divided, deep green foliage. Fragrant, semi-double to double blooms open creamy-yellow flushed with pink and with darker pink flares at the base of each petal before aging to creamy-white with a pink, bluish-lavender picotee edging

A bushy perennial, to around 90cm high, with strong stems and divided, dark green leaves. Light pink, single to semi-double flowers, with darker pink flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

A medium-sized deciduous tree with grey bark, brownish-grey on the younger branches and reaching a height of around 8-10m (27-33ft). The foliage in spring emerges red and matures in summer to bright green. In autumn it turns to bright yellow. The yellow-green, male and female catkins are produced separately on the same tree in April. After fertilisation, the female flowers develop into hop-like clusters in late summer to autumn, containing winged seeds that disperse on the wind when ripe

A deciduous shrub to 1.2m high, with ovate, glossy dark green leaves with serrated edges, and dark reddish-brown stems. In summer, broad flat lace-cap flower heads open to clusters of tiny white fertile flowers, surrounded by large, showy white florets with rounded petals

A bushy, deciduous shrub to around 1.5m tall with ovate, serrated foliage that emerges bronze-green in spring before aging to dark green. Rounded flowerheads borne from summer into early autumn comprise white flowers fringed with pink that age to a creamy-white

A compact, clump-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage. Very pale, creamy-yellow flowers with darker yellow centres appear from January through until late spring. Self-seeds freely if left unattended so a good variety for naturalising in grassy areas

A deciduous shrub to 1m high, with ovate, pointed green leaves with serrated edges. In summer, lace-cap flower heads hold clusters of tiny white fertile flowers surrounded by large, showy white florets with lightly feathered edges

primary_name: Hydrangea macrophylla 'La Vie en Rose' (Rendez-vous Series) (H)
description: A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub to around 120cm in height, with coarsley toothed dark green foliage. Pink to white streaked mophead flower heads, appear from June through to September. Flowers may appear more purple-blue on acid soils
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy shrub with dark, aromatic green foliage and pale apricot-peach lipped flowers held on dark calyces from summer through to autumn.

A compact, clump-forming, deciduous to semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial, producing stems to 40cm high and green, aromatic divided foliage, which can turn reddish-bronze in autumn. Clusters of small, intensely pink flowers are produced above the foliage in spring and then sporadically until autumn. Its size and long-flowering season make it a useful subject for growing in pots.

A vigorous, upright, deciduous shrub with dark green ovate leaves on dark red stems. Flowers appear on large dense panicles from late summer, opening creamy white then maturing to pale pink and finally dark pink

alternative_names: panicled hydrangea 'Jane'|Hydrangea paniculata 'Little Lime'|Hydrangea paniculata [Little Lime]
description: A compact, rounded upright deciduous shrub to around 1.5m in height, with ovate, dark-green leaves that turn to yellow in the autumn. Large panicles of lime green flowers fade to cream, developing a pink blush as they mature, appearing from July through to September

primary_name: Molinia caerulea subsp. arundinacea 'Les Ponts de Cé'

description: A clump-forming daffodil, to around 35cm high, with grey-green, strap-shaped leaves. Flowers are scented and upward facing, with slightly swept-back white petals and a long, bright yellow cup
A perennial bulb, to around 65cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are tall and densely double, with light green, fringed petals turning purple at the tips
Compact, clump-forming perennial to 35cm tall with lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Funnel-shaped white flowers marked with purple blotches and dark streaks are borne from summer into early autumn

A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced raspberry-red flowers with orange centres appear from summer through until the autumn

A compact, clump-forming, evergreen herbaceous perennial with strap-like variegated mid green leaves with cream to pale yellow margins. Erect stems bearing umbels of trumpet shaped violet-blue flowers with a darker vein down the centre of each petal appear in the summer

A tender, evergreen shrub to 60cm tall, prized for its brightly coloured summer flowers, which are grouped into densely packed, domed flowerheads. Individual blooms emerge orange, and change to red as they age, with both colours appearing in a single flowerhead. Grow in a temperate greenhouse or as summer bedding

A compact, evergreen shrub to 30cm high, with a spreading habit and upright stems bearing small, lance-shaped, mid green leaves. Flowers are rose pink and double, rounded to urn-shaped, and produced from early summer into autumn

An evergreen shrub to 1.2m high, with an upright to rounded habit and ovate, glossy dark green leaves. Dense clusters of small, fragrant white flowers open from reddish buds in late winter, followed by ovoid blue-black berries

A large tree with a conical habit, up to 10m in height, with glossy dark green leaves with brown, furry undersides. Large, scented, open cup-shaped white flowers are produced from summer through to autumn, even on younger specimens Image credit: Milan havlis © www.havlis.cz

A compact, clump-forming to spreading, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with ovate, spiny-toothed, light green leaflets, flushed red and bronze in spring and flushed red in autumn. In mid-to late spring, slender, wiry stems bear open racemes of maroon to reddish-purple flowers with white-tipped spurs.

primary_name: Dryopteris from Nanjing Botanical Garden, China

description: A bushy, deciduous shrub, up to 4m tall with lance-shaped, green leaves. The short panicles of scented, lilac coloured flowers are produced through the summer. A naturally occuring hybrid between Buddleja alternifolia and Buddleja crispa.

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus Ashwood Garden hybrids, double green-spotted (d)
alternative_names: hellebore Ashwood Garden hybrids, double green-spotted

description: A compact, bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Striking, bright yellow flowers with red edges and curled petals appear on sturdy, upright stems in summer, through until the first frosts of autumn. A good choice for bouquets

An interspecific hybrid resulting from a cross between a Japanese plum and an apricot. The plum parentage is the most dominant. The dark purple rounded fruit has deep red flesh with very sweet intense plum flavour. For warm sheltered sites only. The white, early spring blossom is prone to frost damage and protections is usually needed. Though partly self-fertile it benefits significantly from crosspollination to set good crops. It will pollinate with cherry plums (Prunus ceracifera), early flowering plums and other pluot cultivars. Pollination group 1. Cropping season: August

alternative_names: white fir 'Violacea Prostrate'|Abies concolor Violacea Group prostrate|Abies concolor 'Violacea Prostrata'
description: A low-growing, spreading conifer, reaching 30cm tall in 10 years. Its needles are grey-blue and the large, decorative cones are pale violet ripening to brown

a hardy, garden orchid producing upright stems with large, oval, veined leaves. A clump-forming perennial to 1m with slender, branching stems and small, lance-shaped, mid-green leaves. Produces large, lax, conical sprays of small, white daisies with yellow to dark orange centres, in early to mid-autumn
A tall perennial, to around 1.2m high, with dark near-black stems and narrow, purple-tinted leaves. Branching sprays of pale rosy-violet flowers are produced in autumn
An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 1.5m tall with smooth leaves and purple stems bearing lavender-blue, daisy-like flowers with yellow centres in lte summer and autumn

A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial with horizontal branches of dark green foliage and sturdy stems producing masses of daisy-like white flowers with yellow centres in early autumn, which turn pink once pollinated

A compact, clump-forming perennial with mid-green leaves and clusters of double, bright purple daisy-like flowers with a yellow centre appearing from summer until the autumn.

A seed-raised everbearer, producing small flushes of fruit from late spring to early autumn. The pink flowers are attractive, but the red fruit have poor eating quality

A large-flowered gladiolus, maximum height 115cm high, with dark grey-green sword like leaves. Tall spikes of lilac-mauve flowers with a slightly darker edge appear in August to September

A bulbous perennial, to around 90cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Large, upward-facing, double white flowers with lightly ruffled edges are produced in mid to late summer

A slow-growing, flat-branched, sprawling evergreen conifer to around 3m in height, with bright golden yellow foliage, best in the sun, and red bark. Bright red berries appear in September. A good variety for shaping into a ball

A slow-growing evergreen shrub or tree, to around 3m high, with a columnar, upright habit and needle-like leaves that emerge bright yellow-green, and mature to dark green with pale cream edges. Insignificant flowers in spring are followed, if pollinated, by fleshy red fruits

A compact, bushy succulent subshrub to about 60-90cm in height and width, with glossy, spade-shaped fleshy dark green leaves edged and tinged red. Small starry white or pale pink flowers may be produced in late summer

A deciduous, spreading large shrub or small tree with mid-green leaves. Flowers are distinctive globe shaped, from deep to mid pink, usually flowering in early spring on bare wood, before the plant produces leaves.

A medium-sized, epiphytic orchid with 20-30cm long, leathery leaves. New growth appears from the base of swollen stem - pseudobulb, a storage organ for water and nutrients. They are oval to elliptic-shaped, slightly flattened around the top, carrying 1-3 leaves at the tip. Base of new pseudobulb is partially covered with two pairs of green, leafed sheaths. The plant typically flowers from early summer to autumn on 40-60cm long, arching stems. New flowering stems arise from the axils of young, mature pseudobulbs and the leafed sheaths, carrying up to 15 flowers. Unusually shaped flowers are yellow with dark brown-red spots. Long, slender petals and sepals give the flower its spider-like appearance

primary_name: Iris foetidissima from Picos de Europa

description: Bushy upright rose to about 90cm in height, with glossy small, glossy dark green leaves, and abundant, strongly fragrant, very full crimson-purple blooms with a white centre and prominent gold stamens, from early summer to autumn

Bushy rose to about 1m tall, with leathery, mid-green leaves and lightly scented, large full blooms 12cm across, of apricot, the outer petals paler, produced singely on long sturdy stems, flowering through summer and autumn
A bushy, compact rose to 80cm, with glossy dark green leaves and bearing very fragrant, rich purple-crimson blooms, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn
A compact, repeat-flowering, shrub rose to 1m tall with shiny foliage and fragrant, shallow-cupped, fully-double, mid pink rosettes, 9cm across, from early in summer to late autumn

A mixture of annual climbers growing to about 1.8m with the help of tendrils, and producing very strongly scented, flowers in a mixture of colours includiing white, cream, light and dark pink, lilac, mauve and purple, in summer and early autumn
A compact tuberous rooted perennial to less than 1m in height. It bears Fimbriated form, light bronze flowers above green foliage in summer and early autumn
Bushy, healthy rose to 90cm tall, with glossy green foliage, and clusters of lightly-scented semi-double golden-yellow blooms with golden stamens, repeat flowering through summer and into autumn
A double-flowered cultivar with green foliage and yellow and sugar pink flowers with notched tips to the petals. Flowers appear through summer and early autumn on stems to around 60cm tall
A tuberous-rooted perennial that grows up to 1.8m tall. It bears clear-lemon Ball form flowerheads, up to12cm across, in summer and autumn above green foliage
A tuberous-rooted perennial that grows to 1-1.5m tall. Its Cactus form, yellow flowerheads, in summer and autumn, can be up to 25cm across
A herbaceous perennial up to 1m high, with divided green leaves, and orange-tinged, golden yellow semi-cactus flowers, 25cm across, in summer
A tuberous-rooted perennial that grows to 1-1.5m in height and bears flowers, in summer and autumn, that are a blend of pale yellow and orange
A tuberous perennial to 1-1.5m tall with large, double orchid, clear yellow flowers borne in summer and early autumn above green foliage

A miniature-sized, cool-growing epiphytic orchid with oval-shaped, thick leathery leaves pointed at the end. Each leaf is wrapped in white, papery sheaths. Individual flowers emerge from the central point at the back of the leaf. They flower mainly in winter or spring, but flowers can appear consecutively throughout the year. Up to 3cm large, raspberry-red flowers are large compared to the overall size of the plant. Fused, lateral sepals and narrow petals give them an almost insect-like appearance

Diminutive, compact miniature rose about 30-40cm tall, with glossy dark green leaves and bearing clusters of long-lasting, ruby-red fully double blooms 5cm across, almost continuously produced through summer

Compact rambling rose to 4m tall with healthy, mid-green leaves and clusters of fragrant, small, semi-double, pale pink flowers to 5cm across, lightly flushed peach then fading to creamy-white, with golden stamens and held in sprays on long flexible stems. Flowers borne in great abundance almost continuously through summer and autumn

A small-sized, clump-forming orchid with narrowly cylindrical, 5-15cm long green stems (pseudobulbs). Each pseudobulb is completely covered with thin, leaf-bearing sheaths. Oval, or lance-shaped glossy green leaves are arranged alternately on the upper half or near the top of each pseudobulb. Short flowering stem carrying a dense cluster of flowers appears from the tips of mature pseudobulbs. Each bright pink/purple flower is 2-3cm large with orange lip.

A medium-sized, tropical orchid with 30-40cm long, upright cane-like stems. Each stem (pseudobulb) is also a storage organ of water and nutrients. The canes are covered with alternate thin, leaf-bearing sheaths covered in dense, short black hairs. Leaves are dark green, oval or elliptic, spaced along the whole length of the canes. The plant flowers with short clusters of attractive, star-shaped white or pale green flowers with bright orange lip. Flowers are 5-6cm large, long-lasting and fragrant.

primary_name: × Laeliocattleya Cariads Mini Quinee gx 'Angel Kiss'

description: An evergreen, epiphytic orchid with fleshy, green leaves overlapping the long, pendulous central stem. The leaves are flat, arranged alternately around the stem in one plane, creating a herringbone pattern. Each succulent leaf is 3-5cm long and lance-shaped. Flowers are insignificant, around 1cm and pale yellow; produced on short flowering stems along the central stem in autumn.

A clump-forming annual or biennial to about 60cm in height, with branched stems covered in ferny mid-green foliage, and clusters of delicate, daisy-like flowers to 2.5cm wide, with lavender to purple ray florets and yellow central disc florets, produced over a long period from early summer to autumn

An evergreen perennial alpine forming a compact cushion of rosettes of narrowly oblong leaves, with fragrant, slender-tubed, pure creamy-white primrose-like flowers borne just above the foliage. This variety is believed to be a hybrid between D. odora and D. tapetodes
A cultivar that bears cerise-coloured flowers in summer and early autumn. Height to around 1.2m

primary_name: Primula obconica 'Touch Me Red' (Touch Me Series)

description: A small, semi-evergreen perennial with dark green, lance-shaped foliage. Masses of outward facing, pure white star-shaped flowers provide a long flowering display in summer

A low-growing perennial that forms a neat, evergreen mat of atractive small, round, dark green, toothed leaves. Numerous, outward facing, white, bell-shaped, single flowers are borne on short stalks sitting just above its foliage providing a long flowering display in summer

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid with long, cane-like, stems (pseudobulbs). The stems are green and fleshy when young, maturing to yellow-green. Green, glossy, lance-shaped leaves are approximately 8cm long and 4 cm wide. Upright flowering stems up to 40cm long emerge from the upper nodes on mature stems and bear 6-15 flowers. The flowers are approximately 5-6cm large, pale or dark yellow, with purple/mauve centre of the lip. Petals are usually darker in colour with yellow edges and light brown or mauve overlay. They are twisted upwards at the base.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid producing a clump of leaf rosettes. The leaves are tesselated with pale and dark-green, often purple-spotted underneath. The leaves are narrowly oval, up to 15cm long and 2.5cm wide. Solitary flowers, 8-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 9-20cm long, upright stems. Petals are round, pale yellow or white with dark pink edges and tesselation. Lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. The pouch is round, white, pale or dark pink

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with narrowly oval leaves, 20-30cm long and 4-5cm wide. The surface of the leaves is dark and light green mottled reddish towards the centre of rosettes and underside. Flowering stems up to 30cm tall appear from the centre of the leaf rosettes and carry one, 10cm large flower. The flowers are glossy and long-lasting; dark red, with almost black petals and linear markings on petals and upper sepal

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with narrow, strap-shaped, glossy green leaves. The leaves are leathery, semi-rigid, up to 50cm long and 5cm wide. Upright flowering stems emerge from the centres of the leaf rosettes in spring and summer, carrying two to six flowers. Large flowers, 15-20cm across are yellow or lime-green, with contrasting, dark-brown pattern. The pouch is dark pink or red, often with yellow upper margin

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, tropical, epiphytic orchid, valued for its large, round, bright-coloured flowers. As a typical example of a monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from the central tip on a long, stem-like rhizome. Strap-shaped, green or dark green, alternate leaves up to 40cm long angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves develop at the top, older, lower leaves gradually drop off. A characteristic feature of plant is an impressive root system, hanging downwards at the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Flower stems develop from the axils of leaves, carrying approximately 8 large, waxy, round-shaped flowers. Each flower is over 10cm in diameter, with all petals and sepals uniform in size, shape and colour. They are tessellated in purple-blue, dense, mosaic-like pattern.

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for its large, bright-coloured, long-lasting flowers, often used by florists. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a central tip on a long, central stem-like rhizome, covered in alternate leaf-bearing sheats. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves up to 50cm long angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves grow at the top, old, lower leaves gradually fall off. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system, that hangs down from the base of the plant. New roots grow out of the main rhizome, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from the axils of leaves and main stem, and carry up to 8 large, waxy, round-shaped flowers. 'Purple Ink' is a cultivar with long-lasting, striking dark purple flowers, 8 -10cm across. All petals and sepals are flat, round and uniform in size. Lower sepals have stronger tesselation, giving slightly darker appearance. A very popular cultivar.

A large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for its large, unusual, long-lasting flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from the central tip on a long, stem-like rhizome, covered in green, alternate, leaf-bearing sheaths. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves, up to 50cm long angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves appear on the top of the plant, old leaves, lower on the stem, gradually fall off. A typical feature of the plant is an impressive roots system, of pale aerial roots that hangs downwards from the base of the plant. New thick roots emerge from the central rhizome, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from the axils of leaves and the stem, and carry 6 or more large, flat, round-shaped flowers. This hybrid is typical with its large tesselated flowers, over 10cm across, and with lower sepals distinctively darker to upper half of the flower. Petals and sepals are pale pink, with dark red/maroon spotted markings at the centre, and tesselated pattern covering the lateral sepals.

A medium-sized, epiphytic orchid producing a clump of ovoid pseudobulbs, each carrying four to six, semi-rigid, linear leaves up to 50cm long and 1.5-2cm wide. Up to 20 flowers are carried on pendant flowering stems from early winter. Up to 8cm large flowers vary in colour from orange, salmon or pink, depending on cultivar. The most notable cultivars are 'December Orange' with burnt orange, and 'December Pinkie' with pale pink flowers. The flowers' lip is usually white with dark red markings. Petals and sepals often have pale white or cream edge.

A large-sized, epiphytic orchid up to a meter tall and wide, producing a clump of green, spindle-shaped pseudobulbs, which serve as a storage organs for water and nutrients. A pair of dark-green, stiff, evergreen leaves 25-70cm long and 4-11cm wide are carried at the tip of each mature pseudobulb. The orchid usually flowers in spring on pendulous stems up to one metre long, carrying up 60 flowers, spaced 2.5cm apart. Flowers are 4cm across and cream with a dark-brown pattern on a white lip

A medium-sized, evergreen epiphytic orchid valued for its unusual, spotted, long-lasting flowers. The plant produces a clump of egg-shaped pseudobulbs, covered in leaf-bearing, sheaths. Leaves are semi-rigid, leathery, linear up to 60cm long and 2-3cm wide. The plant flowers on arching flowering stems, emerging from the base of new, mature pseudobulbs in winter and spring. Each raceme carries up to twenty, densely arranged flowers. The flowers are 5-6cm across, pale yellow-green and pink, heavily spotted with irregular dak maroon spots. The lip is pale cream, densely spotted with a yellow centre

An evergreen, epiphytic orchid with narrowly oval leaves to around 60cm long. From winter into spring, long, erect to arching stems bear flowers of the deepest purple to nearly black edged with a thin white line

An evergreen, epiphytic orchid with shining, upright, lance-shaped leaves and long-lasting sprays of fragrant flowers on long stems. Flowers have five green, radiating petals marked with variable amounts of dark red spotting, and a broad purple lip with a white edge

A medium to large-sized epiphytic orchid with broadly elliptic, dark green, leathery leaves. The plant produces a large clump of ovoid pseudobulbs (thickened stems at base of each growth), which serve as a storage organ for water and nutrients. Each pseudobulb carries one 40cm long and 10cm wide leaf. Pendant flower stems up to 20cm long bear one or two large, fleshy, sweetly scented flowers. Flowers of this variety are up to 18cm across, pale yellow with more distinct, dark red markings that cover most of the petals and sepals.
A bulbous perennial to 1.2m in height, with erect, strap-like leaves and rounded clusters of star-like, dark purple flowers in late spring

In summer, mature plants produce brush-like, pinkish-red flowers composed of numerous tufts of stamens

description: A bushy, deciduous shrub to 2.5m tall with broadly ovate deep green leaves that turn shades of yellow and orange in autumn. Dense clusters of scented flowers with crimped, slender petals are a deep golden-yellow suffused with red
A tropical evergreen shrub, with an upright habit, and sparsely branching stems bearing dense whorls of elliptic, deep green leaves with streaks of light yellow-green in the centre

A bulbous perennial to 35cm tall, with 3 flowers per stem. The fragranced flowers are up to about 10cm wide, with white perianth segments and a flattened, divided, soft lemon-yellow coloured, frilled cup that overlaps the perianth segments
An early to mid-season dwarf cultivar with moderately-reflexed yellow outer petals and a funnel-shaped yellow trumpet with a slight orange tinge
An April-flowering daffodil with with creamy white petals surrounding a flattened, pale yellow cup. It produces several flowers per stem
A cactus with solitary, short-cylindrical stems to 20cm tall, with dense, fine yellow spines and numerous bright yellow or orange flowers 2cm across

alternative_names: wine-fragrant chin cactus|Till's chin cactus|Gymnocalycium tillianum
description: A cactus with flattened-globose, grey-green stems to 12cm diameter with 10-13 tubercled ribs, with stout radial spines. Funnel-shaped wine-red or salmon-pink flowers to 5cm across

An upright, deciduous, often vase-shaped, shrub to 4m tall with broadly oval green leaves that turn attractive shades of red in autumn. Slightly fragranced, purple-orange flowers with narrow crimped petals and dark burgundy-red calyx are borne on the bare branches in late winter and spring

An upright, deciduous, often vase-shaped, shrub to 2.5m tall with broadly oval green leaves that turn attractive shades of orange and yellow in autumn. Slightly fragranced, reddish-purple to orange flowers with narrow crimped petals are borne on the bare branches in late winter and spring

A deciduous, rounded shrub to 2.5m tall and wide with broadly ovate leaves that turn shades of yellow and orange in autumn. Clusters of lightly scented, deep orangeflowers with crimped petals are borne on the bare branches in winter

A compact, upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 45cm in height, with green divided foliage and a well-branched habit. Short stems produce rich violet-blue flowers from May to July. Great for pots and containers or at the front of a border

alternative_names: blue amaryllis|Hippeastrum raineri|Amaryllis rayneri|Amaryllis procera|Hippeastrum procerum|Worsleya rayneri

description: A compact climbing deciduous shrub reaching up to 2m in height. Leaves undivided, ovate to oblong, in pairs, green with a more glaucous underside. Flowers are intensely fragrant, borne in clusters at the ends of the shoots. Flower buds are deep purple, opening to pink becoming a deep yellow as the flowers mature

A deciduous, clump-forming perennial with leathery, glossy, jagged- and red-edged leaves forming a low mound to around 15cm tall; leaves often become flushed with red in autumn. From spring into early summer, deep pink flowers are borne on stems to 30cm tall above the leaves

A late season dessert apple producing crops of sweet, aromatic, bright red apples with yellow markings that store well over the winter; this cultivar is noted for its abundant spring blossom but is not self-fertile so will require a pollinating partner from group 3 to set fruit

An evergreen perennial, with fans of stiff, broadly sword-shaped green leaves. In late spring and early summer, produces clusters of pale blue flowers, tightly pressed to upright stems. These are followed by oblong capsules filled with small black seeds in autumn

A group of vigorous evergreen perennials, somewhat larger than the species, often to around 1.2m high in flower but can reach up to 1.75m in ideal conditions. Plants form a large clump of erect, linear leaves, with clusters of white flowers borne on stiff stems in late spring and early summer, followed by conspicuous seed capsules

alternative_names: New Zealand satin flower Formosa Group|Chilean iris|Libertia formosa
description: A robust evergreen plant forming a mass of narrowly sword-shaped, leathery leaves; bowl-shaped white flowers 3cm wide are borne in clusters on stiff stems in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Beta vulgaris subsp. cicla var. flavescens 'Red Magic'

description: A compact, deciduous climber to 1.2m tall. White flowers flushed pink towards the base and with pink-purple central bars are borne from early summer into autumn
A medium-sized, compact deciduous perennial climber with dark green leaves. Large, rich dark pink to pale red flowers with creamy anthers appear from late spring through until early autumn
An evergreen herbaceous perennial that forms a clump of golden variegated strap-like leaves and rounded heads of light blue tubular flowers in Summer that reach approximately 45cm in height.

A compact deciduous shrub to 90cm high, with spiny stems and small ovate leaves that are bright orange in spring, maturing to shades of red and purple. Small, golden yellow flowers in spring are followed by red fruits in autumn
A deciduous, tuberous perennial, to about 80cm in height, with green foliage. Large, bright red decorative flowers, yellow at the base of the petals, appear from July through to October
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with frilly cream-white flowers and a lime-green eye in summer.

A compact, half-hardy evergreen perennial to around 40cm high, with dense clumps of narrow, stiff blue-green leaves. In early to mid summer, produces a few sprays of nodding light blue flowers held above the foliage, occasionally followed by round blue berries

A fully double, perennial coneflower variety producing upright blooms with a prominent lime green pompom surrounded by creamy-white-green ray petals, toothed at the ends. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators
An annual growing to around 60cm tall with lance-shaped leaves and, from summer into autumn, double, bicoloured blooms borne on branched stems in a range of colours
A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 45cm high with wavy-edged, upright green leaves streaked and spotted with white. Bright yellow flowers are borne on sturdy stems in summer

A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 40cm tall. The upright, green leaves are spotted and streaked with white and edged with a thin line of purple; purple flowers are borne erect on sturdy stems in summer
A tuberous perennial up to 70cm tall forming a clump of erect, glossy, white-spotted, dark green leaves. In summer, upright stems bear flowers with spathes in shades of red, orange and yellow

A clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 70cm tall with lightly spotted, dark green, broadly lance-shaped foliage. In summer, pink to dark pink spathes with darker purple to black outer surfaces are borne on upright stems
A rhizomatous perennial, to about 60cm tall, forming upright clumps of broadly lance-shaped, dark green leaves flecked with white. Dark purple flowers are produced in summer
A clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 70cm tall with semi-evergreen, glossy, white-flecked leaves and orange-red flowers in summer

A tuberous perennial to 50cm tall forming clumps of upright, broadly lance-shaped green leaves streaked with white. In summer, predominantly purple flowers flushed with dark pink-reddish shades are borne on sturdy stems

A clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 55cm tall with dark green, broadly lance-shaped leaves flecked and spotted with white. Flowers comprise an outer white spathe flushed cream towards the base surrounding the inner pale yellow spadix
A tuberous, clump-forming perennial with upright, broadly ovate green leaves flecked with white and red to dark pink flowers borne on sturdy stems in summer

A tender perennial to 60cm tall, forming an upright clump of slender, white-spotted, dark green leaves. In summer it produces striking flowers composed of red spathes wrapped round a yellow spadix; the flowers are held on stout, dark red stems. Grow as a houseplant, for summer bedding or cut flowers

A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 30cm high with wavy-edged, upright green leaves and very dark purple to black flowers which appear from summer to early autumn. May be grown as a house or conservatory plant or as a summer patio plant
A compact, hardy evergreen shrub to around 20cm in height, with dark green to copper coloured needle-like foliage with pointed tips

primary_name: Celosia argentea var. cristata (Cristata Group) 'Act Zara'
description: An annual to around 70cm in height with green, veined foliage and broad, bright orange flower combs on tall, strong, unbranched stems. Part of the Celosia Act series, which is known for its bright colors, long vase life, and resistance to disease

A deciduous climber, to around 2m high, with stems tinted purple when young, and oval-shaped green leaves. Flowers are large, pale pink with a fine dark pink edge, and up to 15cm across. Flowers are produced from late spring to late summer, with double flowers produced on last year's wood, and single or semi-double flowers produced on new growth. These are followed by persistent seedheads
An evergreen shrub to 2m. It has sword-shaped leaves to 50cm long; the foliage emerges bronze and becomes green with cream variegation as it matures. A good container plant
A herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 1.25 metres in height with large, white, rounded flowerheads that are uniquely shaped and slightly wonky stems giving the name 'Zig Zag'

A vigorous clump-forming, insectivorous perennial, 40-60cm high. The pitchers are large, lime-green at the base of the tube, fading to white at the back of the hood with deep red veining; hood is dark burgundy red underneath. Large, pendent red flowers are produced on upright stems in the spring
