A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with green, strawberry-like leaves spreading to a width of 50cm. Deep, velvety red semi-double flowers are borne on long stalks 40cm high all summer long

Compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial about 70-90cm tall, with dark green serrated leaves. This cactus form has fully-double, spikey-petalled, soft lemon-yellow flowers to 11cm across, which bloom on long, sturdy, upright stems from midsummer through until the first frosts of autumn

Tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.2m tall, with mid-green foliage. The very large, fully-double, bright pink flowers with slightly incurved, neat, pointed petals, dark pink in the centre and fading towards the edges, are about 20cm across and produced from mid-summer to the first frosts

A Brussels sprout cultivar producing crops of smooth, dark green, sweet and crunchy buttons that remain in good condition on tall, sturdy stalks for several weeks from autumn into winter; this cultivar is resistant to clubroot

A biennial leafy vegetable, usually grown as an annual for its edible buds. This F1 hybrid produces stems to 75cm high, with large, bright green buttons with a sweet flavour. Ready to harvest from October to December depending on sowing time
A purple brussel sprout to 1m with good cropping over a long season

A British bred, hardy annual variety producing sweet and mild flavoured, medium sized sprouts on tall stems that can be harvested between December and February. Noted for its high yields and excellent flavour

A hardy annual vegetable with high yields of smooth, dark-green buttons with an attractive lighter centre on tall stems. A good variety for Christmas sprouts which can be harvested between September and December
A hardy, mid-late season, annual vegetable producing dark-green sprouts on a sturdy column up to 90cm tall. Flavour improves after exposure to cold

A top performing hardy annual sprout that is the customer favourite for flavour in supermarket trials because of its exceptional mild-sweet taste. It has a good holding ability and can be harvested between September and December, perfect for Christmas Day dinner

A quick-growing, bushy evergreen shrub to around 3m in height, with oval-shaped, dark green glossy foliage. Pink buds open to fragrant, near-white flowers in spring, followed by black berries in the autumn. Care should be taken not to confuse 'Grandiflora' with 'Grandiflorum' which is deciduous

Vigorous, stong, upright rambler rose about 3.6m tall, with rich glossy green foliage, and very free-flowering clusters of showy, semi-double, crimson blooms with prominent yellow stamens, once-flowering in midsummer

A hardy biennial grown as an annual vegetable. A British bred Cavolo Nero variety with distinctively tall, narrow dark grey-green leaves which have a savoyed appearance. The leaves can be harvested as baby leaf or left to mature, they have a rich flavour and delicate texture. Shows some resistance to bolting

A popular, hardy annual kale with attractive, densely curled, deep green leaves on tall branching stems. It produces an abundant crop of Winter greens throughout Autumn and Winter, showing excellent hardiness. Can be harvested as baby leaf or left to mature. The flavour is improved with cold temperatures

alternative_names: borecole 'Laciniato'|Brassica oleracea (Acephala Group) 'Laciniato Nero di Toscana Precoce'

description: A Triumph Group tulip about 50cm tall, with single cup-shaped flowers of ivory-white with a blush of bright pink on the edges that develops and spreads as the flower matures, and blushed pale pink on the inside of the petals, the flowers carried from mid-late spring

A compact, short-lived perennial to 60cm tall and wide forming a mound of greyish-green, hairy, lance-shaped leaves. Flowerheads borne from early summer into early autumn on short stems are up to 6cm in diameter and comprise tubular, burnt orange petals often tipped with yellow surrounding a large reddish-brown centre

A vigorous, cold tolerant leek with white stems and dark leaves to a height of 45cm, stands well over a long period without bolting. Tolerates extreme cold well and is resistant to rust. Leeks are herbaceous perennials usually grown as annual vegetables, with upright stems which can be blanched white, and green or blue-green leaves about 30-50cm long; plants may flower by bolting in their first year, or the following year if left overwinter, with stems up to 1.5m high topped by rounded flowerheads 5-9cm across of hundreds of star-like pale pink to white flowers which are visited by bees, in summer.

A traditional French leek with attractive steel blue leaves, very good flavour and tolerates cold weather very well. Leeks, Allium porrum are herbaceous perennials usually grown as annual vegetables, with upright stems which can be blanched white, and green or blue-green leaves about 30-50cm long; plants may flower by bolting in their first year, or the following year if left overwinter, with stems up to 1.5m high topped by rounded flowerheads 5-9cm across of hundreds of star-like pale pink to white flowers which are visited by bees, in summer.

A British bred, hardy biennial vegetable grown as an annual. Noted for its superb vigour and uniformity with thick white shanks and long standing capability in the garden. Also ideal for growing individually as pot leeks.

A hardy perennial usually grown as an annual vegetable, with thick, upright dark green leaves. This F1 hybrid leek produces a good yield of thick, uniform stems, and shows some resistance to bolting. Ready to harvest from November depending on sowing time

A perennial usually grown as an annual, with long, lance-shaped, dark green leaves arching over as they grow. The leaf-bases are wrapped around each other to form the edible 'stem', usually blanched white. If not harvested, plants will go on to flower in summer, producing strong, upright stems to 1.5m topped with a rounded flowerhead of small, star-shaped, white flowers. This is a well-flavoured leek cultivar, with thick stems, standing well for several months, to allow cropping from mid-autumn to late winter

A hardy perennial usually grown as an annual vegetable, with thick, upright blue green leaves. Produces a good yield of uniform stems with easy to peel leaves. Performs well as a second early, ready to harvest from October depending on sowing time

alternative_names: California fan palm|American cotton palm|Arizona fan palm|desert fan palm|petticoat palm
description: a medium to large palm, with a robust trunk. The long leaf stalks have sharp teeth near the base, and the fan-shaped, grey-green blades up to 3m long are erect at first, then spreading and arching. Dead foliage remains on the plant, hanging down to clothe the whole trunk. Creamy-white, tubular flowers are produced in huge sprays up to 5m long, usually in summer
plant_range: SW USA (CA & AZ) & NW Mexico (Bajo Clifornia)

description: A spreading deciduous tree about 15m tall, with pale silver-grey bark, and rounded, glossy green leaves to 10cm across, paler greyish-green beneath that turn yellow-gold in autumn; very fragrant white flowers are borne in pendent clusters, in summer

Compact, bushy, upright herbaceous perennial about 45cm tall, with aromatic, dark green, oval to lance-shaped leaves and long whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped purple-blue flowers which are very attractive to pollinators all through summer to autumn
Compact, clump-forming perennial with mid-green lance shaped leaves, and clusters of rose-pink funnel-shaped flowers with a yellow throat streaked with dark brown, flowering in summer and autumn

A low-growing perennial that forms neat, compact mounds of small, green, toothed, lance-shaped foliage. One of the earliest cultivars to flower, it has numerous, outward facing, vivid violet-blue, bell-shaped single flowers which appear on short stalks, sitting just above its foliage, providing a long flowering display in summer. An easy to grow plant but dislikes wet winters

A clump-forming perennial to around 45cm high in flower, with a spreading habit and simple, downy green leaves. Flowers from late spring to mid summer, with slender stems bearing buds encased in overlapping bracts, which open to large, showy flowers, with a ring of pure white outer florets surrounding a crowd of tiny, rich purple flowers in the centre
A compact, short-lived perennial to 30cm tall bearing yellow flowerheads with central deep red blotches from summer into autumn
A sweet William that can flower for more than one season. Clusters of sweetly scented flowers that open white and fade to pink as they age

primary_name: Echinacea [Double Scoop Lemon Creme] ('Balsclemc') (Double Scoop Series) (d)
description: A highly attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing fragrant, pale yellow, double blooms from summer into autumn with a prominent central pompom surrounded by short, broad, drooping ray petals. Excellent as a cut flower or planted en masse in the border

A clump-forming perennial to 60cm tall with hairy, ovate to lance-shaped leaves. Flowerheads up to 7.5cm in diameter and borne on sturdy, branching stems comprise deep pinkish-red, overlapping ray florets surrounding a bronze to dark brown central cone
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 50cm tall with narrowly ovate leaves and flowerheads of white ray florets surrounding golden-brown cones from summer into autumn

A low-growing, compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial to around 45cm with dark purple to black, divided leaves which may turn greener with too much shade. Large, saucer-shaped single, violet-blue flowers veined with magenta-red appear from May through to July

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 40cm high, forming a mound of lobed, slightly glossy green leaves marked with dark bronze. Very pale pink flowers, with notched petals and faint pink veins, are produced over a long period from late spring
An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and lilac-mauve flowers with a yellow throat in summer

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 30cm tall, with lance-shaped, aromatic, dark green foliage. From mid-summer to early autumn each upright stem carries a whorl of two-lipped, tubular, light purple flowers with decorative, purple-flushed bracts

A compact perennial reaching to 45cm in height but doubling its spreadbyits second year of growth. Greyish-green, toothed, aromatic leaves clothe the stems and densely-packed blue flowers with dark purple calyces are borneon upright spikes in summer and autumn

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage, coated with a silvery powder, and fragrant, double copper-orange flowers, with a barely visible yellow eye, appearing in the spring
An evergreen, perennial, double auricular, to 15cm tall, with rosettes of pale, greyish-green leaves. Clusters of deep red-purple, double flowers appear on short, upright stems in spring

alternative_names: primrose [Belarina Buttercup]|Primula belarina 'Butter Yellow'|Primula 'Belarina Double Yellow'|Primula vulgaris 'Kerbelbut'|Primula [Belarina Butter Yellow]
description: A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage and double butter-yellow flowers with a rosette-shaped collar, appearing from February to May

alternative_names: wood sage [Blue Marvel]|Salvia × sylvestris 'Balsalarv'|Salvia nemorosa 'Blue Marvel'
description: A compact, bushy perennial with aromatic mid-green foliage. Erect flower stems of bright blue flowers appear from summer through to the autumn

alternative_names: small scabious [Flutter Deep Blue]|Scabiosa columbaria 'Balfluttdelu'|Scabiosa columbaria 'Deep Blue'
description: A biennial or short-lived perennial with semi-evegreen, grey-green divided leaves, reaching 35cm. It has blue-mauve flowers on sturdy stems for up to four months through the summer
A compact, mounding perennial to 35cm tall withgrey-green leaves. Branching stems bear a profusion of pink flowers with ruffled petals surrounding the pincushion centre throughout the summer

A compact, rounded evergreen perennial with a mound of lush dark green leaves and masses of fragrant, pale purple flowers with a golden orange blush which appear from spring through to autumn, and sometimes beyond in milder climates

A large, hardy perennial usually grown as an annual vegetable, with thick, semi-upright, mid-green leaves and short, blanched stems. Bred for exhibition purposes due to the heavy leeks it produces, but has a good flavour and tight flesh, making it a great addition to stews, soups and other culinary uses. Sow from January to April for harvesting from September to January

Named after a small island off South Carolina, this heritage variety is a firm favourite due to its crisp, tasty leaves that are delicious in salads and sandwiches. It also boasts good bolt resistance, especially if given a little afternoon shade, and a reasonable resistance to lettuce mosaic virus. This upright variety can grow up to about 30cm tall and can be grown as ‘cut-and-come-again’ or left until a full heart is produced. Sow March – April, harvest June to October.

alternative_names: Sedum mexicanum 'Lemon Coral'|Sedum mexicanum 'Lemon Ball'|Sedum reflexum 'Lemon Coral'
description: A mound-forming, succulent perennial to 10cm tall, with fleshy, needle-like, vibrant yellow-green leaves densely packed on trailing, rooting stems. In summer it produces clusters of small, starry yellow flowers above the foliage

A slow-growing, dwarf cultivar with a mounded habit, the tightly packed short needles are blue grey in colour. This unrushed conifer will grow 30cm by 30cm in ten years. An evergreen focal point for a rock garden or specimen for a conifer collection or a unique bonsai plant

A variety of broad bean, a hardy, upright annual, with square-sectioned stems clothed with oblong, blue-green leaves. Clusters of scented, tubular, black and white flowers are produced all the way up the stem, followed by pods up to 30cm long with an average of six beans per pod

A larger, later cropping cultivar which is sown in spring for harvesting in the summer. Reaches approximately 1.2-1.5m in height, needs full sun and plenty of water when pods are setting for a good yield.

alternative_names: honeyberry 'Honey Bee'|Lonicera caerulea var. kamtschatica 'Myberry Bee'
honeyberry 'Indigo Gem'|Lonicera caerulea var. kamtschatica 'Myberry Farm'

description: An upright to trailing half-hardy deciduous shrub with dark green foliage. Double, pale pink flowers with pale green tips and magenta-purple corollas appear from summer through until autumn

primary_name: Viola cornuta 'Sorbet Lemon Ice Blotch' (Sorbet Series)

description: Robust, evergreen clematis about 1.5-2m tall, with dissected fleshy, glossy, leathery, dark green leaves. Open, flat flowers, 7-8cm across, are borne in panicles in great profusion and have 4-7 but mainly 6 pure white tepals, and short dark yellow stamens, flowering early to mid spring

A compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to 40cm high with wavy-edged, upright green leaves and dark maroon red to black flowers which appear from May to October. May be grown as a house or conservatory plant or as a summer patio plant
A tender perennial with mid green, hairy, strap-shaped leaves. Rich, velvety, deep blue-purple flowers are borne in loose clusters from spring through to autumn

An upright, half-hardy annual to 60cm tall with finely-divided foliage, and from summer into autumn,daisy-like flowers held on branching stems with each lemon-yellow petal fading to white around the edge

A bulbous perennial with upright, lance-shaped grey-green leaves. Fragrant, upright tubular racemes of star-shaped pale to darker yellow flowers appear in April to May if grown outdoors or around February time if grown indoors

A bulbocodium daffodil, 10-20cm high, with green leaves and a long flowering season of upward-facing flowers about 4cm across, cream flushed with yellow towards the base, composed of lance-shaped perianth segments about 1.5cm long and cup-shaped coronas about 2cm long, in early spring

A small, succulent perennial, with a long taproot and thick, oval-shaped green leaves with red margins, arranged in spiral rosettes to around 3cm across. Fragrant white flowers with yellow throats, each around 1.5cm across, are produced in a dense ring around the plant in early summer

alternative_names: Mexican orange [Apple Blossom]|Choisya ternata [Apple Blossom]|Choisya × dewitteana 'Pmoore09'
description: A compact, upright, evergreen shrub to about 1.2m, with dark green foliage composed of three to five slender leaflets. Fragrant, white flowers open from pink buds, giving a two-tone effect, in mid- to late spring and often again in early autumn
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 40cm high with lance-shaped leaves. Flowers borne from midsummer into early autumn comprise a dark brown central cone surrounded by orange to golden-yellow rays

alternative_names: dwarf rock lily 'Purpureum'|Arthropodium purpureum|Arthropodium candidum purpureum
rose deutzia [Yuki Cherry Blossom]|Deutzia [Yuki Cherry Blossom]|Deutzia 'Ncdx2'|Deutzia × rosea 'Ncdx2'
description: A compact, rounded, deciduous shrub to around 60cm tall and wide with ovate, dark green leaves to 7.5cm long that turn attractive shades of purple and bronze in autumn. Panicles of small flowers are borne in late spring and early summer; petals are pink with white margins on the outside and white with a soft pink tint on the inside

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit up to 70cm tall when in flower. It has healthy, mid-green, blade-like leaves and strong, arching flower stems that bear yellow and orange tubular flowers, flushed red towards the edges, from mid to late summer

A compact, clump-forming deciduous tuberous perennial with dark green foliage and double, apricot-orange flowers which pale to yellow at the tips which appear from summer through until the first frosts

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m with mid-green foliage and dark stems. The 10cm flowers, produced from mid-summer to mid-autumn, have a single row of peach and pink outer petals, an inner collar of tubular, pink petals and a yellow centre

A perennial corm with narrow, sword-shaped leaves and erect stems to 60cm, bearing up to 6 funnel-shaped white flowers 5cm wide, marked with yellow on the lower petals, from early spring to early summer
An clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial. Leaves are mid green and strap shaped. Sturdy stems of panicles of trumpet pure white flowers.
A leafy biennial grown as an annual vegetable. This cultivar is a spring cabbage with smooth, dark green leaves, which can be cut as spring greens or left to develop loose hearts.

primary_name: Townsendia parryi from Dead Indian Pass
Eryngium glaciale from Sierra Nevada, Spain

description: A vigorous, semi-evergreen, upright and bushy shrub that can grow to a height of 3m. Its leaves are golden yellow and oval-shaped. Small white flowers in pointed clusters appear between June and July, which are highly attractive to bees. Round black berry fruits are borne in autumn.

primary_name: Linum suffruticosum from the French Alps
Iris aff. gracilipes purple and gold-flowered from Gongga Shan, China
Stachys lavandulifolia from Bolkar Dag, Turkey

description: A clump-forming, tuberous perennial about 80cm in height with toothed, very dark green leaves. Large, fully double, rich, dark ruby-red Decorative flowers with slightly incurved petals, bloom from midsummer until autumn

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous, deciduous herbaceous perennial with green serrated leaves. Peachy-orange, red and yellow double flowers appear from summer through until the first frosts. Good for cutting and border displays
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. White double, Decorative form flowers, creamy-white towards the centre, appear on upright stems from summer until the first frosts
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Tight, neat pompon-shaped white flowers with a pale purple flush appear on upright stems from summer until the first frosts
A compact, upright, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Dark red ruffled double flowers appear on upright stems from summer though until the first frosts of autumn

A low-growing, evergreen shrub to 30cm tall with small, needle-like leaves that are yellow in spring and summer and a yellow-bronze colour in autumn and winter. Pink, bell-shaped flowers are borne in dense racemes from winter into spring
A compact, low-growing evergreen to about 20cm with needle-like, orange-brown foliage. Spikes of tiny, purplish-pink flowers appear from mid-winter to mid-spring

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark green foliage and branched stems bearing dusky rose buds opening to cup-shaped, creamy white single flowers turning redish pink as they mature in late winter and early spring
A low-growing, mat-forming evergreen perennial to around 15cm in height with small, grey-green leaves. Purple flowers with white centres appear on short stems in spring and early summer

primary_name: Dahlia [Happy Days Cherry Red] ('Hdchr23') (Happy Days Series) (Sin)
alternative_names: dahlia [Happy Days Cherry Red]|Dahlia 'Dark Happy Days Cherry Red'|Dahlia 'Hdchr23'
description: A short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 30cm with dark bronzy-green foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers have red, pointed petals, with a dark red central disc opening to yellow

alternative_names: dahlia [Happy Days Lemon]|Dahlia 'Dark Happy Days Lemon'|Dahlia [Happy Days Yellow]|Dahlia 'Hdle105'
description: A short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 30cm with dark bronzy-green foliage, blooming from mid-summer until the first frosts. Single flowers have broad, pale yellow petals and a dark yellow central disc

Tuberous-rooted perennial about 60-90cm tall, with dark stems and mid-green foliage. Flowers, produced from midsummer until the first frosts, have dark reddish-pink outer petals to 7cm wide and a central powder puff of numerous, short, red-tinged, yellow and red petals with toothed tips

A bulbous perennial, to 20cm tall, with erect, grey-green leaves and variable, solitary, nodding, white flowers, in late winter. Bulbs may produce flowers with extra segments, or twin flowers on the same stem, sometimes fused together. The inner segments are marked with a green, inverted V shape at the tips

An unusual annual species to around 150cm in height, with branching stems of dark green, succulent-like leaves. Lightly-fragrant in the afternoon and evening with white, elongated, trumpet-shaped flowers which appear from summer to autumn. More drought-resistant than other species

A semi-evergreen shrub to around 1m (3.2ft). Growth is upright, bushy with mid-green leaves that clasp the stems. In summer it produces an abundance of bright yellow flowers with prominent stamens which emerge from red buds. These are followed in autumn by clusters of oval, red fruit.

Deciduous, small tree to about 3-4m tall, with a narrow, upright growth habit and deeply dissected usually 7-lobed leaves, the reddish spring growth has a silvery sheen then matures to a deep brownish-red, turning vivid red in autumn. Small purple spring flowers are followed by red winged fruits in summer

Shrub or small tree between 2-4m in height. Foliage green, strongly tinted reddish-bronze, contrasting with profusion of pure white bracts which surround small green flower heads, followed by rich autumn colours of deepest mahogany-bronze. Red strawberry-like fruits appear in autumn.

A small, bulbous perennial with narrow, upright, grey-green leaves and relatively large, solitary, nodding, white flowers, the outer petals rounded and full-looking, the inner ones marked with a green, inverted V and green smudges towards the base

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, scented white flowers are produced in late winter, with broad, rounded outer petals with a slight touch of green at the tips, and inner petals marked with an upside down 'v' at the tip and a green blotch at the base. Inner petals are sometimes tinted pale yellow on opening, then fading to white

A clump-forming, bulbous perennial with broad, grey-green leaves and spring flowers borne on stems to around 15cm tall. Flowers are outward-facing with large, broad and cupped outer segments and inner segments blotched green at the base with a small, inverted, green 'V' shape at the apex
Flowers in late spring, bearing creamy-white flowers that open with a pale pink edge to the petals, which spreads and darkens with age to cover the top half of the flower. Height to 50cm

A compact, slow-spreading, elegant, mound-forming deciduous fern with red stems. The fronds have pale green edges and white centres, giving it a frosted ivory appearance. Ideal on a pathway border, in shady areas or for pots and containers
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated, thick blue foliage with a flame-shaped creamy-yellow centre. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 35cm high, with a dense, mounding habit and thick, broadly ovate dark green leaves with narrow cream streaks radiating out from the base of the leaf. Produces loose clusters of bell-shaped pale purple flowers on upright stems in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and yellow centres with a thin white line dividing the two. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A deciduous, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 76cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and purple flowers, with a dark purple eyezone and a pale green throat to 14cm across in summer

An evergreen clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Fragrant flowers are pale purple with a large, wide dark purple eye, green yellow throat and a frilly purple edge to the petals
An evergreen perennial, to 20cm tall, with spreading rosettes of light green leaves. In spring, short stems, held above the foliage, are topped with clusters of double, old gold flowers
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, smooth pale green foliage. Beautiful, double mustard-yellow fragrant flowers, appear in the spring
A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green leaves. Large, raspberry-pink flowers appear on long, strong stems from July through to November. Good for cutting

A short-lived, evergreen perennial to about 50cm. Branching, woody-based stems bear narrow, dark green leaves and terminal clusters of fragrant, dark red flowers which fade to purple, over a long period from spring to autumn
A clump-forming perennial, to around 1m high, with pairs of aromatic, pointed dark green leaves. Rounded flowerheads of tubular, violet purple flowers are produced from mid to late summer

This plant is listed as an invasive non-native species in the UK – see Cultivation section for details A large herbaceous perennial with hairy, lobed, dark green leaves. Tall stems are hollow and hairy. Large compound umbels of white flowers are borne on tall flowering stems in summer, followed by flattened oval brown fruits
This plant is listed on Schedule 9 of the UK Wildlife & Countryside Act as an invasive, non-native species and is banned from sale. See cultivation notes for further details
Upright, bushy rose to about 90cm tall, with mid-green leaves and small clusters of lightly scented, well-formed, double, pale pink blooms repeat-flowering through summer into autumn
An evergreen perennial, to 20cm tall, with rosettes of mealy, yellow-green leaves. Clusters of deep red flowers with pale yellow stripes and eyes are produced on short stems in spring

An herbaceous perennial that reaches appoximately 80cm in height, it produces a clump of strap-like leaves and sturdy flower stems that hold rounded flower heads of purple buds that open to reveal white flowers with a lilac stripe.

An erect, sparsely branched evergreen tree to 6m, bearing burgundy red, sword-shaped leaves to 70cm long at the branch tips. In summer, mature trees produce a mass of tiny, creamy-white flowers in dense clusters to 1m long. A good container plant when young, and makes an architectural tree when mature

A short-lived bushy perennial, with a basal rosette of lance shaped mid-green leaves. It reaches a height of 30-40cm. Deep red flower-heads with golden yellow petal tips open from early summer to autumn.
A clump-forming perennial to about 10cm with a basal cluster of narrow leaves.In summer and autumn produces star-shaped, rich purplish-pink flowers with yellow anthers
A short-lived perennial, often grown as an annual, up to 1.2m high, with lance-shaped green leaves, and racemes of white flowers from summer to autumn
A clump-forming, upright shrub to about 90cm with pale, greyish-green leaves and whorls of pale pink, fluffy flowers in late summer to early autumn

A clump-formiing perennial up to 1.2m high with a basal rosette of green leaves and flowering stems of pincushion-like white flowerheads, throughout the summer if deadheaded; the flowers are good for pollinators, and the seedheads may provide food for finches

Deciduous climber to 2.5m in height, a sport of 'Kiri Te Kanawa' with mid-green leaves and double, lilac flowers to 15cm across, aging to blue, shading pale green at the base of the petals and along the midribs, with red-purple anthers. Double flowers produced on previous seasons old wood and the current seasons new wood, but flowers become smaller as the season progresses

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.1m, with dark stems and mid-green foliage. The semi-double flowers, produced from mid-summer to the first frosts, are 12cm across, peachy-pink, shading to yellow in the centre, with some petals flicked and curved, revealing the dark pink undersides
A bushy, evergreen shrub to 1m tall, with with glossy, leathery leaves. In spring it produces highly fragrant, pink flowers held in clusters at the stem tips
A compact, bushy shrub to around 1.2m tall with dark green, semi-evergreen leaves and in early spring, loose clusters of fragrant, white flowers

primary_name: Delosperma cooperi [Hot Pink Wonder] ('Wowdry1') (Wheels of Wonder Series)
description: A mat-forming evergreen succulent to 10cm tall with fleshy, blue-green leaves. From summer to autumn it bears a profusion of daisy-like flowers to 5cm across; the petals are brilliant pink with a yellow eye. Thrives in full sun on poor soil

A compact, bushy shrub with bright yellow foliage and an abundance of golden-yellow flowers, which are rich in nectar for bees and other pollinating insects, produced from May until June. A striking plant for individual pots.
A short, deciduous bulbous perennial with fleshy strap-shaped leaves and several sturdy stems of large, funnel-shaped flowers which are red with a darker red veining

A fast-growing, semi-evergreen shrub to around 2m high, with palmate grey-green leaves divided into 6-9 leaflets and silky-hairy beneath. Tall clusters of fragrant, pea-like flowers, in shades of pale lavender and violet, are borne at the tips of the stems in late spring and summer

A small, upright, elegant evergreen shrub with a bamboo-like habit to around 1.5m in height, with compound leaves and lanceolate leaflets. These are bright yellow-green becoming darker in winter. Small white flowers in large panicles may appear in summer, but this plant is mainly grown for its foliage

A bushy, upright, evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub to 1.2m tall. Its compound leaves with lance-shaped leaflets are bright pink when young before aging to green splashed with white. Sprays of small white flowers in summer may rarely be followed by red berries

A dwarf, clump-forming bulbous perennial daffodil to around 15cm in height, with green strap-like foliage. Long-lasting, multiple heads of golden-yellow flowers with rosette-like trumpets appear from February to March. A very good variety for pots and containers

A bushy annual to 75cm tall, with very finely divided leaves. In summer it produces white flowers heavily streaked and splashed with blue; the petals surround a boss of purple stamens. Both the flowers and inflated seed capsules that follow can be used for floral arrangements

A summer-flowering, hardy annual, to 60cm tall, with rosettes of divided leaves. The bowl-shaped flowers held erect on wiry stems comprise pure white, slightly crumpled petals, occasionally with a faint pink flush, surrounding a yellow boss of stamens

Vigorous, evergreen climber to 3m or more, with twining tendrils and 3- or 5-lobed, dark green leaves. An erect, rhizomatous perennial to 50cm tall, with stiff, fleshy leaves, tapering to a point. Each leaf bears mottled, light green bands

A low-growing, fast-spreading, clump-forming semi-evergreen perennial with heart-shaped, toothed dark green leaves. Lightly fragrant, soft pink flowers with a white eye appear in mid-spring to early summer. Looks stunning if planted amongst spring-flowering bulbs, and can be cut for posies

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 30cm tall, with mid-green, lance shaped leaves, and clusters of pale yellow, funnel-shaped flowers which have some bright yellow inner petals speckled dark brown, flowering in summer and autumn.
A compact perennial with mid-green leaves cut deeply into three fine lobes. Has pure white flowers with a golden yellow centre late spring and early summer.

A clump-forming upright perennial, with silvery-green thistle-like leaves. Intense blue, spherical flower heads up to 4cm across, are held on tall, grey-green stems throughout the summer.

A shrub up to 25cm high, with a compact habit, evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant violet flowers topped by purple bracts in summer

An intersectional or Itoh peony and an upright and compact herbaceous perennial with attractive, dissected dark green foliage, green in summer, tinged bronzy-red in spring and autumn. Erect stems holding showy, spicily scented, semi-double, saucer-shaped creamy yellow-peach flowers tinged pink appear in summer, with a particularly long flowering period.

A medium-sized, clump-forming perennial to about 40cm high and 80cm across with deeply undulating, narrowly ovate, mid-green leaves with broad, pale yellow margins. Substantial spikes of pale purple, funnel-shaped flowers are produced in summer
A compact, perennial bulb to 30cm in height, with pale green, strap-shaped foliage. White flowers with slightly reflexted petals and a long, frilly, pink and yellow trumpet appear in April

A compact, mound-forming semi-evergreen shrub to 1m in height, with green and cream oval, glossy variegated leaves. The stems are bright red. The clusters of small trumpet-shaped, lightly scented white flowers bloom from midsummer summer into autumn.
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Single white flowers with yellow centres, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly

alternative_names: ginger lily 'Flaming Torch'|Hedychium coccineum var. aurantiacum 'Flaming Torch'

A compact evergreen perennial, forming a low, spreading mound of linear, dark green leaves. Star-shaped, vivid reddish-pink flowers are held just above the foliage in late spring
A deciduous, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped mid-green leaves and sturdy stems which produce large panicles of trumpet-shaped pale to mid blue, sometimes white, flowers in summer
An semi-evergreen, matt-forming alpine with silver-grey to green foliage and small, starry pink flowers
An herbaceous perennial with upright stems of blue-green foliage in threes. Flowers are blue-purple followed by black seed pods

An herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 81cm in height when in flower. It forms a clump of arching, strap-like green leaves and large, yellow-buff coloured flowers with a green throat to 18cm across in summer

A bushy perennial to around 60cm tall with aromatic foliage and long, upright flowering spikes bearing small, pale purple-blue flowers from summer into autumn
A vigorous, bushy perennial to 75cm tall and wide with oval to lanceolate, toothed leaves. Sturdy stems bear spikes of deep violet-blue flowersfrom summer into autumn

An upright, clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial to around 180cm in height, with dark green leaves and spikes of dark red flowers which are fairly late-flowering compared to other cultivars, appearing from September through to November
A tall, rhizomatous perennial, with rosettes of dark green, pinnate leaves and tall, slender flowering stems to 2m high, bearing dark pink, bottlebrush-like flowers to 4cm long in summer

A tall, rhizomatous perennial, with rosettes of green, pinnate leaves and tall, slender flowering stems to 2m high, bearing dark reddish-purple, curving, bottlebrush-like flowers from summer to early autumn

A bushy perennial, to around 90cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Bowl-shaped, fragrant semi-double white flowers are produced in late spring and early summer

An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.5m with large, broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Soft red flowers, fragrant both day and evening, appear from late summer through to October. Best in partial shade otherwise the flowers tend to fade to orange

A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with dark, aromatic green foliage and soft-pink lipped flowers from summer through to autumn.

A bushy, clump-forming, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with leathery dark green foliage and cup-shaped creamy-yellow flowers with a dark wine-red star-shaped eye, appearing from February to April

A compact, strong and sturdy half-hardy annual with feathery green foliage and single, flowers which are white to pink with darker pink edges and yellow centres which appear from July through to October. These make good cut flowers and are very beneficial to pollinating insects

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This tulip has white flowers with pale creamy yellow flaming, produced in late spring. Flowers stand to around 60cm high
A deciduous, rhizomatous, clump-forming perennial with heart-shaped, silver leaves that are veined and edged with green and airy sprays of blue, forget-me-not-like flowers in spring

An upright, deciduous shrub to around 1.2m tall, with ovate, pointed, deeply veined green leaves. Green buds open to upright, cone-shaped white, fragrant flowers, becoming flushed with pink as they mature, appearing from midsummer through to the autumn

A half-hardy, compact, bushy deciduous perennial with dark green foliage and masses of lightly-fragranced white flowers with a yellow eye appearing from summer through until the autumn

A robust and compact, bushy, half-hardy perennial. Petunia [Easy Wave Red Velour] ('Pas933560') (Easy Wave Series)

a tender, trailing perennial grown as an annual, with mid-green, pointed leaves.Double and single flowers in shades of yellow and orange, are produced from mid-summer to autumn

Height around 35cm (14in).

Bulbous perennial about 60cm tall, producing bright-green, strap-shaped basal leaves in spring, which die back before the flowers appear. Clump-forming perennial about 75cm tall, with dark green foliage, and large, distinctive pale to mid-pink flowers to 12cm across, the ray florets are tipped pale green, flowering in early autumn

A bulbous perennial, to around 1.2m high, with upright stems and narrowly lance-shaped, dark green leaves. Large, upward-facing, lemon yellow flowers, brushed and speckled with dark reddish-purple in the centre, are produced in early to mid summer
A dwarf bulbous perennial, to around 45cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped glossy dark green leaves. Upward facing pink to mid pink flowers appear in the summer

A compact bulbous perennial, to around 50cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, upward-facing, light red flowers with dark red speckles are produced in early to mid summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Double white flowers with a pale green stripe down each petal appear in summer

A compact, evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green foliage and clusters of small, fragrant, greenish-white flowers in spring

A spiny evergreen shrub or small tree to 5m tall, with leathery leaves composed of numerous tiny, opposite leaflets. In spring it produces spherical, yellow, pom-pom flowerheads; these are highly fragrant

Vigorous, climbing Noisette rose about 4.5m tall, with almost thornless stems and darkish green foliage. Large clusters of lightly scented, small fully double, blush pink to salmon-pink blooms, in large clusters, repeat-flowering through summer with occasional repeat later in the season. Introduced in 1897
Very compact, well-branched rose to about 30-60cm tall, with pale to mid-green foliage, and bearing lightly fragrant, small, fully double, pinkish-mauve blooms, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

A shrub rose 1.5m high with dark green green leaves and clusters of semi-double red flowers with golden stamens, in early summer and again throughout autumn; leaf-cutting bees may use rose leaves to make nests for their larvae

primary_name: Cardiocrinum giganteum var. yunnanense from Guizhou

description: A spreading, deciduous shrub with arching stems, up to 0.9 -1.2m in the open but taller when grown against a wall. The bright, purplish rose flowers are produced in short racemes from early summer to early autumn, contrasting with the pinnate, grey-green leaves

A multi-stemmed, deciduous shrub to 3m high with oval to oblong glossy green leaves that turn yellow in autumn. Large, fragrant, deep red to purple flowers up to 10cm in diameter are borne from late spring into summer

Short-lived, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall with blue-green, divided foliage forming a basal mound. Large, outward- to upward-facing flowers with dark purple, mid-length spurs and outer petals, and white inner petals, are borne on upright stems from early spring into summer
A compact, evergreen perennial cultivar forming a rhizomatous clump with upright, leathery, green foliage and small clusters of clear pink flowers held atop pinkish stalks in spring
A compact, deciduous climber, to about 1.2m tall, flowering from late spring to early autumn. The single flowers, up to 15cm in width, are deep red with deeper red stamens

Compact, deciduous climber 1-1.2m in height with dark to mid-green leaves and very free-flowering, large, pale pink flowers with wavy, ruffled margins and contrasting red-purple anthers, are borne from early summer to early autumn

Deciduous climber about 2.5m tall, with mid-green leaves and large, single, pale to mid-blue flowers to 22cm across with paler or creamy-white central bars on long, pointed overlapping, tepals, and purple tipped cream stamens, flowering in late spring to early summer and in late summer

Compact, deciduous climber 1-1.2m tall, with mid-green leaves and bearing large, lavender-pink flowers with a central purple-red bar to each petal, and yellow stamens, free-flowering from late spring or early summer to early autumn

An upright, suckering, deciduous shrub to 1.5m tall, with finely toothed, glossy leaves. In late summer and early autumn it produces short, dense spikes of fragrant pink flowers. Grow in a shady border or woodland garden
An upright, deciduous shrub or small tree to around 4m in height with rounded, mid-green foliage. Large, goblet-shaped pale pink striped flowers appear in April

A vigorous, upright, dense clump of slender stems, ranging from green to dark purple-black, with small, narrow green leaves which arch gracefully at the top. Makes an effective screen and ideal also for large container cultivation
A tall, non-invasive, clump-forming bamboo with slender green stems which turn yellow as they mature. Dense, bright green foliage makes this variety ideal for low maintenance hedging and screening

A clump-forming, deciduous, herbaceous perennial, producing narrow, strap-shaped, mid-green foliage, to a height of around 40cm (16in) and spreading to around 40cm (16in). Hemisperical heads of pendulous, funnel-shaped flowers in a deep greyish-blue, are produced in late summer, on straight, green stems, to approximately 1m (39in) high.

An upright, evergreen bushy shrub with oval-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, double pure white flowers with a pale, lemon-yellow centre and a hint of pale pink on the outer petal tips, appear from October to December. Works well with other acid-loving plants such as Azalea, Magnolia or Rhododendron, as a specimen shrub in a container or trained against a wall or trellis

A herbaceous perennial forming a mound of simple stems, bearing slightly blue-green leaves which turn yellow in autumn. The flower buds are steely-blue and open to clusters of five-petalled blue stars over a long period into late summer. This is slightly shorter than the normal form reaching around 50cm, and clumps up faster

A deciduous tree up to 15m tall with three-lobed, bristle-toothed leaves up to 15cm long, the lowers surfaces covered with a greyish down. Panicles of scented, white flowers are followed by bristly, ribbed fruits up to 2.5cm long
An erect, sparsely branched evergreen tree to 3m. It has pink-striped, bronze, sword-shaped leaves to 50cm long; these make a good foil for green-leaved plants. A good container plant
A small and compact perennial that forms neat mounds of lance-shaped, green foliage and abundant, daisy-like bright yellow and red flowers on long stalks, for a long period of time over summer.

alternative_names: dahlia [Dreamy Blush White]|Dahlia 'Dark Dreamy Blush White'
description: A short, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 40cm with dark bronze-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frost bears semi-double flowers with rounded, pale pink petals and a dark brown, central disc opening to orange

primary_name: Alcea rosea 'Spring Celebrities Scarlet' (Spring Celebrities Series) (d)

description: A clump-forming, compact, evergreen perennial with grey-green foliage. Fragrant, double white flowers have a pale lilac centre and serrated edges. Can flower from late spring through to early autumn

A compact and bushy cultivar grown as an annual, flowering from late spring through to the end of summer. Single flowers are white at the edges with a pink and deep red centre, held above narrow green leaves

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing elegant white blooms with narrow, drooping, pure white, ray petals surrounding a prominent central pale yellow cone. Flowers fragrant, excellent for attracting pollinators and using as a cut flower

Compact, upright, perennial coneflower producing apricot-orange blooms from midsummer to autumn. The flowers have narrow, slightly drooping, single petals, surrounding a central brown cone, which gradually mature to soft pink
A clump-forming, cormous perennial with long, strap-shaped green leaves. Produces long, arching spikes of up to 20 soft orange-red flowers from summer to early autumn
A clump-forming, cormous perennial with upright, strap-shaped green leaves. Produces purple-stemmed spikes of tubular to funnel-shaped, orange-red flowers in late summer

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming, dwarf perennial with leathery, dark green foliage and branched stems bearing cup-shaped, single, white flowers with a central boss of golden yellow stamens in winter and early spring

A compact, clump-forming evergreen herbaceous perennial producing large golden yellow to lime green foliage with a dark maroon-blotch in the centre. Star-shaped creamy-white flowers appear on tall, upright stems above the foliage during the summer

A compact, bushy, evergreen shrub to 50cm, with narrow, aromatic, grey-green leaves. In late spring and summer produces dense spikes of tiny, fragrant, purple-pink flowers topped with large, purple-pink bracts
A compact, rounded, evergreen shrub to around 1.2m tall and wide with small, oval golden-yellow to yellow-green leaves. This cultivar is sterile and does not produce flowers

A bushy perennial, to around 75cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Yellow flowers, with paler tips to the petals and rose pink flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

A deciduous, clump-forming, densely-tufted perennial grass about 80cm in height, with upright or arching, linear mid-green leaves and softly bottlebrush-like, narrow, rose pink spikelets in panicles 10-14cm in length, produced in mid to late summer
An erect, herbaceous perennial with dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular deep purple flowers with a white centre over a long period of time in summer.
An evergreen, clump-forming fern with erect, narrowly lance-shaped, bipinnate fronds, with slender-pointed apex and leaflets. This cultivar has fronds almost twice the size of the species.

primary_name: Pulsatilla vulgaris [Pinwheel Blue Violet Shades] (Pinwheel Series)
description: A low-growing, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with green, softly hairy dissected foliage. Dark purple upward-facing, pointed flowers with yellow centres appear from March to April

primary_name: Pulsatilla vulgaris [Pinwheel Dark Red Shades] (Pinwheel Series)
description: A clump-forming deciduous perennial with green, finely dissected basal leaves which have a silky texture to them when young. Dark red, velvety flowers with contrasting yellow centres appear during March and April
A low-growing, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with green, softly hairy dissected foliage. Pure white, upward-facing, pointed flowers with yellow centres appear from March to April
A very compact and bushy perennial with dark green foliage and short racemes of small violet-blue lipped flowers highlighted by reddish-pink bracts in summer.
An semi-evergreen, prostate, compact, perennial alpine. Dark green leaves

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.2m with mid-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frost produces relatively small (10cm) flowers in a light, slightly bluish, pink with a cream centre and cream edges to the petals
A compact rhizomatous perennial, to 12.5cm high, with deeply-lobed pale green leaves with some subtle splashes of variegation. Rose-like double white flowers appear in the spring

A broad, upright spiny deciduous shrub with oval-shaped pink foliage in the spring, variegated with white in the summer and turning soft red in the autumn. Small yellow flowers appear in spring, followed by bright red berries in the autumn

A dense, spreading, deciduous shrub to 1.2m tall with thornless stems bearing glossy dark green leaves. Deep pink, double flowers to 5cm across appear in early spring before the leaves unfurl; this cultivar does not produce fruit
A bushy, deciduous shrub with ovate, toothed leaves and large, domed flowerheads. Flower buds are lime green, opening to paler flowers that fade to white in late summer.

A bushy, upright, deciduous shrub with dark green ovate leaves on dark stems. Flowers are borne on large dense panicles, from late summer, appearing first light green, then white, and maturing to deep pink from the base of the panicle upwards, giving a two-tone effect.

A rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial, up to 90cm high in flower, with glaucous, sword-shaped leaves and scented, bold, brick-red stitch-veined markings over a white base, erect rusty pink standards and golden yellow beards on a yellow base, in May.

A rhizomatous perennial, to 95cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have pale cream standards and falls with faint purple veining, touches of gold and speckles of purplish bronze around the base

A highly attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial bred by Sir Cedric Morris. It has tall, upright, strap-like grey-green leaves and erect stems bearing large, fragrant flowers in late spring-early summer with pale yellow upper petals, known as standards, and yellow-flushed cream-white lower petals, known as falls, with brown veins and yellow beards

An attractive, clump-forming, rhizomatous, herbaceous perennial bred by Sir Cedric Morris, with upright, strap-like, green leaves and erect stems in late spring and early summer bearing dark purple, velvet-black blooms with purple beards
A tender, evergreen subshrub, often grown as an annual, forming a compact, rounded mound to 50 cm tall with divided grey-green leaves and double, bright pink, anemone-centred flowers

A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 40cm high, with small, glossy, divided green leaves with toothed margins. Produces dense, broadly conical clusters of pink flowers in early to midsummer

A compact, extra bushy, hardy annual producing fully double, apricot flowers between May and September until the first hard frost. Easy to grow from seed and perfect as a cut flower. The flowers are edible and are great additions to a summer salad

An evergreen perennial usually grown as an annual, with semi-trailing stems and small, simple leaves. Light orange flowers, with a pale yellow throat outlined in red, are produced over a long period in summer and autumn

An evergreen perennial usually grown as an annual, with semi-trailing stems and small, simple leaves. Vivid, purplish-pink flowers with a yellow throat are produced over a long period in summer and autumn

A compact, bushy, tender perennial, usually grown as an annual, with dark green leaves and very fragrant flowers from May to November. The flowers have pale pink to lavender upper petals, white to pale yellow lower petals, and a yellow eye

A vigorous, slightly mounding and trailing floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces velvety, trumpet-shaped, pale-lilac flowers. It blooms from late spring or early summer into autumn. It trails or gently mounds and spreads around 30 cm to 40 cm so is ideal for hanging baskets and containers.

An upright perennial, to around 80cm high, with thin, lance-shaped green leaves. Tall clusters of fragrant pink flowers, with paler pink centres and dark purple-pink eyes, are produced in mid to late summer
An upright perennial, to around 80cm high, with thin, lance-shaped dark green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant purple flowers with pink and white centres are produced in summer

Bushy old-fashioned rose, rare in cultivation, and about 90cm tall, with dark green foliage. Fragrant, fully double blooms of pale copper and pink, with golden-yellow undertones are borne in small clusters, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn; introduced in 1899

Compact, bushy rose about 1.2m tall, with thorny stems and abundant, crinkled, light to mid-green foliage. Small clusters of fully double, pure white blooms are very fragrant and flower almost continuously through summer to autumn

Bushy shrub rose to about 1.8m tall, with healthy dark green leaves, and bearing lightly scented, semi-double, cherry-red blooms with pinkish-white centres and creamy-yellow stamens, repeat flowering through summer to autumn

Upright bushy Tea Rose about 90cm tall, with rich green foliage. Large, fragrant, classic HT high-centred, fully double white blooms tinged green, are held above almost thornless stems, flowering repeatedly through summer into autumn

Vigorous, spreading rose to 1.2m tall, that can be trained as a small climber, with dark green foliage, and rounded buds opening to sweetly fragrant, fully double, rosette-shaped, pale, blush-pink blooms, repeat flowering through summer and autumn
A large shrub rose to 1.5m in height, with healthy, glossy mid-green foliage and very fragrant, fully-double deep-pink blooms, borne over a long period from late spring to late summer
A bushy upright shrub to 250cm tall, with dark green foliage and large, showy, fragrant, coral-pink flowers from summer through to autumn

Vigorous, bushy rose about 90cm tall, with glossy light green foliage and bearing clusters of fragrant, fully double canary-yellow blooms edged with crimson, produced freely from early summer to autumn

Dense, twiggy hybrid rugosa rose about 90cm tall and wide, with prickly stems and leathery, slightly crinkled and corrugated, bright green leaves. Large, fragrant, fully double, lilac-pink blooms open flat and produced in clusters, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

Vigorous, bushy rose about 75cm tall and wide, with dark green foliage. Very free-flowering, fragrant, semi-double, bright reddish-scarlet blooms in large clusters, repeat-flower from summer to autumn

Large, upright rose about 1.5m tall, with glossy mid-green leaves. Very free-flowering, fragrant, semi-double coppery-yellow blooms, paler with age, have prominent golden stamens, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn followed by oval-shaped orange fruits (hips) in autumn if not deadheaded
A short-lived perennial, often grown as an annual, up to 90cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves, and racemes of white flowers from summer to autumn

An erect, woody-based, deciduous perennial, producing stems to 90cm (3ft) high and a spread of 50cm (20in), with deeply divided, dark-green aromatic leaves. In late summer and autumn, the plants produce sprays of fully-double, white flowers with a lemon yellow centre created by the new unfurling petals. The flowers are long lasting in water and are ideal to grow for cutting. The plants are winter hardy throughout most of the UK, but if grown in colder areas, are best heavily mulched over winter, or lifted after flowering and kept in cold, but frost-free conditions until spring.
A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m with mid-green foliage. White flowers up to 15cm across, with spiky-looking, quilled petals, are produced from mid-summer until the first frost.

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.5m, with mid-green foliage. The 20cm blooms have deep red petals, darkest in the centre, rolled under at the edges to give a spiky effect, and produced from mid-summer until the first frost
An anemone-type cultivar with green, divided foliage and upright stems to 80cm tall bearing flowers with a single row of soft pink outer florets surrounding a double rust-orange centre

A clump-forming, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with leathery dark green foliage and large, cup-shaped, pink flowers with dark pink spotting and a yellow eye, appearing from January through to March
An annual climber growing to about 1.8m with the help of tendrils, and producing very strongly scented, dark purple to black flowers in summer and early autumn

An erect, stout-stemmed, hardy annual to 1m tall, with lobed, hairy leaves. From summer to autumn it produces broadly trumpet-shaped, pure white flowers with silky petals; the flowers are particularly attractive to pollinating insects

An upright annual with small, lance-shaped dark-green leaves and large clusters of white flowers with a subtle yellow eye for a long period of time in summer. Has long branching, wiry stems, very suited as a cut flower
A perennial bulb, up to 50cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are double and rich reddish pink

A perennial bulb with broadly ovate green leaves. This tulip has goblet-shaped flowers, opening pale yellow and fading to creamy white. Flowers are produced in mid to late spring, and stand to around 45cm high

A perennial bulb with broadly ovate green leaves. This tulip has dark reddish purple, goblet-shaped flowers with pointed petals. Flowers are produced in mid to late spring, and stand to around 40cm high
A bushy annual to 45cm with sturdy, upright stems topped by small, very double flowers in dark pink, very pale pink, red, orange and yellow

primary_name: Zinnia elegans 'Benary's Giant Lime' (Benary's Giant Series)
description: A tall, half-hardy annual, having large, double, lime-green flowers to 15cm (6in) across, with a ring of yellow florets in the centre. They are produced on stems up to 90cm (36in) tall. The flowers are produced over a long period and are good to grow for cutting and in wildlife gardens, where they will attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators.

primary_name: Zinnia elegans 'Benary's Giant Wine' (Benary's Giant Series)

description: A bushy, half-hardy annual, with very large semi-double flowers in bright shades of red, pink, yellow and orange; produced on long stems up to 90cm (36in) high, This makes them ideal for growing for cut flowers and for the wildlife garden, where they will be attractive to pollinators such as bees and butterflies.

A mix of half-hardy annuals or short-lived perennials, up to 90cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Open clusters of fragrant flowers, with long tubes and flaring petals, are produced in summer and into early autumn, in shades of white, pale pink and deep pink

A triandrus daffodil to around 50cm tall flowering in mid-spring. The scented white flowers, usually two per stem, are up to 75mm wide with broadly ovate, overlapping perianth segments and a cup-shaped, ribbed and wavy corona
An evergreen shrub to 1.8m, bearing leathery, glossy, dark green leaves. In early winter it produces clusters of highly fragrant white flowers in clusters at the stem tips

A compact, clump-forming perennial houseplant which may grow to around 1.2m in height, with smooth, cylindrical, fleshy grey-green striped leaves which grow outwards from a central clump into a fan shape. Mature plants may rarely produce upright spikes of fragrant, spidery, pinkish-white flowers

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing an abundance of vibrant golden-yellow flowers, measuring 7cm across, with overlapping, drooping ray petals radiating around a central copper-gold cone. Excellent for container growing and attracting pollinators

A large-sized, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with cane-like, noded stems up to 150cm long. The stems (pseudobulbs) are covered in thin, alternate, leaf-bearing sheaths. Oval-shaped, green or dark green, leathery leaves are 8-10cm long. Upright flowering stems up to 45cm long from the upper nodes of mature, leaf-bearing or leaf-less stems. Each raceme carries up to 20 long-lasting, 4-5cm large, yellow flowers with spirally twisted, upright petals.

A large-sized, evergreen orchid with long, upright cane-like stems. Each stem can be up to 120cm long, covered with thin, alternate sheaths. Dark green, leathery, lance-shaped leaves are arranged or the upper half of stems and are 8-15cm long. Arching flowering stems carry up to 20 flowers. Each flower is 5-7cm large, white, occasionally with pale yellow or green centre.

alternative_names: southern white cedar 'Rezek'|Chamaecyparis obtusa 'Rezek' [1]|Chamaecyparis thyoides 'Rezek's Dwarf'|Chamaecyparis obtusa 'Rezek's Dwarf'

description: Bulbous perennials to 50cm tall, producing clusters of up to 10 trumpet-shaped blooms in white or shades of pink on strong, upright stems in autumn, followed by strap-shaped leaves
A bushy, tuberous perennial to around 80cm high, with serrated green leaves. Decorative bright yellow flowers to 13cm across are produced from late summer to early autumn

primary_name: Petunia [Easy Wave Pink Passion] ('Pas882697') (Easy Wave Series)

description: F1 hybrid salad onion (non-bulbing) with upright growth remaining mid to dark green virtually all year round with well-blanched bases, and producing creamy-white flowers in mid-summer

Compact, bushy, rounded, deciduous shrub about 60-90cm tall, with upright stems and toothed, yellow leaves, orange to pinkish-red when young, and orange-red in autumn. Produces bowl-shaped, bright pink flowers in large flattened heads during summer

alternative_names: foxglove 'Dalmatian Crème'|foxglove 'Dalmatian Cream'|Digitalis purpurea 'Dalmatian Cream' (Dalmatian Series)
description: A compact rosette-forming biennial or short-lived perennial, to 50cm high, with toothed, ovate, dark green leaves. Flower spikes bearing creamy flowers with purple-spotted throats are borne in summer; this cultivar typically blooms in its first year

A leek that produces long, thick stems with a mild flavour from autumn onwards. Leeks are herbaceous perennials usually grown as annual vegetables, with upright stems which can be blanched white, and green or blue-green leaves about 30-50cm long; plants may flower by bolting in their first year, or the following year if left overwinter, with stems up to 1.5m high topped by rounded flowerheads 5-9cm across of hundreds of star-like pale pink to white flowers which are visited by bees, in summer.
A seed-raised everbearer, producing small flushes of fruit from late spring to early autumn. The medium-sized , conical berries have some flavour
A compact cultivar suited to growing in containers and produces heavy crops of good-sized, sweet and aromatic fruit over several weeks

primary_name: Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris var. altissima 'Sv1215'

description: A seed-raised everbearer, producing small flushes of fruit from late spring to early autumn. The flowers are a striking, bright red but the dark red fruit are small with little taste
An excellent day neutral, strawberry variety, producing good yields of small, orange-red fruits, with a sweet taste, throughout summer and early autumn
A striking perennial salvia with a neat, bushy structure. Produces masses of deep purple flower spikes on strong, upright stems above aromatic green foliage from July through to September

Vigorous upright shrub rose about 1.5-1.75m tall, with yellow-green glossy, leathery leaves, purple thorns, and bearing clusters of lightly scented, pinkish-red, fully double blooms with a lighter reverse, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn
A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. This Triumph group tulip has dark reddish purple flowers with an orange pink margin, produced in mid-spring. Flowers stand to around 35cm high
A perennial bulb to around 50cm with green foliage and strong stems of large, fragrant, cup-shaped golden yellow flowers appearing in April

Introduced in 1771, this heritage cultivar is still very popular today. It forms a rosette of tender, green, oak-leaf shaped leaves that have a mild sweet flavour. Pick as cut-and-grow-again. Resists bolting. Sow March to July, harvest July to September/October.

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. Decorative form double flowers, produced from mid-summer until the first frost, have white petals, rimmed and tipped with pink, slightly incurved, creating a neat shape 12cm across, with a pink centre

alternative_names: rose of Sharon 'Gandini van Aart'|Hibiscus syriacus [Flower Tower White]|Hibiscus syriacus [White Pillar]
description: A very tall, narrow, pillar-like shrub to 5m, with dark green, lobed foliage and pure white, single to semi-double blooms from mid-summer to mid-autumn

A compact, upright, bushy deciduous shrub with dark green leaves and outward-facing creamy-white flowers with green tips and single, dark violet-purple corollas with pink veining, appearing from summer through until the autumn

A deciduous, tender shrub, compact in growth at no more than 40cm in height. The pale pink and white flowers are less pendulous than many bedding fuchsias, emerging upwards and outwards with blooms from summer through to autumn

A small, deciduous, trailing shrub to about 40cm in height, with dark green foliage and abundant pendent outward facing single to semi-double flowers which have a white corolla and red sepals from summer through to autumn. Very suitable for containers and hanging baskets

A deciduous, upright, bushy shrub with dark green foliage, and abundant pendent but upward facing flowers which have a lavender-blue corolla and rosy-red sepals and stamens from summer through to autumn. Very suitable for containers and hanging baskets

A small and compact, upright, bushy shrub, with dark green foliage, and abundant pendent but upward facing flowers which have a purple corolla and red-pink sepals from summer through to autumn. Very suitable for containers and hanging baskets
A compact, upright, bushy deciduous shrub with dark green leaves, and red-pink flowers with single, purple corollas appearing from summer through until the autumn
Herbaceous perennial grown for its edible properties producing very sweet high quality red taproots and colourful green red-veined leaves.

A mid-late season, very sweet beetroot with mid to dark green leaves veined dark red and with dark red stalks; produces high yields of intense red beets, even in size with very smooth skin. Ideal for picking when young or mature, and for pickling

An excellent variety offered in conjunction with RBG Kew, specially bred for baby beet production. Smooth skinned, well shaped, red fleshed golf ball sized taproots are produced from June to October and are noted as having a particularly sweet flavour
An excellent annual grown as a vegetable for its medium to large, round, edible, deep red taproots that have a fine flavour and firm texture with no inner rings. Perfect for winter storage

A high quality beet variety producing uniform, spherical roots with a deep crimson flesh. It has a full, sweet flavour and is noted for its reliability and vigour. Baby beets can be harvested when golf ball size or left to mature. It shows excellent resistance to fungal diseases

A vigorous cabbage variety that will grow in any free draining soil and stand up until the first hard frost of Autumn. It has an intensely sweet flavour and produces thick, crisp leaves that can be used as an alternative to iceberg lettuce in late Summer and Autumn
A pointed cabbage variety that is quick to mature with a slightly larger head and good standing ability, which can be harvested up to October

An annual vegetable, producing a narrow based pointed cabbage which can be harvested from early Summer to Autumn. An excellent variety for small spaces, growing to 40cm tall, with a remarkably sweet flavour. Shows bolting resistance.

alternative_names: cabbage 'Primo II'|cabbage 'Early Primo Improved'|Brassica oleracea (Capitata Group) 'Early Primo Improved'

description: An unusual annual grown as a vegetable for its fantastic, edible, white skinned taproot that is tender and sweet tasting. An heirloom variety perfect for grating raw into summer salads

alternative_names: beetroot 'Kahira'|beetroot 'Egyptian Turnip Rooted'|Beta vulgaris 'Egyptian Flat'|Beta vulgaris 'Egyptian Turnip Rooted'
description: A flat rooted heritage variety producing smooth skinned taproots with tender, deep red flesh with an excellent flavour. Perfect for early and successional sowings for a prolonged cropping period

A compact, leafy biennial grown as an annual vegetable. This F1 hybrid is a red summer cabbage, producing small, dense, rounded heads with sweet flavour and little core. Can be harvested in July or August depending on sowing time

A Summer variety cabbage producing very uniform and compact hearts with a strong base and good standing ability. It has dark green outer leaves and a tight, light green pointed heart that can be harvested between June and September

A reliable and uniform hybrid variety that can be harvested for its hearts in Spring and Autumn and for greens in Spring, Summer and Autumn. It has attractive, dark green outer leaves with a bright green inner pointed head. The inner leaves are tender and crunchy with an excellent, sweet flavour
Spreading perennial to 12cm tall, with lance-shaped, fleshy, dark green leaves, red beneath and felted with brownish hairs, and in summer produces pinkish-purple flowers in clusters

alternative_names: spider plant|St Bernard's lily|Chlorophytum elatum 'Variegatum'|Chlorophytum capense var. variegatum
description: A clump-forming evergreen perennial with lance or strap shaped leaves, the leaves are variegated with a thick central strip of creamy white and dark green margins. Racemes of tiny white flowers are held on stem that can be up to 60cm long, with no plantlets on the flower stems, and this is a distinguishing feature of this species

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm, with mid-green foliage. Large flowers, 20cm across, produced from mid-summer to the first frost, have long, pointed, yellow petals each finely outlined in red, with a red base, creating a sunburst effect

Tuberous-rooted, clump-forming perennial to about 80cm tall, with dark green leaves. Prolific, fully double flowers, produced from midsummer until the first frosts, are bi-coloured red, heavily tipped white, with slightly incurved petals, to 15cm across

A large, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Magenta-red decorative form flowers, with paler reddish-pink and white streaks, appear from summer until the first frosts

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green leaves. Single, white anemone-shaped flowers with prominent creamy-yellow centres appear from July through until the first frosts of autumn
