description: A fast-growing large shrub or small tree reaching a height and width of between 3 and 4 metres with arching branches. Foliage emerges reddish brown, changing to brownish green. Red-brown catkins appear in the spring and summer followed by brown fruits in the autumn
A slowly spreading bamboo with slender upright canes, and bold dark green leaves streaked creamy-white, to 25cm in length

A deciduous perennial bearing nodding, primrose-yellow, poppy-like flowers of 2-3cm (1-1.5in) in mid-to late summer. Slender, branched stems scramble upwards to a height of 1m (3ft) and have lobed, softly hairy, pale green leaves.

Small, evergreen, upright growing epiphytic orchid. Broadly oval, green or dark green leaves, 10 - 15cm long, emerge from the centre of the plant. New flowering stems form at the base of older leaves. Long lasting flowers are carried on semi-pendulous branched racemes up to 30 cm long, with each branch carrying up to 15 flowers borne in succession. Flowers are bilaterally symmetrical, measuring 3 - 4cm across, violet, faintly striped, vith a plain darker violet lip. A uniquely coloured compact hybrid.

Small sized, evergreen, upright growing epiphytic orchid. Broadly oval, green or dark green leaves up to 15cm long emerge from the centre of the plant and are main storage of water and nutrients. New flowering stems appear from the base of older leaves. Numerous long lasting flowers are carried on semi-pendulous branched racemes, up to 30cm tall. Each flowering stem carries up to 15 flowers, opening in succession. Flowers are bilaterally symmetrical, white with blush of pink and mauve on the reverse. Lip is yellow and spotted in the centre. Compact and floriferous.

Small to medium sized, evergreen, upright growing epiphytic orchid. Broadly oval, silvery mottled leaves emerge from the centre of the plant and are main storage of water and nutrients. New flowering stems emerge from the base of older leaves. Up to 20 fragrant, long- lasting flowers are carried on branched racemes up to 40 cm tall. Dark pink flowers, measuring 4 - 6 cm across are bilaterally symmetrical with pink lip and yellow centre, and distinct while column.
A compact and upright orchid, growing to 30cm tall with numerous, long-lasting yellow flowers, an orange coloured lip and speckled with maroon freckles

A low growing, clump-forming, evergreen perennial with heart shaped to ovate, spiny-toothed, green leaves, flushed bronze and red when young. In spring small yellow flowers are produced on slender upright stems held above the foliage.

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial, to around 45cm high, with narrowly heart-shaped, spiny green leaves, flushed reddish-bronze when young. Small, spidery, white and yellow flowers are held on delicate stems above the leaves from April to May

A fast-growing, large and long-lived evergreen tree with a widely arching, weeping growing habit. It has thick, fibrous, soft and spongey reddish-brown bark and pendulous branches with dark green linear leaves. Small hanging brown cones are produced after inconspicuous flowers. Ideally grown as a specimen in a large park or garden.

A compact and bushy, upright herbaceous perennial with aromatic, dark green, oval to lance-shaped leaves and long whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped lilac-blue flowers which are very attractive to pollinators all through summer to autumn
A tender, compact, mound-forming perennial to 45cm tall, often offered for sale as a winter-flowering pot plant. It is prized for its display of daisy-like, dark pink flowers around a burgundy eye
A deciduous, bulbous, tall herbaceous perennial to around 120cm, with strap-like dark green leaves and large upward-facing, fragrant pink and yellow speckled flowers appearing in summer

A bulbous perennial producing a strong, upright stem clothed in shiny, dark green, lance-shaped leaves and topped in mid to late summer with a cluster of large, upward-facing, soft pink, bowl-shaped flowers with orange anthers
A cormous perennialto 70cm, with sword-shaped leaves. Spikes of rose-pink flowers with cream throats are produced in early summer
A small, compact tuberous-rooted perennial, a miniature decorative form, with double, rich cerise-pink flowers

A compact, clump-forming perennial to 20cm high with nearly rounded, blue-green, wavy and twisted leaves with broad, creamy-yellow margins to 5cm long. Pale purple flowers are borne on short stems in summer

A medium-sized, clump-forming perennial to about 40cm high. The narrow, pointed, mid-green leaves have a broad white border and are deeply waved and twisted. Spikes of funnel-shaped, lavender flowers are produced in late summer
A bushy perennial with dark green, lobed foliage and rose-pink, double flowers from late summer until late autumn
A compact perennial forming a mound of slightly cupped, creamy-white leaves with a green margin to 20cm across. Lavender flowers are borne on upright stems to 30cm tall in summer
A compact, bushy perennial forming a mound oflobed foliage covered in pink double blooms fading to orange-yellow at their centres

A scrambling annual to 30cm with light green, circular leaves supported on central stems. In summer and early autumn flowers open primrose yellow with distinct dark red markings, later becoming suffused with shades of red and pink
An easy-to-grow, upright hardy annual to 30cm in height, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Rich blue flowers with a blue-purple centre appear on thin stems from June to August
A compact chrysanthemum cultivar to 60cm tall and wide producing a dome-shaped mound of dark green foliage covered from early autumn until the first frosts with an abundance of orange flowers
A large, bushy, upright shrub to about 2m unpruned, with heavily veined leaves, and clusters of slightly bluish pink, fragrant, semi-double flowers produced in flushes in summer and autumn
A bushy, herbaceous perennial with dark green leaves to around 70cm in height. Single, dense, vibrant red flowers appear from summer until the first frosts
A bulbous perennial to around 1.2m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Fragrant, upward-facing pale yellow cream flowers with reflexed petals appear in the summer

A small tuberous perennial with mid-green leaves cut deeply into fine lobes. Has striking single violet-blue flowers with black centres from March to April after which it will die back until late autumn.
A small tuberous perennial with mid-green leaves cut deeply into fine lobes. Has striking single white flowers with green centres from March to April after which it will die back until late autumn

A perennial bulb with light green, lance-shaped leaves and double flowers on 40cm tall stems in mid- to late spring. The petals have deeply fringed edges and are generally gold, flushed and streaked with red, but sometimes all dark red, or with green markings

An evergreen, frost-tender subshrub, often grown as an annual, forming a compact mound of finely-divided, deep green foliage to around 45cm tall. A mass of large, single flowers, bright yellow with a brown centre, are borne above the foliage from late spring until the first frosts.

A low-growing, evergreen perennial forming a clump of grass-like leaves. In late spring and early summer it produces spherical, dark pink flowerheads on stiff stems to 25cm tall. A good plant for pollinating insects

A low-growing, clump-forming evergreen perennial with linear, grass-like leaves. In late spring and early summer it produces spherical, white flowerheads on stiff stems to 25cm tall. A good plant for pollinating insects

A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 50cm high, with glossy, divided dark green leaves with toothed margins. This series of cultivars flower slightly earlier than many other Astilbes, producing numerous dense plumes of pinkish-orange flowers in early to mid summer

A compact shrub or small tree to about 1-1.5m tall, with spiny branches and oval, glossy, dark green leaves. From spring to summer it bears fragrant white flowers; these are followed by small, broadly ovoid, yellow fruits. Lemons are best grown in a cool or temperate greenhouse or conservatory and moved outside during the summer months

A compact, deciduous climber to 1.5m in height with dark to mid-green leaves. Mid-blue flowers are single or semi-double with overlapping sepals and creamy-yellow anthers, produced from the leaf bud axils and the end of the stems from late spring or early summer to late summer and autumn

A small, vigorous, vase-shaped tree to around 7m in height. Dark green elliptic pointed leaves turn shades of red in autumn. Remarkable as a very dark pink form. The petal-like elongated pointed bracts, deep pink to fuchshia, appear in profusion for many weeks from May to June. Spherical red strawberry-like fruit appear in the autumn.
An upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with mid-green foliage. In summer erect flower stems appear bearing umbels of reddish-pink flowers

A tropical perennial, with fleshy rhizomes, an upright habit and thin, lance-shaped green leaves with dark red midribs and pointed tips. Tiny, tubular flowers are encased in a cupped rosette of bracts at the end of flowering stems in summer; the upper bracts are bright pink with reddish purple tips

A slowly spreading, mound or mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, mid-green to grey-green leaves. Pink-purple, four-petalled flowers with tiny raspberry-pink flecks at the centre, are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

A white-flowered form of this tender evergreen or semi-evergreen azalea. This species grows up to 2m high, with a branching habit and broadly ovate leaves. Flowers are funnel-shaped, and produced in pairs or small clusters at the tips of the stems in late spring

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1m, with mid-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frost, purple buds open to ice-white flowers, 12cm across, retaining a purple centre and purple tips to the petals
A highly attractive annual marigold variety with erect, dark green foliage and masses of bright, yellow flowers from June to October

A large, half-hardy evergreen shrub with a spreading, open habit and glossy, ovate green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces single, strongly fragrant, white or pale pink flowers to 7cm across in mid spring

A small and compact perennial with green, lance-shaped foliage and numerous, outward facing, pale lilac-blue star-shaped flowers providing a long flowering display in summer. Easy to grow in containers, dislikes wet winters.

A low-growing perennial that forms a neat, evergreen mat of small, round, attractive dark green, toothed leaves. Numerous, outward facing blue or white bell-shaped, single flowers are borne on short stalks, sitting just above its foliage, providing a long flowering display in summer

A robust clump-forming perennial with rounded, grey-green basal leaves and upright, branched stems bear deeply-lobed, pale green spiny leaves and abundant small silvery-white flowerheads in clusters, above narrow, spiny silvery-green bracts 2.5cm long, in mid to late summer

A compact, evergreen, frost-tender succulent shrub on which the stem's growing point has mutated into a line or crest, so that the plant eventually forms a dome to 90cm (3ft) high and 60cm (2ft) wide of ridged, undulating, reddish-green growth that resembles the appearance of brain coral. The small flowers are rarely produced, but can appear in spring and are a pinkish, green-yellow. It is usually grafted onto the stem of another euphorbia species. Its slow growth, temperature requirements and ornamental value make it a useful subject for a sunny window indoors

A clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with a spreading habit and deeply lobed and toothed green leaves. Rich lilac pink flowers, with purple veins and white centres with contrasting near-black anthers, are produced over a long period from early summer into autumn

primary_name: Geranium incanum subsp. magniflorum [La Veta Lace] ('P0135')
Ipomoea batatas [Bright Ideas Rusty Red] ('Floipobirr') (Bright Ideas Series)

description: A semi-evergreen rosette-forming perennial with green leaves and clusters of bi-coloured pale lavender-purple and white flowers with yellow centres, appearing in the spring
A neat and compact rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green wrinkled foliage and large, bicoloured flowers in a range of purples, pinks, yellows and reds from February to May
An herbaceous perennial reaching approximately 60cm in height when in flower with green, linear grass-like leaves and spikes of tubular, golden yellow flowers that emerge in summer and autumn.

A compact, rosette-forming semi-evergreen perennial with dark green textured foliage. Clusters of large single flowers are edged with white which borders the beautiful blue center which is highlighted with a yellow eye. A versatile bedding plant that flowers from January to April
A seed-strain of shrub up to 33cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant blue-purple flowers in late summer
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage and fragrant red flowers, appearing from February to May
A shrub up to 36cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant white flowers in summer

primary_name: Lavandula stoechas [Javelin Forte Deep Purple] ('Labz0004') (Javelin Forte Series)
alternative_names: French lavender [Javelin Forte Deep Purple]|Lavandula stoechas 'Labz0004'
description: A shrub up to 50cm high, with evergreen, aromatic, linear, grey-green leaves, and spikes of fragrant, deep purple flowers topped by pale pinkish purple bracts from late spring to summer
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green foliage and bright, fragrant, fully double golden yellow flowers, appearing from February to May

A compact, clump-forming, evergreen perennial with dark green textured foliage. Large, double, fragrant, bi-coloured lilac-purple and white flowers with a yellow eye appear from February through to May

primary_name: Primula obconica 'Touch Me Pink Galaxy' (Touch Me Series)
Primula obconica 'Touch Me Violet' (Touch Me Series)

description: A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with dark green veined leaves. Clusters of violet-purple flowers with a central splash of burgundy around a yellow eye appear in the spring
A neat, clump-forming perennial producing tight clusters of mildly fragrant yellow flowers with orange centres on stout stems.
A low-growing evergreen perennial, forming dense mats of slender stems with fine, linear mid-green leaves. Tiny white flowers are held up on stems to 4cm high in late spring and early summer
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with aromatic green foliage and deep purple lipped flowers held on dark purple to black calyces from summer through to autumn.

A compact perennial forming a low mound of small, deeply-cut, bright green, moss-like leaves topped in late spring and early summer by short stems bearing upward-facing, cup-shaped white and pinkish-red flowers

A medium-sized, epiphytic, deciduous orchid with terete, cane-like, fleshy, green or brown stems, 30-40cm long. Each stem is covered with thin, leaf-bearing sheaths. Leaves are narrow, 8-11cm long and 1cm wide, bright green, later yellow before falling off in the autumn. Short, pendant flowering stems emerge from the upper nodes of mature canes and bear two to five flowers. The flowers are thin-textured, bright yellow, approximately 4cm large.

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen orchid with dark green, thick glossy leaves. Three to five lance-shaped leaves are alternately arranged near the top of a long, upright, cane-like pseudobulb. Flowering stems emerge from the tip of mature stems and carry 15-20 flowers. Star-shaped flowers approximately 3cm large are held upright above the foliage. Petals and sepals are yellow, with lower sepals usually curved downwards. Constrasting lip is pink-patterned. Petals and sepal also carry the pink, spotted pattern, usually more prominent on the edges of sepals.
An upright perennial bulb to around 50cm with broadly lance-shaped dark green foliage. Creamy-white fringed flowers with purple-pink streaks in the centre appear from April to May

primary_name: Petunia × atkinsiana [Pegasus Queen of Hearts] (Pegasus Series)
Petunia × atkinsiana [Pegasus Patio Back to Black] (Pegasus Series)
description: A tender, trailing perennial, mostly grown as an annual for summer container or bedding displays. It has ovate, sticky and hairy, green to grey-green leaves and, from late spring into autumn, velvety, dark purple-black trumpet-shaped flowers

An evergreen succulent to around 30cm in height, with rosettes of dark green, fleshy, bumpy-textured tapered leaves with toothed edges, which turn dark reddish-bronze in summer when the sunlight becomes stronger. Tube-shaped pinkish-red flowers appear on wiry stems once or twice a year
A tender, upright, clump-forming perennial with thick dark green to dark maroon foliage with a pink border and middle vein. Small pink and white flowers sometimes appear in summer

Francis is a deciduous orchid to 50cm tall with oval, prominently veined leaves. Flowers borne on erect stems in late spring have an ivory white pouch with dark pink to purple markings and long, twisted, purple-striped tepals
A bushy, rounded perennial to approximately 60cm tall and wide. Its aromatic, dark green foliage is covered with large, pink-purple blooms from late summer into autumn

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to around 50cm tall forming a mound of nearly round, puckered, blue-green leaves spreading to 1.2m across; each leaf can reach up to 27cm long and 24cm wide. White flowers are borne on sturdy stems in early summer
A bulbous perennial with leafy stems to 1.5m. Very large, scented, bowl-shaped, deep red flowers are produced in mid- to late summer

A bulbous herbaceous perennial with dark green glossy leaves and double white fragrant flowers which appear from mid to late summer. Double oriental lillies such as this have extra petals rather than anthers so are pollen-free

A dwarf, deciduous bulbous perennial with strap-like dark green leaves and fragrant, dark red flowers with white margins. Flowers are bowl-shaped and upward facing, appearing in July and August. Ideal for pots and containers

A bushy upright shrub rose to about 1m tall with dark green foliage tinged red in spring. Clusters of fragrant, fully double, pale pink, neat, blooms with an apricot to yellow hue in the centre of the flower, open almost flat and fade to cream with age, borne from early summer into autumn

An upright, bushy, repeat-flowering rose to 1.3m tall with glossy foliage and thorny stems. Clusters of fragrant, double, deeplycupped, mid to pale pink blooms with reddish-pink petal edges are borne from summer into autumn

A rounded, repeat-flowering shrub rose to 1.2m tall and wide with dark green, divided foliage. Open sprays of single, lightly scented, pale yellow flowers that fade to cream with age, repeat-flower from summer into autumn
A bushy, herbaceous perennial with lance shaped, mid-green leaves. From early summer to mid-autumn produces flowers in light orange, shading to yellow,on gently curving stems to 70cm high
A low-growing, evergreen perennial, to about 15cm tall, producing fragrant, cream flowers edged with purple from spring to autumn

A cordon tomato grown as an annual, either in an unheated greenhouse or outdoors. The small, conical, red-green fruits with gold streaks are a little larger than cherry tomatoes and are produced in abundance throughout the summer

A naturally compact, self-fertile cherry cultivar forming a bushy shrub or a small tree about 2m tall. The white spring blossom is followed by red fruit which is sour initially, eventually becoming sweet when fully ripe and dark red in colour. Cropping season: July to August
A compact, bulbous perennial with dark green leafy stems to 50cm, bearing large, upward-facing red and orange flowers in summer.
An upright, bulbous perennial with leafy stems to about 60cm bearing upward-facing, rich cream flowers, shading to yellow in the centre of the gently recurved petals speckled with fine, dark red dots

A bulbous herbaceous perennial with dark green glossy leaves and large, double white fragrant flowers which appear from July to August. Double oriental lillies such as this have extra petals rather than anthers so are pollen-free
A trumpet daffodil to 60cm high, with straplike, glaucous green leaves. Flowers have white outer petals and a broad, golden yellow corona with a widely flared rim

A bulbous perennial producing strong, upright stems to a height of 1.2m clothed in shiny, dark green, lance-shaped leaves and topped in early summer with clusters of large, upward-facing, trumpet-shaped scented white flowers with yellow bars on the petals and edged in pale purple

primary_name: Helianthus annuus [Sunbelievable Brown Eyed Girl] ('Sunbeliv01') (Sunbelievable Series)
description: A compact, branching, annual to 60cm tall with dark green, oval leaves. Golden-yellow flowerheads 8-10cm across with a deep reddish-brown ring surrounding the dark central eye are borne in profusion over a long season; this sterile cultivar does not produce seed

A bulbous perennial producing a strong, upright stem clothed in shiny, dark green, lance-shaped leaves and topped in early summer with a cluster of large, outward-facing, creamy-white, bowl-shaped flowers with gently recurved petals and tan anthers
A compact, bulbous perennial with dark green leafy stems to 120cm, bearing large, upward-facing golden yellow flowers in summer.

A compact, evergreen shrub to about 1.2m, with grey stems and small, leathery, yellow leaves. In late spring produces small, yellow, fragrant, star-shaped flowers, followed by reddish berries in autumn

A vigorous, trailing, and sometimes mounding, floriferous tender perennial usually grown as seasonal bedding or a patio container plant. It has oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid-green leaves and produces abundant, Gramophone-trumpet-shaped, purple flowers with a white halo around the outer edge of the flowers. Flowers from late spring to autumn.

A highly attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing long lasting, bright magenta-pink double blooms with a prominent central pompom surrounded by narrow, recurved petals. Deadhead to enjoy extended flowering. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A bright, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, magenta-pink blooms with drooping ray petals surrounding a prominent central orange-red cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A short, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing a crescendo of colour in Summer with salmon pink blooms that mature to pink with short, broad, flat petals surrounding a prominent brown-orange central cone. Perfect for container growing and attracting pollinators

A highly attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing single, pure red blooms with a dark central cone surrounded by perfect, narrow ray petals. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

An attractive, upright, single flowering, perennial coneflower variety with canary yellow petals, semi-quilled and toothed, surrounding a central orange cone. Excellent for container growing and attracting pollinators

Robust, bushy shrub rose about 1.5m tall, with healthy mid-green foliage, and bearing clusters of dark red buds that open to fully double, bright red blooms with ruffled edges, repeat-flowering through summer into autumn. Can be grown as a small climber
A vigorous climbing rose to around 3m tall with glossy, divided foliage. Clusters of fragrant, double pink flowers with apricot shading are borne in summer and autumn
A compact cultivar with well-branched stems to around 40cm tall bearing double flowers with drooping, creamy-white ray florets topped with large, rounded, pompon-like yellow-green cones

A highly attractive and popular, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing masses of vivid orange blooms with a prominent central dark brown cone surrounded by overlapping, flattened rays. This variety has a higher crown count, improved first year blooming and extended flowering period. It is excellent for container growing, attracting pollinators and as a cut flower

A bushy, clump-forming, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with leathery dark green foliage. White flowers, flushed with green or cream, become blushed with pink as they mature, appear from midwinter into spring
A winter or early spring bulbous perennial to 60cm tall, producing at least two stout stems, each bearing 3-4 large, crimson, funnel-shaped flowers to 25cm across

primary_name: Lobelia erinus [Techno Upright Sky Blue Improved] ('Lobz0013') (Techno Series)
Malus domestica from The Square, Wisley

description: A frost-tender, woody-based perennial to 75cm tall with small, aromatic, mid green leaves. Tubular, soft-pink flowers with darker pink streaks are borne in open racemes on dark stems over a long period- usually from early summer to late autumn
A rhizomatous perennial to 80cm with fans of sword-shaped, greyish-green foliage. The flowers, produced in late spring, have golden-yellow, ruffled petals with coppery edges and orange beards
A rhizomatous perennial to 80cm with fans of sword-shaped, greyish-green foliage. The flowers, produced in late spring, have dark brownish or purplish red, ruffled petals, with brown beards

alternative_names: blue star creeper [Fizz 'n' Pop Glowing Purple]|Isotoma axillaris 'Tmlu 1301'
description: A compact, tender, evergreen perennial often grown as an annual to 30cm tall and wide. Relatively large purple, star-shaped flowers to 3.8cm across with small yellow eyes are borne from late spring until the first frosts above the coarsely-lobed foliage

A compact, deciduous shrub with deeply-cut, five- or seven-lobed leaves that emerge yellow in spring with a reddish-pink edge maturing to light green with a pale pink edge to mid-green with a white edge as summer progresses.The foliageturns orange-red in late summer before finally turning red-violet in autumn

A compact annual to 45cm tall with mid- to dark green, lance-shaped leaves; small white flowers in summer are followed by green fruits maturing to bright yellow, mild and sweet-tasting peppers up to 7cm long

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 66cm in height. It forms clumps of arching strap-shaped green leaves and fragrant, creamy-pink flowers with a cream throat to 15cm across in summer

An evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves and sturdy stems of fragrant , scarlet-red flowers with a pale yellow stripe down each centre of the petals and large, yellow-green eye

A semi-evergreen, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with strap-shaped, arching mid-green leaves. Fragrant flowers are purple to dark pink, paler towards the eye, with a yellow green throat and slightly ruffled petals
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 35cm tall with grey-green foliage and tiny, bright yellow flowers clustered to form flattened flowerheads on branching stems from summer into autumn

alternative_names: African lily 'Royal Velvet'|Agapanthus praecox subsp. orientalis 'Royal Velvet'
description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial to about 75cm with relatively narrow, dark grey-green leaves with purple staining at the base of the leaves and flower stems. Rounded flowerheads of funnel-shaped, deep purple flowers with a darker central stripe to each petal, are produced in late summer and early autumn

Clump-forming perennials in a range of heights from about 30-75cm with a neat compact growth habit and robust cold resistance. Dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of funnel-shaped flowers in colour shades of pink, orange and white, profusely flowering from early summer to autumn

A bushy and clump-forming perennial with elongated, lance-shaped green leaves and abundant daisy-like, large, semi-double, golden-yellow flowers with toothed petals held on stalks just above its foliage. An early flowering cultivar providing blooms for a long period of time from spring to late summer

A robust clump-forming perennial with rounded, dark green basal leaves and upright, branched stems bear deeply-lobed, spiny leaves and small, thistle-like silvery-green flowerheads maturing to pale steel blue, above narrow, spiny pale blue-green bracts 2.5cm long, in mid to late summer

A robust clump-forming perennial with rounded, grey-green basal leaves and upright, branched stems bear deeply-lobed, pale green spiny leaves and abundant small white flowerheads in clusters, above narrow, spiny silvery-green bracts 2.5cm long, in mid and late summer

A deciduous shrub, up to around 5m high, with upright to arching, slender stems and narrow, slightly blue-green leaves with paler undersides, that are flushed orange-red when young. Catkins are produced before the leaves in spring; male catkins are purplish, turning yellow as the pollen develops

A leafy biennial, butterhead variety of lettuce, usually grown as an annual, with neat, bushy, fresh green heads and an excellent flavour. A great variety for exhibiting, with good resistance to bolting and some resistance to mildew. Sow from February to July and harvest within just 10 to 12 weeks

A climbing rose to 2.5m tall with dark green divided foliage and clusters of scented, sometimes single but mostly semi-double blooms up to 10cm across comprising pale pink to white petals surrounding a deep pinkish-red eye

A compact floribunda rose to around 60cm tall with glossy, leaves that open deep red before maturing to dark green. Clusters of fragrant, semi-double pink flowers to 4cm wide are borne from summer into autumn

A bushy, upright rose about 1.1m tall, with glossy dark green leaves, and bearing clusters of very fragrant, well-formed, fully double, pale candy pink blooms to 11cm across, repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

A clump-forming, rhizomatous herbaceous perennial with sword-shaped grey-green leaves and large, white flowers with feathered edges, pale yellow veining, wide yellow beards and a pale blue-green signal

A deciduous shrub to 2.5m high, with a slender habit and narrowly ovate, double toothed green leaves that turn red and purple in autumn. In late spring, small, flat clusters of tiny white flowers are produced, followed in autumn by bright red berries

A large, coniferous tree, to 20m tall in its native Florida, but very slow-growing in cooler climates. Rarely seen in cultivation, it has sharp-pointed, needle-like leaves, the new growth being creamy-white

A clump-forming, rhizomatous, hardy evergreen perennial with long, wide, broadly lance-shaped glossy mid-green leaves with pale yellow spots. Rarely, white, star-shaped flowers appear at the base of the plant in spring to summer. Although most often grown as a houseplant, it is also a useful garden plant in mild areas, and is tolerant of shade and drier conditions

primary_name: Cardiocrinum giganteum var. yunnanense 'Big and Pink'

description: A prostrate evergreen shrub with mid-green leathery oval leaves, small cream flowers April to May and unique spiky orange fruit appearing in September. Can be used as ground cover or to train up a wall

Small, deciduous tree to about 2m in height, which is grafted onto a straight trunk giving it an umbrella-shaped weeping habit. Young leaves in spring open dark purple, fading to red-purple and then reddish-green for the rest of the summer, becoming dark yellow before falling in autumn

alternative_names: Himalayan red bells Ken's Giant Red

description: An upright medium-sized deciduous shrub becoming spreading with age, with mid-green, heart-shaped leaves and compact bunches of fragrant, double white flowers flushed pink from May until June
Bushy upright rose to about 1m tall, with healthy green foliage and bearing very fragrant, fully double, cream blooms flushed pale apricot, repeat-flowering through summer and autumn

Vigorous, bushy rose to 90cm tall, with healthy, glossy, dark green foliage and richly fragrant, deep pink, fully double, long-lasting blooms that repeat-flower from early summer to autumn. Especially useful as a cut flower

A hybrid tea shrub grown for long-lasting, richly fragrant, professional cut-flowers. Rounded buds open to large (11cm) pinkish purple blooms borne from early summer over an extended period to the first frosts. Petals can also be used for potpourri. Bred for health, fragrance and a long vase life.

A large, evergreen shrub with pinnate leaves up to 60cm long, divided into close-set pairs of broad, spiny green leaflets with silvery white undersides. Small, yellow flowers are appear in upright clusters in late winter

A large, evergreen shrub, with long, pinnate leaves divided into pairs of broad, spiny green leaflets with silvery white undersides. Small yellow flowers are borne in loose, spreading clusters in late winter

A large, evergreen shrub, with long, pinnate leaves divided into pairs of close-set, broad, spiny green leaflets with silvery white undersides. Leaves tint reddish-bronze in colder temperatures, and small yellow flowers appear in upright to ascending clusters in late winter

Rare shrub rose, native to China, about 1-1.5m tall, with bristly stems and dark leathery leaves, composed of slender leaflets. Single white flowers to 2.5cm across, with prominent pinkish-golden stamens are borne in midsummer and followed by small red fruits (hips) to 1cm across, in autumn

An evergreen shrub or small tree eventually reaching up to 8m tall with papery to thinly leathery, oblong to elliptic leaves up to 10cm long that have glossy, dark green upper surfaces and paler green undersides. In summer, strongly scented white to pale yellow flowers are usually borne singly in leaf axils and are followed by ovoid fruits to around 1cm long that mature to a purple-red colour

A broadly columnar, deciduous tree to about 20m tall, with a spreading or rounded crown, and bright lemon-yellow, heart-shaped leaves to 8cm in length, retaining the colour even in strong sun, and then turning a bright buttery-yellow in autumn. Small, fragrant pale creamy-yellow flowers are borne in spreading clusters of up to 10 flowers in midsummer

A large, elegant, deciduous shrub about 5m tall, with broadly eliptic, pointed dark green leaves, and white buds open to small, bell-shaped, fragrant white or pale rose flowers deepening to carmine and flowering in early summer

A dwarf, shrubby, spreading conifer to 90cm tall, with upright to arching shoots bearing flattened, ferny sprays of tiny, scale-like leaves. The foliage is blue-green with a silvery underside. Suitable for a rock garden or as ground cover

A compact, upright, half-hardy perennial to 30m in height with sparsely toothed, spoon-shaped, glossy, mid green leaves and daisy-like flowers with pale coral red outer petals with a faint purple flush at the base forming a luminous halo and with a contrasting dark purple centre, from summer into autumn

A herbaceous perennial with rosettes 0.5-1m high of evergreen, succulent, lance-shaped leaves, variegated yellow and grey-green; mature plants may produce bright pink stems up to 1.5m high of lime-green flowers with mauve-pink bracts, in midsummer

A semi-evergreen shrub to around 1m (3.2ft). Growth is upright, bushy with dark-green leaves that are strongly flushed with dark purple. In summer it produces bright yellow flowers with prominent stamens. These are followed in autumn by clusters of oval, rich mahogany-purple berries.

A trailing perennial to 15cm tall, with leaves composed of 3-5 pink leaflets with brown centres that become green during summer, and red veins. In summer, spherical, white or pink-tinged flowerheads are produced on stalks above the foliage; these are a good nectar source for bees

A small, evergreen tree to a height of 5-7m with large, long, narrow dark green leaves. Produces clusters of small, white, late spring female flowers followed by sparse orange-red berries in autumn, if pollinated by a male plant

A densely tufted, clump-forming grass with arching, flat green leaves which become bronzed in autumn, and strong, erect stems up to 1.8m high, each with several racemes about 10cm long of brown-red spikelets in late summer which become redder in autumn
A deciduous shrub or small tree with oval-shaped, pale green leaves that are downy when young and often wither early at the tips. Silky, silvery yellow catkins appear before the leaves in spring
A herbaceous perennial 40-50cm high with a compact habit, pinnate green leaves which turn bright orange-yellow in autumn, and creamy white flowers from early summer to midsummer
A herbaceous perennial 50cm high with finely divided green leaves, and racemes of flowers with deep violet-blue outer petals and white inner petals, in early summer
A clump-forming perennial to around 50cm tall with aromatic, toothed leaves and in summer, whorled clusters ofdeep pinkish-red flowers

A subshrub up to 1m high with evergreen, aromatic, ovate, mid-green leaves, and whorled spikes of flowers which are white nearer the base and with varying amounts of purple nearer the tips, or occasionally all purple or all white, from early summer to autumn; the leaves may be used as a culinary herb

A fast-growing, neat, compact, mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing small, fleshy, rich green rosettes flushed a vibrant cherry red, especially strong in colour in spring and early summer. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes the glossy, spoon-shaped leaves, edged with fine white hairs, are a fiery, rich, deep red. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes, the long, spoon-shaped, pointed, green leaves with red tips, in spring, change to honey-gold in summer and become deep red in winter and early spring. Tall spikes of starry creamy flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing large, fleshy rosettes, the narrow, spoon-shaped pale pinkish-purple leaves take on a darker tone in winter. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A low-growing, succulent perennial forming a rosette of fleshy green leaves, each with a pointed red tip. In summer it produces a 15cm tall flowerspike bearing starry pink flowers. The rosette dies after flowering but this variety produces numerous offsets
A shrubby, herbaceous perennial up to around 1m tall that produces velvety deep pinkish-red flowers from late spring into autumn
An evergreen, dwarf shrub with an upright habit and stems to 15cm tall. The variegated, aromatic leaves are green with a white margin and small, pink flowers are borne in summer

A clump-forming, deciduous, tuberous perennial with dark green leaves. Large, open orange and apricot flowers, darker orange on the reverse, appear from June until the first frosts. Good for a mixed flower border or for exhibitions

primary_name: Echinacea [Prairie Blaze Golden Yellow] (Prairie Blaze Series)
description: A compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing true golden-yellow blooms from July to October. Flowers are held on very strongly branched and uniform stems and have slightly recurved and quilled ray petals surrounding a prominent central golden-orange cone. Excellent for cut flowers and attracting pollinators
A small, compact, evergreen shrub to about 40cm with upright growth. The glossy, oval leaves are grey-green with a variable creamy-white margin

An evergreen shrub with large, rounded, deeply lobed, matt-green leaves. The "fingers" of this cultivar are much finer. In early winter produces large, terminal inflorescences composed of ball-shaped clusters of creamy white flowers, followed by black berries in spring

An evergreen, variegated, mat-forming perennial to 15cm tall. The small leaves on new shoots emerge deep pink, before maturing to green with a cream margin. Dense, upright spikes of deep blue-purple flowers are borne in spring, with a second flush appearing in summer

alternative_names: dawn redwood 'Snow Flurry'|Metasequoia glyptostroboides 'Pat's Best White'|Metasequoia glyptostroboides 'Pat McCracken's White'|Metasequoia glyptostroboides 'McCracken's White'

description: A deciduous climber, to around 3m high, with divided, dark green leaves. Small, upward-facing flowers to 10cm across, with broad, overlapping petals in shades of violet, pink and purple, are produced from early to late summer. Early blooms are often semi-double

A deciduous climber to 3m tall bearing dark violet-purple flowers with lighter mottling, 6-8cm in diameter from early summer to early autumn. Flowers produced later in the season are a brighter shade with a darker central stripe

A fast-growing, very large and long-lived evergreen tree. It has thick, fibrous, soft and spongey reddish-brown bark and slightly drooping branches with rich blue linear leaves. Small, hanging brown cones are produced after inconspicuous flowers. Ideally grown as a specimen in a large park or garden.

A vigorous, evergreen perennial to 15cm tall, with wiry stems and linear to lance-shaped leaves to 3cm long. In late spring and early summer it produces a profusion of pale yellow flowers to 2cm across
An herbaceous perennial forming mounds of mid-green leaves. Flowers are white, surrounded by a ruff of white lance-shaped bracts which are tipped with green

A slowly spreading, mound or mat-forming evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, mid-green to grey-green leaves. Pale lavender-purple, four-petalled flowers, that fade to almost white towards their centres, are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer

A slowly spreading, mat or mound-forming, low-growing, evergreen perennial covered in small, ovate, sometimes toothed, hairy, mid-green to grey-green leaves. Deep pink-purple, four-petalled flowers on short stems appear in spring and early summer

A low-growing perennial that forms neat, compact, uniform mounds of small, green, toothed lance-shaped foliage. Numerous, outward facing, blue, bell-shaped single flowers are borne on short stalks sitting just above its foliage providing a long flowering display in summer

A low-growing perennial that forms neat, compact, uniform mounds of small, green, toothed lance-shaped foliage. Masses of outward facing, white, bell-shaped single flowers appear on short stalks, sitting just above its foliage, providing a long flowering display in summer. An easy to grow plant but dislikes wet winters
A short, tuberous-rooted perennial, to about 50cm, with dark stems and green foliage. Fully double vibrant orange flowers are produced from mid-summer to the first frosts

A bushy, tuberous perennial to around 70cm high, with serrated dark green leaves. Double flowers to 10cm across, with soft yellow and peachy orange petals with contrasting dark red undersides, are produced from late summer to early autumn
A dwarf, bedding dahlia to about 30cm with dark green foliage and salmon pink, fully double flowers produced from mid-summer until frosted in autumn
A compact, bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green foliage and upright stems bearing double flowers comprising white petals edged and tipped with pink and pale purple
An early-flowering, compact hardy perennial with narrow, grey-green foliage and double, fragrant white flowers appearing spring to summer. Suitable for pots both indoors and outdoors
An early-flowering, compact hardy perennial with narrow, grey-green foliage and fragrant, double salmon-pink flowers appearing spring to summer. Suitable for pots both indoors and outdoors
An early-flowering, compact hardy perennial with narrow, grey-green foliage and fragrant, bright pink flowers appearing spring to summer. Suitable for pots both indoors and outdoors

A highly attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, pink blooms with a central orange-brown cone and narrow, recurved ray petals. Excellent for cutting and attracting pollinators

An attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing pale orange blooms with a central brown cone and downward arching ray petals. Excellent for container growing, cutting and attracting pollinators

A striking, upright perennial coneflower variety producing bright orange blooms with strongly reflexed petals surrounding a prominent central orange-brown cone. Its compact habit is perfect for container growing. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A highly attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing large, pale pink blooms from early to late summer with some autumn flowering. Flowers have a flattened central orange-brown cone surrounded by short, broad, overlapping, petals. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators
A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with lobed, dark green leaves and solitary, daisy-like, red flowers borne on sturdy stems from late spring into autumn

A compact deciduous shrub to 1m high, with broadly oval, serrated green leaves. Dome-shaped clusters of flowers, with lightly feathered edges to the petals, are produced from early to late summer. Flower colours are deeper at the edges of the petals, and vary depending on the pH of the soil, from deep pink to purple and blue

A clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to 1.2m tall, with ovate leaves, purple-flushed when young. From late summer to early autumn it bears single, red flowerheads that age to coppery orange. A good plant to attract pollinating insects and also makes a long-lasting cut flowers
A compact and bushy perennial with dark green foliage and slender tall racemes of small deep purple-violet lipped flowers in summer.

Sturdy, upright perennial coneflower about 75cm tall, with coarse green leaves and bearing daisy-like blooms, the ray petals in shades of yellow from dark yellow to pale cream, surrounding a cone of yellowish-orange, flowering from midsummer to autumn
A biennial or short-lived perennial with semi-evegreen, grey-green divided leaves, reaching 35cm. It has white flowers on sturdy stems for up to four months through the summer
An evergreen shrub with deep green, elliptical leaves and greenish-white flower buds in autumn opening to fragrant white flowers in spring.

An annual beefsteak tomato producing large, juicy fruit with a good aroma and flavour throughout the summer and early autumn. An indeterminate variety which means it produces fruit throughout the season, and an ideal variety for pots and containers
A plum tomato with a loose habit, which can be grown as a bush or cordon. Heavy crops of red plum tomatoes, that are great for sauces and cooking, are produced in summer

A dwarf daffodil to 17cm high, with very narrow, dark green leaves. Flowers are fragrant and pale creamy yellow, with a funnel-shaped corona and narrow, pointed outer petals. Flowers over a long period from early spring. Suitable for naturalising

A bulbous perennial, growing to 60cm tall, with narrow, upright, strap-like, dark green leaves and tall, sturdy stems bearing large flowers that have lavender blushing standards above delicate, purple veined, white falls with a golden yellow centre spot. Perfect for cut flowers and container growing

A short-lived perennial, often grown as an annual, up to 35cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves, and racemes of scented, open-faced flowers that are bronze-yellow flushed with purplish pink, with white throats, from midsummer to early autumn

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with green, lance-shaped foliage. Upright stems of cone-shaped clusters of milky pale lilac bell-shaped flowers provide a long flowering display in summer. An easy to grow plant but dislikes wet winters

primary_name: Celosia argentea var. cristata (Plumosa Group) [Kelos Fire Orange] ('Bkcelor') (Kelos Fire Series)
description: A compact, upright, bushy, vigorous perennial to around 30cm in height, usually grown as an annual, with oval-shaped, green leaves. Thick plumes of feathery bright orange flowers appear in summer. Perfect for summer pots and containers, as a houseplant or as bedding in a flower border. Drought and heat-tolerant, once established

primary_name: Celosia argentea (Spicata Group) [Kelos Atomic Neon Pink] ('Bkcelanp') (Kelos Atomic Series)
description: A compact, upright, bushy, vigorous perennial to around 30cm in height, usually grown as an annual, with oval-shaped, bronze-green leaves. Thick plumes of feathery bright neon-pink flowers appear in summer. Perfect for summer pots and containers, as a houseplant or as bedding in a flower border. Drought and heat-tolerant, once established

Celosia argentea (Plumosa Group) [First Flame Red] ('Pas905170') (First Flame Series)
description: A compact, bushy, low-growing, vigorous perennial to around 30cm in height, usually grown as an annual, with green foliage. Small, thick plumes of vibrant red flowers appear in summer. Great in pots and containers or at the front of a flower border. Drought and heat-tolerant, once established

primary_name: Celosia argentea (Plumosa Group) [First Flame Scarlet] ('Pas1233915') (First Flame Series)
Celosia argentea (Plumosa Group) [First Flame Yellow] ('Pas1350211') (First Flame Series)
description: A compact, bushy, low-growing, vigorous perennial to around 40cm in height, usually grown as an annual, with green foliage. Small plumes of golden yellow flowers appear in summer. Great in pots and containers or at the front of a flower border. Drought and heat-tolerant, once established

alternative_names: Celosia [Kelos Yellow]|Celosia argentea var. cristata (Plumosa Group) 'Bkcelfyl'
description: A compact, upright, bushy, vigorous perennial to around 30cm in height, usually grown as an annual, with oval-shaped, dark green leaves. Thick plumes of feathery bright yellow flowers appear in summer. Perfect for summer pots and containers, as a houseplant or as bedding in a flower border. Drought and heat-tolerant, once established
A vigorous evergreen shrub with glossy, ovate dark green leaves with sunken veins, and fine hairs on the undersides. Produces small to medium, formal double, deep pink flowers in spring

An evergreen shrub or small tree growing up to 8m tall in the wild but likely to be smaller in cultivation. Elliptic to narrowly oval, leathery, dark green leaves are up to 12cm long and may or may not be toothed. White spring flowers are borne in racemes to 9cm long and have prominent stamens

alternative_names: red tipped Chinese fountain bamboo|Fargesia dracocephala misapplied
description: Dense, clump-forming bamboo about 4m tall, with canes powdery white, then becoming glossy dark green spotted purple. Leaves are dark green, the leaf sheaths with purple tips

A dense, slow-growing, clump-forming bamboo about 4m tall, with canes powdery white, then becoming glossy dark green spotted purple. Variegated leaves are striped white or all white, becoming yellow-green in the summer, then darker in autumn and winter

An upright, perennial coneflower variety producing showy, fragrant blooms with unusual purple-green ray petals radiating from a prominent, central red-brown cone. A quirky addition to the border and excellent for container growing
A compact, clump-forming perennial to 50cm tall with dark green, hairy leaves. Branched stems carry flowerheads of pale yellow ray florets surrounding a golden brown cone, from summer into autumn
A cultivar up to 60cm tall that produces semi-double flowers opening salmon-pink with some soft yellow ray florets at their centres before turning a paler pink with age
A mat-forming evergreen shrub with trailing, rooting shoots and opposite pairs of glossy, dark green leaves. From mid-spring to late summer it produces double, sky-blue flowers to 3cm across

An upright hardy annual or biennial to around 90cm in height, with oval to heart-shaped, toothed, dark green foliage which may be brushed with purple. Large clusters of purple-pink flowers appear in late spring to early summer, followed by flat, round, silvery seed pods. Self-seeds, great as a cut flower and for pollinators

A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with an upright habit and aromatic, dark green, oval to lance-shaped leaves. Long, whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped deep magenta flowers, which are very attractive to pollinators, appear all through summer until the autumn

An attractive, simple coneflower variety from the Fountain Light Purple series, producing open pink-purple blooms with narrow, flat petals extending out from a central red cone. Excellent as a cut flower and for attracting pollinators

A unique bicolor coneflower variety producing colourful blooms blending from bright red-orange at the heart out to a deep yellow. The reflexed petals surround a dark central cone that is extremely attractive to pollinators. Blooms will appear from June to September

A clump-forming perennial, to around 40cm high in flower, forming a dense mound of divided, wrinkled, hairy green leaves with toothed edges. Semi-double flowers with frilly petals, pale apricot in the centres and flushed with pink at the edges, are borne on reddish stems above the foliage in flushes from late spring to late summer

A clump-forming perennial to about 40cm high, forming a mound of lobed, ruffled leaves in shades of gold, copper and reddish bronze. Loose sprays of small white flowers appear above the foliage in late spring and summer
A compact, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with lance-shaped, toothed mid to dark green leaves and upright slender stems of small, deep pink flowers appearing in spring and summer

A bushy, clump-forming, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with silvery-green marbled foliage which intensifies in colour during the summer. Large, forward-facing, dark pink flowers with large lime-green stamens, appear from January to April

primary_name: Helleborus (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) [Cheryl's Shine] ('Epb 31') (Frostkiss Series)
description: A herbaceous perennial up to 60cm high, with overwintering leaves of dark green marbled with cream, and forward-facing flowers of pale pink, darker towards the edges,with conspicuous yellow stamens, from winter to spring; hellebore flowers provide nectar and pollen for early-flying bees

primary_name: Helleborus (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) [Dana's Dulcet] ('Epb 30') (Frostkiss Series)
description: A semi-evergreen clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, dark and light green marbled foliage with a silvery patina. Has branched stems rising above with dangling cup-shaped violet-pink with a hint of green single flowers and a large central boss of yellow stamens in late winter and early spring.

primary_name: Helleborus (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) [Molly's White] ('Epbrd01') (Frostkiss Series)
description: A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, green marbled foliage and branched stems rising above with dangling cup-shaped white turning to lime green single flowers in late winter and early spring.

A bushy, clump-forming semi-evergreen to evergreen perennial with leathery, marbled silver and dark green foliage and white flowers, flushed with pink at the edges and with lime-green centres, which appear from late winter to early spring

primary_name: Helleborus (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) [Reanna's Ruby] ('Epb 32') (Frostkiss Series)
description: A semi-evergreen clump-forming perennial with divided, leathery, green leaves with burgundy speckles, marbled foliage and branched stems rising above with dangling cup-shaped ruby red faintly spotted single flowers in late winter and early spring.

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus (Ashwood Evolution Group) 'Ashwood Yellow Hammer'

description: A deciduous, slow growing cultivar, up to 3.5m tall with contorted stems. Green needles in spring and summer, yellowing in the autumn.

primary_name: Helleborus × hybridus double spotted Lady Series (d)

description: A deciduous tree reaching over 10m in height with ovate mid-green leaves. The fragrant, cup-shaped flowers, produced in spring before the leaves, are creamy white and prolific.

A low-growing perennial that forms a neat, evergreen mat of attractive small, round, dark green, toothed leaves. Numerous, outward facing, deep violet-blue, bell-shaped, single flowers appear on short stalks, sitting just above its foliage, providing a long flowering display in summer
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 1m high, with divided, slightly glossy dark green leaves. Large, pure white double flowers are produced in late spring and early summer

A rhizomatous tender, evergreen perennial to 80cm tall and 35cm wide. Its large evergreen leaves are deep pink to burgundy red with near black veins and margins; small pink flowers are borne from summer into autumn

An evergreen clump-forming perennial with long, thick dark green leaves and long, thin flower stalks which produce dark, velvety plum-red flowers with white edges and a white throat from Spring through to the Autumn. An ideal houseplant

alternative_names: Cape primrose 'Lemon Sorbet'|Streptocarpus [Yellow Blue Eye] (Ladyslippers Series)
description: A compact, tender perennial with hairy, strap-shaped leaves. Tubular flowers up to 5cm across are borne over a long period; petals are pale lemon yellow inside and pale to mid-mauve outside with darker purple streaks at the centre
A bushy, climbing rose to 2m tall, with glossy, dark green leaves and bearing clusters of large, citrus-fragranced, double soft pink blooms, repeat-flowering from summer to autumn

alternative_names: Shenkan maple|Acer pictum f. tricuspis|Acer mono var. tricuspis (Rehder) Rehder|Acer bodinieri|Acer cappadocicum var. tricaudatum|Acer cappadocicum subsp. sinicum var. tricaudatum
description: Rare in cultivation, a small, deciduous tree, to about 10m tall, with slender-stalked, 3-lobed mid-green leaves, turning yellow in autumn. Yellowish-green flower clusters in late spring are followed by brown winged fruits in autumn

Rare in cultivation, a small, deciduous tree about 5m in height, with 7-9 lobed glossy green leaves that are silky-hairy beneath, flushed yellow-red in spring and turn purple-red in autumn. Purplish flowers in late spring are followed by large brown winged fruits

A frost-tender, tuberous evergreen perennial to 1.2m tall, producing striking, heart-shaped, black leaves with purple undersides and a satin sheen on dark, upright stems. A stunning foliage plant, perfect as a houseplant or can be grown outside in containers in a frost-free, sheltered location

alternative_names: dogwood [Empress of China]|Cornus elliptica 'Elsbry'|Cornus angustata [Empress of China]
description: A compact, semi-evergreen small tree or large shrub with oval-shaped dark green glossy foliage, turning more pink to yellow in autumn and winter. Masses of creamy-white flowers (bracts) appear in early summer, once the plant is established, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn

alternative_names: mini angel's trumpet|Acnistus australis|Iochroma australe|Dunalia australis
description: A half-hardy shrub or small tree, evergreen if grown under glass, normally deciduous outdoors. The leaves are downy and the trumpet-shaped, hanging flowers are an unusual, dark lavender-blue
