Iochroma australe 'Bill Evans'|Iochroma australe blue-flowered|Eriolarynx australis blue-flowered|Dunalia australis blue-flowered
Iochroma australe large-flowered|Dunalia australis large-flowered form
Iochroma warscewiczii|Iochroma coelestis hort.|Iochroma nitidum|Iochroma grandiflorum

description: An upright perennial with dark green, lobed leaves and sprays of anemone-type blooms, deep pink in the centre with pale pink outer florets, in late autumn

Fast-growing, narrowly upright tree about 15m tall and 6m wide, oval at maturity, with dense branches and 3-5 lobed, dark green, palmate leaves, grey-green beneath, turning brilliant orange-red and yellow in autumn. Produces upright clusters of tiny red flowers, followed by purple-brown winged fruits
A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 25cm in height with small, semi-trailing, oval pale green leaves. Red flowers appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

An erect herbaceous perennial which flowers earlier than other cultivars of the same species, has dark-green lance-shaped foliage and terminal clusters of fragrant tubular pure white flowers over a long period of time in summer.
A compact, mound-forming evergreen shrub with aromatic grey-green foliage and dense spikes of chunky, fragrant dark pink flowers with paler twisted wings, which appear in June to July
An upright perennial, to around 90cm high, with lance-shaped, glossy green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant, vivid lilac pink flowers are produced from early summer

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial to 60cm tall, prized for its foliage. The dark green leaves are held on long stalks and have curled and wavy margins, giving the plant the look of a giant parsley. Yellow, daisy-like flowers are produced in loose clusters in autumn and winter
A slow-growing evergreen shrub to about 1.5m high, with a spreading habit and large, dull dark green leaves. Produces clusters of pale pink flowers with darker pink margins, in late spring

A dwarf form of the species, growing to a maximum height of 2m (6½ft), making it ideal for smaller city gardens and growing in containers. Juvenile foliage is ovate and an intense blue-green. Adult foliage is sickle-shaped and sage-green. Foliage is aromatic. Hard pruning is required every year in early spring to maintain the production of the more ornamental juvenile foliage. White flowers appear in autumn and are attractive to bees and other pollinators.

primary_name: Eucalyptus pauciflora subsp. niphophila from Mount Bogong, Australia
description: A slow-growing, dwarf form of this species eventually growing to around 8m (27ft) with smooth, cream to white bark with cinnamon and pink shades. The juvenile foliage is blue-green and ovate, while the adult foliage is sickle-shaped and blue green. Young growth and foliage is moderately aromatic when crushed. White, honey-scented flowers are produced in summer.
A small to medium, fast-growing, clump-forming deciduous perennial with heart-shaped, golden veined foliage with wavy edges. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer

A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated, dark green, textured foliage with irregular-shaped yellow margins which turn to white during the summer. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated creamy-white foliage with green margins. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

A large shrub or with delicate, mimosa-like, bipinnate leaves which emerge bronze green and change to dark purple, and a spreading, umbrella habit. Fluffy, fragrant creamy-pink to purple flower-heads, with prominent stamens, open in summer. An exotic-looking plant which is ideal for smaller gardens where space is limited, or in pots and containers

A rhizomatous perennial, up to 90cm high, with upright stems and asymmetric, shallowly lobed, large, glossy dark green leaves that are flushed reddish when young. Large pink flowers are borne on tall stems in summer
Bulbous perennial to 70cm tall, with leaves that remain green during flowering, producing very large violet-purple flowers for several weeks in early and mid summer

A rhizomatous perennial, to 80cm high, with large, glossy, shallowly lobed and coarsely toothed green leaves up to 25cm long. Clusters of small, white or sometimes pinkish flowers are produced in late summer and autumn
A tuberous perennial, with very large, asymmetric green leaves up to 45cm long. Clusters of pale pink flowers are produced in late summer

A handsome herbaceous perennial which may develop a woody base. It is grown for its attractive pairs of green leaves which are deeply veined with serrated margins including one very prominent tooth at the tips. In summer, strings of long pink flowers develop looking like pipecleaners.

A small, perennial corm growing to 8cm tall with long, narrow, dark green leaves marked with a fine, central, white stripe. Produces scented, goblet-shaped, ivory-white flowers in late winter and early spring

A compact bulbous perennial, to around 45cm high, with upright stems and narrowly lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, upward-facing, deep red flowers, touched with purple in the centre, are produced in early to mid summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 90cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Flowers are blush pink, fading to white-cream with dark red spots near the centre of the flower

A bulbous perennial to around 1m high with upright stems and lance -shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, scented, upward-facing red to dark pink flowers with a yellow vein near the centre of each petal appear in the summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 90cm high, with upright stems and narrowly lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, lightly scented, bright orange flowers, with slightly darker reddish-orange edges, are produced in early to mid summer

A perennial bulb to around 45cm in height, with lance-shaped grey-green foliage and strong, upright stems producing large, peony-shaped double white flowers with lilac-pink edges, appearing in April to May

A perennial bulb, to around 35cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. Early flowering, with double white flowers lightly veined with pale tan, and occasionally streaked green at the base of the petals

A vigorous, clump-forming perennial, to around 50cm high, with spreading stolons, upright stems and glossy, coarsely toothed green leaves with long tapered tips. Clusters of small white flowers are produced in the leaf axils in early autumn

A herbaceous perennial, to around 50cm high, with creeping stolons and upright stems bearing textured, asymmetric green leaves with distinctive veining and long, tapered tips. Spikes or sprays of tiny white flowers are produced in summer

A clump-forming perennial, to around 30cm high, with coarsely toothed, deeply veined green leaves with silvery white streaks. Loose sprays of tiny greenish-white flowers are produced in late summer or early autumn

A woody-based perennial, with spreading stolons and upright stems up to 1.2m high. Leaves are bright green, elliptic, and deeply veined with shallowly serrated edges and pointed tips. Sprays of tiny white or pink flowers are produced in the upper leaf axils in late summer and early autumn
A deciduous, clump-forming perennial with triangular, shallowly-lobed leaves and stout stems to 1.8m tall bearingnodding flowerheads to 6cm across made up of deep reddish-purple florets in autumn

A clump-forming perennial to 75cm tall with deciduous, sword-shaped foliage. From midsummer into autumn, arching stems bear upward-facing flowers with golden-yellow petals edged with orange and with a central orange stripe surrounding an orange-red eye

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit up to 90cm tall when in flower. It has healthy, mid-green, blade-like leaves and strong, arching flower stems that bear large, orange-yellow flowers with red stripes in the centres of the petals, from mid-summer to autumn

An aromatic, evergreen tree with silvery-grey bark peeling to reveal cream or pinkish brown patches. Lance-shaped mature foliage is blue-green; rounded juvenile foliage is silvery-blue. Small, white, fragrant, fluffy flowers appear on mature plants in mid- to late summer, followed by woody, rounded, olive-green fruit
A compact, erect, evergreen shrub to 2.5m tall, with glossy, lanceloate leaves, brilliant red when young, later turning dark green. Panicles of small, creamy-white flowers appear in spring

primary_name: Prunus persica var. nectarina 'Nana Red Prolific' (F)

description: A compact perennial to about 45cm, with grey-green, fern-like foliage which carpets the ground before the flowers appear. Upright, branching stems are topped with small, flat, pink-purple flowerheads from June to September

An attractive evergreen perennial forming a creeping rhizomatous clump with large, round, shiny, dark green leaves. Clusters of apple blossom pink, bell shaped flowers with red centres are held atop tall stalks in spring

A deciduous, bushy shrub to around 1.2m high, with a spreading habit and narrowly oval, dark green leaves. Long clusters of lightly scented, light purple flowers are produced at the tips of the stems from early summer into autumn

A dense, bushy, upright evergreen shrub with oval-shaped, variegated yellow foliage with irregular dark green margins and silvery-grey undersides. Small, fragrant, white flowers appear in autumn, followed by orange berries
A compact, deciduous shrub, to around 80cm high, with dark green elliptic leaves with finely serrated edges. Large conical clusters of white flowers are produced in mid to late summer

alternative_names: cut-leaved painted maple|Acer mono f. dissectum|Acer pictum var. angustilobum
description: A fast-growing, deciduous tree about 10-12m tall, with a spreading canopy, and glossy, dark green leaves, 5-7cm long and wide, with 5 deeply-cut lobes tapering to sharp points, and turning golden-yellow in autumn. Upright greenish-yellow spring flowers in clusters are followed by brown winged fruits in autumn

Small, fast-growing, deciduous tree about 10m tall, with large, broad, 3-5 lobed dark green leaves to 15cm long, densely spotted with cream and yellow in early summer then in autumn the leaf colour is clear bright yellow occasionally flushed red. Conspicuous clusters of yellow flowers are produced on bare stems in mid spring followed by greenish-brown winged fruits in summer

A compact evergreen succulent about 30-50cm tall, forming dense clumps of fleshy stems bearing small, blue-green, slightly rounded leaves with shallow, wavy indentations on the edges. Starry flowers in midsummer, open pale green, then become cream to pale yellow

A vigorous, deciduous, twining climber about 9m in height or more with green leaves divided into 9-13 leaflets, bronze when young. Scented, pea-like, blue-mauve flowers, the standard petals are pale mauve with small greenish-yellow eyes and darker wing and keel petals, are produced in long trusses, in mid spring, and may be followed by bean-like, velvety pale green seed pods 15cm long

alternative_names: Japanese maple [Going Green]|Acer palmatum 'Sonkootgre'|Acer palmatum 'Going Green'
description: A small, rounded, bushy tree growing slowly to about 5m tall with luminous green stems. Leaves have seven long, pointed lobes, opening lime green in spring, maturing to bright green, then turning orange and red in autumn. Inconspicuous hanging clusters of small, green flowers are followed by red-flushed, winged seeds

A clump-forming, evergreen herbaceous perennial to around 15cm in height, with three-lobed, kidney-shaped dark green leaves with a faint blush of red to the edges. Single, multi-petalled lavender-blue flowers and a yellow centre appear from February to March

alternative_names: anise-scented sage [Black and Bloom]|Salvia guaranitica 'Black & Bloom'|Salvia 'Balsaloom'|Salvia [Black & Bloom]
description: A tall perennial to 120cm tall, forming a wide clump of stems bearing dark green ovate leaves and loose spikes of vivid cobalt blue flowers, contrasting with black calyx, and opening in mid-summer and autumn
A heritage variety of torpedo shaped, brownish-pink skinned bulbs with a superb flavour, popular for gourmet cooking. Suitable for storing with good resistance to bolting

A dwarf, slow-growing evergreen shrub, rare in cultivation, with thick, glossy and leathery dark green foliage with white, softly hairy undersides. Bright, scarlet-red, funnel-shaped flowers appear in April to May

An evergreen azalea to about 1m high, with a dense, compact habit, and small ovate green leaves. Long-flowering, producing an initial flush of broadly funnel-shaped white flowers in spring, followed by a second flush in summer that can continue into early autumn
A bush, cherry tomato suitable for growing in containers and on patios. It produces plentiful, small red cherry tomatoes, even in cool, wet summers
A cordon salad tomato, suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces heavy yields of medium sized red salad tomatoes and has good blight resistance
A cordon salad tomato suitable for growing in a greenhouse or outdoors. It produces heavy crops of large, red, tomatoes and has good resistance to blight
A bushy, dwarf hybrid variety suitable for patios and containers. Dark red cherry tomatoes are produced over a long season from July right through to November

A cordon tomato grown as an annual either in an unheated greenhouse or outside. This cultivar produces trusses of medium-sized, round, red fruit 70-80 days from sowing and is noted for its good levels of resistance to tomato blight

primary_name: Solanum lycopersicum var. cerasiforme 'Matt's Wild Cherry'

description: A compact, evergreen shrub to around 1.2m high, with pinnate leaves to 16cm long, divided into pairs of spiny, leathery dark green leaflets. Small yellow flowers, with outer petals flushed with mauve, are borne in upright to spreading clusters to 7cm long in late autumn
A deciduous azalea to 1.5m high, with a compact habit and ovate, dark green leaves. Late-flowering, producing clusters of tubular to funnel-shaped, scented bright pink flowers in mid summer

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 1m high, with divided, slightly glossy deep green leaves. Double pink flowers are produced in late spring and early summer, with secondary buds extending the flowering season
A compact, clump-forming perennial forming a low mound of semi-evergreen, finely-divided, aromatic foliage. Flattened flowerheads of tiny, dark orange flowers are borne on upright stems in summer

An upright, deciduous shrub or small, multi-stemmed tree to 4m tall, with peeling, grey and reddish-brown bark and large, glossy leaves. In late summer it produces pale purple flowers with crinkled petals, held in small clusters. Hardier than L. indica and its cultivars, but less spectacular

A deciduous shrub to around 1m high, with a compact, bushy habit and narrow, grey-green leaves. Fluffy clusters of deep blue flowers with prominent stamens are produced from the upper leaf axils and tips of the stems in late summer and early autumn

A vigorous, upright, deciduous shrub with bright green ovate leaves on dark red stems. Can reach up to 2m if left unpruned. This cultivar is early flowering, with cone-shaped clusters of flowers produced from early to late summer. Flowers open creamy white and develop tints of pale pink and then deep pink as the season progresses
A rhizomatous perennial forming a mound of heart-shaped, rough-textured, silvery leaves up to 20cm wide with green edges and veining. Tiny blue flowers are produced in small clusters in spring
A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with long stalks formed with divided green leaves and tall spikes packed with frilly rosettes of soft pale yellow flowers in summer.
A compact evergreen perennial with grey-green leaves. Scented, single flowers are produced in summer. Flowers are magenta-pink with a thin white margin

A compact, clump-forming perennial to about 25cm high, forming a mound of lobed and ruffled leaves that emerge red and deepen to dark ruby red. Loose sprays of small pale pink flowers appear above the foliage from late spring into summer

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 25cm high, with deeply lobed leaves that open bright yellow-green with dark red veins, and mature to green with a silvery flush. Slender stems bear clusters of tiny, bell-shaped pink flowers from late spring into summer

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial with deeply lobed, silver-flushed green leaves, darker at the veins. Slender stems bear panicles of tiny, bell-shaped, pink flowers from late spring into summer.
A mound forming, compact perennial with dark-green foliage and slender racemes of small bicoloured blue and white lipped flowers in late spring and early summer.
Upright, deciduous tree about 6-8m in height, with ovate mid-green leaves. The large, goblet shaped flowers are a vibrant reddish-purple and are produced in abundance in mid-spring

A strongly upright, deciduous small tree to about 6m in height, with velvety, mid-green leaves, flushed bronze when young. Large, fragrant, cup-shaped purple-pink flowers, are white within, and produced in mid-spring, pale pink flowers may appear in summer

alternative_names: greater snowdrop 'Louise Ann Bromley'|Galanthus 'Louise Ann Bromley'
description: A perennial bulb, to 25cm high, with pairs of lance-shaped, grey-green leaves, wrapped one around the other at the base. Solitary, nodding white flowers are produced in mid to late winter, with inner petals marked with a bold, almost x-shaped green blotch

A bulbous perennial, to 15cm tall, with relatively broad, grey-green leaves and solitary, nodding, white flowers, the outer segments pure white, the inner ones marked with a broad, green X, in mid- to late winter
A perennial bulb, to around 14cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with outer petals streaked with pale green, and solid green inner petals
A bushy, evergreen shrub to 90cm tall, forming a neat mound of slender leaves. From late summer into early autumn it produces bright yellow flowers with a boss of golden stamens

Clump-forming, evergreen perennial sedge, about 60cm tall, with slender, finely pointed, dark green leaves, at its brightest in autumn and winter, when edged with orange from summer to early autumn then bronze edged in winter, fading to cream in spring and summer. Carries panicles of green and brown flower spikes on stems 45cm long within the foliage, in late spring

A compact hybrid succulent, with slender, branching stems tipped with small rosettes of fleshy green leaves that are brushed with red at the midribs and margins. Bright yellow flowers are produced on mature plants in summer

A bushy, herbaceous perennial to 60cm tall, with rough, hairy stems. From late summer to autumn it produces daisy-like flowerheads composed of bright yellow ray florets around a central, black cone. The flowers are attract pollinating insects and are also good for cutting

alternative_names: Valder's wisteria 'Lavender Lace'|Wisteria 'Lavender Lace'|Wisteria floribunda 'Lavender Lace'
description: A vigorous, deciduous climber twining clockwise and reaching up to 9m tall. Leaves comprising up to 15 leaflets emerge bronze-green in the spring and turn yellow in the autumn. Drooping flower racemes up to 50cm long are borne in late spring and early summer; each raceme may have in excess of one hundred sweetly-scented flowers with pale violet standards and deeper colouring on the wings and keels

alternative_names: hornbeam [Rockhampton Red]|Carpinus betulus 'Rockhampton Red'|Carpinus betulus 'Lochglow'|Carpinus betulus 'Rockhampton'|Carpinus 'Rockhampton Red'
description: Deciduous tree, with grey bark and a densely branched crown about 15m (50ft) tall when mature. It bears bright green foliage that unusually for a hornbeam turns to fiery reds and oranges in autumn. It can often hold its dead, brown leaves through winter, shedding them in spring. Produces green catkins in late spring and clusters of winged fruit later in the year

Large bamboo forming clumps of dense, dark green canes about 5m tall, tinged purple, maturing to red-brown, dark red in sun with pale hairy sheaths. Delicate, linear mid-green leaves to 13cm long turn orange-red in cold weather

A deciduous, thorny shrub reaching a maximum a maximum height of 4m and spread to 2.5m, with silvery-green leaves. It has inconspicuous yellow-brown flowers which become - if a male is also planted - a large crop of yellow-orange berries. Salt and wind tolerant, it is useful for coastal hedging.
A compact, deciduous shrub up to 1.2m tall, with flowerheads of white to pale pink, double sterile florets, produced in early summer

An evergreen or semi-evergreen shrub to 60cm tall, forming a neat mound of foliage on arching red stems. The leaves bear creamy-white mottling and a pink flush; the best colour is on the new growth. Bright yellow flowers are produced from late summer to early autumn

Deciduous, bulbous perennial which can be grown either as an ornamental or annual vegetable, producing strap-shaped mid-green leaves and densely packed, spherical heads of white flowers on straight stems to 1.2m tall, in mid and late summer

alternative_names: Peruvian lily [Holiday Valley]|Alstroemeria 'Tessumholid'|Alstroemeria [Summer Holiday] (Summer Paradise Series)

description: A compact, clump-forming perennial to around 40cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Funnel-shaped scarlet flowers, with a speckled cream blotch on the upper petals, are borne over a long period from late spring into autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 30cm tall, with dark-green lance shaped leaves and clusters of dark purple-blue, funnel-shaped flowers which have black speckles and a white throat on the upper petals, flowering in summer and autumn.

alternative_names: Peruvian lily [Summer Breeze]|Peruvian lily 'Summer Breeze'|Alstroemeria 'Teshunte'|Alstroemeria 'Summer Breeze'
description: Compact, clump-forming perennial about 60-70cm tall, with mid-green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of funnel-shaped yellow, peach and orange flowers, with yellow-splashed inner petals, and dark brown speckles, flowering in summer and autumn

Compact, clump-forming, tuberous perennial, about 60cm tall and wide, with lance-shaped dark green foliage. Scarlet-red funnel-shaped flowers, with yellow throats flecked dark red, are borne in open, terminal clusters from summer to mid-autumn

Clump-forming perennial about 60-70cm in height, with mid-green lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of long-lasting pink funnel-shaped flowers lightly streaked darker pink, with yellow inner petals that are strongly flecked purple-brown, in summer and autumn

Compact, clump-forming perennial about 70cm tall, with dark green lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of funnel-shaped pink flowers which have a creamy-yellow throat and dark brown speckles on the upper petals, borne in summer and autumn.

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 90cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves and contrasting slate-grey stems. Purple flowers with recurved petals appear in July through until the first frosts

A compact, deciduous tuberous-rooted perennial, to about 100cm, with fleshy, glossy green foliage. Large, multi-petalled dark, rose-pink to purple-pink flowers appear on upright stems from July through to October

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 120cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Bright, coral-pink flowers with hints of lemon-yellow appear from summer through until the first frosts

A tuberous-rooted perennial to about 90cm, with mid-green foliage. From mid-summer to the first frost produces fully double flowers, 10cm across, with long, narrow, swept back petals in a variable mix of lemon-yellow and white
A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 150cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Salmon-red double flowers with yellow centres appear from summer through until the first frosts

A bulbous perennial, to around 80cm high, with upright stems and narrowly lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, lightly scented, upward to outward-facing pink flowers, with a reddish flare and dark red speckles in the centre, are produced in late spring and early summer. Produces an average of four flowers per bulb
A bulbous perennial to around 120cm high with upright stems and lance-shaped glossy green leaves. Upright, chocolate-burgundy to pale orange flowers are produced in early summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, outward-facing, golden orange flowers, with a red flare and dark red-brown spots in the centre, are produced in early to mid summer
A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped glossy dark green leaves. Large, double white flowers with ruffled edges and some dark red spots appear in the summer

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, fragrant, double pink flowers with paler pink edges are produced in mid to late summer. Double oriental lilies such as this have extra petals rather than anthers, so are pollen-free

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, fragrant, double pink flowers, with paler centres, dark pink speckles and ruffled edges, are produced in mid to late summer. Double oriental lilies such as this have extra petals rather than anthers, so are pollen-free

A bulbous perennial, to around 1m high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Large, fragrant, double, bright pink flowers with ruffled edges are produced in mid to late summer. Double oriental lilies such as this have extra petals rather than anthers, so are pollen-free

A bulbous herbaceous perennial with dark green glossy leaves and large, star-shaped double white fragrant flowers with pink edges appearing in July. Unlike other double oriental lillies which do not contain pollen, this variety is unusual as it does contain pollen

A bulbous perennial, to around 90cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped green leaves. Large, lightly scented, outward-facing orange flowers, with deeper orange midribs to the petals, are produced in late spring and early summer
A bulbous perennial,to around 80cm high, with upright stems and lance-shaped, glossy dark green leaves. Yellow flowers have reflexed petals and wide, red markings with red spots near the centre

A large-cupped, clump-forming bulbous perennial daffodil with green strap-like foliage and strong, upright stems bearing fragrant creamy-white flowers, with a dark yellow ruffled cup, from early to mid-spring. Makes an ideal cutting flower

A miniature, clump-forming bulbous perennial daffodil to around 20cm in height, with green strap-like foliage and reflexed yellow flowers which appear in the spring from March to April. A very versatile variety which can be used for rockeries and pots and containers
A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green foliage and tall, strong stems to around 40cm producing large dark maroon red flowers with cream edges from mid April

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves with wavy edges. This Parrot Group tulip has cup-shaped flowers, with heavily fringed, rose pink petals with a narrow orange margin and orange insides. Flowers are approximately 40cm high, and produced in late spring
An upright perennial bulb to around 50cm with broadly lance-shaped dark green foliage. Elegant, flared scarlet-red to dark pink flowers appear in April to May
A perennial bulb to around 50cm with broadly lance-shaped dark green foliage and double, bowl-shaped strongly fragrant peony-shaped lemon-yellow flowers, appearing in late April
A bulbous perennial to around 60cm in height, with grey-green foliage. Double white flowers are edged with purple that spreads further over the petals as the flower matures and appear in April to May
A bulbous perennial with grey-green leaves and sturdy stems to 60cm tall bearing large spring flowers opening creamy-white with pinkish-red flames that become more dominant as the flower ages
A perennial bulb, to around 60cm high in flower, with broadly lance-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are double, with apricot yellow, fringed petals lightly streaked with red

Tender, evergreen species woody climber reaching about 3m or more in height, with narrow glossy, leathery dark green leaves, to 18cm long and white, pink or purple flowers in terminal clusters, produced in early spring, followed by black fruits

Compact, dwarf, thicket-forming, evergreen shrub about 30-60cm tall, with dark green leaves to 6cm long. Bright, rose pink, bowl-shaped flowers 1cm across with a hint of lavender, produced in clusters, early summer

This slow-growing evergreen conifer has a rather interesting habit with fairly open, upright growth from which a single upright stem arises that heads up skywards, giving the appearance of a snake covered in densely arranged blue-green needles. This eccentric tree is not for those who like even and well space growth

A slow-growing evergreen conifer with a narrow, upright habit. The short side branches radiate out from a thick central trunk. The congested growth of dark green needles fans out at the end of the branches, giving it a tail-like appearance. This slow and steady tree will yearly spread 5-10cm and put on 15 – 22 cm in height, reaching 2.5m in 10 years in ideal growing conditions

A small, deciduous, spreading tree to 6m, with peeling grey and brown bark and glossy, dark green leaves; the foliage displays good autumn colour. In summer, large conical clusters of white flowers are produced

A dense, upright, evergreen conifer with a pyramid-shaped habit to around 3m in height. Golden-yellow, soft needle-like foliage retains its colour all year round and is an ideal choice as a specimen plant or as part of a mixed border or hedging
Deciduous shrub rare in cultivation, about 1.2m in height
A deciduous sub-shrub to a height of up to 2m with long, annual, arching shoots bearing clover-like leaves and 15mm in length rose-purple flowers in sprays to 15cm in length in early autumn

A small, suckering evergreen shrub up to 1m high, with pinnate leaves to 18cm long, divided into 3-4 pairs of spiny, glossy dark green leaflets. Small yellow flowers are borne in clusters to 5cm long in spring

While some Mahonias can get too large for smaller spaces this cultivar is more compact and has less prickly leaves with large, frond-like leaves developing in whorls along branched stems. Large clusters of fragrant yellow flowers appear in late autumn/early winter, followed by dark blue-black berries by late summer

An evergreen shrub to around 2m high, with a stiffly upright habit and pinnate leaves clustered at the ends of the branches. Leaves are divided into pairs of glossy green leaflets, each with one to three small teeth at the tips. Small, pale yellow flowers appear in short clusters between spring and early autumn, and are followed by blue-black berries

An evergreen shrub to around 1.5m high, with narrow, pinnate leaves to 22cm long, divided into pairs of close-set or overlapping, narrowly ovate glossy leaflets with spiny toothed edges. New leaves are tinted red in spring. Clusters of small yellow flowers are borne in autumn, followed by black berries

An evergreen shrub to around 1.5m high, with a low-growing habit and pinnate leaves to 40cm long, divided into pairs of narrow, glossy olive green leaflets with spiny edges. Small, yellow-green flowers are borne in short clusters in autumn and winter, and are followed by blue berries

A deciduous shrub or small tree to 7.5m, with toothed, heart-shaped leaves to 15cm long; the foliage develops good autumn colour. In early summer the mulberry fruits ripen; they are edible but M. nigra produces tastier fruit

A slow-growing evergreen tree, to 15m high in its native environment but usually smaller in cultivation, and often multi-stemmed. It has pale, corky bark and narrowly lance-shaped, leathery dark green leaves. An upright, branching, deciduous shrub with finely textured, dissected, dark green leaves. A half-hardy evergreen shrub or tree, reaching up to 15m high in its native range though often smaller in cultivation. Leaves are broadly ovate, glossy and papery in texture, with toothed edges and pairs of sharp spines at the base. Young shoots are coated with fine brown hairs. Clusters of small yellow flowers are produced in the leaf axils from late spring to early summer, followed by disc-shaped green seed pods

A fast-growing large deciduous tree to over 20m. It has large heart-shaped green leaves with a furry texture. Golden brown flower buds are produced in autumn and then open the following spring, before the leaves open. Flowers are large clusters of mauve bells with a sweet smell.

A deciduous Photinia that can become a large shrub or small broad-headed tree, with oblong to oval shaped pale green leathery glossy leaves with prominent leaf veins. Hawthorne like creamy white flowers in spring followed by small egg shaped bright red berries. It has glorious rich golden yellow autumn colour that can develop orange rusty tints. This Photinia will not thrive on shallow chalky or very alkaline soils.

A fast-growing semi-evergreen or deciduous tree to 25m. The leaves are quite narrow and have sharply pointed lobes. They emerge coppery red then become green and are retained through most of the winter before turning yellow and falling, shortly before the new ones emerge

A large semi-evergreen tree to approximately 20m. Elongated, slightly leathery leaves have small teeth along the edges (usually) and are bright green most of the year. Acorns are longer than they are wide, half enclosed in a grey-brown scaly cup

A large, vigorous, deciduous climber to about 9m tall or more, with twining stems and dark green leaves, bronze-flushed when young, divided into leaflets that turn yellow in autumn. Slender, long racemes of sweetly scented, pea-like, pink flowers, marked dark mauvish-pink, produced in late spring, often followed by bean-like velvety, blue-grey seed pods to 15cm long

A vigorous twining climber about 6-8m or more tall, with smooth, glossy green young leaves composed of leaflets, darkening in colour with age. Lightly scented, dense lavender-purple flower racemes to about 30cm long, are produced late in summer, followed by shiny brown seed heads

Vigorous, deciduous, twining climber 9m or more in height with dark green leaves divided into leaflets, emerging coppery-bronze in spring. Lightly scented, pea-like, pale blue-mauve flowers with curled petals are produced on trusses about 30cm long, before the leaves open, and may be followed by bean-like, velvety fawn-grey seed pods 15cm long

The flowers can be up to 15cm (6in) across ifthe plants are disbudded leaving the central bud per stem, to go on to flower. They are long lasting in water and the plants are ideal to grow for cutting or exhibiting. The plants are best heavily mulched over winter, or lifted after flowering and kept in cold, but frost-free conditions until spring.

A mat-forming perennial to 10cm high with lobed leaves forming rosettes of evergreen foliage and small, white, star-shaped flowers held on short stems above the foliage in spring

description: A compact, deciduous shrub to 60cm high, with dense foliage of small, blue-green leaves with a hint of dark burgundy red, turning to a richer red in the autumn. Colour is dependent on light levels. Clusters of small, white flowers appear in late spring to summer. Makes a great low hedge

alternative_names: Bulgarian honey garlic|Allium dioscoridis|Nectaroscordum meliophilum|Nectaroscordum siculum subsp. bulgaricum|Allium siculum subsp. bulgaricum|Allium meliophilum|Allium bulgaricum
description: An upright bulbous perennial to 1.2m tall, with narrow keeled leaves to 40cm long, and umbels of nodding green-tinged cream flowers with purple markings, in early summer, followed by erect seed capsules

alternative_names: Chinese bean tree|Catalpa sutchuensis|Catalpa duclouxii|Catalpa fargesii f. duclouxii
description: A good flowering form bearing panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers of pale pink, with brown and orange-spotted throats. These are followed by narrow bean-like seed pods. Large, simple, pointed leaves are tinged bronze in spring. Matures to a round-crowned tree up to 8m in height

An upright, clump-forming, slow-growing evergreen houseplant to around 60cm in height, with variegated, camouflage-like patterned foliage in shades of dark and pale green and soft cream. Easy to grow in a bright area of the house, away from cold draughts

An evergreen self-clinging climber, with slender stems that can reach to 4m long or more if not pruned. Leaves are oval, heart-shaped at the base, and glossy bright green, with yellow-green new growth
A large deciduous shrub. Leaves maple-like with 3 or 5 serrate lobes. Flowers saucer-shaped, 8cm in width, pure white, in early summer
A large deciduous shrub with maple-like leaves with 3-5 toothed lobes. Flowers saucer-shaped, light mauve, 8cm in width

A soft-wooded deciduous shrub, vigorous and fast-growing, to 5-6m. Leaves are lobed, maple-like and hairy. Flowers are borne 3-4 together at the ends of woolly stalks, each flower to 7.5cm across, with rather silky, usually mauve, flowers with prominent bosses of orange stamens. Floriferous and long-flowering. Several named colour selections are available

A vigorous, evergreen, open tropical shrub or small tree with an open habit, best suited to a conservatory or greenhouse, with heart-shaped, toothed dark green foliage. Long, trumpet-shaped apricot orange to salmon pink highly fragrant flowers, more intensely fragrant at night, appear from June through to October
A vigorous large, more-or-less deciduous shrub with slender-pointed maple-like leaves and bowl-shaped, deep mauve flowers 6cm wide in late spring and summer
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with mid-green, small oval fragrant leaves and white lipped flowers from summer to autumn.

A compact, evergreen shrub to around 1m in height, with small, oval-shaped dark green leaves. Long-lasting trusses of funnel-shaped purple flowers emerge from attractive pink buds in the spring. Great for borders or pots and containers

A vigorous evergreen shrub with an open habit and long, almost lance-shaped dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Produces large, semi-double, peony-form pink flowers, sometimes with pale pink streaks, in spring

alternative_names: Brugmansia sanguinea subsp. vulcanicola|Brugmansia sanguinea subsp. sanguinea var. flava|Brugmansia sanguinea subsp. sanguinea 'Flava'

description: A Viridiflora Group tulip about 40-50cm tall, with strong upright stems bearing single, creamy-white flowers, the petals mottled and streaked with lime green, and produced in late spring

A low-growing, clump-forming deciduous, rhizomatous perennial with large, heart-shaped silver foliage with green veining. Panicles of small, blue flowers with white edges appear in spring. Ideal ground cover for shady areas
A climber to 2m tall producing an abundance of pale purple double flowers from spring into early summer and a second flush of usually single flowers in late summer to early autumn

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing pure white blooms between July and October with a central orange cone surrounded by narrow, toothed ray petals. Excellent as a cut flower

An attractive, upright, perennial coneflower variety growing to 70cm tall and producing magenta-pink blooms from July to October. Flowers have a prominent central orange cone surrounded by narrow, bright pink ray petals. Excellent as a cut flower
A clump-forming perennial, to around 60cm high, with aromatic, dark green leaves. Pale lavender blue flowers, framed by dark purple bracts, are produced from mid to late summer

A clump-forming, deciduous, bulbous herbaceous perennial with glossy green strap-like leaves. Clusters of loose, purple bell-shaped flowers, green inside, open from the bottom up and appear on tall, upright spikes in the spring. An unusual colour combination. Seedheads provide interest over winter

A clump-forming, deciduous, bulbous herbaceous perennial with glossy green strap-like leaves. Clusters of shiny, dark orange-red bell-shaped flowers which open from the bottom up, appear on tall, upright spikes in the spring. Seedheads provide interest over winter

A bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with upright stems, woody at the base, and large, dark green foliage. Large, bright pink flowers with a red eye and white edges appear from July through to September

A bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with upright stems, woody at the base, and large, dark green foliage. Large hot pink flowers with wavy yellow edges and a maroon-red eye appear from July through to September

An upright perennial sometimes grown as an annual, reaching up to 80cm high in flower, with lance-shaped, dark green leaves forming a mound at the base. Upright spikes bearing outward-facing, bell-shaped flowers, rich orange on the outside and paler yellow-orange in the throats, are produced over a long season from late spring to late summer

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing fleshy rosettes to 12.5cm across, the spoon-shaped dark burgundy-red leaves tipped and edged grey-green, the colours changing in shape and intensity through the seasons. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A mat-forming, evergreen succulent producing neat, fleshy rosettes to 3.5cm across, with small, cobwebbed, pale yellow-green leaves, tipped orange-red in summer then flushed pale red in autumn and winter. Tall spikes of starry pale pink flowers produced from mature rosettes, die off after flowering in summer and are replaced by new offsets

A trailing houseplant with large, heart-shaped, glossy green and golden-yellow variegated leaves. May produce spathes of green-white flowers when mature. Leaves can grow to very long lengths making it ideal in a hanging basket or on a shelf. A great plant for using en mass as a living curtain and also as an air purifier

A bushy perennial, to around 70cm high, with strong stems and divided, dark green leaves. Fragrant, semi-double flowers, with salmon pink outer petals and rose pink centres, are produced in late spring and early summer

A bushy perennial, to around 1m high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Large, deep rose pink flowers, with notched petals and darker pink flares at the base, are produced in late spring and early summer

A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated green foliage and white margins. Tall, upright red stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer. A reverse sport of H. 'Raspberry Sundae'
An evergreen shrub with narrow, deep green leaves and long-stalked, lantern-like white flowers borne along the branches from late spring into summer

A clump-forming perennial to 50cm high forming a mound of semi-evergreen, hairy, lobed and toothed leaves. Bright red to dark orange, saucer-shaped, semi-double flowers are held above the foliage on slender stems, flowering over a long period from late spring into early autumn

A compact mound-forming perennial to 20cm high and 45cm wide, with fleshy, variegated ruby-red leaves with pink margins and flat terminal clusters of rose-pink starry flowers in late summer to early autumn

Compact evergreen shrub about 1m in height and 60cm wide, with dark young stems and small, grey-green, wavy-margined, glossy leaves with a creamy-white edge, aging to mottled green tinted pink then crimson in winter. Small, honey-scented, bell-shaped dark purple flowers are produced in clusters, from early summer

A clump-forming, deciduous, bulbous herbaceous perennial with glossy green strap-like leaves. Clusters of shiny, pale yellow bell-shaped flowers which open from the bottom up, appear on tall, dark, upright spikes in the spring, providing an eye-catching contrast. Seedheads provide interest over winter

A clump-forming, deciduous, bulbous herbaceous perennial with glossy green strap-like leaves. Clusters of shiny, bright orange bell-shaped flowers which open from the bottom up, appear on tall, upright spikes in the spring. Seedheads provide interest over winter

primary_name: Ipomoea batatas [Sweet Caroline Sweetheart Jet Black] ('Ncornsp-021shjb') (Sweet Caroline Series)

description: A clump-forming herbaceous perennial with dark green, toothed, lance shaped leaves. Semi-double, slightly frilly, white flowers with yellow centres, flowering for a long period in the summer if dead-headed regularly.

An easy-to-grow, evergreen azalea to around 60cm in height, forming a neat mound of soft green foliage. Large, star-shaped white flowers, with very pale pink lines through the petals and darker anthers, appear in May. Great in containers, borders and rockeries but potentially a little too tender to grow in very cold gardens

alternative_names: Camassia leichtlinii 'Pale Pink'|Camassia leichtlinii pale pink-flowered
description: A deciduous, clump-forming perennial bulb to around 80cm in height, with long, narrow, upright green foliage. Tall spikes of compact, pale pink, star-shaped flowers appear from late spring into early summer

A compact, colourful, hardy annual variety producing unusual, upright, bi-colour blooms from gold to pale orange, set against dark green foliage. Perfect for container growing or planting along the border edge

A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy subshrub with dark green foliage and vibrant pink-fuchsia lipped flowers with a white throat which have a near black calyx with dark stems from summer through to autumn.

Stately, fast-growing, upright, deciduous tree, eventually growing to about 30m tall, with oval mid to dark green leaves that turn golden-yellow in autumn. Insignificant reddish-brown flowers are followed by brown winged fruits. Significant resistance to Dutch elm disease

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark green leaves. Large, lavender-pink, double flowers, fading to creamy white towards the centres, appear from summer through to autumn

alternative_names: stork's bill 'Joe Elliott'|stork's bill 'Album'|Erodium × variabile 'Album'|Erodium balearicum
description: A compact, spreading or cushion-forming, perennial to 10cm tall, with mid-green, oval, slightly-lobed leaves and white flowers, with pink veins, that are produced from late spring throughout the summer

A bushy, deciduous perennial reaching a height of around 120cm, with dark green leaves. Baby-pink bell-shaped flowers with paler edges and contrasting yellow stamens appear from June through to September. Ideal for pots or at the front of a herbaceous border

A dwarf, bushy, deciduous perennial reaching a height of just 40cm, with dark green leaves. Fragrant, white, bell-shaped flowers appear from late May through to September. Ideal for pots or at the front of a herbaceous border

A climber to 2m tall with nodding, tubular flowers to 4cm long comprising 4 tepals fused along their length with tips free and curving outwards Flowers are lilac-purple at the base and creamy-white at the tips and are followed by persistent seedheads
A climber reaching up to 2m tall. Bell-shaped, nodding, deeply-ridged purple flowers with creamy-white margins are borne in summer and followed by persistent seedheads
A spring-flowering, evergreen perennial to about 50cm tall. New foliage emerges reddish-purple in colour and wiry, black stems bear hanging, spurred white-yellow flowers
Deciduous climber, a sport of 'Hagley Hybrid', to about 2-3m tall, with mid-green leaves and large double, fully-petalled shell pink flowers to 15cm across, blooming from early summer to autumn

A deciduous climber, to around 1.5m high, with oval-shaped, deep green leaves. Large, semi-double pure white flowers are produced in late spring and early summer, with a second flush of single flowers later in summer
A semi-evergreen, upright, bushy perennial with aromatic green foliage and creamy-white lipped flowers faintly tinted pink held on purple stems and calyces from summer through to autumn.

A compact and bushy, upright herbaceous perennial with aromatic, marbled dark green and cream, lance-shaped leaves and slender whorled spikes of tubular two-lipped blue-purple flowers which are very attractive to pollinators all through summer to autumn

primary_name: Anemone hupehensis [Little Summer Breeze] ('Anem081') (Little Breeze Series)
alternative_names: Japanese windflower [Emmy Pink Blush]|Anemone hupehensis 'Anem081'|Anemone hupehensis [Little Breeze Kiss]
description: An upright, suckering, deciduous perennial with oval-shaped, toothed dark green leaves. Dark pink flowers with yellow centres appear from late summer through to autumn

alternative_names: Japanese windflower [Summer Breeze]|Anemone [Little Breeze Pink]|Anemone hupehensis 'Anem080'
description: An upright, suckering, deciduous perennial with oval-shaped, toothed dark green leaves. Large, pink flowers with yellow centres appear from late summer through to autumn

primary_name: Aquilegia [Spring Magic Light Red and Yellow] (Spring Magic Series)

description: A highly attractive, compact, upright, perennial coneflower variety producing stunning pink-white blooms in Summer with a central maroon cone surrounded by large, narrow ray petals. Excellent in a border or as a cut flower
A compact plant to around 45cm tall bearing pure white flowers above the mounded foliage in summer

A species of fast-growing, tender annual to around 2.4m in height, with large, oval-shaped, pale green foliage. Sprays of narrow, trumpet-shaped red flowers, fragrant in the evening, appear from summer through to the autumn

A compact, mat-forming, half-hardy, evergreen perennial up to 25cm in height with linear to lance-shaped, sometimes toothed, green leaves and, daisy-like flower heads, outer petals whitish pink, pink-veined with a deep purple centre, from early summer into autumn

primary_name: Phlox paniculata [Early Purple Pink Eye] (Early Series)

description: A rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with succulent, pointed leaves. In spring and autumn the leaves are golden green with dark red edges; in summer they turn lime green all over and in winter they become dark red. Starry pink flowers are held in clusters on leafy stems to 15cm tall in summer. The rosettes die after flowering but are replaced by offsets on lateral runners
An deciduous herbaceous perennial. Medium green strap shaped leaves. Sturdy erect purple stems bearing rounded umbels of trumpet shaped flowers

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and rounded heads of tubular, dark purple-black buds and flowers from mid-summer to autumn.

A compact, deciduous, upright tree about 2-2.4m tall, with leathery, palmate, deeply 5-lobed leaves, bright vibrant red in spring, dark green flushed burgundy-red in summer, turning fiery red in autumn

A compact, evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves with serrated edges. Masses of delicate, fragrant, pale blush pink flowers appear from late winter until early spring. An ideal variety for growing in a container near a doorway, entrance or on a patio to appreciate the fragrance

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a spreading habit and pointed, oval-shaped, dark green foliage turning to shades of red and purple in the autumn. Large pink flowers appear early to mid-summer, darkening as they age, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a spreading habit and pointed, oval-shaped, dark green foliage turning to shades of red and purple in the autumn. Small white to pink flowers appear early to mid-summer, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn

A deciduous small tree or large shrub with a spreading habit and pointed, oval-shaped, dark green foliage turning to shades of crimson red in late summer which become gradually more intense towards the autumn. Small white flowers (bracts) appear in early to mid-summer, followed by strawberry-like pink berries in the autumn

A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 30cm in height with small, semi-trailing, dark green leaves. Pale pink flowers with darker centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn
A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 30cm in height with small, semi-trailing, dark green leaves. Dark red flowers appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

A dense, upright, spreading, semi-evergreen perennial to around 30cm in height with small, semi-trailing, oval dark green leaves. Bright white flowers with yellow centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

A beautiful, upright, deciduous shrub with dark green foliage and a profusion of pure white, heavily fragrant, single blooms appearing in clusters in early summer. One of the most aromatic varieties available and one that which tolerates poor air conditions and cold temperatures

A small, spreading, deciduous tree or shrub to 4m tall with leaves divided into ovate leaflets with serrate edges that turn shades of red, orange and yellow in autumn. Clusters of pinkish-white flowers in spring are followed in late summer and autumn by edible, dark reddish-purple berries

An upright, bushy rose about 75cm tall, with healthy, semi-glossy dark green leathery foliage, and fragrant shapely, fully double blooms produced singly or in well-spaced clusters. The unusual flower colour has been described as coffee mocha or light chocolate-caramel. Repeat-flowering from early summer to autumn

A compact, bushy floribunda rose up to 75cm in height, with dark green foliage. Large, fragrant, peony-like flowers are a blend of creamy-white to dark mauve in the centre and repeat-flower from May through to October

A large-sized, epiphytic, evergreen orchid with upright, cane-like pseudobulbs up to 120cm tall. Six or seven, green, leathery leaves are alternately arranged on the upper half of each pseudobulb, lasting two or more seasons. Each lance-shaped leaf is up to 40cm long and 4cm wide. Upright flowering stems measuring up to 85cm emerge from the upper nodes of mature, leafed or leafless canes and carry many sparsely-spaced, 2-3cm large, pale yellow flowers.

A clump-forming herbaceous perennial, to around 70cm high, with an upright habit and lobed green leaves. Tall, branching stems bear near-white flowers with a halo of purple veins at the base, flushing pink as they mature in late spring to early summer

A tropical, epiphytic orchid with upright, cane-like stems growing from a short creeping rhizome. Spindle-shaped stems are broader in upper half and serve as a storage of water and nutrients. Fleshy, evergreen leaves are carried at the top of each stem and last for a couple of seasons. The leaves are firm, leathery, oval-shaped, up to 15cm long and 3cm wide. Large showy flowers are held on short terminal stems, arising from the tips of new mature growth throughout the year. Emerging flower buds are wrapped in two oval, papery sheaths. Each flower measures up to 10cm across. Flowers may vary in colour in range of pinks, occassionally with darker spots and pink/purple and white/yellow lip

A clump-forming perennial, to around 60cm high in flower, forming a dense mound of lobed and toothed green leaves. Long flowering, with semi-double flowers, in rich shades of coral pink, borne on slender stems above the foliage from late spring to late summer

A medium to large-sized, evergreen orchid with linear, 90cm long and up to 3cm wide, leathery leaves. Egg shaped pseudobulbs are covered with wider, leaf-bearing, basal sheaths. Arching flowering stems emerge from the base of young mature pseudobulbs in late winter and spring. Each stem is up to 70cm long, carrying ten large, long-lasting flowers. Each flower measures up to 11cm across. Colour of flowers varies depending on cultivar; from pale yellow, green or pink, with darker markings of the lip

A medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with linear or narrowly-oval leaves. Each leathery leaf is 50cm long and 2cm wide. In late winter and spring an upright flowering stem carrying densely arranged flowers appears. The flowers are waxy, up to 6cm large, cream, pale yellow or pale pink. The colour depends on the name of the cultivar

primary_name: Angelica archangelica subsp. decurrens from Kazakhstan

alternative_names: Crocus sieberi subsp. sublimis 'Michael Hoogs Memory'

description: A compact, upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial to 60cm in height, with green divided foliage. Strong, upright stems produce dense spires of cobalt-blue flowers with purplish blotches from June to August
A compact, bushy perennial with aromatic mid-green foliage. Erect flower stems of sky-blue flowers appear from summer through to the autumn

A half-hardy, bushy deciduous perennial with a neat and compact habit and dark green foliage. Clouds of sweetly-fragranced burgundy red and creamy yellow flowers with burnt orange centres appear from summer through until the autumn

A low-growing evergreen perennial, forming dense mats of slender stems that root at the the nodes, with fine, linear, bright lime green leaves held in pairs along the stems. Tiny white flowers are held up on stems to 4cm high in summer

A compact, evergreen perennial forming a clump of large, dark green, glossy leaves with attractive, white, bell shaped flowers, with dark pink-red calyces, held atop tall stems in spring. Plant in a sunny position for optimal flowering and leaf colour
A vigorous bushy perennial, to around 80cm high, with strong stems and divided, deep green leaves. Single, dark reddish-purple flowers are produced in late spring and early summer

primary_name: Capsicum annuum var. annuum Longum Group early jalapeño
description: A Jalapeno chilli pepper producing medium hot, elliptical shaped fruits, up to 7.5cm long, maturing from green to red. The fruit is noted for ripening two weeks earlier than other Jalapeno peppers and can be harvested July to October

A strong, clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial to around 100cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves and long stems. Salmon-pink flowers with slightly twisted petals, pink tips and a subtle yellow base, appear from summer through until the first frosts

A tall, tuberous-rooted perennial to about 1.2m, with mid-green foliage. Very large, ruffled flowers, around 27cm across, have long, slightly twisted petals in pale pink streaked with darker pink, and are produced from mid-summer until the first frost

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 120cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Bright, golden yellow double flowers with an orange blush appear on dark stems from summer through until the first frosts

A tall, bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Large, rounded purple-pink flowers, with creamy-yellow at the base of the petals, appear on upright stems from summer through until autumn

A tuberous perennial to 30cm with long-stalked, deeply lobed, mid-green foliage. In late spring and early summer, upright, branching stems bear fully double flowers with many rows of satiny petals, each bloom having a different mix of gold, coffee, bronze, dark red or dusky pink shades
A Triumph Group tulip about 40cm tall, with single cup-shaped flowers of a velvety deep purple, white-flushed at the base, and produced from mid to late spring
A Double Early Group tulip about 40cm tall, with large, fully double flowers of rich carmine-purple, flowering very early, in mid March/April

Compact, bushy, evergreen shrub, to about 3m tall, with glossy, dark green leaves. Bowl-shaped, lightly-scented flowers are creamy-white, opening from greenish buds, in mid-spring to early summer and intermittently through to autumn

A compact, erect deciduous shrub or neat upright small tree to 4m in height, of compact habit, with oval, green-bronze leaves when young which turn shades of orange and red in autumn. Clusters of small, star-shaped white flowers are produced quite early in spring followed by edible but quite tasteless dark purple to black berries that the birds will love in autumn
An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves with serrated edges. Single, fragrant white flowers appear from October throught to January

A palm-like shrub or small tree, with a freely clumping habit and colourful, upright to arching, strap-shaped leaves with dark purple-brown centres, bright green margins and orange midribs. In late spring and early summer, mature plants produce a mass of tiny creamy-white flowers

A mix of biennial or short-lived perennials usually grown as annuals, to around 60cm high, with oval-shaped, bristly green leaves. Double and semi-double flowers, in soft shades of yellow, burnt orange, peach and dark pink, are borne on leafy, upright stems from late summer into autumn
An Asiatic lily up to 75cm tall producing outward-facing, pollen-free flowers with velvety, pale yellow-cream reflexed petals from early to mid-summer

primary_name: Salix lapponum from Glen Lochay, Scotland
Salix lapponum from Glen Doll, Scotland
Paeonia rockii from Tai Bai Shan, China

description: A bushy, spreading evergreen sub-shrub or woody-based perennial, with aromatic, wrinkled grey-green leaves finely edged with cream. Spikes of light purple flowers are produced in early summer

A large, slow-growing perennial cactus, up to 2m high at maturity, with upright green stems to 10cm thick, branching from the base. Stems have up to 27 ribs, and areoles producing clusters of pale yellow spines. On mature plants, funnel-shaped white or pale yellow flowers are preceded by a profusion of fine red hairs growing from the flowering side of the plant

alternative_names: Jordan's rosemary|Algerian rosemary|Rosmarinus eriocalyx var. pallescens|Rosmarinus eriocalyx
description: An aromatic evergreen shrub native of Spain and North Africa. Has a dense habit with deep-green linear leaves and two-lipped flowers, deep violet-pink on the upper lip and lavender-blue on the lower lip in spring and summer.
A clump-forming, bulbous perennial to around 50cm in height, with lance-shaped, grey-green foliage. Glossy, dark maroon-purple to almost black flowers appear on tall stems in May

A compact, perennial bulb to around 25cm with broadly lance-shaped dark green foliage and double, bowl-shaped cherry-red flowers appearing in April. Ideal for pots and containers or bedding in windy parts of the garden

primary_name: Tulipa 'Duc van Tol Red and White' (1)

description: A perennial bulb to around 55cm in height, with broadly lance-shaped green leaves and strong stems. Large, goblet-shaped, fiery orange flowers with subtle hints of pink, red and yellow, appear from April to May
A dwarf bulbous perennial to 40cm with green foliage and purple flowers, pink at the edges, which open in the sun and appear in March to April
A bulbous perennial to 45cm with dark green foliage and goblet-shaped soft burgundy-red flowers, creamy-yellow at the base, appearing from late April to early May
A Double Late Group tulip about 25-30cm tall, often with several buds per bulb. Fully double, peony-like flowers open violet-mauve with pale green streaks on the outer petals, flowering in April/May

A trailing, tropical evergreen about 60cm tall, with dense, glossy, leathery, rich green, lance-shaped leaves, and from summer to autumn it bears terminal clusters of flared, tubular bright red flowers
A tropical evergreen perennial, to around 50cm high, with upright stems bearing lance-shaped green leaves marbled with pale silvery green on the upper surface

A tender, epiphytic, evergreen perennial about 50cm tall, with glossy, bronze-flushed, dark green, arrow-shaped, leaves to 50cm long, on tall leaf-stalks, and glossy, heart-shaped, bright, orange-red spathe flowers with yellow spike-like spadices, produced through the year

A tender, evergreen epiphytic perennial about 50cm tall, with glossy dark green, arrow-shaped, leaves to 50cm long, on tall leaf-stalks, and glossy, heart-shaped, creamy-white spathe flowers with a toucn of green, with yellow spike-like spadices, produced through the year

A compact, slowly spreading, mounded, mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, sometimes toothed, grey-green leaves. Four-petalled flowers in shades of purple are produced in short spikes from early or mid-spring

A bushy, woody-based deciduous perennial to 1.2m tall, with upright white stems bearing finely divided aromatic, grey-green leaves to 5cm long, and long terminal panicles of tiny blue flowers in late summer and early autumn
A deciduous climber, to around 3m high, with mid-green leaves. Large, violet blue flowers, with a narrow streak of white in the centre of the petals, are produced in late spring and early summer
A compact, half-hardy perennial to around 60cm in height, with silvery-grey, aromatic foliage. Upright spikes of lavender-blue flowers appear from August to September
A deciduous, upright, bushy perennial which has grey-green aromatic foliage with long, silvery spikes holding clusters of very small violet-blue flowers in summer.

alternative_names: perovskia 'Little Spire'|sage 'Little Spire'|Salvia yangii 'Little Spire'|Perovskia atriplicifolia 'Little Spire'
description: A compact, erect, deciduous sub-shrub, with white stems, to 60cm in height. It bears aromatic, deeply-divided, grey-green leaves and open, upright panicles of small violet-blue flowers in late summer to early autumn

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 90cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Greenish-yellow buds open to large red flowers which fade to a warmer tone as they mature; appearing from July through to October

A bushy, clump-forming robust and vigorous tuberous perennial to around 100cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Bright pink flowers with plum-purple hues, appear on dark purple-black stems from summer through until the first frosts

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid hybrid; with long, cane-like, fleshy, green pseudobulbs. Four to six dark green, leathery leaves are alternately arranged on the upper half or near the top of each pseudobulb. Each lance-shaped leaf is 8-14cm long and 3cm wide. Upright flowering stems up to 30cm long emerge from the nodes along the mature canes and bear 12 to 15 flowers opening in succession. Each flower is 6.5-7cm across, dark pink-fuchsia with a white throat.

A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 25cm in height with small, semi-trailing, oval mid-green leaves. Large, soft, pale pink flowers with darker centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn

A dense, compact, semi-evergreen perennial to around 20cm in height with small, semi-trailing, oval pale green leaves. Bright white flowers with a touch of blush pink towards the centres appear on wiry stems from summer to early autumn
An erect, slow-growing tree to 2m tall, with cane-like stems and narrow, strap-shaped, red-flushed leaves emerging in tufts from the tops of the stems

A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub to 80cm high, with a rounded habit and broadly ovate, dark green to bronze leaves with toothed edges. A large-sized, evergreen orchid with linear, dark green leaves up to 90cm long and 2cm wide. Ovoid pseudobulbs covered with basal leaf sheaths carry six to ten leaves. The orchid flowers in early spring on upright or arching stems up to 100cm tall, carrying up to 30 flowers. The flowers are white, pale pink or cream, depending on cultivar, each measuring 7-9cm across. Perhaps the most famous cultivar 'Westonbirt' with large pure white flowers and with pink markings on the lip was originally registered in 1911. It is the first orchid hybrid which was identified a tetraploid - carrying four (instead of two) sets of chromosomes, which set a start to a very successfull history of breeding.

A large-sized evergreen orchid, producing a clump of ovoid, up to 10cm long pseudobulbs. The pseudobulbs are covered with leaf bases, each carrying 7 to 9, semi-rigid, linear leaves 50-90cm long and 1.5-4cm wide. Pendant flowerings stems up to 75cm long, carrying 10-30 flowers emerge from the base on young pseudobulbs in summer. Flowers are approximately 4cm large, with dark maroon petals and sepals and white lip with burgundy-purple spots and yellow ridge in the centre.

A medium to large-sized, evergreen epiphytic orchid with linear, 80cm long and 2cm wide, leathery leaves. In late winter and early spring, arching flowering stems bearing ten or more flowers emerge from the base of previous-year's mature pseudobulbs. The flowers are large, waxy and long-lasting. Each flower measures approximately 8-10cm across. Petals and sepals are bright yellowish-green, lip is white with dark red markings along the bottom edge

A medium to large-sized, evergreen epihytic orchid, producing a clump of egg-shaped pseudobulbs, enclosed in six to ten, leaf-bearing sheaths. The leaves are linear, dark-green and leathery, 60-80cm long and 1.5-3cm wide. Upright and arching flowering stems emerge from the base of mature pseudobulbs in late winter and spring. Each flowering stem measures up to 80cm, and carries up to 20 flowers. The flowers are star-shaped, cream, pale yellow or pale green, waxy and long-lasting

primary_name: Cymbidium Flamingo gx 'Memoria Sir George Holford'

description: A medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with linear, dark-green, leathery leaves up to approximately 60-80cm long and 1.5-2cm wide. Upright or arching flowering stems emerge from the base of new mature pseudobulbs in late winter and spring and carry ten or more, 6cm large flowers. Waxy, long-lasting flowers are white and pale pink, with darker pink in the middle of petals and sepals. The lip has characteristic yellow crest and dark red markings in the lower half

A medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with linear or narrowly-oval leaves. Each leaf is semi-rigid, leathery, approximately 60-80cm long and 1.5-2cm wide. Upright or arching flowering stems emerge in late winter and early spring from base of new, mature pseudobulbs. Each stem measures 50-90cm and carries ten or more, 6-8cm large flowers. The flowers are pale pink, waxy and long-lasting. The lip has characteristic yellow crest and dark red markings in lower half

description: A medium to large-sized, evergreen epiphytic orchid producing a clump of egg-shaped pseudobulbs, enclosed with 11 to 14 basal, leaf-bearing sheaths. Leaves are approximately 40cm long and 1-2cm wide. The plant flowers on erect stems, 20-30cm long, carrying two to three flowers in spring to summer. The flowers are fragrant, white with dark red markings on the lip.

primary_name: Cymbidium Ruanda gx 'Queen of the Pinks'

description: A medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid producing a clump of egg-shaped pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulbs is covered with wider, basal leaf-bearing sheaths, carrying 9 to 15, linear, lance-shaped leaves up to 90cm long and 2-3cm wide. Flowering stems appear from the base of young, mature pseudobulbs in winter and spring and reach up to 50cm tall. Upright, arching stems carry 3 to 15 flowers. The flowers are fragrant, white with a dark maroon marking and yellow, crested lip

description: A medium-sized, lithophytic orchid with long, upright or pendulous cane-like stems up to 90cm long. Deciduous, bright green, oval-shaped leaves, measuring 8-10cm are alternately arranged along the stems. Leaves usually drop off before the flowers appear, but sometimes they remain on the plant for longer than one season. Pendulous flowering stems up to 15cm long emerge from the upper nodes of leafless canes and carry 15-20 fragrant, long-lasting flowers. Each flower measures approximately 3cm across. Petals and sepals are pure white, with amethyst-coloured lip, from which the plant gets its name.

primary_name: Dendrobium Gatton Monarch gx 'F. J. Hanbury'

description: A miniature, epiphytic, tropical orchid with 5-13cm long, flat stems. 4-7cm long leaves are arranged near the top of the stems. Arching flowering stems 1cm short, emerge from the tips of mature, leafed or leafless stems and carry two to four (occasionaly up to 6) flowers. Flowers vary in colour from yellow, or white to pinkish. Each flower measures approximately 2cm.
A large-sized, tropical epiphytic orchid with cane-like upright stems up to 100cm long.

A small-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid. Upright, clump-forming stems (pseudobulbs) are spindle-shaped, up to 10cm long and bears one leathery, dark-green, 7-8cm long leaf. Pendant flowering stems 15-20cm long emerge from the nodes of leafed or leafless stems and carry 5 to 15, well-spaced, fragrant flowers. Each flower is 2.5-5cm large, bright yellow, usually with darker yellow or orange centre.

primary_name: Dendrobium Miss Florence E. King gx

description: A medium to large-sized, epiphytic orchid with long, cane-like stems. Glossy, alternate leaves are 5-8cm long. Two to four fragrant flowers 6-7cm large are carried on short flowering stems, emerging from nodes on mature, leaf-bearing or leaf-less canes. Flowers are white with pale pink edges and dark maroon centre.

A medium to large-sized, epiphytic orchid with upright, cane-like stems up to 80cm long. Each stem (pseudobulb) is covered with alternate, thin, leaf-bearing sheaths. Leaves dark green, are oval shaped, 5cm long. Flowering stems emerge from the upper nodes and tips of mature pseudobulbs and carry two to four, white, long-lasting flowers. Each flower is 7-10cm large, with white petals and sepals. The lip is white with bright green throat and contrasting dark maroon stripes.

description: An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing a clump of small, oval-shaped, 9cm long and 1-3cm wide pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb carries a single, 10-40cm long and 1-5cm wide leaf. Leaves are variable, linear or elliptic, rounded apically. In autumn and winter, flowering stems emerge from the axils of sheaths covering mature pseudobulbs. Each stem up may be 7-30cm long and carries single, yellow and brown, fragrant flowers. Each flower is 4-9cm large with darker, often almost black lip. Mature plants grown in optimal conditions often produce large numbers of flowering stems, flowering simultaneously.

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing a clump of oval-shaped, slightly flattened pseudobulbs, each measuring approximately 4cm in diameter. Each pseudobulb is covered in several sheaths and carries one, 20-50cm long, linear, leathery leaf. Flowering stems emerge from the axils of sheaths and pseudobulbs throughout the year. Each 15-20cm long stem carries a single, 8cm large, white flower with yellow lip

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing a clump of small, oval-shaped, 2-3cm tall pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb carries one, up to 50cm long and 0.5cm wide, linear leaf. In late winter and spring, flowers emerge from the base of the new pseudobulbs. Each 2cm large flower is carried on a 1.5cm short stem. Waxy, long-lasting flowers vary in colour - from yellow-brown and red to dark maroon

An epiphytic, evergreen orchid producing a clump of 2cm small, oval-shaped pseudobulbs growing from a long, upright or pendulous rhizome, completely covered in thin sheaths. Each pseudobulb carries one, 25cm long a 0.5cm wide, linear, grassy leaf. Free-flowering throughout the year, flowering stems emerge from the base of mature pseudobulbs. Each 1cm short stem carries a single, brown-red flower with wine-red lip with white tip. Flowers are fragrant, measuring 1.5 -2.5cm across

A medium to large-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid producing a clump of oval to elliptic pseudobulbs. Each pseudobulb is covered in thin sheaths and carries one, 25-30cm long and 3-4cm wide, leathery, elliptic leaf. In summer, flowering stems emerge from the base of the maturing pseudobulbs. Each 10-15cm long stem carries single, up to 20cm large, attractive, scented flower. Petals and sepals are thin, curved, forward-facing, bright yellow, white at the base with dark brown markings

description: A medium-sized, epiphytic orchid with upright, 15-30cm long, evergreen leaves. New growth appears from the base of the swollen stem - pseudobulb. Each pseudobulb is a storage organ for water and nutrients. They are egg-shaped, slightly flattened and partially covered by one or two pairs of green, leafed sheaths. The plant typically flowers in winter, spring or autumn on up to 45cm long, upright or arching stems. New flowering stems arise from the axils of young, mature pseudobulbs and the leafed sheaths. Each stem carries 8 to 20 white, star-shaped flowers, often with dark burgundy red spots and toothed edges. Each flower measures 5-10cm across.

primary_name: Oncidium Gold Coin Butte gx 'Gay Dancers'

description: A small to medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid with upright, 20-40cm long, linear leaves. New growth appears from the base of swollen stem (pseudobulb). The pseudobulbs are egg-shaped, 3-8cm long and 3-5cm wide, compressed at the top, each carrying two or more leaves. The plant typically flowers in autumn and winter on pendulous, often branched, 15-60cm long stems. New flowering stems arise from the axils of leafed sheaths, wrapped around young, mature pseudobulbs. Flowers are up to 2cm large, white or pale cream and sweetly scented. Large, mature plants are able to produce numerous flowering stems for an impressive display.

Paphiopedilum Alma Gevaert gx 'Mme. Maurice Mertens'

description: A compact, small-sized, semi-terrestrial orchid with rigid, leathery leaves. Elliptic leaves are mottled green and grey, up to 15cm long and 5cm wide. Solitary, almost stem-less flowers are produced in spring. The flowers are up to 9cm large, almost rounded. Petals and dorsal sepal are larger compared to the size of pouch, white or pale cream, covered with dark brown-red spots.

primary_name: Paphiopedilum Bordeaux de Valec gx 'La Tuilerie'

description: A small to medium-sized, semi-terrestrial, evergreen orchid producing rosettes of rigid, leathery leaves. The leaves are strap-shaped to elliptic, up to 25cm long and 5cm wide, greyish green with dark green mottling. Maroon and green flowers, 7-9cm across appear in spring on 20-40cm long, terminal stems. Petals and sepals are white, with green and maroon stripes and a glossy, maroon pouch.
