description: A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with dark green, mottled, narrow, elliptic leaves, 20-30cm long. Solitary flowers, 7-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 15 -30cm long, upright stems. The flowers of this primary hybrid are large compared to size of the plant; white or pale green, with hairy edges, covered in a dark, veined pattern.

A dwarf, clump-forming, semi-terrestrial evergreen orchid. Leaves are matt, dark green, up to 25cm long and 2-3cm wide. Solitary flowers, 9-10cm across appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 15-25cm long, upright stems. The pouch (or slipper) is a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. The lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. White petals with lime-green stripes are twisted, with wavy, hairy purple edge. Dorsal sepal is white with dark green and purple pattern.

A semi-terrestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with narrow elliptic leaves, dark green mottled with light green. This primary hybrid flowers with two or more attractive flowers on 30-60cm long stems that emerge from the centre of the leaf rosettes. Flowering stem and flower buds are dark, covered with tiny brown hair. Large flowers can measure 10 or more centimetres. The pouch is medium or dark pink. Petals and dorsal sepal are pale cream with an oustanding mosaic pattern with dark pink stripes.

A small, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with 4 to 6 dark green mottled leaves up to 14cm long. Upright flowering stems emerge from the centre of the leaf rosette and carry one or two flowers. Each white flower is approximately 6cm diameter with dark brown spotted markings. The pouch (modified lip) is white or pale cream, sometimes with dark spots. The petals are large and rounded, giving the flower its characteristic appearance.

A small-sized, clump-forming, evergreen orchid species with narrowly oval, tesselated leaves up to 23cm long and 5cm wide. Solitary flowers, 10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 20-30 cm long, upright stems. The pouch (or slipper) i s a modification of the lip that traps insects and consequently provides an ''escape route'' that results in pollen collection and flower pollination. The lateral sepals are fused, mostly hidden behind the pouch. Petals are green, bright pink widened, and round at the ends. The upper sepal is bright green, dark in the centre of the flower with few, thin stripes.

A small-sized, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with dark green, mottled, oval-shaped leaves approximately 15cm long. Solitary flowers, 8cm across, are carried on short upright stems that appear from the centre of the leaf rosette. This primary hybrid has large, rounded, pale cream petals with characteristic dark-pink mosaic pattern and pink edge on petals and dorsal sepal. The pouch is bright pink with darker pink veins.

description: A semi-terestrial, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with up to 20-30cm long, dark-green, mottled leaves, purple underneath. Solitary flowers, 7-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 10-20 cm long, upright stems. Large pouch is pale pink, with petals and upper sepal covered in darker, rose-pink mosaic pattern.

Solitary flowers, 7-10cm across, appear from the centre of the leaf rosette and are carried on 10 -20cm long , upright stems. The pouch (modification of the lip) is pale yellow or pale pink. Petals are elliptic with wavy edge, pale-yellow or pink, with small dark dots around the centre of the flower. Upper sepal is white, pale green or yellow, spotted around the centre.

A medium to large-sized, clump-forming, evergreen orchid with linear, bright green, glossy leaves up to 60cm long. Flowering stems, 50-60cm long emerge from centre of the leaf rosette and carry up to 6 large flowers. This primary hybrid carries the most attractive characteristics of its parents. The petals are very long, narrow with thin stripes and small brown spots. The upper sepal is large, white or pale yellow with dark brown stripes. The pouch, which a modification of lip is yellow or brown, veined.

Three to five large flowers are carried on 70cm long, terminal inflorescences, emerging from the centre of the leaf rosettes in summer. Petals are narrow, and long, typically curved downwards with dark brown spots. The pouch is pink or brown veined. White upper sepal is marked with dark brown linear pattern.

plant_range: NE India to SW China & Vietnam

description: A medium-sized, evergreen, cool to warm-growing, monopodial orchid; growing as an epiphyte or lithophyte on rocks in primary mountain forests. New growth emerges from a central tip on a long, central rhizome, covered tightly in leaf-carrying sheaths. Dark-green, channelled leaves are rigid, curved or straight. Characteristic, thick, silvery-green roots are formed at the base of the main stem. In autumn or winter, up to 75cm long racemose inflorescences appear from the main stem, carrying up to 50 fragrant flowers, each approx 5 - 6cm across. Flowers may wary in colour, but are usually white, with pale pink or pale purple lip.
plant_range: E India, SE Asia, S China

description: A medium-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for its unusually coloured, long-lasting flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a central tip on a long, central rhizome, while old, lower leaves gradually drop off. Strap-shaped, green or dark-green leaves up to 50cm long angle out from the stem, covering it completely. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system that hangs downwards at the base of plant. New roots emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from axils of leaves and main stem and carry a large number of waxy, pale blue or pale pink flowers. This naturally occuring primary hybrid has been described in 1897. The petals and sepals are elongated, with undulate edges. Petals are twisted in 90° angle. Each inflorescence carries 8-12 butterfly-like flowers.

A medium-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid, valued for its unusually coloured, long-lasting flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from a central tip on a long, stem-like rhizome, covered with green, alternate, leaf-bearing sheaths. Strap-shaped green or dark green leaves angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves appear from the top of the plant, old, lower leaves gradually drop off. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system of pale aerial roots that hangs downwards from the base of plants. New roots emerge from the rhizome, following the ascending growing trend. Long inflorescences appear from axils of leaves and the stem and carry 10 or more waxy, long-lasting, pale purple flowers. Petals are twisted in 90° giving flowers a butterfly-like appearance.

A small to medium-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a tip on a central rhizome, which is covered completely with alternate, strap-shaped, green or dark-green leaves. With the new leaves growing at the top, old, lower leaves gradually drop off. Leaves angle out from the main stem. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system, that hangs downwards at the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the main stem, following the ascending growing trend. Multiple inflorescences up to 45 cm long appear from the axils of the leaves and the main stem, and carry up to 20 fragrant, small flowers. Petals and sepals are pale brown and tesselated, while prominent front facing lip is pink, sometimes pale purple. Contrasting centre and back side of flowers are white. Flowers have a thick waxy texure, and measure approx 5cm across.

A medium to large-sized species of evergreen, tropical, epiphytic orchid, valued throught history for its unusual flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from the tip on a long, central rhizome. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves angle out from the main stem, and as new leaves appear from top, older, lower leaves gradually fall off. Compared to other species, leaves are set higher on the alternate bracts, covering the main stem. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive root system that hangs downwards at the base of the plant. New root emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from axils of leaf sheaths and stem, and carry 5 -14 flowers. Plant may produce multiple, occasionally branched inflorescences, carrying up to 50 flowers in total. The number of flowers per stem depends on the age of plant. Three colour variations occur naturally, with the pale blue being most famous. Pure white and pale pink variations can also be found. Flowers are waxy, 10 cm wide, with typical tesselation, creating a characteristic pattern on the sepals and petals. The petals are twisted at the base, giving the plant a butterfly-like resemblance, described by many plant hunters and botanists.
plant_range: E India & S China to Myanmar, Laos, & Thailand

description: A small-sized, evergreen, epiphytic orchid species. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from the tip of a long central rhizome, covered in alternate leaf-carrying sheaths. Linear, strap-shaped leaves are green or dark-green, up to 30cm long and 1-3cm wide. As new leaves emerge at the top, older leaves lower on the stem gradually drop off. New roots emerge from the stem, following the ascending growing trend. 1 -2 inflorescences appear from the axils of leaf sheaths in spring, carrying 4-8 waxy, fragrant flowers, 3-4cm in diameter, flowers are yellowish-brown, with thick, brown pattern. Clawed petals and sepals have pale yellow edge.

This hot-growing species has been a break-through in breeding many modern yellow hybrids, notably in 1950s and 60s. Its progeny carries bright yellow colour, longevity and sweet fragrance of their flowers. However, due to hot-growing, natural environment, its hybrids are less cold-tolerant that the blue-flowered species.

A large-growing, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid species. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from the central tip of a long rhizome, covered in leaf-bearing, green sheaths. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves up to 30cm long, angle out from the main stem. As new leaves emerge from the tip, old leaves lower on stem gradually fall off. Large aerial root system hangs downwards at the base of the plant, attaching to any surface is it grows. New, thick roots grow directly from the main stem, and follow the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences, up to 15cm long emerge from axils of the leaf sheaths, in late winter and spring. Each flowering stem carries 4-6 waxy flowers, approx. 5cm in diameter. A distinctive feature of this species and its hybrids is its lip: with two large, white, fiddle-shaped side lobes. Flowers are usually bright yellow, but dark yellow-orange and pale varieties occur in nature and in cultivation.

A large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid, valued for it unusual flowers. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from the cetral tip of the long, stem-like rhizome, covered in anternate, green, leaf-bearing sheats. Strap-like, green or dark green leaves up to 60cm long angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves appear from the top, old, lower leaves gradually fall off. A characteristic feature is is an impressive root system, hanging downwards from the base of plant. New roots emerge from the main stem, following the ascending growing trend. Multiple, long inflorescences emerge from axils of leaf sheaths and carry large number of butterfly-like, pale pink, or pale purple flowers. This primary hybrid is one of the first hybrids bred in Europe in 1920s. It produces large number of well-spaced, tesselated flowers, with petals twisted downwards. Lip is narrow, pink.

A large-sized, evergreen, tropical, terrestrial orchid species, growing in hot conditions in full sun. As a typical example of a monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a central tip on a long, slender, scrambling, stem-like rhizome. Terete, pencil-like leaves are attached to alternate leaf sheaths, covering the rhizome. As new leaves emerge from the top of the plant, old, lower leaves gradually drop off. Long, adventurous roots attaching to any surfaces in their surrounding emerge directly from the stem, following the ascending growing trend. The plant flowers in spring and summer on inflorescences 30cm long, sheated at base, carrying 2-12 large flowers, opening in succession. Flowers are showy and long-lasting, with large wide, prominent lip, with covered with pink markings. Side lobes and centre are darker, petals and sepals are white or pale pink.

A medium sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid species. As a typical example of a monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from the central tip on the stem-like rhizome, covered with green, leaf-bearing, alternate bracts. Strap-shaped, green or dark green leaves, up to 50cm long angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves grow from the top, older, lower leaves gradually fall off. Characteristic root system hangs downwards from the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the main stem, following the ascending growing trend. As they grow, they attach to any surface, anchoring the plant. Inflorescences emerge from the axils of leaves and main stem, and carry up to 8 scented, heavy- textured flowers, measuring approx. 7cm across. Petals and sepals are rounded, red-bronze, white at the back, with large darker spots, sometimes completely covering the surface. Centre of the flower is distinctly white. Prominent, broad, cupped lip is rose-pink or purple.

A medium-sized, evergreen, tropical orchid hybrid. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, new growth emerges from the central tip of the long, stem-like rhizome, covered in alternate leaf-bearing sheaths. Strap-shaped leaves up to 50cm long, angle out from the main stem. As new leaves grow from the top, older, lower leaves gradually drop off. A characteristic feature of the plant is an impressive roots system, that hangs downwards from the base of the plant. New roots grow from the main stem, following the ascending growing trend. Inflorescences emerge from the axils of leves and carry 8-10 large, flat, waxy flowers. Kasem's Delight gx is a historically important hybrid, that has given progeny to many modern breeding lines, mainly grown in Thailand. Large, flat round-shaped flowers measuring up to 10cm in diameter. All petals and sepals are flat and uniform in colour and size. They are heavily patterned with darker spots and mosaic-like tesselation.

A medium sized, evergreen, hot growing epiphytic orchid species. As a typical example of monopodial orchid, the new growth appears from the central tip on the long, stem-like rhizome, covered in leaf-bearing, green sheaths. Strap-shaped, green leaves angle out from the main stem. As the new leaves grow from the top, old, lower leaves gradually drop-off. A characteristic feature of the plant is a large roots system, formed at the base of the plant, providing anchor on the branches of trees. New roots emerge from the stem, following the ascending growing trend. 45cm long inflorescences emerge from the axils of leaves and carry up to 25, vaxy, fragrant, long-lasting flowers. Petals and sepals and disctinctively tilded backwards, with prominent column facing forwards. Small flowers, measuring 4cm across, are yellow or white, with many striped or spotted, brown markings. Three colour and shape varieties are accepted, occuring naturally in wild.

A large-sized, evergreen, tropical epiphytic orchid species. Green or dark green, strap- shaped leaves, up to 40cm long, angle out from the central stem. As the new leaves emerge from the top, the older, lower leaves gradually drop off. Leaves of this species are less densely arranged on the stems, with the sheath more prominently wrapped around the stem. New roots emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Flowering stems develop from the axils of leaves measuring up to 25cm and carry 10 to 12, waxy, long-lasting, fragrant flowers up to 5cm large. White on outer surface, flowers are pale brown to dark maroon, tesselated and heavy-textured. Lip is pale pink or pale purple, with white centre on the column.

description: A large-sized, evergreen, tropical, cool-growing epiphytic orchid growing on trees at higher altitudes in Philippines. Green, linear, alternate leaves up to 20cm long angle out from the main stem. As new leaves appear on the top, older, lower leaves gradually drop off. A characteristic feature of the plant is a system of aerial roots, hanging downwards at the base of the plant. Roots are silvery-green when dry and are a main source of water and nutrients, as well as anchoring support for the plant on the branches of trees. New roots emerge from the central stem, following the ascending growing trend. Flower stems up to 30cm long carry 8-15 fragrant, long-lasting flowers. Each flower is approx. 5cm in diameter. Petals and sepals are yellow, heavily covered with red, or chestnut-brown markings. Prominent feature is the lip, which is divided into two forks, with frilled edge. A large-sized, evergreen, tropical, hot-growing epiphytic orchid species. As an example of monopodial orchid, the new growth emerges from a central tip on top of the upright, stem-like rhizome. A characteristic feature is an aerial root system at the base of the plant. New roots emerge from the main rhizome, following the ascending growing trend. This species has been a major element in developing modern hybrids for its characteristic flat, two-tone, long-lasting flowers. The flowers - 8 to 12cm in diameter, are carried on a 30cm long stems. The inflorescences, often produced in pair, flower simultaneously, are usually shorter than leaves, and carry 7 - 10 densely arranged, fragrant flowers. Petals are slightly smaller than sepals, and rounded. Two lower sepals are disticntly dark, with red tesselated pattern. Dorsal sepal and petals are white or pale pink, with dark brown-red spots around the centre of flower. Small lip is three-lobed, with the two side lobes distinctly wider that other species.

A compact, leafy biennial usually grown as an annual. A cross between the texture of a cos and taste of an iceberg, this variety has boat-shaped green leaves and, depending on sowing, will be ready to harvest from summer to autumn

alternative_names: fen ragwort|bird's tongue|marsh groundsel|Senecio palludosus|Senecio paludosus

A deciduous climber, to around 2.2m, with mid-green leaves. Flowers are semi-double, very pale pink with a white bar and lightly wavy edges, and are produced in late spring and early summer, sometimes with a second flush in early autumn

A hybrid, autumn-flowering cormous perennial with strap-like green leaves appearing in the spring, after the funnel-shaped, lilac to pale pink flowers

primary_name: Dahlia 'Go Go Speckled Pink' (Go Go Series) (D)
description: A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated dark green leaves and double pink flowers, speckled with dark rose-red, appearing from summer through to autumn. A good variety for borders or for pots and containers
A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to about 30cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of large, funnel-shaped white flowers, appearing from June through until October
A bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark red foliage and yellow and red daisy-like double flowers with red centres which appear from July through until September
A slow-growing perennial succulent, forming a dense rosette of long, sword-shaped, fleshy green leaves, edged and tipped with sharp spines. Leaves flush deep red in sunny, dry conditions

A medium-sized, clump-forming deciduous perennial with slightly wavy, variegated green foliage with butter-yellow veining. New leaves emerge green all over. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with mid-green, leathery foliage and double, frosted plum-purple flowers, appearing in the spring

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, to around 50cm high, with narrowly heart-shaped green leaves with spiny margins. Spidery golden-yellow to orange-brown flowers with long narrow spurs are held on delicate stems above the leaves in spring. Leaves are tinted bronze in spring and autumn

A perennial bulb, to around 18cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves, slightly folded back at the base. Solitary, nodding flowers are produced in late winter and early spring, with outer and inner petals almost entirely green, with a fine white edge

A hardy, dwarf, deciduous tree to around 1.25m in height. Deeply lobed foliage emerges chartreuse green with purple-green edging in spring, changing to oranges and reds in the autumn. More sun tolerant than other palmatum cultivars and good for pots and containers due to its compact habit

A very rare, clump-forming, rhizomatous evergreen perennial with paddle-shaped green leaves. Large, spidery yellow flowers with dark maroon red edges and centres grow directly out from the rhizome in June. Performs best in containers out of direct sunlight as this may bleach the foliage
A single-flowered cultivar, to 1m in height. It bears flowers with pinky-purple petals, yellow at the base and with a yellow eye on dark stems above green foliage in summer and early autumn

A clump-forming, evergreen succulent, up to 20cm in height, forming a rose-shaped rosette of fleshy, grey-green leaves with white, waxy coating, pointed tips and a pink blush. Yellow-orange flowers appear on long, thin stems above the foliage in summer

A compact, upright, bushy deciduous shrub (and more vigorous than the other Bella varieties), with dark green leaves and bright red-pink flowers with double pale pink corollas and prominent pink stamens, appearing from summer through until the autumn

A medium-sized, very hardy large shrub or tree up to 8m in height, with dark green, glossy leaves with furry bronze-brown undersides. A compact, hardy deciduous shrub to around 50cm in height, with small, oval-shaped green foliage. Masses of cream flowers with darker centres appear from May through to October

A perennial bulb, up to 25cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves, slightly folded back at the base. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with ridged petals marked with a dark green inverted 'u' shape at the tip, and a faint pale green blotch towards the base

A compact, deciduous, rounded shrub, semi-evergreen in milder winters, to around 1m tall, with ovate dark green leaves and star-shaped yellow flowers with prominent central yellow stamens, flowering over a long period from early summer into autumn with large green berries appearing in September. An ideal variety for front of border or as a patio and container plant

A perennial bulb, to around 20cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, scented white flowers are produced in late winter, with broad, ridged outer petals, flaring and slightly upturned at the tips and marked with a dark green blotch in the centre. Inner petals are marked with a deep green, upside down heart-shaped blotch

A perennial bulb, to around 20cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Inner petals are marked with an x shaded deep green towards the tip and paler at the base

A tufted, evergreen fern to 50cm, grown as a houseplant, with large, glossy, mid-green fronds with a paler yellow-green stripe in the centre. A good addition to a flower arrangement as they are long-lasting, as well as terrariums or bottle gardens. Hardy in milder, coastal regions within the UK

A bulbous perennial usually grown as an annual for its edible shoots. One of the few varieties of 'all year round' spring onion, it has upright, dark green leaves with bright white shanks and a mild flavour. Sow anytime from March to early Dec

A perennial bulb, to around 10cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, double flowers are produced in late winter, with white outer petals, and a cluster of inner petals marked with a green bridge at the tip, spreading into a broad green blotch at the base
A compact, bushy, mound-forming, herbaceous perennial with narrow, mid-green foliage. Large, golden flowers with a red eye are produced from early summer to early autumn

A bushy, clump-forming, tuberous perennial to around 110cm in height, with dark green serrated leaves. Soft, lavendar-pink flowers with a creamy-white centre appear from summer through until the first frosts

A hardy, annual heirloom variety of brussels sprout preferring long, cool summers. The sprouts have a sweet flavour when harvested after frost and each stem will produce about 50-100 sprouts. This variety is suitable for growing in a pot or container

A perennial bulb, to around 10cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, double white flowers are produced in late winter and early spring, with curved, spreading outer petals, and a dense cluster of shorter inner petals with broad, deep green marks at the tips

A clump-forming, upright perennial, to around 50cm high, with narrowly sword-shaped, slightly grey-green leaves. Flowers have light yellow standards, with a violet-blue wash on the styles, and rich mustard-coloured falls. Lightly scented. Midseason

A bushy perennial grown as an annual vegetable for its edible tubers. A high-yielding, second early potato ready to lift in July/August, with waxy, pale yellow flesh, good for salads and for boiling. A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. A perennial bulb, up to 20cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves slightly folded back at the base. Nodding, scented white flowers are produced in late winter, with broad outer petals marked with a dark green inverted heart shape and slightly flared at the tips. Inner petals are marked with a deep green x shape
A slow-growing perennial succulent, forming a rosette of fleshy leaves up to 2m across at maturity. Leaves are grey-green, finely edged in dark red and tipped with red spines

A rhizomatous perennial, to just over 1m high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are sweetly scented, with violet-coloured standards with darker veins, reddish purple falls touched with yellow at the base, and an orange and purple beard
An upright, evergreen shrub or small tree with large, mid-green, leathery, glossy foliage. Bright cherry-red, double flowers with splashes of white appear from January through until April

A high quality annual cauliflower with very white flower heads (curds) which are resistant to discolouration and have a good flavour. Ready for harvesting from July through to October

A bushy, deciduous herbaceous perennial with dark red to dark green foliage and red and orange daisy-like flowers with dark red centres which appear from July through until September

A medium-sized deciduous tree with an upright habit, especially when young, later spreading to a slender oval-shaped crown. Leaves are lobed and deep green, turning orange and yellow in the autumn. Inconspicuous yellow-green flowers are produced in spring, followed by winged seeds in autumn

A small, slow-growing, hardy, deciduous tree with an upright, bushy habit. Deeply lobed foliage emerges bright red in spring, changing to dark red-purple in summer then finally to a striking bright red in the autumn. A good variety for pots and containers
A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to about 35cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of large, funnel-shaped dark purple flowers appearing from June through until November

A vigorous, semi-evergreen or deciduous climber about 4m tall, with long-stalked, dark, glossy green leaves. Great for covering walls, fences or pergolas and will tolerate some shade

A compact, deciduous, rounded shrub, semi-evergreen in milder winters, to around 1.5m tall, with ovate dark green leaves and large, star-shaped yellow flowers with prominent central yellow stamens, flowering over a long period from early summer into autumn with large green berries appearing in September. A perennial bulb, up to around 25cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves slightly folded back at the base. A perennial bulb, to around 10cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding white flowers are produced in late winter, with a narrow yellow ovary, broad outer petals, and inner petals marked with a thick, olive green, upside down 'u' shaped near the tip that blurs into yellow up to the base

A species of evergreen, climbing vine with thick, oval-shaped glossy variegated dark and light green, yellow and red succulent foliage. Fragrant, star-shaped white flowers appear in late summer to autumn

A cormous, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial with an upright growing habit and dark purple-green, blade-like foliage. Strong, arching flower stems produce bicoloured red and yellow tubular flowers from summer through until the autumn

A hardy, strong, deciduous tree to around 1.8m. Deeply lobed foliage is variegated pink, green, yellow and white in the spring, fading to cream in summer then finally red in autumn. The pale yellow-green and pink bark provides winter interest

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, double white flowers are produced in late winter and early spring, with broad, curving outer petals, and a mass of inner petals marked with a fine upside down v at the tip, and a paler green blotch near the base

A succulent evergreen subshrub, with an open habit and branching stems tipped with large rosettes of fleshy, lime green leaves with a variegated creamy-yellow edge. A deciduous tree, to around 8m high, with a spreading habit and large, oval-shaped green leaves. Large pink flowers, streaked with darker pink on the outsides, are produced before the leaves in spring
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with rounded, cupped textured variegated green foliage and irregular yellow margins. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer

plant_range: Tropical Africa and India to Taiwan

description: A mat-forming evergreen succulent, producing large rosettes of fleshy leaves with pointed tips and fine hairs along the edges. Leaves are bright green in the centre of the rosette, with a red flush at the base that spreads as the leaves flatten out
A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub to around 180cm in height, with coarsley toothed bright green foliage. Masses of pink mop head flower heads appear from July through until the autumn

An evergreen shrub to a height of 1.5m with oval-shaped, glossy dark green foliage and a branching habit. Clusters of trumpet-shaped, fragrant white flowers, flushed with pink, appear from August to October
A slow-growing perennial succulent, forming a rosette of very broad, fleshy green leaves edged with red-brown spines. Young leaves sometimes have a grey-green bloom
A small, clump-forming deciduous perennial with rounded, slightly cupped dark green foliage. Upright stems of pale lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with variegated, pale green foliage with yellow flecks and wavy edges. Upright stems of lavender pink-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, lance-shaped yellow foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with glossy, dark green foliage blushed with red. Upright red stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in the summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, pale yellow variegated foliage and green margins. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A medium, clump-forming deciduous perennial with long, textured and wavy bright yellow foliage. Upright stems of lavender-purple flowers appear in summer
A compact, upright perennial, to around 50cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant, clear pink flowers with darker pink eyes are produced in summer

A compact, clump-forming evergreen perennial with a trailing habit. Slightly pointed, smooth oval foliage is striped yellow to grey-green with grey-purple undersides. White flowers appear regularly from late spring through to summer

A very compact, slow-growing, clump-forming evergreen perennial with heavily-branched stems which spread across the surface. Rounded, smooth oval foliage is olive green with mottled, pale to very pale purple stripes and grey purple red undersides

Clump-forming perennial introduction from Bressingham Gardens by the curator of the Dell Garden. Slender, grassy, dark green foliage, and a late and long flowering display of dark burnt-red flowers that open to coral-red, held on stiffly upright stems 90-120cm tall, and flowering from early to late autumn

A dwarf, clump-forming perennial with rosettes of dark green, rounded leaves with a reddish tint to around 30cm in height. A good choice for colour in a shady border or rock garden and also makes a good houseplant

primary_name: Anemone hupehensis [Summer Breeze Snow] (Summer Breeze Series)

Compact, free-flowering clump-forming perennial

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial, upright at first but quick to trail as the stems become heavier. Oval-shaped, smooth foliage is mid-yellow with grey-green stripes, which fade as the plant matures, with dark grey-purple undersides. Flowers are white with pink edges but rarely appear on plants grown indoors

A clump-forming evergreen perennial, initially with an upright habit but changing to trailing as it grows. Pointed, oval foliage is variegated grey-green becoming more grey-purple to dark red in bright sunlight. Pale grey stripes give a shimmery effect and become flecked with dark purple in bright sunlight. Undersides are purple. Pink-purple flowers do not appear very often

A clump-forming evergreen perennial which initially has an upright habit, quickly changing to trailing as it grows. Wide, smooth, slightly furry oval foliage on short stems is dark grey-purple, with dark purple undersides. Pink flowers may appear all year round but are rare on plants grown indoors

alternative_names: silver inch plant 'Purple Plush'|Gibasis geniculata 'Purple Plush'
description: A clump-forming evergreen perennial, initially with an upright habit but changing to trailing as it grows. A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green foliage and tall, strong stems to around 45cm. Single flowers are a rich dark purple-red to violet-purple and appear around late April

A bushy, clump-forming, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with leathery dark green foliage and double, cup-shaped apricot-orange flowers with raspberry-red flushed edges and a green eye, which appear from February to April

A deciduous climber, to around 2.5m, with leaves divided into three mid-green, elliptic leaflets. Flowers are nodding, bell-shaped with recurved tips, and pale lilac pink with darker purple veins, and are borne singly in the leaf axils from midsummer to early autumn

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, double white flowers are produced in late winter, with long outer petals, and a neat cluster of inner petals marked with a broad green blotch that fades up towards the base

A clump-forming, deciduous perennial to about 60cm tall, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves, and clusters of large, funnel-shaped rich dark purple flowers, appearing from June through until September

A compact, clump-forming perennial, up to 50cm high, with green leafy, branching stems. Flowers have red to orange petals surrounding a large brown central cone, and are produced from midsummer into autumn

A clump-forming perennial, to around 60cm high, with lobed, hairy green leaves that tint reddish-bronze in autumn. Masses of rich purple flowers with darker veins are produced in a single burst in midsummer

A vigorous, mat-forming evergreen succulent, producing large rosettes of fleshy leaves that are pink at the base and lime green at the tips. Pink colour intensifies in summer. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers are produced from mature rosettes in summer; these die off after flowering and are replaced by new offsets

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 60cm in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and an abundance of rounded heads of tubular, two-toned flowers which fade from blue to white as they mature, from mid-summer to autumn

A low-growing, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial to around 50cm high, with basal rosettes of lobed and toothed green leaves. Prolific, long-lasting, semi-double brigh pumpkin-orange flowers are held on stems above the foliage from May to July then produce a second flush of blooms in the autumn. Tolerant of sun or part shade

A rhizomatous perennial, to 90cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are large, with soft yellow standards touched with pink, and deep raspberry red falls. Midseason

A compact, hardy, deciduous, clump-forming perennial with strap-like green leaves and upright, dark red hairy stems. Single, daisy-like flowers which are dark pinkish-red with a brown central cone, appear from mid summer, sometimes lasting through until the autumn. The dark red stems contrast beautifully with the flowers

A hardy perennial usually grown as an annual vegetable, with thick, semi-upright, mid-green leaves. Produces long, slender stems and is ready to harvest from November depending on sowing time. A giant swiss variety which shows some resistance to rust and is ideal for baby leek production
A leafy biennial, usually grown as an annual. This mixture of red and green lettuce have a range of textures and sizes for cut and come again harvesting

A low-growing, tuberous perennial with rosettes of broadly heart-shaped, glossy dark green leaves mottled with silver. Glossy, bright yellow flowers are produced in early spring. Leaves die back after flowering
A mat-forming evergreen succulent, producing large rosettes of fleshy, slightly grey-green leaves that flush pink and purple in the sun
Clump-forming perennial about 1m tall, with greyish-green linear leaves, and bearing tall spikes of yellow flowers with orange filaments, produced from midsummer to autumn
A low-growing, tuberous perennial with rosettes of broadly heart-shaped, dark bronze-coloured leaves with scalloped edges. White flowers are produced in early spring. Leaves die back after flowering
A low-growing evergreen or semi-evergreen perennial, forming mats of glossy, deeply veined, bright yellow-green leaves. Spikes of tubular, violet blue flowers are produced in mid to late spring
An upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with deeply divided mid-green leaves and branched stems bearing compact heads of small dark ruby red flowers in summer

A mat-forming evergreen succulent, producing large rosettes of fleshy, bright green leaves with pointed, reddish-brown tips. Tall spikes of starry pink flowers are produced from mature rosettes in summer; these die off after flowering and are replaced by new offsets

A deciduous climber, to around 3m, with purple-green young stems and leaves divided into three mid-green, elliptic leaflets. Flowers are nodding, bell-shaped and violet-blue, and are borne singly in the leaf axils from midsummer to early autumn

alternative_names: Cleome hassleriana [Clio Magenta]|Cleome spinosa 'Clio Magenta'|Cleome spinosa 'Dcleo2'

description: A very large 'tree' dahlia to around 3m in height, grown mainly for its fresh green foliage as it has an almost tropical feel. Thick, sturdy stems are bamboo-like and the large leaves are similar to Elder in shape. May produce single pink-purple flowers with orange centres from late October if grown in milder parts of the country or in a conservatory or greenhouse
A slow-growing, deciduous tree, to around 10m high, with large, broadly elliptic green leaves. Large, rich pink flowers with paler pink insides are produced before the leaves in spring

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage and fragrant, dark purple flowers, darker towards the centres, with white centres, appearing in the spring

A dwarf, compact, easy to care for deciduous shrub with variegated green and purple foliage and masses of bell-shaped ruby red flowers which appear from spring to early summer. Ideal for pots and containers or a small flower border
A popular, vigorous, hardy, ridged cucumber with a good flavour, which is easy to grow outdoors or indoors. Depending on sowing time, ready to harvest from July onwards
A succulent evergreen subshrub, forming a large, flat rosette of spoon-shaped, spirally arranged green leaves, with a broad cream-coloured margin edged with pink

A compact, mounding, trailing, floriferous tender annual with oval shaped, sticky and hairy mid to light-green leaves. Lightly fragrant, ruffled, fully double, pink flowers with darker magenta-pink veining appear from May through to the autumn. Ideal for hanging baskets and containers

A first early, high-yielding, vigorous heirloom variety of brussels sprout ready for harvesting from late August through to October. Sprouts are evenly spaced allong the stem and an attractive dark green in colour

A low-growing, tuberous perennial with rosettes of broadly heart-shaped, waxy dark green leaves with scalloped edges. Lrage, golden orange double flowers are produced in early spring. Leaves die back after flowering

A compact, evergreen shrub to around 150cm in height, with oval-shaped, bright, golden yellow foliage. Clusters of small, pink flowers appear along the stems from June to October. Makes an ideal neat, low-growing hedge and copes with heat well

A tall, bushy, clump-forming giant cactus variety with serrated dark green leaves and semi-double, spikey yellow flowers appearing on sturdy stems from summer through to autumn. A good variety for borders or for cut flowers and exhibiting

An upright, clump-forming perennial to around 70cm, with aromatic grey-green foliage and long spikes of bicoloured orange and yellow flowers from spring to autumn, which become more cream to salmon pink in colour as the temperatures become cooler towards the autumn

A compact, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial alpine producing stems to 20cm high and cut, dark red foliage. Clusters of bright blue flowers are produced above the foliage from spring through to summer

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. Flowers are large, double and peony-like, soft, creamy-white with raspberry-pink edging. As the flowers open, they become more buttery in colour with further raspberry markings. Stands approximately 20cm high, and flowers in late Spring

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves and double, bowl-shaped showy lilac-pink flowers on sturdy stems. Stands approximately 40cm high, and flowers in late Spring. Matches well with the darker purple 'Negrita'

alternative_names: slender-petalled ginger lily 'Ziyadum'|Hedychium from Ziyadum, Myanmar
description: An upright, rhizomatous perennial to 1.5m with large, broad, lance-shaped dark green foliage. Spidery, pure white flowers with very pale yellow centres, fragrant both day and evening, appear from late summer through to October

A clump-forming deciduous perennial to 60-90cm tall, with deeply dissected, greyish-green leaves composed of leaflets, and bearing tall stems with clusters of small dark crimson egg-shaped flowerheads during late summer and autumn
This plant is listed on the CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) as a protected species. See the RHS pages on importing and exporting plants for further details
A compact, evergreen shrub to around 120cm in height, with oval-shaped, glossy dark green foliage. Clusters of fragrant, sugared almond pink flowers appear along the stems from June to October
A rhizomatous perennial, to around 1m high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have golden brown standards and violet falls with golden brown edges. Mid season

alternative_names: Persian cyclamen [Absolu de Morel]|Cyclamen persicum 'Absolu Victoria'
description: A tender, tuberous perennial to 30cm high, with heart-shaped, dark green foliage with silvery-green marbling. Small, fragrant, twisted white flowers with magenta-pink petal tips appear from autumn through to spring. A great choice to include in a glasshouse alpine display
A clump-forming, cormous perennial with long, strap-shaped green leaves. Produces arching spikes of downward-facing, bright red flowers in late summer
A compact perennial to around 40cm high, with toothed green leaves. Slender spikes of intense blue flowers are produced from June to August. A good choice for patio pots and containers

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial to about 30cm high, forming a mound of lobed, dark green leaves flushed with dark bronze, in some cases appearing almost black. Tall sprays of small white flowers are borne on slender stems above the leaves in late spring and early summer

A hardy, deciduous, heavy-cropping walnut tree around 5m tall, with dark green foliage. More compact than other varieties it has delicate, but fairly inconspicuous pale green catkins which appear in spring, turning into green fruit in late summer from which edible walnuts can be extracted. Walnuts are produced on quite young trees - usually less than ten years old. Most walnut trees will need a pollinator of a different variety, even if self-fertile

A compact rhizomatous perennial, to around 60cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped green leaves. Flowers have a light musky scent, and white standards and falls brushed and speckled with purple. Early season

alternative_names: French lavender [Lavinnova Plum Delight]|Lavandula stoechas [Plumberry Ruffles]
description: A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with narrow, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant, dark purple flowers, topped with large, ruffled, plum-coloured bracts, are borne on short stems from early to late summer
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, toothed pale green foliage and fragrant, dark, reddish-brown flowers with golden yellow centres, appearing in the spring
An upright deciduous shrub, to around 1.2m high, with lobed, aromatic deep green leaves with pale undersides. Hanging clusters of pink flowers are produced alongside the leaves in mid- to late spring
A deciduous tree, with an upright habit and large, oval-shaped green leaves. Early flowering, producing large, deep reddish-pink flowers before the leaves in spring
A compact perennial, forming a mound of dark green foliage. Tall, slender spikes of small white flowers touched with pink are produced in late spring and early summer

A compact, hardy, deciduous, clump-forming perennial with strap-like green leaves and upright, hairy stems. Single, daisy-like, fragrant, bright lemon yellow flowers with a green central cone are produced in profusion from mid summer, sometimes lasting through until the autumn

A compact, low-growing, mat-forming evergreen alpine perennial to around 10cm height, forming rosettes of green finger-shaped leaves, with small clusters of bright pink flowers 10mm wide borne on erect stems to 5cm tall in early summer

A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, mid-green, leathery foliage and fragrant, delicate, slightly frilled pale primrose-yellow flowers, with darker yellow centres but no 'eye', appearing in the spring
A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves and single, cup-shaped rose-pink flowers with finely fringed petals. Stands approximately 40cm high and flowers in late Spring

A dwarf perennial, to around 35cm high, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have deep purple standards, creamy white falls with broad purple edges, and an orange beard tipped with purple, and are produced from late spring to early summer

A rhizomatous perennial, to around 45cm high, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers are scented, with long, violet blue standards and falls, and an orange beard. An historic cultivar bred in the 1880s

alternative_names: French lavender [Lavinnova Purple Supreme]|Lavandula stoechas [The Prince]
description: A compact, bushy evergreen shrub, with narrow, aromatic grey-green leaves. Dense spikes of small, fragrant purple flowers, topped with large, ruffled purple bracts, appear on short stems from early to late summer

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. Flowers are large, double and peony-like, dark rose-pink with green stripes on the outer petals. Stands approximately 50cm high, and flowers in late Spring
An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall, with broad, short, variegated, cream and green striped leaves. Clusters of soft orange flowers with yellow throats appear on erect stems from March to May

An evergreen perennial to 55cm tall, with strap-shaped, striped and variegated, pale yellow-green leaves. Clusters of translucent peach-orange flowers with a red edge and pale orange throat appear on erect stems from March to May
A compact, bushy evergreen shrub to around 100cm high, with small, rounded, glossy dark green leaves. Slender spikes of bright pink flowers are produced from summer into autumn

A compact, hardy, bushy deciduous tree with rounded, lobed dark green foliage. A heavy cropper with medium-sized pale brown fruits when ripe, with a good flavour, appearing in late summer to early autumn. Self fertile

A clump-forming perennial, to round 1m high in flower, with upright, narrowly sword-shaped, grey-green leaves. Flowers have short, light violet standards, rich reddish purple falls with a white halo at the base and a yellow signal. Mid to late season
Clump-forming perennial plant with grassy mid-green leaves, and bearing stems to 1m in height of pinkish-orange buds opening creamy-yellow flowers, in early to midsummer

A vigorous perennial to about 1.5m tall, forming a clump of upright stems bearing coarse, hairy dark green leaves to 25cm in length, with winged stalks. Clusters of tubular, rich purple flowers 2cm in length appear in late spring and summer

A compact, hardy, deciduous, clump-forming perennial with strap-like green leaves and upright, hairy stems. Single, daisy-like flowers are bright purple-pink, with a greenish-brown central cone, appearing from mid summer, sometimes lasting through until the autumn. The flowers keep their colour well

A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated dark-green leaves and double sunset-coloured flowers in pinks, purples and yellow, appearing from June through to November. A good variety for borders, pots and containers or for cut flowers

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Early flowering, producing nodding, solitary flowers in mid winter or sometimes late autumn. Flowers have spreading outer petals brushed with pale green, and deep green inner petals with a fine white edge

primary_name: Brassica oleracea var. alba (Capitata Group) 'Robinsons Champion'
description: A giant variety of annual cabbage with large, round heads and a full flavour. Ideal for cooking and for making coleslaws. Matures from September and is frost hardy
A bushy deciduous shrub, to around 1m high, with arching stems and narrow, slightly grey-green leaves. Cone-shaped clusters of lightly scented lilac purple flowers are produced from midsummer

A clump-forming perennial, to around 85cm high in flower, with narrowly sword-shaped, slightly grey-green leaves. Flowers have short, ruffled white standards heavily brushed with purple, and broad white falls with purple veining
An evergreen perennial to 75cm tall, with strap-shaped green leaves. Clusters of cream flowers with golden yellow throats appear on erect stems from March to May

A compact rhizomatous perennial, to around 55cm high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped green leaves. Flowers are lightly scented, with yellow standards and cream falls lightly streaked with reddish purple

A late-season, annual, large-headed savoy cabbage with attractive, wrinkled, emerald green foliage and a tender texture and sweet flavour - more so than other savoy varieties. Harvest from November through to February. An attractive variety to include in an ornamental border
A compact evergreen perennial, forming a low, spreading mound of linear green leaves. Masses of pink flowers with deeply notched petals cover the foliage in late spring

A large deciduous tree, with an upright habit and oval-shaped green leaves. Flowers are cup-and-saucer shaped, and deep reddish pink on the outsides, with paler streaks inside the centre of the petals. Flowers on bare stems, though slightly later than some other varieties, so often avoiding the worst of the frost

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 40cm high, forming a mound of lobed and toothed, dark purple leaves. Tall sprays of deep pink flowers are borne on slender stems above the leaves in late spring and early summer

An upright, clump-forming deciduous herbaceous perennial producing stems to 30cm high and finely cut green foliage. Clusters of violet-blue flowers with darker purple veining are produced above the foliage from spring through to summer. Ideal for ground cover

A slow-growing, dwarf evergreen conifer, to around 60cm high in 10 years, with a spreading habit become more upright as it matures. Short, flat, dark green needles with silvery undersides are arranged in dense rings around the branches

A strong, compact, deciduous shrub to around 120cm in height, with coarsley toothed dark green foliage. Very large double, white mophead flower heads, made up of lots of smaller double flowers, appear from June through to autumn

primary_name: Hylotelephium telephium [Seduction Hot Rose Dark Stems] (Seduction Series)

description: A sweet cherry producing abundant white blossom in spring that is followed by pale yellow fruit flushed red, with aromatic, sweet, spicy-flavoured whitish to pale yellow flesh. Cropping season: late June – early July Pollination group 3
A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green foliage and tall, strong stems to around 30cm. Double, bowl-shaped fragrant flowers are pink with a cream and green base, and appear in mid Spring

An annual mediterranean vegetable also known as 'Broccoli Rab' or 'Rapini' which can be translated as 'Turnip Greens'. It has long, serrated green leaves with edible florets hidden randomly amongst the foliage, similar to sprouting broccoli. Eaten when the heads are young, they taste like a cross between spinach and broccoli but also have a tangy, mustard-like taste more similar to a turni[. Easy to grow and requires little space, so good for pots and containers. If regular sowings are made, can be harvested from May through to October
A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green foliage and tall, strong stems to around 40cm. Single flowers are dark purple and appear from around mid April

A sweet cherry producing abundant white blossom in spring that is followed by glossy purplish-red, rounded fruit resistant to splitting, with fairly firm, dark red sweet flesh. Cropping season: mid May – early June. Pollination group 2

A perennial bulb, to around 15cm high, with narrow, grey-green leaves. Nodding, semi-double white flowers are produced in late winter, with a narrow green ovary, long outer petals, and two rows of inner petals with a loose x shape green marking

An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall, with strap-shaped green leaves and tight clusters of pale peach orange flowers, turning darker as they mature, appearing on erect stems from March through to the summer

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. Flowers are coronet-shaped, long-lasting and dark plum-purple with irregular, curled petals. Stands approximately 50cm high, and flowers in late Spring

A robust, clump-forming perennial to around 90cm in height, with rounded, silvery grey-green spikey leaves. Clusters of small purple and blue flowerheads appear above narrow, spiny silvery-green bracts on upright, branched silver stems, in mid and late summer

alternative_names: Astrantia major [Magical Diamonds Soft Pink]|Astrantia major 'Ruiastpi'
description: An upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with deeply divided mid-green leaves and branched stems bearing compact heads of small pink and green flowers surrounded by green-tipped white bracts in summer

A clump-forming perennial, to around 85cm high in flower, with narrow green leaves. Early flowering, with short, spreading white standards with purple edges, and broad reddish-purple falls with large yellow signals at the base

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves. A parrot variety with large, fragrant, double bright red flowers with hints of yellow and dark purple. Stands approximately 30cm high, and flowers in mid to late Spring
A slow-growing evergreen conifer, to around 1.8m in 10 years, with a dense, conical habit. Stiff, sharp-tipped blue-green needles are arranged radially around branching stems
A succulent evergreen subshrub, with thick stems tipped with rosettes of broadly spoon-shaped, pointed green leaves the flush red in strong light. Hardier than some other varieties

A clump-forming perennial, to around 60cm high, with upright stems and narrow, dark green leaves that are flushed reddish purple, especially when young. Yellow-green flowers are produced at the tips of the stems in late spring and early summer. Foliage retains some red colouring throughout the summer, especially on the backs of the leaves, and colour deepens to near black as the temperatures drop in autumn
An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall, with strap-shaped green leaves and green, cream and pale orange flowers turning darker orange as they mature, appearing on erect stems from March through to May

A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green foliage and tall, strong stems to around 55cm. Large, single, oval-shaped flowers are yellow, fading to apricot-yellow flushed with raspberry-pink, and have a pale apricot-orange interior. Flowers appear mid to late spring
An evergreen perennial to 60cm tall, with broad, short, green leaves and clusters of orange flowers with paler throats appearing on erect stems from March to May
A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial to 40cm, with grey-green leaves and feathery spikes of dark purple flowers during the summer and autumn

primary_name: Espostoa lanata subsp. ruficeps unnamed cultivar

description: A perennial bulb with broadly lance-shaped green leaves and single, cup-shaped candy-pink flowers, white at the base, and finely fringed petals. Stands approximately 35cm high and flowers in late Spring
A bulbous perennial grown as a vegetable with upright, blueish-green leaves. Flat-top bulbs with pink flesh and pink skins with a mild, sweet flavour provide an abundant, early crop and store well
A bushy evergreen shrub, with linear, aromatic silver leaves. Spikes of relatively large, scented purple flowers are borne on slender stems in summer

A clump-forming, semi-evergreen perennial, to around 30cm high, forming a mound of lobed and toothed, yellow-green and amber coloured leaves with reddish undersides. Tall sprays of white flowers are borne on slender red stems above the leaves in late spring and early summer

An upright, clump-forming herbaceous perennial with deeply divided mid-green leaves and branched stems bearing compact heads of small white and pink flowers surrounded green-tipped white bracts in summer

A tall, bushy, clump-forming giant cactus variety with serrated dark green leaves and semi-double, spikey pure white flowers appearing on sturdy stems from summer through to autumn. A good variety for borders or for cut flowers and exhibiting
A bushy deciduous shrub, to around 1m high, with arching stems and narrow, grey-green leaves. Cone-shaped clusters of lightly scented deep purple flowers are produced from midsummer

A tall, bushy, clump-forming semi-cactus form with serrated dark green leaves and semi-double, spikey soft orange-yellow flowers appearing on sturdy stems from summer through to autumn. A good variety for borders or for cut flowers and exhibiting

An annual italian plum vine tomato with small, almost seedless, egg-shaped fruits which are ready to harvest from July through to September. A great variety for salads, and for drying for winter use. Stores well for months

A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated near-black leaves and double, bright magenta-pink flowers appearing from July through to October. A good variety for the front of a border or for pots and containers

A deciduous shrub or small tree, to around 3m in 10 years, with oval-shaped, deep green leaves. Large, creamy white flowers are produced in late spring, followed by strawberry-like fruits that ripen to pinkish-red. New leaves produced in hot summers are often flushed yellow and red, before turning orange and red in autumn

primary_name: Viola × wittrockiana 'Frizzle Sizzle Mini Yellow' (Frizzle Sizzle Mini Series) (P)

Viola × wittrockiana [Frizzle Sizzle Mini Tapestry] (Frizzle Sizzle Mini Series) (mixed) (P)

Viola × wittrockiana 'Frizzle Sizzle Lemonberry' (Frizzle Sizzle Series) (P)

description: A compact, semi-evergreen free-flowering annual with indented green foliage and frilly, speckled dark purple velvety flowers with a yellow eye which appear from winter through to spring
A spreading, evergreen perennial to about 15cm, producing dark purple flowers over a long period from mid-spring to mid-autumn

A clump-forming, evergreen perennial, upright at first but soon starts to trail. Pointed, smooth, oval-shaped foliage is green to purple with two thin, broken silver stripes, sometimes overlaid with pale cream, yellow, white or pink stripes
A bushy, evergreen sub-shrub or woody-based perennial, to 60cm tall, with small, aromatic leaves and spikes of widely spaced, deep red-purple flowers from summer to late autumn

A succulent evergreen subshrub, with thick stems tipped with rosettes of long, narrow, variegated green and pale yellow leaves that are edged with fine hairs. Leaves tint pink to dark red in strong light

An evergreen, herbaceous perennial that reaches approximately 1m in height when in flower. It produces a clump of green, arching strap-like leaves and an abundance of rounded heads of tubular, dark purple to almost black flowers from mid-summer to autumn

A compact, biennial Kohl Rabi grown as an annual, with an unusual and interesting purple globe-shaped swollen stem and oval, blue-green leaves. It has a sweet, crunchy taste and texture. Can be eaten raw in salads or cooked. Ready to harvest from June to September

A mat-forming, evergreen perennial to about 10cm high, with small, hairy, grey-green leaves. Pure white, four-petalled flowers are produced in short spikes from mid-spring to early summer
A compact, rosette-forming, evergreen perennial with spoon-shaped, mid-green, leathery foliage and delicate white flowers, with a hint of pale yellow as the buds open, appearing in the spring
A dwarf perennial, to around 35cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant, bright pink flowers are produced in summer
A deciduous tree, with an upright habit and oval-shaped green leaves. Flowers are scented, deep pink at the base with pale, near-white insides, and are produced before the leaves in spring
A dwarf perennial, to around 35cm high, with lance-shaped green leaves. Rounded clusters of fragrant, deep reddish pink flowers are produced in midsummer

A hybrid of Pachyphytum and Echeveria, this succulent houseplant grows to around 15cm forming rosettes of thick, fleshy pointed blue-green foliage with pink-tinged edges and tips. Tubular-shaped yellow flowers with pink edges can sometimes appear in summer. Foliage colour may vary throughout the year, depending on fluctuations in light and temperature

An upright, deciduous, often vase-shaped, shrub to 4m tall with broadly oval green leaves that turn attractive shades of orange and yellow in autumn. Slightly fragranced, bright pink flowers with narrow crimped petals are borne on the bare branches in late winter and spring

A clump-forming, compact perennial to around 70cm in height, producing a mound of divided blue-green leaves. Pale green buds open to semi-double flowers with tightly-packed petals giving a frilly effect. Flowers are cerise at the base to white at the tops of the petals and appear in late spring to early summer

alternative_names: begonia [Shangri-La]|Begonia circumlobata 'Monshayne'|Begonia circumlobata 'Chandler's Hardy'|Begonia hemsleyana 'Chandler's Hardy Silver'

primary_name: Polystichum setiferum Plumosum Group Washfield form

description: A bushy annual 'no heat' peruvian chilli with ovate, mid-green leaves. Produces small cream flowers with a golden centre from the leaf axils in summer, which go on to produce hanging, bullet-shaped edible fruits which turn from green to red as they ripen. Fruits are fairly thick-walled and firm with a sweet and fruity flavour

A low-growing evergreen perennial, forming mats of variegated leaves, with pale green centres edged with creamy white and dark green. Spikes of tubular, violet blue flowers are produced in mid to late spring
A compact, clump-forming, herbaceous perennial to around 25cm in height, with a neat mound of divided green leaves. White spurred flowers are produced on short, slender, upright stems in spring

A clump-forming, deciduous herbaceous perennial, to 55cm tall, with a rosette of toothed and prickly, lance-shaped, dark green leaves emerging from pointed buds. In summer, short spikes bear white flowers hooded with lilac-purple bracts. The leaves, stems and flower spikes are covered with silky hairs

A compact, hardy bushy deciduous perennial with lobed dark green leaves. Single, pure white flowers with yellow centres appear on short stems from late summer through to autumn. Ideal for growing in pots and containers
An upright, bushy, suckering deciduous perennial with lobed mid-green leaves. Single, dark rose-pink flowers appear from late summer through to autumn

A rhizomatous perennial, to around 1m high in flower, with upright, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves, and tall, branching stems bearing 7 to 9 flowers. Flowers have ruffled, pure white standards and falls, and a white beard touched with yellow at the base. Late midseason

A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated bronzey dark-green leaves and double lilac pink flowers, burgundy red underneath, appearing from July through to November. A good variety for borders, pots and containers or for cut flowers

A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated dark-green leaves and large, double pale pink, pale orange and white striped flowers, appearing from July through to November. A good variety for borders, pots and containers or for cut flowers

A bushy, clump-forming perennial with serrated dark-green leaves and double, fimbriated rose-pink and yellow flowers, appearing from July through to November. A good variety for borders, pots and containers or for cut flowers

A dwarf, clump-forming perennial with rosettes of dark purple-green, scalloped leaves to around 25cm in height. Masses of star-shaped pink and white flowers with yellow centres appear in contrast with the leaves from September through the autumn. A clump-forming bulbous perennial with green, strap-like foliage and large, slightly reflexed white flowers with a green eye, appearing from March to April
Vigorous clump-forming perennial with dark green, softly-hairy, divided leaves, and narrow plumes of flowers in mid to late summer
A spreading deciduous large shrub or tree with ovate leaves to 20cm in length, and drooping clusters of small, fragrant white flowers and small spindle-shaped fruits covered with light brown hairs

Fl. star-shaped, 42mm wide, facing upwards; perianth segments 8mm long, lanceolate, acute, opening yellow, maturing to white with yellow towards base, spreading, plane, smooth and of heavy substance, separated; corona 30mm long, funnel-shaped, ribbed, yellow, constricted near mouth, mouth wavy and shallowly lobed, with rim minutely crenate. Dwarf. Mid-season

A clump-forming, bulbous perennial, to 15cm tall, with strap-shaped green foliage. Densely packed flower spikes produce small green buds opening to sweetly fragranced, almost waxy clusters of tiny pyramid-shaped snow-white and powder-blue flowers which fade to darker blue and appear in the spring. Very weather-resistant

A neat, compact, clump-forming bulbous perennial with upright, narrow pale green strap-like leaves. Upright stems produce grape-like clusters of small, fragrant white flowers, blushed pink towards the end of the season, in spring

A vigorous, compact, clump-forming, perennial bulb, with narrow, neat linear green leaves. Densely packed spikes of small, pure white flowers, fading to blush pink as they finish flowering, appear in the spring over a long flowering period. Shows good weather resistance

Fl. 90mm wide; perianth segments 35mm long, broadly ovate, blunt, white, spreading, plane or with margins a little incurved, creased and of heavy substance, overlapping half; the inner segments narrower, shouldered at base; corona 33mm long, funnel-shaped, smooth, orange, with a broad hand of yellow at base (to halfway along perianth) and a fine band of yellow at rim, mouth ribbed and slightly flared, with rim notched. Mid-season. Sunproof

Fl. forming a double triangle, 100mm wide; perianth segments 33mm long, roundish, very broad, white, spreading, plane, smooth and of membranaceous substance, overlapping half; the inner segments narrower, more nearly ovate; corona 22mm long, narrow funnel-shaped, angled, coral pink, mouth straight, ribbed and wavy, with rim notched. Mid-season to late. Sunproof

Fl. rounded, 78mm wide; perianth segments 25mm long, rounded, very broad, blunt, mucronate, lemon yellow, slightly reflexed, plane, smooth and of heavy substance, overlapping half or more; the inner segments narrower, ovate, shouldered at base, scarcely mucronate, more nearly spreading, plane or with margins incurved; corona 24mm long, peachy pink, split into six segments, each closely overlying a perianth segment forming and inner and an outer whorl of three, lobed, with lobes overlapping, wavy or lightly frilled. Mid-season. Sunproof

A large, spreading, deciduous shrub or small tree, with bright green, pointed, oval leaves which turn yellow in autumn. Hanging clusters of small, fragrant, white flowers are produced in late spring and early summer, followed by five-ribbed fruits

primary_name: Hydrangea paniculata [Living Red Velvet] ('Lc No19') (Living Creations Series)
description: A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub, to around 100cm high, with strong branches of oval-shaped, dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Large, densely packed cones of creamy-white flowers turn to dark, reddish-pink as they mature, appearing in mid to late summer. Its compact form makes it a great choice for flower borders, pots and containers or smaller gardens
A clump-forming, bushy tuberous perennial with dark green serrated leaves. Large, striking dark-red to black decorative form flowers, appear from summer until the first frosts

primary_name: Hydrangea paniculata [Living Little Rosy] ('Lc No16') (Living Creations Series)
description: A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub, to around 70cm high, with strong branches of oval-shaped, dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Cones of white flowers turn gradually to dark pink as they mature. Its compact, neat habit makes it a great choice for flower borders, pots and containers or smaller gardens

primary_name: Hydrangea paniculata [Living Milk & Honey] ('Lc No17') (Living Creations Series)
description: A compact, bushy, deciduous shrub, to around 90cm high, with strong branches of oval-shaped, dark green leaves with finely serrated edges. Large, densely packed cones of creamy flowers, which may become faintly blushed with pale pink and honey-yellow as they mature, appear in mid to late summer. Its compact, rounded form makes it a great choice for flower borders, pots and containers or smaller gardens

This hibiscus will really earn its place in your garden due to its enormous, slightly flatter, flowers (up to 19cm diameter!) and a long flowering period from June sometimes right into autumn. The exotic flowers are bright pink with a red centre and are set against glossy, deep green leaves making this a lovely option for a sunny border

description: A bushy, upright annual with large ovate leaves with wavy margins, and funnel-shaped lavender or pinkish flowers to 20cm long, followed by spiny fruits 5cm long

alternative_names: duo ban bao zi hua|Nomocharis meleagrina

primary_name: Lilium sealyi from Pianma, Yunnan, China (IX)

alternative_names: centipede plant|ribbon bush|ribbon rush|Homalocladium platycladum|Muehlenbeckia platyclados|Homalocladium platycladium

description: Fl. 78 mm wide, forming a double triangle, facing down; perianth segments ovate, mucronate, brilliant greenish yellow 6B, reflexed, plane, smooth and of heavy substance, overlapping; the inner segments narrower; corona cylindrical, smooth, white, mouth flared and slightly ribbed. Mid-season

Fl. forming a double triangle, 110 mm wide; perianth segments very broad, mucronate, greenish white (155A), spreading, with margins incurved, smooth and of heavy substance, overlapping; the inner segments narrower; corona funnel-shaped, ribbed, vivid yellow 9B, mouth flared and frilled, with rim crenate. Early

Fl. rounded; perianth segments roundish, very broad, rounded at apex, mucronate, white, spreading, plane, creased and of heavy substance, overlapping half or more; the inner segments narrower, scarcely mucronate, somewhat shouldered at base; corona funnel-shaped, angled, deep reddish pink, mouth flared and wavy, with rim crenate. Mid-season. Sunproof

Fls 1-3 but usually 2 per stem, 72 mm wide; perianth segments broadly ovate, blunt, somewhat truncate, opening green, becoming tinged with medium yellow, with slight white mucro, spreading, plane, overlapping one-third; the inner segments narrower, with margins wavy; corona cup-shaped, closely ribbed, medium green with a suffusion of yellow, with a line of golden yellow at rim, mouth straight. Early

Perianth segments very broadly ovate, blunt, yellow, with slight white mucro, spreading, with margins minutely incurling, smooth, overlapping half; the inner segments more narrowly ovate, shouldered at base, with margins a little wavy; corona bowl-shaped, red, with mouth shallowly lobed, rim entire. Mid-season

Fls XX per stem, forming a double triangle; perianth segments ovate, blunt, mucronate, spreading, plane or with margins incurved, smooth and of heavy substance, overlapping one-third; the inner segments scarcely mucronate; corona cup-shaped, smooth, mouth straight and even, with rim entire. Very early. Height XXX Sunproof. Intensely sweetly scented

Fl. rounded, 98 mm wide; perianth segments very broad, shouldered at base, rounded at apex, brilliant greenish yellow 6B, spreading, with margins incurling, smooth and of heavy substance, overlapping; the inner segments narrower; corona cup-shaped, smooth, strong orange 25A, mouth straight and even, with rim entire. Mid-season
